Name: WomanUp & Pitch (Michigan Women Forward)
Description: Michigan Women Forward runs five WomanUp & Pitch competitions across the state each cycle, with awards of $10,000 (first), $5,000 (second), $2,500 (third), $1,000 (audience choice) and $500 to every non-winning finalist. Eligibility: a Michigan-based for-profit business that is at least 51% woman-owned; cannabis, weapons and adult entertainment businesses are excluded, and previous finalists who did not win may reapply after one year. Applying means submitting a two-page concept paper with a $20 fee at cognitoforms.com/MichiganWomenForward/WomanUpPitchApplication. Selected finalists receive coaching, mentorship and expert guidance to build their business plan and pitch, and free info sessions run during the application window. For the 2027 cycle, applications opened August 10 and close October 4, 2026, with the competitions held February–March 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Michigan-based for-profit business, at least 51% woman-owned. Excludes cannabis, weapons and adult entertainment. Previous non-winning finalists may reapply after one year.

Name: Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant
Description: Printed Matter awards three unrestricted $10,000 grants to independent publishers of artists' books, along with a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair. Eligible publishers need at least one year of publishing history, a record of releasing one or more titles annually, active operations with future titles planned, and generally small-scale distribution. No application fee. The 2026 round closes October 4.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Independent artists'-book publishers, 1+ year history, 1+ title per year, currently active with titles planned, generally without major distribution support. Past Publisher Work Grant winners ineligible. No application fee. Direct application: https://printedmatterinc.submittable.com/submit/357163/printed-matter-publisher-work-grant-2026 . Winners also receive a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair.

Name: Detroit Legacy Business Project Grant
Description: The Detroit Legacy Business Project supports small businesses that have operated in Detroit for over 30 years and contribute to the city’s cultural identity. Grants provide financial assistance and business support to help these longstanding businesses continue their impact. Funding includes $2,500 and $5,000 microgrants, $15,000 grants per council district, and one $50,000 citywide grant, with a total of 30 awards per round.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- 30 years of business in Detroit
- Significant historic, economic, cultural, or social contribution to the City
- Committed to retaining core product and service categories

ELIGIBLE BUSINESS TYPES (merged from duplicate record rechAzIdNQWC1pzXN):
- For-profit Sole Proprietorships
- General Partnerships
- Limited Partnerships (LP)
- Limited Liability Partnerships (LLP)
- Corporations (Inc., Corp.)
- Limited Liability Companies (LLC)
- Low-profit Limited Liability Company (LC3)
- Faith-based organizations, subject to 24 CFR § 570.200(j), participating in registered and licensed for-profit commercial activity
- Independently owned businesses that participate in retailers' cooperatives are eligible to apply
- A nonprofit enterprise that sells a product or service to the public or other companies, where that product or service has been sold for the last 30 years

Awards range from $2,500 and $5,000 microgrants to $15,000 per council district and one $50,000 citywide grant, 30 awards per round, distributed across all seven city council districts. Priority to first-time applicants. Funds are issued as reimbursements or prepayments for approved projects.

Name: Detroit Startup Fund
Description: The Detroit Startup Fund is a City of Detroit initiative that provides grants and support to help Detroit-based founders and tech startups launch, scale, and create jobs. Eligible startups can apply for $15,000 seed grants or $50,000 scale grants, with applications due by March 2, and must demonstrate growth potential and a positive impact on Detroit. The program is part of a broader effort by the city to reduce barriers, foster innovation, and strengthen Detroit’s startup ecosystem.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- You or your startup must be based in Detroit
- Your business should be able to grow and offer something that helps the city or makes life better for Detroiters
- You agree to officially register as a Detroit-based business
- You’re willing to share updates and results with the City of Detroit and DEGC

Name: Arts for Learning Maryland — Access for All Grants
Description: Access for All provides grants that subsidize the cost of bringing professional teaching artists into Maryland schools and early-childhood centers. Grants cover up to 80% of program costs for assemblies, residencies, workshops, and professional development, reducing financial barriers to arts education.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maryland public schools serving PreK–12 and early-childhood sites, including Judy Centers and licensed childcare centers.

Name: Chicago Neighborhood Market Grant Program
Description: The Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection is distributing $450,000 in one-time grants of up to ten thousand dollars to food entrepreneurs and farmers market operators serving communities with inequitable access to fresh food. Allies for Community Business manages the program, which targets small retail food businesses operating a physical storefront in priority geographies historically affected by disinvestment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Food entrepreneurs and farmers market operators
- Small retail food businesses operating a PHYSICAL STOREFRONT in priority Chicago geographies
- Focus on businesses that are both economic anchors and food access points in neighborhoods historically impacted by disinvestment
- Serving communities with inequitable access to fresh, healthy and affordable food

$450,000 total; one-time awards up to $10,000 each. Applications close September 25, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. CST. The Spanish-language application becomes available September 2, 2026.

Information session: Tuesday September 8, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., presented by Allies for Community Business (A4CB), covering eligibility criteria and application prep.

Administered by A4CB on behalf of BACP. Funded by the Road to Recovery Plan using American Rescue Plan Act Local Recovery Funds (ALN 21.027).

Name: Wisconsin Fast Forward Worker Training Grant
Description: Wisconsin's Department of Workforce Development reimburses employers for customized, business-driven occupational training that helps unemployed, underemployed and incumbent workers qualify for full-time employment, higher-level positions or increased wages. The program is open to companies of any size across all industry sectors. Awards range from five thousand to four hundred thousand dollars, with larger amounts available to consortiums acting as lead applicants.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Open to ALL INDUSTRY SECTORS and COMPANIES OF ANY SIZE
- Wisconsin employers reimbursed for customized, business-driven occupational training
- Training must qualify workers for full-time employment, higher-level positions, or increased wages
- Covers unemployed, underemployed and incumbent (existing) workers
- Consortiums serving as applicant lead organisations may receive awards above $400,000

50% MATCH REQUIRED - cash or in-kind, equal to half the grant award. This is a significant commitment and is not mentioned in most summaries of the program.

REIMBURSEMENT MODEL: costs are repaid after approved training is delivered, so the employer must be able to fund the training first.

Current round deadline: 3:00 p.m. Central Time, Monday October 5, 2026. DWD publishes a Grant Program Announcement, scoring rubric, application instructions, FAQs and a webinar for applicants.

Name: Third Wave Fund - Mobilize Power Fund
Description: The Mobilize Power Fund is a rapid-response grant supporting gender-justice organizations responding to unexpected, time-sensitive opportunities or threats. It can fund organizing, healing justice, conflict resolution, mutual aid, direct action, emergency safety/security, and similar movement-building responses.
Amount: Up to $10,000; coalitions of 2+ groups can request up to $20,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organizations/groups rooted in and accountable to communities impacted by gender oppression; budget under $500,000; response must address an unexpected change/incident within the previous 6 months.
Not prioritized: Individuals, planned events, ongoing programming, budget shortfalls, fundraising, startup costs, or long-term campaigns.
Additional info: Applications accepted as written proposal, video, or phone interview. Applicants generally hear back 4–6 weeks after the deadline

Name: Healthworx Accelerator
Description: Two-stage accelerator for early-stage, for-profit healthcare companies with a market-ready product. Stage 1 is a 12-week curriculum, virtual plus in-person, on navigating the health insurance landscape, venture funding, and industry pain points, paired with a $25,000 investment and support for future fundraising. Stage 2 is an optional nine-month mentorship with industry partners pursuing commercial pilots, offered based on alignment and not guaranteed to all participants. Participants also get mentorship, access to industry stakeholders and VCs, and a peer community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a for-profit incorporated healthcare company offering healthcare technologies or services, with a clear scalable product or model currently in market or ready to launch, and a full-time team. No geographic restriction and no revenue limit stated. Applications for the 2026 cohort are open as of September 2026. No application or program fee stated.

Name: Citi Foundation Global Innovation Challenge: Preparing Youth for AI
Description: The Citi Foundation is committing $25 million across up to 50 nonprofit community organizations, each receiving $500,000 over 24 months, to help low-income youth aged 15-24 prepare for an AI-driven labor market. Three funding areas: cultivating AI and human-centric skills (AI fundamentals, ethics, prompt engineering, paired with problem-solving and critical thinking); expanding digital access (community hubs with shared devices, open-source AI, low-connectivity tools); and building NGO capacity to integrate AI into existing youth employability programs. Fourth edition of the Challenge.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY — the Citi Foundation Funding Approach states plainly that for-profits are not eligible, and also excludes private foundations, individuals, and sole proprietorships. Applicants must be registered nonprofits under local law; U.S. applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities. FISCAL SPONSORS ARE NOT PERMITTED. Organizations advancing to Round 2 must supply externally audited financials covering some part of calendar year 2024 or later. Mission or strategic priorities must focus on serving low-income individuals. Registered schools, universities, and government entities are eligible. No minimum or maximum organizational budget. GEOGRAPHY IS RESTRICTED: the project must serve one or more listed target geographies, and U.S. eligibility is COUNTY-LEVEL, not nationwide — named counties in CA, CT, FL, IL, MD, NJ, NY, NV (Clark), SD (statewide), VA, plus Washington D.C. Check the Summary & FAQ PDF before investing time. Two rounds: Letter of Inquiry due October 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET; LOI decisions end of November 2026; invited full applications early December 2026; final decisions by end of May 2027; grants start on or after June 1, 2027, paid $250,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. One LOI per organization; multi-partner proposals need a single lead. English only. No application fee. Apply via citi.fluxx.io/apply/Challenge.

Name: Toast Changemakers Program
Description: Toast awards fifteen $10,000 cash grants ($150,000 total) to independent U.S. restaurants, cafes, food trucks, and bars that are already fighting hunger in their communities. Applicants are judged on demonstrated impact, feasibility of their plan for the funds, and innovation. Administered in partnership with Hello Alice and the Global Entrepreneurship Network, under a $5 million, five-year Toast commitment to fighting food insecurity.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to U.S. restaurants, cafes, food trucks, and bars/lounges — Toast POS customers are NOT required. Applicants must show an existing track record of addressing local food insecurity (community meals, food donations, or food bank/nonprofit partnerships) plus a concrete plan to expand that work with the funds. Selection runs through two review rounds judged by Toast, GEN, and Hello Alice. 2026 cycle: applications opened September 10, 2026, close October 1, 2026, winners announced November 10, 2026. Prior-cycle detailed thresholds (likely but unconfirmed for 2026): applicant is the leading executive, 18+ (19 in AL/NE), legal resident of the 50 states, DC, or Puerto Rico; independently owned for-profit food service; max 15 locations; fewer than 50 employees per location; operating at least 6 months; $3M or less revenue per location. No application fee. Apply via Hello Alice at helloalice.com/opportunities/grants/toast.

Name: Milwaukee Commercial Revitalization Grants
Description: The Commercial Revitalization Fund, run by Milwaukee’s Department of City Development, provides grants to businesses and property owners to renovate storefronts, improve building facades, and activate vacant commercial spaces to strengthen neighborhood business corridors. It includes multiple programs with varying funding caps (generally covering up to 50% of project costs), such as signage, façade improvements, storefront activation, and retail investment tied to job creation. Overall, the fund aims to enhance the physical appearance, economic activity, and vitality of commercial areas in the city.

Name: Makers Mindset x The Equity Studio Grant
Description: Five women-owned U.S. consumer packaged goods businesses in beauty or wellness each receive $10,000 in equity-free funding, plus group mentorship with Nancy Twine (Makers Mindset) and Anna Sweeting (The Equity Studio), community access, and exposure across both platforms. Businesses must sell CPG products in beauty or wellness, have annual revenue between $50,000 and $2M, less than 10 employees, and be revenue-generating for at least one full year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must be legally registered in the United States and sell CPG products in Beauty (skincare, color cosmetics, haircare, scalpcare, bodycare, oralcare, fragrance, hygiene, family & baby) or Wellness (supplements, ingestibles, nutritional powders, functional foods and beverages, better-for-you food, longevity and performance, hormone care). No more than 10 employees. At least 51% women ownership. Annual revenue between $50,000 and $2 million. Revenue-generating for at least one full year. Prior-cycle finalists were required to attend a 'Pitch the Panel' session; expect the same. Applications opened September 9, 2026 and close October 9, 2026; winners announced November 2026. Apply at makersmindset.com/mm-eqs-2026-grant-application/.
Industry: Beauty & Personal Care,Health / Wellness,Consumer Packaged Goods,Food & Beverage

Name: Moving Mountains Grant (Leon H. Sullivan Charitable Trust)
Description: A $10,000 cash award from the Leon H. Sullivan Charitable Trust for Philadelphia businesses. Designed to stabilize and strengthen day-to-day operations, this grant prioritizes core operating needs that unlock capacity, reduce risk, and sustain or grow revenue. Applicants need three years of operating history and under $250,000 in revenue. North Philadelphia businesses receive priority.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit small businesses only — nonprofits are not eligible. Must be owned and operated in Philadelphia, with priority given to North Philadelphia zip codes 19121, 19122, 19123, 19125, 19130, 19132, 19133, and 19140. Annual revenue must be less than $250,000. Minimum three years of continuous operation. Must demonstrate business stability and growth potential. The application collects demographic information, but the page states this is for research purposes only and is not used to determine eligibility. Applications opened September 7, 2026 and close Friday, October 9, 2026. No application fee.

Name: Business Food Waste Mitigation Grant Program (Empire State Development)
Description: Empire State Development's Business Food Waste Mitigation Grant Program awards $50,000 to $750,000 competitively for machinery and equipment that collects, processes and recycles food waste – such as compactors, dehydrators, depackagers, windrow turners, grinders, forklifts and trucks – plus infrastructure to distribute byproducts like compost. New York State municipalities and nonprofits undertaking food waste mitigation projects apply, and may apply on behalf of New York-based businesses, which join as co-implementors. Apply through the Consolidated Funding Application (apps.cio.ny.gov/apps/cfa/) by October 9, 2026 at 4:00 PM.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Lead applicant must be a New York State municipality or a nonprofit undertaking a food waste mitigation project; NY-based businesses can participate as co-implementors on an eligible applicant's project. Eligible costs are food waste collection/processing/recycling machinery and equipment and byproduct distribution infrastructure.

Name: LA County East LA Small Business Recovery Grant
Description: LA County's Department of Economic Opportunity is offering one-time recovery grants to small businesses physically located in County-designated impact areas for the June 17, 2026 Lineage Fire or the May 22, 2026 East Los Angeles oil spill. Commercial brick-and-mortar businesses receive $3,000; home-based businesses with customer presence, sidewalk vendors and mobile businesses receive $1,000. Applicants must demonstrate a qualifying disruption. If demand exceeds funding, a weighted lottery and waitlist apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Direct application: https://recoverygrant.aidkit.org/apply (AidKit). Operating at the eligible location at least 30 days before the incident date; 100 or fewer employees including affiliates; $6M or less average annual gross receipts; applicant is majority owner; eligible business type; documentation required. Applications opened September 17, 2026; deadline extended from Oct 1 to Oct 9. For-profit small businesses; nonprofits not named as eligible. $3,000 commercial brick-and-mortar; $1,000 home-based with customer presence / sidewalk vendor / mobile.

Name: First Peoples Fund Yéego Action Grants
Description: First Peoples Fund's Yéego Action Grant provides fast, small awards to Native artists for a specific professional opportunity or for a hardship hindering their creative practice. Requests range from one hundred to twenty-five hundred dollars, and partial funding may be awarded. Applications close at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time on the tenth of each month, and applicants are notified of decisions by the end of that month.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Enrolled member of, or proof of lineal descent from, a U.S. federally or state-recognized tribe; or proof of Alaska Native or Native Hawaiian ancestry
- At least 18 years old
- U.S.-based resident
- Practicing artist
- Not enrolled in a degree-seeking academic program
- Not a current First Peoples Fund grantee or fellow
- Has never previously received a Yéego Action Grant
- Individual applications only; no group submissions

Applications close 3:00 p.m. MT on the 10th of each month. Next round closes 9/10/2026.

Apply via the Submittable portal: https://firstpeoplesfund.submittable.com/submit/ba051627-6ff7-44fc-8aa6-bd0f9911ee98/yeego-action-grants

Name: Markets for Makers Vendor Applications
Description: Markets for Makers is a curated, juried pop-up market series connecting independent makers, artisans, and small businesses with thousands of in-person shoppers across the U.S. Vendors are selected based on product quality and originality, branding/presentation, online presence, and the overall balance of categories at each market.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to independent makers, artisans, and small businesses selling handmade or original products. Categories include jewelry, fashion, home goods, art, beauty products, specialty foods, and more; Markets for Makers uses a juried selection process and limits the number of vendors in each category.

Name: City of Raleigh Facade Rehabilitation Grant
Description: This program offers matching reimbursement grants of up to $10,000 to help small business owners and property owners refurbish the exterior of their commercial buildings. Designed to revitalize Downtown and older commercial districts, the grant enhances curb appeal, stimulates local economic activity, and supports long-term growth.

Name: Whole Foods Market Store Giving
Description: Whole Foods Market's store-level giving program, which funds nonprofits working on food access, environmental stewardship, and other community needs in the areas surrounding its stores. Decisions are made by a network of Whole Foods team members who vote on submitted requests to address needs within their local communities. Cash support only – the program does not provide gift cards or in-kind donations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY. Eligible: registered US 501(c)(3) nonprofits, Canadian charitable organizations, and UK charitable incorporated organizations, all of which must demonstrate verified nonprofit status. INELIGIBLE: individuals, for-profit businesses, political entities, and organizations that discriminate based on race, ethnicity, or culture. Support goes to communities surrounding Whole Foods Market stores, so proximity to a store is effectively required. Focus areas are food access, environmental stewardship, and community needs. Cash only — no gift cards or in-kind donations. Requests are submitted through the Whole Foods Community Engagement Portal. Q4 2026 cycle: applications due October 11, 2026; team member voting October 27 - November 8, 2026. No application fee.

Name: For Farmers Grant
Description: The For Farmers Movement provides grants to small and mid-sized U.S. farms that produce food or farm products for sale in their communities. Basic grants range from $500–$1,000, collaborative grants can reach $3,000, and invitation-only transformational grants range from $5,000–$10,000 for projects such as equipment, infrastructure, irrigation, cold storage, soil improvements, repairs, innovation, and loss recovery. Farmers can be nominated by community members or nominate themselves, but homesteaders and animal sanctuaries are not eligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Nominate a Farmer!
When you nominate a farmer, amazing things happen. First, they find out they were nominated and that's powerful. BUT your nomination unlocks a bunch of opportunities for grants, workshops, support, gratitude, connection with eaters, new supporters, and other farmers. For starters, nominated farmers will be invited to apply for a high-impact grant through the For Farmers Movement and the possibility of being invited to apply for a second, much bigger transformational grant. SO, good on you!

Name: AgeTech After Dark @ CES 2027
Description: Pitch competition from AARP's AgeTech Collaborative seeking market-ready products and services that make aging easier, including accessibility, caregiving, and longevity solutions. Selected finalists pitch in Las Vegas on January 7, 2027 and receive a complimentary CES 2027 ticket; the winner takes a $10,000 grand prize and finalists may be invited into AARP's AgeTech accelerator.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Solutions must be ready for market, though prototypes are accepted. Focus areas include accessibility, caregiving, and longevity. Applications close October 12, 2026 at 11:59 pm. The pitch event runs January 7, 2027, 7:00-9:00 pm in Las Vegas, NV alongside CES. Finalists receive one complimentary CES 2027 ticket and may be invited to join the AgeTech Collaborative accelerator; the pitch winner receives $10,000. No application fee listed.

Name: Lowell (NC) Facade Grant
Description: The City of Lowell, North Carolina offers matching reimbursement grants to businesses and commercial property owners improving building exteriors in line with the city's Facade Improvement Standards. Awards run from $500 to $2,500 per facade on a 50/50 matching basis, with final amounts set at city council discretion. The second 2026 grant cycle is open and closes in October.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Commercial property owners and businesses in Lowell, NC. Projects must comply with the city's Facade Improvement Standards. 50/50 matching reimbursement, $500 minimum to $2,500 maximum per facade; council determines final award amounts. Ineligible: improvements begun before approval, interior work, false fronts, window and door replacement, demolition of historic features, roof repairs, and materials that do not match the original or neighbouring structures. Cycle announcement: https://lowellnc.gov/2026-facade-grant-applications-now-open-for-second-grant-cycle/

Name: Philadelphia Park to Broad Fall Small Business Fund
Description: The Park to Broad Small Business Fund offers $500–$2,000 one-time grants to storefront businesses in Brewerytown, Fairmount, Francisville, and Spring Garden for specific projects that support business growth, such as community events, equipment purchases/repairs, or marketing campaigns.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS
- Storefront business in Fairmount, Brewerytown, Francisville, or Spring Garden. See exact boundaries at this link. Home-based businesses are not eligible at this time. https://drive.google.com/file/d/15B865wC8C7QCixf93b0eiiJOcC48wJaq/view
- Applicants must be a Park to Broad Business Network member. Join at any level (lowest is free) at this link. https://www.parktobroad.org/network
- Proposed project/improvement must be completed within six months.
- Payroll, rent, inventory, and construction costs are ineligible grant requests
- Applicants did not receive a Small Business Fund grant in spring 2026

Application link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfzYQOtVaBBFjf9dSQmEHdV7AwxMLv1IA15pq1RtYPac5VaZg/viewform

Name: 2027 Tools Competition
Description: The Learning Engineering Tools Competition is a global funding competition for education technology that uses digital tools, data and learning science to improve learning outcomes. Prize levels include $50,000 Catalyst awards for early-stage tools, $150,000 Growth awards for products with users and traction, and $300,000 Transform awards for established platforms with 10,000 or more users. The competition supports innovation across K–12, postsecondary education and workforce development.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to individuals and teams at all phases of development — from early ideas to established platforms — including edtech innovators, researchers, students, and educators. The 2027 timeline is expected to be announced in September 2026; sign up for updates on the site. The 2026 cycle closed January 21, 2026. No application fee listed.

Name: Marshalls Good Stuff Accelerator Program (mPowered by Marshalls)
Description: The Marshalls Good Stuff Accelerator Program, developed with Luminary, is a 12-month virtual program for 40 participants that includes a $5,000 grant, expert-led learning, and peer connections to support personal and professional goals. Applicants of all backgrounds are welcome, including students, stay-at-home parents, professionals, and business owners, with the broader goal of expanding opportunities for women in their lives, workplaces, and communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to legal residents of all 50 US states, DC, or Puerto Rico who are 18 or older. NO BUSINESS OWNERSHIP REQUIRED — applicants at any career stage are welcome, and the program is open to all backgrounds and demographics. No purchase necessary and no application fee. 40 participants are selected. Applications opened September 9, 2026 and close October 13, 2026; notifications go out November 18 - December 10, 2026; the program runs January through December 2027. The $5,000 grant is issued as a 1099-MISC and recipients are responsible for the taxes. Apply at marshallsgoodstuff2026.dja.com.

Name: New England Public Art Learning Fund
Description: The Public Art Learning Fund provides professional development support directly to artists working in public art across New England. Grants of $500 to $3,000 fund opportunities such as conferences, workshops, trainings, and discussions, including travel beyond a commutable distance from the artist's home. Applicants must reside full-time in one of the six New England states and maintain an active Creative Ground profile.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Artist who resides full-time and makes work in one of the six New England states
- Artistic practice must engage the public realm, or the artist must demonstrate they are expanding their practice toward public artmaking
- Must have an active Creative Ground profile
- Professional development must specifically relate to strengthening the applicant's own public art practice
- The opportunity must occur during the grant period
- Travel expenses eligible only beyond a commutable distance from the artist's home

Deadline Tuesday, October 13, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET, for opportunities taking place January 1 - December 31, 2027. Administered by the New England Foundation for the Arts.
Industry: Visual & Fine Arts,Arts & Crafts,Creative Economy,Career Development

Name: Arts & Business Council of Greater Boston Creative Entrepreneur Fellowship (CEF)
Description: Seven-month professional development cohort from the Arts & Business Council of Greater Boston for 8-10 individual artists and creative solopreneurs building a sustainable professional practice. Fellows receive personalized goal setting, one-on-one technical assistance and coaching, skills-training seminars, resources in English and Spanish, and a stipend for business-related purchases. Now in its 14th program year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For individual creative practitioners — solopreneurs, entrepreneurs, and artists working to build a professional practice. Disciplines include visual artists (public artists, photographers, painters), craft artists and artisans, performing artists, writers, and more. 8-10 individuals selected competitively; semi-finalists are interviewed. Applications ran September 7 - October 13, 2026; the cohort runs December 2026 through June 2027. No revenue limit, business-stage minimum, or industry requirement stated. Free to participate. The program includes a stipend for business-related purchases, but the dollar amount is not published.

Name: Illinois Creative Accelerator Fund
Description: The Illinois Arts Council awards $10,000 taxable grants to individual Illinois artists through a randomized selection run with the Illinois State Lottery, with each IAC region receiving its own allocation. Applicants must be 21 or older, Illinois residents established before October 14, 2025, with an active practice since at least 2023, and not enrolled in a degree program. FY27 applications opened September 2 and close October 14.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists 21+, Illinois residency established before 2025-10-14, active practice since at least 2023. Degree-program students ineligible except PhD candidates past coursework. Prior FY25/FY26 CAF recipients ineligible. Selection is randomized, not merit-scored; each IAC region receives its own allocation. Grants are taxable. FY27 applications opened 2026-09-02.

Name: Intuit IDEAS Program
Description: Intuit IDEAS is a 12-month accelerator giving small businesses free QuickBooks, Mailchimp, and TurboTax software, Credit Karma access, and monthly coaching from Intuit tax and bookkeeping experts. Participants also receive a technology grant for hardware and a cash grant on completing the program. Cohorts run in selected U.S. metros, plus a nationwide cohort for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Registered small business with an active customer base and a desire to grow
- Ideally at least one year in operation
- Teams of 1-9 employees perform best, though larger companies are considered
- Must operate in an eligible U.S. program market, OR be a military veteran or military spouse entrepreneur (nationwide cohort)
- Should live within approximately 40 miles of the selected metro for in-person events
- S Corporations, Partnerships, and other entities eligible; C Corporations are NOT eligible
- Nonprofits cannot apply
- Current Intuit employees, contractors, and experts are ineligible
- Ineligible activities: federally illegal activities, real estate with more than 3 properties, cryptocurrency

2026 markets: Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, and West Virginia. Los Angeles has a separate dedicated cohort application.

2026 cycle: deadline September 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PT. Tentative acceptance notifications early September 2026; final acceptance November 2026. 12-month program requiring 3-5 hours monthly. $5,000 grant awarded on successful completion.

Name: Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition Grants for Artists
Description: The Oklahoma Visual Arts Coalition (OVAC) offers Grants for Artists to support Oklahoma-based artists in creating visual art for public presentation, advancing professional development, or leading community projects. Grants are available for artists working in visual media, curation, and art writing, with awards based on artistic merit and grant-specific criteria.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- You must be 21 or older to apply for a grant.
- Grant recipients must have held at least 12 months of residency in Oklahoma prior to the submission deadline.
- If you are awarded a grant you must wait one year before reapplying.
Individuals can only only submit one application per cycle.​
- You may not request a grant to reimburse spent funds.
- Artists currently enrolled in BFA or MFA programs are not eligible to apply.
- Recipients of MOMENTUM Spotlight and THRIVE are not eligible to apply within one year of their reward disbursement of the stated programs. If you are awarded a THRIVE Grant, you are eligible to apply, but your proposed project may not be the same as your Thrive proposal or a new iteration of said project.

Name: New York Health Foundation Special Projects Fund
Description: The NYHealth 2026 Special Projects Fund offers one-time, nonrenewable grants for innovative projects that improve the health of New Yorkers – especially marginalized communities. The fund prioritizes projects with potential for scaling, replication, or statewide systems impact.

Name: New Orleans Activate Downtown Grant
Description: The Downtown Development District of New Orleans offers matching grants to convert long-vacant ground-floor commercial spaces into occupied, public-facing businesses. Awards cover up to fifty percent of eligible tenant build-out costs, including interior build-outs, accessibility improvements, storefront renovations, lighting, signage, security enhancements and building system upgrades. Both property owners and business tenants may apply, and the district prioritizes locally owned independent businesses filling visible storefronts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Ground-floor commercial space within Downtown Development District boundaries
- Space must have been vacant for at least one year
- Property owners and business tenants both eligible
- Project must result in new public-facing business occupancy
- 50% match required; award capped at $20,000
- Eligible costs: interior build-out, accessibility, storefront renovation, lighting, signage, security, essential building systems
- Priority: activating long-vacant storefronts, new retail activity, locally owned independent businesses, financing-gap projects

Applications opened 7/13/2026, close 10/15/2026, winners announced 11/2/2026. Applicants encouraged to meet with DDD staff first; submit to stronger@downtownnola.com.

Name: Stephen L. Tadlock Veteran Business Grant (Founders First CDC)
Description: Founders First CDC awards this grant in memory of U.S. Navy veteran Stephen L. Tadlock. Twenty finalists share a $20,000 fund, each receiving a $1,000+ micro-grant plus free enrollment in Founders First's Passport Community ($1,499 value) or Zebra Leadership ($1,699 value).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: U.S. military veteran serving as CEO, President or Business Owner; active U.S.-based business; annual revenue no more than $5 million; 2-100 employees; at least 1 year in business.

Name: Imminent Research Grants (Translated)
Description: Imminent, the research center of the translation company Translated, funds five projects a year at $20,000 each in the field of language services and language technology. The call is open to startuppers, researchers, innovators, authors, university labs, organizations and companies, anywhere in the world. Priority research areas are language economics, language data, machine learning algorithms for translation, human-computer interaction and the neuroscience of language, though applications can be made in any field of research. The first-round submission is a 250-word project pitch, the team's qualifications and the concrete deliverables; 20 finalists are then asked for a detailed project description and a two-minute video, and some are interviewed. Half the funding is paid on signing the agreement and half on the final report, with two milestone meetings during the project year, and recipients publish an article about the project on Imminent's website within one year. Questions go to imminent@translated.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to startuppers, researchers, innovators, authors, university labs, organizations and companies, located anywhere in the world. Five grants of $20,000 each are awarded annually. Submission deadline October 1, 2026. Application is a 250-word project pitch, team qualifications and concrete deliverables; 20 finalists submit a detailed project description and a 2-minute video. No application fee. Contact imminent@translated.com.

Name: CFDA x Frazier Family Foundation Empowered Vision Award
Description: The Council of Fashion Designers of America and the Andrea W. and Kenneth C. Frazier Family Foundation identify a designer showing exceptional creativity, business acumen and potential for long-term success. The recipient receives a one hundred thousand dollar grant, tailored mentorship across core business areas, a full year of paid consultant support, and national visibility. Two additional finalists also receive cash prizes.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Emerging Black designer / Black-owned fashion business
- Judged on exceptional creativity, business acumen, and potential for long-term success

RECIPIENT RECEIVES: $100,000 grant, tailored mentorship in core business areas, ONE YEAR OF PAID CONSULTANT SUPPORT, and national visibility. Two additional finalists receive cash prizes (amounts not published).

Now in its second year. The 2025-2026 recipient was Daveed Baptiste.

Name: Science Discovery on Main Street
Description: A Main Street America program funded by the Simons Foundation helping rural Main Street communities identify local science assets and build science-related programming that draws visitors and grows local pride. Discovery Grants of $10,000 support mapping science resources and developing programming ideas; a select number of grantees then receive additional Implementation Grants to carry out the activities they proposed.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT open to for-profit businesses - Main Street America designated community organizations (accredited or affiliate) in good standing only. Must be in a rural area with a population of 50,000 or less, demonstrate commitment to science programming through partnerships, and have an annual operating budget under $1 million. Direct application: https://nationalmainstreetcenter.submittable.com/submit . 2026 cycle opened September 1 and closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Questions to sciencediscovery@mainstreet.org.

Name: NY NOW HANDMADE (Designer-Maker & Global Design)
Description: Juried exhibition section within the NY NOW wholesale trade market at the Javits Center, connecting artisan makers and designer-craftspeople with retail buyers. Two curated tracks: Designer-Maker, for independent designers and craftspeople producing small-batch hand-made work, and Global Design, for makers rooted in distinct cultural or regional design traditions. Selection is by an independent committee of designers, retailers, and industry tastemakers, and accepted makers gain access to agency partner networks including Ivystone, Simblist, and Harper Group.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT FUNDING — this is a juried application for paid exhibitor booth space, not a grant. Acceptance is a curatorial decision; the accepted maker then pays for the booth. Open globally, no revenue limit or business-stage requirement stated. Product categories: Gift, Fashion Accessories, Tabletop, Textiles, Jewelry, Decorative Accessories, or Other. Wholesale experience is preferred — the application asks for prior orders and active wholesale accounts. An optional 'Handmade in America' designation requires products made entirely by hand in the U.S. from raw material to finished piece, with no outsourced or machine manufacturing. Applications for the Winter 2027 Market (January 31 - February 2, 2027) close October 15, 2026. Booth pricing is not published — contact sales@nynow.com.

Name: Houston Land Bank Third Ward Early Capacity Building Grant Fund
Description: Houston Land Bank, with Rice Management Company, is deploying $1 million in capacity-building grants to organizations and businesses serving Houston's Historic Third Ward. Two tiers scale with organizational maturity: up to $15,000 (Tier 1) and up to $75,000 (Tier 2). Funds strengthen internal operations rather than finance a specific project, and recipients also get information sessions and technical assistance on budgeting, reporting, and outcome documentation. Focus areas include economic development, food access, community health, workforce growth, civic engagement, and cultural preservation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to BOTH for-profit and nonprofit applicants — the fund names nonprofits, grassroots organizations, small businesses, entrepreneurs, and faith-based organizations. Applicant must provide direct service or impact within Houston's Historic Third Ward (Harris County, TX). Tier 1 requires a minimum of 2 years of operations; Tier 2 requires a minimum of 5 years plus a strong track record of community impact in Third Ward, ability to manage larger-scale funding and reporting, and an established organizational structure. No revenue cap and no developer or contractor requirement — despite the land-bank sponsor, this is not restricted to housing developers. Applications open September 15, 2026 and close October 15, 2026; awards announced December 2026. Two information sessions already passed (in-person July 16, virtual August 3, 2026). No application fee stated.

Name: Intuit IDEAS Program - LA28 Cohort (Los Angeles)
Description: A dedicated Los Angeles cohort of Intuit's IDEAS program, tied to LA28 and targeting LA-area businesses in construction, sports and entertainment event services, and creative, marketing and media services. The 12-month program provides free access to QuickBooks, Mailchimp and TurboTax, monthly business coaching plus executive coaching, access to Intuit tax and bookkeeping experts, and Credit Karma access. Participants receive a $5,000 grant upon successful completion of the program, plus an optional $1,000 technology grant for eligible business technology needs.
Amount: $5,000 on program completion (plus optional $1,000 technology grant)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a Los Angeles-area registered small business working in construction, sports and entertainment event services, or creative, marketing and media services. C CORPORATIONS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE, and current Intuit employees are excluded. Ideal applicants have been operating at least one year; Intuit notes smaller teams of 1-9 employees have performed best, though businesses of various sizes are encouraged to apply. No minimum or maximum revenue requirement is specified. The LA cohort has its own application, which opened by the end of August 2026, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no published close date. The program runs 12 months, and the $5,000 grant is paid on successful completion rather than up front. Apply at values-partnerships.wizehive.app/program/ideas/applicant/application/info. Questions: intuit-IDEAS@intuit.com.

Name: Boston Public Market 2026-27 Entrepreneurship Forum
Description: The 2026–2027 Boston Public Market Entrepreneurship Forum, powered by Citizens Bank, is open to New England small businesses that can provide goods or services to the Boston area and have no more than one retail location as of June 2026. The program includes six monthly seminars on business planning, branding, marketing, finance, and related topics, with eligible participants able to compete on Pitch Day for grant stipends and up to one year of free rent space in Boston Public Market.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Based in New England and able to provide goods/services to the Boston area
- No more than one retail location as of June 2026
- In order to compete in the Pitch Day, a business owner or representative must attend all Forum sessions

Name: Pave HER Way Grant Program
Description: Pave HER Way is a national nonprofit funding individual women whose work changes conditions for other women. Three tracks are offered: the Change Agent Prize for established leaders, awarded by nomination only; the Disruptor Award, which sponsors a project or idea with public benefit for women and girls; and need-based Financial Aid for education costs or personal hardship. Recipients also receive mentorship and cohort access.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Identify as a woman, age 18 or older
- U.S. resident or citizen
- Not an employee, relative of an employee, or board member of Pave HER Way
- Change Agent Prize: demonstrated record of work helping other women; BY NOMINATION ONLY, no direct applications
- Disruptor Award: a project or idea with clear public benefit for women and girls; mentorship and cohort participation required
- Financial Aid: need-based, up to $30,000, for education costs or personal hardship

Applications open August 31, 2026. No closing deadline has been published.

Name: Nosh Live Pitch Slam
Description: Nosh Live (BevNET/Nosh) hosts a Pitch Slam for emerging packaged food brands at its Nosh Live conference (December 3–4, 2026, Marina del Rey, CA). Six finalists pitch for five minutes in front of retail buyers and investors; the grand prize is a $10,000 BevNET advertising package plus a strategy session and live interview, and all finalists receive free conference tickets. Applying is free.
Amount: $10,000 advertising package plus strategy session (no cash)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Emerging packaged food brands (pre-launch allowed) with finished packaging and product available to sample; company in good legal and financial standing; the U.S. must be the primary target market. At least one founder must present in person at Nosh Live in Marina del Rey, CA on December 3–4, 2026 (free admission for up to two founders; travel and lodging at the brand's expense); finalists attend a 30-minute webinar in early November. Six finalists, four-minute pitches plus Q&A. Free to apply. Application form: https://form.jotform.com/bevnetcom/NL-PitchSlam-2026. Questions: Carolyn Craven, ccraven@bevnet.com. Coffee brands should confirm eligibility for the food (vs. beverage) competition.

Name: Michigan Black Business Alliance Biz Wiz Grant
Description: Michigan Black Business Alliance is oepning up BizWiz Grant applications to entrepreneurs in Flint, Kalamazoo, and Grand Rapids. BizWiz provides grant funding for services that help entrepreneurs grow and sustain their businesses, including business operations & strategy, legal services, marketing, and accounting.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Details from MBBA here: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dc_Rq5QIFod/

Name: Cuyahoga County Business Boost Initiative
Description: Cuyahoga County’s new Business Boost Initiative will provide $250,000 in total grant funding, with individual awards ranging from $1,000 to $10,000, to help small businesses stabilize, modernize, and grow. In addition to funding, selected businesses will receive support through the County’s Office of Small Business, including resource navigation and technical assistance. Applications open September 16, 2026 and are due October 16, 2026.

Name: Vimeo Short Film Grant
Description: Second annual grant program from Vimeo awarding five emerging filmmakers $60,000 each to produce an original short film. Beyond the cash, recipients receive access to Panavision camera packages, OWC storage, ShotDeck's image library, a Vimeo Advanced subscription, distribution on Vimeo.com plus in-person screening opportunities, and one-on-one mentorship from the jury of acclaimed filmmakers (the 2026 jury includes director Kogonada and cinematographer Jomo Fray).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Aimed at emerging filmmakers developing original short films. Five recipients selected by a jury of acclaimed filmmakers, who also provide one-on-one mentorship. Vimeo's page references directing teams and collaborations as well as international production options, so both appear to be accommodated — but the detailed eligibility criteria sit behind unexpanded FAQ sections and could not be read. Submissions opened September 21, 2026; the closing date is not published (see Review Notes). Applications go through vimeo.slideroom.com. No submission fee is stated, though the page does not affirmatively say it is free. Vimeo advises checking the updated official rules for this round rather than relying on the 2025 criteria.

Name: LaunchLNK Grant Program (Lincoln, NE)
Description: Grant program administered by the Lincoln Partnership for Economic Development through its StartupLNK platform, running since 2018. Six early-stage scalable startups each receive a $20,000 non-dilutive cash grant plus more than $23,000 in in-kind services from a Dedicated Partner Network — product strategy consultation, legal services for formation and fundraising, IP law credits, office planning, coworking membership, prototype development credits, branding and messaging strategy, and chamber of commerce membership with promotional opportunities. The program's 36 graduates have collectively raised more than $100 million in follow-on funding.
Amount: $20,000 cash plus $23,000+ in in-kind services (6 recipients)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage scalable startups based in Lincoln, Nebraska, OR able to have a presence in Lincoln during the year of grant participation. Must have a goal and vision for business growth and scalability, and be able to explain the problem the startup is solving, who experiences it, and how significant it is. Selection prioritizes companies where the grant could spur revenue and job creation and attract additional capital investment in Lincoln. All industries welcome — the recent cohort spans ag-tech, medical devices, food delivery, and software. Three rounds: Round 1 due October 16, 2026 at 11:59 CST (about 45 minutes; basic profile plus problem and customer questions), results by October 23; Round 2 due November 20, 2026 (2-3 hours; product, business model, competition, growth), results by early December; Round 3 in early December is a 30-minute virtual panel pitch and Q&A. Six recipients announced by year-end 2026 as the 2027 cohort. No application fee stated.

Name: Pipeline Angels Pitch Summit
Description: Pipeline Angels runs virtual Pitch Summits where founders present to cohorts of newly trained angel investors. Selected companies deliver a ten-minute pitch followed by ten minutes of Q&A, and each participating angel commits a minimum of $5,000, typically through a SAFE or convertible note. Companies may also present to the broader investor community for additional syndicate participation. Women and non-binary founders are strongly encouraged to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- For-profit legal structure (e.g. C-corp, LLC)
- Duly organized and validly existing as a company in a U.S. state
- Social and/or environmental mission strongly encouraged
- Women and non-binary founders strongly encouraged to apply
- Attendance at a Founder Information Session is MANDATORY before an application is considered
- Broad industry focus; no stated revenue or stage requirement

Each participating angel commits a minimum of $5,000; cohorts run 5-10 members. No application deadline is published. East class summit October 17, 2026; West class summit October 18, 2026; funding expected by late December 2026. Screening and investment decisions are made by the participating angels. Pipeline Angels is now a program of the Institute for Entrepreneurial Leadership (IFEL).

Name: One Mind Accelerator
Description: The 2027 One Mind Accelerator is a 10-week hybrid program for pre-seed, seed, and Series A startups developing mental health solutions, with priority areas including serious mental illness, youth and maternal mental health, and precision psychiatry. Selected companies receive mentorship, investor introductions, fundraising support, and business development opportunities, with in-person opening and closing weeks in Menlo Park, California. Backed by leading philanthropists and corporations, OMA aims to accelerate the creation of accessible, equitable, and personalized mental healthcare innovations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: We work with for-profit mental health companies ranging from pre-seed to Series A. We work with companies around the world, but our core strengths are helping companies address the US market. We have worked with several european-based companies to help expand their reach in the US. There are no cutoffs for revenue, although the majority of companies are post-revenue and have significant proof points for achieving product-market fit. We do not accept non-profit organizations at this time.

Name: BioLabs Rochester MN Golden Ticket 2026
Description: Annual competition from BioLabs Rochester awarding one life sciences startup a year of fully paid individual bench space and membership at its fully equipped laboratory in Rochester, Minnesota, plus office space. The winner also gets access to the BioLabs startup community and industry connections through its partner network. BioLabs states a no-strings-attached model — the company retains complete intellectual property ownership and no equity is taken.
Amount: one year of fully paid lab bench space, membership, and office space (in-kind)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to life sciences companies working in oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neuroscience, cell/gene/regenerative therapies, aging and longevity biology, translational medicine, or research tools such as lab automation. No geographic restriction, company stage requirement, or funding-raised limit is stated on the page. Selection timeline: applications due October 20, 2026; finalists identified by end of October; virtual presentations during the week of November 2; in-person award ceremony November 16, 2026 at BioLabs Rochester. One winner. No application fee stated. Questions: goldenticket@biolabs.io.

Name: Humanity AI Open Call for Grants
Description: A $10 million open call from Humanity AI, a coalition of ten philanthropies — Doris Duke Foundation, Ford Foundation, Lumina Foundation, Kapor Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Mozilla Foundation, Omidyar Network, David and Lucile Packard Foundation, and Siegel Family Endowment — running a $500 million five-year collaborative grantmaking effort. Grants of $75,000 to $1,000,000 over up to three years fund community-led AI work, meaning work where the affected communities define the goals and shape the approach. Three focus areas: education, labor and economy, and humanities/arts/culture. Three approaches funded: shaping AI governance and standards, building AI that reflects community values, and challenging misaligned AI deployments.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits only as lead applicant — must be a U.S.-based 501(c)(3). Individuals must apply through a fiscal sponsor or in collaboration with a 501(c)(3). FOR-PROFITS MAY PARTICIPATE IN COLLABORATIONS BUT CANNOT BE THE LEAD APPLICANT. Work must serve U.S.-based communities. 2026 Humanity AI grantees may apply only as collaboration partners, not as leads. Preference for work using open-weight or open-source AI models where applicable. Two-phase process: Phase 1 initial proposals due Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 4:59 p.m. PT / 7:59 p.m. ET; selected finalists then submit budgets and measurement plans in Phase 2, with some invited to interviews; awards announced early spring 2027. Grant terms run up to three years. No application fee.

Name: Pitch 26 (Venture 313 Detroit)
Description: Non-dilutive pitch competition from Venture 313, the Gilbert Family Foundation-backed Detroit startup capital coalition (TechTown Detroit for grants, Invest Detroit Ventures for equity, Detroit Development Fund for debt). Awards $100,000 in total cash prizes with 0% equity taken. Runs in three phases: an open Phase I application, an invite-only Phase II, and a live finals pitch at Detroit's Bonstelle Theatre on December 8. Target sectors are fintech, mobility and advanced manufacturing, healthcare innovation, green energy and sustainability, consumer and business software, agritech and food systems, and edtech.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Tech-enabled businesses OPERATING IN THE CITY OF DETROIT (city-level, not metro or county) and legally structured in the State of Michigan, with early traction and a pilot-ready product — not idea stage. A Michigan LARA entity ID number is required. Optional self-identification is offered for businesses at least 51% owned by women, people of color, veterans, or people with disabilities; this is self-ID only, not an eligibility requirement or set-aside. Timeline: Phase I applications close Wednesday, October 21 (open to all); Phase I selection October 22-30; Phase II applications November 2-10 (invite only); Phase II selection November 11-28; finalists announced November 30; finals event Tuesday, December 8 at the Bonstelle Theatre, Detroit. Applications are submitted via Airtable. Contact: info@venture313.com.

Name: Entreprenista 100 Awards
Description: Annual awards program from Entreprenista honoring 100 women founders across all stages, judged on business growth, impact, brand presence, and personal narrative. Recognition only — honorees receive the Entreprenista 100 designation, a company and founder profile on the Entreprenista 100 site, recognition across Entreprenista's digital and social platforms, a digital award badge for marketing use, an invitation to the awards celebration and Founders Weekend, winners-only networking events, and ongoing media visibility through the year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NO CASH PRIZE — recognition, PR, and network access only. Open to private for-profit or nonprofit business owners who are legal residents of the United States or Canada (excluding Quebec), age 18+. The business must have a woman founder or at least one active woman co-founder involved in operations. No minimum revenue, business age, or company size — pre-revenue businesses are explicitly welcome. One entry per company. 2026 cycle: early entry deadline Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (fee discount only, not the application deadline); final deadline Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET; winners announced March 2027. Entry fees, from the submission platform: Entreprenista League members $59 early / $89 standard; non-members $99 early / $149 standard. All fees non-refundable. Apply at entreprenista.secure-platform.com/site.
Application Fee: $59-$149 (see Review Notes — tiered by membership and early entry)

Name: National Fund for Women Microgrants
Description: The National Fund for Women (NFW) offers monthly microgrants ranging from $100 to $5,000 to women for a range of needs — from immediate financial relief to business growth capital — with new grants dropping on the first of each month and applications closing on the 22nd.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Am I eligible to apply?
The National Fund for Women provides microgrants to individuals experiencing financial need, with a focus on addressing systemic inequities that disproportionately impact women. While we prioritize funding for women, we do not discriminate on the basis of sex and consider all eligible applicants consistent with our mission.

Name: Forrest E. Mars, Jr. Chocolate History Grant
Description: The Forrest E. Mars, Jr. Chocolate History Grant supports projects that explore and share chocolate’s role in global history, culture, and innovation. With a minimum of $50,000 in total funding, the program funds immersive experiences, research, educational resources, and publications that bring chocolate’s cultural stories to life. Special emphasis is placed on educational impact, diversity, and audience reach. Winners will be announced at the Heritage Chocolate Society Annual Meeting on February 18–19, 2026, in Washington, D.C.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- You must be a not-for-profit organization or Non-profit 501(c)(3)/individual. researcher/an organization not operating primarily to make a profit. OR You must be a teacher/educator in a K-12 public school in the United States.
- You must be present at the meeting of the Heritage Chocolate Society (HCS) either in-person or digitally to receive your grant.
- Grants must be executed prior to the following HCS meeting.
- Grant winners are required to present their results, either in-person or digitally, at the following HCS meeting.
- All publications must be approved by Mars, Incorporated prior to being produced.

Name: CIC Massachusetts Social Impact Program
Description: CIC Massachusetts is launching a Social Impact Cohort to support BIPOC, women, and veteran-led small businesses from socially and economically disadvantaged groups across Massachusetts. This Growth Stage Cohort, beginning January 2026, will offer specialized programming to help historically underserved entrepreneurs scale and thrive. The initiative is funded by the Minority Business Development Agency’s Capital Readiness Program.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Our ideal candidates are small growth-stage businesses, companies, or organizations who may meet one or more of the following criteria:
- Are in approximately pre-seed – Series A
- Are actively fundraising or about to pursue funding opportunities 
- Are currently scaling their operations – including but not limited to expanding to new markets, preparing to hire, etc.
- Have a product in-market
- Candidates should have businesses based in Massachusetts. Founders should identify as one or more of the following: BIPOC (Black Indigenous, or Person of Color), female, or veteran entrepreneurs coming from socially or economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

Name: Missouri Neighborhood Assistance Program (NAP)
Description: Missouri Department of Economic Development program that helps approved community development projects attract private contributions by giving eligible donors state tax credits equal to 50% or 70% of their qualified donations. Eligible projects address education, job training, community services, crime prevention, or physical revitalization. This is not a direct grant — approved applicants must raise the project funding from eligible donors, who then claim the credits.
Amount: up to $250,000 in 50% tax credits; up to $350,000 in 70% tax credits
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: FY27 Round 2 opens September 14, 2026 and closes October 23, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Eligible applicants are Missouri not-for-profit corporations, 501(c)(3) organizations, educational institutions, and Missouri businesses that meet program requirements. Missouri businesses may apply only when the proposed project falls outside the company's normal scope of business, addresses an identified community need, and involves residents in project leadership. Eligible donors include businesses, sole proprietors, farmers, and shareholders, partners, or members in pass-through entities. Preference has gone to projects serving previously underserved areas of Missouri. Contact: community@ded.mo.gov or 573-522-9062.

Name: We Are Moving The Needle MicroGrant
Description: We Are Moving The Needle offers two MicroGrant funds for U.S.-based music producers, engineers, songwriters, and similar behind-the-board creators: an Early-Career MicroGrant of $500–$1,000 for those with 0–5 years of experience, and a Mid-Career MicroGrant of $2,500 for those with 5+ years of experience looking to take their career to the next level. Funds are intended for professional skill development and career-advancing needs such as equipment, courses, travel for internships, or breaking into new markets — not artist development. The current review cycle closes June 28, 2026 at 11:59pm, with applications reviewed three times per year on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility requirements:

Music producers, engineers, songwriters, or similar creators with a commitment to growing a career behind the board.

0-5 years of experience (including rising college seniors).

US Citizen or Permanent Resident.

Demonstrated interest in advancing your career, whether that's covering travel for an internship or assistantship, enrolling in an advanced audio course, or investing in new equipment.

MicroGrant funds are intended to support professional skill development and career-advancing needs, rather than artist development.

Name: Downtown Houston Facade Improvement Grant
Description: The Downtown Redevelopment Authority offers grants to revitalize building exteriors within the TIRZ 3 boundaries in downtown Houston. Both property owners and tenants may apply, with awards reaching two hundred fifty thousand dollars for qualifying facade work. Applicants complete a grant application and budget template available on the authority's grant programs page, and the 2026 cycle closes at 5pm on the stated deadline date.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Property owners and tenants of buildings within TIRZ 3 boundaries
- Project must revitalize the building facade or exterior
- Requires completed application form plus budget template

Deadline Friday 10/23/2026 at 5pm. Administered by the Downtown Redevelopment Authority. Contact: Marlon Connley, Manager of Small Business Support Programs.

Name: Northeast SARE Farming Community Grant
Description: Northeast SARE funds multistate and regional projects advancing regenerative and sustainable agriculture at the intersection of nutrition and health. Roughly $1.5 million is available this cycle, with typical awards between two hundred fifty thousand and five hundred thousand dollars. Supported work spans marketing and business strategies, crop production methods, livestock and aquaculture operations, economic and social sustainability, and ecological knowledge development.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Projects must be multistate or regional in scope and serve farmers and farming communities
- Northeast SARE region: CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT, WV and Washington DC
- Work must advance regenerative and sustainable agriculture at the intersection of nutrition and health

FUNDS: marketing and business strategies, crop production methods, livestock and aquaculture operations, economic and social sustainability, ecological knowledge development.
DOES NOT FUND: general public education, food donation efforts, public awareness campaigns, or community and school gardening initiatives.

Approximately $1.5 million available this cycle. Proposals due October 26, 2026 by 4:00 p.m. ET. Eligibility questions: northeast-fc@sare.org

Three other Northeast SARE programs share this October 26, 2026 deadline: Research and Education, Research for Novel Approaches, and Professional Development. Those are aimed at researchers, educators and service providers rather than farm businesses, and are not recorded separately here. The separate Farmer Grant (for commercial farmers, $5,000-$30,000) is its own record and its call is currently closed.

Name: Northeast SARE Research for Novel Approaches Grant
Description: One of Northeast SARE's large grant programs, supporting research into novel approaches in sustainable agriculture where the concept is promising but not yet proven. Applicants need not be farmers themselves; individuals working as consultants or sole proprietors and for-profit businesses may apply, so long as the beneficiaries are farmers. Roughly five million dollars is available across this and the two other large research programs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants need NOT be farmers. Eligible applicants include individuals (typically consultants or other sole proprietors) and FOR-PROFIT BUSINESSES, as well as institutions and organizations
- The people who BENEFIT from the grant must be farmers, meeting Northeast SARE's definition: a farm that sold, or could have sold, $1,000 or more in commercial product the previous year
- Northeast SARE region: CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT, WV and Washington DC
- Applicants may submit two preproposals per program, but if invited to submit multiple full proposals, only ONE full proposal may be submitted across all three large research programs

Proposals due October 26, 2026 by 4:00 p.m. ET. Approximately $5 million is available across the three large research programs combined.

Shares its deadline with Farming Community, Research and Education, and Professional Development - all recorded separately.

Name: Northeast SARE Research and Education Grant
Description: One of Northeast SARE's large grant programs, funding sustainable agriculture research paired with education and outreach that reaches farmers directly. Applicants do not need to be farmers themselves; individuals working as consultants or sole proprietors and for-profit businesses may apply, provided the people who benefit are farmers. Roughly five million dollars is available across this and the two other large research programs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants need NOT be farmers. Eligible applicants include individuals (typically consultants or other sole proprietors) and FOR-PROFIT BUSINESSES, as well as institutions and organizations
- The people who BENEFIT from the grant must be farmers, meeting Northeast SARE's definition: a farm that sold, or could have sold, $1,000 or more in commercial product the previous year
- Northeast SARE region: CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT, WV and Washington DC
- Applicants may submit two preproposals per program, but if invited to submit multiple full proposals, only ONE full proposal may be submitted across all three large research programs

Proposals due October 26, 2026 by 4:00 p.m. ET. Approximately $5 million is available across the three large research programs combined (Research and Education, Research for Novel Approaches, Professional Development).

This grant shares its deadline with Farming Community, Research for Novel Approaches, and Professional Development - all recorded separately.

Name: Northeast SARE Professional Development Grant
Description: One of Northeast SARE's large grant programs, funding training and professional development for agricultural service providers so they can better support farmers in sustainable agriculture. Applicants need not be farmers; individuals working as consultants or sole proprietors and for-profit businesses may apply, provided the ultimate beneficiaries are farmers. Roughly five million dollars is available across this and the two other large research programs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants need NOT be farmers. Eligible applicants include individuals (typically consultants or other sole proprietors) and FOR-PROFIT BUSINESSES, as well as institutions and organizations
- The people who BENEFIT from the grant must be farmers, meeting Northeast SARE's definition: a farm that sold, or could have sold, $1,000 or more in commercial product the previous year
- Northeast SARE region: CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT, WV and Washington DC
- Applicants may submit two preproposals per program, but if invited to submit multiple full proposals, only ONE full proposal may be submitted across all three large research programs

Proposals due October 26, 2026 by 4:00 p.m. ET. Approximately $5 million is available across the three large research programs combined.

Shares its deadline with Farming Community, Research and Education, and Research for Novel Approaches - all recorded separately. Note this program funds training for agricultural service providers (extension staff, consultants, technical advisors) rather than farm operations directly.

Name: Rally Accelerator
Description: A 16-week accelerator by Rally in Central Florida supporting early-stage social & environmental ventures with mentorship, pilot opportunities and housing/travel support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage social or environmental ventures ready for pilot; committed team; may require travel to program.

Name: Houston Fifth Ward Community Investment Fund - Grant Cycle 1
Description: The Community Investment Fund awards grants for community-led projects benefiting residents and businesses in Houston's Historic Fifth Ward. Grant Cycle 1 funds two priority areas: workforce development, including job readiness, training, apprenticeships and employment services; and small business support, including technical assistance, entrepreneurial training, marketing, and access to capital. Nonprofits, community organizations, small businesses and entrepreneurs with a clear Fifth Ward connection may apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Nonprofit organizations, community-based organizations, small businesses, entrepreneurs, and other eligible entities
- Must demonstrate a clear connection to the Fifth Ward through location, service area, organizational history, partnerships, or population served
- Project must directly benefit Fifth Ward residents, businesses, or the community
- Must propose measurable goals and outcomes
- Must submit a complete project budget plus required organizational and financial documentation
- Must agree to comply with grant reporting requirements if selected

Priority areas for Cycle 1: Workforce Development and Small Business Support. Meeting eligibility does not guarantee funding; review is based on alignment with priorities, community benefit, feasibility, and available funds. Administered by Fifth Ward Community Redevelopment Corporation.

Name: Reno-Tahoe Airport Gaming Concession RFP
Description: The Reno-Tahoe Airport Authority is soliciting proposals to operate gaming services in the airport terminal and its new concourses. The solicitation is part of a concessions program expansion adding roughly forty percent more concessions space at an airport serving about 4.6 million passengers annually. The program invites prime concessionaires as well as small, medium, local and ACDBE-certified businesses and franchisees to participate.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Open to prime concessionaires operating multiple spaces within a category
- Also open to small and medium businesses, local businesses, ACDBE-certified firms, and franchisees of national or other brands
- Primes expected to partner with smaller-scale and ACDBE-qualified enterprises

Gaming RFP released August 2026; proposals due 10/27/2026. Prospective bidders encouraged to submit a Business Engagement Form and use the Interested Parties Directory to find prime partners. Full RFP documents on the Authority's Solicitation Opportunities page. No cash award - concession contract.

Name: Main Street Rising Tour - Houston
Description: Houston stop of the Main Street Rising Tour, a multi-city program from Hello Alice in partnership with Google, with Etsy and PayPal as additional partners. The event itself is free and open to all small business owners. Attendees get AI training for business growth, live coaching from Google, PayPal and Hello Alice experts, professional headshots, a 6-week virtual accelerator program, networking, and a digital 'Main Street Riser' badge. Separately, attendees may apply to pitch live at the event for a cash prize — one pitch winner per stop.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility requirements
- Businesses operating in Texas
- Have a venture-scalable or venture-viable product or service as defined; and
- Be fully operational (actively conducting business and generating revenue) and tech-enabled (utilizing digital tools, platforms, or systems to support core business operations)

Name: NYC SBS Customized Training Grant Program
Description: NYC’s Customized Training Grant Program (run by the Department of Small Business Services) reimburses NYC-based for-profit businesses for up to 60% of employee training costs to help solve business challenges, adopt new tools, expand services, or upskill staff. Grants range from $10,000 to $400,000, require training at least five employees (or applying as a consortium), and businesses pay upfront then receive quarterly reimbursements with a commitment to raise wages after training.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Businesses must be based in NYC, for-profit, and operating for more than one year
- Businesses must train at least five employees*
- Businesses pay for training costs up front and get reimbursed on a quarterly basis
- Employees can take different trainings
- Employees have one year to complete training
- Upon completion of training, businesses must provide wage increases
* Businesses with less than five employees can apply jointly as a consortium to meet the trainee requirement. Please contact us for more information on applying as a consortium.

Name: City of Chicago Workforce Solutions Grant
Description: The Workforce Solutions program provides Chicago businesses with reimbursement grants – up to $250,000 and potentially covering 100% of training costs – to support job training for current employees and new hires.
