The program prioritizes Chicago-based small- to mid-sized businesses across many industries, covering expenses like employee training, materials, and instructor costs, while excluding certain business types and non-training-related expenses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- A company, organization, or nonprofit located in, expanding into or relocating to the City of Chicago
- An active non-profit organization, such as an industrial council, community development corporation, business/trade association or labor organization
- A company, organization or nonprofit planning to remain operational in their community area for a term no less than three years
- A financially sound business/organization not solely dependent on Workforce Solutions grants to stay in business

Name: SEED SPOT DC Launch Camp
Description: Free one-day in-person bootcamp in Washington, D.C. for very early-stage founders, focused on pitch development and customer definition. Participants build a pitch presentation, develop a customer profile, get feedback from mentors, and receive breakfast and lunch. The durable benefit is lifetime SEED SPOT Alumni Program membership, which carries ongoing mentorship and funding-resource access.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NO CASH AWARD — this is free training and network access, not funding. Open to early-stage entrepreneurs in the prototyping phase or 1-5 years from launch; ideally ventures have a minimum viable product and at least one sale or one customer. Any industry. Full-day participation commitment required. Targeted at underrepresented entrepreneurs — the page names BIPOC, women, transgender, non-binary, people with diverse abilities, low and moderate income, military veterans, LGBTQIA+, immigrants, and rural residents. Free to apply and free to attend. Applications close October 30, 2026; program runs Friday, November 6, 2026, 9:30 AM - 4:00 PM in Washington, D.C. (venue TBD).

Name: 2026 SE Michigan Small Business Pitch Competition (Torch of Wisdom Foundation / Delta Sigma Theta Southfield)
Description: Pitch competition for Southeast Michigan small businesses, presented by the Economic Education Series partners — the Torch of Wisdom Foundation, Inc. and the Southfield Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. Winners will receive $5,000 for first prize, $3,000 for second prize, and $2,000 for third prize. The Economic Education Series is a Fifth Third Bank-sponsored financial literacy program running free seminars on business financing, estate planning, housing affordability, and tax strategy; this competition is its small business component. Winners receive prize funding to support business growth and sustainability.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a registered small business operating in Southeast Michigan — Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw, Livingston, Monroe, or St. Clair County. Brick-and-mortar, online, and hybrid business models are all accepted. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to community engagement. INELIGIBLE: previous winners of this competition; anyone serving on Torch of Wisdom Foundation boards or committees; anyone affiliated with Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.; and anyone within defined family or household relationships to an ineligible party. Applications close Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. No application fee stated. Funder background: torchofwisdomfoundationinc.com/economic-education-series.

Name: California Digital Divide Grant Program
Description: NONPROFIT AND SCHOOL DISTRICT ONLY - for-profit businesses are not eligible. The CPUC funds projects that close broadband access, device affordability and digital skills gaps in underserved California communities. Round 4 awards one $100,000 grant to a qualifying small school district and two grants of up to $50,000 to nonprofits, from $200,000 total. Applicants must partner with eligible schools or districts.
Amount: $100,000 (district) / up to $50,000 each for two nonprofit awards; $200,000 total, 3 awards
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: FOR-PROFIT BUSINESSES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE. Open only to 501(c)(3) nonprofits with a demonstrated record deploying community technology projects, and to rural or urban small school districts (under 2,500 ADA, 50%+ free/reduced-price meal eligibility). Applicants must partner with eligible schools/districts and submit partnership agreements and recommendation letters. Opened 7/6/2026; awards announced January 2027; 90-day performance period.

Name: Awesome Foundation
Description: Awards $1,000 monthly micro-grants with no strings attached to creative and impactful projects, funded by local chapters of volunteer trustees.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Awesome Foundation is an ever-growing worldwide community devoted to forwarding the interest of awesome in the universe. Created in the long hot summer days of 2009 in Boston, the Foundation distributes $1,000 grants, no strings attached, to projects and their creators. At each fully autonomous chapter, the money is pooled together from the coffers of ten or so self-organizing “micro-trustees” and given up front in cash, check, or gold doubloons.

Name: Freed Fellowship Grant
Description: Awards a $500 monthly grant to underrepresented small business owners, with all recipients eligible for a $2,500 year-end grant; includes business feedback and a free two-month trial to a mentoring community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any micro or small business owner in the US is eligible. We especially encourage women, minorities and others considered underrepresented or overlooked to apply.

Name: Amber Grants
Description: WomensNet is dedicated to supporting women entrepreneurs. Each month, they offer multiple funding opportunities for women-owned businesses, including 3 $10,000 Amber Grants each month, and a $50,000 year-end Amber Grant.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
As long as you’re a woman who is 18 years or older, your business is 50% women-owned, and operates in the United States or Canada — you’re eligible to apply.

Non-profit organizations that are revenue-generating are eligible for our grants. To qualify, non-profit businesses must have 501(c)(3) status, and at least 50% of their top leadership, including the Board President or CEO, must be women.
Industry: Health / Wellness,Food & Beverage,Climate & Sustainability,Beauty & Personal Care,Education & Child Care,Arts & Crafts,Technology,Apparel & Accessories

Name: Galaxy Grant
Description: Offers a $2,500 grant open to women and minority entrepreneurs to help build and grow their small businesses. Provided by Hidden Star, a nonprofit dedicated to supporting underrepresented business owners with financial assistance, resources, and tools.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All women and minority business owners are eligible.

Name: HerRise MicroGrant
Description: Grants for under-resourced women entrepreneurs - including women of color - running U.S.-based, women-owned businesses with less than $1M in revenue. Funds can be used for tech, marketing, equipment, and more.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Your business must be:
- 51% owned by women 
- Currently registered in the US
- Less than $1 million in gross revenue

Name: YippityDoo Big Idea Grant
Description: Awards two $1,000 grants each month - one to a for-profit and one to a nonprofit women-owned business. Includes access to a mindset coaching group to support entrepreneurial growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- For-Profit Women Entrepreneurs/Small Business Owners, Women Owned Businesses that are at least 50% owned and run by a woman.
- Ages 18 or over, within the United States.
- Your business can already be started or in idea stage

Name: Breva Thrive Grant
Description: Breva’s Thrive Grant awards one trade subcontractor or emerging general contractor $5,000 plus one year on the Breva platform each quarter. It supports contractors who invest in their crews and communities by hiring, training, retaining workers, and paying suppliers on time.

Name: Chicago Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF)
Description: The SBIF provides reimbursement grants for permanent building improvements and repairs to industrial and commercial properties within designated Chicago TIF districts. Eligible tenants and property owners can receive between 30%–90% of project costs, up to $150,000 for commercial and $250,000 for industrial properties.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is eligible?
- Business properties located in a TIF district where SBIF funds are available and the SBIF is open for applications
- Commercial businesses with gross annual sales up to $9 million on average over the previous three years
- Commercial property owners with net worth up to $ 9 million and liquid assets up to $500,000
- Industrial businesses with up to 200 full-time employees
- Residential projects are not eligible for SBIF grants

Name: Goldman Sachs 10k Small Businesses
Description: Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses is a national program helping entrepreneurs grow revenues, create jobs, and expand economic opportunity. Participants gain access to practical training, expert support, and a powerful network of 16,000+ graduates across all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico. Applications are open for both national (online) and local (in-person) cohorts, with deadlines about 3 months before each cohort’s start date.

Name: Sky's The Limit Grants
Description: Sky's The Limit awards monthly grants of $2,500 to underrepresented entrepreneurs. Entrepreneurs need to create an account and create a pitch page to participate in monthly grants, and also gain access to mentorship, tools and resources, and special events.

Name: Roy W. Dean Short Film Grant
Description: The Roy W. Dean Grant (From the Heart Productions) supports independent films that are unique and contribute to society, open worldwide for documentaries, narrative features, shorts, web series, and multimedia projects in any production phase with budgets under $500,000. The winner receives $3,500 cash plus $20,000+ in services/discounts. Applications have a $48 fee ($38 student) and require materials like a proposal/synopsis, budget, distribution plan, and a work sample link.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Budget Must Be Under $500,000
- Open to Filmmakers from Any Country
- For Any Phase of Production from Development to Post-Production
- Films Can Be Any Length
- Live Action or Animated

Name: The Pollination Project
Description: The Pollination Project’s Daily Grant Program awards 365 microgrants each year, offering up to $500 to help volunteers and grassroots organizations launch or grow community-driven charitable projects. Rather than limiting funding by issue area or geography, it considers any eligible project worldwide that promotes a more just, sustainable, and compassionate world.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We accept applications from individuals, groups, and startup not-for-profit organizations based anywhere in the world as long as the work is volunteer-led and fits the following guidelines.

For All Applicants:

Your project must serve charitable community purposes and not personal gain.
You/Your organization must not already be a recipient of TPP’s Daily Grant.
Your project’s total budget must be under $10,000 USD.
You can request up to $500 USD in TPP grant funding.
You or your organization must be able to receive a wire transfer.
For Organizations:

No paid staff (occasional professional services such as web design, accounting, etc. are allowed).
No organizational promotion or advocacy for animal agriculture.
Annual budget must not exceed $50,000.
Types of Projects We Do Not Fund:

Animal farming activities or animal products (such as meat, eggs, honey, milk, and leather). Click here for more information.
Academic and research projects.
One-time donations.
Beekeeping projects producing honey for sale or human consumption.
Support for political parties, campaigns, or elections.
Projects that discriminate based on race, ethnicity, sexuality, gender, age, or faith.
Projects that evangelize or require beneficiaries to participate in faith-based practices.
Items We Do Not Fund:

Payments to a grantee or grantee’s family for their time or services.
Synthetic/chemical fertilizers, pesticides, or fungicides.
Non-recycled paper.
One-time use disposable plastic products.

Name: Hinge One More Hour Fund
Description: One More Hour was a $1 million Hinge initiative designed to combat loneliness by funding organizations and social groups that create more opportunities for Gen Z to connect in person. The program funded practical costs such as equipment, transportation, instructors, and other expenses that make community activities accessible
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: "In general, we are interested in established groups that meet regularly, are free or low cost to participate in, with a unique focus on creating in-person connection opportunities for Gen Z."

Name: Good Food Awards (2027 Cycle)
Description: The Good Food Awards recognize U.S. craft food and beverage producers whose products meet both taste and social and environmental responsibility standards. Producers submit finished retail products across 18 categories, which are evaluated in a blind tasting and then vetted against sourcing, labor, and sustainability criteria. Up to three winners and five finalists are named per category in each of five U.S. regions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- U.S.-based company, including U.S. territories
- Product made in a licensed kitchen, facility, or plant meeting state and local regulations
- Product ready for retail sale
- All ingredients meet FDA and/or USDA standards; uncommon ingredients must be on the GRAS list
- Co-packed products allowed if made from the producer's own recipe with verifiable sourcing and regular QC
- Producer must demonstrate fair wages, safe work environments, annual DEI training, and culturally respectful marketing
- Companies over $100M revenue: 12+ weeks paid parental leave, board diversity, clean five-year workplace safety record
- Maximum 4 entries per category per producer; fees non-refundable

Non-monetary: medal, winner seal for packaging, publicity. Entry window October 1-31, 2026. Blind judging Jan 15, 2027; finalists May 2027; winners July 2027; celebration July 25-27, 2027 at the Summer Fancy Food Show, NYC.

Name: Kentucky Proud Promotional Grant
Description: The Kentucky Department of Agriculture reimburses Kentucky Proud members for up to half of eligible marketing and promotional costs, including advertising, web design, packaging and labels, photography, signage and trade show booth fees. Awards reach eight thousand dollars a year but cannot exceed ten percent of the applicant's reported direct Kentucky farm impact. Applications are reviewed monthly while funds remain.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a Kentucky Proud member - SUPPORTER STATUS IS EXCLUDED
- Must be age 18 or older
- Cannot be delinquent in state taxes
- Must complete a notarized affidavit and an EZ Vendor Registration Form

AWARD MATH: reimburses up to 50% of eligible expenses, max $8,000 per year, and CANNOT EXCEED 10% of reported direct Kentucky farm impact. LIFETIME CAP of $36,000 beginning with 2014 funds.
Farm impact = the dollar value of agricultural products bought, sold, grown, raised, produced and sourced from Kentucky farms BEFORE processing - not the finished retail product value.

ELIGIBLE: radio/TV ads (Kentucky Proud logo required), web design/maintenance/digital advertising, branded clothing and giveaways (employee use only), labels/packaging/retail displays (logo permanently incorporated), trade show booth fees and hookups, UPC/bar codes, graphic design, vehicle wraps (pre-approval required), business cards, brochures, signage, direct mail, photography, banners. Demos reimburse a flat $100 per event, max 10% of the total request.
INELIGIBLE: staff time, items from the Kentucky Proud At-Cost Program, food/rentals/labor for events, jars and bottles, logo stickers or decals alone.

CYCLE: applications due the last day of each month; review meetings the second Wednesday of the following month. Must sign the agreement within 30 days of approval and use funds within 6 months.

Name: AARP AgeTech November Open Mic Pitch Challenge
Description: Online pitch competition from AARP's AgeTech Collaborative seeking products and services that empower people to choose how they live as they age. Selected companies deliver a three- to five-minute pitch followed by a five-minute Q&A before a panel of industry experts, and may be invited into AARP's free, equity-free eight-week AgeTech accelerator, which provides consumer research, mentorship, marketing support, and connections to investors and testing partners.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Products must be at least at minimum viable product (MVP) stage. Focus areas include financial resiliency, healthcare, social engagement, accessibility, caregiving, and longevity, or healthspan and wellness solutions that help people stay active as they age. Applications opened September 1, 2026 and close September 30, 2026 at 11:59 pm; finalists are announced around November 2, 2026 and the pitch event runs online November 19, 2026, 3:00-5:00 pm. No cash prize and no application fee listed — the value is the pitch platform and a possible accelerator invitation.

Name: Orange County (NC) Business Investment Grant Program
Description: Orange County's Economic Development office funds non-farm business investment and expansion in the county using quarter-cent sales tax revenue. Eligible uses are marketing and advertising, inventory and supplies (including computer software), purchase of equipment and/or machinery, workforce expansion including employee salary, and tenant up-fit or leasehold improvements; purchase quotes or invoices matching each use must be included in the application, and for workforce expansion the application must give position detail and wage information. The business must be physically located in Orange County in appropriately zoned space (a virtual address or P.O. Box does not qualify) and must have been operating and generating sales for at least 6 months for the Small Grant or at least 12 months for the Large Grant, which also requires additional financial information and a formal business plan. Applicants must have no past-due Orange County tax, fee or fine, and no owner or affiliated business may receive more than $10,000 across County grant programs in a three-year period. Grant funds cannot reimburse expenses incurred before the funds are received. A pre-application meeting with an Orange County Economic Development staff member is required before applying, and applications are submitted through Submittable. Priority goes to applicants demonstrating a clear need to grow, hire staff and add to the commercial tax base, with preference for those hiring Orange County residents and using Orange County vendors.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Non-farm for-profit or non-profit business physically located in Orange County, NC in appropriately zoned space (virtual address or P.O. Box does not qualify); farmers use the Orange County Agricultural Grant instead
- Operating and generating sales for at least 6 months (Small Grant, up to $5,000) or at least 12 months (Large Grant, $5,000.01-$10,000)
- Large Grant also requires additional financial information and a formal business plan
- No past-due Orange County tax, fee or fine; current on any existing Orange County Small Business Loan or Emergency Small Business Loan payments
- Must wait 6 months from a previous award before reapplying; max $10,000 per owner/affiliated business across County grant programs over three years
- Non-profit applicants: workforce expansion is the only eligible use
- Required pre-application meeting with Orange County Economic Development staff; applications submitted through Submittable
- Deadlines 5:00 pm on February 28, June 30 and October 31 each year; cycles may close early if funding is depleted

Name: 2027 SALON TODAY 200 (salon, spa and barbershop recognition)
Description: SALON TODAY magazine's annual program recognizes 200 salons, spas and barbershops across North America for business performance and management practice, and honorees are celebrated at an industry event. The 2027 application adds a Talent Recruitment & Retention category. It is open to salon, spa and barbershop owners in North America; apply through the online application linked from the announcement. Questions: stacey.soble@bobit.com or nicole.johnson@bobit.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Salon, spa and barbershop owners in North America. Application fee not stated on the announcement.

Name: Association for a Better New York Grant
Description: The ABNY Foundation offers $10,000 grants to small and mid-size nonprofits with 50 or fewer employees providing direct services within New York City’s five boroughs; applicants must have 501(c) status or a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor. Funding supports economic opportunity programs, including career training, small business support, and commercial district development, or civic engagement initiatives that expand civic literacy, participation, and leadership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Be a small or mid-size non-profit with 50 employees or less that provide direct services within the 5 boroughs of New York City.
- Grantees may only receive an award for a maximum of three consecutive years. Previous grantees with three consecutive awards must wait one-year before becoming eligible for a new grant award from the Foundation.
- Applying organizations must be designated under the 501(c) Section of the United States Internal Revenue Code or possess Fiscal Sponsorship from a registered 501(c)3 organization under the United States Internal Revenue Code. For profit organizations are not eligible for grants awards from The ABNY Foundation.

Name: ReStore Boston
Description: ReStore Boston is a City of Boston grant program that supports for-profit businesses and commercial property owners in improving storefront signage and facades to boost foot traffic and strengthen neighborhood commercial corridors. The program reimburses 50–90% of eligible project costs (up to $8,000 for signage and $200,000 for facade improvements) and includes access to professional design and architectural assistance; businesses pay upfront and are reimbursed by the City. Grants are competitive, prioritize businesses in low- to moderate-income areas, and follow a structured process from application and verification through design, permitting, and construction, with multiple review deadlines each year.
Amount: up to $8,000 for signage and up to $200,000 for facades
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To apply for the ReStore Boston program, your business must meet the minimum requirements listed below. 
- Your business must be a for-profit business, not a nonprofit. 
- Your business must have a physical storefront. 
- You must have at least 3 years remaining on your lease and permission from your landlord to make the improvements.
- You must have funds available to cover your portion of the total cost.
- You must be in good financial standing with the City of Boston and cannot have outstanding bills with the Assessing Department, Boston Water and Sewer Commission, Public Works, or Inspectional Services. 
- Your storefront cannot be in disrepair caused by negligence.
- Your storefront cannot have solid roll down grates or backlit plastic-shield sign boxes. However, the City of Boston will help pay for solid grates to be removed if you are selected for ReStore Boston and agree to remove them.

Please note: A majority of the grants for this program are for low-moderate income areas, and for businesses that meet National Objectives. These are designations set by the federal government.  The Office of Small Business will determine if your business meets low-moderate income certification and National Objectives after we receive your complete application.

Name: Sparkplug Foundation Grant
Description: The Sparkplug Foundation provides one-year grants ranging from $1,000 to $20,000, with most awards between $10,000 and $15,000, to early-stage organizations and new nonprofit projects focused on education, community organizing, or music. It prioritizes grassroots, community-led work with limited access to traditional funding and supports 501(c)(3) nonprofits or fiscally sponsored groups with budgets under $1 million, particularly projects centered on inclusion, justice, and community accountability.

Name: SXSW EDU Launch Startup Competition
Description: Pitch competition for early-stage education startups, held at SXSW EDU in Austin March 13-16, 2027. Finalists and semifinalists pitch before industry experts, investors, and educators and gain access to SXSW networking events. Three awards are presented: the Launch Award, the Impact Award, and the Community Choice Award.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage startups in the education market with an established management team, a public-facing website, and demonstrated user traction, engagement, and adoption metrics. Companies that have raised more than $8 million from combined funding sources at the time of application are ineligible. Past SXSW EDU Launch finalists and semifinalists are not eligible to apply. A startup may present at only one SXSW startup event — if selected for more than one, you must choose. Judging weighs creativity, scalability, product effectiveness, team, and potential to improve educational outcomes. $60 application fee.

Name: SCBWI Impact and Legacy Fund Independent Bookstore Grant
Description: The Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators' Impact and Legacy Fund awards three $1,000 grants a year to independent bookstores. The funds pay for a public program or event featuring a children's book author, illustrator or translator that is open to the community and increases foot traffic or awareness of the store. A store qualifies as independently owned if it has three or fewer owners, is a corporation with five or fewer shareholders, is a cooperative with fewer than 10 employees, or is a partnership; chains and franchises are not eligible, and SCBWI membership is not required. Applications are submitted through a Google Form that asks for the bookstore's name, address, web and social presence, employee count, and four short answers of up to 100 words each covering what makes the store's community unique, the challenges the business faces, how the grant would be used, and the expected impact on the business and the community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Independently owned bookstores: three or fewer owners, corporations with five or fewer shareholders, cooperatives with fewer than 10 employees, or partnerships
- Chains and franchises are not eligible
- SCBWI membership is not required
- No location or years-in-operation restriction published
- Funds must be used for a public program or event featuring a children's book author, illustrator or translator, open to the community
- 2026 application window: September 1 to November 1, 2026
- Apply via Google Form: https://forms.gle/zo2aeRefGufQMhnq8

Name: Mitsubishi Electric America Foundation (MEAF) National Grant
Description: The Mitsubishi Electric America Foundation funds 501(c)(3) organizations for projects that help youth with disabilities (defined as birth through about age 26) build employment and leadership skills, or that remove barriers to employment. Projects must take an innovative approach with measurable employment outcomes and be national in scope or a replicable model; locally based activities without broader impact are not funded. MEAF makes 6 to 12 grants a year of $10,000 to $100,000 per year for one to two years. Proposals are accepted online July 15 through November 1, with funding decisions by March 15 and projects starting on or after April 1.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY: 501(c)(3)s. Youth with disabilities (birth to ~26); employment/leadership outcomes; national scope or replicable model required.

Name: Entrepreneurs Roundtable Accelerator
Description: ERA offers early-stage NYC startups seed capital, hands-on support, and co-working space along with access to 500+ expert mentors across tech, product, marketing, sales, and investment. ERA runs two four-month programs per year and selects companies globally that can leverage NYC as a springboard to scale their products, services, or applications. Participants receive an initial $150K investment on a 6% post-money SAFE with potential for follow-on funding.

Name: 100x Impact Accelerator
Description: 100x Impact Accelerator empowers visionary social entrepreneurs to achieve outsized, systemic change through evidence-based research, catalytic capital, and world-class mentorship. Backed by the London School of Economics, 100x helps ventures define their endgame and scale impact not through endless fundraising, but through sustainable models like government adoption, digitisation, and open-source solutions. With £150,000 in funding, a 12-week accelerator, and lifelong community support, 100x transforms bold ideas into “social unicorns” tackling global challenges from climate to democracy.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We want to make sure that you get the most value and the right level of support from 100x. Below, we’ve set out our criteria to help you see if you’re in the right place.

To be considered, your venture must meet all of the following criteria:
- Impact-first venture – Venture is explicitly focused on social and/or environmental impact, and agnostic to legal form (ie structured as non-profit or for-profit)
- Delivering impact within at least one of our eight Impact Areas
- Ambition to scale – You have a clear vision for reaching hundreds of millions of lives through your intervention, that may also shift an entire system or market. We prioritise ventures with a credible route to systems-level change, whether through replication, open infrastructure, market transformation, or integration into public or private delivery systems.

In addition, we prioritise ventures that can demonstrate some or all of the following:
- Can be registered or operating from anywhere in the world
- Impact achieved to date has reached at least 50,000 end-users (B2C) or indirectly impacted at least 500,000 people (via B2B or B2G channels), with clear evidence of delivery and uptake
- Operating with a team of 4 or more full-time paid employees
- Raised at least USD 250,000 in capital from any source
- Established partnerships supporting scale – Active partnerships with government, large NGOs, multilateral organisations, or commercial distributors that support scale or systems integration

Name: Y Combinator (YC)
Description: Y Combinator (YC) is a three-month accelerator program that invests $500,000 in startups – $125,000 for 7% equity via a post-money SAFE and $375,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE. The program helps startups build better products, gain users, and prepare for fundraising through intensive mentorship, group and one-on-one office hours. It culminates in Demo Day, where founders present to top investors, followed by lifelong access to YC’s alumni network, ongoing office hours, and exclusive deals and resources that continue to support founders as they scale.

Name: MIT Solve 2027 Global Challenges
Description: MIT Solve's annual open-innovation Global Challenges source tech-based social-impact solutions worldwide. Selected Solver teams enter a nine-month support program with funding, mentorship, and access to MIT's network. The 2027 cycle runs five tracks: Global Learning, Global Health, Global Climate, Global Economic Prosperity, and the Indigenous Communities Fellowship.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All five 2027 challenges open September 22, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT and close November 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST — a tight six-week window. Historically open to tech-based solutions from for-profits and nonprofits worldwide; 2027 eligibility rules are not yet posted. Solve states on its Become a Solver page that last year's Solver teams received an average of $40,000 each, from a pool of more than $1 million in prize funding at selection, plus a nine-month support program. Per-challenge prize amounts for 2027 are not yet published. No application fee. Individual challenge pages: solve.mit.edu/challenges/2027-global-learning-challenge, /2027-global-health-challenge, /2027-global-climate-challenge, /2027-global-economic-prosperity-challenge, /2027-indigenous-communities-fellowship.
Industry: Technology,Social Impact,Education & Child Care,Health / Wellness,Climate & Sustainability

Name: Inc. Female 500 Founders
Description: The 2027 Inc. Female Founders 500 recognizes women founders of independent organizations, with honorees receiving national recognition, media exposure, and a dedicated company profile on Inc.com. Applications highlight leadership and company accomplishments over the past year; the early-rate deadline is November 6, 2026 ($295), and the final deadline is December 11, 2026. Honorees will be announced in spring 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All female founders of independent (not a subsidiary or division of another company) organizations are encouraged to apply.

Name: Polsky Small Business Financial Fundamentals Program
Description: A 12-week intensive program (Jan–Mar 2027) for South and West Side Chicago businesses seeking to strengthen financial skills and prepare for capital readiness. Participants receive tailored technical assistance in business finance education, financial reporting, and capital pathways, plus one-on-one coaching. Open to business owners with $250K+ in annual revenue who are pursuing bank loans or fundraising. Requirements include financial statements (at minimum a P&L), commitment to attend all sessions (virtual + two in-person gatherings), and readiness to make strategic shifts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - South and West Side business owners with annual revenues approximately $250,000-$500,000 who are actively seeking to secure capital through a bank loan or other fundraising are welcome to apply.

Name: A.I.R. Fellowship Program
Description: 12-month fellowship for emerging and underrepresented women & non-binary visual artists with a solo exhibition, stipend, and professional development in NYC region.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Women or non-binary visual artists 18+, NYC five-borough residents, no NYC solo show in the past decade, not currently enrolled in a degree program. 2027-2028 fellowship: 6 emerging artists, anonymous three-round review, results April 2027, fellowship runs Sept 2027 - Aug 2028. Info session 10/29/2026.

Name: Asian Cultural Council Fellowships and Grants
Description: Annual open call by the ACC for artists, scholars, and cultural organizations to engage in cross-cultural exchange between Asia and the U.S., offering fellowships and project grants.
Amount: NY Fellowship $38,000 / Individual Fellowship up to $35,000 / Graduate Fellowship $15,000 per academic year / Organization Grant up to $50,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Citizens or permanent residents of ACC-eligible Asian countries, the US, or Afghanistan/Pakistan, with 5+ years in an eligible discipline (waived for the Graduate Fellowship). 2027 global cycle open 10/1/2026 - 11/10/2026 9:59 a.m. ET; recommendation letters due 11/16/2026. Grant activity period 8/1/2027 - 12/31/2028.

Name: Max and Victoria Dreyfus Foundation Grant
Description: The Max and Victoria Dreyfus Foundation makes grants to U.S.-based, IRS-qualified nonprofits, including educational, skills-training and other programs for youth, seniors and persons with disabilities, and favors organizations for which a small amount of money can make a large difference. Awards typically range from $1,000 to $20,000, and a request cannot exceed $20,000 or 25% of the organization’s average annual income over the past three years. Apply online with a letter of request of up to three pages, a summary of the organization’s purpose and use of funds, the most recent Form 990, a program budget and the 501(c)(3) determination letter. Requests submitted by November 10, 2026 are considered for the Spring 2027 award round.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY: IRS-qualified U.S. nonprofits. Request may not exceed $20,000 or 25% of average annual income over the past three years. No grants to individuals.

Name: Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grants
Description: The Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grants provide project-based funding of about $500–$3,000 for U.S.-based visual and performing artists or poets with public presentation opportunities or unexpected costs for projects close to completion. Applicants must have confirmed performance or exhibition dates, and the program prioritizes innovative, contemporary, experimental work rather than general production, albums, music videos, conferences, or living expenses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Artists who make innovative, experimental work are eligible to apply. FCA considers all elements of an application in context to determine if an artist’s work aligns with our mission to support experimental practices.

To understand if an applicant’s practice aligns with FCA’s mission, staff members and panelists review: work samples, how the proposed project is described, any explanation the artist gives about the experimental nature of their approach or process, the venue at which the work is being presented, and the context in which the applicant has been working. Does the work push against, expand upon, or break from established artistic practices and/or does the work subvert mainstream norms, narratives, or aesthetics? Do the venues at which the artist’s work has been or will be presented have a history of presenting experimental art or a mission to do so? Does the applicant identify with a community of experimental art makers?

Many applications are declined each month because the applicant’s work is not a fit for FCA’s mission of supporting experimental, contemporary work in the arts. For examples of projects and artists FCA supports, please refer to past grant recipients and projects on our website.

Additionally:

Applicants must be living in the United States or U.S. territories and have a U.S. Tax ID Number (SSN, EIN, ITIN, or other).
Applicants must have committed performance or exhibition opportunities, and be able to provide specific dates at the time of application.
Applicants must be individual artists, or an individual representing an artist collective, ensemble, or group. Curators, producers, workshop organizers, organizations, or arts presenters are not eligible to apply.
If multiple artists are working collaboratively on a project, the artist who received the invitation to present work and/or who is organizing the presentation opportunity should submit the application.
Artists enrolled in any degree-granting program or school are not eligible to apply. This includes high school, undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs.

Name: Interledger Foundation Local Impact Mini Grants
Description: Micro-grants from the Interledger Foundation for grassroots work advancing digital financial access. Fundable activities are broad and include storytelling and content creation alongside meetups, workshops, hackdays, and research. Projects must be completed within six months of grant acceptance, with priority for those wrapping by December 31, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to community organizations, nonprofits, cooperatives, civil society groups, local fintech startups, social enterprises, and individual practitioners with a concrete project plan. Both registered and unregistered entities may apply, so a solo practitioner or unincorporated group qualifies. No prior experience with Interledger required. Open worldwide, but priority goes to projects serving communities in the Global South and in rural or peri-urban regions; applicants in OFAC-sanctioned countries are ineligible. Applications opened July 6, 2026 with rolling review through November 11, 2026 — earlier submission is materially better than waiting for the close. Submitted via Submittable. No application fee. Note this is a financial-inclusion program, not general creative funding: a creative project needs a genuine tie to open payments or digital financial infrastructure.

Name: LMCC Creative Engagement 2027 (Manhattan Arts Grants)
Description: Lower Manhattan Cultural Council's Creative Engagement program funds individual artists and nonprofit organizations for projects and activities that offer Manhattan communities diverse artistic experiences, for projects taking place from Inwood to the Battery during the calendar year (the 2026 round awarded over $500,000). The 2027 guidelines and application open in fall 2026 – sign up for LMCC's mailing list or email CreativeEngagement@LMCC.net to be notified.
Amount: project grants (2026 round awarded $500,000+ in total)
Deadline Type: TBA – 2027 guidelines and application open fall 2026
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists and nonprofit organizations presenting public arts projects in Manhattan during the grant year.

Name: Preserve Route 66 Legacy Business Grant Fund
Description: The National Trust for Historic Preservation funds small, independently owned legacy businesses and businesses occupying historic or older buildings in communities along the Route 66 corridor. Grants support exterior repair, signage, murals, painting and other preservation-minded improvements that keep long-standing businesses viable. No match is required. The 2026 round opened September 1 and closes November 12.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Direct application portal: https://www.grantinterface.com/Home/Logon?urlkey=nthp - Owner 18+, registered business in good standing with a physical location in a community, neighborhood or tribal land along Route 66. National franchises and nonprofits ineligible. No match required. Funder quote: 'The grant application will open on September 1, 2026, and be due November 12, 2026 at 11:59pm your local time.'

Name: Robin Hood Catalyst Program
Description: The Catalyst Program is a 16-week accelerator designed for startups with traction (under $150K revenue in a 12-month period or raised less than $500K, excluding grants) to scale impact through funding, coaching, and community. Participants receive $100K funding (SAFE for for-profits or grant for nonprofits), weekly programming led by experienced founders and investors, 1:1 coaching, functional workshops, and workspace at BRL Lab.
Amount: $100,000 (investment for for-profits / grant for nonprofits, plus follow-on)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Teams must be building scalable tech solutions, already have developed an MVP with traction, with an alignment to low-income New Yorkers and Americans, in general. Whether you’re focusing on housing, education, future of work, health, financial services, or any area impacting economic mobility for all, we want to hear from you. You can apply as a solo founder or as part of a small team. Companies must not have earned more than $200k in total revenue within any given 12-month period or raised more than $500k (excluding grants).

Name: Chicago Neighborhood Opportunity Fund (NOF)
Description: A capital development grant program provided by City of Chicago Department of Planning and Development that supports small business and cultural projects located on eligible commercial corridors on the West, Southwest, and South Sides of Chicago. Grants reimburse up to 75% of eligible project expenses for new construction, storefront build-outs, facade repair, etc.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Project must be located on an NOF-eligible or priority commercial corridor; eligible project types include commercial (office, retail), cultural (museums, theaters), or nonprofits with a commercial on-site component; expenses must be for permanent capital improvements; grants are reimbursements, not upfront funding.

Name: SXSW Pitch
Description: SXSW Pitch is the festival's flagship startup showcase, staging selected companies in front of venture investors, angels, corporate scouts and press over two days in Austin in March 2027. Eight categories run from artificial intelligence to sustainability technology. Entry is fee-based and tiered by date, one entry per company, and is open to companies that launched after January 2024 and have raised no more than ten million dollars.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Product or service must have launched after 2024-01-01. One entry per company. Founders must retain ownership. Maximum $10 million raised in prior funding. Must fit one of eight competition categories. Applications via cart.sxsw.com; fees non-refundable whether or not the company is selected as a finalist. Early Bird entry June 23 - September 13, 2026 ($105); Regular entry September 14 - November 13, 2026 ($225). Event March 16-17, 2027, Austin TX.

Name: Blue Ridge Labs Catalyst Program
Description: Robin Hood’s Blue Ridge Labs Catalyst is a 16-week accelerator for early-stage tech startups and nonprofits improving economic mobility for low-income New Yorkers, offering $100,000 plus tailored coaching, mentorship, and community connections; funding is a grant for nonprofits or a SAFE with a 5.5% equity conversion entitlement for for-profits. Applicants must have a working product with traction, no more than $150,000 in revenue in any 12-month period, and no more than $500,000 raised, excluding grants. The program runs February–June 2027 with two required in-person days per week in NYC.

Name: Smart Start Workforce Grants (Illinois)
Description: Quarterly State of Illinois workforce grants for licensed child care centers, family child care and group family child care homes operating full-day, full-year (eight consecutive hours a day, five days a week, 47 weeks a year). Centers must have at least 15% of licensed capacity enrolled in CCAP; family child care needs at least one CCAP-enrolled child. Centers receive $4,750–$6,250 per classroom per quarter depending on age group; family child care receives $2,250 plus additional funding for assistants. FY27 Round 3 opens October 1, 2026 for renewals from previously funded programs and closes Friday, November 13, 2026; no new applications are accepted in Round 3. Applicants complete a mandatory orientation and submit through the Gateways Registry Director Portal with a W9, Certificate of Good Standing, classroom rosters, staff listing and signed attestation.
Amount: $4,750–$6,250 per classroom per quarter (centers); $2,250+ (family child care)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Licensed IL child care centers/homes operating full-day, full-year with CCAP enrollment minimums. Round 3 (FY27) is renewals only.

Name: U.S. Venture/Schmidt Family Foundation Grant
Description: Supports nonprofits improving lives in areas like education, health, and equity. Grants support a wide range of funding requests including specific program needs, capital support, and general operating support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify for funding from USV/SFF, organizations must meet the following criteria:
- Designated as public charities by the IRS, with preference given to those holding 501(c)(3) status.
- Demonstrate direct involvement or support from a U.S. Venture team member or shareholder (e.g., board membership, volunteering, or donor engagement).

Name: Live Your Dream Award
Description: Cash awards to support the education and training of women who are the primary financial support for their families, administered by Soroptimist.
Amount: $1,000 club / $3,000-$5,000 region / up to $10,000 international (up to $16,000 cumulative)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Women with financial responsibility for dependents; enrolled or accepted in a program; additional criteria apply.

Name: D-Prize Global Competition
Description: The D-Prize Global Competition offers up to $20,000 in seed funding to early-stage entrepreneurs launching ventures that scale proven solutions to extreme poverty, across sectors like health, agriculture, and livelihoods. It targets individuals ready to start and grow a new organization (typically under 18 months old) and commit full-time to expanding a single, evidence-based intervention.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
D-Prize is for new organizations. Most of our awardees are first-time entrepreneurs. Most have not yet launched their organization, nor have they raised other funding. We especially encourage those from low-and-middle income countries to apply. See who we recently seeded.

We will consider applications from existing organizations only if your core focus is distributing an existing and evidence-based poverty intervention. We typically will not support organizations with more than 18 months of full time operations or that have raised more than $30,000 USD in outside funding.

Name: Village of Savoy Building and Property Enhancement Program
Description: The Village of Savoy’s Building and Property Enhancement Program provides a reimbursement grant covering 50% of eligible project costs, up to $10,000, to help small businesses and commercial property owners improve the appearance and functionality of commercial properties village-wide. Applications are accepted twice a year (May 1–15 and Nov 1–15), and funds are reimbursed only after the project is completed, inspected, and paid receipts are submitted. Eligible upgrades are mainly visible exterior and safety/accessibility improvements (plus some code-compliance/accessibility interior work), and recipients must maintain the enhancements and stay in the location for at least two years.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- For this grant program, a small business is defined as a commercial enterprise that is independently owned, operated, and controlled, and has 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees (under 2,000 payroll hours per week) at the time of application.
- Owners of property, where the subject property is occupied by a business that is a small business as defined in this document or where such property owner, has executed a lease agreement for future occupancy with a small business as described in this document.
- Property must not have any outstanding code violations.
- Unit must be zoned for and operate as commercial use.
- For mixed-use properties, funds may only be used for eligible commercial components.
- Unit must have a current or proposed commercial use. If vacant, applicant must submit an executed lease or purchase contract.
- All properties must have current commercial insurance for the proposed property.
- Business entity must be a sales tax revenue generating business.
- Applicant(s) must be the end user of the commercial space. Building owners are eligible to apply if proposed use of funds is for signage that promotes the businesses within the property.
- Payment of all property taxes and/or assessments, general and special, must be current.
- Neither the owner of record, the tenant, nor any of their principals may be in default of any
obligations to the Village, including, but not limited to, fines, ordinance violations, debts, or otherwise (including personal property taxes and fees owed to the Village).
- The applicant must be able to commit to remain in the location and maintain enhancements for at least two (2) years.
- Applicants who have not received previous grant funds will be given priority consideration.
- All project elements must comply with all adopted and applicable Village rules, regulations, codes, and design standards.

Name: Small Business Readiness for Resiliency Mitigation Grant
Description: The Small Business Readiness for Resiliency (R4R) Mitigation Grant, sponsored by Verizon and administered by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation, funds projects that help small businesses prepare for natural disasters, such as backup power, flood barriers, and storm shutters. To apply, businesses must complete one of two free disaster resilience courses on Verizon’s Small Business Digital Ready platform.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to small businesses. NO DISASTER DECLARATION REQUIRED — this is the distinguishing feature versus the SB2R recovery grant. To unlock the grant application, create a free account on Verizon Small Business Digital Ready and complete a 15-30 minute small business disaster resilience course on the platform. Application window: September 29 through November 15, 2026. Funds are for pre-disaster mitigation projects at the business. Free to register and free to apply; no application fee. Administered by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation — full program terms at uschamberfoundation.org/solutions/disaster-response-and-resiliency/small-business-readiness-for-resiliency. A Digital Ready specialist can be reached at 888.483.3206. Note the SB2R recovery grant's broader exclusions (fewer than 500 employees, valid EIN, franchise limits, ineligible business categories) may also apply here — check the Terms and Conditions.

Name: Nebraska Individual Artist Fellowship
Description: Recognition program for Nebraska-based artists across literature, filmmaking/performing arts, and visual arts; funds must be used for new art, presentation, training, or research.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: THE 2027 CYCLE IS LITERARY ARTS ONLY (fiction, non-fiction, poetry) - the eligible discipline ROTATES ANNUALLY, so re-check it every cycle. Applicants must be 19+, Nebraska residents for 24 months prior and throughout the fellowship year, not enrolled undergraduates in their discipline, and the originator of the work. Applications via Foundant.

Name: Tory Burch Foundation Fellows Program
Description: The Tory Burch Foundation Fellows Program empowers women entrepreneurs with the resources, mentorship, and community needed to scale their businesses and lead with purpose. Fellows join a network of over 400 women founders, gain access to expert coaching and strategic advisors, and receive self-paced educational tools tailored to their business growth. The program emphasizes collaboration, intentional leadership, and long-term impact within a supportive entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
2026-27 CYCLE: applications open 22 September 2026 and close 17 November 2026; fellows selected May 2027. The Deadline field holds the EXPECTED OPEN DATE (22 Sept 2026) per the Coming Soon convention - the actual application deadline is 17 November 2026.

Applicant Criteria
- A woman entrepreneur who owns the largest or equally largest stake in a qualifying business (see Company Criteria)
- Has a significant role in managing the Qualifying Business
- 21 years or older as of the application due date
- Proficient in English
- A legal resident of the United States and its territories

Company Criteria
- For profit, from any industry
- Majority (51% or more) owned and controlled by women
- Generating minimum of $75,000 annually. There is no maximum revenue requirement.
- Formed under United States law and operating in the United States

Name: Queens Arts Fund: New Work Grant
Description: Project-based grants to Queens-based emerging individual artists or artist collectives to produce new work not previously presented.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: INDIVIDUAL Queens artists: must reside in Queens or hold a full-time Queens studio lease, be 18+ by 12/31/2026, not be full-time degree-seeking, and have received no 2026 QAF New Work funding. Work must be previously unpresented with a public component in calendar 2027. 2027 cycle opened 9/22/2026 10:00 a.m. ET, closes 11/17/2026 5:00 p.m. ET.

Name: Queens Arts Fund: Arts Access Grant
Description: Project-based grants to Queens-based artists, artist collectives, and small nonprofits to support public arts & cultural programs in Queens.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: ORGANISATIONAL, not individual - nonprofit-leaning: 501(c)(3)s or unincorporated artist collectives, existing 1+ year, operating budget under $100,000 in at least 2 of the last 3 years, Queens-based. Same 2027 window as the New Work Grant: opened 9/22/2026, closes 11/17/2026 5:00 p.m. ET, notifications Spring 2027.

Name: Howard Gilman – A.R.T./New York Small Theatres Fund (FY28–FY29)
Description: Two-year general operating support grants of $7,500–$10,000 per year for NYC-based theatre companies with annual budgets between $15,000 and $250,000 that have been operating for at least two years. 501(c)(3), LLC, fiscally sponsored and unincorporated companies are all accepted; A.R.T./New York membership is not required. Applications are submitted through A.R.T./New York's online grant portal (opens 9/29/26 at 10am ET); info sessions are held in late summer 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NYC-based theatre companies operating for 2+ years with annual budgets of $15,000–$250,000; 501(c)(3), LLC, fiscally sponsored and unincorporated companies eligible; membership not required.

Name: Techstars Accelerator
Description: Techstars runs three-month programs designed to help entrepreneurs achieve product-market fit, gain traction, and access capital and mentorship. Current programs accepting applications include healthcare-focused accelerators (Northwestern Medicine & Techstars Healthcare Accelerator and Techstars AI Health Baltimore) and broader programs (Techstars Anywhere Accelerator, Techstars Boston Accelerator, Techstars Chicago, Techstars New York City Accelerator, Techstars London Accelerator, and USC and Techstars Accelerator).
Amount: $20k for 5% equity and $200k via uncapped SAFE

Name: The Hopper Prize
Description: Global open call for individual artists offering unrestricted cash grants plus visibility via a digital archiving platform.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to artists worldwide in all media; unrestricted cash; bi-annual open call.

Name: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics Foundation Research Grants (Molly Kellogg / Julie O'Sullivan Maillet)
Description: The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics Foundation runs eleven named research grants from $3,000 to $20,000. Most target doctoral students, faculty, or early-career researchers, but two are open to practicing credentialed dietetics professionals: the Molly Kellogg Grant ($3,000), explicitly available to RDs and DTRs pursuing nutrition counseling research, and the Julie O'Sullivan Maillet Research Grant ($3,000), for work demonstrating the value of dietetics professionals to public health. The Vegetarian Nutrition DPG Research Grant ($10,000) is open to RDN, DTR, or dietetic student members. The Foundation's page states applications for the 2027 grant cycle open in September 2026; exact close dates are not published on the page, so email grants@eatright.org to confirm dates and whether Academy membership is required.
Amount: $3,000 - $20,000 (Molly Kellogg and Julie O'Sullivan Maillet are $3,000 each)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Varies by grant. Molly Kellogg Grant: open to RDs and DTRs conducting nutrition counseling research. Julie O'Sullivan Maillet Research Grant: open to those demonstrating the value of dietetics professionals to public health or their evolving role. Vegetarian Nutrition DPG Research Grant: RDN, DTR or dietetic student member (DPG members preferred). Most other Foundation grants are limited to doctoral students, faculty, or early-career researchers with limited prior funding. Academy membership requirements not stated on the page - confirm with grants@eatright.org.

Name: SFO Terminal 3 Travel Convenience Store Small Business Set-Aside
Description: San Francisco International Airport is soliciting a small-business operator for a 493-square-foot travel convenience store in Terminal 3, Boarding Area E. The lease is set aside for certified small businesses. Applicants generally need at least three years of relevant operating experience, at least one million dollars in annual sales during qualifying years, and must meet SFO's small-business certification requirements. This is a concession lease rather than a grant.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- At least three years of relevant operating experience
- At least $1 million in annual sales during qualifying years
- Must meet SFO's small-business certification requirements (set-aside lease)
- 493 square feet, Terminal 3, Boarding Area E

Deadline November 18, 2026.

NOTE: this is a CONCESSION LEASE opportunity, not a grant - there is no cash award. The value is the airport retail location itself. Relevant to businesses pursuing airport retail or concession footprints.

Name: Nina Mason Pulliam Charitable Trust
Description: The Nina Mason Pulliam Charitable Trust funds nonprofits in Maricopa County, Arizona and Marion County, Indiana through three giving areas: Helping People in Need, Protecting Animals and Nature, and Enriching Community Life. The Trust does not accept unsolicited applications: organizations first contact a program officer or email info@ninapulliamtrust.org, and submit a full application only if invited. Health programs are excluded except services for people who are visually impaired. Invited applications are reviewed in three rounds each year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY: Maricopa County AZ or Marion County IN. Invitation only after contacting a program officer. Excludes health programs (except visually impaired), research, sectarian purposes, programs for incarcerated/recently released individuals.

Name: Chicago Commercial Corridor Storefront Activation Program
Description: The Chicago Commercial Corridor Storefront Activation Program is a $30.5 million City of Chicago grant program that helps small businesses and property owners improve vacant or underused storefronts in 12 designated South and West Side corridors. It covers up to 75% of eligible project costs and also provides technical help with things like marketing, accounting, design, and permitting. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with quarterly deadlines.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Projects eligible for grant funding include:
- Renovation of vacant commercial spaces to attract new small business tenants
- Renovation of commercial spaces with existing small business tenants.
- Facade improvements or other improvements to existing commercial buildings and storefronts for curb appeal or to improve function
- To be eligible for a CCSA grant, applicants must demonstrate:

Property location in an approved CCSA commercial corridor
- Site control (ownership of the property or permission from the property owner to make proposed improvements)
- Eligible business activity
- Good standing with the Illinois Secretary of State and City of Chicago

Name: Jersey City Heights Holiday Market Vendor Application
Description: The Riverview Farmers Market is accepting vendor applications for the 2026 Heights Holiday Market, held December 5, 2026 at Riverview-Fisk Park in the Jersey City Heights. It is open to artists, makers, jewellers, apparel and home goods sellers, specialty and prepared food producers and local retailers.
Amount: In-kind: vendor space at a one-day holiday market
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to artists, makers, craftspeople, jewellery vendors, apparel and home goods sellers, specialty food producers, bakers, prepared food businesses and local retailers. Applications are reviewed to build a diverse, balanced line-up; space is limited and applying does not guarantee acceptance. Event Saturday 5 December 2026, 10am-4pm, Riverview-Fisk Park, Jersey City Heights, NJ. Vendor fees start at $85 for applications submitted by 30 September 2026 (fees rise after that date). Direct application (Google Form): https://forms.gle/1bhnijdRwcRJjo4m8

Name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants
Description: Quarterly grants for organizations addressing local needs.​ Focuses include economic opportunity, advancing sustainability, and strengthening community. Open to 501(c)(3) charities, public entities, and educational groups; must be Deed-verified and have a Spark Good account.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organizations must have a Spark Good account and be verified by Deed, Walmart’s third-party verification service provider.

Organizations must serve the same service area that the facility they are requesting funding from serves. Eligible entities must be a:
501(c)(3) public charity: An organization holding a current tax-exempt status and classified as a public charity under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, listed on the IRS Master File and conducting activities within the United States; classified as a public charity under Section 509(a)(1), (2) or (3) (Types I or II); and Deed verified.
Government entity (non-501(c)(3)): U.S. federal agencies territories and commonwealths, state agencies and departments and political subdivisions (including cities, counties, municipal agencies). 
School: All K-12 public or nonprofit private schools, charter schools, community/junior colleges, state/private colleges, or universities. Institutions must have a NCES (National Center for Education Statistics) number or 501c3 tax status and be verified with Deed. 
Church or other faith-based organization with a proposed project that benefits the community at large, such as food pantries, soup kitchens and clothing closets and Deed verified.

Note: Non-charities, including organizations such as 501(c)(4)s, (c)(6)s, and (c)(19)s like homeowner’s associations, civic leagues, or volunteer fire companies, are not eligible.

Name: Causability Creator Grants
Description: Causability offers $5,000 unrestricted grants to U.S.-based creators who partner with local nonprofits to develop programs benefiting both artists and socio-economically marginalized communities. Grants support a wide range of creative disciplines and may be used for events, workshops, performances, audience participation projects, or fundraisers, with costs covering things like venue rental, supplies, marketing, and creator compensation. Applicants collaborate with a nonprofit to define a project theme and demonstrate community impact.

Name: Truist Foundation Grant
Description: The Truist Foundation Grant supports U.S.-based nonprofits that create economic opportunity by building career pathways to mobility and strengthening small businesses. Grants fund sustainable, innovative initiatives — such as launching or expanding programs, developing curricula, or purchasing equipment — rather than ongoing operational expenses. Eligible applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities aligned with the foundation’s priorities, and applications are reviewed three times a year (March 31, July 31, and November 30).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Qualifying organizations meet basic criteria to be considered for charitable funding at Truist and may move forward with a grant application; however, meeting the qualifying organization criteria does not guarantee a grant will be provided.
- The following types of organizations may qualify to receive funding:
- Grants may be approved for organizations classified as 509(a)(1) or 509(a)(2) public charities under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. This includes churches (for secular, charitable programs only), educational organizations, hospitals, and publicly supported organizations.
- Organizations, as well as the intended use of funds, must align to one of the established Truist Foundation giving pillars and must not fall under the “non-qualifying” or “ineligible” categories below. Additionally, evaluation of each grant request will be based on such factors as program management and budget, sources of income population served, distinctive features and community impact.
- All organizations must be U.S.-based.
- All organizations must comply with the USA Patriot Act.

Name: Threadneedle Alley Foundation Grant
Description: Nonprofit foundation supporting midlife entrepreneurs from underserved communities with $5,000 grants plus mentorship. Aimed at people pursuing business ownership later in life who face financial barriers to starting or growing a business.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to U.S.-based midlife entrepreneurs from underserved communities who are facing financial challenges and pursuing business ownership later in life. No sector restriction stated. The application window runs October 1 through November 30, 2026, with winners announced February 15, 2027. Applications are submitted through a Google Form linked from the site. No application fee stated. The foundation provides mentorship alongside the grant. No age threshold for 'midlife' is defined on the site — worth confirming directly.

Name: Shophand $5k Small Business Boost Grant
Description: The Shophand Small Business Boost Grant provides $2,500 in no-strings-attached cash and $2,500 in Shophand technical support + services to help non-techie small business owners solve key tech or operations challenges.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To apply, you must:
 - Have fewer than 50 employees
- Generate under $5 million in annual revenue
- Be a for-profit business
- Be actively operating (not just an idea)
- Be based in the United States
- Follow Shophand on Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook.
- OPTIONAL (but preferred): Have used a “Your Shophand” service during the current application cycle
- Preference will be given to applicants who have used a “Your Shophand” service during the current application cycle.

Name: Brooklyn Org Microgrants
Description: Brooklyn Org offers one-year microgrants of up to $10,000 to small, community-based nonprofits in Brooklyn with annual budgets under $100,000, supporting organizations not yet eligible for their larger strategic grants.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible organizations 
- must be 501(c)(3) or fiscally sponsored, based in or actively working in Brooklyn, and have at least one year of operations. 

Additional Information: 
Applications are accepted on a rolling basis twice per year, with funding awarded in September and February.

Name: Entreprenista Evolve Grant
Description: The Entreprenista Evolve Grant is a quarterly $5,000 grant for women founders in the U.S. who have been in business for at least a year and are generating $100K+ in annual revenue. The grant is intended to help established women-owned businesses grow to their next level.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible: 
- Woman-owned or woman-led business in the U.S.
-Generating $100k in annual revenue 
- You've been in business for at least 1 year 
- Not a previous winner

Name: Georgia's Own Foundation
Description: Georgia’s Own Foundation offers grants primarily to local nonprofits that empower youth, with most awards typically ranging from $200 to $5,000 and at least 85% supporting youth-focused causes like education, health, housing, arts, and sports. Applications are opening in spring 2026.

Name: A Blade of Grass's Field Fund
Description: A Blade of Grass's Field Funds program distributes 50 grants of $500 each annually to U.S.-based individual artists and collaborative groups with a demonstrated history of socially engaged art. The $500 grants can support gathering costs, accessibility and translation services, and documentation and archiving expenses, with all eligible applications entered into a random selection process giving every applicant an equal chance of funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility
To be eligible to apply for this opportunity, practitioners must:
Be currently located in the United States and able to receive taxable income.
Propose a use for $500 that supports your eligible creative practice and fits the open call’s theme.
Be an individual artist or collaborative with a demonstrated history of creating socially engaged art.* (Field Funds does not accept applications from nonprofit organizations or commercial businesses.)
*Field Funds uses the terms artist and socially engaged art, but we understand that not all practitioners identify with the same language. Regardless of how they describe their work, eligible applicants will be able to show in their application that their practice:
Applies creative strategies and interventions that make society more just, kind, safe, and free.
Involves and builds relationships with communities and collaborators in meaningful ways.
Employs processes and skills beyond those used in creating studio artwork or traditional performance—including advocacy, dialogue, facilitation, organizing, and research.

Name: Mid-America Arts Alliance Catalyze Program
Description: The Catalyze Program, run by Mid-America Arts Alliance with support from the Windgate Foundation, provides $10,000 fellowships to 25 artists annually in central Arkansas and the Arkansas Delta. Open to creatives in 31 counties who have at least three years of experience and a commitment to advancing their practice, the program combines flexible, practice-based funding with professional development, one-on-one mentoring, and strategic guidance.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: ARKANSAS RESIDENTS ONLY - 52 named counties, despite M-AAA's six-state region. Counties include Pulaski, Garland, Saline, Lonoke, Faulkner, Conway, Perry, Hot Spring, Pope, Yell and Ouachita, plus 41 more. FY2027 cycle opened 10/1/2026 9:00 a.m. CT and closes 12/1/2026 5:00 p.m. CT. Retreat May 1-2, 2027. Award paid $9,500 June 2027 + $500 June 2028.

Name: Nearshored Manufacturing Grant
Description: Get Nearshored is offering three $1,000 manufacturing grants (a $3,000 total pool) to U.S.-based small businesses with under $5M in annual revenue that sell physical products and are actively looking to nearshore production to the U.S., Canada, Latin America, or Europe. Winners can use the funds toward inventory/production (including samples, materials, or packaging) and also receive introductions to vetted manufacturers, expert nearshoring guidance, and a feature on the platform.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must make under $5M in annual revenue
- Must produce a physical product 
- Actively looking to nearshore their production in the USA, Canada, Latin America or Europe.
- Must be based in the US

Name: Citizens Bank Grant Program
Description: Citizens Bank's grant program funds nonprofits in two priority areas — Workforce Development (job training, career education, and coaching) and Financial Empowerment (financial literacy, small business development, and homeownership education) — with priority given to programs serving LMI and/or BIPOC communities. The program is available to organizations in 17 states and D.C., including CA, CT, FL, MA, NJ, NY, PA, and VA among others. Workforce Development applications are due May 22, 2026, while Financial Empowerment applications are due December 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
At Citizens, we believe that when people are given the support and resources to reach their potential, we all flourish. That’s why we proudly invest our time, talent and resources to drive impact by empowering individuals to thrive, small businesses to succeed and communities to flourish.

Citizens invests in nonprofits creating measurable impact through innovative programs. Our philanthropic priorities are Workforce Development and Financial Empowerment. At Citizens, we strive to collaborate closely with high-impact nonprofit organizations and build strong partnerships that include opportunities for colleague volunteerism and joint storytelling. Citizens deeply supports the markets we serve. We welcome programmatic grant applications from organizations in the following geographic areas: CA, CT, DC, DE, FL, MA, MD, MI, NH, NJ, Metro NY, OH, PA, RI, Upstate NY, VA and VT.

Please answer the following eligibility questions to ensure your organization and/or program align with Citizens' philanthropic focus areas and priorities. If at completion of this questionnaire, your program is eligible you may choose to submit a preliminary application. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee funding.

Citizens' Grant Eligibility
Citizens focuses on two specific funding areas:

Financial Empowerment – Through our Financial Empowerment grant program, Citizens partners with nonprofits creating measurable impact through innovative programs that give people and small businesses the confidence and tools they need to budget, save, invest, be financially healthy and ultimately inspire them to pursue new and greater goals. Citizens prioritizes partnerships that provide opportunities for Citizens' colleagues to teach healthy financial practices.

Priority consideration will be given to eligible financial empowerment activities targeted to LMI and/or BIPOC communities focused on: Basic Financial Education (Adult or Youth), Entrepreneurship, Homebuyer / Homeownership Education, Small Business Development, and/or Tax Preparation (VITA).

The application deadline for Financial Empowerment applications is December 1; funding is awarded in April of the following year.

Workforce Development - We fund programs that help build the workforce of the future through job training, career education and career coaching programs. In addition, we seek opportunities for Citizens' colleagues to host mock interviews, and participate in career fairs or career panels to support our partner’s clients. Priority consideration will be given to eligible organizations that demonstrate capacity and a track record of successful workforce training programs targeted to 15–39-year-olds, low and moderate income, and/or BIPOC communities.

The application deadline for Workforce Development applications is May 22; funding is awarded in September.

Organizations must demonstrate their programs are directly and substantially focused on Financial Empowerment or Workforce Development as described above to be considered for funding.

Name: Fashion Trust U.S. Financial Grant
Description: Fashion Trust U.S. awards financial grants split among five winners across ready-to-wear, jewelry, accessories and a graduate category. Each winner also receives a year-long in-depth mentoring program covering budgeting, social media growth, strategy, digital marketing, merchandising and wholesale, plus global press exposure and access to a fashion, business and entertainment industry community. Applying is free and applicants may enter more than once.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business must be in operation 2-7 years
- Business must be BASED AND REGISTERED IN THE U.S.
- U.S. citizens AND non-citizens are both welcome to apply
- Applicants may apply multiple times

CATEGORIES: Ready-to-Wear; Jewelry (fine or fashion); Accessories (hats, shoes, bags, gloves, socks, scarves, belts); Graduate Award.
GRADUATE AWARD is a separate track for those who completed their programs in 2024, 2025 or 2026 - the 2-7 year operating requirement does not fit this category the same way.
