WINNERS RECEIVE: a share of the financial grant funding (distributed among five winners), a one-year in-depth mentoring program covering budgeting, social media growth, strategy, digital marketing, merchandising and wholesale, global press exposure in top publications, and access to the fashion/business/entertainment industry community. A Sustainability Award additionally recognises a finalist with strong sustainable practices.

Free to apply. Deadline December 1.

Name: 2027 National Small Business Week Awards
Description: The SBA's annual awards program recognizing America's small business owners, run alongside National Small Business Week, which will be celebrated May 2-8, 2027. Winners receive an invitation to a two-day event in Washington, D.C. with networking and educational sessions, a trophy, features across SBA social media and web properties reaching more than 1 million small business owners, a media opportunities kit, and a digital badge for websites and email signatures. District-level winners may also be honored at local ceremonies.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nominations close at 3:00 PM ET on December 7, 2026, submitted at SBA.gov/nsbw. SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS MAY NOMINATE THEMSELVES, or be nominated by a third party. 2027 categories per the SBA's October 2026 announcement: State Small Business Person of the Year (one from each state, D.C., Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam), National Small Business Person of the Year (the agency's highest honor), Small Business Manufacturer of the Year, Exporter of the Year, Blue Collar Small Business of the Year, Rural Small Business of the Year, Veteran Small Business of the Year, Phoenix Award for Small Business Disaster Recovery, and Phoenix Award for Small Business Disaster Recovery - Mitigation. All nominees are subject to background checks, and adverse findings may cause disqualification. Detailed per-category eligibility lives on separate SBA pages. Award recipients are recognized at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. during National Small Business Week, May 2-8, 2027. No nomination fee. Questions: smallbusinessweek@sba.gov.

Name: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready $10,000 National Grant
Description: The Verizon Small Business Digital Ready Grant offers $10,000 awards to 10 small businesses each month from June through December 2026. To apply, eligible U.S.-based for-profit business owners must complete two courses or events on the platform. Once submitted, the application remains eligible for future monthly selections throughout 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply for the Verizon Small Business Digital Ready $10,000 national grant, you must meet the below criteria:

- Have an account on Verizon Small Business Digital Ready. 
- Complete any combination of two courses, virtual events (including recorded events), or in-person events* on the Digital Ready platform anytime in 2026 to unlock the grant application. Once unlocked, you can apply once at any time to be considered as finalists are selected monthly throughout the year.
- Be a for-profit business based in the U.S., Puerto Rico, or the U.S. Virgin Islands. Nonprofits are not eligible to apply. 
- Be 18 years of age or older.
- Be able to share and provide proper business and financial verification documentation (W-9s, ACH) if selected as a finalist.
- Eligibility is based on accurate and complete submission of the grant application.

Current directors, officers, employees and contractors of LISC or Verizon and such individuals' family members (spouse, parents, children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and spouses of children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren) may not be eligible to receive an award. Priority is given to applicants who have not received a prior grant; prior Digital Ready grant recipients are still eligible to apply but not likely to be awarded a second grant.

*Only in-person events listed on the In-Person Events page are eligible. To receive credit, you must scan the event’s QR code while onsite. For details on how credit is awarded, please refer to the specific event page.

Name: EforAll Business Accelerator Program
Description: The EforAll Business Accelerator Program is a free, 12-week online program designed to help aspiring entrepreneurs turn their ideas into successful businesses. It offers hands-on business training, mentorship from experienced professionals, and peer support teams for collaboration and accountability. Participants gain access to online resources, office hours, and a final showcase event, empowering them to build critical skills, confidence, and real momentum for business growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Whether you’re at the idea stage, have a side hustle, or have already started your business or nonprofit, this program is for you. We support entrepreneurs from all backgrounds and industries. Must be 18+ years old and living in the U.S.

Name: Teiger Foundation Hosting Grant
Description: The Teiger Foundation's Hosting Grant awards up to $75,000 to US-based curators or artistic directors who are presenting and meaningfully adapting a contemporary visual art exhibition or project that originated at another institution. Applications are accepted four times a year, and awarded organizations may only receive one hosting grant per calendar year. Projects must already exist before being hosted, and proposals that present exhibitions without curatorial adaptation or collaboration are not competitive.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This grant category supports host curators who actively adapt existing exhibitions. Adaptations might include developing new public programs, collaborating with local partners, and/ or supplementing or otherwise modifying the exhibition checklist, layout, and/ or interpretive materials. Projects presented exactly as at the originating institution, without curatorial engagement or meaningful collaboration, are not competitive.

Projects must be pre-existing to be eligible. Eligible projects include exhibitions and performances grounded in contemporary visual art. We welcome experimental formats, please feel free to propose new approaches.

Name: Columbus Arts Festival 2027 Artist & Vendor Application
Description: Outdoor fine-art festival on the downtown Columbus riverfront, produced by the Greater Columbus Arts Council and free to the public. Hosts roughly 230-250 exhibiting visual artists across 16 media categories plus performance stages and food vendors. Applications are open for artists, emerging festival artists, musicians, performers, spoken word artists, and food vendors.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
PAID BOOTH APPLICATION — not a grant. Juried; open nationally to visual artists across 16 media categories. Up to 10 applications per applicant. Requires 5 images including a mandatory booth shot. $40 non-refundable jury fee to apply, plus a booth fee if accepted (2027 booth amounts are not published on the ZAPP listing). One grant-adjacent component exists: GCAC runs an Emerging Festival Artist Program supporting Central Ohio artists with little or no festival experience — whether that program waives the booth fee or pays a stipend could not be confirmed. Festival site (blocks automated access but loads in a browser): columbusartsfestival.org/apply/visual-artists.

Details from Columbus Art Fest: https://www.instagram.com/p/DdCNb5kICYE/?hl=en
Application Fee: $40 jury fee (non-refundable); booth fee additional, not published

Name: California Underserved and Small Producer Program (CUSP)
Description: CDFA's CUSP program delivers drought and extreme-weather relief payments to small-scale and socially disadvantaged California farmers and ranchers through regional administering partners. Producers can receive up to $20,000 in drought relief plus up to $20,000 in extreme-weather relief within a 12-month period. Application windows are staggered by provider; the CCOF Foundation window runs through December 11, 2026.
Amount: Up to $20,000 drought + up to $20,000 extreme weather (max $40,000 per 12 months)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: CCOF Foundation application: https://www.ccof.org/foundation/grants-education/hardship-assistance-fund/ - CA agricultural producers with gross annual revenue up to $400,000 (dairy up to $1,000,000); socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers prioritized. Windows vary by administering provider: CCOF rolling 1/5/2026-12/11/2026; CAFF 9/1-9/21/2026 and 4/1-4/30/2027; Inland Empire RCD 2/1-6/30/2026.

Name: Decoy Pour to What's Possible Grant Program
Description: The Decoy Pour to What’s Possible Grant will award one emerging creative $10,000 to support a creative project, continuing education, or career development in fields such as film, television, music, theater, and fine arts. Applicants must be U.S. residents age 25 or older working in or pursuing a creative career; residents of CO, MA, MD, NH, NJ, and PA are excluded. Applications are due December 15, 2026, and require creative work samples, a résumé/CV, a professional biography, and a 500–1,000-word response outlining career goals and how the funds would be used.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The grant is open to individuals working in or pursuing a career in a creative role in a creative industry, including but not limited to television, film, music, theater, and fine arts.

ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS MUST:
Be age 25 or older at the time of submission
Be a legal resident of the United States, excluding Massachusetts and jurisdictions where the Program is prohibited or restricted
Reside in the United States both when applying and when the award is distributed
Be currently working in or pursuing a career in a creative role in a creative industry

Name: Rooted Farmers Grants & Scholarships
Description: Rooted Farmers offers three programs to strengthen local agricultural systems: Community Roots provides $500–$1,500 for U.S. farms with 3+ years of experience and community food access projects; Growing Roots provides $500–$2,000 for U.S. producer hubs with 4+ producers; and Deepening Roots offers need-based fee forgiveness up to 90% for established hubs in year 3+ with 5+ producers and $250k+ in annual sales. The two grant programs also include a free year of Rooted Farmers Pro and bi-monthly coaching. The Deepening Roots scholarship is rolling year-round and includes platform support, grower discounts, onboarding, and coaching for at least one year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All three programs require a U.S. base; no state or region restriction. COMMUNITY ROOTS: FARM GRANT ($500-$1,500) — 3+ years of experience owning or running farming operations, and the proposed project must benefit 3+ farms. GROWING ROOTS: HUB STARTUP GRANT ($500-$2,000) — hubs of 4+ producers, with at least half of member farms having 3+ years of growing or production experience. DEEPENING ROOTS: HUB SCHOLARSHIP (fee forgiveness, no cash) — hubs in year 3+ of operations, 5+ producers, annual sales volume of $250,000 or more, and new to using Rooted Farmers. Community Roots and Growing Roots close December 15, 2026; Deepening Roots is rolling. Applications go by email using per-program Request for Applications documents and Terms and Conditions agreements linked from the page. No application fee stated. Contact: reachout@rootedfarmers.com.

Name: Oneness Revival Team NGO Grant
Description: The Oneness Revival Team (ORT) offers two types of annual grants — a SEED Grant for first-time ORT applicants and a THRIVE Grant for previously funded organizations — both awarding $25,000 to $50,000 to registered nonprofits worldwide with annual operating budgets under $50,000. Funds can be used for project launches, capacity building, programmatic activities, or expanding successful programs that have demonstrated impact. The application deadline is December 20, 2026 at 5:00pm local time.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Oneness Revival Team NGO Grant Application 2026
The Oneness Revival Team (ORT) is thrilled to announce its 4rd annual grant cycle for 2026, designed to support NGOs making a meaningful impact in their communities. We welcome applications from non-governmental organizations (NGOs) with annual budgets under $100,000 USD from any region worldwide. This grant cycle aims to empower grassroots initiatives, drive sustainable development, and strengthen the capacity of NGOs working towards positive social, economic, and environmental change.

📅 Application Deadline: December 20, 2026, at 5:00 PM (local time)

ORT offers two types of grants to cater to both new and previously funded NGOs:

1. SEED Grant (1-Year)
The SEED Grant is a one-year general support or project grant designed for:
✔️ NGOs that have never received funding from ORT before.
✔️ NGOs that prefer to apply for the SEED Grant rather than the THRIVE Grant.

📌 Grant Amount: $25,000 – $50,000 USD per year

This funding can be used to:

Launch or scale a new project that aligns with ORT’s mission.
Strengthen organizational capacity and enhance operational effectiveness.
Support programmatic activities, advocacy efforts, or community outreach.


2. THRIVE Grant (1-Year)
The THRIVE Grant is a one-year general support grant, exclusively available to:
✔️ NGOs that have been previously funded by ORT and are in good standing.
✔️ Organizations looking to expand or sustain ongoing projects with ORT’s continued support.

📌 Grant Amount: $25,000 – $50,000 USD per year

This funding is intended to:

Expand successful programs that have demonstrated impact.
Strengthen long-term sustainability and enhance operational effectiveness.
Support strategic initiatives that drive transformational change in communities.
Eligibility Criteria
To apply for either grant, NGOs must:
✔️ Be a registered non-profit organization in their respective country.
✔️ Have an annual operating budget under $50,000 USD.
✔️ Demonstrate a clear mission, objectives, and measurable impact.
✔️ Have transparency in financial management and accountability practices.
✔️ Submit a detailed proposal, including a project plan, budget, and expected outcomes.

How to Apply
Interested NGOs must submit their application online through the ORT portal before the deadline. The application should include:
✅ A completed grant application form.
✅ A detailed project proposal outlining goals, activities, and expected impact.
✅ A budget breakdown of how the funds will be utilized.
✅ Proof of non-profit registration and legal status.
✅ A list of key team members and organizational structure.

📌 Email: info@onenessrevivalteam.info
📌 Submission Deadline: December 20, 2026, at 5:00 PM

Name: National Association for the Self-Employed Growth Grant
Description: Offers up to $4,000 in small business grants for National Association for the Self-Employed (NASE) members. Grants are awarded year-round, with completed applications reviewed quarterly in January, April, July and October.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, you must be a NASE member in good standing.

The following members may apply immediately:
- Annual Members
- Veteran Members
- Silver Members (Paying Annually)
- Gold Members

The following members may apply after 90 days of membership:
- Monthly Members
- Silver Members (Paying Monthly)

Name: Secretsos™ Small Business Grant
Description: Awards $2,500 grants quarterly to small businesses, with a focus on entrepreneurs often overlooked by traditional investors; funds can be used flexibly for growth and operations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: As long as you are 21 years or older and have an active business that operates in the eligible states and territories of the United States – you are eligible to apply. (Businesses with a primary physical location in Alaska, Florida, Hawaii, New York, and Rhode Island are not eligible.)

Name: Spectrum Reach Pay It Forward
Description: In-kind advertising and marketing resources for small businesses (including an original 30-second commercial, free traditional TV And streaming advertising, local marketing expert support) through Spectrum Reach's Pay It Forward initiative.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in eligible Spectrum markets.

Name: Outta Excuses Small Business Grant
Description: The Outta Excuses Grant Initiative awards small business owners and 501(c)(3) nonprofits $3,000 each quarter (plus a $10,000 annual grant) to help them start, structure, brand, scale, or fund their ventures without burnout.

Name: ELEVATED Cities Business Development Program
Description: ELEVATED Cities is Our Village United’s 12-week virtual business development program for entrepreneurs who’ve already made progress and want structured guidance, proven growth strategies, and a supportive network to scale with intention and impact. The program offers training, tools/resources, community connections, and a pathway to a competitive pitch competition where some businesses can win $10,000–$15,000 in grant funding. Target cities include Chicago, St. Louis, Milwaukee, Detroit, Columbus, Indianapolis, and Minneapolis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Growth-stage entrepreneurs
- Revenue under $100k
- Already operating with paying customers
- Entrepreneurs past the idea stage

Name: Impact Funding Solutions IMPACT Grants
Description: Impact Funding Solutions offers quarterly IMPACT Grants of $1,000 to help businesses and nonprofits fund community-impact work, with an online application portal and a review process that selects one business and one nonprofit recipient each quarter. Eligible business applicants include sole proprietors, small businesses/startups, and social enterprises in the U.S. or Canada, with winners announced on the 15th of the month after the quarter.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We invite business owners in Canada and the USA to apply for an IMPACT Grant if you meet the following criteria:
- Sole Proprietors: Entrepreneurs running a one-person show with a clear vision for making a difference.
- Small Business Owners: If you operate a small business or startup.
- Social Enterprises: If your venture falls under the umbrella of social enterprise

Name: California Fire Foundation Wildfire Disaster Relief & Recovery Grant
Description: The California Fire Foundation has an open Disaster Relief & Recovery grant for California-based fire departments, firefighter associations, tribes, and nonprofits running wildfire relief and long-term recovery projects in Los Angeles and Ventura counties. Grants typically range from $25,000–$100,000 for projects like community recovery/outreach, recovery planning and education, first responder training, equipment (including PPE), and vegetation/fuels reduction, with quarterly reviews and funding based on the submission window.

Name: FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust Grant
Description: The FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust awards grants to 501(c)(3) nonprofits primarily in Florida, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, and South Carolina. The Trust’s areas of interest are: arts and culture; community, housing and social services; education; historic preservation; medical programs; and scientific research.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Application Guidelines
The website portal is only open during these two four-month application cycles. The entire process (from initial registration to final approval) can take up to six months. Your submitted contact information on our website must be kept up to date throughout the entire process in order for you to receive communications from us on a timely basis regarding your application, including mailings of approved award checks. We must have the current contact person’s name, email address and an up-to-date mailing address in order to mail grant award checks and pertinent documents should your application be approved. It is your responsibility to keep our website updated with this information throughout the application process.

REQUESTS FOR GRANTS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED BY MAIL OR EMAIL. YOU MUST APPLY ONLINE.

THE ONLINE APPLICATION PROCESS INVOLVES THE FOLLOWING THREE STEPS:

1. REGISTRATION
If your organization has previously applied to be considered for a grant, you are already registered. Submit your new “Letter of Intent” when the portal is open using your existing credentials. In the event of a forgotten password, please follow the “Forgot Password” prompts to reset your password.

If your organization has not previously applied, the application process begins with an applicant registering their organization on our website during one of the four-month application periods indicated above. We recommend that the supplied organization name be identical to your 501(c)(3) filing. Upon successful registration, an automated “Welcome” email will be sent. If you do not receive the “Welcome” email, please email kelly@fjbrothertoncharitabletrust.org for assistance.

2. LETTER OF INTENT
A “Letter of Intent” should then be submitted, which will be reviewed by the Trustee. This is a brief overview of your proposal to help the Trustee quickly decide if the grant request meets the Trust’s charter and criteria. Applicants will be notified by email within 2-3 weeks regarding acceptance or denial. If accepted, the applicant will move on to the full grant application. If you do not hear back from us within 2-3 weeks after submitting an LOI, please email kelly@fjbrothertoncharitabletrust.org for assistance.

3. GRANT APPLICATION
If the Letter of Intent is accepted, the Applicant will complete and submit a full grant application before the application period deadline (either December 31 or June 30 depending on the current application period). Please note: all uploaded documents on the website during the application process must have filenames with only alpha/numeric characters. No special characters are allowed (e.g., periods, commas, dashes, underscores, asterisks, etc.).

Final decisions are made approximately two months after each grant application cycle deadline at the next semi-annual Advisory Board meeting. Advisory Board meetings are held in February and August, after which all approved grant distributions are processed. You will be advised by email of either approval or denial after the Advisory Board meets. It is imperative that you keep all of your contact information on our website up-to-date throughout the entire application process, which could be up to six months depending on your date of submission, in order to receive communications regarding your application.

If your grant application is approved, Progress Reports for all approved grants are due every six months after receiving a grant award and should be submitted through the online grant portal. Further guidelines regarding submission of Progress Reports for all approved grants will be sent with the grant award check.

PLEASE NOTE: The Trust receives many grant requests during each application cycle. It is highly recommended that you apply early in the four-month application cycle as grant requests submitted late in the cycle may not allow enough time for completion of the three-step online application process outlined above. If the entire three-step process is not completed before the deadline date, the grant application will expire.

Grant Restrictions
Foreign limitations: The FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust is legally restricted from contributing, in any manner, grant funds which would be utilized outside of the United States or its possessions. It does not fund non-United States-based charitable organizations nor the work of United States based organizations abroad.

United States limitations: The primary geographic areas of funding include the following states: Florida, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, and South Carolina. Exceptions to the geographic guidelines are granted only when the Trustee or an Advisory Board Member has personal knowledge of an organization which otherwise conforms to the Trust’s guidelines.

The FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust does NOT approve grant requests to organizations lacking tax exempt status under I.R.C. Section 501(c)(3).

Further, as a matter of general practice, The FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust does NOT normally approve grant requests falling into the following categories:

Legal aid programs
Loans
Moving expenses
Public opinion polls, surveys and research studies
Public policy and/or advocacy groups
Deficit financing
Grants to individuals
The FJ Brotherton Charitable Trust requires that prior grantees wait at least 18 months from their grant award date before applying for additional funding.

Name: Downtown Raleigh Storefront Upfit Grant
Description: Raleigh Civic Ventures, supported by the Downtown Raleigh Alliance and funded by the Duke Energy Foundation, offers up to $10,000 toward interior and storefront build-out for new and expanding ground-floor businesses in designated downtown Raleigh storefront areas. A $2,500 booster is available to businesses with majority diverse ownership. Interest forms are accepted on a rolling basis against a $50,000 pool.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: New retail, restaurant, service and experiential businesses; existing retail expanding floor area by 30% or more; pop-ups with a minimum three-month lease. Must be in a designated downtown Raleigh storefront area. Professional offices and bars are ineligible. Up to $10,000 in priority areas, up to $5,000 elsewhere, plus a $2,500 booster for businesses 50%+ owned by minorities, women, LGBTQ+ people, veterans or people with disabilities. Current pool $50,000 (Duke Energy Foundation). Interest forms accepted on a rolling basis: https://downtownraleigh.org/upfit-grant-interest . Next stated application deadline 1 January 2027, tentative and contingent on funding.

Name: The Baltimore Farmers' Market 2027 (Vendor Application)
Description: Large Sunday-morning outdoor market running most of the year under the Jones Falls Expressway in downtown Baltimore, produced and managed by Create Baltimore, a nonprofit. The 2027 season runs April 4 through December 19, 2027, Sundays 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM, excluding May 30 (Artscape conflict). Vendor slots are available in artisan, farm, food, and alcohol categories.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: PAID BOOTH APPLICATION — no grant, stipend, or free booth component. Free to apply for all vendor categories, but accepted vendors pay meaningful seasonal fees: Artisans $1,400 full season, $467 per trimester, or $50 per occasional single Sunday; Alcohol vendors $1,500 per 10'x10' space (max 2); Farm vendors $500 per 10'x10' space (max 6); Food vendors $1,600-$2,500 per 10'x10' space depending on type (max 4). A 5% discount applies for paying the full season by April 4, 2027. Applicant must be the business owner, in good standing with the health department, and hold all required permits and licenses. Applications close Friday, January 8, 2027.

Name: Braze Tech for an Equitable Future
Description: Product grant program from Braze, running since 2020, supporting underestimated founders with free access to its customer engagement platform. Recipients receive 12 months of the Braze Go package free — unlimited push notifications, in-app and browser messaging for up to 75,000 monthly active users, and 500K message credits — plus 6 weeks of onboarding services, a dedicated Customer Success Manager for year one, free Braze certifications, and eligibility for discounted renewal rates.
Amount: 12 months free Braze Go package + onboarding and support (in-kind; ~$26,500 product value per prior cycle)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit startups only — not nonprofits. Aimed at founders with limited access to traditional growth capital. Must be bootstrapped or have raised less than $30 million in venture funding, and have under 100 employees. Must have a compatible SDK plus the engineering and marketing resources to implement and run the platform. Geographic focus: APAC, EMEA, and North America. Current cycle runs September 28, 2026 through January 15, 2027. Applicants complete a brief inquiry form first, then receive access to the full application, which takes roughly 30 minutes. No application fee stated.

Name: Her Agenda Breakthrough Grant
Description: The Breakthrough Grant is a $5,000 grant created by Her Agenda to support women entrepreneurs seeking resources to grow and overcome barriers in their businesses. Open to entrepreneurs with an operating business who are subscribed to the Her Agenda newsletter.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must:
- Be entrepreneurs with an operating business.
- Be subscribed to the Her Agenda newsletter (a requirement for eligibility).

Name: HBO Short Film Award (American Black Film Festival)
Description: One of the longest-running short film competitions for Black filmmakers, presented by HBO in partnership with the American Black Film Festival and produced by NICE CROWD. The award is Oscar-qualifying: the winner becomes eligible for consideration in the Live Action Short Film category at the 100th Academy Awards. Five finalists are selected to screen at the festival, with one grand prize winner. ABFF's 31st edition runs May 20-23, 2027 in Los Angeles.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Films must run a maximum of 20 minutes including credits. The director must be 18 or older. Entrants must be of African descent and the work should reflect themes and narratives connected to the African diaspora. U.S. and international entries accepted; English language or English subtitles required. Post-production must have been completed on or after January 1, 2026. No prior broadcast, cable, or online exhibition — any current or previous public exhibition disqualifies. Must be a first-time submission to this award; previous finalists are ineligible. HBO and NICE CROWD employees and affiliates are ineligible, as are filmmakers with current HBO projects. The Los Angeles premiere requirement that binds ABFF's other categories is waived for this category. Two fee tiers: early deadline October 1, 2026 at $30, final deadline January 24, 2027 at 11:59 PM PST at $75 — submitting by October 1 more than halves the fee. Fees are per film. Notification April 9, 2027.
Application Fee: $30 early (by 10/1/26) / $75 final; $22.50 / $67.50 for ABFF Gold Members

Name: Fund for Investigative Journalism
Description: The Fund for Investigative Journalism offers grants to freelance journalists, staff reporters, and media outlets for impactful, nonpartisan investigative reporting across formats like print, broadcast, books, documentaries, and podcasts. Funding ranges from up to $2,500 for seed or follow-up reporting, up to $10,000 for regular grants, and up to $40,000 for Alicia Patterson Fellowships, with the next regular and seed grant deadline on April 27, 2026.

Name: Tampa Entrepreneur Microgrants
Description: The City of Tampa's Entrepreneur Support Hub offers three microgrants to low- and moderate-income microenterprises inside city limits. BASE provides up to fifteen hundred dollars to businesses operating under twelve months, STEP up to three thousand dollars to businesses operating twelve months or longer, and SCALE covers an owner's down payment contribution toward a commercial microloan. Applicants must first complete technical assistance and obtain a referral form.
Amount: BASE up to $1,500; STEP up to $3,000; SCALE up to $10,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Microenterprise with five or fewer full-time-equivalent employees including owners
- Business must operate within Tampa city limits
- Owner household income at or below 80% Area Median Income (approx $83,000 for a family of four), OR business serves an LMI neighborhood where 51%+ of residents qualify
- BASE: in operation under 12 months. STEP: in operation 12+ months, business plan required
- SCALE: covers up to 20% of a business loan, max $10,000 citywide or $15,000 under the Fresh Food Initiative
- Must complete required technical assistance and obtain a Microgrant Referral Form first

DEADLINE CORRECTION: the city's page states twice that all referrals must be submitted by 2/15/2027. The 9/15/2026 date circulating elsewhere is not supported by any city source.

Name: Chicago Community Development Grants (CDG)
Description: A tiered grant program by the City of Chicago to support business- and community-development projects via new construction or rehabilitation of commercial, mixed-use, institutional, cultural or industrial uses. Grants are available at small, medium and large levels depending on project scope.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible applicants include business owners, property owners, non-profits and community developers; projects must be revenue-generating (commercial, office, retail, mixed-use, light industrial) and located within City of Chicago; funding is reimbursement-based up to 75% of eligible expenses; project must demonstrate community benefit / job creation.

Name: Artists and Creatives Grants
Description: The Community Engagement Artists and Creatives Grant awards between $500 and $2,500 to independent artists and collectives creating new, community-engaged work, with a spring deadline of March 15 and a fall deadline of September 15. The spring cycle is open to artists anywhere in the US, while the fall cycle is limited to California-based artists. Nonprofits, student projects, arts festivals, and religiously affiliated activities are not eligible, and previous grantees must wait two years before reapplying.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Our fall grants (deadline September) are open to artists living or working in California. Our spring grants (deadline March) are open to artists living or working anywhere in the US.  

This grant funds community engaged art. We provide grants to independent creatives (including collectives and collaborators) needing support for producing and/or presenting artistic projects relating to or engaging a community.

Building collaborative connections.  The grant is intended to fund the execution of community-engaged projects. Please review our mission statement to understand how we define community engagement. 

This is a project-based grant. Our grant funds artistically-excellent community engaged projects that  present new and imaginative possibilities. We prioritize funding the creation of new artworks and are not likely to fund art classes, take-home art kits, or exhibitions of studio artwork in preexisting galleries unless the proposal centers a clear and purposeful collaboration with a community.

Grants are usually limited to $500 - 2,500, but in rare circumstances we may provide funding up to $5,000. We suggest that most artists apply for funding under $2,500 unless advised otherwise.

This grant supports individual artists and/or artist collectives. The following are not supported by this grant: arts festivals; nonprofit and for-profit organizations; student projects (undergraduate or graduate); residencies; research symposia; studio rent; conferences; theaters; festivals; activity affiliated with religious organizations of any kind.

Successful grantees are eligible to reapply every two years. Successful applicants to this grant should wait at least two years before reapplying for funding.

This grant encourages applications from artists who have historically been underrepresented. Although this grant is open to all artists, we especially encourage applications from those who have been historically underrepresented in the arts. This includes, but is not limited to, artists who are Black, Indigenous, People of Color, Queer, Trans, Deaf, Disabled, Immigrant or Refugee, or Self-Taught.

Name: Grassroots Fund Grow Grants
Description: Grassroots Fund Grow Grants provide $1,000–$4,000 to established, volunteer-driven grassroots groups in six New England states (CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT) to sustain or expand their community-based work. Eligible groups must have at least three active organizers, an annual budget generally under $100,000 (up to $150,000 in some cases), and focus on local initiatives; formal nonprofit status is not required. Applications are due the third Tuesday of March and September, with funding decisions announced in late June and early January.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We only fund:
- Groups doing local, grassroots work in Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Vermont.
- Groups who have 3 or more organizers actively involved in decision-making on project priorities and actions.
- Note that groups do NOT need to have formal tax status or a fiscal sponsor.  A group only needs a bank account in the group's name (see FAQs below to learn how to set that up).

We don't fund:
- Individuals.
- Groups who spent more than $150,000 last calendar year.
- For profits requesting funds to cover business expenses.
- National or international work.
- Lobbying or partisan political activity.
- Acquisition of land and/or buildings.
- Studies with no follow-up action.
- Publication of books or reports.
- Micro-, mini-, re-granting programs.
- Retroactive (pre-dating application submission) expenses.

Name: Pennsylvania Small Business Advantage Grant
Description: Pennsylvania DEP's Small Business Ombudsman's Office awards $7,500 to $12,000 to Pennsylvania small businesses for projects that cut energy use, pollution or waste - lighting, HVAC, boiler and equipment upgrades, process improvements and stormwater runoff reduction. The FY2026-27 round opened 11 September 2026 and runs until 19 March 2027 or until funds are exhausted. Award size scales with environmental impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Pennsylvania-based businesses with 100 or fewer full-time employees. Project must produce at least $500 and at least 20% annual savings in energy or pollution-prevention costs. FY2026-27 round opened 11 Sept 2026, closes 19 March 2027 or when funds are exhausted, whichever is first. Applications are submitted through DCED's Single Application for Assistance: https://www.esa.dced.state.pa.us/login.aspx . Contact ra-epadvantagegrant@pa.gov or 717-783-9640.

Name: Alaska Micro Enterprise Grant
Description: The Alaska Mental Health Trust Authority funds this grant, administered by the UAA Center for Human Development, to help Trust beneficiaries start, expand or acquire a micro enterprise. Allowable costs include business licenses, insurance, permits, inventory, raw materials, equipment, supplies, and rent or lease of space. A micro enterprise is defined as a business with capital needs under thirty-five thousand dollars and fewer than five employees.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicant must be an Alaska Mental Health Trust beneficiary
- Business must qualify as a micro enterprise: capital needs under $35,000 and fewer than five employees
- Must attend an orientation session and submit eligibility documentation before the online application unlocks
- Request $500 - $12,000; $12,000 lifetime cap per person

TIMING WARNING: fall deadline is 9/16/2026 at 12 p.m., but both required fall orientations (8/5/2026 and 8/19/2026) have already passed, which may make this cycle unreachable for new applicants. Next cycle deadline 3/24/2027.

Name: General Brooklyn Org Funding
Description: Brooklyn Org offers multi-year general operating support of up to $45,000 per year for up to three years to 501(c)(3) nonprofits or fiscally sponsored organizations that advance racial justice and serve communities across Brooklyn. Eligible organizations must have a minimum annual budget of $100,000, maintain a physical presence in Brooklyn, and grants will not exceed 20% of the applying organization's annual budget.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Be incorporated as a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization or be working under the auspices of an authorized fiscal sponsor
- Have a minimum annual budget of $100,000.
- Have a regular physical presence in Brooklyn. All non-Brooklyn-based organizations must apply for support for their relevant Brooklyn-based work

Name: City of Rockville Business Grants
Description: The City of Rockville offers three business grant programs through REDI: the MOVE Program (up to $40,000 for new businesses relocating into Rockville), the Business Expansion Fund (up to $40,000 for existing Rockville businesses expanding to a larger space), and the Small Business Impact Fund (for established businesses with 3+ years of operation seeking to scale through specific projects like marketing, signage, or equipment upgrades). All three programs require a pre-application meeting with REDI staff and have application deadlines of April 30 and September 30 each year. The page also outlines additional county and state funding programs available to Maryland businesses, ranging from workforce training grants to venture capital investments.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The City of Rockville business grant application period is now open! These grants are designed to help businesses within the City grow and thrive.⁠
⁠
📦 Rockville MOVE Grant: for startups moving into their first commercial space OR existing businesses relocating to Rockville⁠
⁠
↔️ Business Expansion Fund: for Rockville businesses ready to scale into additional or larger space⁠
⁠
🌱 Small Business Impact Fund: financial assistance for small- and medium-sized businesses to scale through projects that strengthen business development and sustain growth⁠




MOVE Eligibility: 
• The business must be relocating or expanding from outside the corporate limits of the City of Rockville, or a business moving into their first commercial space.
• The business must sign a lease and remain within the City for a minimum of
three years or purchase a property within City limits.
• This program supports Class A & B office and industrial space and is properties categorized as retail and flex.
• Leased or purchased space must be greater than or equal to 1,000 square feet for office, industrial, or flex and greater than or equal to 500 square feet for retail.
• Business must be in good standing with the city, county, state, and landlord.
• Applicants can operate in any industry sector. Franchises and chains will be
considered on a case-by-case basis.
• This is a one-time grant, and the maximum award is $40,000. Amounts are
based on the availability of funds. 


Expansion Eligibility: 
The business must currently reside within the City of Rockville corporate limits.
• The expansion lease or purchased space must be greater than or equal to 1,000 square feet for office, industrial, or flex and greater than or equal to 500 square feet for retail.
• This program supports Class A & B office and industrial space and properties categorized as retail and flex.
• Funds can be used for the build-out process or the purchase of furniture.
• The business must sign a lease and remain within the City for a minimum of three years.
• Business must be in good standing with the city, county, state, and landlord.
• Applicants can operate in any industry sector. Franchises and chains will be
considered on a case-by-case basis.
• This is a one-time grant, and the maximum award is $40,000. Amounts are based on the availability of funds. 



SBIF Eligibility: 
• Be an active business located within the City limits of Rockville, having been in operation for a minimum of three years.
• Identify a project or projects to scale the business.
• Demonstrate how the business contributes to the public by creating or retaining jobs for traditionally under-employed populations, fostering a positive social impact by partnering with local nonprofits and creating or providing key business uses and services for local residents.
• Applicants can operate in any industry sector. Franchises and chains will be
considered on a case-by-case basis.
• Business must be in a leased, coworking, or owned space within the City of
Rockville limits. REDI Incentive Review Process 4
• The company must be in good standing with the city, county, and state.
• Business must be in good standing with the city, county, state, and landlord.
• Businesses must remain in the City for a minimum of one year. Amounts are
based on the availability of funds.

Name: Etsy Emergency Relief Fund
Description: Offers quarterly grants to Etsy sellers impacted by federally declared disasters within the past year. Applicants must have had an active Etsy seller account for at least one year and be in good standing with Etsy.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
All Etsy sellers are eligible for a grant if they have experienced a federally declared natural disaster within the past year, have been an active seller on Etsy for at least one year, and their accounts with Etsy are in good standing. 

More details about eligibility:
1. Experiencing a disaster means that you have suffered a federally declared natural disaster that fits the following definition, and your business is located in the disaster area:
- A “natural disaster” is a recent, unforeseen natural event that has significantly and adversely affected a seller’s ability to produce and/or market their work, that has created an immediate need for relief funds and/or assistance.

2. At least one year on Etsy means that you have had an active seller account on Etsy for at least one year.

3. Having an account in good standing means that you have a record of good customer service (as determined by Etsy), and you are not in violation of Etsy’s Seller Policy, Intellectual Property Policy, or any other policies.

Name: Small Business Readiness for Resiliency grant
Description: Helps small businesses prepare for disasters through planning resources and support. Eligible businesses impacted by a federally declared disaster can apply for $5,000 in quick-turn relief funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to receive a grant from the Small Business Readiness for Resiliency Program, a business must meet the following criteria.  
- Have fewer than 500 employees 
- Complete the Emergency Preparedness Checklist for Small Businesses
Have at least one physical or online business location within the United States or its territories (Puerto Rico, Guam, Northern Marianas, U.S. Virgin Islands, America Samoa)  
- Have a valid employee identification number (EIN); a social security number cannot be used for this program  
- Not be part of a franchise brand with more than 25 corporate-owned stores, or more than 250 stores in total  
- Not be in an ineligible business category (as defined in the Terms and Conditions)
- Have its principal physical location in a county that receives a major disaster declaration and qualifies for Individual Assistance  
- Have been financially harmed by a disaster and incur an uncovered loss  
Incur applicable disaster-related damages or losses that equal or exceed $5,000  
- Agree to all the Grant Program Rules
- More information on eligibility and process can be found here: https://www.uschamberfoundation.org/disasters/small-business-readiness-for-resiliency-program-faqs

Name: Book Industry Charitable (Binc) Foundation Grant
Description: Helps bookstore owners, booksellers, and comic store employees and owners with unforeseen emergency financial needs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a regular full- or part-time bookseller or comic employee/owner at a brick-and-mortar, mobile, or pop-up, bookstore or comic shop in the United States, Puerto Rico, The U.S. Virgin Islands, or Guam
- Must have been employed for a minimum of 90 days OR an employee of a bookstore or comic store closed within the past 6 months (employee must have a minimum of 12 months tenure)
- OR were employed by Borders Group in the year 2011
- OR are the immediate family member of a deceased bookseller
- AND are experiencing an unforeseen financial hardship resulting from a specific, qualifying life event.

Name: Josephine Collective
Description: The Josephine Collective is a women-led group of angel investors providing early-stage angel investment for tech-enabled, for-profit businesses based in the U.S. Founders can apply anytime, with a streamlined process aiming for a 3-week turnaround from pitch to funding. Investments range from $10K–$100K based on collective interest.

Name: Power Forward Small Business Grant
Description: Grants for Black-owned small businesses (1–25 employees) based in MA, ME, NH, RI, VT, or parts of CT. Recipients also receive marketing support and national visibility through the Boston Celtics, Vistaprint, and NAACP partnership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Qualified applicants must be Black-owned small businesses with 1 to 25 employees and be based and operating in Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Vermont, or select areas of Connecticut*. Applicants should be able to demonstrate the impact their small business has on their greater community and showcase how they intend to use the $25,000 grant award.

Name: Wish Local Empowerment Program
Description: Provides financial support to Black-owned small businesses through a $2M fund. Roughly 4,000 Wish Local partners will receive grants to promote equity and diversity in U.S. entrepreneurship.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, you must fall under all of the categories listed below:
- You have a Black-owned business
- You are 18+ years of age
- Your store has 20 or fewer employees
- Your store is a brick-and-mortar shop within the United States
- Your store earns an average annual revenue under $1M
- If selected for the program, you must join Wish Local

Name: Hustler's Microgrant
Description: Presented by Deja Vu Parker (WBLS) and HerSuiteSpot, this grant supports passionate U.S.-based entrepreneurs with $1,000 and access to valuable business resources.

Name: McKinsey Next 1B Program
Description: A growth-focused accelerator for Black-owned consumer brands. Combines McKinsey’s professional development and industry expertise with access to a powerful network of Black founders, major retailers, and investors to help participants scale.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
For the Next 1B: Founders program: Eligible businesses are typically more than one year in maturity with anywhere from $250k-$5M in annual revenue, and sells consumer products

For the Next 1B: Scalers program: Scalers works through a non-profit organization with businesses that are typically one or more years in maturity and have at least $10 million in annual revenue.

Name: NSF Seed Fund
Description: The National Science Foundation invests up to $2M in seed funding and takes zero equity. NSF funds startups across nearly all technology areas and markets like artificial intelligence, energy, medical devices, robotics, semiconductors, and many more.

Name: Compass Grant
Description: The Compass Grant helps Delaware small businesses grow internationally by reimbursing up to 50% of eligible, pre-approved international marketing and business development expenses. This includes support for international travel and related activities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Compass Grant is for export-ready Delaware small businesses. Please note the Compass Grant is NOT for startups.

Your business must meet the following requirements to qualify for Compass Grant funds:
- Company must have operations in Delaware. Those companies incorporated in Delaware without physical operations here are not eligible for Delaware grant funding.
- Applicant must be a U.S. citizen.
- Product must be made in the USA – there is a 51% U.S. content requirement.
- Companies must meet SBA size standards for eligibility, which vary by NAICS code and type of business. Please verify before completing the application.
- Company must be in business for no less than one year to qualify for grant funding.
- Company must demonstrate an understanding of the costs associated with exporting and doing business with foreign producers, including costs of freight forwarding, customs brokers, packing and shipping.
- Company must have a strategic export plan in effect.
- Accounting, Legal, and Technical Service Firms may be eligible, provided they have international clientele and can prove the intent to expand their business of exporting professional services.

Name: Main Street Acquisition Support Grant (NJEDA)
Description: Offers up to $50,000 in reimbursement to eligible New Jersey small businesses that have purchased a commercial property to operate from. The grant covers closing costs for properties closed on after 10/1/2024.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants, which can be for-profit or non-profit entities, must also meet the following requirements:
- Must meet the SBA definition of a small business based on their NAICS code.
- Closing must have taken place after the application was open to the public and grant application date must be no later than one year from date of closing.
- Applicants must provide a current Tax Clearance Certificate from the NJ Division of Taxation prior to receiving NJEDA approval.
- Applicants must be in substantial good standing prior to approval with NJEDA, the NJ Department of Labor, and NJ Department of Environmental Protection, with all decisions of substantial good standing at the discretion of those entities. 
- Only a new purchase is eligible; the closing cannot be a refinance of an existing loan.  The property purchased can’t be for residential use only, and vacant land is not eligible.   
- If a real estate holding company purchases the property, the small business that will be occupying the location must apply, however it must meet the SBA’s definition of a small business that will be located on and operate from the purchased property.  The small business must either wholly own the real estate holding company, or the ownership of both entities, and percentage of ownership, must be the same. In such situations, the small business will be the applicant and the holding company will be a co-applicant.  If the holding company that purchased the property does not have the same owners or ownership percentage as the small business or is not wholly owned by the applicant, then the applicant will be ineligible for this product. Loan must be an arm’s length transaction with a conventional lender (SBA, CDFI, MDI, bank, credit union, or any state, county, city administered loan with underwriting standards accepted) Awardee must certify to operating a commercial business from the NJ project location/building that was purchased for a five-year compliance period. 
- Applicants are permitted to lease a portion of the purchased property to a third-party.

Name: Expanding Business Ecosystems (EBE) Accelerator
Description: The EBE Business Accelerator Program empowers small businesses and minority-owned enterprises across Virginia by providing essential resources in Capital Readiness, Financial Literacy, Government Contracting, and Business Development. Graduates can win up to $1,500 as part of a pitch contest.

Name: California Paid Family Leave Small Business Grant
Description: Offers $1,000–$2,000 to small CA businesses with employees using Paid Family Leave, helping cover training, recruitment, or upskilling costs. Businesses with ≤50 employees are eligible for $2,000; those with 51–100 employees may receive $1,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business Size and PFL Participation: Small businesses in California who have 1-100 employees and have at least one employee who used California's Paid Family Leave program (PFL) on or after June 1, 2024.
- California Registration:  Your business must be registered to do business in California and be in active status with the California Secretary of State's Office.
- California Employer Account Number (CEAN):  You must have an active CEAN under which your employees are listed for payroll. Important Note for PEO Users:  If you use a Professional Employer Organization (PEO) for payroll services, your business  must be listed on the CEAN used for payroll reporting. Businesses that utilize a PEO and file under the PEO's CEAN  do not qualify.  To verify the CEAN used, look at your DE9 form (CA Employer's Quarterly Return). The employer listed should be your company, not the PEO. 
- Employee's EDD Customer Account Number: You must provide the employee's EDD Customer Account Number, which is a unique 10-digit number provided to the employee by the EDD. It is NOT the employee's social security number. You may need to ask your employee if they will provide it to you.

Name: Gottlieb Emergency Grant
Description: Provides emergency funding to professional painters, printmakers, and sculptors who have been practicing for 10+ years and are facing unexpected catastrophic events—such as illness, accident, fire, flood, or natural disaster.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for this program, an artist must be able to demonstrate a minimum involvement of ten years in a mature phase of his or her work. Artists must work in the disciplines of painting, sculpture or printmaking. Each application will be reviewed by the directors, who will exercise their discretion in considering it, and will determine the amount of each award. Applicants should note there is a set amount appropriated for these grants each fiscal year; once this budgetary limit has been reached, the Foundation will not be able to judge any additional requests on their merits.

Second-party requests are honored only when the applicant is physically unable to communicate with the Foundation. Review procedures for completed applications begin as soon as they are received. Full review generally takes about four weeks from the time an application is complete. Situations with imminent deadlines will receive priority.

Name: Warrior Rising
Description: National nonprofit serving veteran entrepreneurs through four programs: LaunchPoint (SDVET) for service-disabled veterans turning ideas into businesses, Warrior Academy for self-paced business planning, Warrior University for established and growing businesses, and Business Showers, live pitch competitions awarding non-dilutive funding with no strings attached. Also runs masterclasses and open office hours. Applications are rolling and processed in roughly 7 to 10 days.
Amount: Free programs; Business Showers award non-dilutive grants of $2,000-$150,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
U.S. military veteran entrepreneurs, plus active duty, Guard and Reserve members, military spouses and immediate family members. LaunchPoint (SDVET) is specific to service-disabled veterans.

Program ladder: Warrior Academy (self-paced online course in business fundamentals) -> Warrior University (advanced training for established and growing businesses, delivered over two evening sessions per quarter, covering strategy, business model design, customer discovery, competitive analysis and go-to-market planning; graduates earn a certificate) -> Business Showers (invitation-only pitch events limited to Warrior University graduates, awarding $2,000-$150,000 in non-dilutive grants).

Applications are rolling and continuously open; the funder states it "strives to accept and assist veterans at any point in the process of starting their own business," with applications processed in about 7-10 days.

Apply: https://www.warriorrising.org/apply/
Warrior University registration: https://wkf.ms/3NDKrPX
No application fee. Contact info@warriorrising.org or 1-833-932-7397 for current cohort dates.

Name: City of Northglenn Business Utility Assistance Grant
Description: Program is available to new or existing businesses in the Northglenn Urban Renewal Authority area. Provides up to 50% reimbursement for water, wastewater, and stormwater system upgrade costs, with a maximum reimbursement of $15,000 or $16,500 if a Northglenn contractor is used for the improvements.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be a licensed storefront commercial business and/or property owner located within the Northglenn urban renewal area that generates sales, use and/or property tax revenues. If the business is leasing the property, authorization from the building owner to apply for funding is required. Not-for-profit organizations, religious institutions, home-based businesses, or residential living facilities do not qualify. Tenants must have a minimum of two years remaining on their lease or an option to renew. Multiple landowners of a common center can each apply individually to maximize grant funding for comprehensive property improvements that serve the entire center.

Name: Hispanic Owned Business Grant (Louisiana)
Description: The Hispanic Chamber of Commerce of Louisiana (HCCL) and the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce Foundation (HCCF), in partnership with Entergy, are offering grants to support Hispanic-owned businesses in Louisiana disproportionately impacted by COVID-19 and natural disasters. These grants will help offset financial losses and provide resources for recovery and growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
In order to be considered eligible, you must meet the following requirements:
- Be at least 51% Hispanic owned business for profit
- Be a “small business” as defined by the Small Business Administration size standards.
- Have been in business for at least 12 months prior to January 2020.
- Have a business revenue of US Dollars.
- Be able to demonstrate economic business loss.
- Be agreeable to participating in at least three (3) business resource and training sessions hosted by HCCL/HCCLF.
- Be LED Certified
- Be/Become a Member of Hispanic Chamber of Commerce Louisiana (HCCL)
- Federal or State documentation confirming business location
- Verification of EIN (Employee Identification Number)
- 2020/2021 Profit and Loss Statements, Schedule C
- State of Louisiana proof of good standing

Name: Olga's Kitchen Grant
Description: Olga’s Kitchen Grant supports aspiring women entrepreneurs in Michigan who embody the passion, ambition, and vision of Olga Loizon, founder of Olga’s Kitchen. Open to women entrepreneurs in Michigan.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must meet the following criteria:
- Be living in Michigan
- Identify as a woman 
- Business must be located in Michigan 
- Be able to write a personal statement demonstrating financial need 
- Must provide a formal Business Plan

Name: Advanced Industries Export Grant (Colorado)
Description: The Advanced Industries Export Grant supports Colorado-based small and medium-sized advanced industries technology businesses that want to start or expand exporting. The grant reimburses up to 50% of approved international business development and marketing costs, with a maximum award of $15,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, your business needs to:
- Manufacture an advanced technology and influence one or more of Colorado’s advanced industries (learn more below).
- Have headquarters in Colorado or have at least 50% of your employees based in Colorado.
- Employ fewer than 200 employees globally.
- Be new to export or expanding to a new export market.
- Have at least two years of sales experience in the United States.
- Be registered with the Colorado Secretary of State(opens in new window) and in Good Standing.
- Have a commercialized product or service to export.
- Be export-ready (learn more below).

Name: ExportMD Program (Maryland)
Description: ExportMD Program helps Maryland-based small and mid-sized businesses offset international marketing costs. Awardees can receive up to $5,000 in reimbursement for expenses like travel, website development, or virtual trade show registration. Funded in part by the U.S. Small Business Administration, the program supports companies looking to expand globally.

Name: Kentucky Export Initiative STEP Grant
Description: For Kentucky small businesses seeking international export assistance, the State Trade Expansion Program (STEP) grant is available to reimburse for allowable development expenses.

Name: Atlassian for Nonprofits
Description: Atlassian for Nonprofits offers eligible organizations 75% off teamwork tools plus free product support sessions. Nonprofits can access discounted licenses for products like Jira Service Management, Jira Product Discovery, Bitbucket, Trello, Statuspage, and Rovo, helping teams collaborate, manage projects, and boost productivity more effectively.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
If you’re ready to move beyond the free license, 75% discounts on Atlassian Cloud apps are available to nonprofit organizations that are:
- Non-governmental: independent from government control
- Non-commercial: operating on a not-for-profit basis and for the public benefit
- Non-political: or against any political party, candidate, or campaign
- Recognized as a nonprofit: in the country in which you are registered, in accordance with the eligibility criteria for that country

Name: Philadelphia Small Business Catalyst Fund
Description: The Philadelphia Small Business Catalyst Fund offers grants of up to $50,000 to help small businesses and entrepreneurs across the city grow and thrive. With a $5 million fund, the program provides both funding and strategic guidance to businesses demonstrating strong need, growth potential, and economic impact. Led by the Philadelphia Department of Commerce, this initiative is designed to fuel collaboration and accelerate business growth citywide.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Businesses that generated under $2 million in revenue in 2025 can apply for funding. The business must also be:
- Located in Philadelphia.
- Up to date on City taxes or have an approved tax payment agreement.
- Registered and licensed with the City of Philadelphia.
- Able to accelerate business goals with targeted funding and support.
- To learn more about what businesses are eligible to apply, see our FAQs.

Applicants need to show:
- A clear expansion plan.
- Contribution to local economic impact, such as strengthening Philadelphia neighborhoods and creating jobs.
- Resilience and innovation despite challenges accessing traditional funding.

Name: McKinney Innovation Fund
Description: The McKinney Innovation Fund, located in the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, offers nondilutive grants of up to $200,000 to support tech startups in their early growth stage. The Growth Grant provides funding for startups that establish their primary headquarters in McKinney. Typically, 50% of the grant is awarded upfront, with the remaining 50% performance-based over a 3-year term tied to milestones. Funds can be used for key hires, product development, and customer acquisition.

Name: Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center Milestone Circles
Description: Milestone Circles is a free 12-week entrepreneurship program by the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center, supported by the Wells Fargo Foundation. It helps U.S.-based founders accelerate their business growth and leadership through curated peer cohorts, expert mentorship, and milestone-driven learning. Participants gain practical tools, community support, and mentorship to achieve strategic company growth and strengthen their leadership skills.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Milestone Circles is open to all U.S.-based entrepreneurs—whether you’re in the early stages of launching a startup or actively scaling a growing business. There are no industry restrictions and no cost to join.

Name: Small Certified Supplier Innovative Finance Program
Description: Revenue-based financing and advisory program from Founders First for certified small suppliers to accelerate growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small certified suppliers seeking non-dilutive growth capital.

Name: First Interstate Bank Grants
Description: Community grants supporting nonprofits in areas such as community development, education, and workforce in First Interstate's service regions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) nonprofits operating in eligible communities.

Name: We Make Change
Description: Matches skilled volunteers with impact startups and nonprofits needing talent. Enables remote collaboration to accelerate social ventures.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Impact startups and nonprofits; volunteers seeking skills-based opportunities.

Name: Clif Family Foundation Grant
Description: Grants for organizations working to strengthen the food system, enhance community health, and support environmental stewardship. Prioritizes grassroots groups and measurable impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) nonprofits focused on food systems, environment, and community health.

Name: NY Pre-Seed and Seed Matching Fund Program
Description: New York State program that matches venture investments into pre-seed and seed-stage startups to catalyze growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NY-based startups meeting program and investor criteria.

Name: Canva for Nonprofits
Description: Provides eligible nonprofits with free access to Canva's premium design tools to support communications, branding, and fundraising efforts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Verified nonprofits meeting Canva's eligibility guidelines.

Name: American Express Leadership Academy
Description: Leadership development program for emerging nonprofit and social sector leaders. Focuses on skills building, peer learning, and impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Senior leaders at registered NONPROFITS; region-restricted. 2027 cohort applications open for The Americas (academy 3/9 - 3/12/2027) and EMEA (7/6 - 7/9/2027); Asia Pacific 2027 dates TBC.

Name: Microsoft for Startups
Description: Offers startups cloud credits, technical resources, and go-to-market support through Microsoft's startup programs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Startups meeting Microsoft's program criteria.

Name: Bob Woodruff Foundation Grants
Description: Funding to high-impact nonprofits serving veterans, service members, and their families. Focus areas include mental health, housing, and economic opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits serving veteran and military communities with evidence-based programs.

Name: Military Entrepreneur Challenge
Description: Pitch competition by Second Service Foundation for military-connected entrepreneurs, offering capital, coaching, and community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Veterans, active-duty, guard/reserve, and military spouses who are entrepreneurs.

Name: Savvy Fellowship
Description: A free, self-paced online program for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs featuring mentorship, assignments, and pitch opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs globally.

Name: Ashoka Fellowship
Description: Global fellowship for leading social entrepreneurs driving systems change. Provides a lifelong community, strategic support, and visibility.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Social entrepreneurs with innovative solutions and systems-change potential.

Name: Texas Skills for Small Business Grant
Description: The Skills for Small Business Grant helps Texas employers with fewer than 100 employees train new and existing workers through local community and technical colleges. Funded by the Texas Workforce Commission, the program offers up to $2,000 per new employee and $1,000 per incumbent employee for customized, job-relevant courses. By supporting skill development in areas like customer service, sales, and technology, the program strengthens small businesses and the state’s workforce.

Name: Alchemist Accelerator
Description: Alchemist Accelerator is a premier program designed to help early-stage founders gain mentorship, traction, and funding through a structured yet highly personalized experience. It combines curated group sessions – like weekly peer gatherings, expert workshops, and Feedback Summits – with individualized mentoring from successful entrepreneurs and investors. Founders participate in Alchemist from wherever they choose to work and build their companies.

Name: AI2 Incubator
Description: The AI2 Incubator partners with top technical founders and deep domain experts to build applied Al startups that solve meaningful, real-world problems. Participants receive up to $600K investment, up to $1M in AI compute, and deep technical support from the Allen Institute for AI (AI2) network, known for its 200+ PhDs and open-source AI contributions. With a track record of 40+ companies valued at $1B+ and notable successes like Yoodli, Lexion, and Ozette, it combines funding with hands-on AI expertise to turn cutting-edge research into impactful startups.

Name: Forum Ventures Accelerator
Description: Forum Ventures is a leading early-stage fund and accelerator dedicated to helping B2B SaaS founders build and scale their companies. Through its Forum for Founders pre-seed program ($100K investment, 15-week mentorship) and Forum Seed fund, it provides capital, go-to-market guidance, and a strong SaaS founder community. Since 2014, Forum has backed 400+ startups that have collectively raised nearly $1B from top-tier VCs like Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and Salesforce Ventures.

Name: IndieBio Accelerator
Description: IndieBio is a global biotech startup program and venture fund under SOSV that invests up to $525,000 at pre-seed and provides intensive, high-touch support for early-stage founders working on breakthrough biology-based innovations. IndieBio offers deep mentorship from multiple partners, access to labs in New York and San Francisco, a strong alumni network, and long-term follow-on investment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We look for companies with deep scientific insights aimed at solving intractable or difficult problems that will impact 1B+ members of humanity. Human and Planetary Health is our mission. We see biology as a technology that can be applied across all verticals which can include therapeutics, the future of food, biomaterials, biological tools, diagnostics, synthetic biology, genomics, and data analysis to just name a few areas.

Companies can be based on hardware, software, or wet-biology and go straight to consumers or sell to business.

For the therapeutics track, because only $250K is upfront and the other $1.75 million is over time, we are looking for truly novel platforms and methodologies that need this time to prove their concept.

Name: HAX Accelerator
Description: HAX, part of global VC firm SOSV, is a hands-on venture program that invests $500,000 at pre-seed in hard-tech startups solving major challenges in climate, sustainability, automation, and human health. Founders join a 6-month residency in HAX’s 35,000-sq-ft Newark facility where they receive deep engineering help, rapid prototyping resources, and access to top manufacturing and investor networks.

Name: Antler Residency
Description: The Antler Residency is a full-time, in-person program where aspiring founders build teams, validate ideas, and launch startups with support from Antler’s global network of advisors, partners, and investors. Antler has offices in 27 cities across six continents.

Name: Entrepreneurs First Accelerator
Description: Entrepreneurs First (EF) is a talent-first accelerator that backs exceptional individuals before they have a team or even an idea, helping them find a cofounder and rapidly build a venture-scale company. Through its structured 12-week FORM program and 12-week LAUNCH program in San Francisco, founders receive expert guidance, cofounder matching, office space, global networking, and equity-free living-cost support. Teams that pass EF’s Investment Committee can then receive up to $250,000 in equity investment plus access to top-tier investors, perks, and Silicon Valley ecosystem exposure.

Name: LAUNCH Accelerator
Description: LAUNCH, founded by Jason Calacanis, is an organization dedicated to supporting founders through its global startup conference, top tech podcasts, and its high-intensity 12-week accelerator program. Each year it invests millions into roughly 40 early-stage founders, with accelerator cohorts giving startups access to 700+ investors and deep growth mentorship.

Name: MuckerLab Accelerator
Description: MuckerLab is a mentorship-driven accelerator in Southern California that supports internet and software founders through deep, hands-on company building. Working with only 20–25 startups per year, MuckerLab partners closely with founders for up to a year to reach key milestones and secure funding.

Name: South Park Commons Member Residency
Description: SPC Member Residency is a home for builders in the -1 to 0 phase who are exploring what to do next, testing ideas, and building meaningful relationships. We expect members to participate actively and join with full-time focus, having wrapped up previous commitments before onboarding. After applying, you can expect a follow-up within 1–2 weeks and an offer decision within 4 weeks.

Name: The David Prize Nomination
Description: The David Prize awards $200,000 each to five New Yorkers with bold, transformative visions to improve life across the city’s five boroughs. Open to individuals — whether independent or affiliated with an organization — the Prize celebrates people with the conviction and creativity to strengthen communities, culture, and the city’s future. Funding is unrestricted. The nomination is always open.

Name: Gold House Ventures
Description: Gold House Ventures is an early-stage fund backing industry-shifting startups led by exceptional multicultural – especially Asian Pacific – founders. Through capital, an accelerator, and an invitation-only founder network, they provide resources, community, and cultural uplift to help API entrepreneurs scale.

Name: Next Generation DTC Founders Grant
Description: The Next Generation Consumer Product Founders Grant, run by Goodie Nation and SHOPLINE, provides up to $50,000 in non-dilutive funding plus access to SHOPLINE's e-commerce platform (including a store build with white-glove migration), mentorship, roundtables, and media exposure to help consumer-product brands scale. It is aimed at DTC-first companies in Apparel & Fashion, Food & Beverage, Health & Beauty, and Home & Furniture, with annual revenue between $25,000 and $15M and a registered U.S. or Canadian business entity. Applications are rolling until all grant funds are awarded.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We’re looking for consumer product brands generating between $25,000 and $15 million in annual revenue in the following categories:
- Apparel & Fashion
- Food & Beverage
- Health & Beauty
- Home & Furniture
Industry: Apparel & Accessories,Food & Beverage,Beauty & Personal Care,Consumer Packaged Goods,Retail

Name: Southeast Overtown/Park West Community Redevelopment Agency Small Business Grant Program
Description: The SEOPW CRA Small Business Grant Program provides targeted funding to small businesses within the Southeast Overtown/Park West redevelopment area to support growth, job creation, and neighborhood revitalization. Eligible businesses can use funds for operational costs, infrastructure, and long-term sustainability, with applications reviewed first-come, first-served. Applications must be submitted by email or delivered in person to the Overtown Business Resource Center or the SEOPW CRA office during stated hours.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify for grant funding, applicants must meet the following criteria:
- The business must be located within the Southeast Overtown Park West Redevelopment area boundaries.
- The business must possess a valid City of Miami business license.
