- The business must be in good standing with local, state, and federal regulations, including tax compliance.

Priority consideration may be given to minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses, and those that can demonstrate job creation or community impact.

No Multiple Applications: Applicants cannot apply more than once every 60 days

Name: Bluegrass Bartenders Fund
Description: The Bluegrass Bartenders Fund is a hardship relief program that provides immediate financial assistance to spirits-industry professionals working at locally owned independent businesses in the Louisville Metro area. Run by Louisville-based The LEE Initiative and APRON Inc., it helps cover essential living costs like rent, utilities, childcare, and medical bills. It’s designed to offer both urgent support and a longer-term safety net for Louisville’s hospitality community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify for a grant you must be employed in a locally owned, Louisville area, independent restaurant for six months.
You must apply no later than 6 months after the onset of need.

Financial Hardship Assistance:
*Triggered by a specific unusual event (such as illness, death, accident, crime or other personal event)
*Financial need and lack of other resources must be substantiated
*Expenses must be proven
*Hardship must be beyond employee’s control

Eligible Financial Hardships Include:
*Residential fire or flooding
*Acts of nature that result in major property damage to primary residence or automobile
*Death of an employee or an immediate family member resulting in a financial hardship
*Other person financial hardships
*Theft/loss of essential property

Financial Hardships that Cannot Be Granted under APRON, Inc. Guidelines Include:
*Lost wages due to missed time from work
*Items covered by insurance or governmental assistance
*Elective, routine or ongoing medical expenses
*Bad debt/overdue bills from ongoing financial problems
*Legal fees and expenses associated with divorce or child custody issues
*Personal bankruptcy
*Illegal behavior or situations that occur while you are under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
*Circumstances within the applicant’s control (such as normal maternity expenses, traffic violations, etc.)
*Slow business, cut or not enough hours, not making enough money

Name: Fearless Fund
Description: Fearless Fund invests in women of color–led companies raising pre-seed, seed, or Series A, with a mission to close the VC funding gap for founders building scalable, high-growth businesses. They look for resilient teams (at least one full-time founder), a defensible competitive advantage, an incorporated (or incorporating) business with strong financials and an exit plan, and evidence of product traction. Typical initial checks are up to $3M in exchange for at least 10% ownership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Fearless Fund considers investments in early-stage, high growth ventures that meet the following criteria:
- Led by a high quality, resilient management team with at least one full-time founder: The management team should have deep industry knowledge as well as an understanding of their product, new and existing competitor's products, and their potential market share. Strong management teams will exhibit enthusiasm and confidence in their team’s ability to execute. We see our investment as a partnership with our entrepreneurs and appreciate those who communicate effectively with their investors.
- Have a sustainable competitive advantage: Competitive advantages can include high barriers to entry (if no IP, then trade secrets that can allow a reasonable amount of time to become market leader), disruptive technology, unique/valuable partnerships, etc. 
- Established C-Corporations (or LLCs on path to incorporation): Must have a strong business model, 5 year pro-forma, and clearly defined and well-researched exit strategy. 
- Ability to scale rapidly and achieve strong returns for investors: We generally prefer to see 3-5 year projections with scalability in excess of $20 million (minimum). We prefer opportunities that can be accelerated with support from plus opportunities that can be accelerated with support from our investment team, partners, and advisors.

Financial Considerations:
- Funding ask: Should be in line with the company’s stage of growth. 
- Stage of Company: Fearless Fund invests in Pre-seed, Seed and Series A stage deals. At a minimum, the company should have proof of concept and preferably a minimum viable product that has some customer traction. 
- Investment Size & Ownership: Our initial investment will be no larger than $3M and we seek at least 10% ownership of portfolio companies.

Name: Female Founders Fund
Description: Female Founders Fund is a seed-stage venture fund that invests exclusively in female-founded companies. It focuses on sectors like e-commerce, media, platforms, advertising, and other web-enabled services, and its portfolio includes brands such as Minibar, Maven, WayUp, Thrive Global, Zola, and BentoBox.

Name: Global NY Fund Grant Program
Description: The Global NY Fund supports New York State small and mid-sized businesses (and eligible nonprofit economic development organizations) with reimbursable export grants and loans to help them expand direct exports and create jobs. Companies can receive up to $25,000 and nonprofits providing export assistance can receive up to $100,000, with reimbursements covering up to 50% of project costs for companies and up to 75% for nonprofits. Grants can cover market customization, participation in trade shows, export workshops, and product adaptations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
For Profit Companies:
- Located in New York State
- Have 500 or fewer employees in New York State
- Intend to begin exporting or expand export sales in foreign markets
- At least one of the following:
1. 51% of the value of finished product or service originates in New York, the calculation of which includes the value of the raw materials and component parts, manufacturing process, advertising and promotion, distribution, warehousing, and designs and other intellectual property
OR
2. A business that is certified as a local producer through a regional chamber of commerce or economic development agency (e.g., Made in NY; Made in Brooklyn)
- Business is viable and in existence for at least one year by the date of application for the Global NY Fund Grant
- Demonstrated need for grant assistance
- Demonstrated understanding of costs associated with exporting and doing business with foreign buyers, including costs of freight forwarding, customs brokers, packing, shipping, marketing, etc.

Not-for-profit organizations:
- Located in New York State
- Have a demonstrated history of helping New York State businesses export and/or contribute to state or regional economic development through the promotion of international trade
- Be (or become) registered and up-to-date with its filing with the Office of Attorney General’s Charities Bureau, certified in the Office of the State Comptrollers’ VendRep System, prequalified with New York State Grants Gateway, and in compliance with all other relevant statutory requirements
- An unincorporated trade association may be a co-applicant with a NYS not-for-profit organization, IDA or LDC, but the latter entity must be the contractual party if a grant is awarded
- All not-for-profit organizations must be prequalified in order to do business with New York State and to apply for grants. In order to prequalify, not-for-profit organizations must submit an online Prequalification Application through the Grants Gateway. The Prequalification Application is comprised of five components to gauge your organizational structure and the types of services you provide. The required forms and document uploads are all part of the Document Vault.  Resources to complete the application and associated document vault can be found in the Quick Links Section of the Grants Gateway website.

Name: Hivers & Strivers Capital
Description: Hivers & Strivers is an investment firm that backs highly scalable companies founded and led by U.S. military veterans, pairing capital with deep operational support and a powerful LP network. They typically invest $100K–$1M checks and stay actively involved through strategic guidance and connections, with a track record they say has produced strong returns. Open to veteran founders.

Name: Kapor Capital
Description: Kapor Capital is an Oakland-based venture capital firm that invests in early-stage, tech-driven startups aiming to close gaps of access and opportunity for low-income communities and communities of color in the U.S., especially African-American and Latinx communities. They prioritize founders committed to building diverse, inclusive teams (via their Founders’ Commitment) and invest across sectors like education, work, finance, justice, food, and health.

Name: Invest Atlanta Small Business Improvement Grant
Description: Invest Atlanta’s Small Business Improvement Grants offer up to $50,000 to small businesses and commercial property owners/tenants located in seven City of Atlanta Tax Allocation Districts (TADs) to fund interior and exterior property improvements. Projects must be under 15,000 sq. ft., use at least 25% of funds on visible exterior upgrades, and provide a minimum 10% match; eligible costs include things like signage, windows, landscaping, HVAC, plumbing, and certain design services (capped at 10%).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements
- Project must be less than 15,000 square feet.
- A minimum of 25% of funds must be used for exterior improvements.
- All exterior improvements must be visible from the public right-of-way.
- Eligible exterior improvements include: painting, lighting, windows, doors, framing, signage, canopies, awnings, gates, fencing, landscaping, building surface repairs, ground surface upgrades.
- Interior improvements should significantly enhance the customer and employee experience.
- Eligible interior improvements include: flooring, walls, ceilings, HVAC, water heaters, plumbing, electrical, and structural repairs to walls, floors, stairs, and interior doors.
- Certain soft costs, such as architectural and planning services, are eligible but shall not exceed 10% of grant amount.
- Awardees must provide a match equal to at least 10% of the grant award and demonstrate the project as proposed would not happen without the TAD grant assistance.

Exclusions
- New construction
- Properties owned or occupied by a government or public agency
- Properties used for residential purposes
- Churches and religious institution facilities (commercial buildings owned by churches or religious institutions are eligible)
- Operations, inventory, and other soft costs
- Smoke shops, night clubs, liquor stores, businesses that derive majority of revenue from gambling activities, tobacco and alcohol sales, or adult businesses

Name: Clark County, NV District A Tenant Improvement Grant Program
Description: Clark County, NV District A’s Tenant Improvement Grant Program offers up to $25,000 to eligible small businesses and commercial property owners in unincorporated Commission District A to fund property upgrades like tenant improvements, façade renovations, signage, and beautification projects that benefit the local community. Applicants must meet size and revenue limits (generally under 20 employees and under $2M revenue), hold a valid Clark County license, and be in good standing (no recent bankruptcy or unpaid taxes).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Qualified Small Business Criteria
- Owns a small business in unincorporated District A
- U.S.-based and not government-controlled
- Fewer than 20 full-time employees
- Less than $2M in annual gross revenue
- Valid Clark County business license
- No bankruptcy in the past 5 years
- No unpaid taxes or conflicts with Clark County
- Not engaged in prohibited business activities – see FAQ for list

Qualified Property Owner Criteria
- Owns commercial property in unincorporated District A
- Less than $2M in annual lease revenue
- No bankruptcy in the past 5 years
- No unpaid taxes or conflicts with Clark County
- Not engaged in prohibited business activities – see FAQ for list

Name: Google Ad Grants
Description: Google Ad Grants provides qualifying nonprofits up to $10,000 per month in free Google Search ads to promote their missions. These ads help organizations raise awareness, attract donors, and recruit volunteers by reaching people searching for causes like theirs on Google.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See eligibility requirements for Google for Nonprofits: https://www.google.com/nonprofits/eligibility/

Name: Staten Island Arts Grants
Description: Staten Island Arts offers project grants for Staten Island-based artists, collectives, and nonprofit organizations to support original artistic work, cultural programming, and arts education, with an emphasis on public engagement and community impact. For the 2026 cycle, applications open November 17, 2025 and are due January 31, 2026, with award amounts generally ranging from $500 to $5,000 depending on the category (including options for first-time applicants, returning grantees, nonprofits, school partnerships, and senior center residencies).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Applicants must be Staten Island residents or Staten Island-based nonprofit organizations.
- All applications are digital and must be submitted through our grants portal; no paper applications or hard copy work samples will be accepted.
- All artistic cultural disciplines— humanities and cultural studies, digital and interactive media, literary, performing, and visual arts, crafts, and folk arts —are considered.
- All grant-funded projects must be completed and presented to the public within the calendar year they are awarded.

Name: Angel Philanthropy Smart Family Fund
Description: Angel Philanthropy is a small family foundation that funds early-stage nonprofits with strong potential for scalable social impact, especially those that are still proving their model and don’t yet have extensive outcome data. They provide first-time grants of $25,000–$100,000 and pair funding with mentorship to help organizations strengthen their programs and become ready for larger, long-term funders.

Name: Roger I. and Ruth B. MacFarlane Foundation Grant
Description: The Roger I. and Ruth B. MacFarlane Foundation makes mostly invitation-only grants in two tiers: Category Two awards of $200,000–$250,000 (focused in 2026 on climate change and environmental protection) and Category One grants of $25,000–$75,000 supporting a broader range of trustee priorities (e.g., education, health, housing, immigrant rights, and women/girls). While they primarily fund U.S.-focused work, they may support U.S.-based nonprofits working internationally, and they accept Letters of Inquiry.
Industry: Nonprofit,Social Impact,Education & Child Care,Health / Wellness,Climate & Sustainability

Name: Cisco Global Impact Cash Grant Program
Description: Cisco’s Global Impact Cash Grant Program supports nonprofit and NGO-led, early-stage, tech-enabled solutions that tackle major social challenges in four priority areas: crisis response, education, economic empowerment, and climate resilience, with a strong emphasis on serving economically underserved communities (65%+ of participants). Organizations can submit a Letter of Inquiry year-round to be considered for invitation to a full application, and first-time grants are capped at $75,000, with proposals evaluated on impact metrics, scalability, leadership, and innovative use of technology.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Global Impact Cash Grants multiply the impact of eligible organizations around the globe with national or multinational operations. Before applying, invited NPOs/NGOs can determine their eligibility by reviewing the requirements below and the grant giving policies.

Organizational and programmatic requirements
- Organizations within the United States must be recognized by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) as tax exempt under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3) and classified by the IRS as a public charity.
Organizations from outside the United States must provide information and documents to determine whether the organization is the equivalent of a U.S. public charity.
- Programs to be funded must serve an audience greater than 65 percent economically underserved, relative to the average standards of the target geography.
- Organizations and programs must focus on at least one of our social investment sectors: crisis response, education, economic empowerment, and/or climate impact and regeneration.
- For education, crisis response, and economic empowerment proposals, we will also consider proposals that address environmental sustainability within the context of that investment area. For example, we would consider funding an economic empowerment program that specifically focuses on creating green jobs.
- An organization's overhead is not to exceed 25 percent. (Organizations are occasionally exempt from this requirement; however, they must be exceptionally aligned with Cisco's values and criteria, and they must clearly explain and justify their overhead costs. Exemptions to the requirement on overhead expenses are determined on a case-by-case basis.) Cisco Foundation does not tend to make grants to colleges and universities. In the case that such a grant may be made, Cisco Foundation does not support additional institutional overhead rates for colleges and universities.
- The maximum request amount for first-time grant recipients is US$75,000.

Ineligible programs and/or activities
Proposals in the following areas are not eligible for a Global Impact Cash Grant:
- Miscellaneous exclusions: general operating expenses, other than directly associated with the program itself; individuals; research programs; membership-based activities; programs that promote or serve one culture, race, religion, population group, or political viewpoint—rather than the community at large; religious, political, or sectarian organizations (Note: A direct service program run by a faith-based organization may be eligible. See our grant giving policies.)
- Hospitals: private or public hospitals; hospital foundations; medical centers, research centers, etc. (Programs based in a hospital may be eligible; however, grant funds must go exclusively to direct service in the community, not to general hospital operating expenses.)
- Healthcare: programs focused on improving physical or mental health
Schools and scholarships: private, public, or charter schools; school foundations, booster clubs, and/or fundraising organizations affiliated with a particular school; colleges/universities; scholarships, stipends, or loans within a program; and/or school-related activities such as field trips, research programs, etc.
- Events: athletic events, competitions, tournaments; conferences, seminars, workshops; festivals, field trips, or other recreational events; fundraising events or sponsorships (benefit dinners, walks/runs, concerts, sports teams, etc.)
- Philanthropic: capital building funds, challenge grants, grant-making organizations (all other foundations including private foundations, family foundations, school foundations, etc.)
Industry: Nonprofit,Technology,Climate & Sustainability,Education & Child Care,Economic Empowerment,Social Impact

Name: NBA Foundation Grant
Description: The NBA Foundation provides grants to local and national nonprofits that serve under-resourced youth ages 14–24 by expanding school-to-career pathways through job readiness, skills training, job placement, and career advancement. Eligible organizations must be a registered 501(c)(3) (or Canadian equivalent), operate in an NBA team market, serve at least 25 youth annually, and submit required documents through the FLUXX portal; funding supports workforce development projects and broader economic mobility efforts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Your organization must:
- Be a registered 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or a T3010 if operating in Canada
- Have a current IRS Form 990 or Form 990 or Form 990-EZ from the most recent fiscal year
- Focus on promoting school-to-career employment opportunities targeting under resourced youth ages 14-24 years old in a market with an NBA team
- Serve a minimum of 25 youth annually across your programs
- Submit an organizational budget, program budget, and list of board members

Name: Tony Robbins Foundation Grant
Description: The Tony Robbins Foundation offers grant funding to nonprofits worldwide that align with its mission to improve quality of life for “those often forgotten,” including youth, seniors, people experiencing hunger or homelessness, and incarcerated populations. To apply, eligible organizations must be a 501(c)(3) (or internationally recognized nonprofit), have been active for at least one fiscal year, and first submit a 3-page online Letter of Intent; only selected applicants are invited to complete a full application.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered, your organization must: 
- Be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or an international organization with government-recognized nonprofit status with proof of status.  Be an active nonprofit for at least one fiscal year with tax documentation.  Have a mission statement that aligns with The Tony Robbins Foundation’s mission. 

We do not offer funding for: 
- Individuals seeking funds for personal, business or other use.  
- Start-up costs for nonprofits, businesses, groups or individuals.  
- Organizations with a mission outside of our areas of focus.

Name: Illinois State Trade and Export Promotion (ISTEP) Program
Description: Illinois’ ISTEP program helps Illinois small businesses grow exports by offering technical help plus reimbursements for trade missions, individual foreign sales trips, product compliance certifications, website localization/ecommerce, and export credit insurance. Funding is first-come, first-served, and eligible firms generally must be Illinois-based, SBA-sized (under 500 employees), operating at least a year, and meet revenue/content requirements, applying through the online form with support from an SBDC International Trade Center or state trade specialist.

Name: Morgan Stanley Small Business Academy
Description: Morgan Stanley’s Small Business Academy is a program designed to help small business owners strengthen their business skills, stand out in procurement processes, and expand their professional networks so they can better compete for work in financial services and other industries. It includes a 12-week virtual, instructor-led course followed by a yearlong mentorship, with potential grant/funding opportunities for participants who complete the curriculum and successfully pitch a business case. Small businesses in the US need to have $100k in annual revenue and 3+ years in business to be eligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Small businesses based in the United States, Canada, or Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA
- Certified small businesses and those operating in underserved communities.
- Registered as a for-profit company with an annual revenue (net profit) of at least:
--United States and Canada: $100,000 USD and no more than $2,000,000 USD
--EMEA: $50,000 USD and no more than $1,000,000 USD
- Incorporated and operational for United States and Canada: 3-12 years or EMEA: 2- 12 years, satisfies at least one of Morgan Stanley’s services, and participants are members of their business’s executive committee (max. of two participants representing one business).

Name: Stanford Startup Law Sustainability Program
Description: Stanford’s Startup Law: Sustainability program provides free (pro bono) legal services to early-stage U.S.-based climate/sustainability/impact ventures—nonprofit or for-profit—that have raised less than $500K, with priority for Stanford-affiliated teams (including pre-formation entities). It’s a selective, rolling-admissions program: applicants may be invited to a video interview, and accepted teams sign an engagement letter to be paired with a practicing attorney and law students.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage non-profit or for-profit entities that are focused on climate, sustainability, and impact and who have fundraised less than $500,000 may be eligible for pro bono legal help. Priority will be given to Stanford-affiliated teams. Entities can be pre-formation. We are not currently assisting entities based outside of the United States.

Name: Jay L. Smith Family Foundation Grant
Description: The Jay L. Smith Family Foundation funds U.S.-based IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofits whose work aligns with its mission of strengthening families, advancing healthcare (with a noted preference for Alzheimer’s cure research and related care), and serving disadvantaged communities.

Name: NSF STEM K-12 Grant
Description: NSF’s STEM K-12 (NSF 25-545) funds fundamental, applied, and translational R&D that advances STEM teaching and learning in K-12 formal and informal settings, including work that leverages AI and emerging technologies to strengthen U.S. STEM education and the future workforce. Full proposals are accepted anytime, with awards typically ranging from $25,000–$750,000 for 1–3 years (about 40 awards anticipated, depending on funds and proposal quality).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Proposals may only be submitted by the following:
- Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs): Two- and four-year IHEs (including community colleges) accredited in, and having a campus located in the US, acting on behalf of their faculty members. Special Instructions for International Branch Campuses of US IHEs: If the proposal includes funding to be provided to an international branch campus of a US institution of higher education (including through use of sub-awards and consultant arrangements), the proposer must explain the benefit(s) to the project of performance at the international branch campus, and justify why the project activities cannot be performed at the US campus.
- Non-profit, non-academic organizations: Independent museums, observatories, research laboratories, professional societies and similar organizations located in the U.S. that are directly associated with educational or research activities.
- For-profit organizations: U.S.-based commercial organizations, including small businesses, with strong capabilities in scientific or engineering research or education and a passion for innovation.
- State and Local Governments
- Tribal Nations: An American Indian or Alaska Native tribe, band, nation, pueblo, village, or community that the Secretary of the Interior acknowledges as a federally recognized tribe pursuant to the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994, 25 U.S.C. §§ 5130-5131.

Name: City of Jacksonville Veteran Grant Program
Description: The City of Jacksonville’s Veteran Grant Program offers up to $2,000 per eligible veteran entrepreneur in Duval County to support business development through tangible asset purchases, with funds paid out as reimbursement after submitting paid invoices and proof of payment. To qualify, the business must be at least 6 months old, the applicant must complete a required small business education course, and submit documents like a Duval County ID, DD-214, business annual report, and a recent asset receipt (within 180 days).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Grant allocation of up to $2,000 per veteran entrepreneur
- Attend and complete mandatory small business education course
- Residence and business must be located in Duval County
- Business must be established for a minimum of 6 months
- Funds may be used to assist with the development and growth of an eligible business
- Proceeds must be used for tangable assets
- Grant funds shall be disbursed on a reimbursement basis, following receipt of paid invoices and proof of payment

Name: Jacksonville Facade Renovation Matching Grant Program
Description: Jacksonville’s Office of Economic Development offers a reimbursable Façade Renovation Matching Grant for existing businesses in designated economically distressed areas, funding improvements to building sides/fronts visible from public streets (e.g., painting, masonry repair, windows/doors, signage, lighting, landscaping, decorative fencing). Eligibility requires the property be in good standing (taxes current, no liens/violations, code-compliant, owner consent if renting), and grants match private investment up to $7,500 (Level 1) or $15,000 (Level 2)—with the match waived if a city-approved JSEB completes the work. Applications are reviewed by OED, work must be approved before starting, and funds are paid after completion with receipts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Project must be located in a designated economically distressed area (see map).
- Business structures must be in compliance with all existing city, state and federal building code, regulations and permitting requirements as a prerequisite to the receipt of funds.
- All property taxes must be paid and current.
- There should be no outstanding liens or code violations.
- A Notarized Property Owner's Affidavit of Consent is required for renters

Name: Grand Rapids Community Foundation Grant
Description: Grand Rapids Community Foundation has awarded more than $245 million in grants since 1922 and funds partners across areas like education, health, environment, arts/culture engagement, neighborhoods, and economic prosperity, with an explicit commitment to being actively anti-racist and advancing equity and justice. Eligible applicants (typically 501(c)(3)s, government entities, or those with a fiscal sponsor) focused on Kent County, Michigan start with a brief pre-application, and selected projects move to a full proposal + site visit before approval and disbursement.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: We invite partnerships from 501 (c) (3) nonprofits, government entity, or those willing to attain a fiscal sponsor. Please note that the Community Foundation’s primary geographic focus is Kent County, Michigan. Previous recipients are eligible to apply.

Name: Food Hero Mobile Food Truck Apprenticeship
Description: The Food Hero Food Truck Apprenticeship Program is a paid, Chicago-based opportunity offering hands-on culinary training, business coaching, and real-world food truck experience. Designed for aspiring food entrepreneurs, career changers, and veterans, the program supports participants in building a future in food. This U.S. Department of Labor–certified apprenticeship prepares adults across Illinois to earn while they learn and to launch careers or businesses in the mobile food economy. Graduates receive a DOL Apprenticeship Certificate, ServSafe certification, and industry-aligned credentials (NRA/ACF).

Name: City of Palm Springs Facade Improvement Program
Description: The City of Palm Springs Facade Improvement Program offers a dollar-for-dollar matching grant up to $7,500 to help property owners or tenants improve storefront exteriors and signage and encourage investment in commercial properties citywide. Eligible upgrades include items like signs, awnings, exterior paint/surface treatments, paving (off public right-of-way), lighting, fencing, windows/glazing, and landscaping, and funds are reimbursed after work is completed with proof of payment and before/after documentation. Businesses must be open to the public and free of building code violations or tax liens to qualify.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Property owners or tenants located in leased or owned commercial properties throughout the City of Palm Springs.

A business owner (tenant) that is not the property owner must show evidence of the right to alter the property, or consent from the property owner.

Name: City of Dallas District 7 Exterior Improvement Grant Program
Description: Dallas’s District 7 Exterior Improvement Grant Program offers reimbursable grants to eligible for-profit small businesses in (or immediately adjacent to) City Council District 7 to fund permanent exterior upgrades that improve building appearance, safety, and functionality in South Dallas. Grants can cover projects like façade renovations, hardscape/streetscape improvements, permanent murals or art, ADA upgrades, and energy-efficiency improvements, with awards up to $50,000 and required private matching funds (e.g., 20% match for projects up to $25,000). Businesses must be current on City taxes and meet program restrictions, and improvements must be maintained for five years after award.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- For-profit small businesses (property owner or tenants; tenant applications require property-owner consent).
- Must be current on all City of Dallas taxes and free of liens or defaults on prior city agreements.

Applicants must not operate as:
- Sexually oriented businesses (Chapter 41A)
- Liquor stores
- Pawn shops
- Body piercing studios
- Tattoo studios

Name: Detroit Small Business Tech Fund
Description: Detroit and the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation (with funding from Rocket Community Fund) launched the Detroit Small Business Technology Fund, a microgrant program awarding $1,000 tech grants to 140 Detroit-based microbusinesses. Eligible businesses must be located in Detroit, have 10 or fewer employees and under $500,000 in annual revenue, and be connected to one of nine partner neighborhood/business organizations that will help select grantees. Grants can be used to buy technology like hardware, software, POS systems, e-commerce/accounting tools, and AI platforms to modernize operations and improve competitiveness.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - Must be affiliated with one of the partner organizations: East Warren Development Corp, Grandmont Rosedale Development Corporation, Live6 Alliance, Southwest Detroit Business Association, Michigan Black Business Alliance, Arab American Chamber of Commerce, ProsperUS Detroit, TechTown Detroit, and Michigan Women Forward.

Name: OpenAI Cybersecurity Grant Program
Description: The OpenAI Cybersecurity Grant Program supports the development of AI-powered defensive cybersecurity tools through funding, API credits, and other support, with applications accepted on a rolling basis. As of February 5, 2026, the program expanded to focus on large-scale deployment, committing $10M in API credits and introducing Trusted Access for Cyber alongside GPT-5.3-Codex. Grants prioritize practical, defense-focused projects that deliver broad public benefit, with awards typically made in $10,000 increments.

Name: Justworks HR & Payroll Grant
Description: The Just Thrive Program from The Well Work and Justworks provides service credits for HR and payroll support, aiming to expand equitable access to core business infrastructure for entrepreneurs. Eligible Justworks PEO customers can receive up to $6,000 (Starter Credit) if formed in the last 12 months, or up to $2,000 (Boost Credit) if the business is over a year old. To qualify, businesses must have at least 2 W-2 employees and be 50%+ owned by someone from a historically excluded group (or be an anti-racism–focused nonprofit).

Name: JobsOhio Small Business Grant
Description: The JobsOhio Small Business Grant provides up to $50,000 to eligible Ohio small businesses to help fund growth investments like facility improvements, equipment, software, and training. To qualify, a business must have $100K–$25M in annual revenue, at least one year of operating history, be in a JobsOhio target industry with primarily B2B revenue, and show the project will increase payroll/employment by at least 10%; retail and professional services are not eligible. You apply by contacting your regional JobsOhio Network Partner to confirm eligibility and start the application.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- $100k - $25M in annual revenue
- At least one year of operating history
- Be in a JobsOhio target industry with primarily B2B revenue

Name: Robert G. Wilmers Integrity Prize
Description: Annual award recognizing leaders who demonstrate integrity in leadership and service to community across fields like arts, education, environment, and social justice. In 2026 and beyond, three recipients receive $100,000 awards.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Individuals striving to better the world in eligible fields (arts, education, environment, etc.).
- May apply directly or be nominated by another person.

Name: Block Advisors by H&R Block – Small Business Financial Readiness Boost Camp (Hello Alice)
Description: Boost camp providing financial-readiness education and resources for small business owners through Hello Alice and partners. Participants receive structured training and support focused on business finances.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- U.S.-based small business owners meeting program requirements described on Hello Alice.
- Submit application through Hello Alice during the active application period.

Name: Forum Ventures B2B Accelerator
Description: Pre-seed accelerator for early B2B tech startups offering a structured program, mentorship, and an investor network. Includes operational support and a large bundle of business perks (e.g., cloud credits and tools).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Early-stage B2B tech startups (pre-seed focus).
- Teams ready to pitch via Forum’s application form and interview process.

Name: Portland Affordable Commercial Tenanting Grant
Description: The Affordable Commercial Tenanting (ACT) Grant from Prosper Portland provides reimbursement-based funding to property owners and small business owners negotiating a lease to help cover tenant improvements, permitting, and related costs to open a storefront. The program supports inclusive small business growth in the Interstate Corridor and Gateway Regional Center TIF districts, requiring at least a three-year lease with below-market or otherwise affordable terms. Eligible businesses generally include entrepreneurs with displacement history or limited access to capital, and grants can be awarded up to $300,000 depending on project scope and community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Both small business owners and property owners are eligible to apply. Property owners can be non-profit or private entities if they lease to a qualified small business.

Name: Portland Local Small Business Expanded Repair/Restore Grants
Description: The Affordable Commercial Tenanting (ACT) Grant from Prosper Portland provides reimbursement-based funding to property owners and small business owners negotiating a lease to help cover tenant improvements, permitting, and related costs to open a storefront. The program supports inclusive small business growth in the Interstate Corridor and Gateway Regional Center TIF districts, requiring at least a three-year lease with below-market or otherwise affordable terms. Eligible businesses generally include entrepreneurs with displacement history or limited access to capital, and grants can be awarded up to $300,000 depending on project scope and community impact.

Name: Portland Prosperity Investment Program (PIP)
Description: The Affordable Commercial Tenanting (ACT) Grant from Prosper Portland provides reimbursement-based funding to property owners and small business owners negotiating a lease to help cover tenant improvements, permitting, and related costs to open a storefront. The program supports inclusive small business growth in the Interstate Corridor and Gateway Regional Center TIF districts, requiring at least a three-year lease with below-market or otherwise affordable terms. Eligible businesses generally include entrepreneurs with displacement history or limited access to capital, and grants can be awarded up to $300,000 depending on project scope and community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The grant is for businesses and property owners, and may be used for both physical improvement (hard costs) and eligible consulting assistance (soft costs) to support for-profit related business and property-related improvements associated with commercial, industrial, mixed-use, and market-rate housing projects.

Name: North Miami Economic Development Small Business Grant
Description: The City of North Miami’s Economic Development Small Business Grant (funded by CDBG) offers eligible local for-profit and nonprofit businesses reimbursement of up to $7,500 for approved expenses, with businesses required to contribute at least 20% upfront. Applicants must have a physical commercial location in North Miami, be low-to-moderate income, employ no more than five full-time employees, have operated for at least one year, and meet several compliance requirements (e.g., active Sunbiz status, current city tax receipt, no liens/violations). Funds are paid in a single reimbursement after receipts are verified, and expenses made before city approval aren’t eligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify, a business owner must meet all the following:
- Be registered as a for-profit or nonprofit organization with a physical commercial location within the City of North Miami.
- Own at least 25% of the business.
- No more than one (1) application submitted per business.
- Be classified as LMI (low to moderate income) based on prior year personal and business income tax returns (please see income chart).
- Employ no more than five (5) full-time employees, including the business owner.
- Be in continuous operation for at least (1) year before your application submittal date.
- Have not received CRA or CDBG funds within the past (5) years.
- Hold a current City of North Miami Business Tax Receipt (BTR) and Certificate of Use (CU)
- Applicant must have legal immigration status in the U.S. (For more information, please see SAVE).
- Be listed as “active” on Sunbiz.org.
- Have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number via (SAM.gov).
- No more than one (1) location, not part of a national chain or franchise.
- Have no unresolved violations or liens with the City of North Miami.
- Owner/Operator or Applicant shall have no pending litigation with the City of North Miami.

Name: San Francisco Accessible Barrier Removal Grant
Description: San Francisco’s Office of Small Business offers reimbursement grants of up to $10,000 per location to help small businesses comply with ADA Title III by funding accessibility improvements such as equipment, construction, design services, CASp inspections, and permit fees. Eligible businesses must be registered in San Francisco, meet revenue and employee limits, and operate a place of public accommodation, with funds awarded on a rolling, first-come basis as available. Grants are paid as reimbursements after work is completed and documented, though businesses may apply initially with a quote for eligibility review.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Your business must: 
- Be registered in San Francisco, with a 7-digit BAN 
- Be a place of public accommodation (open to the public as defined by the Federal ADA) 
- Have less than $2.5 million in annual gross revenue for a single location 
- Have less than $8 million in gross revenue for a single business with multiple locations 
- Have a current average of 100 or fewer employees 
- Be the owner/operator of the business location 
- Property owners may only be eligible if they also own and operate the place of public accommodation.

Name: Big Grove for Good Neighborhood Micro-Grant
Description: The Big Grove for Good Neighborhood Micro-Grant Program offers $250–$1,000 rolling micro-grants to fund small, community-led projects that strengthen neighborhoods through connection, equity, and quality-of-life improvements. Eligible ideas include accessibility enhancements (ramps, benches, community fridges), environmental stewardship projects (clean-ups, tree planting), community connection events (celebrations, workshops), and neighbor-nominated support projects.

Name: Evergreen Climate Innovations Investment Application
Description: Evergreen Climate Innovations’ 501vc® Investment Fund offers $250,000 investments in pre-seed and seed climate tech startups working on mitigation, adaptation, or other environmental challenges. Eligible companies must be based in the Greater Midwest (including states like IA, IL, IN, WI, MI, MN, MO, OH, CO, NE, western PA, and others), and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis within spring/fall investment cycles lasting about five months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Focus: Climate tech across mitigation, adaptation, and other environmental challenges
- Stage: Pre-Seed and Seed
- Geography: Based in the Greater Midwest region of the United States (IA, IL, IN, WI, MI, MN, KS, MO, OH, TN, KY, ND, SD, CO, NE, and western PA)

Name: Downtown Athens, GA: Business Reach Grant for Interior Renovation
Description: The Business Reach Grant Program, run by the Athens Downtown Development Authority, offers 50% matching funds (up to $10,000) for eligible interior renovations of downtown businesses. It aims to boost employment, attract new businesses, and support existing ones — though cosmetic upgrades and routine maintenance don't qualify. Applicants must submit project details, cost estimates, and photos, and agree to maintain improvements for at least 3 years.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any business currently located in the ADDA boundary or any business that intends to open in the ADDA boundary is eligible to apply. For information regarding district boundaries, contact Rachel Swartz at 706-353-1421, or Rachel@downtownathensga.com.

Name: Ben Franklin Technology Partners Challenge Grant
Description:
The Ben Franklin Technology Partners Challenge Grant is a Pennsylvania state-funded program that provides grants to regional nonprofit organizations (the Ben Franklin Technology Partners) to invest in high-growth tech companies through funding, business assistance, and entrepreneurial infrastructure development. Partners must meet a minimum 1:1 match of private sector funds and are accountable through annual independent audits, quarterly invoices, and detailed impact reports. The program prioritizes small companies with commercial potential, requires Pennsylvania presence for at least five years post-project, and is governed by regional Boards with at least 50% private industry representation.

Funding is determined by four Ben Franklin Technology Partners: 
1. Ben Franklin Technology Partners of Southeastern Pennsylvania
2. Ben Franklin Technology Partners of Northeastern Pennsylvania
3. Ben Franklin Technology Partners of Central & Northern Pennsylvania
4. Innovation Works (Ben Franklin partner for Southwestern Pennsylvania)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Entrepreneurs
- Start-up & early-stage companies
- Established companies
- Investors
- Higher education
- Research and BFTP alumni companies

Name: Emergent Fund
Description: The Emergent Fund is a rolling, monthly rapid-response grant program supporting movement and frontline communities responding to urgent, unanticipated crises or opportunities to build power.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
-January 2026 - March 2026 grant cycles will be by invitation only. They will resume open-access, monthly rapid response grant cycle April 1st. 
- Emergent Fund accepts prescreens for grant proposals starting the 1st of the month and closes the 3rd Thursday of the month.

Our Advisory Council makes grant decisions and awards on a monthly basis, usually at the end of each month. Typically, you will receive an update on the status of your proposal within 4-5 weeks.

Eligibility: 
- Eligible applicants must have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status or a fiscal sponsor, and grants are not intended for ongoing operating support, direct services without an organizing foundation, or individuals. Open grant cycles resume April 1, 2026, with applications due the 3rd Thursday of each month at 5:00 p.m. PST.

Name: Lendistry Small Business Summer Program
Description: Small Business Summer is a program run in partnership with Lendistry that recognizes and supports small business owners in the Los Angeles area. The program is looking for LA-based businesses that serve their customers well while making a positive impact in their community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- small business owner in the LA area
- provide valuable products or services while also making a positive impact on the community

Name: Baltimore Community Spruce-Up Program
Description: The Central Baltimore Partnership's Community Spruce-Up Program awards grants of $7,500 to $25,000 for neighborhood-driven public space improvement projects across 11 Central Baltimore neighborhoods. Priority goes to projects promoting healthy living, early childhood development, and community gathering, with eligible applicants including neighborhood associations, merchant groups, and nonprofits serving the designated area. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and must include a full application, completed budget, and a letter of support from the local community association.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants may be neighborhood associations, merchant groups, or other not-for-profit organizations located in, or serving, the neighborhoods of Abell, Barclay, Charles North, Charles Village, East Baltimore-Midway, Greenmount West, Harwood, Oakenshawe, Old Goucher, Remington,  Wyman Park, and/or the Waverly Main Street.

Name: Downtown Partnership of Baltimore's Facade Improvement Program
Description: The Downtown Partnership of Baltimore's Facade Improvement Program provides grants to business and property owners for exterior upgrades including signage, awnings, lighting, masonry repair, and window and door improvements within Downtown Baltimore. The program is administered in coordination with the Baltimore Development Corporation, and all improvements must meet DPOB's Storefront Criteria. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
DPOB FIP funds must be used for eligible exterior improvements identified in BDC's FIG Application. Applicants must have evidence of ownership or have an executed letter of intent/lease for property located within the Downtown Management Authority (DMA) district. At DPOB's discretion, FIP funds may be issued as an advance that, when spent, can serve as the upfront cost required to request reimbursement from BDC for their matching funds. 



Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Prior to applying to BDC's and DPOB's facade programs, a site visit will be required. To make an appointment for a site visit, or to discuss your plans further and verify alignment with DPOB's Storefront Criteria, please contact econdev@dpob.org

Name: BNIA- Jacob France Institute Technical Assistance
Description: The Baltimore Neighborhood Indicators Alliance (BNIA-JFI) is offering free technical assistance to Baltimore City nonprofits, community organizations, and academic institutions, including help with survey design, data analysis, GIS mapping, and navigating publicly available community datasets. Organizations can request up to one hour of pro bono assistance per year by emailing bnia@ubalt.edu with details about their needs and timeline. BNIA-JFI anticipates taking on one to three pro bono requests per month, so early submissions are encouraged.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
Reach out to us at bnia@ubalt.edu with the following information:
- Your personal information, including name, title, organization, email or phone number.
- Whom does your organization serve?
- What do you need assistance with?
- What information sources have you already looked at?
- If you are planning to use this information to apply for a grant or any other time-sensitive publication, please include information on where you are sending it and what the due date is.

Name: Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant for Artists
Description: The Pollock-Krasner Foundation awards unrestricted grants of up to $50,000 to professional painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, with funds usable for any purpose that supports the artist's practice, including new work, studio space, supplies, or living expenses. There is no deadline as applications are accepted on a rolling basis, and the review process typically takes nine to twelve months. The grant is open to actively exhibiting visual artists worldwide, excluding students, and does not fund video, photography, generative art, performance, film, or craft.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: professional visual artists who are painters, sculptors, and/or artists who work on paper, including printmakers.

Name: Ohio TechCred
Description: Ohio’s TechCred program helps employers upskill workers by reimbursing up to $2,000 per employee for completing approved, short-term, technology-focused credentials. Eligible Ohio employers apply for funding, sponsor employees’ training, and receive reimbursement after workers successfully earn credentials and submit required documentation. The program emphasizes industry-recognized, tech-related skills and is open to businesses of all sizes, with a maximum of $30,000 in reimbursement per application period.

Name: Beta Boom Investment
Description: Beta Boom is a venture capital firm that invests in pre-seed and seed stage software companies outside of Silicon Valley, focusing on areas like enterprise solutions, fintech, digital health, and SaaS. They typically participate in funding rounds of $2.5M or less with valuations under $10M, and require U.S. incorporation (preferring Delaware C-Corps). They do not invest in hardware, e-commerce, crypto, biotech, or several other industries, and do not fund companies headquartered outside the U.S. or in the San Francisco Bay Area.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Beta Boom invests $350-500K in pre-seed software startups led by founders who defy the Silicon Valley mold. Startups must be based in the U.S. and outside of Silicon Valley.

Eligibility:

We invest in software companies in a broad range of industries.
If in doubt, please apply.

Name: Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity Food Cart Program
Description: The Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity (DEO) is distributing at least 280 free, California Health Code-compliant food carts to sidewalk vendors operating in unincorporated LA County or the City of Los Angeles, funded through the American Rescue Plan Act. Four cart types are available (cold-hold, cut fruit, hot holding, and integrated grill), and selected vendors must obtain the necessary permits before receiving their cart. Applications opened January 12, 2026 and will remain open while supplies last, with the full process from application to cart pickup taking up to 12 weeks.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To ensure applicants are ready to acquire their permits, all applicants must be at least 18 years old and submit the following:

California Seller’s Permit
Note: A Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is required to obtain a Seller’s Permit.
Government-issued photo identification (Driver’s license, passport of any country, Matricula Consular, etc.)
Doing Business As (DBA)/Fictitious Business Name Filing, required for any business that operates under a name that is different from the owner’s legal last name or the name of the registered entity
If vending in the City of L.A., applicants must also submit a City of L.A. Business Tax Registration Certification (BTRC)

Must be a sidewalk vendor that vends food (non-prepackaged).
Must also be self-employed and operate no more than one permitted cart from a location at any given time, which would include the awarded cart.
Applicants may NOT apply on behalf of an employer.

Applicants must:

Live in Los Angeles County
Operate a vending business in either:
Unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County, or
The City of Los Angeles
Applicants will be required to provide operating location(s) and residential address.

To find out if you operate in eligible vending business areas of the County or the City, please visit the links below:


*When using the LA County District Locator tool 1) input your address and 2) if results include the word “Unincorporated” it means the address provided is within the unincorporated area of LA County.

**When using LA City neighborhoodinfo.lacity.gov, enter the address(es) where you operate without any periods (e.g. 14410 Sylvan St instead of 14410 Sylvan St.). If not in the City, it will not show any results.


Must be an existing business currently in operations and operating continuously for more than 12 consecutive months.

The vendor will be asked to provide the following:

Business license, vendor permit, and other similar documentation OR
Vendor declaration confirming date of operation and business-related records

Applicants with household annual income above $75,000 are not eligible. Businesses may submit tax returns, profit and loss statements, or other similar documentation.

Businesses operating in the City of Los Angeles must have experienced financial loss and impact because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Those NOT awarded a Small Business Mobility Fund Formalization Grant will be prioritized. If applying to operate a cart in the City of Los Angeles, cannot have previously received an ARPA-funded grant or award.


Applicants cannot have a record of repeatedly violating Health and Safety regulations. Businesses with a record may be considered if able to prove significant effort towards addressing violations and meeting the requirements set forth by the County’s and City’s sidewalk vending regulations.

Optional Documentation:

Statement and any supporting documentation addressing any past violations, if applicable
Documentation showing corrective actions, if applicable

Applicants will have to show proof of ability to transport and store carts in accordance with CA Health Code Regulations prior to being awarded a cart.

Required Documentation:

Photographs of storage space
Storage agreement or letter from property owner (if not storing at home)
Brief explanation of transportation method and vehicle description

Name: City of Chicago Sidewalk Cafe
Description:
Through the BACP-issued sidewalk café permit, brick-and-mortar retail food establishments and tavern licenses can extend onto the sidewalk directly in front of or adjacent to their establishment. Chicago’s sidewalk café season runs from March 1 through the end of February, and permits are required; this year, businesses can choose a new 2-year permit option instead of renewing annually. Applications must be completed online through the BACP portal with required documents like a valid business license, insurance, site photo, and site plan, and café setups must meet rules on enclosure, pedestrian clearance, posting permits, ADA seating, and removability.

Costs start at $600 and rise based on café size, and alcohol service is allowed only for businesses with a valid liquor license and dram shop insurance; BYOB is not allowed. Separate permits are needed for things like pergolas, and seating in parking areas must be permitted through CDOT instead.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Required Documentation:
- Valid Retail Food Establishment or Tavern Business License
- General Liability Insurance & Policy Endorsement Page, and Dram Shop Insurance if Serving Liquor
- Photograph of Proposed Site
- Site Plan of Sidewalk Café
- If Extending, Proof of Notice to Neighboring Business

Permit Requirements: 
- Cafes must be located on the sidewalk only.
- Cafes may extend in front of a neighboring property that is not a retail food or retail liquor establishment. If extending, applicants must show proof that they have notified the neighboring owner and occupant of their plans. Insurance must cover the full extent of the cafe boundaries.
- Cafes must have a boundary that fully encloses the permitted area and separates the area from the remainder of the public way (other than the entrance). Entrances must be 3-5ft wide and shown on site plan.
- There must be a 6-foot clearance for pedestrians along the sidewalk, and the cafe must have at least 1 foot of clearance from the curb line.
- Once approved and paid, sidewalk cafe permits must be printed and posted along with the cafe site plan on the exterior wall or window of the main entrance to the business.

Name: Newark Alliance Grants
Description: he Newark Alliance's Experience Newark Event Sponsorship Program offers micro-grants of $500 to $2,500 to Newark-based nonprofits, community groups, small businesses, and residents who host public events that celebrate Newark's culture, drive foot traffic to commercial areas, and engage the community. The program runs in six cycles throughout the year, with the current open cycle (Cycle 3) focused exclusively on FIFA World Cup–themed indoor events between June 27–July 19, 2026, with an application deadline of April 1, 2026. A Summer cycle (Cycle 4) is also upcoming, covering events from July 20–September 14, 2026, with applications closing June 15, 2026.

Eligible events must be FIFA World Cup– or soccer-themed and aligned with official FIFA World Cup matches. Events should meaningfully engage attendees around the World Cup through programming, activities, or live match viewings and must be open to the public. To qualify, your business must host an indoor event or utilize outdoor space on private property, so that a Special Event Permit or Department of Public Safety resources will not be needed for street closures or public safety.

Applicants proposing to host FIFA World Cup watch parties must apply for and obtain the appropriate public viewing license through FIFA for their proposed match dates. For more information visit https://publicviewing.fifa.org/public_viewing .
