Name: Plug In Ventures' Pre-Accelerator
Description: Plug In Ventures' Pre-Accelerator is designed for early-stage Black and Latinx founders who are pre-revenue or early-stage, working toward product-market fit, and preparing to launch, fundraise, or apply to accelerators. The program offers mentorship, tools, investor access, and strategic connections to help founders move from idea to traction with a scalable, tech-enabled company.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is Eligible to Apply? 
- Pre-revenue or early-stage
- Pre-MVP or MVP-ready
- Preparing to apply for accelerators or raise funding
- Focused on product-market fit
- Looking to validate their business model or customer demand
- Committed to growing a scalable, tech-enabled company

Name: The Standard's Corporate Giving Program
Description: The Standard's Corporate Giving Program awards grants of $500 to $25,000, averaging around $3,000, to 501(c)(3) nonprofits aligned with one of four focus areas: Healthy Communities, Disability and Empowerment, Cultural Development, or Education and Advancement. Priority goes to organizations serving communities where The Standard's employees live and work. There are no set deadlines; applications are reviewed year-round with decisions communicated within about four weeks.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a charitable, nonprofit, tax-exempt organization under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Service code
- All requests for funding must be submitted through the online portal
- Must align with at least one of the four focus areas: Healthy Communities, Disability and Empowerment, Cultural Development, or Education and Advancement
- Priority to organizations serving communities where The Standard's employees live and work
- Excludes individuals, political activities, and certain sponsorships or restricted uses

Grants range $500 - $25,000 (average ~$3,000). Reviewed year-round, decisions within about four weeks.

Related: the separate Standard Charitable Foundation offers grants of $5,000 to $25,000 (average $10,000) in the same focus areas excluding Cultural Development, with a more selective invitation-based full application process and trustees meeting twice yearly.
Industry: Nonprofit,Economic Empowerment,Social Impact,Health / Wellness,Education & Child Care

Name: Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation Youth Enrichment Grant
Description: The Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation awards grant funding of up to $10,000 to non-profit organizations with youth service and enrichment programs, such as after-school programs, support for computer labs, educational scholarships, families and youth in abuse and domestic violence situations.

Name: Chicago Neighborhood Retail Activation Program
Description: Chicago’s Neighborhood Retail Activation Program supports small businesses and commercial corridors harmed by the 2023 and 2024 summer storms, especially those that depend on foot traffic. The program focuses on specific corridors in Austin, Belmont Cragin, and West Garfield Park, with local delegate agencies managing outreach and selection for interested business owners and property owners.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Specific corridors in Austin, Belmont Cragin, and West Garfield Park.

Name: LvlUp Ventures Ecosystem Funding for CPG brands
Description: LvlUp Ventures’ CPG Fund is part of a centralized funding appliation that allows founders to apply once to access LvlUp funds and 25+ venture partners, along with pitch competitions and execution programs. The CPG Fund specifically provides $10,000–$150,000+ strategic investments to early-stage consumer brands, paired with hands-on support in fundraising, marketing, and DTC growth, as well as access to a broader ecosystem of investors, tools, and scaling resources.

Name: NYC CoolRoofs Program
Description: NYC CoolRoofs is a City of New York program that installs energy-saving reflective roof coatings on eligible buildings to reduce heat, lower carbon emissions, and improve air quality, while also providing paid workforce training and construction credentials to job-seeking New Yorkers. No-cost installations are available to nonprofits, affordable housing, schools, hospitals, and cultural centers, while other building owners can receive low-cost installations by covering only the price of the coating material. The program is a partnership between the NYC Department of Small Business Services, the Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice, and The HOPE Program, with an annual goal of coating one million square feet of rooftops.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Rooftop Criteria

Your building must meet all the following criteria to be eligible for coating with the NYC CoolRoofs Program.

The rooftop must be flat.
The rooftop must be in good condition with minimal cracking.
The roof must be easily accessible (no hatch, ladder, or window access).
The roof must be free of dangerous machinery or equipment that could impede work or put workers at risk.
The roof must have appropriate 3’8” parapet.
The roof must be one of the following types:
Granulated cap sheet
Asphalt
Modified bitumen
Bitumen
Cost

NYC CoolRoofs offers cool roof installations at no cost or low cost to select buildings as outlined below, with priority given to non-profits and affordable housing.

No-cost installations are offered to:

Non-profits
Affordable/low-income housing
Community or recreational centers
Schools/colleges/universities
Hospitals or medical care clinics
Museums/theaters/other cultural centers
Select cooperatively owned housing
Low-cost installations are offered to:

All other building owners that can cover the cost of the coating, which is provided at a discounted rate through vendors participating in the NYC CoolRoofs program. NYC CoolRoofs will provide the labor, technical assistance, and materials (e.g. paint brushes, rollers, gloves, etc.) at no charge if the building owner(s) pays for the coating.

Name: Gowanus Business Relocation Grant Program
Description: The Gowanus Business Relocation Grant Program offers grants of up to $50,000 to small businesses displaced by New York City's rezoning of the Gowanus area in Brooklyn, to help offset the costs of relocating to an eligible site within New York City. Businesses must be located within the designated rezoned blocks and lots and demonstrate a direct business loss resulting from the rezoning. The program is available through 2031 and is administered by the NYC Department of Small Business Services, with funding dependent on availability.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements
Businesses may apply for a grant by submitting a complete application to the NYC Department of Small Business Services (SBS).

Applicants must be within the designated block and lots of the rezoned area and demonstrate their eligibility to the satisfaction of SBS.

Key documents required as part of the application include, but are not limited to:

- Copy of lease for the move-out location
- Evidence of direct business loss(es) which can include business financial statements, federal and local tax statements, and other documentation requested by SBS to verify loss
- Use this tool to determine if your business has experienced direct loss as a result of the city’s rezoning of the Gowanus area in Brooklyn (Microsoft Excel format)
- Itemized list of moving/relocation costs, including date, dollar amount and corresponding invoice(s), and proof of payment (e.g. canceled checks, bank statements, credit card statements, etc.)
- Any other documentation requested by SBS to ensure program qualification

Name: LA Commercial Acquisition Fund
Description: The LA County Commercial Acquisition Fund (CAF) is a public-private partnership that provides forgivable loans to small businesses, nonprofits, and mission-aligned developers to purchase vacant or underutilized commercial properties throughout Los Angeles County, with the goal of revitalizing commercial corridors and reducing small business displacement. Awardees must agree to 30-year property covenants requiring below-market rents, community-serving tenants, and at least 51% of commercial space leased to small businesses. The Cycle Two application is expected to open May 5, 2026, with priority given to projects along specific commercial corridors in each of the five LA County Supervisorial Districts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small Businesses

A for-profit entity that is independently owned and operated and is not dominant in its field of operation. It must have $16 million or less in average gross annual revenue receipts in the most recent three years with 100 employees or fewer (or a manufacturer with 25 or fewer employees) as defined by the State of California.¹


Non-profit Organizations

All types of active nonprofit organizations with legal standing, including community development corporations, and community land trusts). Non-profits must be active and in good legal standing, with Nonprofits Articles of Incorporation; Organization Bylaws; Organizational Chart of Entity and Affiliates; and 501(c)(3) articles of incorporation.  


Small-scale Developers

A real estate development entity with a background in commercial or mixed-use projects, serving local and regional County of LA residents. To be eligible, it must be independently owned and operated (not a subsidiary or affiliate of a larger national or institutional development firm); has a cumulative development volume of $50 million or less over the past five years; has completed or currently owns no more than five income-producing properties or projects.¹

Name: Home Depot Foundation Path to Pro Education Grant
Description: The Home Depot Foundation's Path to Pro Education Grants program offers grants of up to $10,000 to accredited K-12 schools, community and technical colleges, and nonprofits with existing construction trades programs, to modernize training spaces or purchase tools and equipment. Part of a $1 million investment across all 50 states, the program aims to help address the skilled labor gap in construction as 41% of the current workforce is expected to retire by 2031. Applications are accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis with no set deadline.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What organizations qualify for this program?
- Accredited K-12 schools with an existing construction skilled trade program
- Accredited post-secondary institutions (community and technical colleges) with an existing construction skilled trade program
- 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations with an existing construction skilled trade program

Name: American Heart Association Ventures - Social Impact Funds
Description: The American Heart Association's Social Impact Funds provide financing to both nonprofit and for-profit organizations working to address social drivers of health — specifically in the areas of health care access, food security, and economic empowerment — with a focus on under-resourced communities. The funds pair financing with capacity-building support, and any financial returns generated are recycled back into the program. To date, more than $45 million has been committed across 155+ organizations nationwide, though no specific grant application or deadline information was listed — interested organizations should contact the AHA directly for funding opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
Entrepreneurs and organizations addressing social drivers of health in under-resourced communities are eligible to apply. We support both for-profit and nonprofit organizations whose programs align with the Association’s mission and the Social Impact Funds focus areas.

Name: AlphaLab Pittsburgh Accelerator
Description: AlphaLab is Pittsburgh's leading startup accelerator, operating since 2008 across four specialized tracks — Software, Gear (hardware), Health (life sciences), and Robotics — providing founders with capital, mentorship, workspace, and a collaborative community focused on customer acquisition and investor readiness. The program takes a cohort-based approach tailored to each founder's industry, with strong ties to Pittsburgh's tech ecosystem and institutions like Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Pittsburgh. No specific application deadline or funding amount was listed, so interested founders should visit AlphaLab's website or attend virtual office hours for current cycle details.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Paving Paths to Success for Entrepreneurs
AlphaLab is Pittsburgh’s leading accelerator and has been supporting startups since 2008. We cover several focus areas, including software, hardware, life sciences, and robotics. All participants receive the same core support, with resources tailored to their industry.


AlphaLab Tracks

1. Software track 

AlphaLab Software is one of the earliest and most prestigious software startup accelerators in the nation. Established in 2008 as one of the first accelerators in the U.S., it has grown into one of the premier programs that make Pittsburgh a technology hub.


2. Gear Track

AlphaLab Gear helps hardware startups refine their products, strengthen their supply chain, and go to market. Established in 2013 as one of the first three dedicated hardware accelerators in the world, this track addresses the 75% of the economy devoted to physical goods.


3. Health Track


AlphaLab Health gives life sciences startups a real-world proving ground for their products. Established in 2020 as a collaboration with Allegheny Health Network, AlphaLab Health equips startups with capital, clinical mentorship, private office space, and biosafety level 1 (BSL-1) laboratories.


4. Robotics Track
The Robotics Factory Accelerate program capitalizes on Pittsburgh’s unparalleled strength in building robotics and automation companies. The program gives founders the tools they need to go from concept to commercialization by providing guidance on business and building prototypes and offering access to manufacturing resources, including a production-grade prototype scale shop.

Explore More

Name: Samsung Mobile Advances
Description: Samsung Mobile Advances (SMA) is an open innovation program that provides non-dilutive grant funding, mentorship from Samsung experts, and opportunities for strategic partnerships and potential investment to startups working on technologies relevant to Samsung's mobile ecosystem. Eligible startups must be headquartered in the U.S., Canada, Europe, Israel, China, Japan, or India, and work in areas such as AI, XR, health, foldables, wearables, connectivity, or security. Applications for SMA 2026 are currently open, with pitch day in September and final selections announced by end of October 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Areas of Interest
We are interested in startups working across, but not limited to: AI, XR, Power, Health, Camera, Audio, Foldable, Wearable, Sensors, Materials, Connectivity, and Security.

Locations
Startups headquartered in the following regions are eligible to apply: Europe, the United States, Canada, Israel, China, Japan, and India.


STEP 1. Application Submission
Submit a 6-month project proposal outlining your proof-of-concept development plan and its potential impact for Samsung Mobile.


STEP 2. Application Review
Our team will review your proposal. You will be notified of the outcome by August.


STEP 3. Pitch Day & Final Announcement
Shortlisted applicants will be invited to Pitch Day in September to present their projects to a panel of Samsung experts. Final selections will be made and announced by the end of October.

Name: San Francisco Downtown Business Fund
Description: The Downtown Business Fund, launched in April 2026, provides move-in grants of up to $500,000, affordable loans of $100,000 to $1 million with discounted interest rates, and expert technical assistance to businesses looking to open or expand along the Powell Street and Moscone Convention Center corridors in downtown San Francisco. The fund prioritizes experience-driven, tourism-oriented, and anchor businesses with strong plans and proven track records that will activate street life and drive foot traffic to these priority corridors. Applications are evaluated on a rolling monthly basis with limited funds available, so early submission is encouraged.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Criteria
The Downtown Business Fund seeks to support:

Established, credible operators of all sizes with strong business plans and proven experience
Experience-driven and tourism-oriented businesses that activate street life
Anchor businesses that will drive further investment and foot traffic
Existing businesses on priority corridors making meaningful investment to drive new audiences, offerings, and communities to downtown
Our priority areas along the Powell Street Corridor, from Union Square to Market Street, and the Moscone Center Corridor along Stockton and 4th streets.

Name: City of Richmond - Small Business Facade Improvement Program
Description: The Richmond Small Business Facade Improvement Program offers grants of up to $15,000 per commercial address to small businesses in Richmond's Transformative Climate Communities areas — specifically the Iron Triangle, Coronado, and Santa Fe neighborhoods — for exterior storefront upgrades that improve curb appeal, safety, and visibility. The program has $300,000 in total funding available and is designed to revitalize commercial corridors and support locally owned retail businesses. The program launched December 29, 2025 and remains open through December 2026 or until funds are exhausted, with early applications encouraged.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small Business Facade Improvement Program
The Richmond Small Business Facade Improvement Program helps small businesses in the Transformative Climate Communities (TCC) coverage areas make impactful upgrades to their storefronts—enhancing curb appeal, improving safety, and increasing visibility to attract more customers.



With $300,000 in total funding available, eligible businesses can receive grants of up to $15,000 per commercial address in the TCC areas (Iron Triangle, Coronado and Santa Fe) for exterior improvements that strengthen both their business and the surrounding community.



This program is designed to:

Revitalize Richmond’s commercial corridors with vibrant, welcoming storefronts
Support small, locally owned retail businesses
Boost economic activity and community pride


The program launches December 29, 2025 and will remain open through December 2026, or until all funds are awarded.



Funding is limited—early applications are encouraged.

Name: City of El Monte 2026 Small Business Grant Program
Description: The City of El Monte's 2026 Small Business Grant Program offers grants to eligible businesses located within El Monte city limits that have been in continuous operation for at least six months and are in good standing with the City. Funds are limited and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, with businesses that have previously received City grant funding, home-based or online businesses, and those in gaming, liquor, tobacco, marijuana, or manufacturing categories all ineligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
City of El Monte 2026 Small Business Grant Program
The 2026 El Monte Small Business Grant Program is currently accepting applications from eligible businesses. To qualify, businesses must have been in continuous operation for a minimum of six (6) months, be in good standing with the City, and submit all required documentation at the time of application.

Applications may be downloaded or obtained in person at the Housing Counter located in City Hall West during regular business hours. Only complete applications with all required documents will be accepted.

Grant funds are limited and will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Businesses that have previously received funding through this program are not eligible to reapply. The City reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate the program at any time without prior notice. Submission of an application does not constitute or guarantee approval or award of grant funds.

Ineligible Businesses:
Businesses that meet one of the following criteria are not eligible for participation in the program. 
     • Business that has previously received grant funding from the City 

     • Business that does not meet qualifications for LMA or LMJ National Objectives 

     • Businesses that fall into the following categories: gaming, liquor or tobacco stores, marijuana dispensaries

        and manufacturing 

     • Business or activity that does not comply with local, state or federal laws 

     • Businesses with active code violations 

     • Home-based or online businesses 

     • Businesses outside of the City of El Monte city boundaries 

     • Businesses currently in the process of bankruptcy proceedings

Name: DIV FUND
Description: The DIV Fund is a development-focused R&D grant program that supports innovative solutions with the potential to cost-effectively improve millions of lives, offering three stages of funding: Stage 1 Pilot grants up to $200,000, Stage 2 Test & Scale grants up to $500,000, and Stage 3 Scale grants up to $1.5 million. All innovations are evaluated on three core criteria — evidence of impact, cost-effectiveness, and potential to reach over 1 million people at scale — with applications accepted on a rolling basis year-round through an online portal. The fund is open to a wide range of applicants and scaling pathways, including government, philanthropic, and private market routes.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What We Fund
The DIV Fund is an R&D engine for development, supporting innovative solutions with the potential to cost-effectively improve millions of lives.

We combine risk-tolerant capital with evidence-driven decision-making to back bold ideas, identify what works, and scale the most cost-effective innovations. Our portfolio approach balances experimentation with evidence, while our tiered funding model right-sizes risk.

Our Funding Stages
The DIV Fund offers three stages of grants. Across all stages, we prioritize investments that maximize expected social returns. To assess this, we consider key drivers of social returns in our reviews, such as unit costs, per-person impact, and crucially, scaling potential, including the probability of greater scale as a result of DIV Fund investment.

Name: Smart & Final Charitable Foundation
Description: The Smart & Final Charitable Foundation provides donations to local nonprofit organizations in communities it serves, especially groups focused on health and wellness, education, hunger relief, youth sports and development, and disaster relief. Eligible applicants must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits located in California, Arizona, and Nevada, and aligned with one of the foundation’s giving priorities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Smart & Final Charitable Foundation strives to give back to and nourish the communities we serve in California, Arizona and Nevada through our Pillars of Focus:
Health & Wellness
Education
Hunger Relief
Team Sports & Youth Development
Disaster Relief

If your non-profit organization is located in a community we serve, is registered as a 501(c)3 and meets one of the Pillars of Focus, we encourage you to apply for a donation.

Name: BOK Financial Grants
Description: BOK Financial and the BOKF Foundation contribute an average of $8 million to nearly 800 nonprofit organizations each year, focusing on improving quality of life and economic wellbeing in Arkansas, Arizona, Colorado, Kansas, Missouri, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas. Their giving is guided by four pillars: basic needs (supporting services like food, housing, healthcare, and safety for vulnerable populations), education (advancing access to quality education from early childhood through higher education and financial literacy), economic development (strengthening local economies through workforce development, job training, and community investment), and community partnerships (including strategic support for organizations like United Way that mobilize resources and collective impact across communities).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Must be a 501(c)3 serving one of the following areas:
Arizona -Phoenix Area
Arkansas - Fayetteville/Bentonville Area,
Colorado - Denver/Boulder/Colorado Springs
Kansas/Missouri - Greater Kansas City
New Mexico - Greater Albuquerque Area
Tennessee - Greater Memphis Area
Texas - Austin
Texas - Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex
Texas - Greater Houston
Texas - San Antonio
Oklahoma

Name: Missouri Arts Council Express Grants
Description: The Missouri Arts Council grant program is designed to support and expand Missouri’s arts ecosystem by funding organizations that provide public access to arts, cultural programming, and arts education, while also strengthening the economic and community impact of the creative sector. Its broader goal is to invest in sustainable arts infrastructure across the state, ensuring that artists, audiences, and communities benefit from increased opportunity, visibility, and resources.

Name: Kickstarter x Google Next Wave Fund
Description: The Next Wave Fund is a joint initiative by Google and Kickstarter that supports early-stage tech startups and small businesses with funding, training, and resources to help them launch and grow through crowdfunding. Selected participants receive a $10,000 pledge toward their Kickstarter campaign, hands-on guidance, access to Google training programs, and marketing exposure. The program targets small teams building innovative products in areas like hardware, software, gaming, and connected technology, with applications accepted on a rolling basis.

Name: Lynwood Commercial Facade Improvement Program
Description: The City of Lynwood's Commercial Façade Improvement Program offers financial assistance of up to $20,000 to eligible businesses and property owners on Atlantic Avenue, Imperial Highway, and Long Beach Boulevard for exterior improvements including painting, signage, door and window repairs, lighting, security bar removal, and anti-graffiti film. The program is available on a first-come, first-served basis with limited funding, and is open to retail, restaurant, and service businesses on the designated main corridors. To apply, contact Avant Garde city consultants at (909) 816-5623 or mibarra@agi.com.co, or pick up an application at the Community Development Department at 11330 Bullis Road.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Businesses:

Businesses on main corridors: Atlantic Avenue, Imperial Highway, and Long Beach Boulevard
Retail, restaurant, or service businesses
Commercial properties that include retail, restaurant, or service businesses
Other commercial business or property types (cultural, office, etc.) may be considered on a case-by-case basis if located within one of the designated main corridors

Eligible Improvements:

Exterior painting (city-approved neutral or earth-tone colors per Ord. #1572)
Door and window repair or replacement
Installation of anti-graffiti film on windows and doors
Roof parapet walls to screen or enhance rooftop equipment
Professionally designed signage
Lighting improvements, including safety lighting
Security bar removal
Optional: Enhanced security features (video surveillance, upgraded locks, etc.)
Correction of code violations

Supplementary Façade Improvements:

Decorative brick, stone veneer, and/or tile accents
Decorative roof parapet walls
Moldings, cornices, and trim
Landscaping improvements

Name: Google AI Certificate for Small Businesses
Description: Grow with Google offers free AI training and tools for small businesses, including the Google AI Professional Certificate, tutorial videos, and resources for using AI in marketing, finance, operations, and strategy. Eligible SMBs can also access three months of Google AI Pro and Google Workspace Business Standard at no cost, with enrollment and redemption deadlines in December 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: This offer is specifically available to small and medium-sized businesses based in the United States. To qualify, your business must have 500 employees or less and possess a valid Employer Identification Number (EIN). These scholarships are intended to help local businesses upskill their workforce and remain competitive by adopting essential AI skills through the Google AI training available on Coursera.

Name: W.K. Kellogg Foundation
Description: The W.K. Kellogg Foundation funds community-driven work that helps children, families and communities thrive, especially around early childhood, maternal and child health, food systems, family-sustaining career pathways and racial equity. Grants are open year-round, with priority geographies in the U.S. plus parts of Mexico and Haiti; applicants start by submitting an LOI through Fluxx and typically receive next steps within 30 business days.

Name: City of Santa Ana Small Business Incentive Program
Description: The City of Santa Ana's Small Business Incentive Program offers reimbursement grants of up to $5,000 for commercial locations and up to $2,500 for home-based businesses to for-profit microenterprises with 5 or fewer employees that have been in operation no more than three years. Funded by HUD's Community Development Block Grant program, eligible businesses must be located in Santa Ana, hold a valid business license, and have household income within 80% of the Orange County median income limits. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis — interested businesses should contact Gabriela Cramer at (714) 647-5385 or Gcramer@santa-ana.org for current availability.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Summary of Eligibility Requirements:

Businesses must meet the following eligibility requirements:

Located in Santa Ana and in operation no more than 3 years from the date of the application
Microenterprise - a for-profit business with 5 or fewer employees (including all owners)
Valid and Active Santa Ana Business License
Valid Certificate of Occupancy or Home Occupation Permit issued by the City of Santa Ana
Income Eligible: The business owner(s) and household family income for all family members 18+ must be within 80% of the Orange County median income limits set by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) - 2025 Income Limits (Effective April 1, 2025).
Income is based on Adjusted Gross Income, Line 11 of most recent IRS 1040 Tax Returns

Name: Bank of America Neighborhood Builders
Description: Bank of America's Neighborhood Builders program awards grants of $100,000 to $400,000 paid over two years to established 501(c)(3) nonprofits focused on stable housing (affordable housing, rental housing, homeownership) or income creation (workforce development, entrepreneurship, financial resilience), with the grant capped at 10% of the organization's most recent annual revenue. Recipients participate in a two-year leadership development program for both their Executive Director and an Emerging Leader, both of whom must have been at the organization for at least two years.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To become a Neighborhood Builder®:

You must be a recognized 501(C)(3) nonprofit by the IRS
The total grant amount cannot exceed 10% of your organization’s most recent annual revenue. Neighborhood Builders® awards range from $100,000 to $400,000 paid over two years.
For example, an organization with $1 million in annual revenue would be eligible for an award of $100,000 paid over 2 years.
Serve communities in these markets
Have filed taxes with the IRS for each of the last two fiscal years and be financially sound
Have at least a three-year plan to advance the impact of your nonprofit’s mission
Be able to participate in a two-year leadership training program for both your nonprofit Executive Director/President/CEO and an Emerging Leader
Have an Executive Director/President/CEO and an Emerging Leader that have been at the organization for at least two years (in role)
Agree to return your learnings to your community and nonprofit team
Not have received grant funding from Bank of America Neighborhood Builders® or Champions program on or after October 2019
2026 awardees must align to the following funding areas
Stable housing: Creation and preservation of affordable housing, long-term rental housing, and home ownership opportunities.
Income Creation: Workforce development, advancing entrepreneurship, and financial resilience.

Name: Baton Rouge Area Foundation E.J. and Marjory B. Ourso Family Foundation Fund
Description: The E.J. and Marjory B. Ourso Family Foundation Fund, administered through the Baton Rouge Area Foundation, supports nonprofit organizations serving South Louisiana with creative or beneficial projects in education, healthcare, human services, and religion. Priority is given to projects that build on human initiative and service to others, and applicants must submit a detailed application including a project summary, narrative, budget, financial documents, board authorization, IRS determination letter, and related attachments. Proposals are reviewed quarterly, and funded organizations must provide both fiscal and narrative reports on how the grant was used and its community impact.

Name: Michigan Consumers Energy Foundation Grant
Description: The Consumers Energy Foundation funds capital projects, programs, and operating support that benefit Michigan communities, especially in areas where Consumers Energy has a business presence in the Lower Peninsula. Grants must align with the foundation’s priorities of People, Planet, and Prosperity, including reducing poverty and supporting vulnerable residents, protecting Michigan’s land, water, and air, and strengthening local economies through neighborhood revitalization, job growth, entrepreneurship, arts, and culture.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: We are primarily focused on communities in Michigan's Lower Peninsula where Consumers Energy has a business presence. We will consider requests from organizations located elsewhere for programs or projects that significantly benefit our state and the communities served by Consumers Energy.

Name: Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation Grants
Description: The Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation accepts grant applications year-round from organizations working in Southeast Michigan and Western New York within its focus areas. The foundation prioritizes established organizations with creative, bold, feasible projects that address important regional needs, offer strong community impact, and may involve coalition-based approaches.

Name: PNC Foundation Grow Up Great Grant
Description: The PNC Foundation provides grants to eligible tax-exempt nonprofit organizations in communities where PNC has a significant presence, with a focus on early childhood education and economic development. Its education funding emphasizes PNC Grow Up Great initiatives serving children from birth to age five, especially children from low- to moderate-income families, while economic development grants may support affordable housing, small business assistance, community services, arts and culture, and neighborhood revitalization.

Name: San Francisco Green Business Program
Description: The San Francisco Green Business Program offers up to $1,000 in prebates or rebates to help businesses pay for climate-friendly purchases and upgrades. Eligible expenses can include LED lighting, ventilation system upgrades, water-efficient plumbing fixtures, 100% renewable energy, compostable or reusable foodware, ENERGY STAR equipment, eco-friendly cleaning products, and recycled-content paper products.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Prebates and rebates are available on a first-come first-served basis for newly recognized Entry-Level or Certified San Francisco Green Businesses.

Businesses must meet at least one of the following criteria:
Annual revenue less than $250,000, OR
Is a non-profit organization, or a fiscally sponsored project of a non-profit organization, OR
Is located in one of the following zip codes: 94102, 94103, 94107, 94108, 94109, 94110, 94112, 94115, 94116, 94118, 94121, 94124, 94127, 94130, 94132, 94133 or 94134

Name: Makahakama Foundation Launchpad Program
Description: Makahakama Foundation’s LaunchPad program supports under-resourced U.S. entrepreneurs with annual revenue between $20,000 and $250,000 by providing hands-on financial mentorship, bookkeeping support, accounting tools, and practical education. Participants receive four months of 1:1 support from a bookkeeper mentor, access to classes and clinics, and a $500 grant upon successful completion of program milestones. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
LaunchPad is designed for under-resourced entrepreneurs who:
- Are physically located and fully operating in the United States
- Have annual revenue between $20,000-$250,000
- Aspire to hire employees in the future
- Want to develop strong financial habits and learn how to read and interpret financial statements
- Feel challenged to afford professional bookkeeping services
- Are open to using technology to digitize their business and have
access to a smartphone, computer and internet
- Are comfortable speaking and understanding English
- Are committed to engaging in the program and
completing surveys

Name: Seattle SmART Ventures Grant
Description: Seattle’s SmART Ventures grant is a year-round, small-awards program that provides $500–$1,500 for innovative arts and culture projects that expand cultural participation, especially for underserved communities or applicants who may not qualify for other City arts funding. Applicants must attend an information session before applying, and projects are evaluated on audience expansion, innovation, community impact, artistic potential, public access, and feasibility.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
If my organization is more than three years old, may I apply? 
No matter what your organization's age, you may apply if your group is not currently funded by our Centering Art & Racial Equiity, Youth Arts, or Neighborhood and Community Arts funding programs.

If I've received funding from your CityArtist Projects, may I apply?
If you are currently funded through our CityArtist program or if you've received funding from our CityArtist program within the last four (4) years, then you are NOT eligible to apply for SmART Ventures.

If I've received funding from SmART Ventures before, may I apply?
Yes. You may receive funding a maximum of TWO times through the SmART Ventures Grant. Applicants who have previously been funded are encouraged to pursue other funding opportunities through our office or elsewhere.  

I'm under the age of 18. May I apply? 
Yes. We are happy to receive project ideas from young people! But you will need an adult who can sign the contracts and receive the funds on your behalf.

What if my project takes place in Seattle, but I or my group is based outside of Seattle? 
If you are based just outside the city of Seattle but your project or event will take place in Seattle and will benefit Seattle residents, you may still be eligible to apply. Please bring this issue to the attention of staff in your initial conversation.

Name: Seattle Small Business Capital Access Program
Description: Seattle’s Small Business Capital Access Program helps eligible Seattle for-profit small businesses reduce borrowing costs by paying down 20% of an eligible loan principal or up to $30,000, whichever is less. Businesses do not apply directly for the award; instead, participating community lenders determine eligibility after loan approval. Eligible businesses must be independently owned, located in Seattle, operating for more than 12 months, have an active Seattle business license, no more than 50 FTE employees, and no more than $2 million in annual gross revenue.
Amount: Eligible small businesses can receive up to $30,000 or 20% of loan principal amount (whichever is less)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for CAP, businesses must:
Be a for-profit business, independently owned, and located within Seattle city limits.

Have an active City of Seattle Business License.

Be in operation for over 12 months.

Have filed City Business and Occupation (B&O) taxes and paid taxes in full if owed or comply within two months of selection.

Have no more than 50 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees.

Have an annual gross revenue of no more than $2 million.

Be in good standing with state and local agency requirements.

Be current on loan payments at the time of the principal paydown award.

Name: TEDCO Social Impact Fund
Description: TEDCO’s Social Impact Funds invest in Maryland-based early-stage technology startups led by economically underserved founders, with two pathways: the Pre-Seed Builder Fund and the Inclusion Fund. The Pre-Seed Builder Fund typically invests $100,000 via convertible note in pre-seed tech startups with a principal place of business in Maryland, at least one full-time employee, a majority Maryland-based workforce, and at least 50% founder ownership by individuals demonstrating economic disadvantage. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis through TEDCO’s online application, and funded companies may also receive executive support, mentorship, networking, and other Builder Fund resources.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We welcome pre-seed technology startups from all industries to apply. However, to be applicable, a company must meet all the following qualifications:

Principal place of business is in Maryland
At least one full-time employee
More than half of the workforce based in Maryland
No less than 50% of founders demonstrate economic disadvantage

Name: Inner Sunset Neighborhood Vibrancy Fund
Description: The Inner Sunset Neighborhood Vibrancy Fund provides $5,000–$20,000 grants to ground-floor, brick-and-mortar businesses in San Francisco’s Inner Sunset to improve storefronts, strengthen business operations, or activate vacant commercial spaces. Funding is available through three tracks—Storefront Beautification, Technical Assistance, and Storefront Activation—with eligibility and permitted uses varying by track. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

Eligibility & Requirements
Before applying, review the eligibility and requirements below for the grant track you would like to apply for.


Storefront Beautification
Funding For: Exterior enhancements to improve storefront facades & corridor appeal

Funding Type: Reimbursement-Based Grant*

Funding Type: Direct Vendor Stipend & Referral

Award Amount: Up to $5,000

Eligibility:
Must have:

Existing ground-floor, brick-and-mortar business open to the public in the Inner Sunset
Active Business Account Number

Not home-based, formula retail, religious institutions, parking lots, or mobile businesses

Funding Type: General Operating Grant

Award Amount: Up to $20,000

Eligibility:
Must have:

New or expanding business
Previous business experience
Signed commercial lease or letter of intent (minimum 1-year commitment) for ground-floor, brick-and-mortar business intended to be open to the public in the Inner Sunset
Demonstrated business concept through a business plan
Not formula retail, religious institutions, parking lots, or mobile businesses
Funding CAN be used for:

Lease & space set-up
Equipment & fixtures
Financial management (e.g. budgeting, bookkeeping)

Workforce management (e.g. hiring, human resources)

Non-commercial uses
Short-term pop-ups
Debt repayment
Personal expenses
Ongoing operating expenses beyond the start-up phase
Non-business-related expenses
Required Application Materials:

Signed lease or Letter of Intent (minimum 1-year term)*
Business plan with operating budget
Narrative on business and neighborhood impact
*Grant funds will only be disbursed after a signed lease is submitted and approved by SF New Deal.

Name: California Community Impact Grant
Description: Ability Central’s California Community Impact Grants provide $500–$5,000 to eligible nonprofits and educational institutions supporting communication and information access for Deaf, disabled, and neurodivergent people in California. Applicants must have annual budgets under $1 million, use funds within three months, and may receive up to two awards totaling $10,000 per year. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must:

Be a registered 501(c)(3) or 501(h) nonprofit, or a qualifying educational institution

Have an annual operating budget under $1,000,000

Demonstrate ethical management and organizational capacity

Have reliable, ethical, and experienced personnel overseeing the organization and project

Name: KeHE Trend Finder
Description: KeHE’s Virtual Trend Finder is a product discovery program from KeHE, one of North America's largest distributors of natural, organic, specialty, and fresh products, that connects emerging brands with its Category Management team for potential retail distribution. Food, non-alcoholic beverage, health and beauty, vitamins and supplements, foodservice, pet, baby, and household brands can apply to pitch their products, with standout suppliers eligible for a "Golden Ticket" that fast-tracks onboarding and provides promotional opportunities at no cost.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible products may fall within one or more of the following categories: 

Food Products (Fresh, Shelf Stable, Refrigerated, or Frozen) 
Non-Alcoholic Beverages
Health & Beauty
Vitamins & Supplements
Foodservice
Pet Food & Care
Baby
Household & General Merchandise
KeHE does not distribute CBD, THC, or alcohol products. Submissions in these categories will not be considered.
Industry: Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care,Food & Beverage

Name: Chicago Uptown Community Events Grant
Description: The Uptown Community Events Grant provides $500–$5,000 to support free, public events held within the Uptown SSA district, with preference for outdoor programming that activates public spaces and benefits the neighborhood. Grants may cover up to 50% of the event’s total budget, with award amounts influenced by expected attendance. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis while funding remains available, and events must receive approval before they begin.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Any business, organization, or individual that will be programming a community event within the Uptown
SSA district is eligible to apply for a grant. Preference will be given to businesses, organizations, and
individuals that reside within the district. See the description below and attached map. The boundaries
include:
• Both east and west sides of North Broadway from Irving Park Road on the south to Foster Avenue on the north
• Both east and west sides of Sheridan Road from Irving Park Road on the south to Foster Avenue on the north

• Both the north and south sides of Lawrence Ave. from Magnolia Ave. on the west to Clarendon Ave. on the east
• Both the north and south sides of Leland Avenue from Racine Avenue on the west to Sheridan Road on the east
• Both the north and south sides of Wilson Avenue from Clark Street on the west to Clarendon Avenue on the east
• Both the north and south sides of Montrose Avenue from Clifton Ave. on the west to Clarendon Ave. on the east
• Both the north and south sides of Buena Avenue from Kenmore Ave. on the west to North Broadway on the east
• The north side of Irving Park Road from Kenmore Avenue on the west to Clarendon Avenue on the east

Name: Chicago Uptown Curb Appeal Rebate Program
Description: The Uptown Curb Appeal Rebate Program helps small businesses and property owners within the Uptown SSA improve storefronts and façades through upgrades such as new signage, awnings, windows, and other exterior improvements. Approved projects may receive reimbursement for up to 50% of eligible costs, capped at $5,000, and applicants must receive SSA Commission approval before beginning construction.

Name: CA World Stage Ready Forgivable Loan Program
Description: A forgivable loan program presented by TMC Community Capital and promoted by the Crenshaw Chamber of Commerce to help California small businesses prepare for major events, attract more customers, and grow with expert support. The loan has favorable terms: 12 months to repay, 0% interest, a possible 12-month deferment, and up to 100% forgiveness if program requirements are met.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be for-profit business owners in California, have generated revenue for at least 12 months, and can include ITIN holders; no minimum FICO score is required. Excluded industries include adult entertainment, cannabis, rideshare, real estate, and weapons/ammunition

Name: Nathan Cummings Foundation Advancement Grants
Description: The Nathan Cummings Foundation's Advancement Grants provide up to $250,000 per year for up to two years to help organizations scale promising solutions or advance project-based work that promotes racial, economic, and environmental justice. The foundation accepts letters of inquiry on a rolling basis and prioritizes innovative, community-driven organizations – particularly those working in the U.S. South – that are building long-term systems change.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We support organizations based in the United States, its Territories, and Israel-Palestine. We are particularly interested in work focused on the U.S. South (see below). 

NCF supports work in the American South focused on advancing racial, economic, and environmental justice, devoting a minimum of 40% of all assets to the region. While potential partners may apply for funding from Racial, Economic, and Environmental Justice focus areas at the national level, NCF invites proposals for partnerships in the following 13 states (AL, AR, GA, KY, MO, OK, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN, VA, WV). NCF also is emphasizing regional opportunities to counter-act economic drivers of inequality and injustice; NCF’s initial insights emphasize exploring the links between Inclusive Green Economy, Economic Security, and Racial Wealth Gap focus areas.

Name: Kickstarter Culture Fund
Description: The Kickstarter Culture Fund is a $1 million fund supporting independent creators in arts, fashion, film, and music through direct contributions to their Kickstarter campaigns. Selected creators also receive promotional support and, for particularly innovative projects, additional campaign guidance.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Projects must be in one of the following categories: Art, Photography, Dance, Theater, Film, Fashion, or Music.

Your Kickstarter campaign status must be live or in draft (with at least a main image and description).

Projects must launch before or on December 31, 2026.

Applicants must meet Kickstarter's location requirements. See our Help Center for more information.

Name: Philadelphia Free Business Tax Preparation Program
Description: The City of Philadelphia provides eligible small businesses with free local, state, and federal tax-preparation assistance, including help navigating changes to Philadelphia's tax structure. Services are provided virtually and in person through City-selected tax professionals, including multilingual providers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses must have $250,000 or less in 2025 revenue. New businesses filing for the first time are eligible, and home-based businesses qualify. Landlords and property-rental businesses are excluded.

Name: Philadelphia Storefront Improvement Program
Description: The Storefront Improvement Program (SIP) helps Philadelphia businesses and commercial property owners improve their storefronts through façade and security improvements, such as painting, lighting, signage, awnings, and masonry repairs. The City reimburses a portion of eligible project costs to strengthen neighborhood commercial corridors.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Available to eligible businesses and commercial property owners making qualifying exterior/storefront improvements. Projects must meet City requirements, and construction cannot begin before the application is submitted/approved.

Name: Illinois Innovation Voucher Program
Description: The Illinois Innovation Voucher Program helps Illinois-based for-profit small and mid-sized businesses collaborate with qualified Illinois nonprofit higher-education institutions to access research expertise, facilities, and labs. Vouchers cover up to 75 percent of an eligible research engagement, capped at $75,000, for activities such as R&D, prototyping, testing, and commercialization support. Businesses must have their principal place of business in Illinois and remain there for the duration of the engagement.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a for-profit Illinois-based business: principal place of business in Illinois, OR if not located in Illinois, employs at least 100 full-time employees in Illinois (as defined under Section 5-5 of the Economic Development for a Growing Economy Tax Credit Act)
- The business must remain in Illinois for the duration of the research engagement
- The partnering institution must be a qualified Illinois-based nonprofit institution of higher education

Eligible activities: prototyping, testing, product/process development, technology implementation, commercialization, research expertise, and innovation/technology audits.

Does NOT fund: travel, rent, internal salaries, standard training, general software, website/mobile-app development, advertising, branding, marketing, or general business/legal consulting.

Vouchers cover up to 75% of an eligible engagement, capped at $75,000.

Name: Portland Vacant Storefront Grant Program
Description: Prosper Portland provides matching funds to help businesses occupy vacant street-level storefronts within the City of Portland. The program reimburses up to 75 percent of eligible costs, covering physical tenant improvements as hard costs and consulting assistance as soft costs. Award ceilings vary by business type, with grocery stores eligible for the largest awards. A one-time pool of $800,000 funds the program first-come, first-served.
Amount: up to $100,000 (grocery); up to $50,000 (restaurant); up to $25,000 (retail)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business owner, or property owner leasing to an eligible business
- Business located in the City of Portland; owner resides in Portland
- Valid City of Portland business license and current Oregon business registry
- Lease with at least 3 years remaining on a vacant street-level storefront
- Property zoned commercial/mixed use, employment, industrial, or multi-dwelling
- Current on all financial obligations including taxes and debt
- Locally owned if a franchise or a business with 3+ locations
- Reimburses up to 75% of eligible project costs (matching funds required)
- Ineligible: nonprofits, national franchises not locally owned, THC retailers, e-commerce-only businesses without a storefront, food carts and trucks

Applications opened August 17, 2026, reviewed first-come first-served until the $800,000 is expended.

Name: NYC Contract Financing Loan Fund
Description: The Contract Financing Loan Fund provides working capital loans to New York City businesses that hold or are bidding on contracts with city agencies or city-funded entities, as either prime contractors or subcontractors. Loans carry a fixed annual interest rate of up to 3 percent, with closing fees of up to 3 percent. NYC Small Business Services screens applicants and refers them to participating lenders.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must operate an active business
- Must be seeking financing as a prime contractor or subcontractor on a contract with a city agency or a city-funded entity

Fixed annual interest rate up to 3%; closing fees up to 3% at closing. Application flow: create or access an SBS Connect account, submit a financing assistance request selecting "Contract Financing," an account manager responds within two business days, then SBS assists with submission to the lender. Final credit determination is made by the lender, not by SBS.

Name: National ACE Empower Program
Description: Empower is a multi-state small business development program led by the California Asian Pacific Chamber of Commerce with National ACE, Start Co., and CMG Alliance. It provides growth-stage business owners with structured training and individualized technical assistance covering operations, leadership, revenue strategy, capital readiness, and government contracting. Services are provided at no cost through public funding and partner support, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Small business owners and entrepreneurs operating in one of 21 eligible states: AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, HI, IL, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, NV, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA, WI
- Business must be actively operating; concept-stage businesses are not eligible
- At least one year of operation or initial revenue activity
- Seeking to strengthen internal systems and operations
- Interested in government contracting or next-phase growth
- Ready to commit to structured learning plus hands-on technical assistance

No cash award; services are free. Submit intake form, CAPCC reviews for eligibility and fit, applicant matched to a support track. Most applicants hear back within about 2 weeks; acceptance is not guaranteed. Contact: skushida@calasiancc.org

Name: NY Linked Deposit Program
Description: The New York State Linked Deposit Program lowers borrowing costs for established in-state businesses by having the state place a matching deposit with the participating bank at a reduced rate. Lenders pass the savings on as an interest rate two or three percentage points below the prevailing rate for four years. Proceeds fund modernization projects such as equipment, facility expansion, new technology, and related working capital.
Amount: up to $4 million per project; $6 million lifetime maximum
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business headquartered in New York State
- Manufacturing firms: 500 or fewer full-time NYS employees
- Service businesses: independently owned, not dominant in their field, 100 or fewer full-time NYS employees
- Agricultural firms: 500 or fewer full-time employees
- Technology/innovation businesses: 100 or fewer full-time employees
- Minority- and women-owned businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned firms, and CDFIs also eligible
- Loan term must be at least 48 months; reduced rate guaranteed for 4 years, with possible four-year extensions
- Not eligible: start-ups, personal services, professional services, and retail (retail permitted only in distressed census tracts with 100 or fewer NY employees)

Rate reduced 3 points for MWBEs, distressed-area firms, technology and agricultural firms, and defense manufacturers; 2 points for all other eligible applicants. Loan must be arranged through a participating lender. Lenders are barred from charging origination, handling, service, or refinancing fees.

Name: Wisconsin Main Street Bounceback Technical Assistance
Description: The Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation funds no-cost business training and one-on-one consulting delivered through the Universities of Wisconsin and the Wisconsin SBDC. Offerings include hour-long workshops, six-week cohort courses, on-demand video tutorials covering law, lending, accounting, marketing and HR, and confidential advising available in English and Spanish. Registration costs are paid directly by the program, with no upfront payment or reimbursement required.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Owner, employee, or staff member of a for-profit small business
- Fewer than 500 employees
- Based in Wisconsin
- Currently operating and open for business
- Nonprofits, municipalities, and pre-venture businesses explicitly excluded

TIME-LIMITED: the program's own FAQ states the technical assistance ENDS SEPTEMBER 2026 - within weeks of this record being created. The separate WEDC Main Street Bounceback grant stopped accepting applications in December 2022; only the technical assistance remains.

Name: San Jose Disability Access Improvement Grant Program
Description: San Jose's Planning, Building and Code Enforcement department helps small businesses pay for disability access improvements in two phases. Phase 1 provides up to eight thousand dollars as a credit against CASp inspection costs and city plan review, permit and inspection fees. Phase 2 reimburses up to twenty-five thousand dollars for professional design services, construction labor, and accessible furniture, fixtures and equipment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- No more than 50 employees
- Commercial business, nonresidential property, or a nonprofit current with California's Registry of Charitable Trusts
- Valid City of San Jose business tax certificate
- Business actively operating; tenants must have at least one year remaining on the lease
- Phase 2 reimburses 100% of paid invoices and 80% of the cost estimate for remedial improvements

AMOUNT CORRECTION: the commonly cited $8,000 is Phase 1 only and materially understates the program - total available is up to $33,000 across both phases. Contact Juan Borrelli, Small Business Ally (Juan.Borrelli@sanjoseca.gov, 408-975-2655) for current funding status.

Name: Scranton Business Facade Improvements Grant
Description: The City of Scranton's Department of Economic and Community Development reimburses businesses for half the cost of exterior renovation projects, up to ten thousand dollars per business. Eligible work includes windows, doors, signage, lighting, awnings, masonry, painting, landscaping and sidewalks; fencing, roofing and parking lots are excluded. Businesses must be in HUD-defined low-to-moderate income areas, current on taxes and trash fees, with no outstanding code enforcement issues.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business located in a HUD-defined low-to-moderate income area within Scranton
- Current on all taxes and trash fees
- No outstanding Code Enforcement issues
- 50% match required - grant covers 50% of exterior renovation costs, capped at $10,000 per business
- Eligible: windows, doors, signage, lighting, awnings, masonry, painting, landscaping, sidewalks
- Excluded: fencing, roofing, parking lots

Program announced 7/10/2026; applications remain open until project funds are expended. Contacts: Liza Carroll (lcarroll@scrantonpa.gov), Tom Cipriano (tcipriano@scrantonpa.gov).

Name: Orlando Business Assistance Program
Description: The City of Orlando shares the cost of development fees for new and expanding small businesses inside city limits. The program pays fifty percent of assessed fees up to twenty thousand dollars, with the business covering the other half. Eligible costs include building permit fees, sewer and transportation impact fees, and right-of-way infrastructure improvements such as sidewalk repairs, streetlighting, water and sewer lines, and EV charging installations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- New or expanding for-profit small business, per the SBA definition
- Located within, or relocating to, Orlando city limits
- Must obtain or hold a City of Orlando Business Tax Receipt
- Current on federal, state, and local taxes
- Must obtain building permits for the proposed work
- No outstanding code enforcement violations, liens, or debt owed to the city
- Business pays 50% of assessed fees; program covers the remaining 50%

Not a reimbursement - the city pays its half of the fees directly at assessment rather than repaying the business afterward. Contact: economicdevelopment@orlando.gov, 407-246-2821.

Name: San Diego Makers Arcade Holiday Fair Vendor Application
Description: Makers Arcade runs a juried holiday market at the Port Pavilion on the Broadway Pier in downtown San Diego. Vendors sell physical products only, including handmade goods and pre-packaged food items; service businesses, food trucks and experience vendors are not accepted. Applicants are selected on craftsmanship, design, booth presentation and category balance, and pay a booth fee plus a non-refundable application fee.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Vendors must sell physical products only - handmade crafts and pre-packaged food items qualify
- Service-based businesses, food trucks and experience vendors excluded
- Juried selection on craftsmanship, design, attention to detail, cohesive booth setup, clear pricing, brand-aligned signage
- Organizers balance the lineup and avoid oversaturating product categories

Booth fees: Regular Indoor 5'x9' $405; Half Indoor 5'x5' $275; Outside 10'x10' $405; Outside Half 5'x10' $275.
Applications opened 7/3/2026; priority deadline was 7/20/2026. After that, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as space allows, then via waitlist - a vendor applying now is competing for remaining space. Event: Saturday 12/12/2026 and Sunday 12/13/2026, 10am-5pm.
Industry: Arts & Crafts,Retail,Apparel & Accessories,Creative Economy,Visual & Fine Arts

Name: Downtown Houston Alfresco Grant
Description: The Houston Downtown Management District funds outdoor activation of downtown businesses through the Alfresco Grant. Awards reach ten thousand dollars for non-permanent fixtures such as seating, umbrellas and planters, with an additional five thousand available for permanent fixtures including awnings and lighting. Businesses and property owners must review the district's design guidelines and meet with the Downtown Houston team before applying, and applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Downtown Houston businesses and property owners
- Up to $10,000 for non-permanent fixtures (seating, umbrellas, planters)
- Additional $5,000 for permanent fixtures (awnings, lighting)
- Must review design guidelines and meet with the Downtown Houston+ team before applying
- Applications accepted on a rolling basis

Funded by the Houston Downtown Management District - a DIFFERENT funder from the Downtown Redevelopment Authority facade grant on the same page. Match requirement and precise boundary not stated.

Name: Novato Tenant Improvement Grant
Description: The City of Novato provides matching grants covering up to fifty percent of eligible tenant improvement costs for businesses and commercial property owners. Projects under ten thousand dollars may be fully funded at the Selection Review Panel's discretion. Once limited to downtown businesses, the program is now open citywide and operates first-come, first-served until funds are allocated, following an eleven-step process including an SBDC consultation and design review.
Amount: 50% match; projects under $10,000 may be fully funded
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Active business license in Novato
- Located within city limits (program expanded from downtown-only to citywide)
- Active commercial property
- No pending code violations on the property
- Non-property owners must obtain written consent from the property owner
- Cannot have received a grant within the previous two years
- 50% match required, except projects under $10,000 which the City may fully fund at the Selection Review Panel's discretion

Open continuously until all funds are allocated; first-come, first-served. Eleven-step process: application, eligibility review, SBDC consultation, design proposal, City selection, design review, construction, City inspections, completion and reimbursement, ongoing maintenance obligation. No maximum dollar cap is published beyond the 50% match structure.

Name: Start Small Think Big
Description: Start Small Think Big is a nonprofit connecting small business owners with pro bono attorneys and financial professionals for one-on-one help. Legal work covers entity formation, contracts, trademark searches, online business questions and employment issues; financial services cover pricing, cash flow, cost analysis, bookkeeping setup and capital readiness. Legal assistance is limited to businesses based in New York or California, while financial and marketing services are nationwide.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business currently operating and selling goods or services
- At least $500 in recurring sales over the past 3 months
- Less than $1M in revenue over the past year
- Total household income below 750% of Federal Poverty Guidelines
- TOTAL HOUSEHOLD ASSETS BELOW $100K (excludes primary residence, 401(k), and repayable loan capital) - this is the binding constraint for most applicants
- Must identify with one of the listed communities: entrepreneurs of color, immigrant communities, LGBTQIA+, justice-impacted, veterans, people with disabilities, low-income individuals, women
- Excluded: nonprofits, real estate, financial services, MLMs, large corporate franchisees, co-ops over 5 partners, marijuana businesses, businesses outside the U.S.

GEOGRAPHIC SPLIT: legal services are NY and CA only. Financial and marketing services are nationwide.

Name: Erie Downtown Facade Reimbursement Grant
Description: The Erie Downtown Partnership reimburses commercial property owners and businesses in the Downtown Improvement District for exterior facade improvements on primary building entrances. Awards cover up to fifty percent of project costs to a maximum of ten thousand dollars, and require a one-to-one financial match with reimbursement issued only on proof of completion and payment. Projects are evaluated on transformational impact, historic preservation, code compliance and vacancy reduction.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Assessed commercial property owners and businesses within the Downtown Improvement District
- District boundaries: Bayfront to 14th Street; Holland Street (west) to Sassafras Street (east)
- Improvements must be to the exterior facade of the primary building entrance
- 1:1 financial match required
- Reimbursement issued only upon proof of project completion and payment
- Must first contact Emily Fetcko (814-455-3743, emily.fetcko@eriedowntown.com) to verify eligibility and fund availability
- Requires application form, design plans, funding commitment letters, and a description of project benefits; online only
- Evaluated on transformational impact, historic preservation, compliance improvements, vacancy reduction, adaptive reuse potential

Awarded on a rolling basis until funds are fully allocated.

Name: NYC VOLS Microenterprise Project
Description: Volunteers of Legal Service matches New York City microentrepreneurs with pro bono attorneys for transactional legal work, including entity selection and formation, governance documents, contract drafting and review, employment law compliance, intellectual property and cybersecurity. The project also runs community legal education workshops and clinics. It does not handle litigation, landlord-tenant disputes or conflicts with third parties.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business owner resides in NYC, or the business operates in NYC
- HOUSEHOLD INCOME BELOW 500% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (roughly $78,000 for a single-person household) - genuinely means-tested
- Personal assets below $100,000, excluding primary residence
- Unable to afford private legal representation
- Separate nonprofit track: NY-incorporated nonprofits or community-based organizations (BIDs, LDCs, merchants' associations) in LMI neighborhoods with gross revenue up to $200,000
- Excluded matters: landlord-tenant litigation, disputes with third parties

Intake via helpline or downloadable intake form.

Name: Seattle Accounting and Business Consulting (ABC) Program
Description: The City of Seattle's Office of Economic Development provides up to forty hours of free one-on-one consulting to small businesses and nonprofits, capped at ten hours in each of four subject areas: accounting and bookkeeping, business development, loan readiness, and marketing and branding. Consultants are matched after application review, participants have six months to use their hours, and engagements typically run two to three months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Physically located within Seattle city limits
- Active City of Seattle business license
- No more than two locations
- 50 or fewer full-time employees
- Annual gross revenue under $5 million
- For-profit businesses and nonprofits both eligible

Must sign an NDA via AdobeSign after applying; review takes up to 5 business days. Up to 10 hours in each of four areas. Six months to use allotted hours. 2026 application form is live at abcapplication.fillout.com/2026abc.

Name: San Diego Outdoor Business Grant (Spaces as Places)
Description: The City of San Diego reimburses businesses for creating outdoor dining and retail spaces under its Spaces as Places program. Reimbursement is issued across three phases covering permitting fees and inspections, professional design drawings, and construction labor and materials. Businesses in the San Diego Promise Zone or low-to-moderate income areas receive higher permitting and design caps, raising the total available from fifteen thousand to twenty thousand dollars.
Amount: up to $15,000; up to $20,000 in Promise Zone or LMI areas
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Located in the City of San Diego
- Valid City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate
- Independently owned and operated commercial tenant
- Majority or primary business owner must be a San Diego County resident
- Higher award tier (Category B) requires location in the San Diego Promise Zone or a low-to-moderate income area
- Ineligible: owners with 20%+ stake who previously applied; restaurant groups that already applied; chains with 7 or more locations; businesses engaged in illegal activity

Reimbursed across three phases: permitting fees and inspections, professional design drawings, construction labor and materials. Funding available until expended; administrator responds within 10 business days.

Name: California Employment Training Panel (ETP) Small Business Program
Description: California's Employment Training Panel reimburses small businesses for the cost of structured job training for new or existing employees (8–200 hours of instruction per trainee), with owners allowed to train alongside staff. The Small Business Program has a dedicated funding allocation each fiscal year ($5.7M in FY 2026/27). Many small businesses participate through a training provider's Multiple Employer Contract, which handles the paperwork.
Amount: Reimbursement of employee training costs (8–200 hours per trainee)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit California businesses with 100 or fewer employees in California (no more than 250 worldwide) that pay into the state Unemployment Insurance fund; trainees must meet ETP's post-training wage floor. Reimbursement rates are published on ETP's site.

Name: UNFI UpNext Emerging Brands Program
Description: UNFI's UpNext program is a supplier-development track for emerging natural and specialty brands that gives selected brands a dedicated supplier-development manager, mentorship, retailer presentations, and trade-show and pitch-slam opportunities. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. It is a distribution and buyer-access program rather than a cash award.
Amount: In-kind: supplier development support and retailer presentations
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Emerging natural/specialty CPG brands that are wholesale-ready; no published revenue floor, but brands should be prepared for multi-region retail distribution. Submissions run through a RangeMe profile.
Industry: Food & Beverage,Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care

Name: Alameda County Workforce Development Board On-the-Job Training and Employer Training Subsidies
Description: The Alameda County Workforce Development Board offers employer incentives for businesses in Alameda County: On-the-Job Training "provides companies with subsidies for hiring and retaining local area job seekers," and the Customized/Incumbent Worker Training program provides a subsidy for training and retaining existing staff. The page also lists the state Homeless Hiring Tax Credit (up to $10,000 per eligible hire, up to $30,000 per year). Businesses start by contacting the board's business services staff.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Employers located in Alameda County (outside the City of Oakland's separate workforce board area); hires for On-the-Job Training subsidies come through the county workforce system. Contacts listed on the page: Javier Contreras, (510) 259-3831 (On-the-Job Training); Darlene Sloan Hawkins, (510) 259-3864 (Customized/Incumbent Worker Training).

Name: Alameda County Green Business Program Certification and Rebate
Description: The Alameda County Green Business Program (part of the California Green Business Network) certifies businesses that meet energy, water, waste, and pollution-prevention standards, with free consultations and waste audits – the City of Berkeley offers free hands-on help to its businesses. Certified businesses receive a decal, directory listing, and city marketing, and the California Green Business Network rebate offers up to $500 per business ($1,000 for eligible businesses) toward certification-related upgrades, subject to funding availability. Certification typically takes six weeks to six months.
Amount: Up to $500 rebate ($1,000 for eligible businesses) plus free certification
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any business located in Alameda County, CA; free to enroll. Berkeley businesses can request free certification help from the City of Berkeley (berkeleyca.gov/community-recreation/news/get-help-become-certified-green-business). Rebates are subject to availability of funds.

Name: KeHE ELEVATE Emerging Brands Program
Description: KeHE ELEVATE is the distributor's development program for early-stage natural, organic, and specialty brands (capped at roughly 200 brands), offering a dedicated point of contact, education, retailer introductions, and promotional opportunities to help brands scale through KeHE's distribution network. KeHE says it is actively searching for program candidates; applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Distinct from KeHE Trend Finder, its three-times-a-year product discovery event.
Amount: In-kind: brand development support and retailer introductions
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Emerging natural/organic/specialty CPG brands not yet widely distributed; brands apply online and are selected by KeHE (program size limited). Submissions typically require a RangeMe profile.
Industry: Food & Beverage,Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care

Name: Alameda County Small, Local and Emerging Business (SLEB) Certification
Description: Alameda County's SLEB certification gives certified small, local, and emerging businesses up to 10% bid preferences on eligible County contracts (5% small + 5% local) and lists them in the County's preferred-vendor database for purchases under $100,000. The County directs 20% of contracts over $25,000 to SLEB-certified firms. Certification is free and applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Amount: Up to 10% bid preference on Alameda County contracts
