Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses with a fixed office in Alameda County and a local business license for at least 6 months that meet the SBA size standard for their industry; the "Emerging" tier is for businesses under 5 years old. Program overview: gsa.acgov.org/do-business-with-us/vendor-support/small-local-and-emerging-businesses/. SLEB Unit: (510) 891-5500.

Name: Pacific Community Ventures BusinessAdvising.org
Description: Oakland-based nonprofit Pacific Community Ventures matches small business owners with volunteer expert advisors for free one-on-one virtual mentoring across 27 areas, including funding strategy, financial planning, hiring and compensation, supply chain, B2B sales, and green certification. Business owners in the program receive on average 15 hours of free advising valued at more than $2,900. Sign-up is on the Qooper mentoring platform; mentors communicate in 50 languages.
Amount: About 15 hours of free 1:1 business advising (valued at $2,900+)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; open to small business owners nationwide (virtual). Create a profile on the Qooper platform (mentoring.qooper.io/join/2aff1e), select or get matched with an advisor, and schedule a first meeting. No revenue, industry, or demographic requirements stated.

Name: Nevada APEX Accelerator (government contracting assistance)
Description: Free, taxpayer-funded program of the Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development that helps Nevada businesses pursue federal, state and local government contracts: workshops and webinars, one-on-one counseling, marketing to specific government buyers and prime contractors, help with quotes, bids, proposals and pre-/post-award compliance, access to specifications and regulations, and networking/teaming assistance. Offices in Las Vegas ((702) 486-0586) and Carson City ((775) 687-9921); NVAPEXAccelerator@goed.nv.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit Nevada businesses in any county. To become a client, read the 'About Nevada APEX' flyer and complete the Client Questionnaire Form (wet signature required). All services are free.

Name: Silver State Works – Nevada Employer Hiring Incentives
Description: Nevada DETR program implemented by the EmployNV Business Hub that lets employers receive up to $2,000 or more per employee in financial incentives or training allowances for new hires. Options include On-the-Job Training contracts (reimbursement of up to 50% of the participant's initial agreed gross wage for the contract period, paid monthly on documentation) and Incentive-Based Employment (wage and training subsidies for full-time hires of 32+ hours/week for up to four months, with a wage-retention supplement of up to $500 after each 30 days of successful employment, up to 120 days). Southern Nevada (702) 486-0129; Northern Nevada (775) 284-9660; silverstateworks@detr.nv.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Employers with a current Nevada Unemployment Insurance account in good standing, valid state and local business licenses, open full-time positions (32+ hours per week paying at least $17/hour), and vendor registration with the Nevada State Controller's Office (processing up to 20 business days).

Name: Nevada Gov eMarketplace (NGEM) – Supplier Registration
Description: Nevada's centralized, no-cost online procurement portal: suppliers register once to receive requests for bids and proposals from participating public entities, including the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority (which lists all of its general bid opportunities on NGEM), Clark County, City of Las Vegas, Henderson, North Las Vegas, Carson City, UNLV, UNR, CSN, Clark County School District, Harry Reid International Airport, RTC, Las Vegas Metro, SNWA/LVVWD, UMC and others. Solicitations are published online and bids/proposals are submitted through the portal.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any contractor or supplier; registration is free (Register link at nevada.ionwave.net/VendorRegistration/PreliminaryInfo.aspx). Suppliers must register and accept the site terms to be considered for solicitations.

Name: Nevada SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Nevada Small Business Development Center provides free, confidential one-on-one advising on starting, growing and managing a business – business plans, financing and loan packaging, market research, cash-flow management and strategic planning – plus workshops, seminars and courses (e.g., business licensing info sessions, AI tools for small business). Las Vegas-area centers include Las Vegas, Henderson, City of North Las Vegas, Urban Chamber, Vegas Chamber, UNLV and S. Nevada AAPI locations; (800) 240-7094.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nevadans starting or growing a business; advising is free and confidential. Request an advisor at nsbdc.ecenterdirect.com.

Name: Film Nevada Crew & Services Directory (Nevada Film Office)
Description: The Nevada Film Office's crew and services directory is the primary resource production companies use to hire Nevada-based crew, producers, photographers, equipment vendors and production-services businesses when filming in the state. Listings are reviewed by Film Nevada before approval, and productions contact listed businesses directly. Registration takes about 15 minutes at nv.reel-scout.com/crew_registration.aspx; the separate location library is free to list properties in.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a Nevada resident (upload a Nevada driver's license) or a business with a physical location in Nevada (upload a Nevada business license). Crew & services directory listing costs $25/year; the location library is free.

Name: Nevada Emerging Small Business (ESB) Certification
Description: State certification program (established 2014, administered by the Governor's Office of Economic Development) that helps Nevada small businesses contract with government agencies. Certified firms can use the ESB designation when marketing to Nevada state and local agencies and are listed in the ESB directory. The application asks for address, legal structure, date established, capabilities, gross receipts for the last 3 years and number of employees; determination within 90 days; certification valid for two years. Government Contract Advisors: (775) 687-9903 Carson City, (702) 486-2700 Las Vegas, procurement@goed.nv.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nevada small businesses within the program's employee-count and gross-receipts tiers (thresholds are not stated on the program page – confirm with GOED). Application and renewal are free; apply at goed.nv.gov/emerging-small-business-directory/.

Name: Fund for the City of New York – Cash Flow Loan Program
Description: Interest-free bridge loans for 501(c)(3) organizations providing services in the New York City area that are waiting on committed funds (government contracts, foundation grants). A one-time 2% service fee is deducted at disbursement, repayment is typically 60–90 days, and loans are usually approved within 3–5 business days. Contact Andrew Walrond, Vice President of Loan Programs: awalrond@fcny.org, (212) 925-6675.
Amount: bridge loan sized to the committed funds (0% interest, 2% fee)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving the NYC area with committed but not-yet-received funds.
Application Fee: None (2% service fee deducted at disbursement)

Name: Louisiana Hudson Initiative – Small Business Certification for State Contracting
Description: Certification that gives Louisiana small businesses greater access to state purchasing: for purchases under $25,000, agencies can waive the requirement for additional quotes when a certified company submits a reasonable one, and certified bidders receive 10% of the total evaluation points on state RFPs. Apply at ledsmallbiz.com (LED reviews within two business days), then register with the Office of State Procurement and submit annual updates.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Independently owned Louisiana businesses with fewer than 50 full-time employees, under $5 million in average gross receipts, and Louisiana-resident owners.

Name: Nevada Child Care Licensing (DSS) – Opening a Licensed Child Care Facility
Description: Nevada's Division of Social Services licenses child care under NAC 432A and publishes the start-to-finish path for new providers: the Getting Started guide, licensing application and background-check process, required training, the online licensing system, and the list of local jurisdictions that license their own facilities. Child Care Licensing: (702) 631-3037.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Anyone opening a child care home or center in Nevada.

Name: Apple Independent Repair Provider Program
Description: Gives independent repair shops that perform out-of-warranty iPhone and Mac repairs access to genuine Apple parts, tools, training, service guides, diagnostics and resources, with certification exam fees waived for approved businesses. Reviews take up to four weeks.
Amount: N/A (parts, tools, training access; certification exam fees waived)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Established repair businesses with a commercial walk-in location (no residential addresses), Apple-certified technicians, a company-domain email address, a business license, and photos of the storefront and reception area.

Name: Louisiana SBDC – Free Business Advising
Description: The Louisiana Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential advising on business plans, financing and marketing, plus training programs and market research, through nine regional centers serving all 64 parishes (the Acadiana center at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette serves Iberia Parish). State office: (866) 782-4159, info@louisianasbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Louisiana small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs.

Name: LED Small and Emerging Business Development (SEBD) Program (Louisiana)
Description: Louisiana Economic Development certifies small businesses at no charge and provides business and management training – marketing, accounting, business planning, legal assistance – plus SEBD Roundtables and one-on-one help from subject-matter experts. Apply at ledsmallbiz.com; recertify every five years.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Owner must have lived in Louisiana for at least a year, work 20+ hours a week in the business, and have a personal net worth under $400,000 (excluding home, business assets and retirement accounts); business at least 51% owned by qualifying individuals, based in Louisiana, for-profit, and under $1.5 million in net worth.

Name: The Children's Cabinet – Provider Coaching, CDA Fee Support & T.E.A.C.H. Scholarships (Nevada)
Description: The Children's Cabinet helps new Nevada child care providers get started and market their programs, runs the free Pathways to Program Success coaching program for center directors and owners, pays Child Development Associate credential fees through its CDA Training Support application, and connects staff to T.E.A.C.H. Early Childhood Nevada college scholarships for home providers, teachers and directors working 30+ hours a week in licensed facilities. 775-856-6200.
Amount: free coaching; CDA fees ($425/$125); college scholarships
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nevada child care providers and early-childhood staff; T.E.A.C.H. scholarships require 30+ hours/week in a licensed facility.

Name: The Children's Cabinet – Child Care Start-up Grants (Nevada)
Description: Start-up grants from Nevada's early-childhood grant administrator that help family child care homes, group family child care homes and centers with the cost of licensing fees and some classroom materials and furnishings. Complete the Start-up Grant Application (fillable PDF) and send it to the ECE Grant Team; call 775-856-6200 to confirm current amounts. The same team funds CDA credential fees ($425 initial, $125 renewal) through its CDA Training Support application.
Amount: covers licensing fees and some classroom materials/furnishings (set per application)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nevada child care providers (family homes, group homes, centers) who have started the licensing process.

Name: Materials for the Arts (MFTA) – Free Materials for NYC Arts Nonprofits
Description: New York City's creative-reuse center gives free donated materials – fabric, furniture, props, paper, art supplies – to member organizations from its 35,000-square-foot Long Island City warehouse. Apply through the online form and send the required documents to applications@mfta.nyc.gov; shop by appointment once approved.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofit arts or cultural organizations located in NYC with at least two years of arts programming (also NYC public schools and city agencies).

Name: SeaChange Capital Partners – Loans for NYC Nonprofits
Description: SeaChange makes flexible working-capital, bridge and real-estate loans to nonprofits working in Greater New York City whose financing needs cannot be met by conventional lenders – generally $25,000 to $2 million at 4–6% over 2–5 years – and runs NYC Bridge Funding for the Arts for A.R.T./New York members. Advisory services are pro bono; apply through the form on its site or call (844) 869-7842.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits working in Greater New York City that cannot obtain financing from conventional lenders.

Name: SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert)
Description: Free SBA certification for veteran-owned small businesses. Certified VOSBs and SDVOSBs can pursue sole-source and set-aside contracts at the VA under its Vets First program – the VA reserves at least 7% of its annual contracting dollars for certified VOSBs and SDVOSBs, and at least 5% of all federal contracting dollars are set aside for SDVOSBs government-wide. Apply through MySBA Certifications; 1-866-SBA-HELP.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: At least 51% veteran-owned (or service-disabled veteran-owned), registered as a small business on SAM.gov, and within SBA size standards for the industry. No fee to apply.

Name: Oklahoma SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Oklahoma Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one business management advising, workshops, and technical assistance across the entire state, including Oklahoma City. Advisors help package loan requests and walk businesses through SAM.gov registration and city and state contracting; the OKC office runs sessions with the City of Oklahoma City's purchasing team. Request an advisor at business.oksbdc.org or call (580) 745-2877.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Oklahomans starting or growing a business; advising is free and confidential.

Name: TMAC – Texas Manufacturing Assistance Center
Description: TMAC is the NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership center for Texas. Its North Texas–Metroplex region is hosted by UT Arlington with an office at 7300 Jack Newell Blvd. S in Fort Worth. It works with construction as well as manufacturing companies on business and growth strategy, advanced manufacturing technology, quality management systems, supply chain, and workforce development – useful for taking a prototype toward a manufactured product. (800) 625-4876.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Texas manufacturers and manufacturing-adjacent businesses (including construction). Regional centers cover the whole state; some services are fee-based.

Name: Contra Costa County Small Business Enterprise (SBE) Program
Description: The county's Board of Supervisors targets awarding at least 50% of eligible contract dollars to small businesses. The SBE Program covers county-funded contracts up to $200,000, including professional and personal services. Related categories include DBE, DVBE, LBE, MBE and WBE.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Per California Government Code Section 14837: independently owned and not dominant in its field, principal office in California, no more than 100 employees including affiliates, and $15 million or less average annual gross receipts over the previous three tax years.

Name: Norcal SBDC – Free Business Advising (Government Contracting Specialty)
Description: The Norcal SBDC network runs 18+ regional offices and satellites across Northern California, including an East Bay center covering Contra Costa County, and provides no-fee confidential advising plus weekly livestream training. It has dedicated specialists in government contracting who can walk a business through state SB and county SBE certifications and then help it bid. Sign up at norcalsbdc.org/join or call (833) ASK-SBDC / 833-275-7232, Mon-Fri 9am-5pm.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in Northern California. Advising is free and confidential.

Name: North Texas SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The North Texas SBDC network provides no-cost, confidential advising on business planning, financial analysis, marketing strategy, and financing, plus workshops on startup, loan, planning, tax, and financial-statement topics. Advisors do loan packaging routinely. Use the "Search by County" tool on the site to find the field center for a given county. 214-860-5831.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in the 49-county North Texas region (includes DFW, Parker and Tarrant counties). Advising is free and confidential. Note: txsbdc.org is the separate South-West Texas Border network and does not cover DFW.

Name: California Small Business (SB) Certification – 5% Bid Preference
Description: Certified small businesses receive a five percent preference on competitive State of California solicitations. On low-price awards the preference equals 5% of the lowest non-small-business bid (capped at $50,000 per bid); on scored awards it adds 5% of the top non-small-business score. Combined with other preferences the total is capped at 15% of the bid or $100,000, whichever is less. Certification is done through the Cal eProcure portal.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: California-based small businesses meeting the state's SB size standards; certify through Cal eProcure. No fee.

Name: MissouriBUYS – Supplier Registration
Description: MissouriBUYS is the State of Missouri's statewide eProcurement system, operated by the Office of Administration Division of Purchasing. Suppliers register once, at no cost, to be listed as an approved state vendor and to receive automatic notice of bid opportunities in the commodity codes they select. Solicitations are published and responses submitted through the portal. Division of Purchasing: 573-751-2387.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any business or individual wishing to sell to the State of Missouri. Registration is free and requires an EIN or SSN and selection of applicable commodity codes.

Name: Missouri APEX Accelerator (government contracting assistance)
Description: Free program run through University of Missouri Extension that helps Missouri businesses win federal, state and local government contracts. Procurement specialists identify contracting opportunities, guide businesses through the bidding process, and complete SAM.gov registration at no cost. Coverage is assigned by county — the site publishes a county coverage map and an online contact form to reach the specialist for a given area.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Missouri businesses seeking government contracts. All services are free; contact a center near you or submit the online form to become a client.

Name: Missouri SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Missouri Small Business Development Center network provides free, confidential one-on-one advising on business plans, financial projections, pricing, loan packaging, market research and growth planning, plus workshops and training. The Southeast Missouri State University center (920 Broadway, Cape Girardeau, 573-651-2929) covers Bollinger, Butler, Cape Girardeau, Carter, Dunklin, Iron, Madison, Mississippi, New Madrid, Pemiscot, Perry, Reynolds, Ripley, Scott, St. Francois, Ste. Genevieve, Stoddard, Washington and Wayne counties. Other centers cover the rest of the state.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Missourians starting or growing a business; advising is free and confidential. Request an advisor through the center's sign-up page (SEMO center: missouri.ecenterdirect.com/signup?centerid=19).

Name: Live6 Alliance – Livernois-McNichols Corridor Business Support
Description: Live6 Alliance is the nonprofit planning and development organization for the Livernois-McNichols area of Detroit, including the Avenue of Fashion. It works on commercial corridor development, storefront and streetscape improvements and small business support, and circulates corridor-specific grant, event and marketing opportunities to businesses on the strip. Live6 is one of the nine partner organizations that nominate businesses for the Detroit Small Business Technology Fund. Contact through the website's contact form.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses located in or serving the Livernois-McNichols corridor of Detroit. No cost to engage.

Name: Going PRO Talent Fund (Michigan LEO)
Description: Michigan's Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity makes awards to employers to train, develop and retain current and newly hired employees, including registered apprenticeship training. Training must be short-term and lead to an industry-recognized, transferable credential. Awards have averaged $36,680 per employer and about $1,380 per employee trained; employers with fewer than 100 employees have received 59% of all awards. Employers begin with a fact-finding conversation with their local Michigan Works! Talent Fund key contact, then apply through the Work-Based Learning Online Management System (WBLOMS). FY2026 employer-led collaborative applications opened July 7, 2026 and stay open until funds are exhausted. Questions: LEO-TalentFund@michigan.gov.
Amount: varies (average $36,680 per employer; ~$1,380 per employee trained)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Michigan employers of any size
- Training must be short-term and fill a demonstrated skill gap
- Training must lead to an industry-recognized, transferable credential
- Start with a fact-finding conversation with the local Michigan Works! Talent Fund key contact before applying through WBLOMS

Name: Motor City Restore (Motor City Match Restore Track)
Description: Motor City Restore is the storefront-improvement track of Motor City Match, run by the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation. It provides matching grants covering up to 50% of project costs, to a maximum of $25,000, for exterior facade work, signage and decorative lighting, murals and art-related facade elements, awnings, bicycle racks, landscaping, drainage, and parking lot, patio and outdoor space improvements. Open to Detroit business owners and landlords who have been actively operating in a commercial storefront in the City of Detroit for at least one year. Applications are submitted through the Restore Track on MotorCityMatch.com. Contact: (844) 749-8359 or motorcityrestore@degc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Business owner or landlord of a commercial storefront in the City of Detroit
- Actively operating in that storefront for at least 1 year
- Project must be an eligible exterior/curb-appeal improvement
- Grant is a match: covers up to 50% of project costs, max $25,000

Name: Michigan SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Consulting
Description: The Michigan Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one consulting across the full life cycle of a business - start, scale and sell - covering business planning, financial projections, financing and loan packaging, market research, marketing and SEO, cybersecurity and exporting, plus live and on-demand training. A dedicated growth team serves businesses with 10+ employees and $1M+ in revenue. Request a consultant through the online form; a regional consultant is assigned by county.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; open to Michigan small businesses at any stage. Submit the online business consulting request form and a regional consultant is assigned by county.

Name: DanPaul Foundation Grant
Description: The DanPaul Foundation funds programs that directly serve the health, education, development and welfare of youth. Grant amounts can be up to $15,000 per calendar year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofits. No geographic restriction, no stated budget floor and no operating-history requirement. Excludes individual/family requests and lobbying.

Name: Kars4Kids Small Grant Program
Description: Kars4Kids awards small grants, typically $5,000, to US-based 501(c)(3) organizations whose primary mission serves children. Funding areas are youth development, mentorship and education. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through a form on the grants site; the funder responds in 4-6 months and notes decisions may take up to a year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: US-based IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) whose primary mission serves children. Programming must be secular / non-religious in focus.

Name: Georgia Secretary of State - charitable organization registration
Description: Charitable organizations soliciting contributions in Georgia register with the Securities and Charities Division using Form C-100, signed and notarized, with financial statements (requirements vary by annual revenue), the most recent IRS Form 990 or 990-EZ, and the IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter. Initial registration is $35 and renewal is $20; registration is valid for 24 months and the renewal window opens 90 days before expiration. Exemptions exist under O.C.G.A. section 43-17-9. Phone (470) 312-2640; file at georgiasos.seamlessdocs.com/sc/charitiesdivision.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Charitable organizations soliciting contributions in Georgia, unless exempt under O.C.G.A. 43-17-9.

Name: SCORE Atlanta - free business mentoring and workshops
Description: SCORE Atlanta provides free, unlimited one-on-one mentoring from volunteer experts, plus workshops on pricing, business planning, branding, customer service and HR, along with business templates, recorded webinars, online courses and live chat with mentors. The chapter serves metro Atlanta and surrounding North and West Georgia communities including Fulton, DeKalb, Clayton, Fayette, Douglas, Henry, Coweta and Carroll counties. Phone 1-800-634-0245.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and organizations in metro Atlanta and North/West Georgia. Mentoring is free; the chapter's grant-finding resources reference both nonprofits and for-profits.

Name: TechSoup - donated and discounted technology for nonprofits
Description: TechSoup gives validated nonprofits, charities, libraries and foundations access to donated and discounted technology from more than 60 donor partners including Microsoft, Adobe, Cisco and Intuit, plus community forums and free learning resources. Standard membership and catalog access are free; TechSoup Plus is $200 per year and adds Plus Catalog discounts, Engagement Hub webinars, guides, workshops, consultations and free courses for up to 10 people. Products carry a per-item administrative fee.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Validated nonprofits, charities, libraries and foundations. Free membership tier; TechSoup Plus is $200/year.

Name: Georgia Center for Nonprofits (GCN) membership
Description: GCN is Georgia's statewide nonprofit membership association. Membership includes Nonprofit University training, a member helpline, member-only learning and networking sessions, 15% off Work for Good job postings, up to $100 off certificate series, advocacy, and a monthly newsletter of Georgia funding opportunities. Dues are tiered by budget across 10 tiers, starting at $145/year for budgets of $99,000 and under and rising to $1,100/year for budgets of $10M and over. Main line (678) 916-3000; membership (678) 916-3080, membership@gcn.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Georgia nonprofit organizations. Budget-tiered dues; no operating-history requirement.

Name: Florida SBDC at the University of North Florida – free business consulting
Description: The Florida SBDC at the University of North Florida provides 100% no-cost, confidential one-on-one consulting to small businesses and startups in 18 Northeast Florida counties, including Duval, covering startup, growth, business continuity, government contracting and agribusiness, plus low-cost training. Request an appointment at floridasbdc.org/request-for-consulting/ or contact 904-620-2476 / smallbiz@unf.edu, 9am-5pm ET.
Amount: free (consulting at no cost; low-cost training)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and startups in the 18 Northeast Florida counties served by the UNF center: Alachua, Baker, Bradford, Citrus, Clay, Columbia, Dixie, Duval, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Lafayette, Levy, Marion, Nassau, Putnam, St. Johns, Suwannee and Union. Consulting is 100% no-cost and confidential, covering startup, growth, business continuity, government contracting and agribusiness. Request an appointment at floridasbdc.org/request-for-consulting/ or contact 904-620-2476 / smallbiz@unf.edu, 9am-5pm ET.

Name: California Capital FDC Small Business Loans (Sacramento CDFI)
Description: Sacramento-based CDFI offering microloans up to $50,000 across 24 counties including Sacramento, Yolo and El Dorado, and small business loans up to $150,000 through the EDA Revolving Loan Fund in Sacramento, Yolo, Nevada, El Dorado and Placer Counties. Also administers the California State Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (up to 80% guarantee on bank loans, max $2.5M) statewide for businesses with 1-750 employees. Rates up to 9.75%; terms 5-7 years, fully amortized, no prepayment penalty. Fees: $100 application, 3% loan fee, $250 documentation. Funding in 60-90 days from a complete application. Apply at cacapital.org/loans; phone (916) 442-1729; 1792 Tribute Rd., Suite 270, Sacramento, CA 95815. California Capital also runs a Women's Business Center and the Sacramento Valley SBDC, both offering free counseling.
Amount: Up to $50,000 (microloan) / up to $150,000 (EDA revolving loan fund)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses in the served counties. Credit score is not the primary factor - the lender evaluates history of handling credit, and applicants must be current on all debt. Startups with under 2 years of sales are welcome but must work with business counselors and show a secondary income source and industry experience; expanding businesses need one year of financial projections. Collateral required (business assets, equipment or real estate); personal guarantee from owners with a 20%+ stake. Eligible uses: working capital, inventory, machinery and equipment, tenant improvements, and acquisition of an existing business facilitating significant expansion. Debt refinancing and consolidation are not eligible.

Name: City of Sacramento Business Solutions Center
Description: A single intake point run by the City of Sacramento's Office of Innovation and Economic Development consolidating small business support: one-on-one consultations with business counselors in partnership with California Capital Financial Development Corporation, city fee credits of up to $2,500 toward permitting, licensing or inspection costs, microgrants up to $5,000 for equipment/digital tools, and SizeUp Sacramento for market and competitor data. Access is through the 311 Portal - create a 311 account at 311.cityofsacramento.org, add your business profile, and submit a "Business Resources" service request. The counseling hours satisfy the five-hour technical assistance requirement attached to the microgrant.
Amount: Up to $2,500 in city fee credits, plus free counseling and data tools
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses located within City of Sacramento limits. Free.

Name: City of Sacramento Small Business Microgrant Program
Description: The City of Sacramento's Office of Innovation and Economic Development awards microgrants of $2,500 to $5,000 from a $250,000 pool to for-profit businesses operating inside city limits. Reviewed monthly on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted. Applications run through the City's Submittable platform; the link comes from City staff or a business counselor. Start by registering your business on the 311 Portal at 311.cityofsacramento.org and submitting a "Business Resources" service request.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit businesses with an operating address within City of Sacramento limits. Must have completed at least 5 hours of technical assistance through the City's Business Solutions Center and hold active business registration/permits (Business Operations Tax Certificate, Secretary of State filing). Home-based businesses must show at least $25,000 in prior-year gross revenue. Eligible uses: replacing worn equipment essential to operations, new equipment/supplies that boost productivity, software/technology. Ineligible uses: staffing costs, inventory replenishment, general working capital. Ineligible business types: nonprofits, cannabis dispensaries, liquor stores, adult entertainment, casinos.

Name: Ventura County SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Small Business Development Center serving Ventura and Santa Barbara counties, hosted by the Economic Development Collaborative and part of the LA Regional SBDC Network. It provides no-cost one-on-one advising and low-cost training across the business lifecycle: startup assistance (business planning, financial projections), new business support (financial packaging, cash flow management) and growth services (rebranding, advanced web development). Office: 4001 Mission Oaks Blvd, Suite A-1, Camarillo, CA 93010; 805.409.9159.
Amount: Free advising and low-cost training (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Ventura and Santa Barbara counties. No revenue, industry or demographic requirements stated. Request an appointment at https://lasbdcnet.ecenterdirect.com/signup?centerid=93 or call 805.409.9159.

Name: WBENC Women's Business Enterprise (WBE) Certification
Description: National certification verifying that a business is at least 51 percent owned, controlled, operated and managed by one or more women. It is the credential most large corporations require for their supplier-diversity programs and vendor lists. Administered through 14 Regional Partner Organizations; the process involves a documentation review and a site visit. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must be at least 51 percent owned, controlled, operated and managed by a woman or women, with unrestricted control and day-to-day management by the woman owner(s). Processing fee is $350 for businesses under $1M annual gross revenue; effective July 1, 2026 a 3% credit card processing fee applies to all application submissions.

Name: Duval County Public Schools – Purchasing Services Vendor Registration
Description: Duval County Public Schools purchases goods and services, including spiritwear, uniforms, awards and promotional items, through its Purchasing Services department at 1701 Prudential Drive, Suite 322, Jacksonville, FL 32207. The district also operates an Office of Economic Opportunity for small and minority vendors. The vendor registration path is not published on the department page, so call (904) 858-4848 to ask how to join the bidders list and which commodity codes apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to businesses wishing to sell goods or services to Duval County Public Schools. Specific registration requirements and any small/minority vendor program criteria are not published online — confirm by phone at (904) 858-4848.

Name: Riverside Arts Market (Jacksonville) – Vendor Application
Description: Year-round Saturday market (10am-3pm) at 715 Riverside Ave, Jacksonville, FL 32204, with more than 300 rotating vendors. As of Aug 2026 the market is at capacity with no open application round; prospective vendors submit the Future Vendor Interest Form linked from the applications page, which staff review on an ongoing basis. Contact vendors@riversideartsmarket.org or 904-389-2449. Booth fees are not published; nonprofit informational booths are offered at reduced fees.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Vendors are selected on artisanship (products must be meaningfully made by the vendor, not just assembled), authenticity, branding and social presence. No revenue or time-in-business minimum stated. Currently waitlist only — submit the Future Vendor Interest Form.

Name: JSEB Certification – City of Jacksonville Small & Emerging Business
Description: Certification that qualifies a small business for the City of Jacksonville's contracting and subcontracting participation goals, for up to nine years from the first City contract with two possible one-year extensions. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Contact jseb@coj.net or (904) 255-8840. A separate JSEB Access to Capital short-term working capital loan program for certified businesses delivering to the City is listed on the site as PENDING as of Aug 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Average annual gross revenue over the immediately preceding three-year period not exceeding $12,000,000; reside in Duval County for 12 consecutive months before applying OR maintain an established business in Duval County for 18 months while residing in Duval, St. Johns, Nassau, Baker or Clay county for one year; ownership held at least one year and business existing at least one year; 51% minimum ownership by qualifying individual(s); U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident; CPA-prepared financial statements; training/education/mentoring every 24 months. Required documents include photo ID, proof of citizenship, three years of business federal tax returns, current business tax receipt, capabilities statement, three executed contracts or invoices, equipment and asset inventory, and a business lease or rental agreement.

Name: NYC Business Solutions - Financing Assistance
Description: NYC Small Business Services provides free one-on-one financing assistance to New York City businesses: an account manager helps identify the right financial product, reviews and prepares application documents, runs loan repayment calculations, and connects the business to banks, credit unions, nonprofit lenders and SBA programs, including SBA loan forgiveness paperwork and payment deferment options. Programs reachable through the service include the Contract Financing Loan Fund (up to $1,000,000), NYC Future Fund ($25,000-$500,000), New York Forward Loan Fund 2 (up to $150,000) and SBA Disaster Assistance. The same NYC Business Solutions Centers run free business courses; the Upper Manhattan center is at 361 West 125th Street, 2nd Floor. Call 888-SBS-4NYC (888-727-4692) Monday-Friday 9am-5pm or request assistance at sbsconnect.nyc.gov.
Amount: Free service; connects to loan programs from $25,000 to $1,000,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to business owners located in New York City. No revenue, credit or industry minimums stated for the advisory service itself; individual loan programs carry their own criteria.

Name: Accompany Capital Small Business Loans (NYC)
Description: Accompany Capital is a New York City CDFI, historically focused on immigrant and refugee entrepreneurs, with staff speaking up to 15 languages. Products include Microloans of $1,000-$50,000 at 8% fixed for 6 months to 3 years; Small Business Loans of $50,000-$75,000 (up to $100,000 for repeat borrowers) at 8% fixed for up to 3 years; the NYC Future Fund Loan of $25,000-$150,000 at 7.5% fixed for up to 5 years with revenue-based repayment; SBA Community Advantage loans up to $350,000 at 9.99% fixed for up to 10 years; a NYC Child Care Loan of $5,000-$25,000; and Credit-Building Loans up to $2,000. Most products carry a $25-$50 application fee and a 1% closing fee (3% on the NYC Future Fund). Apply online or contact Richard Portilla at (516) 202-6502 or rportilla@accompanycapital.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business located in one of New York City's five boroughs; owner 21 or older; positive cash flow; no bankruptcy in the past 24 months. No minimum credit score on microloans, small business loans, SBA Community Advantage or credit-building loans. The NYC Future Fund loan requires 12+ months operating, $50,000+ in annual revenue and one year of tax returns.

Name: UMEZ Small Business Loans (Hybrid Microloan, Term Loan, Line of Credit)
Description: Upper Manhattan Empowerment Zone loans for businesses located in Upper Manhattan. Three products: a Hybrid Microloan of up to $50,000 at 3% over 48 months (up to 25% forgivable) for working capital including marketing; a Term Loan of $50,000 to $249,000 at a fixed, market-competitive rate over roughly 5 years for start-up financing, expansion, machinery and equipment, leasehold improvements, limited refinancing, and working capital; and a revolving Line of Credit of $50,000 to $100,000 reviewed annually.
Amount: up to $50,000 (Hybrid Microloan); $50,000 - $249,000 (Term Loan); $50,000 - $100,000 (Line of Credit)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses must be located in Upper Manhattan. Hybrid Microloan: requires an existing commercial lease, 2+ years of operations, annual revenue over $100,000, positive operating income, a personal guaranty, and no tax liens; up to 25% of the loan may be forgivable. Term Loan: requires sustainable cash flows, experienced management, a business plan, a meaningful equity contribution, and a personal guaranty; $125 application fee. Line of Credit: requires 2+ years of operations, business revenue of at least 10x the requested amount, positive operating income, a personal guaranty, and no tax arrearages; $125 application fee. Expect roughly 2-3 months from application to funding. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

Name: Allies for Community Business (A4CB) small business loans
Description: Allies for Community Business is a Chicago-based CDFI lending to Illinois and Indiana small businesses, including home-based and online businesses run by state residents. Products include term loans and lines of credit of $500-$500,000, Credit Builder loans up to $2,500, and revenue-based financing of $50,000-$500,000. Loans up to $25,000 carry 12% with 3% in closing fees (14.1% APR); above $25,000, 10% with 3% in closing fees (12.1% APR); standard term is 36 months. Revenue-based financing is capped at 19.9% APR over 60-72 months with a 3% commitment fee. Funding can come in as little as 24 hours for eligible borrowers. Apply at a4cb.loanwell.com or call (312) 275-3000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business registered and in good standing with Illinois or Indiana, with a federal EIN, SSN or ITIN
- At least 6 months of business activity for standard loans (established businesses preferred)
- No minimum credit score; underwriting reviews 24 months of debt management history and monthly cash available, with an average of no more than 3 NSF fees per month
- No personal asset liens on loans under $250,000
- Excluded industries: financial services, illegal activities, firearms, pornography, marijuana sales, certain entertainment venues, religious instruction, government entities, lobbying, and speculative real estate

Name: Florida APEX Accelerator (government contracting assistance)
Description: Florida APEX Accelerator provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one consulting on all aspects of federal, state and local government contracting, plus training workshops on procurement and research tools for contract opportunities, specifications and award data. Consultants are embedded across the state. Start with the readiness checklist at flapex.org/checklist, register for no-cost consulting on the site, or email info@flapex.org.
Amount: free (consulting and training at no cost)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any Florida business, regardless of size, with the capability to work with government agencies at the federal, state or local level.

Name: SBA Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) Federal Contract Program
Description: Free SBA certification opening access to federal contracts set aside for women-owned small businesses. The federal government's goal is to award at least 5% of all federal contracting dollars to WOSBs each year. Certification is free through MySBA Certifications at certifications.sba.gov. The EDWOSB tier requires each qualifying owner to have personal net worth under $850,000, three-year average adjusted gross income of $400,000 or less, and personal assets of $6.5 million or less.
Amount: certification (no cash award); free to apply
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must meet SBA small business size standards and be at least 51% owned and controlled by women who are U.S. citizens, with women managing day-to-day operations and making long-term decisions.

Name: Women's Business Development Center (WBDC) – Chicago
Description: Chicago's women's business center, which has worked with more than 118,000 entrepreneurs over 40 years. Provides one-on-one and group business advising, cohort-based programs and workshops, WBE and WOSB certification, private-sector and government contracting support, and capital access including financial education, direct lending and Kiva microlending. Office at 8 South Michigan Avenue, 4th Floor, Chicago, IL 60603; 312.853.3477.
Amount: Free advising, certification and capital access
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Women business owners in the Chicago area. WBE certification requires at least 51% women ownership and control. No revenue or time-in-business minimum stated for advising.

Name: Chicago Artisan Market – Vendor Application
Description: A curated Chicago maker market accepting around 100 vendors from roughly 1,000 applications, with no application fee. Categories include art, fashion, home goods, ceramics, woodworking, jewelry, candles, soaps and skincare, food and beverage, kids' items and pets. Remaining 2026 dates: Fulton Market October 18, November 15 and December 13; Oak Brook outdoors October 3-4; Ravenswood November 28-29. Booth fees run $225-$450 at Fulton Market, $395-$650 at Ravenswood, and $395-$450 for two-day outdoor markets (which require a white 10'x10' tent). Spaces held with a $100 deposit until roughly 60 days before each market. Contact events@stylechicago.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Makers and small brands able to staff a booth at Chicago-area markets. Food and beverage vendors must use licensed commercial kitchens. No application fee; booth fees apply on acceptance.

Name: City of Chicago M/WBE Certification
Description: The City of Chicago certifies Minority-Owned and Women-Owned Business Enterprises. Certification is valid for five years, is recognised by other government agencies and some private-sector organisations, and is what makes a business eligible for the City's M/WBE contracting goals. Applications go through the Department of Procurement Services, Certification and Compliance Division, 121 North LaSalle Street, Room 806, Chicago, IL 60602; 312.744.4900.
Amount: Certification; access to City contracting goals
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses at least 51% owned AND at least 51% controlled by one or more minority group members or women.

Name: Shoppe Object Global Artisan Project
Description: Shoppe Object is a wholesale home and gift trade show; its Global Artisan Project is a curated section for artisan brands dedicated to preserving craft techniques, supporting artisan communities and promoting handmade work. Selected brands receive a 4'x8' booth with painted hard walls, lighting and brand signage, a choice of display fixtures, coaching from ByHand, promotion in Shoppe Object's marketing, and six months of Shoppe Online. Next New York show is February 7-9, 2027. Participation cost and application deadline are not published on the funder's page – email inquiry@shoppeobject.com to confirm terms.
Amount: Subsidised trade-show booth, coaching and promotion (cost not published)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Artisan brands with a wholesale distribution plan and marketing materials ready. Exhibitors must be available for the show plus two setup days, staff the booth with a representative present, and set up a digital catalogue on Shoppe Online. Full eligibility criteria are not published – confirm with the organiser.

Name: Illinois APEX Accelerator (government contracting assistance)
Description: The Illinois APEX Accelerator network, funded in part through a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of Defense and administered through the state's Business Information Center, gives existing Illinois businesses one-on-one confidential counseling on federal, state and local government contracting. Services include market research, bid matching and notifications, certification assistance, proposal review, and seminars, with particular focus on small, disadvantaged and women-owned firms. Businesses connect through the local center locator on the DCEO page or the statewide training calendar at ilsbdc.ecenterdirect.com/events.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All existing Illinois businesses. Services are free; find and register with the nearest APEX center through the locator on the DCEO page. Centers are hosted by the Women's Business Development Center, Illinois SBDC hosts, SIU, Bradley University and College of DuPage, among others.

Name: Airport Minority Advisory Council (AMAC) Membership
Description: AMAC is the national nonprofit trade association advancing minority- and woman-owned participation in aviation and airport concessions, with 8 regional chapters and membership tiers for airports, corporations, businesses, students, and individuals. Members get access to an aviation-industry network, business-development connections and mentorship, a members-only resource library and directory, and 11 active committees. The AMAC Foundation also runs the Runway to Success competition, open to businesses at least 51% minority- or woman-owned that supply goods or services to aviation, with regional pitch rounds leading to a national final at the Airport Business Conference. Contact: (703) 414-2622, info@amac-org.com.

Name: Shasta-Cascade SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Shasta-Cascade Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising to Northern California small businesses, covering business funding, financial planning, marketing and growth, alongside no-cost webinars and training events and specialty programs in import/export, agriculture and rural business, and restaurants. Offices are at 1305 Sacramento Avenue, Redding, CA 96001 and 412 W. Miner Street, Yreka, CA 96097. Phone: (530) 222-8323. Register for an advisor at sbdcsc.org/join.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in the Shasta-Cascade region of Northern California, at any stage. Advising is free and confidential; sign up through the online registration form.

Name: New York State MWBE Certification (Empire State Development)
Description: New York State certifies Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprises through Empire State Development, and certified firms are listed in the state Directory of Certified Firms used for New York State contracting and for meeting agency MWBE utilization goals. Requirements: at least 51% owned, operated and controlled by minority group members and/or women who are U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens; generally at least one year in operation with active, independent operation; no more than 300 employees averaged across four calendar quarters; each qualifying owner's personal net worth under $15 million after allowable deductions (primary residence, stake in the firm, and qualified retirement savings up to $750,000 are exempt); and Authority to do Business in New York State from the Department of State, with current personal and business federal and state tax returns. Start with the MWBE Certification Assessment Tool, then submit through the Empire State MWBE Hub at mwbe.esd.ny.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- At least 51% owned, operated and controlled by minority group members and/or women who are U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens
- Generally at least one year in operation, actively and independently operated
- No more than 300 employees, averaged across four calendar quarters
- Personal net worth of each qualifying owner under $15 million after allowable deductions
- Authority to do Business in New York State from the Department of State
- Current personal and business federal and state tax returns with all schedules
- Out-of-state firms should seek certification in their home state first

Apply via the MWBE Certification Assessment Tool, then the Empire State MWBE Hub.

Name: NYC M/WBE Certification Program
Description: New York City's Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise certification lists a business in the NYC Online Directory of Certified Businesses, which City agencies and prime contractors use to find vendors, and opens access to networking events, customized courses and targeted business meetings. Requirements: the business must be legally operating in New York State, have at least one year of selling goods or services, be at least 51% owned by U.S. citizens or permanent residents who are women and/or members of a designated minority group (Black, Hispanic, Asian-Pacific, Asian-Indian, Native American), be a sole proprietorship, LLC, corporation, LLP, LP or general partnership, and have its main office in the five boroughs or a designated NY/NJ county. Application and renewal are free; certification runs on a five-year renewal cycle. Apply through SBS Connect; questions go to mwbe@sbs.nyc.gov or NYC Department of Small Business Services, 1 Liberty Plaza, 11th Floor, New York, NY 10006.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Legally operating in New York State
- At least one year of selling goods or services
- At least 51% owned, operated and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents who are women and/or members of a designated minority group
- Eligible structures: sole proprietorship, LLC, corporation, LLP, LP, general partnership
- Main office in the five boroughs, or a designated NY/NJ county with substantial NYC market presence
- Documentation required: tax returns, proof of citizenship, business licenses, contracts, ownership documents

Free to apply and to renew; five-year renewal cycle. Applications submitted through SBS Connect.

Name: The Hatchery Chicago (shared commercial kitchens and storage)
Description: The Hatchery is a 67,000-square-foot food and beverage incubator at 135 N. Kedzie Ave, Chicago, IL 60612, offering shared and private commercial kitchens, storage, and co-working space alongside business planning support, access to financing, classes and online courses, a service-provider database, and networking events. Membership and incubation cohort options are available, and kitchen tours can be booked through the website. Phone: 312-283-5723.
Amount: Commercial kitchen, storage and co-working membership (pricing on request)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Chicago-area food and beverage businesses needing licensed commercial kitchen, prep or storage space. Membership and cohort options; contact for pricing, licensing and insurance requirements.

Name: NASE Growth Grants
Description: NASE awards up to $4,000 to member businesses for marketing, advertising, hiring, facility expansion, equipment, software, training, and other specific growth needs. Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed quarterly. A $120 annual NASE membership is required to apply immediately. Monthly members must wait 90 days. Funds cannot be used for existing debt or rent/mortgage.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be NASE members in good standing at application and continuously through the award. Annual members may apply immediately; monthly members must wait 90 days before consideration. The standard annual membership is $120. Required application materials include a statement of grant use, a business plan, a recent tax return or profit-and-loss statement, and a photo. Funds may support marketing, hiring, equipment, software, facilities, and training, but may not pay existing debt or rent/mortgage.
Application Fee: $120 annual membership required for immediate application

Name: North Carolina electronic Vendor Portal (eVP) registration
Description: The NC electronic Vendor Portal is the internet application that allows companies and individuals to register to do business with the state of North Carolina. A registered vendor account lets you respond electronically to specified solicitations and receive nightly solicitation notifications for the commodity codes you select, and it is also the entry point for NC Small Business Enterprise certification and NC eProcurement. Registration is completed online at evp.nc.gov; guidance for new vendors is at eprocurement.nc.gov under Vendor Training, and questions go through the NC eProcurement contact page.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any company or individual wanting to do business with the state of North Carolina. Registration is completed online at evp.nc.gov. New-vendor guidance is at https://eprocurement.nc.gov/training/vendor-training/registering-evp.

Name: Alamance Community College Small Business Center (free counseling and workshops)
Description: The Small Business Center at Alamance Community College is part of the state-funded North Carolina Small Business Center Network and provides free confidential one-on-one counseling, online learning, and workshops for current and aspiring business owners on marketing, finance, business modeling and expanding operations. Director Phydesia Lewis can be reached at pglewis406@alamancecc.edu or 336-506-4312; the center's general line is 336-506-4311 and it is located on the main campus at 1247 Jimmie Kerr Road, Graham, NC 27253.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free and open to current and aspiring business owners; part of the NC Small Business Center Network based in Alamance County. Counseling is confidential and one-on-one. Contact Director Phydesia Lewis, pglewis406@alamancecc.edu, 336-506-4312; general line 336-506-4311; 1247 Jimmie Kerr Road, Graham, NC 27253.

Name: DC Small Business Development Center (DCSBDC)
Description: The DC Small Business Development Center, hosted at Howard University and funded in part by the U.S. Small Business Administration, provides one-on-one consulting, training and information resources to new and existing businesses. Advising areas include starting and growing a business, government contracting, capital readiness, cybersecurity readiness, AI and operational efficiency, financial literacy and export services. New clients register for advising online. Phone: (202) 806-1550, Info@dcsbdc.org, 2600 6th St. NW, Room 128, Washington DC 20059.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to new and existing businesses in the District of Columbia. Services are extended to the public on a nondiscriminatory basis; language assistance services available. New clients register for advising online.

Name: DC Certified Business Enterprise (CBE) Certification
Description: Certification through the DC Department of Small and Local Business Development gives a business preference in procurement opportunities offered by the District of Columbia. To qualify, the principal office must be physically located in Washington, DC, the business must be independently owned and more than 50% DC-based owned (or owned by a non-DC entity that is more than 50% owned by DC residents), and leadership must perform managerial duties from that DC office. A business must also meet one of four local-connection tests: more than 50% of employees are DC residents, more than 50% of owners are DC residents, more than 50% of business assets excluding bank accounts are in DC, or more than 50% of gross receipts are DC-based. New applicants submit an online application with supporting documents for DSLBD review. DSLBD: (202) 727-3900, dslbd@dc.gov, 441 4th Street NW, Suite 850 North.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Principal office physically located in Washington, DC; independently owned and more than 50% DC-based owned, or owned by a non-DC entity more than 50% owned by DC residents; leadership performs managerial duties in the DC principal office. Must also meet one of four local-connection tests: over 50% of employees are DC residents, over 50% of owners are DC residents, over 50% of business assets (excluding bank accounts) are in DC, or over 50% of gross receipts are DC-based.

Name: Kentucky Small Business Tax Credit (KSBTC)
Description: Kentucky's Office of Entrepreneurship offers state tax credits to small businesses that both hire and invest. Qualifying businesses have fifty or fewer full-time employees, have created and sustained at least one new full-time position for a year, and have put at least five thousand dollars into qualifying equipment or technology. Credits run from three thousand five hundred to twenty-five thousand dollars annually, scaled to jobs created and investment made.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- 50 or fewer full-time employees
- Must have hired at least one NEW full-time employee and SUSTAINED that position for one year
- That employee must earn a minimum of $10.88 per hour
- Must have invested at least $5,000 in qualifying equipment or technology
- Open to most industry segments, including retail and service businesses

Credit ranges from $3,500 to $25,000 per year, scaled to jobs created and investment levels.

Apply by completing the KSBTC Application with all required supporting documentation. Contact the Office of Entrepreneurship: cedsbsd@ky.gov or 800-626-2930. No application fee mentioned.

Name: Sip Shop Eat Bay Area Vendor Application
Description: Sip Shop Eat runs curated pop-up markets built to connect emerging small businesses with new customers and drive in-person sales. Two Bay Area events are upcoming: a two-day indoor market in San Francisco and an outdoor holiday market at Cityline Sunnyvale. Vendor packages include pre-event training and digital promotion through Sip Shop Eat's own channels alongside the booth space itself.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Curated selection of emerging small businesses
- Vendor package includes pre-event training and digital promotion through Sip Shop Eat's channels

VENDOR COST: $350 for a 5'x10' space; $450 for a 10'x10' space.

UPCOMING BAY AREA EVENTS:
- San Francisco: November 7-8, 2026 (two-day indoor market)
- Sunnyvale: December 5, 2026 (outdoor holiday market at Cityline Sunnyvale)

No application deadline is published - applications appear to be accepted on a rolling basis until each event fills. Apply well ahead of the event dates.

Location note: tagged CA (San Francisco) plus CA, since Sunnyvale has no matching location option in this database.
Industry: Retail,Consumer Packaged Goods,Apparel & Accessories,Arts & Crafts,Food & Beverage

Name: SF Fairmont Holiday Rooftop Faire Vendor Application
Description: The Fairmont San Francisco hosts an open-air holiday market in its rooftop gardens on Nob Hill, featuring independent vendors across categories including jewelry and apparel. The faire runs across two separate weekends, and vendors may apply for individual dates rather than committing to the full run. Table and booth space is charged per day at two size tiers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Independent vendors across categories including jewelry and apparel
- Held outdoors in the Fairmont's rooftop gardens, Nob Hill, San Francisco
- VENDORS MAY APPLY FOR INDIVIDUAL DATES rather than the whole run

VENDOR COST: $150 per day for a 6' table; $250 per day for a 10'x10' space.

EVENT DATES: November 27-29, 2026 and December 18-20, 2026.

No application deadline is published - apply ahead of the event dates.

Name: Illinois Product Program
Description: The Illinois Department of Agriculture runs a free logo program identifying agricultural and food products produced, processed, packaged or headquartered in Illinois. Members may place the Illinois Product logo on packaging and marketing materials and gain visibility through the department's events and marketing initiatives. A companion Homegrown by Heroes logo is available to Illinois farmers, ranchers, fishermen and producers who have served in the U.S. military.
Amount: free logo licence, marketing and promotional exposure
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business must produce, process, or package food or agricultural products IN Illinois, or be headquartered in the state
- Separate membership paths for producers ("Become a Member") and retailers ("Become a Retailer")

MEMBERS RECEIVE: the right to use the Illinois Product logo on packaging and marketing materials, plus visibility through Illinois Product events and marketing initiatives. Per Anny's summary this also includes retail promotions, food-service initiatives, special events, trade shows, state fair exhibits and listing in the Illinois Product database - the program page confirms events and marketing initiatives generally but does not itemise these.

COMPANION PROGRAM: Homegrown by Heroes provides a distinct logo for Illinois farmers, ranchers, fishermen and producers who have served or are serving in any branch of the U.S. military.

No application deadline; membership is open on a rolling basis. Contact: Illinois Department of Agriculture, 801 E. Sangamon Ave, Springfield, IL 62702-1813.
Industry: Agriculture,Food & Beverage,Marketing & Brand Management,Consumer Packaged Goods

Name: Maine Micro-Enterprise Assistance Program
Description: Maine's Department of Economic and Community Development funds micro-enterprise assistance through its Community Development Block Grant program. Participating communities receive an annual allocation and pass support to local micro-enterprises for working capital, interior renovations, exterior improvements such as signage, painting, siding, awnings, lighting and display windows, and project planning. Assistance may be delivered as grants or loans, with grants structured as forgivable loans.
Amount: up to $50,000 per business; up to $150,000 per community annually
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
IMPORTANT STRUCTURE: this is a CDBG program administered through PARTICIPATING COMMUNITIES, not applied for directly with the State. A business works with its municipality, and availability depends on whether that community has an active allocation.

- Maximum $150,000 per community annually; individual businesses capped at $50,000
- Grants are structured as FORGIVABLE LOANS; communities may provide assistance as grants or loans
- Where anticipated loan repayments exceed $35,000, a CDFI or Community Based Development Organization must manage repayment and relending

ELIGIBLE EXPENSES: working capital, interior renovations, exterior improvements (signage, painting, siding, awnings, lighting, display windows), and planning activities for project development.
INELIGIBLE: infrastructure (sewer, water, roads, parking) and residential-only buildings.

Standard CDBG micro-enterprise rules generally require five or fewer employees including the owner, and low-to-moderate income qualification for the owner - but neither is stated on this DECD page. Confirm with the municipality or DECD.

Name: WorkSource Oregon On-the-Job Training (OJT)
Description: Wage reimbursement for Oregon employers who hire and train new employees. Employers are reimbursed for up to 50% of a new hire's wages during their first months of on-the-job training, capped at $5,000. Delivered at no cost through local WorkSource Oregon business services representatives, alongside recruitment support, tax credit identification, wage analysis, apprenticeships, and internships.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Oregon employers hiring new employees who need skills training. Employers work with a local WorkSource business services representative to set up an OJT agreement; candidates are typically referred through WorkSource and iMatchSkills. No application deadline — available on a rolling basis. Detailed eligibility requirements and application procedures are set by local workforce boards and are not published on the statewide page, so contact a local WorkSource office to begin.

Name: Catapult @ Penn GSE
Description: Virtual accelerator from Catalyst @ Penn GSE for education entrepreneurs, supporting ventures from idea through scale. Cohort members receive roughly 150 hours of searchable, personalized online content plus coaching from matched advisors across five focus areas: leadership, product development, efficacy, technology, and fundraising. Members work alongside Penn GSE faculty and researchers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to education entrepreneurs and edtech ventures across stages, from early idea to scaling platforms. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Contact catapult@gse.upenn.edu for current cohort details.

Name: WorkSource Seattle-King County Employer Services
Description: Free workforce support for King County employers, including candidate recruitment, job postings, hiring events, and workforce planning. Employee development options include On-the-Job Training with reimbursement for training costs, apprenticeships and pre-apprenticeships, internships and work experience, and Incumbent Worker Training to upskill current staff. Retraining support includes the Customized Training Program, which offers interest-free training loan assistance, and the state Job Skills Program, which funds half of training costs against an employer match.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to employers in Seattle and King County. Services are free; no deadline — available on a rolling basis. Employers start by submitting the Employer Inquiry Form on the site, and a business services representative determines which programs and funding apply. Reimbursement percentages and dollar caps for On-the-Job Training, the Customized Training Program, and Incumbent Worker Training are not published and are set case by case.

Name: USDA Farm Storage Facility Loan (FSFL) Program
Description: USDA Farm Service Agency loans that finance eligible on-farm storage and handling facilities and equipment. Eligible structures include grain bins, hay barns, bulk tanks, and cold storage facilities, plus drying, handling, and storage equipment and storage/handling trucks — new or used, permanent or portable.
Amount: up to $500,000 (storage facilities); up to $100,000 (storage and handling trucks); microloans up to $50,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to producers of eligible commodities, including fruits, vegetables, floriculture, hops, maple products, dairy, eggs, unprocessed poultry and meat, grains, oilseeds, peanuts, pulse crops, hay, hemp, honey, rye, aquaculture, and renewable biomass. Regular FSFLs require a 15% down payment and a three-year production history; microloans of up to $50,000 require only a 5% down payment and waive the production-history requirement. Loan terms run 3 to 12 years. Interest rates are set by USDA based on loan term and the date of approval — as of September 2026 they range from 4.250% (3-year) to 4.875% (12-year). Applications are accepted year-round through your local FSA county office. No application fee listed.

Name: Atlanta Business Readiness Loan Fund (ABRLF)
Description: Invest Atlanta pilot loan fund helping small businesses in Atlanta's commercial corridors prepare for and capitalize on large city-sponsored events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup and Super Bowl LXII, through investments in marketing, inventory, and customer experience. Uses streamlined underwriting for faster approvals.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to businesses located within commercial corridors inside Atlanta city limits. Loans range from $5,000 to $15,000. Interest rates run from 3% to Prime, set by a cash flow analysis of the applicant. Terms up to three years and cannot exceed the term of the applicant's lease. Requires a 5% match, which may be cash or in-kind. $100 application fee. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis; the fund is one of several Invest Atlanta loan programs listed on the small business loan programs page.

Name: King County Small Contractor and Supplier (SCS) Certification
Description: Free certification that helps eligible Washington small businesses compete for government contracting and purchasing opportunities. Certified firms receive a fair market range scoring preference on goods and services contracts, evaluation points on consulting contracts, and participation requirements favoring SCS firms on construction contracts — and qualify automatically for opportunities with the Port of Seattle, Sound Transit, and Seattle Colleges.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a for-profit small business licensed in Washington State that meets U.S. Small Business Administration size standards, with no more than $31.84 million in gross receipts averaged over three years and a majority owner personal net worth under $2.047 million (excluding primary residence and equity in the business). Free to apply, no deadline. Two paths: standard submission with a CPA affidavit (about 10 business days) or a personal net worth statement plus tax returns (15-30 business days); firms already certified as state MBE/WBE qualify via fast-track without a separate application. Questions: SCSCertification@kingcounty.gov. This is a certification, not funding — it opens access to contracts rather than awarding money.

Name: Downtown St. Louis Retail Incentive Program
Description: Incentives from the St. Louis Development Corporation supporting businesses that activate and improve street-level storefronts in Downtown St. Louis. Three tiers are available: up to $15,000 for pop-up retail, up to $50,000 for tenant improvements at new retail establishments, and up to $5,000 for qualifying sidewalk cafe or retail-display improvements.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For businesses activating ground-floor storefronts in the Downtown and Downtown West neighborhoods of St. Louis. The Tenant Improvement tier covers up to 25% of interior and exterior improvement costs to a $50,000 maximum and is open to property owners, prospective owners, current tenants opening a second location, and prospective tenants; all applicants must secure landlord consent and sign a minimum 12-month lease for ground-floor space. Administered by St. Louis Development Corporation in partnership with Greater St. Louis, Inc. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.

Name: Danville Business Promotion Grant
Description: The Town of Danville reimburses licensed local businesses for marketing and promotion tied to public-facing events, up to $5,000 per event. Funded activity must align with the Town's Comprehensive Economic Development Plan and reflect Danville's marketing attributes - historic, small-town, recreation, foodie destination, family-friendly and arts-focused. Materials must carry approved Town branding and the #LiveLocallyDanville hashtag. Reimbursement requests are due within 60 days of the event.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Valid, current Town of Danville business license required. Events/projects must be open to the public and align with the Town's Comprehensive Economic Development Plan. Applications for events July 1, 2025-June 30, 2026 awarded as received; applications for events July 1-December 31, 2026 awarded in June 2026. Reimbursement claims due within 60 days of event conclusion. Direct application form: https://www.danville.ca.gov/FormCenter/Business-Resources-12/Business-Promotion-Grant-Application-202-130 . Contact Melysa Vander Mel, 925-314-3379.

Name: NY Employee Training Incentive Program (ETIP)
Description: Empire State Development's Employee Training Incentive Program gives New York employers a refundable tax credit covering 50 percent of eligible skills-training costs, up to $10,000 per employee, plus 50 percent of stipends paid to qualifying interns, up to $3,000 each. Businesses in strategic industries apply to ESD before training begins and must show a ten-to-one benefit-cost ratio. Roughly $5 million in credits is available statewide each year.
Amount: 50% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per employee; 50% of intern stipends up to $3,000 per intern
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must be located in New York State, operate in a strategic industry, make a significant capital investment, and demonstrate a benefit-cost ratio of at least 10:1. APPLICATIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED TO ESD BEFORE TRAINING BEGINS. Internship component limited to employers with fewer than 100 employees in advanced technology, life sciences, software development or clean energy; internships cannot exceed 12 months, and interns cannot be current/former employees or displace regular workers. Excluded: accounting, utilities, finance, hospitality, law, medical/dental practices, real estate, restaurants, retail/wholesale. Statewide cap $5 million annually, up to $1 million for approved internship programs. Preliminary application: https://esdnys.microsoftcrmportals.com/ETIP-Application---preliminary/ . Contact etip@empire.state.dev

Name: San Francisco Downtown SF Vibrancy Loan & Grant Fund
Description: A $3.6 million City of San Francisco fund, with lending administered by Main Street Launch, that helps new and expanding small businesses occupy ground-floor vacant storefronts in designated downtown areas. It offers fixed 4% loans of $25,000 to $100,000 repayable over five years with no minimum credit score, alongside grants of up to $50,000. Applicants also receive technical assistance through SF SBDC plus legal support on entity formation and lease negotiation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must occupy a ground-floor, public-facing vacancy in a designated downtown SF area; new or expanding for-profit business with a valid San Francisco business license; at least 51% owned by a US citizen or permanent resident; no chains or franchises; no minimum credit score. Loan inquiry: https://mainstreetlaunch.org/about-us/loan-inquiry-main/ . Page last modified July 2026. Technical assistance via SF SBDC; legal support via Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights.

Name: Michigan APACC AAPI Small Business Membership Grant
Description: The Asian Pacific American Chamber of Commerce, sponsored by General Motors, covers the full cost of a one-year APACC membership for AAPI-owned small businesses and AAPI professionals in Michigan. The Silver (Entrepreneur) tier serves AAPI-owned companies with 50 or fewer employees; the Bronze (Individual) tier serves Asian or Pacific Islander professionals. Recipients gain chamber access, networking and supplier-diversity connections in exchange for attending four APACC events annually.
Amount: In-kind - sponsored one-year APACC membership (Bronze $200 / Silver $300 value)
