Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Silver (Entrepreneur) tier: AAPI-owned small company with 50 employees or fewer. Bronze (Individual) tier: individual professionals of Asian or Pacific Islander descent employed in the public or private sector. Recipients must attend four APACC events per year and complete a membership feedback survey at renewal. Sponsored by General Motors. Apply via PDF form linked on the program page. Contact events@apacc.net or 248-430-5855.

Name: Media Linvilla Orchards Winter Makers Market
Description: Linvilla Orchards in Media, Pennsylvania hosts an outdoor winter makers market across four consecutive weekends from late November through December 2026. Artists and makers of fine art, crafts, paintings, graphic art, drawings and other artisan goods can book a single weekend or the full season. All products must be handcrafted by the exhibitor; imported, franchised and mass-produced merchandise, food, beverages and plants are excluded.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All products must be handcrafted by the exhibitor. Excluded: imported merchandise, franchised products, food/beverages, plants, offensive materials, participatory activities. Booth 10'x15'; vendors supply tent, tables and displays. Fee $90 per weekend or $300 for the full season. Acceptance on a rolling basis, no later than three weeks after the application date. Market weekends November 28-29, December 5-6, 12-13, 19-20, 2026, Sat/Sun 10am-4pm. Setup 7:30-10am. Weather cancellations transfer to another weekend or refund minus $10.

Name: Lansing Facade Improvement Program
Description: The Lansing Economic Development Corporation reimburses commercial property owners and tenants for permanent exterior building improvements citywide. Three tiers are offered: a Transformational Grant of up to $30,000 for major rehabilitation, an Aesthetic Grant of up to $10,000 for targeted exterior work, and a Design Grant of up to $5,000 for professional design services with no match required. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing, first-come first-served basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Property must be within Lansing city limits, zoned for commercial use, and have an operating business (or be renovating for one). Property taxes and city obligations must be current. Commercial tenants may apply with written owner permission. Transformational and Aesthetic tiers require a 50% match; Design Grant requires no match. Governed by the FY2026-2027 FIP Program Guide. Contact Kahleea Washington, 517-512-5122.

Name: LA County Shop Local Marketing Lab
Description: A no-cost six-week virtual marketing program from the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity, launched August 2026. Participants attend weekly interactive workshops, get one-on-one office hours with marketing advisors, access on-demand educational video content, and leave with a customised marketing plan for their business. Basic and advanced learning tracks are offered so both newer and more established operators can enroll.
Amount: In-kind - free six-week virtual marketing program with 1:1 office hours and a custom marketing plan
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business located in Los Angeles County with 100 or fewer employees and $19 million or less in annual revenue. No cost to participate. Also referred to as 'Marketing Lab+'. Announcement: https://opportunity.lacounty.gov/la-county-launches-new-technical-assistance-programs-to-help-small-businesses-access-capital-and-strengthen-financial-health/

Name: San Francisco Vacant to Vibrant
Description: A program of SF New Deal and the City of San Francisco that turns vacant downtown storefronts into temporary pop-up retail, food and arts spaces. Small business activators receive $2,000 to $10,000 plus technical assistance, while participating property owners get up to $5,000 toward tenant improvements and utilities. The team secures storefronts, permits and grant funding on the operator's behalf. Applications are reviewed within 30 to 45 days.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses, artists or organizations with pop-up readiness and previous experience operating retail, food or arts spaces or events in San Francisco; prior pop-up experience preferred but not strictly required. Direct application: https://airtable.com/appqt6uN2Gj2jaast/pagmCF4VQ5E5ky2tC/form . Run by SF New Deal with a 14-member advisory committee. Contact vibrantSF@sfnewdeal.org / (415) 480-1185.

Name: Berkshire County BBEC Professional Expertise Grant
Description: The Berkshire Black Economic Council awards micro-grants covering professional services that Black-owned businesses in Berkshire County need but struggle to pay for - accounting, bookkeeping, web development, grant writing, graphic design, legal services, marketing and general consulting. Awards reach $1,500 and are reviewed and granted on a rolling, first-come first-served basis through the council's submission portal, with no fixed annual closing date.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be for-profit OR nonprofit Black businesses or entrepreneurs located inside Berkshire County, Massachusetts. Funds restricted to professional services (accounting, web development, grant writing, graphic design, legal, marketing, consulting). Reviewed and awarded on a rolling basis, first come first served. Direct application: https://berkshirebec.submittable.com/submit . Contact assistant@berkshirebec.org for full guidelines.

Name: Durham Tech Small Business Center (free counseling and seminars, Durham and Orange counties)
Description: Part of the NC Community College Small Business Center Network, the Durham Tech Small Business Center provides free, confidential one-on-one counseling for new and existing business owners, free business skills seminars and workshops (in person and as webinars), and a resource centre of business literature and local community information. It serves Orange County from 136 E Rosemary St, Chapel Hill, NC 27514 and Durham County from 701 W Main St, Durham. Register for counseling through the NCSBC portal linked on the centre's site. Hours are Monday-Friday, 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; (919) 536-7241 ext. 4316, sbc@durhamtech.edu.
Amount: free one-on-one counseling, seminars and workshops (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to new and existing small business owners in Durham and Orange counties, NC. Free. Register for counseling through the NCSBC portal linked from the centre's site; (919) 536-7241 ext. 4316, sbc@durhamtech.edu.

Name: Miami-Dade County Small Business Enterprise (SBE) certification
Description: Miami-Dade County certifies local firms as Small Business Enterprises so they can compete for County contracts and set-asides. The Goods & Services category (SBE-GS) covers firms providing goods or services other than construction, architectural or engineering work, and caps average gross receipts at $8 million; separate categories exist for construction (SBE-CON) and for architecture and engineering (SBE-A&E). All SBE programs require an active Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax receipt held for at least one year, a physical location in Miami-Dade County (home-based offices must meet zoning requirements), and personal net worth for each owner not exceeding $3.5 million. Applications are submitted online through the County's Business Management Workforce System. Questions: 305-375-3111.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Active Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax receipt held at least one year; physical location in Miami-Dade County (home-based offices must meet zoning requirements); personal net worth per owner not exceeding $3.5 million. Revenue caps: SBE-GS average gross receipts up to $8M; SBE-A&E up to $6.5M ($8M for engineering, surveying and mapping); SBE-CON $8M-$15M depending on contractor type. Related County programs: Local Developing Business (LDB) for MIA aeronautical services, DBE and ACDBE (federal). Application fee not stated on the County page.

Name: Florida SBDC at FIU – free business consulting (Miami-Dade)
Description: The Florida SBDC at FIU is the Florida SBDC Network's center for Miami-Dade County, and has also served Monroe County since 2018. It provides confidential, no-cost consulting from experienced business consultants covering business strategy, market research, financing guidance and connections to capital, and government contracting access through the Florida APEX Accelerator, along with student-led AI-focused consulting projects. The center does not make loans or provide investment capital. Request a consultant through floridasbdc.org/request-for-consulting/.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in Miami-Dade and Monroe counties. Consulting is 100% no-cost and confidential. Request an appointment at floridasbdc.org/request-for-consulting/. The Jacksonville-region equivalent is the Florida SBDC at UNF, which serves 18 Northeast Florida counties only — use this FIU record for South Florida businesses.

Name: Alabama SBDC at South Alabama
Description: The Alabama Small Business Development Center at the University of South Alabama serves an eight-county region of southwest Alabama, including Mobile. It provides confidential one-on-one advising at no charge to Alabama entrepreneurs and small business owners, covering business planning, financial analysis, government marketing and procurement, exporting and importing, and procurement certifications, plus training that includes after-hours and weekend sessions. Register through the online client registration form on the ASBDC site. Office: 358 St Louis St, Mobile, AL 36602, 877-825-7232, open 8 a.m.-5 p.m. weekdays; the network also lists a University of South Alabama campus office at 600 Clinic Drive, Room 328, Mobile, AL 36688, (251) 460-6078.
Amount: free one-on-one advising and training (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free and open to Alabama entrepreneurs and small business owners in the eight-county southwest Alabama region served by the South Alabama center, including Mobile. Register through the online client registration form (eCenter Direct) on the ASBDC site, or call 877-825-7232. Basic demographic information is collected for funding partners.

Name: SCORE Alabama
Description: SCORE Alabama provides free expert mentoring and resources to small businesses in Birmingham, Montgomery, Mobile and communities across Alabama, plus bordering areas of Mississippi and Florida. Services include one-on-one mentoring, in-person and online workshops and webinars, business templates and educational resources, and real-time chat advice with mentors. Mentoring is free for the life of the business. Request a mentor by entering your ZIP code on the site and using the Find A Mentor option; the chapter operates virtually and can be reached at (251) 385-6667.
Amount: free mentoring and workshops (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free and open to any small business owner or aspiring entrepreneur in Alabama and bordering areas of Mississippi and Florida. No industry, revenue or demographic requirements. Request a mentor by ZIP code through the Find A Mentor option on score.org; the chapter operates virtually. Phone (251) 385-6667.

Name: LiftFund Small Business Loans
Description: LiftFund is a nonprofit CDFI headquartered in San Antonio that lends across Texas. Loans run from $500 to $10 million with terms of 1 to 15 years and rates as low as 0% on some programs, and LiftFund states an average of 2-3 days to fund from receipt of a completed application with all documentation. Eligible uses include equipment, inventory, working capital, operating expenses, commercial real estate and start-up costs. LiftFund publishes no minimum credit score or minimum time in business and works with applicants who may not qualify for traditional financing, including those with limited credit or collateral. Apply at liftfund.com/apply-now or call (888) 215-2373. Note: LiftFund is not a Mona partner lender, so there is no referral link.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- No published minimum credit score or minimum time in business
- Works with applicants who may not qualify for traditional financing, including limited credit or collateral
- Eligible uses: equipment, inventory, working capital, operating expenses, commercial real estate, start-up costs
- Detailed eligibility guidelines are downloadable on the site

Name: PeopleFund Small Business Loans
Description: PeopleFund is a Texas-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit, U.S. Treasury-certified CDFI and SBA lender serving the whole state, with offices in Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, Houston, San Antonio, El Paso, Lubbock, Lufkin and the Rio Grande Valley. It lends to startups, nonprofits and existing small businesses — startups make up 53% of its clients — and describes its underwriting as flexible with personal consideration of each application. Products include equipment purchases, working capital term loans, revolving lines of credit and SBA 504 loans for real estate, lending up to $5 million through the SBA. There is no fee to apply and no prepayment penalties. Apply at peoplefund.org/get-a-loan or call 1-888-222-0017. Note: PeopleFund is not a Mona partner lender, so there is no referral link.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Texas businesses statewide; startups, nonprofits and existing small businesses all eligible
- Aeris A+ rated CDFI and SBA lender; flexible underwriting with personal consideration of each application
- No fee to apply, no prepayment penalties
- Credit score, time-in-business and revenue minimums are not published — confirm by phone

Name: UGA Small Business Development Center – Gwinnett Office (Lawrenceville)
Description: The University of Georgia Small Business Development Center’s Gwinnett office provides consulting on business growth, operations improvement and access to capital, including help with SBA loan applications and business planning, plus training such as a free Access to Capital workshop (other courses carry a fee). Consulting is by appointment only – request assistance at georgiasbdc.org/request-for-assistance. 2530 Sever Road, Suite 202, Lawrenceville, GA 30043; (678) 985-6820; gwinnett@georgiasbdc.org.
Amount: consulting by appointment; some workshops free, others fee-based
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and prospective owners served by the UGA SBDC Gwinnett office (Lawrenceville). By appointment only; no walk-ins.

Name: Montana SBDC – Billings (Big Sky Economic Development)
Description: The Montana Small Business Development Center provides free, confidential one-on-one business advising – from market research and financial projections to loan packaging – plus educational workshops. The Billings center is at 201 N. Broadway Ave., Billings, MT 59101: (406) 869-8404, lorene@bigskyeda.org. Request an advisor at mtsbdc.ecenterdirect.com/signup?centerid=3.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; for small businesses and prospective owners in the Billings / Yellowstone County region. Hosted by Big Sky Economic Development. Regional Director Lorene Hintz.

Name: Central Oklahoma Workforce Innovation Board – Incumbent Worker Training Grant
Description: The Central Oklahoma Workforce Innovation Board (COWIB) awards up to $10,000 to established employers to pay for job-specific occupational skills training for their existing employees (soft-skills and general orientation training are not covered). The employer must not have relocated in the past 120 days and must raise each trainee’s wages by at least 5% after the training is completed. Trainees must have been with the employer for 6+ months, earn under $54,080 a year, and live in COWIB’s service area, which includes Canadian, Cleveland, Hughes, Lincoln, Logan, Okfuskee, Oklahoma, Pottawatomie and Seminole counties. Download the application from the COWIB page; questions to cowib@cowib.org or (405) 622-2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Established employer, not relocated in the past 120 days; trainees with 6+ months tenure, under $54,080 annual income, living in Canadian, Cleveland, Hughes, Lincoln, Logan, Okfuskee, Oklahoma, Pottawatomie or Seminole county; trainee wages must rise 5%+ after training. Religious and political organizations ineligible.

Name: TEDC Creative Capital – Microloan
Description: TEDC Creative Capital is an Oklahoma CDFI and SBA lender. Its Microloan provides up to $50,000 (average about $12,000) statewide for most business purposes, at a fixed rate tied to the Prime Rate, with terms up to 6 years; collateral is considered. There is a $35 application fee per owner, plus packaging and closing fees that vary by loan type. (918) 585-8332.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Oklahoma small businesses statewide. No published credit-score minimum; collateral considered.

Name: REI Oklahoma – SBA Microloan
Description: REI Oklahoma is a statewide nonprofit lender with offices in Durant and Oklahoma City (318 NW 13th Street). Its SBA Microloan provides up to $50,000 for equipment or tools, inventory or materials, working capital, hiring and onboarding employees, and operating costs; a typical structure is 90% loan and 10% borrower equity. Rates, terms and credit requirements are set per application. Apply through the online form or call (800) 658-2823.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Oklahoma startups and expanding small businesses. No published credit-score or time-in-business minimum; typical 10% borrower equity.

Name: Central Oklahoma Workforce Innovation Board – On-the-Job Training and hiring services
Description: COWIB, the federally funded workforce board serving central Oklahoma including Canadian County, offers employers On-the-Job Training contracts with up to 50% wage reimbursement for up to 6 months, paid Work Experience internships with 100% of wages and workers’ compensation covered, free job postings on EmployOklahoma.gov, in-person hiring events, and weekly “Hot Jobs” listings shared with 50+ partner organizations. All services are free to employers. cowib@cowib.org, (405) 622-2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Employers in COWIB's central Oklahoma service area (includes Canadian, Cleveland, Logan, Oklahoma, Pottawatomie and Seminole counties). Free.

Name: Business Impact NW Small Business Loans
Description: Business Impact NW is a nonprofit community lender serving Washington, Oregon, Idaho and Alaska, including rural areas and businesses with limited collateral. Small business loans run $5,000 to $750,000 (commercial real estate up to $1.5M), with average rates of 11%-13%. Businesses operating 0-2 years submit a business plan, financial projections, a personal financial statement and collateral, and put in 10-20% of the loan amount as an equity injection; businesses operating 2+ years submit two years of tax returns and current financials. Applicants hear back within 7-10 business days, followed by 4-6 weeks of underwriting. Apply at businessimpactnw.org/loan/apply/ or call 206-324-4330 (Washington).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit small businesses in WA, OR, ID and AK, start-ups included. New businesses (0-2 yrs): business plan, projections, personal financial statement, collateral, 10-20% equity injection. Credit minimum not stated on the current site (the 2022 Impact Loan flyer listed 600+).

Name: Whatcom SBDC at Western Washington University – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Whatcom Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising from Certified Business Advisors to Whatcom County business owners and entrepreneurs, covering marketing, HR, management, finance, market research, business planning and forecasting. Sign up as a new client at wsbdc.ecenterdirect.com/signup?centerid=265, call (360) 650-7232 (Español: (360) 650-7940), or email SBDC@wwu.edu.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Whatcom County, WA business owners and entrepreneurs, including start-ups. No cost.

Name: FORGE Community Loan Fund – SBA Microloans (Arkansas)
Description: FORGE is a nonprofit community loan fund serving all 75 Arkansas counties (plus select counties in Oklahoma, Missouri and Louisiana). Its SBA microloans go up to $50,000 with terms up to 6 years for start-ups, newly established and growing small businesses; it also offers a General Credit Fund, USDA Rural Development loans (up to $250,000 or 75% of project cost in eligible rural areas) and EDA loans (up to $150,000). Credit history is reviewed but no minimum score is published. A one-time $35 membership fee applies if approved. Apply by contacting (479) 738-1585 or forge@forgefund.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- All 75 Arkansas counties; select OK, MO and LA counties
- SBA microloans: start-ups, newly established and growing small businesses
- No published minimum credit score
- $35 one-time membership fee if approved

Name: Arkansas Small Business and Technology Development Center (ASBTDC)
Description: ASBTDC provides one-to-one confidential consulting and market research at no charge, plus low-cost workshops, covering business plans and start-up, financial analysis and budgeting, financing and loan preparation, and marketing. Centers operate in Little Rock, Fayetteville, Fort Smith, Jonesboro (Arkansas State University, serving northeast Arkansas: 870-972-3517, asu@asbtdc.org), Magnolia, Russellville and West Memphis. State office: 800-862-2040.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any Arkansas small business or aspiring entrepreneur; consulting is free.

Name: Communities Unlimited Arkansas Small Business Loans
Description: Communities Unlimited is a nonprofit CDFI lending to small businesses across Arkansas, from $1,000 to $200,000 with rates and repayment terms set case by case. There is no minimum credit score: the lender looks at what the business does, what it earns or expects to earn, what the owner has put in, and whether the plan holds up. Start-ups are eligible, including businesses that have not yet generated revenue. Loans cover start-up costs, working capital, equipment, inventory, expansion, building or business purchases, and credit-building. Contact a loan officer at (479) 443-2700 or candance.brooks@communitiesu.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Arkansas businesses statewide
- No minimum credit score
- Start-ups eligible, including pre-revenue businesses (assessed on the plan)

Name: Birmingham Business Resource Center (BBRC)
Description: The Birmingham Business Resource Center describes itself as a one-stop shop for small business finance and growth, offering one-on-one counseling, workshops, business plan reviews, loan pre-qualification preparation, connections to recommended financial institutions, and access to SBA loans through its sister organization. It focuses on small businesses seeking loans under $100,000 to launch or expand. 1500 1st Ave N, Unit 12, Birmingham, AL 35203; (205) 250-6380 (Monday–Friday); info@bbrc.biz.
Amount: free counseling and loan preparation (loan terms set per applicant)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Birmingham-area small businesses and entrepreneurs seeking to launch or expand, particularly those looking for loans under $100,000. Specific loan amounts, rates and credit/time-in-business minimums are not published — call (205) 250-6380.

Name: Greater Birmingham Small Business Development Center (at Innovation Depot)
Description: The Greater Birmingham SBDC, hosted by The University of Alabama and based at Innovation Depot (1500 1st Ave North, Birmingham, AL 35203), provides one-on-one, confidential, no-cost advising to entrepreneurs and existing small businesses in Jefferson and Shelby counties, covering business planning, access to capital, procurement, and international trade. Appointments are strongly encouraged: register through the online client registration form at asbdc.ecenterdirect.com or call 877-825-7232 or (205) 348-1582.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free and open to entrepreneurs (including pre-launch) and existing small businesses in Jefferson and Shelby counties, Alabama. Register at asbdc.ecenterdirect.com or call 877-825-7232.

Name: WyoMicro Small Business Loans
Description: WyoMicro is a Wyoming-based microlender, lending since 1999, that makes small business loans of $500 to $50,000 statewide at fixed rates of 6.50%–9.50% APR, with fixed monthly payments and terms up to 6 years (closing fees apply). Loans can fund startup costs, expansion, working capital, equipment, inventory or operating expenses, and WyoMicro evaluates the whole applicant rather than credit score alone. The process is a short intake form, a business plan, a conversation with their team about financing needs, then a guided application; borrowers receive lifetime access to business advising and professional consultations. 307-460-3943, info@wyomicro.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Wyoming small businesses, startups and expanding businesses. No published credit-score or time-in-business minimum; business plan required. Fixed 6.50%–9.50% APR, up to 6-year terms, closing fees apply.
Application Fee: None (closing fees apply at loan close)

Name: Wyoming SBDC Network – free business advising
Description: The Wyoming Small Business Development Center Network provides no-cost, confidential business advising and training for Wyoming small businesses, covering starting a business, growing a business, market research, government contracting, cybersecurity, innovation funding and its Manufacturing and Onshoring Hub. Regional directors cover every county. Advising is by appointment, Monday–Friday 8am–5pm with after-hours appointments on request; select your county on the contact page to connect with your local advisor.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any Wyoming small business or entrepreneur; no cost. Northeast region (Campbell, Crook, Johnson, Sheridan, Weston counties) is led by Regional Director P.J. Burns.

Name: SCORE Columbus / Central Ohio – free business mentoring
Description: SCORE’s Columbus chapter provides free expert mentoring for the life of a business, plus workshops and webinars (some workshops cost $10–$35), to businesses in Franklin County and surrounding counties including Delaware, Fairfield, Licking, Union, Madison, Pickaway and Ross. Request a mentor by entering your ZIP code on the site or by calling (614) 664-7267; office at 65 E State Street #1350, Columbus, OH 43215.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free for small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Franklin County (Columbus) and surrounding counties including Delaware, Fairfield, Licking, Union, Madison, Pickaway and Ross. No industry, revenue or demographic requirements.

Name: Delaware County (OH) Small Business Development Center – Delaware Area Chamber of Commerce
Description: The Delaware County Small Business Development Center, run through the Delaware Area Chamber of Commerce as a public/private partnership, provides confidential one-on-one advising at no charge on business plans, strategic planning, start-up guidance, access to funding, entity selection, tax planning, marketing strategy, market research and financial analysis. Appointments are held at the Chamber office with certified business consultant Kevin Hammond – schedule by calling (740) 369-6221 or emailing dachamber@DelawareAreaChamber.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free and confidential; for small businesses and prospective owners in Delaware County, Ohio (a Marysville location also serves the Union County area at (937) 642-6279). Book by phone at (740) 369-6221.

Name: ECDI (Economic & Community Development Institute) – Ohio small business loans
Description: ECDI is a Columbus-based CDFI and SBA microlender making loans to Ohio for-profit small businesses: up to $30,000 for start-ups and up to $50,000 for businesses operating 1+ years (average loan size $21,000), with repayment up to 120 months, rates comparable to market and SBA averages, closing costs of no more than 5% and a $25 application fee per applicant. The process is a loan inquiry, a virtual orientation (recommended), a business plan, a full application with documentation, and collateral/equity requirements. Start a loan inquiry at tfaforms.com/4961276 or call 1-888-210-3039.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit businesses in Ohio. ECDI's loans page publishes no minimum credit score or revenue; a partner-published ECDI guide (havencollective.works) recommends a personal credit score of 590+. Collateral/equity and a business plan are required. Lender content — Free User reports only, never Subscribers.

Name: Access CDFI – Nevada Business Expansion Loan Fund
Description: Las Vegas-based Access CDFI (Access Community Capital) offers the Nevada Business Expansion Loan Fund in partnership with the Nevada Governor’s Office of Economic Development: loans of $1,000 to $250,000 at interest rates generally between 5% and 8%, 12–72 month terms, and an average 3% origination fee, for small businesses and start-up companies located within or expanding to the State of Nevada. Access CDFI does not publish a minimum credit score or time-in-business requirement. Apply online at application.accesscdfi.com or call 1-855-758-2334 (info@accesscdfi.org; 9205 W. Russell Road, Bldg 3, Las Vegas, NV 89148).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and start-up companies located within or expanding to the State of Nevada. No published minimum credit score or time-in-business requirement. Average 3% origination fee.
Application Fee: None (average 3% origination fee on funded loans)

Name: ProsperUs Detroit Microloan
Description: ProsperUs Detroit, a certified CDFI, makes relationship-based small business loans of up to $50,000 to for-profit businesses located in Detroit, Hamtramck, Highland Park, Inkster or Wayne County. Borrowers must be registered with Michigan LARA, have an EIN, an active bookkeeping system, and a profit/loss statement or business plan; some business traction is preferred. Fees: $50 application fee, $250–$630 closing fee (can be built into the loan), and $15 UCC lien filing fees. Allow about 3 months from application to approval. Apply at prosperusdetroit.org/apply-lending or call 313-586-0655.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- For-profit business located in Detroit, Hamtramck, Highland Park, Inkster or Wayne County
- Registered with Michigan LARA; EIN required
- Active bookkeeping system and a profit/loss statement or business plan
- Some business traction preferred
- Rates and terms not published on the lending page

Name: Massachusetts SBDC – Central Regional Office (Clark University, Worcester)
Description: The Massachusetts Small Business Development Center Network’s Central Regional Office, hosted by Clark University in Worcester, provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one business advising, technical assistance and training programs for prospective and existing for-profit businesses. Request an advisor through the MSBDC client portal at clients.msbdc.org. 125 Woodland Street, Worcester, MA 01610; (508) 793-7615, sbdc@clarku.edu.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Prospective and existing for-profit businesses in Massachusetts. Services are complimentary; register at clients.msbdc.org to request an advisor.

Name: Pathway Lending – Small Business Loans (Tennessee CDFI)
Description: Pathway Lending is a Tennessee CDFI that funds established small businesses, with offices in Knoxville, Nashville, Chattanooga and Memphis. Loans start at $10,000. It sets no fixed minimum credit score – its loan clients typically have a score above 600 – and weighs cash flow, collateral and the owner’s experience alongside credit. Rates and terms are set per application. Knoxville office: 4 Market Square, Suite 233, (865) 888-7901; Nashville (615) 425-7171; Chattanooga (423) 205-3450; Memphis (901) 560-4737.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Established Tennessee small businesses. No fixed minimum credit score; loan clients typically above 600. Lender content – for Free User Loans sections only.

Name: Tennessee SBDC – Knoxville Office
Description: The Tennessee Small Business Development Center provides free one-on-one business consulting and training, including business plan development, financial planning, marketing, and government contracting guidance. The Knoxville office is at 9721 Sherrill Blvd, Suite 123, Knoxville, TN 37932, open Monday–Friday 8:00am–4:30pm; meetings are by appointment – call (865) 246-2663.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Knoxville area; meetings by appointment.

Name: CDFI Friendly Evansville Region – CDFI loan referral
Description: CDFI Friendly Evansville Region does not make loans itself; it connects businesses in the Evansville region with community development financial institutions (CDFIs) – U.S. Treasury-certified lenders that serve borrowers traditional banks often do not. Submit the CDFI Referral Inquiry form and the team introduces you to one or more CDFIs, which set their own loan sizes, rates and credit criteria. The site also lists technical assistance resources for small businesses. Contact: info@cdfifriendlyevansville.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses, cooperatives, nonprofits, developers and individuals in the Evansville, Indiana region. Referral only – loan sizes, rates and credit requirements are set by each CDFI after introduction. Referral form: https://forms.zohopublic.com/cdfifriendlyevansvilleregion14/form/CFERCDFIReferralInquiryForm/formperma/Uj3dxee7RNvPi8HysLV3BNKVu19DS3lw0T6RSt5bRZU

Name: Southwest Indiana SBDC – free business advising (Evansville)
Description: The Southwest Indiana Small Business Development Center, hosted by the Evansville Regional Economic Partnership, provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one business advising and low-cost training on business planning, financial projections, start-ups, market research, marketing, financing, and succession planning. E-REP membership is not required. Innovation Pointe, 318 Main Street, Suite 400, Evansville, IN 47708; 812-423-2020, info@evvregion.com. Request an advisor at isbdc.ecenterdirect.com/signup.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; open to small businesses and start-ups in the Southwest Indiana region. No E-REP membership required.

Name: Tech Futures Group – Sacramento Valley SBDC (free advising for tech startups)
Description: Tech Futures Group is the technology-startup program of the Sacramento Valley SBDC network. It provides free one-on-one mentoring with Entrepreneurs-in-Residence plus specialist advising on intellectual property, fundraising, financial planning and access to federal grants – “no-cost, no-equity, no-strings.” Since 2012 it has advised 538+ tech startups and facilitated $194 million in capital funding. Apply at techfuturesgroup.org/tfgapplication or call (916) 655-2100; 1792 Tribute Rd, Suite 455, Sacramento, CA 95815.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Technology startups based in Northern California (Sacramento Valley SBDC service area). Free; no equity.

Name: AWS Activate Credits
Description: AWS Activate gives self-funded startups up to $5,000 in AWS credits through the Activate Founders tier (starting at $1,000, with potential for additional awards), and startups backed by an accelerator, angel investor or VC firm in the Activate Provider network up to $200,000 through the Portfolio tier. Eligible companies are pre-Series B, founded in the last 10 years, and have an AWS account on a paid tier plan. Apply with an AWS Builder ID using a professional email; responses typically arrive within 5–10 business days.
Amount: up to $5,000 in credits (Founders); up to $200,000 (Portfolio)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Pre-Series B startups founded in the last 10 years with an AWS account on a paid tier plan; Portfolio tier requires an Organization ID from an Activate Provider.

Name: Google for Startups Cloud Program
Description: The Google for Startups Cloud Program gives pre-funded (bootstrapped) startups $2,000 in Google Cloud credits to build and iterate on an MVP, and seed-to-Series A startups up to $200,000 in credits – up to $350,000 for AI-first startups. Credits cover Google Cloud’s AI stack, including Gemini models, AI agents, TPUs/GPUs, BigQuery and Google Workspace, with pay-as-you-go pricing and no lock-in. Apply for the tier that matches your funding stage at cloud.google.com/startup.
Amount: $2,000 in credits (pre-funded); up to $200,000 ($350,000 AI-first) for seed–Series A
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Startups; tier set by funding stage (pre-funded/bootstrapped; seed to Series A; Series B+).

Name: NC Small Business and Technology Development Center (SBTDC)
Description: The SBTDC is North Carolina’s statewide small business and technology development center, providing expert, no-cost guidance from experienced counselors to businesses at every stage, including pre-revenue start-ups. Services cover starting a business, access to capital and financing, marketing and research, strategy and financial performance, government contracting, technology commercialization and international business. Request counseling at sbtdc.org/become-a-client; office locations are listed at sbtdc.org/locations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: North Carolina businesses at any stage, including pre-revenue start-ups. No cost.

Name: Solano-Napa SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The Solano-Napa Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising on business growth, finance, loans and funding, human resources and marketing, plus workshops, training programs and startup support, with services available in Spanish. It serves Solano and Napa Counties from 500 Chadbourne Road, Fairfield, CA 94534. Request an advisor at solanonapasbdc.org/join, call (707) 646-1071, or email info@solanonapasbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and startups in Solano and Napa Counties, California. Advising is no-cost and confidential.

Name: Pennsylvania Charitable Organization Registration (Form BCO-10)
Description: Charitable organizations that solicit contributions in Pennsylvania register with the Department of State’s Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations by filing Form BCO-10, unless excluded or exempted under the Act. The annual fee is $15 for organizations receiving $25,000 or less in contributions, rising to $100 ($25,001 to under $100,000), $150 ($100,000 to under $500,000) and $250 (over $500,000). The form and attachments are submitted by mail using the fillable PDF on the Department’s charities page. (717) 783-1720 or 1-800-732-0999 (within PA).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Charitable organizations soliciting contributions in PA, unless excluded or exempted. Initial registration is required before any compensated person solicits, or within 30 days of receiving more than $25,000 in gross contributions.

Name: Pennsylvania Association of Nonprofit Organizations (PANO) – membership
Description: PANO is Pennsylvania’s statewide association of nonprofits. Membership for organizations with budgets under $50K is $110 a year (2026 rates) and includes the “Ask PANO” service for questions on bylaws, fundraising and nonprofit management, free Standards for Excellence resource packets, online and in-person training for staff, board members and volunteers, discounted accounting and other services through its Corporate Partner Directory, and referrals to capacity-building consultants. (717) 236-8584.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Pennsylvania nonprofit organizations. Dues scale with budget; under $50K budget is $110/year (2026).

Name: Minnesota Small Business Development Center – Twin Cities SBDC
Description: Minnesota’s SBDC network provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one business consulting and training through nine regional centers; the Twin Cities SBDC serves Minneapolis and Hennepin County. Find the center and request an advisor through the DEED SBDC locator at mn.gov/deed/business/help/sbdc.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Minnesota small businesses; Twin Cities SBDC covers Minneapolis/Hennepin County.

Name: MN PROMISE Act Grants – Round 2 (Minneapolis & Saint Paul)
Description: The State of Minnesota’s PROMISE Act grant program, administered in Minneapolis and Saint Paul by the Neighborhood Development Center, funds for-profit small businesses located in eligible areas of the two cities with gross annual revenue of $750,000 or less in the most recently completed tax year; businesses that received a Round 1 grant are not eligible. Funds can be used for working capital, payroll, rent or mortgage payments, utilities, equipment and other operating costs. Home-based and online businesses qualify if they have claimed the IRS home-office deduction (Section 280A(c)(1)). Check the address against the eligibility map at mnpromiseact.org/eligibility, then apply online with your Minnesota Secretary of State registration and most recent tax return (or filed extension). The full process takes at least 12 weeks, and grantees must keep operating for 12 months after the award. Application help: (651) 379-8102.
Amount: set per business (about $50 million available at the start of Round 2)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- For-profit small businesses (and qualifying nonprofits) in eligible areas of Minneapolis and Saint Paul — check address on the map at mnpromiseact.org/eligibility
- Gross annual revenue $750,000 or less in most recent tax year
- Not a Round 1 grantee
- Home-based/online businesses must have claimed the IRS Section 280A(c)(1) home-office deduction
- Documents: MN Secretary of State registration, most recent tax return or IRS Form 7004 extension
- Must maintain operations 12 months after award; process takes 12+ weeks

Name: Northside Economic Opportunity Network (NEON) – North Minneapolis
Description: NEON supports low-to-moderate income entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis and surrounding communities with trainings and workshops, business development help (feasibility assessments, business model evaluation and growth planning), business loans for established businesses including commercial real estate financing, access to external grant programs, industry-specific business incubator programs, and NEON Spaces coworking. 1007 West Broadway Ave. N., Minneapolis, MN 55411; 612-302-1505, info@neon-mn.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Low-to-moderate income grassroots entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis and surrounding communities.

Name: Elevate Hennepin – free business advising for Hennepin County
Description: Hennepin County’s Elevate Hennepin connects Hennepin County business owners to advisors, services and resources at no cost: one-on-one Navigators who identify the best resources for a business’s needs, consultations with vetted advisors, cohort programs (CEO Start, CEO Now), workshops on topics such as cash flow management and business protection, and weekly 1 Million Cups networking events. Request help through “Schedule a consultation” on the website.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Hennepin County business owners; services at no cost.

Name: Justine PETERSEN – Small Business Loans (St. Louis CDFI)
Description: St. Louis-based CDFI and SBA microlender. SBA Micro-Enterprise Loan: $500–$150,000 at 7.25%–11%, up to 72 months, 3% closing fee. CDFI Micro-Loan: up to $50,000 at 12%–20%, 6% closing fee. SBA-guaranteed Community Advantage Loan: up to $150,000 at Prime + 6%, 10-year term, 10% equity injection for startups. Loans require 100% collateral, with up to $3,000 available unsecured on the Micro-Enterprise Loan. A USDA Micro-Enterprise Loan (up to $150,000 at 9.5%) is available in rural Missouri only. Apply through the online Loan Service Request form or call (314) 533-2411; 1023 N. Grand Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63106.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and startups primarily in the St. Louis area; USDA product limited to rural Missouri addresses. 100% collateral required. No published minimum credit score or time in business. Non-partner lender — list without endorsement language.

Name: Missouri SBDC – St. Louis Metro (free one-on-one business advising)
Description: The Missouri Small Business Development Center provides free, confidential one-on-one advising on business plans, financial projections, pricing, loan packaging, market research and growth planning, plus workshops and training. St. Louis County is served through the MU Extension St. Louis Metro Area Office, 8225 Florissant Rd, St. Louis, MO 63121; 314-200-2705.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; open to entrepreneurs and small business owners in St. Louis County. Call ahead before visiting the office.

Name: Ohio SBDC at Terra State Community College – free business advising (Erie, Ottawa, Sandusky and Seneca Counties)
Description: The Ohio Small Business Development Center at Terra State Community College in Fremont provides free, confidential one-to-one advising and entrepreneurial training programs to prospective and existing small business owners in Erie, Ottawa, Sandusky and Seneca Counties (fees may apply to some workshops or seminars). Contact director Bill Auxter at (419) 559-2210 or bauxter@terra.edu; office at 2830 Napoleon Rd., Fremont, OH 43420.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free for prospective and existing small business owners in Erie, Ottawa, Sandusky and Seneca Counties, Ohio. No industry, revenue or demographic requirements stated. Some workshops or seminars may carry a fee.

Name: Justine PETERSEN – SBA Microloans and Community Advantage loans (St. Louis CDFI)
Description: Justine PETERSEN is a St. Louis-based CDFI and SBA microlender. Its SBA Micro-Enterprise Loan goes up to $50,000 (average under $10,000) at 7.25–11% with terms up to 72 months and a 3% closing fee; 100% collateral is required, with up to $3,000 available unsecured. Its SBA-guaranteed Community Advantage loan goes up to $150,000 at Prime + 6% (adjusted quarterly) on a 10-year term with a $2,500 packaging fee; start-ups need a 10% equity injection. A CDFI Micro-Loan (up to $50,000, 12–20%) and a 6% Able Biz loan for business owners with disabilities are also offered. Apply through the online Loan Service Request form or call 314-533-2411.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Start-ups and existing small businesses; collateral required on most products; Community Advantage start-ups need a 10% equity injection. USDA microloans are for rural Missouri only.

Name: Missouri SBDC in the St. Louis Region – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Missouri Small Business Development Center’s St. Louis Region office provides free, confidential advising for start-ups and existing businesses, plus training, for Jefferson, Lincoln, St. Charles, St. Louis and Warren counties and the City of St. Louis. 911 Washington Ave., Suite 815 (Lammert Building), St. Louis, MO 63101; 314-241-1005. Sign up for services through the online portal or the contact form on the center’s page.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Start-ups and existing small businesses in Jefferson, Lincoln, St. Charles, St. Louis and Warren counties and the City of St. Louis, MO. No cost.

Name: North Metro Denver SBDC - Free One-on-One Business Advising
Description: The North Metro Denver Small Business Development Center, hosted by Front Range Community College, provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one business advising plus training and workshops at minimal or no charge, covering business planning, financial management and marketing strategy. It serves Adams and Broomfield counties, and services are open to any small business eligible to receive federally funded services. Request an advising session at sbdc.colorado.gov/colorado-sbdc-login. 303-460-1032, northmetro.sbdc@frontrange.edu.
Amount: no-cost advising; training and workshops at minimal or no charge
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any small business eligible to receive federally funded services. The North Metro center serves Adams and Broomfield counties; other Colorado SBDC centers cover the rest of the state.

Name: City of Westminster Job Training Incentive Grant (Colorado)
Description: The City of Westminster reimburses 50% of employee training costs, up to $5,000, for businesses in manufacturing, technology and innovation, financial services, aerospace and defense, and business support services. Retail and restaurant businesses are not eligible. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis using the fillable application form (English and Spanish) on the city's Grants & Financial Resources page. Westminster Economic Development: 303-658-2108, ecodevo@westminsterco.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business located in the City of Westminster, Colorado, in one of the eligible sectors: manufacturing, technology and innovation, financial services, aerospace and defense, or business support services. Retail and restaurant businesses are excluded. Reimbursement basis. Rolling applications via the fillable PDF on the city's Grants & Financial Resources page.

Name: City of Westminster Small Business Scholarship (Colorado)
Description: The City of Westminster reimburses 50% of tuition, fees and course materials for continuing education, up to $1,000 per business each year. It is open to licensed Westminster entrepreneurs and business owners with 50 or fewer employees. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis using the fillable application form (English and Spanish) on the city's Grants & Financial Resources page. Westminster Economic Development: 303-658-2108, ecodevo@westminsterco.gov.
Amount: 50% of tuition, fees and materials, up to $1,000 per business per year
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Licensed City of Westminster, Colorado entrepreneurs and business owners with 50 or fewer employees. Reimbursement basis, capped at $1,000 per business per year. Rolling applications via the fillable PDF on the city's Grants & Financial Resources page.

Name: Arizona Loan Guarantee Program (AZLGP / SSBCI)
Description: The Arizona Commerce Authority's SSBCI-funded loan guarantee program backs loans to Arizona small businesses that do not qualify for traditional financing because of shortfalls in cash flow, credit history, credit score or collateral. Eligible uses include start-up costs, working capital, equipment, inventory, asset purchases and business property improvements (passive real estate is excluded). Businesses must be Arizona-based with no more than 750 employees; certain business types are excluded. Loan sizes vary by lender, roughly $1,000 to $2 million. There is no application to the ACA — apply through one of the participating lenders, which include DreamSpring, Border Financial Resources, Desert Financial Credit Union, Clearinghouse CDFI, Community Investment Corporation, Groundswell Capital, Growth Partners Arizona, Prestamos CDFI, Vantage West Credit Union and WaFd Bank.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Arizona-based businesses with no more than 750 employees; certain business types excluded. Apply through a participating lender rather than the Arizona Commerce Authority.

Name: Maricopa SBDC – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Maricopa Small Business Development Center, part of the Arizona SBDC Network, provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising to small businesses across Maricopa County, together with workshops and training. Advising is available by Zoom, by phone or in person, with centers throughout the county and a main office at GateWay Community College, 108 N. 40th Street, South Building, Phoenix, AZ 85034. Request an advisor at clients.azsbdc.net/reg.aspx?mode=counsel&center=93010&subloc=0 or call 480-784-0590.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to small businesses and prospective business owners located in Maricopa County, Arizona. No fee, no revenue or industry requirement.

Name: Growth Partners Arizona – small business loans
Description: Growth Partners Arizona is a Phoenix-based CDFI lending to Arizona small businesses and pairing its loans with coaching. Microloans and the Arizona Microenterprise Loan Program run $15,000-$50,000 at 9.25% with a 2-3% admin fee and terms up to five years; Growth Loans run $51,000-$150,000 at 9.25% with a 3% admin fee. There is no prepayment penalty on any product. Microloans and the Microenterprise program require at least one year in business; Growth Loans require two years of tax history and annual revenues of $50,000 or more. Funds can be used for growth and expansion, equipment, long-term working capital and, for Growth Loans, tenant improvements, property renovations and debt consolidation. The Microenterprise program serves Mohave, La Paz, Yavapai, Coconino and Maricopa Counties. Offices in Phoenix, Flagstaff and Tucson; headquarters at 2828 N. Central Ave Suite 1011, Phoenix, AZ 85004.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Arizona-based businesses. Microloans and Arizona Microenterprise Loan Program: at least 1 year in business, generating revenue; Microenterprise is limited to Mohave, La Paz, Yavapai, Coconino and Maricopa Counties. Growth Loans: at least 2 years of tax history and $50,000+ annual revenue. Apply at form.typeform.com/to/TOfeqkic (microloans/growth) or growthpartnersaz.nedhelps.com/?flow=inquiry (microenterprise).

Name: Working Solutions CDFI – California Small Business Loans
Description: Working Solutions is a statewide California CDFI making small business loans of $5,000 to $100,000 at a fixed 11% interest rate over a 3-year or 5-year term, with no collateral required and a $50 application fee. There is no minimum revenue and no minimum credit score. The business must be located in California or planning to relocate there, and at least one owner with a 20% or greater stake must live in California and have a year or more of demonstrated same-industry experience; startups are eligible if that owner has a secondary income source. All owners with a 20%+ stake must be 18 or older with a valid SSN or ITIN, with no past due accounts, active tax liens or civil judgments, and no active or recently discharged bankruptcy within the last 12 months. Nonprofits, cannabis, passive real estate, gambling, lending and banking, and adult services are ineligible; smoke shops, liquor stores and firearms businesses need additional review. Apply at workingsolutions.org or call (415) 780-1217.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: California-based small businesses, including startups. No minimum revenue or credit score. At least one owner with a 20%+ stake must reside in California and have 1+ year of same-industry experience; startups must show a secondary income source. $50 application fee.

Name: HOPE Credit Union – Small Business Loans
Description: HOPE Credit Union is a member-owned community development financial institution that has served businesses and entrepreneurs in the Deep South since 1994. Small business loans go up to $250,000 and cover unsecured business loans, equipment loans, vehicle loans, share-secured loans and commercial real estate purchase or refinance. Membership and credit approval are required. Minimum credit score, time in business and revenue are not published, so call to confirm current terms. Phone: 1-877-214-HOPE (4673).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Business located in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi or Tennessee
- Credit union membership required
- Subject to credit approval
- Minimum credit score, time in business and revenue not published

Name: State of Mississippi MAGIC Supplier Self-Registration
Description: Businesses that want to sell to Mississippi state agencies register in MAGIC, the state's supplier system, through the Supplier Self-Registration portal at sus.magic.ms.gov. Registered suppliers can be found by state buyers and can respond to state solicitations. A paper Supplier Registration Form can be submitted directly to an individual state agency instead of using the portal. The MMRS Call Center handles registration questions and duplicate-record errors at (601) 359-1343, Option 2.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to any business wishing to sell goods or services to Mississippi state agencies. Register online at sus.magic.ms.gov or submit a paper Supplier Registration Form to the agency you want to work with.

Name: SCORE – Free Small Business Mentoring
Description: SCORE offers free mentoring for the life of the business to any aspiring or established owner of a U.S.-based business. Mentors are current and former entrepreneurs and industry specialists who volunteer, covering sales, marketing, finance, accounting, operations and technology, with sessions held virtually or in person. Submit a request by entering your ZIP code at score.org or browse mentor profiles directly; mentors typically respond within 48 hours. Phone: 1-800-634-0245.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to any aspiring or established owner of a U.S.-based business. Free, with no revenue, industry or demographic requirements.

Name: Mississippi SBDC Network – Free One-on-One Business Counseling
Description: The Mississippi Small Business Development Center Network provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one counseling with business counselors, plus workshops, across three tracks: Start (business planning, feasibility studies, legal structure, financial projections, start-up workshops), Grow (digital marketing training, market research access, business resiliency planning) and Scale (financial analysis, digital transformation, market research, international trade, cybersecurity through the RISE Center). Request counseling at clients.mississippisbdc.org, call 1-800-725-7232, or email info@mississippisbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to Mississippi small businesses and aspiring entrepreneurs. No cost. Request counseling online or by phone.

Name: Communities Unlimited – Small Business Loans
Description: Communities Unlimited is a CDFI lending to small businesses across seven Southern states. Loans run from $1,000 to $200,000 and are underwritten in house. Start-ups are eligible but must have an alternative source of income. Collateral and a personal guaranty are required, and the application asks for a personal financial statement, two years of personal tax documents and business financial projections (application forms are available in English and Spanish). Phone: (479) 443-2700; Economic Development Loan Officer Candence Brooks, (479) 595-5053.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Business located in AL, AR, LA, MS, OK, TN or TX
- Start-ups permitted with an alternative source of income
- Collateral and personal guaranty required
- Personal financial statement, two years of personal tax documents, and business financial projections may be required

Name: Ohio SBDC at the Summit Medina Business Alliance (Akron) – free business advising
Description: The Ohio Small Business Development Center at the Summit Medina Business Alliance serves Summit, Portage and Medina counties with no-cost one-on-one advising from Certified Business Advisors, plus training seminars covering business basics, business plan writing and financial management. Office at 526 S. Main St., Ste. 601, Akron, OH 44311; (330) 375-2111. Request an advisor through the “Request Business Advising” link on akronsbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free for small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Summit, Portage and Medina counties (Akron metro). No industry, revenue or demographic requirements.

Name: HFLA of Northeast Ohio – interest-free business loan
Description: HFLA of Northeast Ohio makes interest-free business loans of up to $20,000 at 0%, with no prepayment penalties or fees, to small businesses and start-ups that need capital to meet demand and grow. Applicants must live and do business in Cuyahoga, Lake, Lorain, Geauga, Medina, Portage or Summit county, have enough income to make the monthly payments, and lack the ability to obtain the needed funds from a conventional lender such as a bank or credit union. Applications go to HFLA’s Business Loan Committee with business and personal financial documentation; business debt consolidation is not funded. Apply online at application.interestfree.org/start.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Live and do business in one of the seven HFLA counties: Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Medina, Portage, Summit. No published minimum credit score. Must show income sufficient to repay and inability to obtain conventional financing. No religious requirement. Lender content – Free User reports only, never Subscribers.

Name: The Audacious Project
Description: TED's collaborative philanthropy initiative, which pools commitments from a donor community to fund a small annual cohort of roughly 8-10 organizations pursuing unusually large-scale social change. Funding requests are uncapped and awards have historically run into the tens of millions per project — the donor community committed $1.03 billion to the most recent 13-organization cohort, and $4.6 billion to 70 projects over eight years. Applicants enter through a short idea survey; only invited candidates advance through vetting, proposal co-development with the Audacious team, and a public launch at a TED Conference.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY — individuals aged 18+ may apply on behalf of a nonprofit, NGO, institution, or collaboration. For-profit companies are outside the stated applicant types. HARD THRESHOLD: minimum annual operating budget of at least $2 million — the most common disqualifier. Global, no country restriction. All issue areas considered; the screen is the ambition and scale of the idea, not the sector. As of June 15, 2025 there is no submission deadline — idea submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis. Four phases: idea survey, invitation and vetting, proposal co-development with the Audacious team, then funding and public launch via TED Talks. No application fee.

Name: West Central Minnesota SBDC – free one-on-one business consulting
Description: The West Central Minnesota Small Business Development Center, hosted by M State, provides free one-on-one consulting on business plans, financial projections, marketing strategy, operations and bookkeeping, plus workshops and cohorts, for businesses in Becker, Clay, Douglas, Grant, Otter Tail, Pope, Stevens, Traverse and Wilkin counties. Request a consultant at mnsbdc.ecenterdirect.com, call (218) 299-6605, or email SBDC@Minnesota.edu.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses in Becker, Clay, Douglas, Grant, Otter Tail, Pope, Stevens, Traverse and Wilkin counties, MN. One-on-one consulting is free; occasional workshop fees.

Name: Stevens County Economic Improvement Commission – City of Morris Micro Loan
Description: The Stevens County Economic Improvement Commission (SCEIC) offers micro loans of under $5,000 to businesses in the City of Morris, MN, for starting a business or supporting smaller operations. SCEIC also runs county-wide Gap Financing and Business Assistance loan programs and a City of Morris Storefront Renovation loan of up to $50,000. Applications are downloaded from sceic.org and returned by email, mail or in person; (320) 585-2609.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses located in the City of Morris, MN (Stevens County). Rates and terms not published.

Name: West Central Initiative – Small Enterprise Loan
Description: West Central Initiative, a regional community foundation and lender in west-central Minnesota, makes Small Enterprise loans of $1,000–$50,000 to manufacturing, service and some retail businesses in Becker, Clay, Douglas, Grant, Otter Tail, Pope, Stevens, Traverse and Wilkin counties. WCI typically requires a business plan, cash flow projections, satisfactory credit history and a personal guarantee, and usually lends alongside a bank as gap financing. Applications are downloadable from wcif.org/loans; (218) 739-2239 or (800) 735-2239, wci@wcif.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses in WCI's nine-county service area (Becker, Clay, Douglas, Grant, Otter Tail, Pope, Stevens, Traverse, Wilkin) plus portions of White Earth Nation; business plan, satisfactory credit and personal guarantee typically required; bank participation usual.

Name: Miami Valley SBDC (Dayton) – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Miami Valley Small Business Development Center, based at the Entrepreneurs’ Center (31 S. Main St, Dayton, OH 45402), provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising on business planning, cash flow and profitability, financial projections, market strategy, employee management and export readiness, plus workshops. It serves Montgomery, Champaign, Clark, Darke, Greene, Miami, Preble and Shelby counties, with appointments also held in Miamisburg and Troy. Request an advisor through the Ohio SBDC client portal (clients.ohiosbdc.ohio.gov) or call 937-210-9460.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in Montgomery, Champaign, Clark, Darke, Greene, Miami, Preble and Shelby counties, Ohio. No cost. Appointments by request through clients.ohiosbdc.ohio.gov or 937-210-9460.

Name: SCORE Greater Cincinnati and Dayton – free business mentoring
Description: SCORE’s Greater Cincinnati and Dayton chapter provides free, confidential business mentoring plus workshops (free to $125) for businesses starting, growing or scaling across Greater Cincinnati, Dayton, Northern Kentucky and Southeast Indiana. Request a mentor by entering your ZIP code on the site or by calling (513) 549-0818; office at 3700 Park 42 Drive, Suite 140A, Cincinnati, OH 45241.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Aspiring and existing businesses in Greater Cincinnati, Dayton, Northern Kentucky and Southeast Indiana. Mentoring is free; workshops range from free to $125.

Name: Salt Lake SBDC (Salt Lake Community College) – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Salt Lake Small Business Development Center, hosted by Salt Lake Community College and part of the Utah SBDC network, provides no-cost consulting, training and resources to businesses in Salt Lake and Summit counties, including start-up assistance and tax planning. Submit the Online Request for Counseling on the center's page, or call 801-957-5441. Office: 9750 South 300 West, Sandy, UT 84070.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and prospective owners in Salt Lake and Summit counties, Utah. No cost.

Name: Utah Microloan Fund
Description: Salt Lake City nonprofit lender offering loans of up to $50,000 (start-ups up to $25,000 in their first year) at fixed rates generally between 10% and 14%, repaid over up to six years, with no prepayment penalty and a $50 application fee. Borrowers must be Utah residents with a business registered in Utah, an open business checking account and no active bankruptcy in the last 12 months; collateral is not always required. Loans can fund starting, operating or growing a Utah business; MLMs and real estate or building purchases are not eligible. Process: mandatory virtual loan orientation (Tuesdays at 9am), work with an SBDC or Women's Business Center advisor, online application, then a 30-minute Zoom presentation to the loan team; loans close about a week after approval. 801-746-1180; 154 E Ford Ave, Ste A, Salt Lake City, UT 84115.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Utah resident; business registered in Utah; open business checking account; no active bankruptcy in last 12 months. Not eligible: MLMs, real estate/building purchases, out-of-state businesses.

Name: Carolina Small Business Development Fund loans (North Carolina CDFI)
Description: Statewide nonprofit community lender offering small business loans of up to $350,000 with flexible repayment terms, serving all 100 North Carolina counties and all industries (excluding “sin” businesses), for both emerging entrepreneurs and established businesses. Applicants start with a business consultation request, work with a Business Solutions Officer, and may be asked for personal and business tax returns, financial statements, a business plan and management resumes. Consultation form: forms.carolinasmallbusiness.org/4855655; phone 919-803-1437.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: North Carolina businesses in all 100 counties, emerging and established; all industries except sin businesses. No credit score, time-in-business or revenue minimum published.

Name: Johnston Community College Small Business Center (free counseling and seminars, Johnston County NC)
Description: Part of the NC Community College Small Business Center Network, the Johnston Community College Small Business Center offers free one-on-one business counseling, seminars, webinars and workshops on starting a business, business plans, marketing, funding, bookkeeping and taxes, plus information and resources. Located at 245 College Road, Smithfield, NC 27577; (919) 209-2015, jccsbc@johnstoncc.edu. Schedule counseling through ncsbc.net or by contacting the center; participants must be 18 or older.
Amount: free one-on-one counseling, seminars and workshops (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Current and aspiring business owners, 18+; serves Johnston County, NC. All services free.

Name: Mason Small Business Development Center (Fairfax County)
Description: Mason SBDC provides no-cost one-on-one business counseling and training workshops (marketing, financing, government contracting, pitch preparation and more) to small businesses in Fairfax County, Arlington, Prince William County, the Cities of Fairfax, Manassas and Alexandria, and the Town of Herndon. Request an advisor through the Virginia SBDC portal at clients.virginiasbdc.org, call (703) 261-4105 or email help@masonsbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and aspiring owners in Fairfax County, Arlington, Prince William County, the Cities of Fairfax, Manassas and Alexandria, and the Town of Herndon. Free.

Name: ECDC Enterprise Development Group (EDG) – Fairfax County Microloan Program
Description: EDG, an Arlington-based CDFI lender, runs Fairfax County's microloan program: small, short-term loans for startups and small businesses that typically cannot qualify for traditional bank financing, paired with one-on-one business coaching, financial literacy training and credit-building support. Borrowers must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or lawful permanent residents with low-to-moderate income. Apply online at edgusloanapp.org; EDG: 703-685-0510, info@edgus.org. County contact: Wendy Lemieux, 703-424-1805.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Startups and small businesses (Fairfax County program; EDG serves the metro Washington area)
- U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or lawful permanent residents
- Low-to-moderate income

Name: Virginia Small Business Financing Authority (VSBFA) – Microloan Program
Description: The Virginia Small Business Financing Authority makes direct microloans of up to $150,000 to qualifying Virginia businesses, with no bank participation required and repayment terms generally of 5–7 years. Funds can be used for equipment and fixed assets, working capital and business acquisition; construction, non-owner-occupied real estate and debt refinancing are not eligible. Applicants submit the Microloan Application and a Personal Financial Statement; a one-time, non-refundable $150 application fee applies. Contact: (804) 786-6585.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Virginia business in good standing with the State Corporation Commission
- Credit score of 650 or higher
- Annual revenue of $10M or less (last 3 years), net worth of $2M or less, or fewer than 250 employees

Name: UGA SBDC in Atlanta – free one-on-one business consulting
Description: The University of Georgia Small Business Development Center’s Atlanta office (3475 Lenox Road NE, Suite 300, Atlanta, GA 30326) serves Fulton County with consulting on business startup, access to capital and loan preparation, sales and marketing, financial performance, and growth planning. Appointments only, no walk-ins; request consulting through the online form, at 404-282-4803, or atlanta@georgiasbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and prospective owners in Fulton County. By appointment only; no walk-ins. The SBDC does not provide funding. Office opened July 1, 2026.

Name: Invest Atlanta – Atlanta Cares Revolving Loan Fund (ACRLF)
Description: Invest Atlanta’s citywide Atlanta Cares Revolving Loan Fund lends $10,000 to $100,000 at 1% to 3% to small businesses located within Atlanta city limits. There is a $100 application fee. Confirm the business address is inside city limits with the City’s property lookup (gis.atlantaga.gov/propinfo), then apply through Invest Atlanta’s online portal. Contact: smallbusinessloans@investatlanta.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses located within Atlanta city limits (citywide). $10,000–$100,000 at 1%–3%. $100 application fee. Invest Atlanta’s page does not state credit or time-in-business minimums. Apply via portal.neighborlysoftware.com/investatlanta.

Name: Ramsey County Open to Business (free business advising)
Description: Ramsey County’s Open to Business program, delivered with the Metropolitan Consortium of Community Developers (MCCD), gives current and aspiring business owners anywhere in Ramsey County free one-on-one technical assistance: business plan development, feasibility analysis, cash flow and financing projections, marketing planning, city and state licensing help, and loan packaging and other help obtaining financing. Monthly office hours are held at locations across the county, with walk-ins welcome. Ramsey County Community & Economic Development: 651-266-8010; Ramsey County business advisor Luis Mendoza (MCCD): 612-789-7337, lmendoza@mccdmn.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All current business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs intending to establish, purchase or improve a business within Ramsey County, MN. No cost. MCCD loan amounts and terms are not published on the county pages — contact the advisor.

Name: Battle Born Growth Microloan Program (Nevada SSBCI)
Description: Nevada's State Small Business Credit Initiative microloan program, run by Battle Born Growth, offers fixed-rate loans of up to $250,000 at WSJ Prime plus up to 4%, with 36–72 month terms; the rate does not change after closing. Open to Nevada small businesses with 100 or fewer full-time employees and less than $5 million in annual revenue (credit and eligibility restrictions apply); minority-owned, women-owned and rural businesses are encouraged to apply. Complete a free, no-obligation three-step online preapplication at nvmicroloans.org, get matched with a participating mission-driven lender or CDFI, then complete the full application and credit review with that lender.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nevada small businesses with 100 or fewer full-time employees and less than $5 million in annual revenue; credit and eligibility restrictions apply (no published minimum credit score or time in business). Free preapplication.

Name: Finanta – Nonprofit Financing (Southeastern & Central PA CDFI)
Description: Finanta (formerly Community First Fund) is a community development financial institution that makes loans to nonprofit community organizations to develop and support community programs, and works with nonprofits to develop commercial real estate into community assets and to support affordable rental housing. It also offers small business microloans (under $50,000) and larger small business loans. Applications are accepted from organizations in 16 Pennsylvania counties (Adams, Berks, Bucks, Chester, Cumberland, Dauphin, Delaware, Franklin, Lancaster, Lebanon, Lehigh, Montgomery, Northampton, Perry, Philadelphia and York), plus Kent, New Castle and Sussex counties in Delaware and Camden County, New Jersey. Apply online at finanta.lendwithspark.com/loan; Philadelphia office 267-236-7000, with responses within two business days.
Amount: Varies (small business microloans under $50,000; nonprofit loan amounts not published)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofit community organizations (and small businesses, via separate products) located in Adams, Berks, Bucks, Chester, Cumberland, Dauphin, Delaware, Franklin, Lancaster, Lebanon, Lehigh, Montgomery, Northampton, Perry, Philadelphia or York County PA; Kent, New Castle or Sussex County DE; or Camden County NJ. Nonprofit loan minimums and credit criteria are not published.

Name: Puerto Rico SBTDC – free business advising and training
Description: The Puerto Rico Small Business Technology Development Center, based at Inter American University of Puerto Rico in cooperation with the U.S. Small Business Administration, provides free advising and training to entrepreneurs in all sectors on business establishment, growth, innovation, export development, manufacturing and technology commercialization, with centers including San Juan and Carolina. Request an advisor through the advisory request form on the website, at 787.625.1515, or at asistenciavirtual@prsbtdc.org.
Amount: free advising and training (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; available to all legal residents and citizens of the U.S. Hato Rey office: 268 Ponce de León, The Hato Rey Center, Suite 1400, San Juan PR 00918.

Name: COFECC (Lendreams) – SBA Microloan (Puerto Rico)
Description: San Juan-based, U.S. Treasury-certified CDFI lending to Puerto Rico small businesses from $500 up to $5 million, including SBA Microloans of $500 to $50,000, SBA 504, Rural Development loans for new or established businesses, and an 80/20 recovery program (80% loan, 20% grant), plus business mentoring. Apply at lendreams.com/solicitar or call (787) 756-5080 / (787) 756-5082 (Mon–Fri, 8am–5pm; Avenida Chardón #171, Suite 407, San Juan).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Puerto Rico small businesses. Credit, time-in-business and document requirements are not published on the site; confirm by phone.

Name: PathStone Enterprise Center – Puerto Rico small business loans
Description: CDFI small business loans in Puerto Rico, mostly $15,000 to $60,000, repaid within about five years at fixed rates between 7.50% and 9.50%, for equipment, inventory, working capital, expansion, new employee pay and business establishment costs. Credit history is considered; new businesses submit a full business plan with a market study and marketing strategy, existing businesses a brief summary. $100 application fee. Call (787) 658-1640 to request an application.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Puerto Rico businesses, new or existing; credit history considered. Office: 606 Ave. Tito Castro Suite 204, Ponce PR 00716.

Name: Colmena66 – Puerto Rico entrepreneur resource network
Description: A program of the Puerto Rico Science, Technology & Research Trust that connects entrepreneurs to Puerto Rico’s business support organizations through a free resource navigator, event calendar, guides, grant information sessions (Acércate al Grant) and business acceleration initiatives such as Levanta Tu Negocio. Phone: (787) 525-4111, 8:30am–5:30pm.
Amount: free referrals and programs (no cash award)
