Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; open to entrepreneurs and businesses in Puerto Rico at any stage, from ideation through growth.

Name: Capital Region Chamber Micro Loan Programs (Albany, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Saratoga counties)
Description: The Capital Region Chamber administers three micro loan funds for early-stage and existing businesses in Albany, Rensselaer, Schenectady and Saratoga counties: the Capital Business Assistance Fund (companies unable to access traditional financing), the Capitalize Albany Fund (businesses located in or relocating to the City of Albany with employment potential) and the HUD Fund (low-to-moderate income business owners in Albany County). New businesses can borrow $1,000–$25,000 and businesses operating 2+ years up to $50,000, at WSJ Prime + 2% for up to 5 years, for fixed assets, real estate and working capital (not delinquent taxes or refinancing). Special emphasis on minority- and woman-owned companies. $100 non-refundable application fee. Start with the Borrower Inquiry Form or call 518.431.1400.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses in Albany, Rensselaer, Schenectady or Saratoga County, NY. New businesses up to $25,000; 2+ years in business up to $50,000. No published credit minimum. Startups encouraged to complete the Entrepreneur Boot Camp.

Name: Capital Region SBDC at the University at Albany – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Capital Region Small Business Development Center, hosted by the University at Albany, provides free advising, business education, funding guidance and training courses to entrepreneurs and small business owners in Albany, Columbia, Fulton, Greene, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Warren and Washington counties. Appointments are held in person at the Albany office (ETEC Building, Suite 146, Harriman Campus Road, Albany, NY 12222), at outreach centers, by video or by phone. Sign up at nysbdc.ecenterdirect.com/signup?centerid=10, call 518.442.7232 or email sbdc@albany.edu.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Free; entrepreneurs and small business owners in Albany, Columbia, Fulton, Greene, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Warren and Washington counties, NY.

Name: Amplify Albany Grant Program (Capitalize Albany)
Description: Capitalize Albany’s Amplify Albany grants fund short- and medium-term activities and events that leverage the City of Albany’s assets, drive visitors to its commercial districts and generate media attention – for example outdoor markets, pop-up shops, shopper reward programs, festivals and other events. Existing businesses, nonprofits, business improvement districts and neighborhood associations may apply on a rolling basis through the online form, or by emailing the fillable PDF application to grants@capitalizealbany.com; an application checklist, budget worksheet and program guidelines are posted on the program page. Contact: (518) 434-2532.
Amount: varies by project (amount not published; see program guidelines)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: City of Albany, NY only. Existing businesses, nonprofits, business improvement districts and neighborhood associations. Projects must be activities or events that leverage the City of Albany's assets and promote its commercial districts.

Name: Tennessee SBDC – Memphis Office
Description: The Tennessee Small Business Development Center provides free one-on-one business consulting, including business plan development, financial planning, marketing plan development, sources of capital, social media guidance, business growth planning, government contracting and international trade. The Memphis office is at the Maxine A. Smith Center, 8800 East Shelby Drive, Suite 112, Memphis, TN 38125, open Monday–Friday 8:00am–4:30pm, with a satellite office at the Greater Memphis Chamber (100 Peabody Place, 10th Floor); meetings are by appointment – call 901-333-5085 or use Request Consulting on the office page.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in the Memphis area; meetings by appointment only.

Name: USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program
Description: The USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program matches financially under-resourced inventors and small businesses with volunteer patent attorneys and agents who prepare and file patent applications at no charge. Applicants generally need gross household income below three times the federal poverty guidelines (regional programs may set different criteria), must show an understanding of the patent system by having filed a provisional application or completing the USPTO certificate training course, and must be able to describe the invention and how it works. Apply through the regional program for your state on the Patent Pro Bono coverage map, or email probono@uspto.gov.
Amount: free patent legal help (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Gross household income below 3x federal poverty guidelines (regional programs may differ); provisional application filed or USPTO certificate training completed; able to describe the invention.

Name: City of Austin Small Business Division – free classes, coaching and office hours
Description: The City of Austin’s Small Business Division offers free business training, educational events and coaching for entrepreneurs, including monthly small business classes (with hybrid options) and Small Business Office Hours that connect owners with City departments such as Economic Development, Financial Services, Austin Public Library, Austin Energy and Small and Minority Business Resources. Reserve a spot through the event links on the division’s page.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Austin entrepreneurs and small businesses; classes, coaching and office hours are free.

Name: Texas State University SBDC (Austin) – free one-on-one business advising
Description: Part of the South-West Texas Border SBDC Network, the Texas State University Small Business Development Center provides no-cost, confidential business advising to startup and existing businesses in the Austin and Central Texas area. Its office is at 505 E. Huntland Drive, Suite 505, Austin TX 78752. Complete the intake form on the center’s eCenter Direct portal to request an advisor and allow about 7 business days for a response. 512-420-9379, sbdc@txstate.edu.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Startup and existing small businesses in Austin and Central Texas. Advising is free and confidential; request through the eCenter Direct intake form (allow ~7 business days).

Name: SCORE Chicago – free business mentoring
Description: SCORE Chicago matches entrepreneurs and small business owners in the city of Chicago and northern Cook County with volunteer mentors for free one-on-one mentoring, and runs workshops and webinars on business planning, finance and accounting. Mentoring is free for the life of the business. Request a mentor on the website by ZIP code or call (312) 725-0123; the office is at 332 South Michigan Avenue, Chicago, IL 60604.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Entrepreneurs and small business owners in the city of Chicago and part of Cook County (up to northern Cook County). Free.

Name: Chicago Cook Workforce Partnership – On-the-Job Training wage reimbursement
Description: Through the Chicago Cook Workforce Partnership’s On-the-Job Training service, employers in Chicago and Cook County that hire and train eligible Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) participants can be reimbursed up to 50% of the new hire’s wage rate to offset training costs. The service is delivered through a network of partner agencies listed on the program page. Contact a listed agency or the Partnership at (708) 580-8686 (1 N. Dearborn St., Ste 750, Chicago, IL 60602).
Amount: up to 50% of new hire's wage rate
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Employers in Chicago / Cook County hiring eligible WIOA participants. Employer size limits and training duration not published on the page; confirm with a partner agency.

Name: Illinois SBDC at the Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The Illinois Small Business Development Center hosted by the Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce provides no-cost, one-on-one advising to Chicago-area entrepreneurs and small business owners on business planning, financing, market research, marketing and branding, customer relations, technology, strategic planning and government contracting. Chamber membership is not required. Sign up at ilsbdc.ecenterdirect.com, call (312) 494-6790, or email sbdc@chicagolandchamber.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Chicago-area small business owners and entrepreneurs. Free; chamber membership not required.

Name: Inland Empire SBDC – Free One-on-One Business Consulting
Description: The Inland Empire Small Business Development Center, hosted by Cal State San Bernardino’s Center for Entrepreneurship, serves San Bernardino and Riverside Counties with free business consulting and technical assistance on starting and growing a business, including access to capital. Book a free consultation through the “Book Now” link on the center’s page (entre.csusb.edu/content/sbdc-team); office at 5500 University Parkway, JB284, San Bernardino, CA 92407.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and aspiring entrepreneurs in San Bernardino and Riverside Counties (Inland Empire), California. Consultations are free.

Name: UGA SBDC at Kennesaw State University – free one-on-one business consulting
Description: The University of Georgia Small Business Development Center's Kennesaw office (3333 Busbee Drive, Suite 500, Kennesaw, GA 30144, inside the KSU Center) serves Cobb and Cherokee counties with no-cost consulting and training on capital access and SBA loans, marketing, financial management, operational improvement, and growth planning. Appointments only: (470) 578-6450 or kennesaw@georgiasbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and prospective owners in Cobb and Cherokee counties. By appointment only. The SBDC does not provide funding.

Name: Propel Nonprofits – lending for Minnesota nonprofits
Description: Propel Nonprofits is a CDFI that lends only to 501(c)(3) nonprofits in Minnesota and adjacent states (Wisconsin, Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota) and Native nations in those regions. Products are microloans of $5,000–$50,000 with a maximum 3-year repayment; working capital loans typically $20,000–$600,000, including lines of credit against reimbursing contracts and short-term bridge financing against committed grants; and community facility loans of $50,000–$2 million for building acquisition, improvements, repairs, equipment and construction. Interest rate, collateral, structure and repayment period are set loan by loan, with terms from a few months up to 10 years. A Community Asset Builder loan for BIPOC-led nonprofits acquiring or renovating facilities may also carry a feasibility grant for project planning. Apply at propelnonprofits.org/services/lending or call (612) 249-6700.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Native nations in those regions.

Name: Niagara Falls Small Business Property Improvement Program
Description: A $5 million Empire State Development initiative, administered by the N.F.C. Development Corporation, that reimburses up to 50% of property improvement costs to a maximum of $100,000 per property in downtown Niagara Falls. It funds facade restoration and building upgrades for commercial, retail and mixed-use development within the USA Niagara Development District. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Property must sit inside the USA Niagara Development District in the south end of Niagara Falls, NY (roughly bounded by John B. Daly Blvd east, Niagara Falls State Park west, Niagara Scenic Parkway south, Third Street to Cedar Ave north). Applicant must have site control. Minimum total project cost $25,000. Grants cover up to 50% of costs, $100,000 maximum per property. Projects must align with local or regional comprehensive plans. Program guidelines and application (Nov 2025 revision): https://cms3.revize.com/revize/niagarafallsny/Nov%202025%20NFSBPIP%20Program%20Guidelines_Updated%20Nov%202025.pdf

Name: Grafton Storefront Improvement Program
Description: The City of Grafton, North Dakota reimburses up to 50% of exterior rehabilitation costs, to a maximum of $10,000, for storefronts visible from the public right-of-way. Eligible work includes awnings, canopies, lighting, paint, doors and windows, signage and removal of incompatible exterior finishes. Applications are reviewed competitively by the city's Economic Development Committee on a rolling basis; approval is required before work begins.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to building owners, or to store proprietors/tenants with written lease authorization and at least two years remaining on the lease. Improvements must be visible from the public right-of-way. Licensed contractor bids required; building permit mandatory; before/after photos required. Reimbursement is paid against invoices and proof of payment. Approval must be obtained before work starts - applications go to the Community Development Director, then the Building Official for code review, then the Economic Development Committee for competitive evaluation. Contact City of Grafton (701) 352-1561.

Name: New Mexico State Purchasing – Supplier Registration and Resident Business Preference
Description: New Mexico's State Purchasing Division at the General Services Department runs the state's Online Procurement System, where suppliers create an account to be notified of solicitations. Registration asks suppliers to select accurate Commodity Codes so that relevant bids are routed to them. New Mexico also offers two preference certifications that apply in state procurement competitions, the New Mexico Resident Business Preference and the Resident Veteran Preference, both applied for through the MVD certification portal at secure.mvd.newmexico.gov/residentcertificate. Supplier Support Desk: (505) 827-0499 or (505) 827-0477, SPDInfo@state.nm.us; login and password issues, 800-233-1121.
Amount: no fee stated for registration (vendor access to state solicitations)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses selling goods or services to New Mexico state agencies. Resident Business and Resident Veteran preferences require certification through the New Mexico MVD certification portal.

Name: New Mexico SBDC – Las Cruces (Free One-on-One Business Advising)
Description: The New Mexico Small Business Development Center in Las Cruces serves potential and existing small businesses in Doña Ana and Sierra Counties with no-charge, confidential one-on-one consulting covering business planning, marketing strategy, financial resources and loan package preparation, plus seminars, international trade assistance, and government contracting support through the APEX Accelerator program. Management consulting and training courses are free, though nominal fees may apply to some training. The center is at 2345 Nevada Avenue, Suite 101, Las Cruces, NM 88001, open Monday–Friday 8am–5pm, with face-to-face, Zoom and phone consultations and Spanish-language services. Appointments are encouraged: (575) 527-7676 or sbdcinfo@nmsu.edu.
Amount: free consulting and training (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Potential and existing small businesses in Doña Ana and Sierra Counties, New Mexico.

Name: SBA Office of Native American Affairs and the 8(a) Business Development Program
Description: The SBA's Office of Native American Affairs facilitates access to business growth and expansion tools for small businesses owned by Native Americans, and points owners toward the 8(a) Business Development Program, which helps small, disadvantaged businesses compete for federal contracts. The SBA also lists free technical assistance organizations serving Native-owned businesses, including the National Center for American Indian Enterprise Development (Mesa, Arizona), ONABEN (Portland, Oregon and Tulsa, Oklahoma), and Rural Enterprises of Oklahoma, Inc. (Durant, Oklahoma).
Amount: free (certification and technical assistance; no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Native American-owned small businesses. The 8(a) Business Development Program is for small, disadvantaged businesses seeking federal contracts.

Name: City of Colorado Springs – Mobile Food Vendor License
Description: Required for anyone selling or taking orders for food from the public right-of-way in Colorado Springs. The application needs approval from the county health department in El Paso County, City Planning and Land Use Review, and City Sales Tax, plus a copy of the health inspection. The license is valid for one year; the annual fee is $110 for the first unit and $25 for each additional unit. Apply and check status through the City Clerk’s online application portal.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Mobile food vendors (food trucks, carts) operating on the public right-of-way in the City of Colorado Springs.

Name: Colorado SBDC – Pikes Peak Region (Free One-on-One Business Advising)
Description: The Pikes Peak Small Business Development Center serves El Paso County with no-cost, confidential one-on-one business advising and low-cost training. Businesses not yet operating or in operation for less than a year attend a Start Up Day class before accessing free advising. Catalyst Campus, 559 E. Pikes Peak Avenue, Suite 101, Colorado Springs, CO 80903; 719-667-3803, info@pikespeaksbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and aspiring entrepreneurs in El Paso County / Pikes Peak region, Colorado. Start-ups and businesses under 1 year must attend a Start Up Day class first.

Name: Colorado Enterprise Fund – Small Business Loans and Colorado Startup Loan Fund
Description: Colorado Enterprise Fund, Colorado’s first nonprofit lender, makes small business loans of $10,000 to $1,000,000 to start-ups and existing businesses in Colorado only, with rates and terms tailored to each business. Qualifying factors include collateral to secure the loan; applicants do not need to have been turned down by a bank first. CEF also administers the state-funded Colorado Startup Loan Fund for entrepreneurs who haven’t borrowed before or need a smaller-than-average loan (for-profit, 25 or fewer full-time employees, under $2 million in gross annual revenue). Apply through the CEF customer portal (cef.myloanpanel.com) or call 303-860-0242.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Colorado start-ups and small businesses; collateral required. Startup Loan Fund: for-profit, ≤25 FTE, <$2M gross annual revenue.

Name: Nevada Arts Council – Professional and Workforce Development Grant for Artists
Description: The Nevada Arts Council’s FY27 Professional and Workforce Development Grant reimburses up to $2,000, with no match required, for a practicing artist or creative’s registration fees, travel and lodging for professional development – conferences, workshops, classes, artist residencies and seminars. Applicants must be individual artists aged 21+, Nevada residents for at least one year, U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents, and not degree-seeking students; one grant per applicant per fiscal year. Apply online at nevadaartscouncil.submittable.com at least 30 days before the activity; reimbursement claims are due within 45 days of the event or by June 30, 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists only (practicing artist or creative); Nevada resident for at least one year before applying; age 21+; U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident; not a degree-seeking student. Funds registration fees, travel and lodging for professional development (conferences, workshops, classes, residencies, seminars). Application opened June 1, 2026; apply at least 30 days before the activity; first-come, first-served while funds remain; one grant per fiscal year; reimbursement claims within 45 days of the event or by June 30, 2027.

Name: Federal Bonding Program (free fidelity bonds for hiring returning citizens)
Description: The U.S. Department of Labor’s Federal Bonding Program issues free fidelity bonds that insure employers against loss of money or property through an employee’s dishonest acts (theft, forgery, larceny, embezzlement), with 100% coverage and no deductible. Bonds cover the first six months of employment at no cost to the employer or the job applicant, and are available for job seekers whose backgrounds, including justice involvement, pose barriers to employment. Request a bond through your state bonding coordinator via bonds4jobs.com.
Amount: Free fidelity bond covering the first six months of employment (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any U.S. employer hiring a job seeker whose background poses a barrier to employment, including people with records of arrest, conviction or incarceration. Request through the state bonding coordinator (bonds4jobs.com).

Name: City of Festivals Special Event Support Program (Sacramento)
Description: City of Sacramento program supporting special events held within a designated program boundary area. Grants are reimbursement-based across two categories: first priority is services provided by City of Sacramento staff and departments, and second is non-City expenses such as private security, portable restrooms, and equipment rental where the need exceeds available City services. Award amounts are set by a screening panel based on demonstrated need. Administered by Convention and Cultural Services.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: REIMBURSEMENT, NOT UP-FRONT CASH — funds reimburse event costs after the fact. Both nonprofit and for-profit entities appear eligible; nonprofits must provide a copy of 501(c)(3), 501(c)(6), or other not-for-profit tax status. The event must be located within the designated program boundary map area in the City of Sacramento. Applications are accepted continuously (rolling), but must be submitted NO LESS THAN 20 CALENDAR DAYS prior to the event date, and applicants should allow 45 WORKING DAYS for processing. Applications are screened by a panel. No application fee and no match requirement stated. Contact: Rebecca Bitter, RBitter@cityofsacramento.org, 916-808-8225.

Name: Seated Together Small Business Microgrant Program
Description: Microgrants for for-profit small businesses from Seated Together, LLC, a veteran-owned company based in South Daytona, Florida. Awards are $750, rising to $1,000 for businesses that are at least 51% veteran-owned. The program's stated differentiator is scale: it deliberately keeps the applicant pool small — "hundreds of applicants instead of tens of thousands" — so that each business has a better chance of standing out. Applications are reviewed by a Review Committee on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to for-profit small businesses. Applicant must be at least 18 and authorized to act on behalf of the business. Priority consideration reportedly goes to businesses in Volusia County, Florida and Washington, D.C., and to businesses that are at least 51% veteran-owned (veteran-owned applicants are eligible for the higher $1,000 award). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, with only ONE ACTIVE APPLICATION PER BUSINESS at a time — a business may reapply only after its current application is closed, withdrawn, or resolved. A non-refundable $5.00 processing fee is required with each application; the Terms state the fee does not guarantee funding and does not improve the likelihood of selection. AI drafting tools are explicitly permitted, though the applicant remains responsible for accuracy. Applicants retain ownership of submitted materials but grant a limited license for program administration and promotion. Governing law is Florida, with venue in Volusia County. Sponsor: Seated Together, LLC, 927 Beville Road Suite 10, South Daytona, FL 32119, operations@seatedtogether.com.

Name: UGA Small Business Development Center – Augusta Office
Description: The University of Georgia SBDC’s Augusta office provides no-cost one-on-one business consulting – business planning, financial analysis, access to capital and loan packaging, and marketing – plus workshops for small businesses in the Augusta area. 2907 Professional Pkwy., Suite B, Augusta, GA 30907; (706) 650-5655.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and prospective owners in the Augusta, GA area. No cost for one-on-one consulting.

Name: CSRA Business Lending – CSRA Direct Loans (Augusta, GA)
Description: An Augusta-based nonprofit lender serving businesses throughout Georgia and South Carolina. Its CSRA Direct Loans go up to $500,000 at a 6.50% fixed rate with a 1% fee, funding growing or emerging businesses and often smaller projects that provide a community benefit and may not meet normal SBA eligibility guidelines; most are subordinate to other financing the business is receiving. Credit and time-in-business requirements are not published – confirm with a loan officer. Apply at csrabusinesslending.com/apply-now or call (706) 210-2010 (3626 Walton Way Ext., Suite 1, Augusta).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Growing or emerging businesses in Georgia and South Carolina. No published credit-score or time-in-business minimum; 1% fee.

Name: UH Texas Gulf Coast SBDC Network – free one-on-one business advising
Description: The University of Houston’s Texas Gulf Coast SBDC Network provides free, confidential one-on-one business advising across 32 Southeast Texas counties through 15 locations, covering business and strategic planning, capital access and loan proposals, financial analysis, sales and marketing, market research and government procurement, for businesses from pre-venture through expansion. Find the local center and request an advisor at sbdc.uh.edu/sbdc/Find_Your_SBDC.asp; network phone (713) 752-8488.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and pre-venture entrepreneurs in the 32 Southeast Texas counties served by the UH SBDC network (Houston metro and Gulf Coast).

Name: T.E.A.C.H. Early Childhood® Florida Scholarship Program
Description: T.E.A.C.H. Early Childhood® Florida offers scholarships that help early learning educators working in Florida earn early childhood credentials and college degrees through accredited institutions with little or no debt, with the goal of better compensation and job stability for the workforce. Apply online through the T.E.A.C.H. portal (login.thechildrensforum.com/teach/landing) or call 877-FL-TEACH (358-3224) / 850-487-6300.
Amount: varies (scholarships toward college coursework and early childhood credentials)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early learning educators (teachers, directors) working in Florida early care and education programs.

Name: Florida Child Care Food Program
Description: The Florida Department of Health’s Child Care Food Program reimburses participating licensed child care centers for nutritious meals and snacks served to children in their care. Centers can join as an independent contractor by completing the prospective contractor intake form at mips.floridahealth.gov/ProspectiveContractor/Intake, or participate through an approved sponsoring organization operating in their county. Contact: 850-245-4323, CCFP@FLHealth.gov.
Amount: ongoing reimbursement for eligible meals and snacks
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Licensed child care centers in Florida, as an independent contractor with FDOH or through an approved sponsoring organization.

Name: Florida SBDC at UCF – free business consulting (Central Florida / Osceola County)
Description: The Florida SBDC at the University of Central Florida provides no-cost, one-on-one business consulting plus seminars and webinars for small businesses in Orange, Brevard, Flagler, Lake, Osceola, Seminole, Sumter and Volusia counties, with a satellite center serving Osceola County. Request a consultant at sbdcorlando.com/consulting or call (407) 420-4850.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses and startups in Orange, Brevard, Flagler, Lake, Osceola, Seminole, Sumter and Volusia counties, Florida.

Name: IFF – Nonprofit Facility Improvement, Equipment & Vehicle Loans (Midwest CDFI)
Description: IFF is a nonprofit CDFI that lends to nonprofits across the Midwest, including Kentucky. Its loan products include facility improvement loans (renovation and leasehold improvements), equipment and vehicle loans, acquisition loans and bridge loans, from $10,000 to $6.5 million+. Loans carry up to 15-year terms with no balloon payments and no prepayment penalties, down payments as low as 5%, and no appraisal or loan-to-value requirements on most loans. Its bridge loans are for 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving low-income communities or people with disabilities that have an independent board of directors. Apply by emailing IFFTeam@iff.org or calling 312-629-0060.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits in IFF's Midwest footprint (IA, IL, IN, KS, KY, MI, MN, MO, OH, WI per IFF's 2026 Bridge Loan Overview). Bridge loans: 501(c)(3) serving low-income communities or persons with disabilities, independent board. No published credit or operating-history minimum on the Capital Solutions page.

Name: CareerSource Broward – On-the-Job Training wage reimbursement
Description: CareerSource Broward’s On-the-Job Training program reimburses employers up to 90% of a new hire’s wages during the training period, for candidates who already have some job-related skills and are trained on the job to the employer’s standards. CareerSource Broward also provides no-cost recruitment services. Submit the short employer interest form and a CareerSource Broward specialist will follow up.
Amount: up to 90% of new-hire wages during the training period
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Employers hiring in Broward County, FL.

Name: Florida Incumbent Worker Training (IWT) Grant – CareerSource Florida
Description: CareerSource Florida’s Incumbent Worker Training grant reimburses Florida companies for training their full-time employees, covering industry- or business-specific skills, technical or computer skills, and foundational skills such as leadership, teamwork and management. Applicants must obtain a Florida Tax Clearance Letter before submitting, then apply online through CareerSource Florida’s portal. Questions: info@careersourceflorida.com.
Amount: reimburses up to 50% of direct training costs (up to 75% for companies with 25 or fewer employees or in rural/distressed areas); the 2025-26 cap was $100,000 per location
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Florida companies training their full-time employees; Florida Tax Clearance Letter required before applying. Enhanced 75% reimbursement for companies with 25 or fewer employees or in rural/distressed areas.

Name: Florida SBDC at FAU – free business consulting (Broward and Palm Beach)
Description: The Florida Small Business Development Center at Florida Atlantic University provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one consulting, virtual or in person, to new and established businesses in Broward and Palm Beach Counties. Areas include strategic planning, loan proposal development, cash flow management, government contracting, export planning, feasibility studies and market research. Request a consultation at floridasbdc.org/request-consulting.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: New and established businesses in Broward and Palm Beach Counties, FL.

Name: The Runway at FAU – Venture Program (Boca Raton)
Description: The Runway, Florida Atlantic University's startup incubator in Boca Raton, runs a Venture Program for high-growth entrepreneurs and startups through three tracks: Incubate, Validate and Accelerate. Accepted companies get access to more than $100,000 in resources and services, including structured mentoring, entrepreneurship programming, customer discovery workshops, connections to early-stage funding, college interns for marketing and business support, pitch coaching and free legal and accounting consultations. Priority goes to ventures aligned with FAU research areas such as environmental science, marine science, AI, cybersecurity, drones, edtech and neuroscience. Apply through the online application on the program page; questions to InnovateFAU@fau.edu.
Amount: more than $100,000 in resources and services
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: High-growth-potential entrepreneurs and startups; strategic alignment with FAU research areas (environmental science, marine science, AI, cybersecurity, drones, edtech, neuroscience, etc.). FAU affiliation and location requirements not stated on the page — confirm with InnovateFAU@fau.edu.

Name: Illinois Small Business Development Center at McHenry County College
Description: The Illinois SBDC at McHenry County College provides no-cost, one-on-one business advising to start-up entrepreneurs and to owners and managers of McHenry County businesses with up to 500 employees, plus monthly workshops and courses on business planning, marketing, finance, operations and technology, and guidance on funding. Become a client through the online portal at ilsbdc.ecenterdirect.com/signup, or contact the center at (815) 455-6098 or sbdc@mchenry.edu (8900 US Hwy 14, Crystal Lake, IL 60012).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: McHenry County, IL businesses with up to 500 employees, plus start-up entrepreneurs; serves legal U.S. residents and citizens. No cost.

Name: NCWorks On-the-Job Training (wage reimbursement for new hires)
Description: NCWorks On-the-Job Training reimburses 50 to 75 percent of a new employee's wages during training, depending on the size of the business, with the higher rate reserved for companies with up to 250 employees. Training contracts cannot exceed six months and are limited to the time the employee needs to become proficient in the job. Contact your local Workforce Development Board Business Services Representative (ncawdb.org/local-boards) or NCWorks Business Services at (800) 562-6333, BusinessServices@ncworks.gov.
Amount: 50-75% wage reimbursement for up to 6 months
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: North Carolina employers hiring new workers who need training to become proficient; reimbursement rate depends on business size (higher for 250 or fewer employees). Arranged through the local Workforce Development Board.

Name: NCWorks Incumbent Worker Training Grant (North Carolina)
Description: NCWorks Incumbent Worker Training grants, administered by the NC Department of Commerce through local Workforce Development Boards, help offset the cost of training employees who have worked for a business consistently for six months or more. Training is intended to support employee advancement and create backfill opportunities for less experienced staff, and funds can cover training needs assessment, instructional design, development and delivery. Businesses contribute to training costs through cash or in-kind contributions scaled by company size. Apply through your local Workforce Development Board Business Services Representative (find yours at ncawdb.org/local-boards) or contact NCWorks Business Services at (800) 562-6333, BusinessServices@ncworks.gov.
Amount: varies (business contributes a cash or in-kind match scaled by company size)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: North Carolina employers training employees who have worked for the business consistently for 6+ months; business provides a cash or in-kind contribution scaled by company size. Apply through the local Workforce Development Board.

Name: Illinois Quality Improvement (QI) Funds – Child Care Resource & Referral
Description: Illinois’ local Child Care Resource & Referral (CCR&R) agencies award Quality Improvement Funds to child care programs working toward or maintaining an ExceleRate Illinois Circle of Quality, in three parts: cohort funds toward the objectives in the program’s Continuous Quality Improvement Plan, training stipends covering required Circle of Quality training for the minimum required staff, and accreditation assistance for programs applying for or maintaining Silver or Gold Circle status. Funds are awarded based on available funding. Apply through the local CCR&R serving the program's county (agency locator at inccrra.org); Grundy, Kankakee, Kendall and Will counties are served by Child Care Resource and Referral (SDA 5), Joliet – (815) 741-1163 or assistance@childcarehelp.com.
Amount: set per award, based on available funding
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Illinois child care programs working toward or maintaining an ExceleRate Illinois Circle of Quality; administered by the local CCR&R.

Name: National Mentoring Resource Center – free technical assistance for mentoring programs
Description: The National Mentoring Resource Center, run by MENTOR, provides youth mentoring programs with no-cost, customized technical assistance on specific mentoring practices, along with webinars, e-learning modules, research and practice reviews, toolkits, logic models and program evaluation and measurement guidance. Request assistance through the website, at (617) 303-4600, or nmrc@mentoring.org.
Amount: free technical assistance and training (no cash award)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Youth mentoring programs in the U.S.; all services are no-cost. The site does not state whether for-profit programs qualify or define a youth age range — confirm with nmrc@mentoring.org.

Name: Hawaiʻi Small Business Development Center – Hilo/East Hawaiʻi Center
Description: The Hawaiʻi SBDC provides no-cost business advisory services, research and analysis, and workshops to small businesses statewide, with language assistance available. The Hilo/East Hawaiʻi Center can be reached at (808) 933-0776 or info@hisbdc.org; sign up for no-cost advising through the online registration at hisbdc.org.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in Hawaiʻi; services offered on a nondiscriminatory basis to all legal residents and citizens in the US. Lead Center (Hilo): (808) 932-8970. Hilo/East Hawaiʻi Center: (808) 933-0776.

Name: Columbia Economic Development Corporation (CEDC) – Revolving Loan Fund and SBA Microloans (Columbia County, NY)
Description: The Columbia Economic Development Corporation in Hudson, NY runs a Revolving Loan Fund for start-up and expanding businesses that create jobs in Columbia County, at competitive rates and terms, and makes SBA Microloans to for-profit businesses in Columbia and Greene Counties with complimentary technical assistance. Loan amounts are not published. Apply by contacting CEDC at 518.828.4718; One Hudson City Centre, Suite 301, Hudson, NY 12534.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Revolving Loan Fund: start-up and expanding businesses that create jobs in Columbia County, NY, meeting CEDC lending criteria. SBA Microloans: for-profit businesses in Columbia and Greene Counties. Credit and time-in-business minimums not published.

Name: Community Loan Fund of the Capital Region – small business loans (Albany, NY CDFI)
Description: Albany-based community lender providing financing and business training to small businesses and entrepreneurs in Albany, Columbia, Fulton, Greene, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Warren and Washington Counties. Loan amounts and terms are not published online. Contact (518) 436-8586 or info@mycommunityloanfund.org; 255 Orange St #103, Albany, NY 12210.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses, entrepreneurs and nonprofits in Albany, Columbia, Fulton, Greene, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Warren and Washington Counties, NY. Minimums not published.

Name: U.S. Bank Foundation Community Possible Grant – Work
Description: The U.S. Bank Foundation’s Community Possible grants fund nonprofits in U.S. Bank markets. The Work pillar covers job-skills training with placement services, small business technical assistance, postsecondary preparation for low- to moderate-income students, and financial education. Full applications are by invitation only; organizations start by submitting an electronic Letter of Interest through the Community Possible Grant Program page.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY: 501(c)(3)s in U.S. Bank markets (25 states incl. Arizona). LOI first; full application by invitation.

Name: Albertsons Companies Foundation – Southwest Division Grant
Description: The Albertsons Companies Foundation’s Southwest division, which covers Albertsons and Safeway communities in Arizona, New Mexico, Las Vegas/Henderson and El Paso, funds 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving the communities where its stores operate. Priorities include health and human services, hunger relief, education, veterans and helping people living with disabilities. First-time grantees typically receive $1,000 to $5,000. Events, capital campaigns, sports teams, fundraising galas and religious or political organizations are not funded. Apply through the foundation’s online grant application; decisions take about 12 weeks after an application cycle closes.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NONPROFITS ONLY: 501(c)(3)s serving Southwest division store communities. Division focus and amounts confirmed via grant aggregators (Grantable, TheShareWay, Instrumentl); the foundation's own guidelines page was unreachable Oct 2, 2026.

Name: UTSA Small Business Development Center – free one-on-one business advising (San Antonio)
Description: The UTSA Small Business Development Center, part of the South-West Texas Border SBDC Network, provides confidential one-on-one business advising at no charge, plus low-cost workshops on a range of business topics and referrals to partner resources. Request advising through the center’s online eCenter form at sasbdc.org. Office: One Riverwalk Place, 700 N. St. Mary’s Street, Floor 5, San Antonio, TX 78205; (210) 458-2460; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Central. New Braunfels clients are served through the SPARK Small Business Center.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small businesses in the San Antonio / New Braunfels area served by the UTSA SBDC (South-West Texas Border SBDC Network, txsbdc.org). Advising is free and confidential; appointments recommended.

Name: Maine Entrepreneurial Resource Corps (MERC)
Description: MTI’s MERC program covers 50% of the fee for short-term (three months or less) projects with vetted Maine-based consultants – marketing, finance, legal services, custom software and more – up to $15,000 a year or $30,000 over a business’s lifetime, plus free self-paced AI coursework through Coursera. Eligible businesses are Maine-based, under $5 million in annual revenue, operating in one of MTI’s seven technology sectors, with an innovation that creates economic impact in Maine and access to matching funds. Complete the interest form, meet the MERC coordinator, apply, choose a consultant and scope the work. (207) 582-4790.
Amount: 50% of consulting project fees, up to $15,000 per year / $30,000 lifetime
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maine-based; under $5M annual revenue; in one of MTI's seven technology sectors; innovation with economic impact in Maine; access to matching funds.

Name: Maine Technology Institute – SBIR/STTR Federal Funding Application Support
Description: MTI’s Technical Assistance Program gives Maine small businesses free expert help pursuing federal Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) R&D funding: strategy meetings, help identifying the right agency solicitations, proposal writing assistance and proposal review. Agency deadlines vary (current topics at sbir.gov/topics). Take MTI’s online SBIR/STTR assessment, then complete the interest form. (207) 582-4790.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maine small businesses pursuing early-stage R&D through federal SBIR/STTR programs; complete MTI's online assessment and interest form.

Name: Maine Technology Institute – Business Innovation Funding
Description: MTI funds technical and scientific innovation at Maine-led companies in seven sectors, including Biotechnology, Composites & Advanced Materials, Environmental Technologies and Precision Manufacturing. Tier 1 (up to $30,000) is for early-stage, pre-revenue or very early revenue companies; Tier 2 ($30,000–$60,000) and Tier 3 ($60,000–$100,000) follow as companies document customer interest and approach commercialization. Applicants need leadership based in Maine, evidence of conversations with potential customers, economic impact potential for Maine, and at least 1:1 matching funds (cash match required; in-kind may be accepted). Start with the self-assessment on MTI’s site, then submit the online interest form through MTI’s portal. MTI, 16 Middle St. STE 201, Portland: (207) 582-4790.
Amount: Tier 1 up to $30,000 (first awards typically $10,000–$30,000); up to $100,000 cumulative per company
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maine-based leadership; technical or scientific innovation in one of seven sectors (Biotechnology, Composites & Advanced Materials, Environmental Technologies, Forest Products & Agriculture, Information Technology, Marine Technology & Aquaculture, Precision Manufacturing); evidence of customer conversations; economic impact potential for Maine; minimum 1:1 matching funds (cash match required, in-kind may be accepted). Rolling; review typically about two months.

Name: CEI (Coastal Enterprises, Inc.) – Wicked Fast Microloan and Business Loans
Description: CEI, a Maine-based community development lender, offers the Wicked Fast Microloan – up to $15,000 for start-up businesses and up to $30,000 for existing businesses at 7.25% for up to 5 years – and Business Loans up to $1,000,000 (higher amounts may be considered) at 6.0%–10.0% over 3–7 years. A Riba-free financing option is available. Apply with the online loan application or loan inquiry form, a Credit Acknowledgement for each guarantor and the business document checklist (a Business Questionnaire is accepted for loans under $50,000). Typical time to approval is 4–6 weeks. 207.504.5900.
Amount: Microloan up to $15,000 (start-ups) / $30,000 (existing); Business Loans up to $1,000,000
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maine-based businesses; start-ups eligible for Wicked Fast Microloans. Credit Acknowledgement required per guarantor; collateral varies by program.

Name: Maine Small Business Development Center (Maine SBDC)
Description: Maine SBDC provides no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising and training for startups and existing businesses on business planning, financing, marketing and management. Select “Request Advising” on the website to be matched with an advisor. Headquarters: 55 Exeter Street, Portland; 207-780-4420.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Maine startups and existing small businesses.

Name: CA Ontario Downtown Storefront Facade Improvement Program
Description: The City of Ontario reimburses half the cost of storefront improvements for businesses and property owners in Downtown Ontario, covering signage, lighting, windows and other exterior work visible from the street. Funded with federal CDBG dollars and structured as a 50/50 matching grant of up to $25,000, paid after City staff verify completed work. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Application form: https://form.jotform.com/241844570977166 - Property owners, or business tenants with documented owner consent. Property must sit between Emporia Street and G Street (100-200 blocks of South Euclid, 100-600 blocks of North Euclid). CDBG-funded; applicant funds 50% of project cost; reimbursement follows City verification of completed work.

Name: CA Long Beach Safe & Secure Grant
Description: Long Beach helps storefront businesses pay for security improvements, with the award sized by storefront footprint. Businesses with storefronts of 1,500 square feet or less receive $750; those between 1,500 and 5,000 square feet, or with at least 25 linear feet of street frontage, receive $1,500.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Long Beach storefront businesses. 1,500 sq ft or less: $750. 1,500-5,000 sq ft, or at least 25 linear feet of street frontage: $1,500.

Name: California STEP Export Voucher Program
Description: GO-Biz's State Trade Expansion Program reimburses California small businesses for up to 75% of pre-approved export promotion costs, capped at $10,000 per federal fiscal year. Eligible expenses include international trade shows and trade missions, U.S. Commercial Service products, EXIM credit insurance premiums, international marketing materials, and website globalization or e-commerce work. Expenses must be approved before they are incurred.
Amount: $500 - $10,000 (up to 75% reimbursement; $10,000 cap per federal fiscal year)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit business organized or incorporated in the U.S. with significant business operations in California; in business at least one year; meets SBA small-business size standards; exports goods or services of U.S. origin or containing at least 51% U.S. content; export-ready. Pre-approval required before incurring expenses. Apply at https://step.business.ca.gov/ (account creation at /Public/AccountCreate.aspx). FY26 guidelines: https://export.business.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/STEP-Program-Guidelines.pdf

Name: CA Long Beach Visual Improvement Program Grant
Description: Long Beach reimburses small businesses and nonprofits for repairing visible damage from crime or vandalism - broken windows, graffiti removal, damaged signage and similar storefront repairs. Grants are up to $1,000. The City accepts preliminary applications continuously and awards as funding becomes available, so submission does not guarantee an award.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits are eligible alongside for-profit small businesses. Business must have been impacted by crime or vandalism on or after October 1, 2023, and be located in the City of Long Beach. Preliminary application only; award subject to funding availability.

Name: TN Collierville Holiday Market Vendor Call (Christmas in Collierville)
Description: The Town of Collierville runs a curated holiday market during Christmas in Collierville, held on four Saturdays between Thanksgiving and Christmas. Vendors apply through the town's interest form and a committee reviews submissions until all booth spaces are filled. There is no cost to participate, and each accepted vendor is provided a 10'x10' tent with three side walls, a six-foot table, two chairs and bistro lighting.
Amount: No cash; free booth with equipment provided
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Vendors offering high-quality hand-made items. NOT accepting food vendors at this time. Space limited; 'Applications will be reviewed by a committee until all booth spaces are filled.' No generators permitted; electrical access not guaranteed. No cost to participate.

Name: Small Business B(AI)sics
Description: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation and U.S. Chamber, with support from Google, deliver free in-person AI training for small business owners through local chambers of commerce. Workshops cover practical AI for marketing, automation and data-driven decisions, with no technical background required. Sessions run through 50+ implementation partners in 30+ states and are listed by month on the program page; registration happens on each host chamber's own site.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to any small business owner or entrepreneur; no prior technical experience required; free to attend. No central registration page or unified calendar - the program page lists sessions by month and attendees must register via the local host chamber (per-session registration is hosted at events.uschamberfoundation.org/<Chamber>/begin).

Name: California Sales Tax Exclusion (STE) Program
Description: CAEATFA, under the State Treasurer's Office, excludes qualifying manufacturing equipment purchases from California sales and use tax. It is a tax benefit rather than a cash award, applied at purchase or claimed back from the vendor or state. The program targets California manufacturers in alternative energy, advanced transportation and advanced manufacturing, and accepts applications on a rolling basis against roughly $100 million in annual authority.
Amount: No cash; sales/use tax exclusion on qualified property. ~$100,000,000 total program authority; per-applicant benefit varies.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Portal listing: https://www.grants.ca.gov/grants/sales-tax-exclusion-ste-program/ - Must be a California manufacturer in one of: alternative source products (solar, renewable hydrogen, biofuels); advanced transportation technologies (zero-emission vehicles, charging stations); advanced manufacturing (food production, aerospace, biopharmaceutical); or processors of recycled feedstock. Businesses, individuals, nonprofits, public agencies and tribal governments all eligible. Open since 9/1/2010 with no close date; awards announced on an ongoing basis.

Name: Michigan Celebrates Small Business (MCSB) Awards
Description: Statewide awards program run by the SBAM Foundation with the Michigan SBDC, MEDC, Small Business Advocate, and the Edward Lowe Foundation, honoring 90+ Michigan small businesses each year. Categories include Michigan 50 Companies to Watch, Michigan 50 Distinguished Alumni, and Veteran-Owned, Minority-Owned, Women-Owned, Disability-Owned, and Micro Business awards, plus the SBDC Best Small Business Awards. Recipients get statewide public recognition, presentation at the Awards Gala, membership in the 1,000+ alumni network, and Capitol Day visibility. The 2027 event runs April 19-20, 2027 in the Greater Lansing area.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: RECOGNITION ONLY — no cash or in-kind prize is stated on any official page. Free to nominate. Business must be headquartered or based in Michigan; statewide, no county restriction. Michigan 50 Companies to Watch: privately held commercial enterprise (not a nonprofit, not publicly traded, not a subsidiary or division), past startup stage, 6-99 full-time-equivalent W-2 employees, between $750,000 and $50M in annual revenue or working capital, and demonstrated intent and capacity for growth. Micro Business: 1-9 employees or under $500,000 in annual revenue. Distinguished Alumni: prior Michigan 50 recipient, Michigan-based, increased employees since the award, $1.25M in annual revenue or working capital. Demographic categories require at least 51% ownership and daily control by the qualifying group (veteran with minimum general discharge; African American, Asian American, Hispanic American or Native American; women who are U.S. citizens; individuals with disabilities). 2027 nominations are open now; nominate at 2027-michigan-celebrates-small-business.events.sbam.org. ATTENDANCE IS PAID — 2026 gala tickets started at $189; 2027 pricing not yet posted, and whether honorees receive complimentary tickets is not stated.

Name: West Coast Craft San Francisco Vendor Application
Description: West Coast Craft is a large juried design and craft market at Fort Mason Center in San Francisco, featuring more than 275 artists and designer brands. The market selects work combining strong design, craftsmanship and distinctive branding. Applying is free, with booth fees charged only on acceptance, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis ahead of the stated deadline.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Juried selection - work is assessed on design, craftsmanship and distinctive branding
- Artists and designer brands; 275+ vendors at the market
- Held at Fort Mason Center, San Francisco

FREE TO APPLY. Booth fees of $375 - $925 depending on booth size are charged on acceptance.

Application deadline October 30, 2026; applications reviewed on a ROLLING basis, so applying early improves the odds of a place.
Event dates: February 13-14, 2027.

Name: Women Founders Grant
Description: $5,000 rolling grants for majority women-founded businesses at any stage, from side hustles to established ventures. Simple application with two questions; $25 non-refundable fee. Winners are chosen based on passion, authenticity, and merit.

Name: Darcy's Business Freedom Grant
Description: The $1,000 Business Freedom Grant, created by Coach Darcy (Darcy’s Business), provides up to $1,000 to help people launch or grow a business. It’s open to anyone with a clear business idea or an existing small business in any industry. Winners are selected based on idea clarity, plan feasibility, expected impact of the grant, and commitment, and are announced live on Coach Darcy’s YouTube channel.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
You're a perfect fit if you have:
- A clear business idea with an actionable plan.
- A business in any industry, product-based, service-based, or digital.
- The commitment to complete a brief application sharing your vision.

Name: Illinois Employer Training Investment Program (ETIP) – Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce
Description: The Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce administers the Employer Training Investment Program with grant funding from the Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity (DCEO). Participating companies are reimbursed up to 50% of the cost of training their employees, whether delivered by the Chamber’s pre-qualified training partners, an outside vendor, or the company’s own staff. The company must operate physically in Illinois, and trainees must be full-time, Illinois-based workers; some restrictions apply to certain training types and travel expenses. To start, submit the inquiry form on the ETIP page or email etip@chicagolandchamber.org.
Amount: up to 50% reimbursement of eligible training costs
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Company must operate physically within Illinois
- Trainees must be full-time, Illinois-based workers
- Restrictions apply to certain training types and travel expenses
- Funds distributed first-come, first-served; chamber membership not stated as required

Name: RAMP — Regional Alliance Marketplace for Procurement (Los Angeles)
Description: LA28 is seeking businesses to apply for its pool of approved restaurants and food vendors. The Regional Alliance Marketplace for Procurement (RAMP) is a free online marketplace listing government contracting opportunities across Los Angeles-region public agencies, launched by the City of Los Angeles with the Los Angeles Business Council to give small and diverse businesses more equitable access to public contracts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT FUNDING — this is a government contracting marketplace. Open to businesses seeking to bid on public-sector contracts in the Los Angeles region, with an explicit aim of improving access for small and diverse businesses. Businesses register on rampla.org and then browse and respond to individual solicitations, each of which carries its own scope, value, requirements, and due date. Opportunities are posted on a rolling basis. Registration appears to be free, though the site could not be read directly to confirm. Relevant certifications (for example City of LA small business or MBE/WBE status) typically strengthen a bid but are set per solicitation rather than by the platform.

Name: Seattle Office of Economic Development Storefront Repair Fund
Description: The Seattle Storefront Repair Fund is a grant that reimburses small, independently owned businesses for costs of repairing physical storefront damage (e.g., broken windows or doors), offering up to $3,000 per incident for as many as three separate incidents. Eligible businesses must have already paid for repairs, meet size and revenue limits, and operate within Seattle, with applications open through December 2026 or until funds are exhausted.

Name: Mountain View Facade Improvement Grant
Description: The City of Mountain View offers matching grants to small businesses, commercial property owners and local nonprofits for storefront exterior improvements. Awards total up to seventeen thousand five hundred dollars, combining twenty-five hundred for architectural design services with a seventy-five percent matching grant of up to fifteen thousand for physical improvements. Eligible work includes awnings, parapets, signage, window displays, exterior painting, murals and door or window refurbishment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Mountain View small business owner, commercial property owner, or a nonprofit serving the Mountain View community
- Must occupy a street-facing commercial building or space - first-floor storefront retail, restaurants, or service businesses
- Valid City business license with no active violations
- Tenant applicants must include the property owner's signature
- Applicant contributes 25% of physical improvement costs; City provides 75% matching funds up to $15,000
- Architectural services capped at $2,500 (roughly 10 hours)
- California state-mandated prevailing wage rates apply to any construction work funded

CORRECTION: not purely rolling - the guidelines state a hard end date of 12/31/2026, or earlier if funds are exhausted. First come, first served. Submit by email to Econ.Dev@mountainview.gov.

Name: New York Foundation for the Arts Fellowship
Description: The NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowship is a $8,000 unrestricted grant for artists who live in New York State and/or one of its Tribal Nations, meant to support an artist’s overall vision rather than a specific project. Eligible disciplines in 2026 include: Craft/Sculpture, Digital/Electronic Arts, Nonfiction Literature, Poetry, and Printmaking/Drawing/Book Arts. Applicants must be 25+, have at least two consecutive years of NYS (or Tribal Nation) residency, not be enrolled in a degree program, and not have won a fellowship in the past five years. For the 2027 cycle, applications will open in Fall 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:
- 25 years or older by the application deadline date
- Current residents of New York State and/or one of the Tribal Nations located in New York State
- Must have maintained New York State residency, and/or residency in one of the Tribal Nations located therein, for at least the last two consecutive years (2024 & 2025)
- Not enrolled in a degree-seeking program of any kind
- Are the originators of the work, i.e. choreographers or playwrights, not interpretive artists such as dancers or actors
- Did not receive a NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowship in any discipline in the past five consecutive years: 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.
- Cannot submit any work samples that have been previously awarded a NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowship
- While collaborating artists are eligible to apply, the total number of artists cannot exceed three individuals (this includes the submitter). Each artist applying  must all meet the eligibility criteria for this award. Artists applying as a collaboration cannot apply separately as an individual in the same year
- Applicants can apply in a maximum of 2 categories each cycle
- Are not a current NYFA employee or have been in the last 12 months, a member of the NYFA Board of Trustees or Artists’ Advisory Committee, 2026 panelist, or an immediate family member of any of the above. 
Artists that have been awarded five NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellowships receive Emeritus status and are no longer eligible for the award

Name: Denver Business Impact Opportunity Fund Grant
Description: Denver Economic Development & Opportunity’s Business Impact Opportunity (BIO) Fund offers construction stabilization grants (up to $15,000) plus technical assistance to small businesses economically harmed by specified city-funded construction projects, with the current round focused on the East Colfax BRT construction corridor. Eligible businesses within 350 feet of the project can apply for a one-time grant—$7,500 for businesses with ≤$100,000 annual gross revenue and $15,000 for those above that threshold – if they meet requirements like eligible NAICS codes, $30K–$5M in 2025 revenue, and demonstrating at least a 20% revenue decline over a 90+ day period due to construction.
Amount: $7,500 (gross revenue under $100K) / $15,000 (over $100K), one grant per business
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The construction stabilization grant is intended to support small businesses that have been impacted by specified city-funded construction projects within 350 feet of their business location. Applicants may apply for a one-time grant.
- $7,500 for businesses with annual gross revenue equal to or less than $100,000
- $15,000 for businesses with annual gross revenue greater than $100,000

Name: CA Los Angeles Genesis For Good Catalyst Empowerment Grant Program
Description: The Catalyst Empowerment Grant provides funding and business-development support to historically under-resourced small businesses in low-to-moderate-income communities in Southern California. Recipients also receive access to Catalyst 360, offering advisory services, technical assistance, education, mentorship, networking, and capital connections.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit businesses with ≤$500K gross revenue, operating 1+ year, ≤10 employees, located in an LMI area, and properly licensed.

Name: Philadelphia 76ers Enrich Program
Description: The Enrich Program, presented by the Philadelphia 76ers and Bank of America, supports independent small businesses that have faced barriers to growth. It offers the top business an official 76ers partnership with marketing, PR, consulting, and networking support, while two additional businesses receive cash awards.
Amount: Grand Prize: official 76ers partnership + marketing/PR/consulting/networking package; 2nd & 3rd place: $10,000 each
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
• Location: Must be founded in and/or operating within the Philadelphia Metropolitan Area.
• Business Type: Must be an independent, non-franchised entity.
• Incorporation: Must be formally incorporated.
• Application: Businesses that clearly articulate how they navigate and overcome systemic challenges will be better positioned in the selection process.

Name: Grow Your Chispa
Description: A partnership between AT&T and the Hispanic Heritage Foundation that awards five ten-thousand-dollar grants to Hispanic entrepreneurs making a direct impact in their communities. The foundation's program page states the award structure but publishes no eligibility criteria, application form or deadline. The most recent recipients announced were five Latina business owners named in May 2024, and no later cycle appears on the foundation's site.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Hispanic entrepreneurs whose businesses make a direct impact in their community
- No further criteria published - no revenue, geographic, business-stage or documentation requirements are stated anywhere on the foundation's page

NO LIVE CYCLE FOUND. The $10,000 x 5 award structure is confirmed on the foundation's own page, but there is no application link, no deadline, and no eligibility detail. The only cycle traceable to the foundation is the May 2024 recipient announcement.

Name: Northeast SARE Farmer Grant
Description: Northeast SARE funds commercial farmers testing new sustainable agriculture ideas through field trials, demonstrations and on-farm research. Awards typically range from five thousand to thirty thousand dollars depending on a project's complexity and duration, and cover farmer compensation for time, project materials, consulting fees, soil testing and outreach. Grants operate on a reimbursement basis, so farms must be able to spend before being repaid.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Commercial farm business owners and farm employees are eligible
- Must meet the U.S. Census of Agriculture definition of a farm: any place from which $1,000 or more of agricultural products were produced and sold during the year
- Farms of all sizes and types, including organic operations
- Northeast SARE region: CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT, WV and Washington DC

FUNDS: farmer compensation for time, project materials, consulting fees, soil testing, and outreach expenses to share results.
DOES NOT FUND: capital improvements (barns, greenhouses), equipment purchases, farm startup costs, or utilities unrelated to the project.
Reimbursement basis - no advance payments, so the farm must be able to expend funds first.

CURRENT CALL IS CLOSED; next cycle dates not announced. Join the Northeast SARE mailing list for the reopening.

Northeast SARE runs six other grant programs from the same hub (northeast.sare.org/grants/get-a-grant/): Farming Community, Graduate Student Research, Research and Education, Research for Novel Approaches, Partnership, and Professional Development. Those are aimed largely at researchers, educators and institutions rather than farm businesses. Known deadlines: Graduate Student Research due Sept 29, 2026 4 p.m. ET; the large grants (Farming Community, Research and Education, Research for Novel Approaches, Professional Development) due Oct 26, 2026 4 p.m. ET.

Name: Honeybook Breakthrough Grant
Description: Provides early-stage marketing and creative consultants with $25,000 in tools, resources, and training to accelerate their growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What will the grant winners receive?
- Ten business owners will receive the Breakthrough Grant package valued at $25,000, which includes: 
- A three-year Premium HoneyBook membership (worth $2,400) 
- $18,000 cash for recipients to invest in additional tools or training 
- Expert business support from seasoned HoneyBook Pros to help recipients optimize their processes and systems (worth over $4,000)
- Plus, winners will gain access to a private peer community and exclusive workshops

Who is eligible for the grant?
The Breakthrough Grant is for early-stage marketing and creative consultants. This includes digital marketers, social media managers, SEO experts, marketing agencies, brand photographers, content creators, and more. 

The program is for individuals that are skilled in their field and committed to their growth but in the early years of their independent career—from recently started to up to three years in business. At this stage, it is common to face financial, operational, or knowledge challenges, which the grant aims to help business owners overcome. 

Backed by experience and a demonstrated commitment to independent entrepreneurship, these businesses are well-positioned to reach the next stage of growth with help from the investment and support offered by the grant. 

When evaluating applicants, we’re particularly looking for businesses that already have a name and clear service offering, have demonstrated a commitment to growing their businesses, have a digital presence, and are based in the United States or Canada, excluding Quebec. 

At this time, we’re only offering the grant to non-HoneyBook members so we can reach a new audience of emerging business owners who are not set up yet with the tools and resources they need to be successful.

Name: Boundless Futures Foundation Her Village Grant
Description: Boundless Futures Foundation’s Her Village Grants provide annual funding to U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits that directly support female entrepreneurs through programs like skills training, mentorship, business education, incubators/accelerators, or access to capital. The foundation awards one grant per year to a mission-aligned organization focused on advancing women’s entrepreneurial resources and networks, especially those that promote social enterprise and address systemic inequities through women-led businesses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Applicants: 
- Female founders 22 years of age and older with businesses registered and operating in the United States. An applicant’s business must:
- Make a clear social impact;
- Be a registered for-profit entity;
- Be earning revenue, and 
- Not be more than five years old.

To be awarded grant funding, applicants must self-report a credit score and agree to a third-party background check. Please refer to the Boundless Futures Foundation website for more information.

Businesses that are eligible for an EmpowHer grant address one of the following social issues through their product or business model: 
- Poverty, Hunger, or Humanitarian Aid
- Sustainability & the Environment

Name: Lenovo Evolve Small Grant
Description: Awards 10 small businesses across North America with a grant that includes a Lenovo technology package, cash, access to mentorship and community support, and AI technology and training.

Name: Start Pivot Grow Accelerator
Description: A national accelerator supporting small and midsize businesses with tailored business education, expert advising, and access to capital. Participants gain access to resources like custom workshops, four free advising sessions, and grant-funded opportunities.
Amount: up to $20,000 (as part of pitch competition)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Own and operate an active business for 2 years or more with current financial statements for validation
- Must earn a minimum of $100,000 in annual revenue as of 2024
- Must have 2 or more employees or contractors (including owner)
- Must be able to attend online workshops, complete self-pace course, complete deliverables and business advising sessions to qualify for pitch competition application

Name: Honeycomb Credit Breakthrough Grant
Description: Offers a $10,000 grant to small business owners for a wide variety of growth initiatives.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to all small business owners. You can use the funds to expand your product line, move to a new space, purchase new equipment, or anything else that will help you breakthrough in 2025! The grant runs from January 17 through April 2, 2025.

Name: Backing Small Businesses Grant Program
Description: A partnership between American Express and Main Street America, the grant program provides $10,000 grants to 500 small businesses with community or cultural significance, plus $30,000 enhancement grants to 25 recipients.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What do we mean by "community reach"?
A small business with community reach is involved in and critical to the surrounding community or serves a cultural- or ability-specific need. These businesses are often long-standing or legacy businesses that provide continuity and a sense of identity to a neighborhood or specific cultural group. Businesses with community reach have also been intentional about developing core values and a business model that supports their communities or addresses an acute community need. For example, a business that regularly hosts free concerts featuring local artists, or a shop that provides goods or services that uniquely serve a customer base in the community.

Name: Creator's Momentum Business Accelerator
Description: An eight-week virtual program for 100 creative entrepreneurs, offering business education, tools for growth, and a $5,000 grant upon successful completion.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Owner of an operating business that contributes to the creative economy, including crafters, artists, makers, musicians, and other creative entrepreneurs
- Owner of a business that has been operational for at least one year and with annual revenue equivalent of less than $500,000
- Owner of a business employing 5 or fewer full- or part-time employees
- Located in any of the 50 United States, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico
- Committed to completing the full program
- Have a business bank account

Name: Fifteen Percent Pledge AI Illumination Grant
Description: Offers a share of a $35,000 grant pool to two Black-owned businesses ($20k for winner and $15k for runner-up). Applicants must attend educational webinars on how to use AI for business growth before applying.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Attend a minimum of 1 of 2 webinars
- Member of the Fifteen Percent Pledge's Business Equity Community
E-commerce business in any category selling a unique physical product
- Black-owned: At least one self-identifying Black person with 50% or more equity in the company
- Between 1-15 employees, including the founder
- There is no minimum revenue requirement for this grant

Name: Creative Business Boost Initiative
Description: Offers $5,000 grants and access to a coaching program for 100 creative entrepreneurs, supporting growth through capital, education, and community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, you must be an entrepreneur who is the leading executive (i.e. Founder) of a small business that meets the below business criteria:
- A legal resident of one of the fifty United States, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico
- Eighteen (18) years of age or older (19 in AL and NE)

Other eligibility criteria includes: 
- Must be a creative entrepreneur (see application link for more details)
- Must have a business that has been in operation for at least 12 months 
- Must have an existing product or service currently on the market
- Must be willing to participate in an 8-week virtual business Boost Camp
- Being a for-profit business located and registered in one of the fifty United States, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico
Industry: Apparel & Accessories,Arts & Crafts,Beauty & Personal Care,Food & Beverage,Film & Media,Retail

Name: BOTOX® Cosmetic Confidence Project
Description: An initiative supporting women entrepreneurs with expert training, mentorship, and access to a vibrant business network; 20 participants will each receive a $20,000 grant to help scale their businesses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, a small business owner must be:
- An entrepreneur who is the leading executive (i.e. Founder and/or President, CEO, CFO, COO, or any other similar title) of a business that meets the below business criteria; and
- Eighteen (18) years of age or older (19 in AL and NE).

To be eligible, a business must be:
- A for-profit business located and registered in one of the fifty United States, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico.

Preference will be given to female entrepreneurs.

Name: Amazon Business Small Business Grants
Description: Awards over $250,000 in grants and prizes to 15 U.S.-based small businesses with under $1M in revenue; includes up to $25,000 in funding, Amazon devices, Business Prime memberships, and business consultations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Contest opens on May 1, 2025.

Eligibility:
