- Open to legal residents of the 50 United States and the District of Columbia who at the time of application (i) are the older of 18 years of age or the legal age of majority in their state of residence; and (ii) are an existing Amazon Business account holder iii) a brand owner of a small sized business; iv) should complete the application in full and enter via the entry form on the grant landing page and v) with an annual revenue of $1 million or less headquartered in the United States (“Eligible Business”). - This Contest is not open to independent contractors, or immediate family members (spouses, domestic partners, parents, grandparents, siblings, children, and grandchildren) or those living in the same household of employees or independent contractors of Amazon.com Services LLC (“Sponsor”), or any entity involved in any aspect of the Contest (including funding, judging or administration), and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, advisors, or advertising/promotion agencies. 
- Participants who have received an Amazon Business Grant in the past will not be eligible to receive a grant through this Contest. Eligible Business may be required to furnish proof of business registration with the US Small Business Administration to be considered for an award. 
- In the event any Eligible Business provides inaccurate information, or does not otherwise meet the eligibility criteria for the Contest, Sponsor reserves the right to disqualify Eligible Business and recover or revoke any applicable awards provided. Sponsor reserves the right to disqualify Eligible Business and recover or revoke any applicable awards provided.

Name: Venmo Small Business Grant
Description: Awards $20,000 grants and mentorship to 10 small businesses with Venmo business profiles, supporting expenses like rent, supplies, marketing, and digital growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Application details for 2025 have not yet been announced.

- Have a U.S. Venmo account and valid business profile on Venmo
- Have less than $50,000 in annual sales
- Have 10 employees or fewer

Name: Stamps.com Small Business Flexibility Grant
Description: Open to U.S.-based professional service businesses (law, finance, healthcare, etc.), this grant supports operational flexibility. All applicants get 2 free months of Stamps.com.

Name: eBay Up & Running Grant
Description: 50 U.S.-based eBay sellers will receive funding and coaching to scale their business.

Name: Pathway to Opportunity Pitch Competition
Description: A pitch competition (formerly known as the National Black Business Pitch) that connects small businesses with corporations seeking innovative suppliers, aiming to foster long-term partnerships and expand supply chain opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To apply for the Pathway to Opportunity competition:
- The owner or co-owner of the company must be at least 21 years of age.
- The company featured in the pitch must be at least 51% owned, operated, and controlled by U.S.-based entrepreneurs.
- The applicant must be the owner, founder, CEO, or controlling shareholder of a company that has been operating for at least three months and agree to the competition guidelines.
- Complete the application and submit your pitch video by June 9, 2025.

Name: New York StartUP! Business Plan Competition
Description: The New York Public Library's Thomas Yoseloff Business Center runs an annual business plan competition, sponsored by Wells Fargo, for start-up-phase founders in Manhattan, the Bronx and Staten Island. Entrants attend an orientation and four virtual training workshops, meet with a business librarian and a business advisor, then submit a full business plan for judging. Cash prizes are awarded to the top three plans.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- 18 years or older to win a cash prize
- The proposed business must operate in Manhattan, The Bronx, or Staten Island
- All applicants and team members must be legal residents or U.S. citizens; the individual applicant or team leader must have legal residence in Manhattan, The Bronx, or Staten Island
- START-UPS ONLY: businesses that have earned more than $10,000 in revenue are NOT eligible
- For-profit businesses only; nonprofits cannot enter
- One entry per person, as an individual or as part of one team
- Must attend an online orientation session
- Must attend all four virtual training workshops (run June through September)
- Must meet at least once with an NYPL business librarian, and at least once with a business advisor
- NYPL and Wells Fargo employees and their family members are ineligible
- Finalists must provide a prior-year tax return and a New York State driver's license or non-driver ID

2025 CYCLE (most recent confirmed): entry form due 11:59 PM June 10, 2025; business plan due 11:59 PM September 9, 2025. The Deadline field holds the ENTRY deadline, since that is the point after which you can no longer join.

Prizes of $15,000 / $10,000 / $7,500 are from the 2024 cycle page; the 2025 rules page does not restate them. Contact: startup@nypl.org

Name: BGE Energizing Small Business Grants
Description: Offers $20,000 grants to small businesses in central Maryland, helping them grow and thrive; open to existing BGE electric and/or gas customers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must be a for-profit business and an existing BGE electric and/or gas customer in good standing with BGE. Other eligibility criteria include:
- Be a for-profit business that has been operating for at least one (1) year at the start of the application
- Existing BGE electric and/or gas customer in good standing with BGE
- In good standing (or on the way to) with the State of Maryland
- A maximum of twenty-five (25) full-time employees
- Annual gross revenues in 2024 of less than $7 million USD
- Demonstrated need for funding to support business and serve customers

Name: Cécred x BeyGOOD Salon & Barbershop Business Grants
Description: 37 grants available for salon and barbershop owners committed to community and craft.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements: 

Minimum of 2 years of experience as a licensed barber, hairstylist, or cosmetologist
Demonstrated financial hardship
Proof of salon or barbershop business ownership or a lease agreement for a salon, suite, booth, or chair
In business for at least 1 year

Name: REI Embark Program
Description: A virtual accelerator for early-stage entrepreneurs of color focused on outdoor or wellness innovation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Check out our application criteria:

You have a business idea at the design or prototype stage and are serious about turning it into a company in the next six months OR you've started your company in the last year but haven't yet done manufacturing and have made less than <$20k revenue.
You are building a product, service, or experience that inspires and equips people in their lives outside including gear, apparel, furniture, mobile app, website, e-commerce, retail, outdoor experience, service, food and beverage, skincare, etc.
You identify as a person of color from the Black, Indigenous, Latina/o/x, Asian American and Pacific Islander communities.
You are based in the United States (US Citizenship is not required) and you are at least 18 years old.
Industry: Food & Beverage,Apparel & Accessories,Retail,Beauty & Personal Care,Consumer Packaged Goods,Climate & Sustainability

Name: Progressive Driving Small Business Forward Grant
Description: For businesses needing commercial vehicles – can be used toward purchase and operating expenses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify, you or your business must:

Be the leading executive of a for-profit U.S.-based business (excluding U.S. territories)
Have 10 or fewer employees
Generate less than $5M in annual gross revenue
Demonstrate a clear need for a commercial vehicle to operate and grow your business
Not be an independent contractor whose primary work is in rideshare or food delivery services

Name: Tailor Operations Resilience Grant
Description: Open to businesses affected by supply chain shifts or policy changes (like new tariffs). This grant supports creative solutions and adaptability.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applications are open to independent U.S.-based ecommerce and omnichannel retailers that made at least $1 million in annual revenue in 2024 and are planning or currently undergoing supply chain transformation in 2025.

We encourage brands in verticals most affected by the new tariffs — like home goods, apparel, electronics, beauty, and custom-made products — to apply.

These requirements reflect the unique type of company that we serve because they usually indicate operational complexity and are typically underserved in the software tool market.
Industry: Beauty & Personal Care,Apparel & Accessories,Consumer Packaged Goods

Name: Google Data Center Community AI Fellowship
Description: Supports local leaders using AI to address community challenges. Includes instruction, individual mentorship, and networking.

Name: SoFi Small Business Big Dreams Sweepstakes
Description: Five business owners will win funding for business expenses. Open to businesses of all types.

Name: Honeycomb Celebration Grant
Description: This grant is open to all small business owners and entrepreneurs, regardless of industry, location, or stage of business.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This grant is open to all small business owners and entrepreneurs, regardless of industry, location, or stage of business. 
If you're building a business with intention and vision—and $2,500 would help you reach your next milestone—you should apply.

We welcome:

Brick-and-mortar or online businesses
Product- or service-based entrepreneurs
Creatives, consultants, makers, and founders across all sectors
Founders from all backgrounds and communities

Name: gener8tor Great Lakes Innovation Accelerator
Description: Accelerator for water tech startups in the Great Lakes region.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All women and minority business owners are eligible.

Name: Mindful Founders Micro-Grant
Description: Emergency funding + mental wellness support for entrepreneurs of all types – including nonprofits.

Name: Global Good Fund Fellowship
Description: A 12-month hybrid fellowship for social entrepreneurs worldwide. Includes executive coaching, mentorship from C-suite leaders, a $10K grant for leadership development, and access to training, tools, and a global network.

Name: Zachary’s Jewelers Small Business Grant
Description: Open to small businesses in Anne Arundel County and surrounding areas in Maryland. Focuses on community impact, employee care, and “people-first” values.

Name: gener8tor Electrify Nevada
Description: $100K investment and mentorship for six high-growth startups in Nevada. The Electrify Nevada Accelerator supports visionary founders pioneering the future of sustainable energy and circular economy solutions. We support innovative entrepreneurs with groundbreaking technologies to accelerate their path to scale-up in Nevada, a state at the forefront of renewable energy and next-gen battery production.

Name: LabStart Fellowship
Description: Supports early-stage climate tech founders with $100k milestone-based funding, 12-months of training, access to networks and technology.

Name: Maude’s Ventures Grant
Description: Seed funding for innovative, scalable ideas that improve care for those living with dementia and Alzheimer’s. Open to nonprofits, for-profits, and individuals seeking early funding to bring new solutions to life.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits, for-profits, and individuals. If an individual is chosen for Maude’s Ventures, they may be asked to create an LLC or similar entity to be the recipient of the investment

Name: Honeycomb x Sengo Spark Grant
Description: For small business owners building bold businesses. Funds can cover essentials like rent, hiring, or a new product launch.

Name: 43North Accelerator
Description: Offers $1M investments (in exchange for 5% equity) and a year-long accelerator program for seed-stage startups. Includes mentorship, resources, and relocation to Buffalo, NY to scale in a vibrant entrepreneurial community.

Name: Grid110 LA Launchpad
Description: A 10-week program by Grid110 for early-stage LA-based startups. Includes business training, mentorship, and community support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Companies must be based in LA, with an interest in growing and connecting with the LA ecosystem.

Name: Muskegon Innovation Hub Grant
Description: The Muskegon Innovation Hub is awarding funds to support small businesses and entrepreneurs disproportionately impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. As part of the funding received, the Hub will award one-time direct grants to eligible small businesses. For the next round of funding, there will be thirteen (13) awards of $5,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small businesses served by our Program must meet specific eligibility requirements. Each business must qualify as Disproportionately Impacted by COVID-19 and have received services or participated in programming at the Hub within the last 6 months. To qualify as Disproportionately Impacted by COVID-19, a business must be at least one of the following:

Minority-owned
SEDI-owned
Geographically located (either business or personal address) in the following areas:        
2015 CDFI Investment Tract
2020 Qualified Census Tract
Rural Michigan Counties
Demonstrate a disproportionate negative impact because of COVID-19

An applicant must have also participated in an eligible program or service at the Hub within the previous six months. Eligible programs/ services include:

Business Coaching/ Consulting
Co-Launch Member
Workshop/ Seminar attendance (ex. Social Marketing Mondays)     
Initial Hub Intake/ Meeting
Other (please specify)

Name: Rémy Martin This is My City Grant
Description: Supports emerging creatives — artists, DJs, designers, cultural entrepreneurs — making a cultural and economic impact in their communities. Includes funding and one-on-one mentorship to scale their vision.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, a small business owner must be:
- An entrepreneur who is the leading executive (i.e. Founder and/or President, CEO, CFO, COO, or any such other similar title) of a business that meets the below business criteria; and
- Twenty-one (21) years of age or older

To be eligible, a business must be:
- A for-profit business located in the United States or Washington D.C

Name: digitalundivided Do You Fellowship
Description: For post-revenue tech-based businesses led by women of color. Includes cohort learning, tailored mentorship, and access to funding readiness tools.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'-  Must be 18 years of age or older.
-  Must have been registered in a U.S. state or territory and actively operating for at least one year.
-  The business must be for-profit.
-  Must be in the post-revenue stage, with a minimum annual revenue of $250,000 or have raised at least $150,000 in funding.
-  The founder must be the majority owner (at least 51%) of the business.
-  The business must be tech-based or innovatively incorporate technology into its business model, products, or services.
-  Must be poised for growth and actively seeking investment to scale.
-  Founders are required to share how and in what way inclusion in this program will disrupt inequities in the entrepreneurial ecosystem or investment landscape in which they operate, or in which digitalundivided operates.

Name: 100+ Accelerator
Description: Global accelerator backed by AB InBev, Coca-Cola, Colgate-Palmolive, Danone, Mondelēz, and Unilever. Funds and pilots sustainability solutions from startups to scale across global supply chains and drive impact toward the UN SDGs.

Name: CitizensNYC Community Leaders Grant
Description: Microgrants for resident-led grassroots or nonprofit groups across all five NYC boroughs, supporting neighborhood-level initiatives and leadership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must meet the following criteria to be considered for a Community Leaders Grant:

They must live in one of New York City’s five boroughs.

Their group or project must be “community-oriented,” meaning it currently has, or will have, two or more volunteers associated with it.

Their group or project must not be profit-generating. They must be nonprofits or grassroots volunteer groups.

Their group or project must have a budget of less than $250,000 (schools and school programs are exempt).

Their group or project must not an affiliate or chapter of a larger organization.

Their group or project cannot promote religious, political, or any other ideology.

Name: Builders + Backers
Description: A no-cost national accelerator for aspiring entrepreneurs at the idea stage—no business plan or experience needed. Choose between a structured virtual cohort or a flexible, self-paced AI-powered track. Includes expert coaching, real-time support, and opportunities to receive non-dilutive capital to bring your idea to life.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who can apply?
- Anyone in the U.S. with a novel idea who is 18 years or older. 
- You don’t need a business plan, pitch deck, or startup experience — just an entrepreneurial idea and the drive to explore it.

Name: Backing Small Business (supported by AmEx)
Description: Grants for U.S.-based small businesses to fund projects that promote sustainable growth, build long-term resilience, and boost local impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Businesses must meet the following criteria to apply:
The applicant must be an owner of the business.
The applicant must be at least 18 years of age or older.
The business must be in a ​“bricks-and-mortar” location and operate in an older or historic main street, downtown, or commercial district in the United States. The business must have occupied their current bricks-and-mortar location since January 1, 2025. (Home-based businesses, even those located in historic neighborhoods, are not eligible. Brick and mortar businesses located outside of historic downtowns and commercial corridors, including, but not limited to, office parks and shopping malls are also not eligible.)
The business must be an independent business and not part of a franchise or a nonprofit.
The business must employ 20 or fewer full-time employees.
The business must have been in operation on or before January 1, 2024.
The business must be a business entity in good standing in the state in which it was formed and the state in which it does business.
The business must have an active business license, if required by state or local government. (Applicants may be asked to provide documentation if selected.) · The business must not have received a Backing Small Businesses grant in any previous cycle, nor received a grant supported by American Express in 2025 (including the Backing Small Business Disaster Recovery Grant Program)

Name: NHE3 Small Business Grant Program (New Haven Equitable Entrepreneurial Ecosystem)
Description: Funded by a $7.2M grant from the Connecticut DECD, this program aims to build a more equitable and resilient small business ecosystem in Greater New Haven. Eligible New Haven-based for-profit businesses can access grants, technical assistance, and consulting support through local entrepreneurial support organizations (ESOs).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for the grant, the answers to the following questions must be “yes”. As part of the application, you will be asked to submit documentation as proof of your eligibility: 
Have you been in business for at least one year (as of the date of your application submission) with a record of sales? If a startup, please indicate on application
Does your business have a record of annual sales/revenue in the last twelve months greater? 
Is your business registered in CT? 
Is your business located in New Haven County, CT?
Is your business in good standing with the CT Department of Revenue Services?
Does your business have an established business checking account? 
Does your business utilize formal digital bookkeeping/financial (e.g., QuickBooks, Sage, FreshBooks, Wave Accounting)? 
Is the business a for profit business?
Is the business owned by a person at least 18 years old?

Name: Andreessen Horowitz Talent x Opportunity (TxO) Accelerator
Description: Supports culturally rooted startups with capital and community. Offers $175K in exchange for 7% equity. Open to U.S.-based founders lacking traditional access to funding networks.

Name: Prose Emerging Entrepreneurs Grant
Description: The Prose Emerging Entrepreneurs Grant, presented in partnership with Ellis Brooklyn, offers a $10,000 grant and mentorship opportunities to support Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AANHPI) entrepreneurs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be Asian American, Native Hawaiian, or Pacific Islander

Name: City of Charlotte Creative Growth Grants
Description: Up to $25,000 in public arts funding for Charlotte-based individual artists and cultural organizations across disciplines.

Name: Commercial Tenant Improvement Program (CTIP)
Description: Provides grants of up to $20,000 to small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that are relocating to, opening, or expanding within Cincinnati. Funds can be used for fixed asset improvements to commercial interiors and up to 10% for soft costs like architectural or engineering fees.

Name: Build in Tulsa Product Pitch Night
Description: An 8-week program for early-stage physical product entrepreneurs to refine their business model, market-readiness, and product strategy. It culminates in a live pitch competition offering up to $36K in non-dilutive funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- The startup must be based in Tulsa, OK.
- Must be a tech or tech-enabled startup in the idea or early stage of development (less than 5 years old).

Name: MaesaMagic Incubator
Description: An incubator program for early-stage beauty and wellness entrepreneurs from underrepresented communities. Backed by Maesa’s legacy of building scalable consumer brands, the program provides $35K in funding along with strategic mentorship and support.

Name: Business by the Bay Pitch Competition
Description: Hosted by the Michigan SBDC, this live pitch event offers small business owners and entrepreneurs in Bay County the chance to pitch their business, gain skills through in-person workshops, and compete for $11k in cash prizes.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is eligible to apply?
- Entrepreneurs, Small Business Owners, and early-stage companies based in/principal location in Bay County, MI.
- Existing businesses must be less than two years old (as of November 13, 2025) with less than $1 million in annual sales. The business start date will be determined by the filing date of the entity formation (DBA, LLC, partnership, corporation, etc.)
- The principal owner of the business must be at least 16 years of age at the time of application.
Note: Non-profits, Marijuana business ventures, loan packaging, gambling, investment or lending, or where the owner is on parole are ineligible. Businesses who have won a cash prize in a previous Business by the Bay Pitch event are also ineligible.

Name: STREETS Global Award
Description: Recognizes mission-driven businesses, nonprofits, and NGOs in hospitality or tourism that are creating positive change through social impact, innovation, and sustainability. Open to organizations in their first 1–5 years of operation.

Name: Simply Hermosa Microgrant
Description: Microgrants for woman-owned businesses in Southern Arizona to support startup costs, business growth, marketing, or other operational needs. Designed to empower women entrepreneurs and strengthen values-driven local enterprises.

Name: BankHER Grant
Description: The BankHER Grant, powered by Her Texas' new funding initiative, is designed to help women entrepreneurs take the next step in their business. Grants can be used for equipment, marketing, inventory, customer experience, or professional development, with the goal of making capital access the norm for women-owned businesses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Business must be following the Instagram pages of BankHER
(@bankhercircle) and Her RGV (@her.rgv)
The grant is open to for-profit corporations, partnerships, LLP, LLC, sole
proprietorships and nonprofit organizations.
Business owner must be 18 years old or older.
Business must be based in the Rio Grande Valley region.
Business must be currently operating — no idea-only or concept-stage
businesses.
51% directly owned and/or controlled by one or more women.
Must have been in business for at least 6 months.
Must have less than $500,000 in annual revenue (BankHER focus is small
business).
Must be able to show how the grant will help your business grow (in simple
terms — no full business plan required).
Must agree to share your story with BankHER if you win, so we can inspire
others.

Name: Carbon 2 Value Initiative Accelerator
Description: A six-month program for global startups developing carbontech solutions, offering a $10K stipend, expert mentorship, and access to networks. The program targets innovations in carbon conversion, carbon capture, carbon sequestration/removal, and enabling hardware technologies. In-person participation is required for events in Boston, New York, and Houston.

Name: Carolinas Beyond Open Small Business Grants
Description: Beyond Open is a competitive small business grant program centered on building economic mobility in the Charlotte community including diverse-owned (minority, woman, veteran, LGBTQ, persons with disabilities) small businesses located in the Corridors of Opportunity, as designated by the City of Charlotte.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: More details about eligibility: https://www.beyondopenclt.com/learn#eligibility

Name: Blueprint Breakthrough Grant
Description: $5,000 flexible funding for for-profit businesses in operation 2 years or less. Open to all industries. Funds can be used for equipment, marketing, or any business need.

Name: Boettcher Foundation Community Connection Grants
Description: Community Connections Grants provide one-time funding of $20,000–$75,000 for initiatives and infrastructure projects that strengthen community ties. Colorado-based nonprofit organizations are eligible to apply. Funding often supports construction of multi-use facilities, shared nonprofit spaces, or strategic investments that expand successful initiatives. Applications are accepted three times per year.

Name: Columbia Small Business Grant
Description: This grant supports both new and existing businesses in Columbia, MO looking to expand, innovate, or improve efficiency. Priority is given to business owners living in economically disadvantaged areas of Columbia, with the goal of boosting local economic sustainability and community impact.

Name: Fast Forward Accelerator
Description: Fast Forward Accelerator supports tech nonprofit founders with funding, mentorship, and community to help scale their impact. Since 2014, the program has supported 100+ tech nonprofits, offering access to capital, networks, and long-term resources for growth.

Name: Distilled Intelligence Pitch Competition
Description: Open to founders at any stage and sector building disruptive technologies in large markets. $1M in prize funding available as investments via modified SAFEs. Applications require a pitch deck and company details, reviewed on a rolling basis (early applications prioritized). Event focuses on high-impact networking and pitching without heavy pre-event requirements.

Name: Purina Petcare Innovation Prize
Description: Purina Petcare Innovation Prize recognizes early-stage companies shaping the future of pet care with innovative products and services. Five winners will each receive a spot in a collaborative business bootcamp with Purina leaders, the chance to pitch at Global Pet Expo, access to the PCI Network of pet industry innovators, and visibility with investors and influencers. Winners will compete for a Grand Prize of up to $50,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The competition is open to any business entity selling products or services that meet the criteria contained in these FAQ, as long as they are willing to abide by the conditions called out in these FAQ and on the application, and they are legally able to travel and work in the US – EXCEPT employees and contractors of Nestlé Purina and/or Active Capital, and current NPPC Suppliers who are all ineligible.

Name: digitalundivided BREAKTHROUGH Program
Description: digitalundivided’s BREAKTHROUGH Program, sponsored by JPMorgan Chase & Co, helps established founders grow their businesses through funding, mentorship, and community. Each selected company receives a $5,000 grant, business advisory support, and access to growth strategies, customer insights, and networking opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
In order to qualify for the program, founders must:
 - Be 18 years of age or older
- Have a business registered for at least a year
- Have a majority ownership of an established business with traction
- Have a technology component incorporated in business (website or mobile app)
- Generate a minimum of $50,000 annual business revenue

Name: South Side Civic Scopeathon
Description: Hosted at the University of Chicago’s Keller Center on Nov 8–9, 2025, this free two-day event connects Chicago nonprofits, small public offices, and social entrepreneurs with UChicago graduate students to scope out data and technology-driven solutions to civic challenges. Unlike a traditional hackathon, Scopeathon focuses on creating customized project plans—from data collection tools to impact measurement systems and database designs. Nonprofits leave with actionable strategies and connections to ongoing student consulting resources and university programs.

Name: Poker Power x IFW $100k "Power Play" Small Business Grant
Description: Poker Power is partnering with IFundWomen to launch a $100,000 small business grant. Ten finalists will be selected to pitch in NYC on November 18, 2025, competing for the $100K award plus 6 months of IFundWomen coaching, 4 Poker Power mentorship sessions, and a 4-week poker course.

Name: Impact Accelerator – SEED SPOT
Description: SEED SPOT's accelerator program for diverse entrepreneurs provide underrepresented founders with tailored support, expert guidance, and funding connections to build sustainable businesses that tackle society's most pressing challenges. Runs October 17–December 5.

Name: Foot Locker Foundation Community Empowerment Program
Description: Grants up to $100,000 for nonprofits in 14 U.S. cities focused on youth programs or capital improvement projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This funding opportunity is open to 501c3 nonprofit organizations that: 

Serve youth in low-to-moderate income communities where support and opportunity are scarce.
Deliver programs and services to connect youth to mentorship, education, career development, and health services.
Have an organizational budget of $5 million or less.
Maintain at least one full-time staff person focused on youth programming. 
Can engage local Foot Locker store team members in volunteer activities tied to the proposed program.
Operate in low-to-moderate income communities within the following 14 cities: Atlanta, GA; Baltimore, MD; Chicago, IL; Dallas, TX; Detroit, MI; Houston, TX; Los Angeles, CA; New York City, NY; Newark, NJ; Oakland, CA; Philadelphia, PA; San Francisco, CA; Tampa, FL; and Washington, DC.

Name: Boettcher Foundation Rural Catalyst Grants
Description: The Rural Catalyst Grant Program supports rural Colorado organizations with capacity-building funds to advance community and regional goals. Grants range from $1,000–$10,000 and can be used for strategic planning, convenings, short-term staffing, one-time operating costs, and other projects. Eligible focus areas include affordable housing, childcare, mental health, placemaking, immigrant and refugee support, rural water management, and more.

Name: Boettcher Foundation Doers & Difference Makers Fellowship
Description: The Doers & Difference Makers Fellowship is a nine-month program that supports 10–12 Colorado community leaders each year with training, coaching, and resources to expand their impact. Fellows participate in over 60 hours of in-person and virtual sessions on adaptive leadership, boundary setting, feedback, networking, and more, while also receiving one-on-one coaching. At the end of the program, fellows may apply for a $10,000 professional development award to further their growth and long-term community impact.

Name: Catalyst by Beemok Pitch Competition
Description: Catalyst by Beemok is a new pitch competition and entrepreneurship showcase for founders across Charleston’s Tri-county (Berkeley, Charleston, Dorchester). The program culminates in a live event on November 8, 2025, where up to $1M in potential funding will be awarded. Beyond funding, Catalyst offers exposure, networking, mentorship, and investor connections for both competitors and attendees.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Catalyst Applicant Criteria:
- Entrepreneurs who live and work in Berkeley, Charleston or Dorchester County
- Startups that are in the early stages and require meaningful capital to unlock their next phase of growth
- Applicants do not need to be revenue-generating, though early sales, customer validation, or evidence of traction is strongly preferred.

Name: Square Cornerstone Grant
Description: Square Cornerstone Grant supports small businesses with both funding and expert guidance. Four selected U.S.-based businesses will each receive a $10,000 grant, plus a year of mentorship from top professionals in finance and wellness, and additional visibility through Square’s newsletters and social channels. Eligible applicants must be current Square sellers with at least 6 months of transactions, fewer than 20 employees, and under $2M in annual revenue.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Current Square seller, with at least 6 months of ongoing transactions
- US based business with fewer than 20 employees
- Must qualify as a small business under SBA guidance and have a gross annual revenue under $2M
- Applicants must be legal US residents and their business must not currently be in bankruptcy or named as a defendant in an active lawsuit

Name: REDF Accelerator
Description: The REDF Accelerator is a 6-month applied learning program for leaders of employment social enterprises (ESEs) to grow revenue, expand impact, and strengthen employee support services. Each enterprise applies with two leaders who participate in 100+ hours of peer-based learning, coaching, and consulting to address real-world challenges. Graduates leave with a tailored implementation plan and receive a $20,000 unrestricted grant (2026 cohort) along with access to REDF’s national community of 200+ ESEs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See more details about eligibility here: https://redf.org/accelerator/eligibility/

Name: HuCapital Pitch Competition
Description: As part of HuCapital Innovation Week in NYC, early-stage U.S.-based tech founders (with a functional MVP) can pitch live for a chance to win $5,000, a VC consultation with sponsor Visible Hands, and recognition on the SEEN 50 list. Preference goes to startups with AI functionality.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Founder Requirement: Applicants must be the founder or co-founder of the startup.
- Business Focus: Must pitch a tech company. Preference goes to companies with some type of AI functionality. Open to industries such as media, finance, healthcare, beauty, consumer, and technology.
- Company Stage: Open to early-stage founders with at least a functional MVP (minimum viable product).
- Geography: Applicants must be based in the United States.
- Use of Funds: The award must be applied toward product development, marketing, operations, or another key area of growth.
- Legal Entity: Applicants must have a registered business entity (LLC, C-Corp, etc.).

Name: Fifteen Percent Pledge Runway to Revenue Accelerator
Description: The Runway to Revenue Accelerator, powered by Victoria’s Secret & Co., is a 12-week virtual program designed to help BIPOC and women-owned businesses — or companies aligned with the Fifteen Percent Pledge — scale and grow. Participants receive $10,000 in grant funding, expert-led workshops on scaling and strategy, networking opportunities, and the chance to pitch for up to $50,000 in additional funding at the program’s final pitch event in Columbus, OH.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Member of the Fifteen Percent Pledge's Business Equity Community, brands MUST sign up and submit full business details to enter the award application
- Business has an annual revenue of at least $100,000 and no more than $1,500,000
- At least one self-identifying person with 51% or more equity in the company identifies as BIPOC and/or woman or business shows a demonstrated commitment to Fifteen Percent Pledge's mission
- Business must be operational for at least 1 year
- Business must sell an intimates, apparel, accessories, activewear/sport, shapewear or hosiery product
- Business must be available to participate in the twelve-week accelerator program outlined below
- Business must be able to willing to travel and attend the in-person pitch competition in Columbus, OH at the close of the program
- Business must be US-based

Name: Johns Hopkins Social Innovation Lab
Description: The Social Innovation Lab (SIL) supports early-stage ventures from Johns Hopkins and the greater Baltimore community that are mission-driven and have demonstrated traction. Participants join a cohort-based program focused on customer discovery, fundraising, impact measurement, storytelling, and more, while gaining access to a broad mentor and funder network. Teams that complete the program receive a $5,000 grant stipend and can compete for a $15,000 prize.

Name: Madeline Haydon Award for Entrepreneurship
Description: Two $10,000 awards will be given to promising CPG entrepreneurs. The award supports entrepreneurs whose vision and leadership demonstrate strong growth potential and alignment with Project Potluck’s mission of advancing diversity and inclusion in the industry.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Project Potluck Grant Program is open to all eligible entrepreneurs, regardless of background, and aims to support a diverse range of founders and business models. 

- Founders of U.S.-based CPG brands currently in market (DTC, retail, or foodservice)
- Applicants must have at least 51% ownership of the business they represent
- Business must be active and have demonstrated traction (e.g., sales, partnerships, retail placement)
- Applicants must be able to clearly articulate how the grant would accelerate their business growth

Name: Once Upon a Farm Brand Builder Grant
Description: One $10,000 grant will be awarded to a CPG entrepreneur with demonstrated innovation, with priority given to businesses headquartered in the Midwest. The grant is designed to accelerate growth for founders building impactful, inclusive brands.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Project Potluck Grant Program is open to all eligible entrepreneurs, regardless of background, and aims to support a diverse range of founders and business models. 

- Founders of U.S.-based CPG brands currently in market (DTC, retail, or foodservice)
- Applicants must have at least 51% ownership of the business they represent
- Business must be active and have demonstrated traction (e.g., sales, partnerships, retail placement)
- Applicants must be able to clearly articulate how the grant would accelerate their business growth

Name: Baked Goods Innovation Award
Description: One $5,000 grant will be awarded to a brand in the baked goods or baking ingredients category. Priority will be given to founders whose businesses show strong traction and potential for growth while advancing representation and inclusion in CPG.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Project Potluck Grant Program is open to all eligible entrepreneurs, regardless of background, and aims to support a diverse range of founders and business models. 

- Founders of U.S.-based CPG brands currently in market (DTC, retail, or foodservice)
- Applicants must have at least 51% ownership of the business they represent
- Business must be active and have demonstrated traction (e.g., sales, partnerships, retail placement)
- Applicants must be able to clearly articulate how the grant would accelerate their business growth

Name: OpenAI Fund for US Nonprofits
Description: OpenAI has launched a $50M fund to support U.S.-based nonprofits and community organizations using AI to expand access, improve services, and foster innovation in areas like education, economic opportunity, healthcare, and community-led research. Grants will be unrestricted and open to both established and emerging nonprofits, including those new to AI.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) NONPROFITS ONLY - for-profit businesses are not eligible. Operating budget over $500K and under $10M; 50 states plus DC.

Name: Echoing Green Fellowship
Description: Echoing Green backs transformational leaders advancing equity across education, climate justice, human rights, health, and more. Fellows receive $100,000 in seed funding over 18 months, along with leadership development, wellness and mental health resources, and expert professional support. They also gain access to Echoing Green’s lifelong global community of innovators, virtual and in-person convenings, and connections to business leaders committed to social change.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See more eligibility requirements here: https://echoinggreen.org/fellowship/apply/

Name: Black Girl Ventures NYC Pitch Competition
Description: The Black Girl Ventures (BGV) 2025 Pitch Program supports early-stage, revenue-generating businesses under $1M led by under-resourced founders in NYC. The program provides coaching, a live crowdfunded pitch competition, and connections to a network of professionals, helping founders access capital, grow capacity, and build community. Awards include: $15,000 for 1st place, $10,000 for 2nd, $5,000 for 3rd. Winners also receive membership to the BGV Connect Incubator.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered for this program, applicants must be :
- Revenue generating
- In good standing
- Located in the city you're applying
 
Ideal Candidate Profile:
- Candidates that have personal values that are in alignment with BGV’s mission and purpose.
- Candidates that exhibit good decision making skills and conduct themselves in an ethical manner that reflects BGV Core Values.

Name: SheaMoisture Dartmouth 2025 Fellowship
Description: The SheaMoisture 2025 Fellowship, in partnership with Tuck Executive Education at Dartmouth, Luminary, and the Fifteen Percent Pledge, will select 10 women-owned small businesses across the U.S. for an immersive entrepreneurial development program. Fellows will receive hands-on business education, personalized mentorship, and access to influential networks to help scale their companies. The program includes a five-day, in-person executive education experience at Dartmouth’s Tuck School of Business (Dec 7–12, 2025), with accommodation covered and up to $500 in travel reimbursement.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Small business with annual revenue between $250,000 and $7,500,000
- Business has a minimum 2-years of operation
- Business is registered in the US or Canada
- Business is at least 50% woman owned
- If accepted, must attend an executive education program on-campus at the Tuck School of Business at Dartmouth College in Hanover, NH in-person from Sunday December 7 through Friday December 12, 2025.

Name: 2025 Alan Hagman Grant
Description: The Alan Hagman Grant awards $6,000 to support photojournalism projects that bring creative attention to important, underreported stories—from human rights to environmental issues. Named in honor of the late Los Angeles Times photo editor and mentor, the grant is administered by the National Press Photographers Foundation (NPPF), which advances visual journalism through education and funding.

Name: NYU Tandon Future Labs Catalyst Accelerator
Description: The NYU Tandon Future Labs Catalyst Program is a 6-month, equity-free accelerator for Pre-Seed to Seed tech startups, offering access to NYU’s research, faculty, and entrepreneurial network. Selected founders receive mentorship, workspace, weekly events, cloud credits (Google Cloud, AWS, Anthropic), startup software discounts, NYU student interns, and publicity opportunities. The program seeks startups tackling major challenges in: AI (Foundational AI, Sensory AI), Hardware & Robotics, Healthcare, Cybersecurity, Communications & Media (AR/VR/MR), Finance, Urban Technology.
Amount: up to $350,000 in-kind (incl. up to $100K AWS/GCP credits)

Name: Mentors + Angels Accelerator
Description: The m+a Accelerator Program is an 8-week hybrid program designed for overlooked and underrepresented founders, with priority given to women, minorities, veterans, and economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs. Participants benefit from the expertise of experienced corporate leaders, entrepreneurs, and investors, as well as access to a strong angel and seed investor network. The program includes three weekly virtual sessions and two in-person events in New York City (networking and pitch). The accelerator is free to join, takes no equity, and culminates in a Demo Day.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The cohort of companies participating in the 2026 the m+a accelerators must be US based, for reasons of logistics. Priority will be given to companies who can easily get to NYC for in-person meetings and mentoring sessions.

Name: The LearningTimes Emerging Educational Filmmaker Grant
Description: The LearningTimes Emerging Educational Filmmaker Grant awards up to $10,000 to U.S.-based emerging filmmakers in the pre-production stage to create films exploring themes of education, teaching, community, and learning. The grant aims to amplify diverse voices and perspectives in conversations about education and its role in society.

Name: 2025 Restaurant Accelerator and Community Fund Grant
Description: The 2025 Restaurant Accelerator & Community Fund Grant, presented by National ACE in partnership with Grubhub, supports small, independent U.S. restaurants seeking growth and long-term success. From October 1–24, 2025, eligible restaurants can apply to join the Restaurant Accelerator program. Those who attend at least three of four virtual sessions in November (Nov. 4, 12, 18, and 25) will qualify for a $5,000 Community Fund Grant to invest in their business. The program especially encourages Asian American and Pacific Islander restaurateurs in economically disadvantaged areas to apply.

Name: City of Champaign New Business and Growing Business Program
Description: The City of Champaign’s New and Growing Business Programs provide reimbursement-based grants to help local small businesses start and expand, with a focus on supporting minority- and women-owned enterprises. Awardees receive up to $20,000 to cover eligible business expenses, contingent on goal-setting with the Small Business Development Center and completion of a detailed business plan. The program emphasizes business readiness through training and technical support rather than upfront funding, fostering sustainable local growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Applicants must be a registered client of the Illinois Small Business Development Center.
- Subject business must operate legally in accordance with all Federal, State, and local laws and regulations, be current with all City taxes, fees, and licenses, and be in good standing with the State of Illinois Secretary of State.
- Subject business may not receive more than $20,000 in small business funding or more than one New or Growing Business award within a five-year period.
- Non-profit organizations, franchise businesses, adult-oriented businesses, liquor stores, cannabis dispensaries, predatory lending, and tobacco/vape shops are not eligible for these programs.

Name: Pegasus Angel Accelerator Lightning Round
Description: The Lightning Round Pitch Competition, hosted by Pegasus Angel Accelerator, showcases bold early-stage founders building breakthrough consumer brands. The top five finalists will pitch live for direct investments of up to $200K each, plus over $1M in perks, media exposure, and entry into the Ignite DTC program powered by Shopline. The winning founder also receives a global press release, newsletter spotlight, and enhanced investor access.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Pre-seed & Seed Stage DTC companies

Name: Ford Foundation JustFilms Application
Description: The JustFilms program by the Ford Foundation provides funding for artist-driven, feature-length documentary films that explore themes of social justice, including gender, race, and disability justice. Grants support projects in development, production, or post-production that demonstrate innovation in storytelling, intersectional representation, and strong alignment with the foundation’s mission.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered for funding, your project must be a documentary feature film (running time of at least 50 minutes) in which the filmmaker/s have creative control. We welcome applications for direct content development, production, or post-production.

The open call does not support student films, narrative films, short films, commissioned films where the filmmaker is not the rights holder to the project, episodic series, new media (AR, VR), podcasts, films that have already premiered or broadcast, or impact or outreach campaigns.

Name: RestorHER x Worth Pursuing Micro-Grant
Description: The RestorHER x Worth Pursuing Micro-Grant Initiative is a collaborative effort designed to empower women entrepreneurs by providing financial support, business development resources, and holistic well-being tools to foster sustainable success. $500 per award.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must be a U.S. resident and at least 21 years old
- Business must be a woman-owned and have 10 or fewer employees
- Business must be a for-profit venture, revenue-generating for at least one year
- Applicant must be the CEO or founder within the company

Name: Black Leaders Detroit Co-Operations Grant Initiative
Description: A grant program by Black Leaders Detroit (BLD) in partnership with Operations School, targeting for-profit businesses owned by persons of African descent in the Detroit area who have been impacted by COVID-19 and have completed certain training programs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be a for-profit business owned by persons of African descent; located in the specified counties; negatively impacted by COVID-19; must have completed training with Operations School or a partner program; must not have received a grant from BLD in the last 12 months.

Name: Hawaiʻi FoundHer
Description: Entrepreneurship program for AANHPI and women-identifying founders in Hawaiʻi, offering mentorship, education, and connections.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Qualification Requirements
- For Profit (structured as an LLC or corporation)
- Proof of Concept (i.e. Sales, Partnerships, Active Users, etc.)
- 51% of FoundHers must be women, of Native Hawaiian, Pacific Islander, or Asian descent, AND based in Hawaiʻi
- Early Stage (under 3 years of existence)
- FoundHers’ values align with our own

Name: ERA VC Pitch Slam
Description: A pitch competition by ERA VC and CPGWire aimed at early-stage CPG founders offering investment and mentorship.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage consumer and CPG brand founders; open to applicants with product/brand in CPG space.

Name: Slauson & Co Winter 2026 Accelerator
Description: A 12-week virtual accelerator by Slauson & Co focused on early-stage, category-defining consumer founders from underrepresented backgrounds to strengthen business, attract investment, and build community.
Amount: $300K funding for 6% via SAFE plus startup discounts/perks
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage founders (especially underrepresented) in consumer or innovation sectors.

Name: Artist Trust Fellowship Awards
Description: Merit-based awards of $10,000 to practicing professional artists of exceptional talent and ability residing in Washington State.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Artists must be 18+, residents of Washington State, individual artists or teams, have not received two or more Fellowship Awards in lifetime.

Name: Huckberry The Dream Year Giveaway
Description: A sweepstakes from Huckberry offering one winner a large cash prize plus travel and store credit to pursue their dream year.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Legal residents of the U.S. (excluding FL & NY) age 18+; see full rules.

Name: Alma Ascent Pitch Competition
Description: A global live pitch competition for immigrant-led early-stage startups, judged by Silicon Valley VCs, offering a prize pool of up to $100,000 and access to mentorship and investor exposure.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage startups (raised < $2M) with at least one immigrant founder; live attendance in Bay Area required.

Name: Safe Space The People's Pitch
Description: Community-centered pitch event where early-stage innovators present ideas for feedback, visibility, and potential funding. Focuses on elevating creators within the Safe Space community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Innovators and creators; participation aligned with event requirements.

Name: Black Girl Ventures LA Pitch Competition
Description: The Black Girl Ventures (BGV) 2025 Pitch Program supports early-stage, revenue-generating businesses under $1M led by under-resourced founders in LA. The program provides coaching, a live crowdfunded pitch competition, and connections to a network of professionals, helping founders access capital, grow capacity, and build community. Awards include: $15,000 for 1st place, $10,000 for 2nd, $5,000 for 3rd. Winners also receive membership to the BGV Connect Incubator.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered for this program, applicants must be :
- Revenue generating
- In good standing
- Located in the city you're applying
 
Ideal Candidate Profile:
- Candidates that have personal values that are in alignment with BGV’s mission and purpose.
- Candidates that exhibit good decision making skills and conduct themselves in an ethical manner that reflects BGV Core Values.

Name: Wells Fargo Woman Evolve Mind Your Business Capital Pitch Competition
Description: Pitch competition supporting women-led businesses with access to capital, mentorship, and exposure. Run in partnership between Woman Evolve and Wells Fargo.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must be a business in operation for a minimum of two years with revenue of at least $25,000 per year. Entrants will need to provide two forms of financials for proof, must have an active US business registration, and a valid EIN number.
- Must be a legal U.S. resident who is 18 years of age or older at the time of entry. 
- Have a Federal EIN Number for the Business Applicant.
- Agree to abide by the contest rules as outlined herein.

Name: Michigan Black Business Alliance Black Wealth Summit Grant
Description: The Black Wealth Summit Grant, presented by the Michigan Black Business Alliance (MBBA) in partnership with BTS and LEAP, invests in Black-owned businesses committed to growth and sustainability. Awarded during the Black Wealth Summit in Lansing, MI, the grant recognizes entrepreneurs who actively participate in the event and demonstrate readiness to scale their ventures. The summit will take place on November 8, 9:30am to 6pm EST at 5660 West Saginaw Highway, Lansing, MI.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Register for the summit: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/black-wealth-summit-tickets-1820210752359

Name: Polsky Small Business Growth Program
Description: The Polsky Small Business Growth Program is a nine-month program that supports small business owners to help them grow and scale their businesses through consulting work completed by top University of Chicago student talent under the direction and support of Booth faculty, Polsky staff and external coaches.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
South and West side business owners seeking to grow their businesses from six figures in annual revenue to over $1M who are seeking to secure larger contracts with corporations and are:
- Ready to make shifts in your business to achieve greater success.
- Seeking to grow your customer base.
- Prepared to spend time to work on your business (and not just in your business), i.e. step away from daily operations to grow the business.
- Able to attend virtual meetings weekly with your dedicated team, and an in-person gathering at the start and close of the program.

Name: Prepshift Bakery Finance Boot Camp 2026
Description: A business education boot camp for growing bakeries and independent food businesses providing coaching in finance, operations, and growth strategies.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Independent bakery or food business owners looking to scale.

Name: The Catalyst Grant
Description: The Catalyst Grant offers $100,000 to help as many as 88 established and growing businesses reach their next stage of development. This grant supports companies looking to expand their workforce, enhance operations, or upgrade facilities, providing the capital needed to scale confidently.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This is a competitive opportunity for businesses that meet all of the following criteria:
- For-profit businesses located in Cook County
- Businesses with at least 1 full-time employee, in addition to the owner (in 2024 and at time of application)
- Businesses with documented revenue between $500,000 and $10 million (in both 2023 and 2024)

- Businesses that operate in one of the following industries:
+Construction
+ Finance and insurance
+ Information technology (IT)
+ Manufacturing
+ Professional services
+ Real estate

- Businesses that can demonstrate evidence of business growth in the following ways:
+ Increase in net income (profit) from 2023 to 2024
+ Increase in full-time employee count between 2023 and 2024

- If awarded, grant funds may be used only for the following expenses:
+ Equipment purchases
+ Facility upgrades
+ Workforce investments

Name: Wherewithal Artist Grants
Description: Wherewithal Grants provide funding for experimental and multidisciplinary visual artists in the Washington, DC area, emphasizing collaboration, research, and artistic discourse. Funded by the Andy Warhol Foundation and managed by the Washington Project for the Arts, the program offers $5,000–$7,500 grants to support research and project presentations.

Name: Black Film Space Emerging Filmmaker Short Film Grant
Description: The Emerging Filmmaker Short Film Grant by Black Film Space offers $3,000 to support a filmmaker creating their first or second short film as writer, director, and producer. Open globally to applicants aged 18+, it seeks bold, original storytelling and diverse perspectives in narrative short films under 20 pages.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
- Applicants must serve as the Writer, Director, and Producer of the proposed short film. Collaborative projects are eligible as long as the applicant is a co-writer, co-director, and co-producer.
- To qualify, applicants cannot have previously completed more than one film in which they served as all three roles — Writer, Director, and Producer (either solo or as a co–writer/director/producer). In other words, you may have written, directed, or produced other films before, but not more than one where you held all three positions at once.
- Your script should be 20 pages or less, not counting the cover page.
Scripts that exceed 20 pages will not be considered.
- Each application must include:
— Screenplay or work-in-progress film (if production has begun) 
— Personal statement
— Production timeline
— Budget
— Optional samples of past video work
- Applicants must submit a narrative short film project. Series and documentaries will not be considered.
- All genres are welcome.
- Applicants may reside anywhere in the world, but must have access to a U.S. bank account to receive grant funds.
- Applicants may submit only one film project.
- Projects that have already completed production are still eligible.
Grant funds may be used toward post-production, festival submissions, or distribution expenses.

Name: FedEx Entrepreneur Fund and Boost Camp Program
Description: The FedEx Entrepreneur Fund and Boost Camp Program, in partnership with Hello Alice and the Global Entrepreneurship Network, offers 150 small business owners a 12-week virtual accelerator focused on business growth, marketing, and financial strategy. Participants gain access to expert-led education, mentorship, and a peer support community, with the opportunity to receive $10,000 in grant funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, a small business owner must be:
- An entrepreneur who is the leading executive (i.e. Founder and/or President, CEO, CFO, COO, or any such other similar title) of a business that meets the below business criteria; and
- Eighteen (18) years of age or older (19 in AL and NE).

Name: Meta Data Center Community Action Grants
Description: Meta’s annual Data Center Community Action Grants program provides direct funding to schools, nonprofits, and community organizations located near Meta data centers. The grants support projects that use technology for community benefit, strengthen local communities, and enhance STEAM education. Applications are open from October 13, 2025, to November 21, 2025, and eligible applicants include U.S. nonprofits and schools, as well as equivalent entities in Europe.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: INTERNATIONAL DATA CENTER COMMUNITIES ONLY - Canada, Denmark, Ireland, Singapore and Sweden. US applicants are NOT eligible and are redirected by Meta to 'The Future is for Everyone Fund'.

Name: Gusto Impact Awards
Description: The Gusto Impact Awards celebrate small businesses making a big difference in their communities – from local cafés to nonprofits changing lives. Across five U.S. regions, winners receive $50,000 in prizes, including cash grants ($10,000), advertising ($40,000), and free payroll service, with over $325,000 awarded nationwide. Thirty small businesses in each region will also receive $500 Visa gift cards.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To enter, your business must:
- Operate in the United States
- Have 75 or fewer employees
- Earn less than $7 million annually
- Have been actively in business for at least one year
- Have an active website and email

Name: 2025 Techsgiving Summit: Small Business & Startup Marketplace
Description: The 2025 Techsgiving Summit in Washington, D.C., will feature a Small Business & Startup Marketplace on December 11–12. Marketplace participants will connect with 4,000+ Summit attendees and potential customers, network with other small business owners, and receive amplification from Techsgiving.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Businesses must have fewer than 50 employees and be in operation for at least one year. Previous participants have represented a wide range of industries, including home decor, beauty, art, IT consulting, and education services.
Application Fee: Selected businesses pay a $600 fee to cover logistics (power, WiFi, 6x6 tables, loading/unloading materials, etc.).

Name: Sephora Beauty Grant
Description: The Sephora Beauty Grant, created in partnership with the Fifteen Percent Pledge, awards one Black-owned beauty business a $100,000 grant to accelerate its growth and visibility. Eligible applicants must be part of the Pledge’s Business Equity Community, have at least $100K in annual revenue, have 51% or more ownership by an underrepresented founder, and have operated for at least a year selling CPG products in categories like skincare, haircare, or makeup.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Member of the Fifteen Percent Pledge's Business Equity Community, brands MUST sign up and submit full business details to enter the award application portal.
- Business sells a product and has annual revenue of at least $100K or more
- Black-owned: At least one self-identifying Black person with 50% or more equity in the company
- Must have been in business for at least 1 year
- Businesses must sell a CPG product:
- Must sell a product in at least one of the following categories: Beauty, Haircare, Makeup / Makeup tools, Skincare, Fragrance, Bath & Body

Name: Start Pivot Grow 90 Day Challenge
Description: The 90-Day Business Growth Challenge offers U.S. businesses free access to the KPIXAI strategy-building platform, expert advising, and national visibility, culminating in the chance to win a $10,000 small business grant. Sponsored by the JPMorgan Chase Foundation, participants use the platform to create a full 2026 growth strategy and complete a final pitch.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible businesses must be U.S.-based, for-profit (or nonprofit), at least 5 years old, earn $250K+ annually, and have at least two employees or contractors.

Name: Makers Future Fund
Description: The Nest Makers Future Fund is a financial readiness and capital access program for U.S.-based maker-entrepreneurs and craft business leaders, providing coaching, peer support, and training to help them reach financial goals and grow. Selected participants receive intensive financial readiness coaching plus a $5,000 “business boost” grant.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants must be located and producing their handcrafted products in the US
- Applicants must use a US bank account for managing their business
- Applicants' businesses must make handcrafted products (i.e., products must be predominantly made by hand, using techniques that involve direct manual effort and craftsmanship). Examples of eligible products include, but are not limited to: textiles, ceramics, jewelry, woodwork, small batch personal care products, etc. 
- While the use of hand tools and electric hand tools are permitted (e.g. heat molds/presses, sewing machines, die-cutting machines, etc.), items produced using industrial machinery or 3D printers are not eligible.
- Have at least one senior team member who can participate throughout the program.
- Be able to dedicate 3-5 hours per week for program participation.
- Be available for weekly live Q&A sessions held 12-1pm EST every Thursday from January-April 2026.
- Be willing and able to share basic accounting records for the past 12 months, if selected.
- Must report more than $15,000 or more in annual revenue for 2024
- Able to share how the $5,000 grant will be utilized for business needs and growth

Name: Latinas in Cannabis Seeds of Change Small Business Grant
Description: Latinas in Cannabis is offering Seeds of Change Small Business Grants for women-owned cannabis businesses and consultancies attending MJBizCon, with applications open through December 4, 2025. Five recipients will each receive $500, and winners will be announced live with a check presentation on December 5 at 12 PM on MJBizCon’s HUB Stage during the Latinas in Cannabis Takeover (a representative must be present). The initiative is sponsor-funded and supports Latinas in cannabis by reducing stigma and creating opportunities for networking, mentorship, and development.

Name: CyberTech|X Accelerator
Description: CyberTech|X Accelerator is a program for early-stage cybersecurity startups, offering strategic support, global connections, and mentorship from a large network of investors, mentors, and industry partners. Participants get warm investor intros, expert coaching, media exposure, major startup perks, and opportunities to pitch and network, with sponsors including groups like Bank of America, EY, and others.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Early-stage startups utilizing proprietary technology to develop cutting-edge cyber products and solutions
- Management team with at least two full-time roles
- Ability to travel to Tampa for a minimum of two visits throughout the program
- Proof of market validation
- Investable, scalable business model
- Well-developed and viable business plan
- Financial stability with a runway of at least 6-12 months

Name: Men Deserve Flowers Prize
Description: The Men Deserve Flowers Prize honors a male founder whose business measurably improves community wellness – physical health, mental well-being, or financial empowerment – especially with meaningful impact on NYC residents (even if the founder isn’t NYC-based). One winner receives a $1,500 microgrant from HuCapital plus a month-long campaign on 50+ LinkNYC digital billboards (total prize valued at $30K+).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify, applicants must meet all baseline requirements:

**Business Type**
- A service-based or online business in industries such as tech, health & wellness, fashion, men’s grooming, food and beverage, productivity, or related sectors.
- A non-franchised brick-and-mortar business located in New York City.

**Focus Areas of Wellness**
Eligible businesses must demonstrate measurable impact in at least one of the following areas:
- Physical health & wellness (i.e. nutrition, fitness, clinical, wearable devices, etc)
- Mental health & wellness (i.e. therapy, productivity tools, meditation apps, etc)
- Financial empowerment (i.e. financial literacy education, investing apps, professional development, etc)
- Liquor- and cannabis-based businesses are not eligible to apply at this time.

**Business Stage**
- Early-stage or growth-stage, defined as:
    - Generating less than $10 million in annual revenue
    - Employing fewer than 50 team members
    - Business must be in operation for at least 1 year

Name: Patrick Leahy Farm to School Grant
Description: The USDA’s FY 2026 Patrick Leahy Farm to School Grant Program provides competitive grants of $100,000–$500,000 (up to $18M total) to increase the use of local foods in Child Nutrition Program meals and connect students to food sources through education like gardens, taste tests, and field trips. Funds can launch or expand farm-to–Child Nutrition Program efforts that combine local procurement with agricultural education to improve child health and strengthen connections between schools and local producers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The following are eligible entities:
- State agencies
- Indian Tribal organizations
- Child Nutrition Program operators*
- Local agencies*
- Agricultural producers*
- Groups of agricultural producers*
- Non-profit organizations*
- All non-profit organizations must include their 501(c)(3) determination letter issued by the Internal Revenue Service.
Note: Under this RFA, all entities marked with an asterisk (*) must be part of a partnership to be eligible to apply.

Organizations applying as any of the entities specified above, but which do not meet the eligibility definitions will be deemed ineligible and removed from competition without further consideration.

For additional information please see the Patrick Leahy Farm to School Grant Program website.

Name: Chasm Momentum Grant
Description: The CHASM Momentum Grant awards one female founder a $25,000 grant to help accelerate her startup’s next stage. It’s aimed at women-led ventures with early traction and a clear plan for how the funding will drive growth, and is judged by Aleen Dreksler, co-founder/CEO of Betches Media.

Name: Workbar's Small Business Grant
Description: Workbar’s Small Business Grant Contest awards one Massachusetts-based small business a $5,000 check plus a year of free unlimited coworking, with additional coworking memberships for two runner-ups (6 months) and the top 10 finalists (3 months).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
For the purposes of this contest, eligible small businesses must meet the following criteria: 
- Applicant is the principal owner of the business
- The business is physically located in or serves Massachusetts 
- Business has been operating for at least 6 months
- Business has an annual revenue of one million dollars ($1,000,000) or less
- Business has 15 or fewer full-time or part-time employees 
- Business has not previously won the Workbar Small Business Grant

Name: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready Grant
Description: After completing two courses on the Verizon platform, small businesses become eligible to access a $10,000 grant application. 50 small businesses will be awarded with $10,000 grants.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who can apply?

Owners of for-profit U.S.-based small businesses. Nonprofits are not eligible. 
Applicants may apply for one business only and must be over the age of 18.
Learn more about the selection process and view the full Terms and Conditions on LISC's website.

Name: Workplace Innovation Now (WIN) Challenge
Description: The Workplace Innovation Now (WIN) Challenge is a $60 million grant initiative led by Aspen Digital and supported by Melinda French Gates’ organization, Pivotal, to scale innovative solutions that help women thrive in a rapidly evolving workplace. The competition focuses on three pillars – Culture & Practices, AI, and Narrative – and will award up to eight grantees per category with $2.5–$5 million each. Its goal is to improve workplace culture, leverage AI for equity, and reshape narratives so all workers, especially women, can succeed.

Name: SKU CPG Accelerator
Description: SKU’s Spring ’26 Track is a 12-week hybrid consumer packaged goods (CPG) accelerator open to market-validated startups nationwide, offering hands-on mentorship from industry experts, investors, and serial entrepreneurs, mostly remote with two in-person events and a final investor showcase pitch. Selected companies trade up to 5% equity for the program’s mentorship, network, and ongoing support, with applications due December 12.

Name: Sonsie x Shopify Mindful Beauty Award
Description: The Sonsie x Shopify Mindful Beauty Award provides $100,000 in resources (cash/credits/prizes), plus mentorship and brand amplification, to help early-stage female-founded beauty and wellness brands grow. Eligible applicants are U.S.-resident female founders with a beauty/wellness store that’s been open less than 12 months or is currently in development.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for the Mindful Beauty Award, applicants must meet the following requirements:
- You are a female founder.
- You are a resident of the U.S.
- You own a store that sells beauty or wellness products.
- Your store has been open for less than 12 months, or you’re currently developing one.

Name: Illinois Grocery Initiative - Equipment Upgrade Grant
Description: Supports independently owned grocery stores in Illinois making energy-efficient equipment upgrades. Open to grocers with <500 employees and ≤4 locations. Stores must accept SNAP/WIC and sell fresh, unprocessed foods.

Name: Hiring Our Heroes’ Small Business Grant Program
Description: Hiring Our Heroes’ Veterans & Military Spouses Small Business Grant Program awards five veteran- or military spouse–owned small businesses one-time grants to help them grow. Four businesses receive $10,000 each and one receives $25,000, funded through the FedEx Founder’s Fund via the Community Foundation of Greater Memphis.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply for the Grant Program, an applicant must be:
- A legal resident of and currently reside in the contiguous 48 states, Alaska and/or Hawaii; and
- A 51% or more owner of a for-profit business owned by an honorably-discharged veteran or military spouse with 3 to 20 employees including the owner, all full or part-time employees, and independent (1099) contractors. For the purposes of this program, veteran or military spouse means:
- any person who previously served in the active duty, National Guard or Reserve components of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force or Coast Guard and has an honorable discharge;
- any person who currently serves in National Guard or Reserve component of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, or Coast Guard; or
- any person who is presently married to a current member of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, Coast Guard, or any National Guard or Reserve components of the military; and
- An owner of a small business with less than $5 million in annual revenue and located in an economically vulnerable community, or the business can otherwise demonstrate financial need brought on by hardship beyond the owner’s control. Economically vulnerable communities are defined as any community in a zip code that receives a “stress score” of 40 or greater, as measured by the Distressed Communities Index.

Name: Global Citizen Cisco Youth Leadership Award
Description: The Global Citizen Prize: Cisco Youth Leadership Award recognizes a 18–30-year-old who has used technology to make a meaningful contribution toward ending extreme poverty. The winner is selected through an application process and the award includes a $250,000 prize paid to the recipient’s organization, with the winner announced at Global Citizen NOW in May 2026 in New York City.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Aged 18-30
- Demonstrated track-record of measurable impact at scale over the last 3-5 years advancing one or more of the Global Goals. 
- Compelling vision and concrete plans for how to extend this work in the next 3-5 years, including how the prize will advance efforts. 
- Inspires other young people to have an impact on achieving one or more of the Global Goals
- Demonstrates the values and embodies the spirit of a Global Citizen and a Global Problem Solver
- Innovates with technology or Internet-based communications to improve efficiency, reach, and magnify impact.

Name: Independent Lens Creator Lab
Description: The Independent Lens Creator Lab is a six-month accelerator for six standout vertical-video storytellers making social-media nonfiction. Participants get up to $36K in production funds, mentorship, and industry support, and will create up to 12 original videos for Independent Lens/PBS social channels. It targets charismatic creators with inclusive, empathetic voices and an engaged Gen Z/millennial audience of roughly 10K–100K followers, with ITVS owning the commissioned videos.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- A U.S. citizen or legal resident of the United States or its external territories and 18 years of age or older. 
- The principal creator of the originally produced content submitted for consideration.
- The principal creator of (1) at least three original YouTube or social media videos with more than 100,000 views per post or (2) at least 10k followers on a single social media account.
- Free to create original commissioned videos for ITVS ownership, with no conflicting third-party agreements.
