- DIGITAL HEALTH & AI: Care delivery, CDS, remote monitoring, and virtual care.
- DEVICES & DIAGNOSTICS: Imaging, digital hardware, and next-gen clinical tools.
- BIOTECH & THERAPEUTICS: Precision medicine, novel therapeutics, and advanced modalities. 
- SYSTEMS INNOVATION: Access, efficiency, mental health, and system transformation.

Name: Brewing The American Dream Bootcamp 2026
Description: Brewing the American Dream Bootcamp 2026 is now accepting applications from eligible food and beverage entrepreneurs in New England, the greater Cincinnati/Covington area, or the greater NYC metro area. The two-month program offers 7 weeks of coaching from 35+ experts plus resources and networks through Samuel Adams and local partners, and all graduates receive a $2,500 grant with a chance at additional pitch competition funding. To qualify, you must be at least a 50% owner of a packaged food/beverage business, be 21+, and have a business bank account.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- You must be at least 21 years old to apply.
- Your business must be located in New England (Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, or Vermont); the greater Cincinnati, OH area; or the greater New York City metro area
- You must be at least 50% owner of a food or beverage business that currently sells packaged products.
- You must have a business bank account.

Name: Women Who Scale Grant
Description: Women Who Scale is a U.S.-wide grant from Herbal Renaissance and the Evals Equity Women’s Fund awarding four $2,500 grants (total $10,000) to women-owned or women-operated businesses that have been operating for at least 1 year and can explain how the funds will help them scale. Winners also get brand visibility/strategic exposure through the partners’ platforms, and applications are due February 20. To be eligible, applicants must complete the brief application (impact, use of funds, growth goals) and meet the social requirements (follow the accounts and tag 10 women business owners).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements:
- Female-owned or female-operated business
- Minimum of 1 year in business
- Business must be U.S.-based
- Demonstrate how the grant will be used to scale
- Submit a brief application outlining: Business impact, Use of funds, Growth and scaling goals

Name: Shipt LadderUp Accelerator Program
Description: Shipt’s LadderUp™ Accelerator Program supports local fresh food organizations – including grocers, food co-ops, farmers markets, and CSAs – by providing industry mentorship, education, and a $5,000 grant to help them scale their impact and navigate the digital food landscape. The program is open nationwide (with emphasis on cities like DC, NYC, Chicago, Detroit, Minneapolis, and Madison) and applications for the 2026 cohort close February 20, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: '- The program is open to local grocers, food co-ops, farmers markets, and CSAs (community-supported agriculture). Organizations nationwide are welcome to apply, but we’re specifically excited to welcome those in DC, NYC, Chicago, Detroit, Grand Rapids, Minneapolis, and Madison, Wisconsin.

Name: ViaPath Foundation Grant
Description: The ViaPath Foundation Impact Grant funds nonprofits that help people and families break cycles of justice involvement and economic hardship, with a focus on reentry/reintegration, family and community stabilization, education and workforce readiness, and advocacy/cross-sector partnerships. The grant is designed to provide not just funding but also tools and collaboration opportunities to expand impact across ViaPath’s program areas, including support for justice-impacted individuals and veterans. The application period runs Jan 26–Feb 20, 2026, and applicants submit a completed application to info@viapath-foundation.com

Name: RISE Residency (Chef Marcus Samuelsson)
Description: Rise Residency at Denniston Hill – created by Chef Marcus Samuelsson – is a first-of-its-kind program for mid-career culinary professionals (e.g., restaurateurs, writers, farmers, sommeliers) offering six months of mentorship, research access, and a 2–3 week creative retreat, plus a $5,000 stipend. Cohort 1 is selecting up to two residents, and applications are due February 20, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Experienced culinary professionals with 5+ years of experience (e.g., chefs, food writers, sommeliers, food entrepreneurs, etc.).
- Ability to participate in the two-week residency/retreat window (May–July 2026, generally required).

Name: Lowe's Into the Blue: Natural Products Expo West – Concept to Commerce (C2C) 2026
Description: Lowe’s is accepting applications through February 20 for its “Into the Blue” event at NHS Concept to Commerce in Las Vegas (March 31–April 2, 2026), where product suppliers can pitch innovative home improvement items for potential placement in Lowe’s stores and on Lowes.com. Selected applicants will meet in person to present products or manufacturing capabilities directly to Lowe’s sourcing teams, though participation does not guarantee a partnership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Brand must apply and be selected for the program by the stated deadline.
- Must be able to participate in Expo West programming (including attendance requirements).
- Product categories and restrictions apply (see official FAQ).

Name: M&F Bank Small Business Grant
Description: M&F Bank’s Empowering Growth Small Business Grant awards two $10,000 grants – one to a Raleigh business and one to a Durham business – to help small businesses in the Raleigh-Durham area grow. Applications run January 1–February 22, 2026, and eligible businesses must be M&F Bank customers in good standing located in Wake or Durham County, with ≤$750K in revenue, ≤25 employees, and ≤10 years in operation (prior winners and certain entities like nonprofits are ineligible).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Your business must have gross revenues of $750,000 or less
- Must have been in business for ten (10) years or less as of January 31, 2026
- Your small business must have twenty-five (25) employees or fewer, including yourself
- Your business must operate in Wake or Durham County
- Your business must be a customer of M&F Bank in good standing
- Previous grant recipients are not eligible to apply

Certain entities, such as nonprofits, real estate investment firms, businesses with M&F Bank vendor ties, and M&F Bank employees or their relatives, are also ineligible. Eligibility rules are subject to change at any time.

Name: UPS Store Small Biz Challenge
Description: The 2026 The UPS Store® Small Biz Challenge invites eligible U.S. small businesses (independent, non-franchised small businesses, 9 or fewer employees, full-time owner) to enter for a chance to win a share of up to $35,000, a trip to Nashville, and a feature in Inc. magazine. After submissions are judged to select nine semi-finalists who complete mentor-led challenges and a public voting phase, the top three finalists compete at a live Nashville event where one grand prize winner is chosen. First place will win $25,000, and runner-ups will receive $5,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open only to individuals (U.S. residents, 18 or older) who own and operate an independent (non-franchised) small business (9 or fewer employees) in the U.S. Up to nine (9) semi-finalists selected to compete in virtual challenges and voting. Three (3) finalists will be selected to compete in live challenges and voting to determine one (1) grand prize winner in Nashville, TN. Cash prizes awarded to finalists based on score in the finals in Nashville. Visit inc.com/theupsstore/rules for complete official rules, including eligibility and judging criteria.

Name: ESSENCE Festival 2026 Vending Partner Application
Description: ESSENCE Festival of Culture® returns to New Orleans July 3–5, 2026, featuring music at the Superdome plus citywide daytime experiences like SOKO MKRT, Beautycon, Food & Wine, and the Community Center. Vendor partner applications are currently open for Black-owned businesses, founders, and community leaders to showcase their work, connect with attendees, and drive visibility and sales, with applications closing February 23. Early-bird tickets are also on sale now.

Name: Advancing Workforce Mobility RFP (Education Design Lab / Credential Engine)
Description: Request for proposals funding projects that advance credential transparency and skills validation for workers Skilled Through Alternative Routes (STARs). Grants are offered at multiple tiers for projects ranging from early-stage exploration to scaling implementations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- U.S.-based nonprofit or governmental organizations.
- Projects focused on advancing credential transparency and skills validation.
- One eligible organization must serve as lead applicant (partnerships encouraged).

Name: Michigan Black Business Alliance Global Growth Accelerator
Description: The Global Growth Accelerator (GGA) is a highly competitive, three-year fellowship from the Michigan Black Business Alliance designed to help Black-owned businesses scale, increase revenue, and expand into new markets through tailored consulting, expert mentorship, and access to flexible investment capital. It targets MBBA Premium members with $500K+ annual revenue, at least three years of profitable operations and filed financials/taxes, and focuses on businesses in the “Success” stage aiming toward “Takeoff” and “Resource Maturity.” Applicants submit detailed business/financial info (including financial statements and credit reports), and MBBA makes final fit/acceptance decisions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The eligibility criteria serve as a guideline, but we take a holistic approach and may consider businesses that show strong potential even if they don’t meet every requirement.
- Premium Member of the Michigan Black Business Alliance 
- Minimum annual revenue of $500,000+
- Three years of filed business taxes/historical financial statements (cash flow, balance sheet, and P&L)
- Profitable operations for at least three years 
- Businesses must be in the Success Stage, aiming for Takeoff Stage and Resource Maturity

Name: CTIA Wireless Foundation Catalyst Grant
Description: Catalyst (run by the CTIA Wireless Foundation) is a competitive grant program for social entrepreneurs with mobile-first solutions that use wireless tech to tackle major challenges in U.S. communities. The program will award $200,000+ in unrestricted funding to at least six applicants, including $100K (1st), $50K (2nd), $25K (3rd) and up to three $10K honorable mentions, plus pitch coaching, communications support, and visibility opportunities. The Phase 1 application deadline is February 24, 2026, with finalists advancing to a Phase 2 round in April.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
In order to be considered, applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:
- Applicants must be registered and operate in the United States and/or the United States Territories.
- Applicants must assume one of the following legal statuses:
-- Nonprofit organization;
-- For-profit organization with a demonstrated commitment to social good; or,
-- B-Corporation.
- Applicants must complete and submit the application form by the submission deadlines. The Foundation will not consider late or incomplete submissions.
- Applicants cannot be past or current CTIA members at any point in the application and awards process.
- Applicants cannot be past Catalyst Winners. Past Catalyst Honorable Mention recipients may apply.
- Individuals are not eligible to apply.

Name: Amazon Devices Climate Tech Accelerator
Description: Amazon’s Devices Climate Tech Accelerator is an equity-free, six-month program (run with Plug and Play) that helps climate tech companies at any stage fast-track the validation and potential integration of their decarbonization solutions into Amazon Devices by connecting them directly with Amazon technical teams and senior decision-makers. Companies receive structured mentorship and integration assessment support plus up to $100K in AWS Activate credits, with focus areas ranging from low-carbon materials and batteries to semiconductors, energy efficiency, AI, and circularity. Applications are due Feb 24, 2026 (10 AM ET), with the cohort kicking off in May 2026 in Hong Kong and finalists ultimately pitching to Amazon Devices leadership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility requirements:
- Have a developed hardware or software tech innovation that can help to further decarbonize Amazon devices products, services, and manufacturing supply chain. We are especially interested in cutting edge technologies to address areas in Displays, Printed Circuit Boards and Assemblies (PCBs and PCBAs), Low Carbon Materials, Semiconductors, Device Batteries, Energy efficiency, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Circularity, or Manufacturing Processes. 
- Have a senior leader available and willing to participate in a hybrid 16-week accelerator that includes up to 2 in-person events.
- Willingness to write documents including but not limited to an Integration Assessment.
- Comfortable working in spoken and written English.

Note: Companies best poised to succeed in the accelerator should have a functioning prototype, a viable business model, and proven financial sustainability.

Name: City of Boston Small Business Month Activation Grant
Description: The City of Boston’s Office of Small Business is offering Small Business Month Activation Grants of up to $9,500 to nonprofit organizations that support Boston’s small business community. Funds will support free, public events in May 2026 – such as workshops, markets, networking events, and business district activations – that provide resources and engagement opportunities for entrepreneurs. Applications open January 30, 2026 and are due February 24, 2026 at 5:00 p.m., with awards announced in March.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- This grant is directed at nonprofits and community organizations with a proven track record of supporting and advocating for small businesses in Boston. Grant recipients must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status. 
- All activations must be free and open to the public, and held within the City of Boston.

Name: Ben & Jerry's Foundation Grant
Description: The  Ben & Jerry's Foundation Jerry Greenfield National Grassroots Organizing Grant Program funds community-based, constituent-led organizations working to confront social and environmental injustice, grounded in the belief that people most impacted are best positioned to lead solutions. It provides unrestricted general operating support (up to $30,000) to small grassroots groups running collective-action organizing campaigns that build power, mobilize communities, and drive systemic change across the U.S. and its territories.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered, each applicant org must:
- Have an annual operating budget under $350,000
- Use grassroots, collective-action organizing campaigns as the primary strategy for creating social change
- Be a non-profit with 501(c)3 status, or have a fiscal agent with this status
- Be U.S.-based and exclusively U.S.-focused

Name: National Endowment for the Arts Grants for Arts Projects
Description: The NEA’s Grants for Arts Projects (GAP) program funds arts projects that help communities experience the arts, celebrate cultural heritage, expand arts education, and support arts-and-health efforts across many disciplines (from music and museums to design, theater, and visual/media arts). Eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) nonprofits, units of state/local government, and federally recognized tribes with at least 5 years of arts programming and a prior-year operating budget of $20,000+; awards typically range from $10,000–$100,000 (with some discipline-specific limits) and require a 1:1 cost share. Applications run in two cycles, with the February 2026 deadlines spanning Feb 12 (Grants.gov Part 1) and **Feb 25 (NEA Portal Part 2).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organizations eligible to apply include:
- Nonprofit, tax-exempt 501(c)(3), U.S. organizations;
- Units of state or local government; or
- Federally recognized tribal communities or tribes.
- Applicant organizations must have completed at least 5 years of arts programming prior to the application deadline. Applicant organizations must have had an operating budget of at least $20,000 in the previous fiscal year.

- Generally, an applicant may submit one application per calendar year.

- Funding is not available in this category for individuals, applications submitted by a fiscal sponsor, commercial/for-profit enterprises, or State Arts Agencies and Regional Arts Organizations.

Name: SkinnyDipped Female Founder Fund
Description: SkinnyDipped is offering a $25,000 Female Founder Fund grant for women-owned food businesses in the U.S. that are already doing $150K+ in annual revenue, plus six months of hands-on mentorship from its leadership team across areas like marketing, operations/supply chain, sales/distribution, and finance. Applications close February 25, and updates will be shared March 8 (International Women’s Day).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Women-owned food businesses in the U.S.
- Generating $150K+ in annual revenue

Name: New Mexico Economic Development Department Creative Industries Division Grant
Description: New Mexico’s Creative Industries Division Business Development & Expansion Grant supports existing for-profit creative businesses with at least three years of operations, offering awards up to $25,000 to fund needs like inventory, equipment, marketing/digital presence, technology/software, and small infrastructure improvements (but not hiring full-time staff). The program prioritizes rural and underserved businesses and those with fewer than 10 employees, consistent with a requirement that 50% of funding go to rural/underserved communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible businesses must:
- Have a minimum of three-year history of operations
- Be a for-profit entity in good standing
Preferential points will be given to businesses with fewer than ten employees including part time staff, and to businesses located in rural areas per statutory language that requires 50% of grant funding to go to rural and underserved businesses, and language that specifies support for projects and proposals that support small creative businesses. Eligible businesses are also identified in the grant FAQ, division statute by industry area, and corresponding NAICS codes available in Appendix C on page 206 of the 2024 Division Study.

Name: Mary Morton Parsons Foundation Grant
Description: The Mary Morton Parsons Foundation offers capital project grants to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits based in (or directly impacting) the Commonwealth of Virginia, across focus areas like arts & culture, education, historic preservation, environment/conservation, civic/community needs, and social services. For Spring 2026, organizations must submit a Contact Form by 5pm Feb 27, 2026 (after the portal opens Jan 12, 2026) and, if invited, submit a full application by 5pm March 16, 2026; awards are typically matching/challenge grants funding up to about one-third of project cost.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Mary Morton Parsons Foundation awards grants to organizations that are exempt under IRS Section 501(c)(3), not classified as a private foundation as defined in Section 509(a), and either located in the greater Richmond region or having a direct impact in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

Name: Hatch Detroit 2026 (Comerica Hatch Detroit Contest by TechTown)
Description: Hatch Detroit 2026 (an official partner program of TechTown Detroit) is now accepting applications through February 27, with the community ultimately voting to decide which business idea they want to see open in Detroit. The grand prize winner receives $100,000 from Comerica Bank, and the Top 10 finalists also get free consulting and in-kind services from TechTown Detroit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Entrepreneurs seeking to open a business in Detroit (and surrounding eligible areas per contest rules).
- Submit application by the stated deadline and participate in contest process (finalist/voting phases).

Name: Les Dames d’Escoffier DC Grants
Description: Les Dames d’Escoffier Washington, D.C. awards annual grants to tax-exempt charitable or educational organizations in the DC area that advance food, beverage, and hospitality through initiatives like community health, sustainable food practices, and culinary education. For 2026, applications are due February 28, with decisions in mid-April and funds distributed in late April/early May, and grantees provide a 6-month program update in December.

Name: Founders' Pool Boost Grants
Description: 5 founders will receive $1,000 flexible grants. Applicants must be U.S.-based businesses that sign up for a 30-day free trial to premium membership for Founders' Pool. Winners announced early March.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Amazon Operating Grant
Description: Funds are allocated towards a women-owned business actively selling and in good standing in Amazon’s store.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants Must:
• Identify as a woman entrepreneur with an established business
• Business must be entrepreneur’s full-time job
• Prove use of funds (documentation, proof from external agency)
• Be a U.S. Citizen
• Have a product-based business (food, beverage, or consumer packaged good)
• Be on and actively selling and in good standing in the Amazon store
• Have more than $5,000 sales
• Submit most recent W2 form
• Not be a previous Enthuse Foundation Grant Winner or Pitch Competition Winner
• If selected, submit Required New Vendor Forms
• Use the funds between June 2025 – June 2026

Name: 2026 Athene Beyond Boundaries Business Summit - Bank of America Pitch Competition
Description: The Athene Beyond Boundaries Business Summit Pitch Competition invites established for-profit small businesses (2+ years in business, under 50 employees, under $2.5M revenue) from any location to apply for a chance to pitch live at the April 14–15, 2026 summit in West Des Moines, Iowa and win thousands of dollars, with multiple winners sharing a prize pot. To apply, businesses must submit a written application plus a 1-minute promo video and a $20 application fee, and finalists must attend the full day on April 14 to be eligible to pitch.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements:
- For anyone & everyone to apply. Small businesses are encouraged to apply.
- Must be an established small business. (Organizations – whether product or service businesses – are defined as more than 2 years in business, under 50 employees and under $2.5M annual revenue.)
- This pitch is for-profit businesses only. No nonprofit pitches.
- Business does not have to be West Des Moines located. ANY business that meets the above requirements is welcome to compete.
- If you have received funds from the past three years at the Athene Beyond Boundaries Business Summit and to make room for new applicants, you are not able to apply for the 2026 event unless you were a ‘surprise fishbowl winner’ from a previous year.

Name: HerGenius Pitch Competition
Description: Impact Ventures’ HerGenius Pitch Competition is for women-founded businesses in North Texas with traction. Eligible companies must be 51% woman-owned/operated, have at least $100K in annual revenue, and be based in North Texas (all industries welcome). Applications close Feb 27, invitations go out March 5, and the top 3 finalists will pitch live in Dallas on March 19, 2026 for a $10,000 grand prize.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- At least 51% owned and operated by a woman
- Must have annual revenue of at least $100k
- Business must be located in North Texas
- Open to all industries

Name: PBS SoCal Community Storyteller Initiative
Description: PBS SoCal’s Community Storyteller Initiative is seeking Southern California–based creators to produce short videos about Los Angeles’s histories, neighborhoods, and cultural legacies as the city prepares for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Selected storytellers will receive production grants, and proposals are due March 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- All Projects must meet the submission requirements and abide by all Rules and Regulations and be suitable for publication, which shall be determined by PBS SoCal in its sole discretion. Project submissions which violate or do not meet the requirements will be declined.
- Any Applicant who submits a Project must be the original author and copyright owner of the submitted Project and that Applicant must have the sole authority and/or has obtained the legal authority from any necessary third party, to grant the permissions and rights granted herein, and no other permission from any other party must be required to grant such rights.
- The submission period begins January 9,2026 and ends March 1,2026 (“Submission Period”). All Project submissions must be received prior to the expiration of the Submission Period. PBS SoCal’s database clock
shall be the official time keeping device for all entries submitted to PBS SoCal.
- Applicants must be eighteen (18) years of age or older as of the date of submission.
- Applicants must be a U.S. citizen or otherwise legally authorized to work in the United States and to perform services in the State of California.
- There is no limit to the number of Projects an Applicant may submit. However, the production schedule may limit PBS SoCal to greenlighting a single Project by each successful Applicant.

Name: CareerX Accelerator
Description: CareerX is an accelerator program powered by NCEE and Britebound that supports late-seed and Series A startups building technologies to expand equitable career pathways for young people and adults. The program connects founders directly with education leaders to test, refine, and scale solutions focused on core academic skills, contemporary skills, lifelong learning habits, and community engagement. Running from April to July 2026, CareerX emphasizes relationship-building over fundraising, does not take equity or fees, and aims to help companies successfully navigate and scale within education systems.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Company Stage: Late seed or Series A (Nonprofits are also welcome to apply if they meet the selection criteria.)
- Revenue: Companies with longer track records and more ARR will have a higher chance of being selected.
- Focus Areas: Solutions that are advancing career-connected learning — building core academic skills, contemporary skills, habits of learning and well-being, community skills, and/or help young people and adults have meaningful careers. Companies whose solutions help leaders create the conditions for career-connected learning and provide career access for adults will also be considered.
- Location: Companies may be based anywhere globally; must have at least some existing revenue earned within the United States.
Participation: At least one C-suite leader must commit to full participation from April – July 2026.

Name: SHE:DC Microgrant
Description: SHE:DC is a Shop Made Brands initiative offering microgrants to help women- and non-binary–owned consumer product makers in the DMV grow their businesses, with applications due March 1. Eligible applicants must be in business for 3 years or less, be retail-ready, and not already have a brick-and-mortar retail lease; this year at least one $2,500 grant and two $1,000 grants will be awarded. Finalists pitch at a March 27 happy hour in Dupont, where attendees vote to select recipients, and all pitch finalists receive professional service scholarships from WACIF.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be creator of a consumer product. 
- Must be woman-or non-binary owned and operated and operated.
- Must be a maker designing or making product in the in the DMV.
- Must be minimally retail ready (social media and web presence and demonstrating success selling in the market).
- Must be in business for less than 3 years and not hold a lease on retail location.

Name: Queens Tech + Innovation Challenge
Description: This Queens-led entrepreneurship program (presented by Borough President Donovan Richards and the Queens Economic Development Corporation) supports early-stage founders with education, mentorship, networking, and five cash awards of up to $20,000 each with no strings attached. Participants can attend live or recorded online workshops from October 2025–January 2026, join monthly in-person networking events through February 2026, and book 1:1 office hours with program mentors. Awards are given across five categories: Consumer Tech, Enterprise Tech, Sustainability, Community, and Food-Based (with Queens storefront requirements for retail food businesses).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Pre-seed or seed stage tech startups still looking to establish a - business model
- Early stage CPG, community-based businesses, currently generating revenue
- High-potential, ready to use a 20K grant to reach their next milestone
- Willing and able to meet the requirements to participate in the Challenge

Name: Portland Community Development Grant for SOVC Orgs
Description: The City of Portland is offering a new “Building Digital Bridges” grant for nonprofits or government agencies serving survivors of violent crime, awarding one organization $140,000 to design or expand trauma-informed digital inclusion programming. Funded projects can cover devices, internet access, digital skills and safety training (including for tech-facilitated abuse), and workforce-focused certifications, with up to 24 months to deliver measurable outcomes in digital adoption, safety, and economic mobility. Applications open January 26, 2026 and are due March 2, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. PT via the City’s Grants Portal.

Name: Veteran Tech Readiness Small Business Grant
Description: The Veteran Tech Readiness Small Business Grant will award three $20,000 grants to eligible veteran-owned micro/small businesses (under 20 employees, at least 51% veteran-owned) operating in or serving Portland to build digital capacity and improve economic mobility. Funds can be used for technology purchases, digital skills training, online presence/marketing, cybersecurity, and internet or technical support. Applications open January 26, 2026 and are due March 2, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. PT via the City of Portland Grants Portal.

Name: Decatur Area Arts Council Grants
Description: The Decatur Area Arts Council’s Regional Arts Partners Grants provide small awards (typically $200–$1,000) to registered 501(c)(3) nonprofits to support arts events and creative arts learning in Macon County and nearby communities. Applications are reviewed twice a year, and projects must start after grant approval.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: '- Must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization

Name: Big Grove for Good Nonprofit Grant
Description: Big Grove for Good Foundation is accepting 2026 applications to award eight $8,000 grants to 501(c)(3) nonprofits – two each in Iowa’s Johnson, Polk, and Linn counties, plus two in the Omaha Metro. The grant supports organizations focused on environmental sustainability, equity & equality, or hyperlocal community support, and includes a year-long partnership with volunteer support from Big Grove staff. Applications are due Monday, March 2.

Name: Local Data for Equitable Communities Grant
Description: Local Data for Equitable Communities is a grant opportunity for U.S.-based nonprofits to collect, analyze, and use local data to address inequities in a specific place, supporting community-led action toward health equity. The program expects to fund up to 30 grants of $50,000 for nine months, focused on one primary topic area (built environment, climate/environment, safety, healthy food access, housing, or transportation) in a defined local geography (e.g., neighborhood(s), city/county, metro area, or tribal area). Full proposals are due March 3, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. CT, with awards notified May 11 and projects starting July 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Awards will be made to organizations, not to individuals.
- Applicants must be nonprofit organizations that are tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) or Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”). The following eligibility exceptions apply:
-- Not eligible to apply: All universities, whether nonprofit, public, or private, whether tax exempt under the Code or not.
-- Not eligible to apply: All state and local government agencies whether tax exempt under the Code or not, including but not limited to, agencies representing states, cities, towns, and villages; public health departments; school districts; and public schools. 
-- Not eligible to apply: Private foundations or nonfunctionally integrated Type III supporting organizations, whether tax exempt under the IRS Code or not.
- Also eligible are organizations that are fiscally sponsored by an eligible tax-exempt 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) organization. The fiscal sponsor is required to provide the total amount of the award to the organization that will perform the program activities as described in the application, less the fiscal sponsorship fee. The fiscal sponsorship fee is an allowable expense under the award. The Foundation may require additional documentation in these cases.
- Applicant organizations must be based in the U.S. or its territories.
- Applicants cannot be a current grantee of the Local Data for Equitable Communities program.
- Organizations may only submit one proposal. 
- Applicant organizations may contract with and collaborate with any type of organization for their projects. Only one eligible nonprofit organization may represent the collaboration as the applicant and be the Foundation’s contact in the application process. 
- The applicant organization must play a substantive role in the project.
See the Call for Proposals for more information on eligible and ineligible activities.

Name: The Community Foundation for Northeast Florida Early Childhood Grant
Description: This grant provides up to $25,000 to nonprofit organizations in Duval County, Florida, that support at-risk children under six years old through early learning centers and programs for parents and caregivers. Eligible organizations must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits with at least a 2-year history and an annual budget of $100,000 or more, and applications are due March 4, 2026. Funded projects must be completed between June 1, 2026, and May 31, 2028.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Nonprofit organizations with current 501(c)(3) status public charity or private operating foundation status, or religious institution
- 2-year work history
- Annual operating budget of $100,000 or above
- Located in and serving Duval County

Name: The Community Foundation for Northeast Florida Food and Needs Insecurity Grant
Description: This grant provides $10,000 to $20,000 to nonprofit organizations in Northeast Florida (Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau, and St. Johns counties) that address food and basic needs insecurity or support people with disabilities. Grant amounts are tiered based on organizational budget: organizations with budgets of $100,000-$250,000 can apply for up to $10,000, while those with budgets over $250,000 can request up to $20,000. Applications are due March 4, 2026, and eligible organizations must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits with at least a 2-year history.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Organizations serving residents experiencing food and basic needs insecurity
- Organizations providing supports for people with disabilities
- Nonprofit organizations with current 501(c)(3) public charity or private operating foundation status, or religious institution
- 2-year work history
- Annual operating budget of $100,000 or above.
- Located in and serving one of these counties: Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau, St. Johns

Name: The Community Foundation for Northeast Florida Supporting Neighborhoods Grant
Description: This grant provides up to $25,000 to nonprofit organizations in Northeast Florida (Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau, Putnam, and St. Johns counties) that foster inclusive prosperity in high-poverty neighborhoods through projects addressing indicators such as decreasing displacement risk, increasing homeownership rates, or strengthening community organizations. Eligible organizations must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits with at least a 2-year history and an annual budget of $100,000 or more, and applications are due March 4, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Nonprofit organizations with a current 501(c)(3) public charity or private operating foundation status, or religious institution
2-year work history
- Annual operating budget of $100,000 or above
- Located in and serving at least one of these counties: Baker, Clay, Duval, Nassau, Putnam and St. Johns

Name: Minnesota Economic Response Fund
Description: The Minneapolis Foundation’s Economic Response Fund offers short-term stabilization grants ($2,500–$10,000) to Minnesota small businesses disrupted in recent weeks by reduced revenue, workforce issues, closures, or safety/security concerns, with support intended for a 30–60 day period. The fund will distribute $4 million on a rolling basis through seven community nonprofit partners, and eligible businesses must have 40 or fewer employees and $3 million or less in annual revenue (nonprofits and governments aren’t eligible). Funds can cover essentials like payroll, rent, utilities, inventory replacement, security/repairs, and other urgent business expenses, and the application stays open until money runs out.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
These grants are designed to support small businesses that have experienced reduced customers or revenue, workforce disruptions, temporary closures, or concerns with safety and security.

Funding is available for businesses that are currently operating as well as those that are temporarily or permanently closed due to disruptions.

Small businesses with a maximum of 40 employees and a gross annual revenue of $3 million or less are eligible to apply. This funding opportunity is not open to nonprofit organizations, local governments, or individual employees applying on their own behalf.

Name: Massachusetts Office of Travel and Tourism FIFA World Cup Grants
Description: Massachusetts’ Office of Travel and Tourism is offering competitive Sports and Entertainment Events Fund grants for FIFA World Cup–related events and support activities in FY26, backed by $10 million in state funding. Eligible applicants (Massachusetts municipalities, public agencies, tribal entities, and nonprofits) can apply for cost-reimbursement grants for expenses like transportation, public safety, accessibility services, signage, event operations, and watch parties, but must provide at least a 1:1 match. Applications are due March 4, 2026 at 3:00pm ET, with awards expected to be announced in March 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
A public agency, municipality, tribal entity, or nonprofit organization incorporated in Massachusetts with 501(c)3, 501(c)4, 501(c)5, 501(c)6, status from the Internal Revenue Service is eligible to apply.

Applicants must
- have begun operations before January 1, 2025.
- be in good standing with the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and the municipality where it is located
- must be current on all taxes due through December 31, 2024
- have active and valid state licenses/registrations if applicable
- be in compliance with MBTA Communities Act (Section 3A of MGL c. 40A) if applicable (municipal applicants only)
- complete the online application, including all required documentation, by the deadline

The following applicants are ineligible to receive funding:
- For-profit organizations
- Public colleges and universities or state agencies
- A fiscal sponsor that will pass through funds to an ineligible organization
- Organizations not located in Massachusetts

Name: 2026 AARP Community Challenge
Description: The 2026 AARP Community Challenge offers grants to nonprofits and government entities for projects that create tangible, quick-action improvements that make communities more livable – especially for people age 50 and older. Funding options include flagship grants (up to $15,000), $2,500 capacity-building microgrants, and demonstration grants (up to $25,000) supporting areas like public spaces, transportation, housing, digital access, and disaster resilience. Applications are due March 4, 2026, with selected projects launching in June and completing by mid-December.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The program is open to: 
- 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), and 501(c)(6) nonprofit organizations recognized by the IRS 
- Government entities 
- Other types of organizations considered on a case-by-case basis

Note: AARP does not fund for-profit companies or individuals.

- Mission Focus: Projects must align with AARP’s mission to serve people age 50 and older.
- Eligible Projects: AARP Community Challenge grants support:
--Permanent, physical community improvements
--Temporary demonstrations that lead to long-term change 
--New, innovative programming pilots or services

Name: SDSU San Diego Angel Conference
Description: Applications for the SDSU 2026 San Diego Angel Conference are open Feb 2–Mar 5, 2026 (with a $49 nonrefundable fee) for U.S. startups seeking exposure to accredited early-stage investors and a chance at an investment. Over a 12-week process, investors review and diligences applicants, select finalists, and then showcase them at the SDAC finale at San Diego State University on May 29, 2026, where investors will make a ~$200,000 investment in at least one company (amount can vary based on dollars raised).

Name: Empower U Grant
Description: The 2026 Empower U Grant is now open and will support five women-owned and led businesses with $10,000 each plus executive mentorship from industry leaders. Applications close March 5 at 12pm PST / 3pm EST and require a 1-minute intro video (uploaded via Google Drive, Dropbox, YouTube, or Vimeo with a public link) submitted at empowerugrant.com.

Name: Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program (HVRP) Grant
Description:
HVRP (which includes the Homeless Veterans’ Reintegration Program, Incarcerated Veterans’ Transition Program, and the Homeless Women Veterans/Homeless Veterans with Children program) is a competitive federal grant from DOL’s Veterans Employment and Training Service focused on helping veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness achieve stable, quality employment. Grantees must deliver individualized, case-managed employment services, connect veterans to local supportive services, and provide or coordinate job training and referrals to help them return to work and access higher-paying career pathways.

Eligible applicants are broad (including nonprofits, state/local/tribal governments, public/Indian housing authorities, higher education institutions, and for-profit/small businesses, including faith-based organizations), but applicants must maintain a physical location in the proposed Service Delivery Area. There is $23M in total of program funding, with 61-63 awards expected of $150,000 - $500,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants include:

Education
- Public and state institutions of higher education
- Private institutions of higher education

Government
- Public and Indian housing authorities
- State governments
- County governments
- Special district governments
- City or township governments
- Federally recognized Native American tribal governments

Nonprofit
- Other Native American tribal organizations
- Nonprofits non-higher education with 501(c)(3)
- Nonprofits non-higher education without 501(c)(3)

Business
- For-profit organizations other than small businesses
- Small businesses

Name: Massachusetts AI Models Innovation Challenge (Mass AI Hub / MassTech)
Description: Grant program supporting projects that develop, fine-tune, or adapt domain-specific AI models to catalyze scientific discovery, commercialization, or public benefit. Awards fund applied AI model work and require collaboration across eligible organizations and industry partners.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Lead applicant must be a Massachusetts-based academic institution or nonprofit (per program eligibility).
- Must include at least one industry partner (collaboration required).
- Proposed work focuses on developing/fine-tuning/adapting domain-specific AI models for applied impact.

Name: Spruce Foundation 2026 Grant
Description: Unrestricted grants for local community organizations. The Spruce Foundation is a 501(c)(3) empowering emerging leaders in Greater Philadelphia to develop as philanthropists and strengthening the region’s generations to come through fundraising and grantmaking for youth-serving nonprofits. The grant cycle includes an open application window and optional info sessions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Local community organization (per Spruce Foundation’s grant criteria).
- Submit application during the open window (Jan 7–Mar 6, 2026).

Name: Community Foundation for Greater Buffalo Grants
Description: The Community Foundation for Greater Buffalo’s competitive grants fund projects in Western New York that advance one of four themes: racial/ethnic equity, economic mobility through education and workforce readiness, climate resilience and environmental stewardship, or regional vibrancy through arts, culture, and architecture. Proposals must clearly tie to one of the Foundation’s specified “Solutions,” such as civic engagement and leadership, improving school readiness and academic achievement for students in low-income households, protecting waterways/strengthening environmental collaboratives, or equitable access to long-term arts instruction for youth in low-income communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Grants are awarded only to organizations that have current Section 501(c)(3) status as determined by the Internal Revenue Service.
- Applicants must be located or delivering services in at least one of the eight counties of Western New York: Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Niagara, Orleans, and Wyoming.

Name: Cook County Restore, Reinvest, and Renew (R3) Program
Description: The Illinois R3 (Restore, Reinvest, and Renew) Program is now accepting applications through March 6, 2026, offering grant funding to organizations serving communities most impacted by violence, incarceration, and economic disinvestment. The program will distribute $50 million across five areas – civil legal aid, economic development, reentry, violence prevention, and youth development – with individual awards ranging from $25,000 to $1 million. Eligible applicants include nonprofits, government, education, and community organizations operating in designated R3 zones, with grants running from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027 (with potential extensions).

Name: San Jose Small Business Start-up Grant
Description: The City of San José’s Small Business Start-Up Grant provides funding to early-stage, for-profit businesses (less than three years old) that are registered and operated within San José. The program will award up to 20 grants – 10 for $10,000 and 10 for $5,000 – to support startup expenses such as licensing, equipment, training, or loan down payments. Eligible businesses must have 35 or fewer employees, commit to required advising or training, and apply by March 6, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Registered in San José and with a business tax certificate less than 3 years old
- Business owners must both operate their business and reside within the City of San José
- A for-profit business
- Maximum up to 35 employees
- Commit to using funds for business startup purposes
- Are open to participate in required advising or training sessions
- Are not a business selling tobacco, cannabis or liquor

Name: Encouraging Development, Growth & Expansion (EDGE)  Grant Competition
Description: Delaware's EDGE Grant Competition is a state-funded program that provides grant funding to small businesses, with up to $400K available for the Entrepreneur track and up to $750K for the STEM track, split among category winners. Eligible businesses must be majority located in Delaware, in operation for less than 7 years, have 15 or fewer employees, and provide a 3:1 state-to-business match.
Amount: Entrepreneur Track: Up to $400K total; STEM track: Up to $750K total
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Be majority located in Delaware
- Be in business for less than 7 years
- Have 15 or fewer full-time employees
- Have less than $700K in assets
- Have a 3:1 match

Name: 2026 EALA New Champions Fund
Description: EALA is seeking “New Champions” in the U.S. – leaders of schools, districts, CBOs, nonprofits, or eligible small for-profits – who are from marginalized backgrounds (or strong allies) and are making measurable progress for students with disabilities and learning differences, especially in underserved communities. Selected recipients receive funding ($35,000 for the New Champion; $5,000 for two runners-up) plus a virtual retreat, yearlong mentorship, and national visibility opportunities. Applications are reviewed online using an RFP-defined rubric by a panel of expert judges, with winners announced in May 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
An EALA "New Champion" fits ALL of the following profile:
- You lead a community-based organization (CBO), school, district, non-profit, or for-profit*
- Your organization is based and operates within the United States.
- You are a leader from a marginalized background or a dedicated ally who has demonstrated a deep commitment to advancing access and belonging in education.
- You are actively working to improve the lives of students with disabilities and learning differences, including those from underserved communities and those who face barriers to educational opportunity.

Name: New Mexico CreativeCon
Description: CreativeCon is a statewide event series organized by New Mexico's Creative Industries Division that connects artists, creative entrepreneurs, and business owners to grants, funding, marketing resources, and support programs available across the state. The events are designed to "unearth the creative ecosystem" by showing creatives that support exists beyond just arts organizations, spanning economic development, tourism, and workforce agencies.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Info: 
- Events are held in communities throughout New Mexico. 
- March 7th- Carlsbad, NM
- March 28th - Raton, NM

Name: eBay Circular Fashion Fund
Description: The eBay Circular Fashion Fund supports early-stage fashion businesses advancing circular economy solutions—from resale and repair to responsible design and regeneration – across the U.S., EU, UK, Australia, Canada, and Switzerland. In 2026, eight finalists will each receive $50,000 plus targeted mentoring, with one global winner potentially receiving a $300,000 investment from eBay Ventures. Eligible businesses must be 6 months–6 years old, apply by March 8, and demonstrate real-world impact aligned with eBay’s fashion ecosystem.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Businesses between six months and six years old across the US, EU, UK, Australia, Canada, and Switzerland
- Applicants should use circular ideas to solve real-world problems, and align with eBay’s fashion business
- A drive to create a positive, lasting impact for people and planet is also a must

Name: Native Arts + Heritage Fund
Description: The Native Arts + Heritage Fund (NAHF), offered by Creative West, provides $2,500 unrestricted grants to Native American and Alaska Native artists, culture bearers, and cultural practitioners across the Creative West region.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 


Additional Info:
Co-designed with Native-centered advisors and community leaders, the fund prioritizes cultural continuity, self-determination, and well-being, and selected recipients also participate in a three-month virtual cohort for connection and shared learning. The application window is January 26 to March 8, 2026.

Name: Meta AI Glasses Impact Grants
Description: Meta’s AI Glasses Impact Grants will fund US-based organizations using Meta’s AI glasses to drive positive social and economic impact. The program offers Accelerator Grants for groups already using the glasses to scale impact (15 grants of $25K and 10 grants of $50K) and Catalyst Grants for new, high-impact applications built with the Meta Wearables Device Access Toolkit (five grants of $200K), plus membership in the Meta Wearables Community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible organizations are:
- A for profit or non-profit organization located and incorporated in the United States. Incorporated for over 12 months and in good standing with the laws of the United States.
- Please note, State, Local, or Federal governmental entities are not eligible.

We welcome applications from organizations of all sizes and industries. While priority areas include skills and employment, health, economic growth, community, accessibility, and support for veterans, we’re open to innovative ideas from any sector.

Name: Go PINK Grant Initiative
Description: The Go PINK Grant Initiative will award $2,500 to one standout founder who leads with authenticity, purpose, and originality. Get Grant Ready Summit attendees can apply by posting a 30–60 second Reel explaining what makes their business unique and how they “GO PINK” to stand out (bonus points for wearing pink, tagging @PinkPrintFirm, and using the listed hashtags). Applications run January 19 to March 9.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be an entrepreneur/non-profit leader, 18+, US or Canada-based, and a participant in the Get Grant Ready Summit.

Name: Maryland State Arts Council Grants for Artists Program
Description: Maryland State Arts Council’s Grants for Artists program provides $2,500 to independent Maryland artists to support working or living expenses, aiming to strengthen artists’ livelihoods and the state’s creative workforce. Eligible applicants must be 18+ Maryland residents with a sustained artistic practice in an MSAC-supported discipline, and they cannot be enrolled in a degree program or have received a grant in the most recent cycle. The FY2026 application deadline is March 9, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants must be an independent artist making work unaffiliated with an institution or organization, and must be:
- Currently engaged in a sustained artistic practice in a discipline supported by MSAC, including forms of dance, music, visual art, public art, folk and traditional arts, media arts, literary arts, and theatre. 
-- “Sustained” means that the artistic practice is ongoing, active, and intentional over time, rather than occasional or solely historical
- Maryland residents who are 18 or older.
-- Those experiencing homelessness are encouraged to reach out to MSAC staff for details on how to apply

Name: Woods Fund Chicago – Grants
Description: Grantmaker supporting community organizing and civic engagement in Chicago. Funding priorities and cycles vary; applicants typically engage via the fund’s published grantmaking process and guidelines.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Organizations aligned with Woods Fund Chicago’s priorities and eligible geography (Chicago/region).
- Follow Woods Fund’s grantmaking process and any current cycle guidance.

Name: San Antonio RevitalizeSA Corridor Leadership Program
Description: The City of San Antonio, in partnership with Main Street America, is accepting applications through March 10, 2026 for the 9-month RevitalizeSA: Corridor Leadership Program, which trains up to 15 local leaders to revitalize neighborhood commercial corridors. Participants complete leadership and strategy workshops and can apply for a CHANGE grant of up to $5,000 to implement a corridor improvement project. The program is open to San Antonio residents or workers with demonstrated leadership and community development experience who can commit to 12 training days over nine months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Currently live or work in San Antonio - minimum 1 year
- Demonstrated work/volunteer efforts on neighborhood initiatives, small business, or local development.
- Demonstrated experience of collaboration with others to drive change in San Antonio.
- Current involvement in economic development activities or demonstrated enthusiasm to learn more.
- Ability to commit to the program timeline and to 12 training days over a 9-month period.
- Have demonstrated leadership experience and a desire to expand leadership capacity.
- Demonstrated leadership experience.
- Passion for commercial corridor revitalization.

Name: 2026 Next Challenge for Media & Journalism
Description: The 2026 Next Challenge for Media & Journalism will award $250,000 to early-stage U.S.-based nonprofit and for-profit media startups and independent creators reinventing local journalism. Division winners can receive up to $50,000, with an additional $25,000 Grand Prize, and all finalists receive a $3,000 stipend to attend the national awards event. Eligible applicants must be launched, actively publishing, under 10 years old, and have earned less than $1 million in revenue in 2025, with applications due March 10, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is eligible for the Catalyst and Cornerstone awards?
- Legally incorporated for-profit and nonprofit media startups based in the United States of America and U.S. Territories. A venture is considered U.S.-based if it is legally incorporated in the U.S. and if the majority of employees and/or contractors live in the United States. Projects with a fiscal sponsor may apply only if the project is intended to become its own independent company or nonprofit organization. The project may not be a program, lab, center, research initiative, or internal venture of a university, nonprofit, or company.
- Legally incorporated no more than ten years prior to the application deadline (no earlier than March 10, 2016).
- Earned less than US $1,000,000 (gross revenue including philanthropic support) in the twelve months ending December 31, 2025. This does not include investment dollars.
- Ventures that are (1) launched and/or actively publishing and (2) are able to provide access to their content, product, or service as part of their application.

Who is eligible for the Pioneer award?
- U.S.-based independent creators (individuals or collaborations). Independent creators do not need to be legally incorporated.
- Exercise editorial control over their own work and are not structurally employed by or contractually subordinate to a media institution that sets editorial priorities, legal strategy, or publishing decisions. This work may not be a program, lab, center, research initiative, or internal venture of a university, nonprofit, or company.
- Earned less than US $1,000,000 (gross revenue including philanthropic support) through their publishing work in the twelve months ending December 31, 2025. This does not include investment dollars.
- Actively publishing and able to provide access to their content, product, or service as part of their application.

Name: MBBA Detroit Small Business Technology Fund Grant
Description: The MBBA Detroit Small Business Technology Fund offers $1,000 technology microgrants to help Detroit-based small businesses adopt tools like POS systems, CRM platforms, and e-commerce solutions. Eligible businesses must be located in Detroit, register for one of the MBBA anniversary events on Eventbrite, have 10 or fewer employees, under $500,000 in annual revenue, operate transactionally, be in good standing with LARA, and have been operating for at least one year. Applications open March 5 and close March 11.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- You must register for one of the MBBA Anniversary events on Eventbrite
- Be physically located within the City of Detroit
- Have 10 or fewer employees (including the owner)
- Have gross annual revenue under $500,000
- Be a transactional business (i.e., generates direct revenue through in-person or online customer transactions)
- Be in good standing with LARA
- Has been operating for at least 1 year

Name: Maryland Prekindergarten Expansion Grant
Description: This Maryland State Department of Education guide outlines a competitive Prekindergarten Expansion Grant that will provide about $26.6 million to expand free, full-day, high-quality pre-K for income-eligible 3- and 4-year-olds across Maryland, with applications due by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EDT. Eligible LEAs, private providers, and Head Start programs must meet Maryland EXCELS quality requirements and submit detailed plans covering program quality, staffing, budgets, family engagement, and measurable outcomes; awards are expected by April 24, 2026 for the July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 grant period.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This funding opportunity is designed for programs who deliver prekindergarten services and participate in the Maryland EXCELS program, including:
- Local Education Agencies (LEAs) or qualified vendors (as defined in COMAR (13a.06.02) and private providers (including, Head Start, Center Based, and Family Child Care programs) who:
- hold a valid license (if applicable)
- are Head Start programs.

Priority will be given to programs with the following Maryland EXCELS ratings (in order of priority):
- Published at level 5 with a plan to maintain this level;
- Publish at level 4 with a plan to achieve level 5 within 5 years (if you fall into this criterion, you
must include a plan to reach level 5 as part of your application); or
- Published at level 3 with a plan to achieve level 5 within 5 years (if you fall into this criterion, you
must include a plan to reach level 5 as part of your application).
Priority will be given to high-quality programs that:
- are seeking renewal or expansion of existing programs with a demonstrable track record of success;
- are in areas of the State that have an unmet need for prekindergarten services; or
- include parental/guardian engagement and educational activities beyond the classroom.

Name: Climate Smart Communities Initiative (CSCI) 2026 Grants
Description: Grants and technical assistance for community-based climate resilience planning and projects in highly climate-vulnerable U.S. communities. Funding supports a partnership between an adaptation practitioner, a community-based organization, and a government entity.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Project and partners must be based in the United States (including territories and Tribal nations).
- Team must include: adaptation practitioner + community-based organization + local/regional/Tribal government partner.
- Adaptation practitioner must be accepted into the Registry of Adaptation Practitioners before the application deadline.
- Project addresses significant climate-change hazards and community vulnerability considerations.

Name: Cigna Improving Youth Mental Health Grant
Description: The Cigna Group Foundation is committing $9 million over three years to support youth mental health (ages 5–18) and the parents, caregivers, and professionals who support them, with a focus on post-pandemic stress and distress. The program funds evidence-informed nonprofit initiatives – especially in underserved communities – that build social-emotional skills, equip adults who support youth, and expand pathways to intervention and care in school-related settings. Grant applications are open until March 12, 2026 at 5 pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Only public charitable organizations currently recognized as tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) or Section 170(b) of the Internal Revenue Code are eligible to receive or benefit from charitable funding from The Cigna Group Foundation.

Name: March 2026 Lakers Youth Foundation YOU Grant Contest
Description: The Lakers Youth Foundation YOU Grant Contest awards $7,500 to one winning nonprofit serving Los Angeles, San Bernardino, Orange, Ventura, or Riverside counties. Proposals are accepted March 1–12, 2026, after which LYF selects up to five finalists for a public vote running March 19–25. Organizations that won a YOU Grant within the past 12 months are ineligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
YOU GRANT is open to legally-existing 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations that
serve one or more of the following counties in the state of California: Los Angeles, San Bernardino, Orange,
Ventura or Riverside (“Qualifying Counties”), except that an organization is ineligible to receive the YOU
GRANT if that same organization was a winner of a prior YOU GRANT within 12 months prior to the
Closing Date. The date used to calculate this 12-month ineligibility period is the closing date of the winner’s
previously awarded YOU GRANT. A Grant Proposal may be deemed ineligible for YOU GRANT if a key
member of the submitting non-profit organization is a director, officer, employee or agent of LYF, The Los
Angeles Lakers, Inc. (“Lakers”), LAL G Team, LLC, the National Basketball Association (“NBA”) or its
Member Teams, NBA Properties, Inc., any of their respective parents, subsidiaries or affiliates, or
advertising, promotional or judging agencies, or if the Grant Proposal fails to comply with any portion of
these Official Rules, or for any other reason, at the sole discretion of LYF.

Name: Miami-Dade District 4 Small Business Grant Program
Description: Commissioner Micky Steinberg's District 4 Small Business Grant Program offers grants of up to $3,000 to for-profit small businesses located in Miami-Dade County's District 4 that have been in operation for at least one year. Funds can be used for inventory, equipment, marketing, minor renovations, and other business-related expenses, but cannot be used for rent, salaries, or debts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
- All businesses must be located in Florida's District 4
- Business must be in operation for at least one (1) year.
- Must be a for-profit business.
- A physical address is required. No P.O. Box as mailing address allowed.
- Home-based businesses can apply.
- The Selection Committee can consider special projects.

Name: SEED SPOT Emerging Brand Accelerator
Description: A 10-week virtual accelerator for early-stage, revenue-generating brands ready to scale into retail. Includes workshops, tailored mentorship, and tools to strengthen brand identity, supply chain, and retailer compliance.

Name: Jack and Jill Foundation Grants
Description: The Jack and Jill of America Foundation funds equity-centered programs for children and families in under-resourced communities through a portfolio of grants focused on education, health & wellness, and family stabilization/economic opportunity. Its grants include Our Village Grants (up to $10,000) for housing/food access/digital connectivity and other family supports, education grants like Reading Corner and College Prep (up to $5,000) and STEM (up to $10,000), and health & wellness grants for nonprofits (up to $10,000) and chapter partnerships (up to $3,000) to expand access to physical and mental health resources.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- 501(c)(3)s
- those with a fiscal sponsor with a 501(c)(3) designation
- those that are public agencies, including school districts

Name: IndyArts Project Grants
Description: Indy Arts Council’s Project Grants provide $2,000–$10,000 to Marion County (Indianapolis) artists and 501(c)(3) nonprofits to create and present arts and culture activities in public spaces (parks, libraries, community centers, etc.). Projects must take place in Marion County between May 1, 2026 and April 30, 2027, and require a letter of support from the public venue.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible artists:
- Are 18 years of age or older.
- Are able to provide a Social Security Number (SSN), Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) or A-Number/USCIS Number.
- Are a resident of Marion County.

Eligible organizations:
- Have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status.
- Are Indianapolis-based and physically headquartered in Marion County.
- Must include artist(s) in their programs or projects and pay them fairly.

Name: Make It In Brooklyn (MIIB) Ag Tech Pitch Contest 2026
Description: Pitch contest for ag-tech startups connected to the Make It In Brooklyn program. Finalists pitch live for cash prizes and support, with judging by industry experts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Ag-tech startup/company with a product or solution relevant to agriculture/food systems.
- Ability to participate in the contest pitch event and any program requirements outlined by MIIB.

Name: LinkedIn Future of Work Fund
Description: LinkedIn’s Future of Work Fund provides grant funding and in-kind support to nonprofits helping young adults (especially those facing barriers) prepare for and succeed in an AI-powered workforce. The fund prioritizes organizations using AI innovation and AI-fluency training –alongside human skills development – to expand economic opportunity, particularly in the U.S., U.K., France, Germany, and India. Applications for the 2026 fund close March 15, 2026, with most grants expected to range from $200,000 to $300,000 USD.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Legally registered nonprofit, charity, or equivalent not-for-profit organization in the country of operation, recognized by the appropriate governing authority
--U.S.-based organizations must hold 501(c)(3) status
--Organizations must be able to receive philanthropic grant funding directly
- Workforce development focus with programs, services, and/or influencing systems that help people access, prepare for, and/or succeed in an AI-powered workforce 
- Demonstrate a clear use of AI innovation to expand economic opportunity and/or commitment to prepare young adults to succeed in an AI-powered workforce
- Support young adults and career starters overcoming barriers to economic opportunity

Name: AAPIC Small Grants Application
Description: The AAPIC Small Grants program awards up to $5,000 to community-driven projects serving AAPI communities across Massachusetts. Funding covers a range of needs including programs, artists, administrative costs, small businesses, and emergency support for food, housing, and legal assistance. The application deadline is March 15, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- 501(c)(3) nonprofits
- Individual & artists 
- Community groups
- small businesses

Name: Mozilla Foundation Democracy x AI Incubator
Description: Mozilla Foundation is seeking proposals for its 2026 “Democracy x AI” Incubator cohort, funding technologists with working, early-traction AI projects that strengthen democracy by improving information quality, boosting institutional transparency/accountability, or protecting civic space. The cohort plans to fund about 10 projects at $50,000 each for 12 months, offering mentorship, workshops, and community support, with a potential follow-on Tier II opportunity of $250,000 for standout projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
You should apply if you have:
- A working technology that people can actually use — not just an idea or wireframe. You've built something functional, even if it's at a very early stage, and you’re ready for what comes next.
- A committed team who can execute over 12 months. If you are selected for this grant, you should be able to hit the ground running without having to do any significant hiring.
- A commitment to openness that will expand the impact of your work. At least some of your code is open source (e.g., you use an open core model, your codebase is closed but you publish open datasets, etc.) or you have a clear roadmap for open sourcing at least part of your codebase and will commit to doing so during the grant period. You'll share learnings publicly, make datasets available where appropriate, and document your process for others to learn from. You believe transparency and community stewardship will make your project stronger. If you’re new to working open, we’ll provide you with the resources and experts to help you navigate things like licensing and creating on-ramps for participation to outside contributors.

Name: DMB Small Business Digital Technical Assistance Program
Description: The Digital Small Business Program, offered by Detroit Means Business (DMB) and the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation, is an application-based initiative helping Detroit small businesses implement and integrate digital tools such as POS, CRM, and e-commerce platforms. Selected businesses receive expert implementation and training to strengthen operations, improve data utilization, and support sustainable growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - Detroit small business

Name: Anthropologie x Nest Fellowship Program
Description: The Anthropologie x Nest Fellowship is an 18-month program for emerging creative entrepreneurs that includes business education, mentorship from Anthropologie executives, and marketing support from both organizations. Fellows also gain direct sales opportunities through Anthropologie.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- create handmade, small-batch apparel, accessories, jewelry, or home decor
- women-led brand

Name: C3 Impact Fund Emerging Developers Capital Program
Description: The Emerging Developers Capital Readiness Program is a six-month cohort-based educational program from Diversified Community Impact and C3 Impact Fund that helps experienced practitioners strengthen skills in capital structures, financial modeling, compliance, and community impact planning for responsible housing and neighborhood revitalization. The program includes workshops, advisory sessions, online tools, and a capstone presentation.

Name: Headstream Accelerator 2026
Description: Headstream Accelerator 2026 is a four-month, virtual-first program for early-stage teams scaling tech-enabled solutions that improve mental well-being for at-risk teens (especially ages 13–19) in or adjacent to education and healthcare, with a preference for historically excluded communities. Selected participants receive a $30,000 non-dilutive stipend, youth co-creation support, and coaching/advisor access, and must have at least a functional prototype and sustainable funding model; applications run Jan 15–Mar 15, 2026, with the program starting in July and an in-person kickoff July 28–30, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: We support early-stage digital solutions advancing youth mental well-being, especially those reaching historically excluded communities. If you have a working prototype, are preparing to launch, or are ready to scale, we encourage you to apply. Note: Idea-stage submissions are not eligible.

Name: 2026 Ladies Who Launch (LWL) Launch Program
Description: Ladies Who Launch’s 2026 Launch Program (with support from Boundless Futures Foundation) will award 10 women-owned, impact-driven small businesses a $10,000 grant plus mentorship and an eight-week training program. Eligible applicants must be U.S.-based, for-profit (not nonprofit/franchise/affiliate), not politically or religiously focused, have an EIN or business bank account, be 51%+ women-owned, and have $100,000–$499,999 in annual gross revenue, with social impact embedded in the product or business model. Applications close March 17, 2026 (11:59pm ET) and winners will be announced by March 31, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Social impact must be part of the business’s product or financial model.
- Located within the United States or US territories.
- Not a non-profit organization.
- Not a franchise, subsidiary, or otherwise affiliated with another organization.
- Must not focus on political or religiously-affiliated work.
- Have an EIN, or a business bank account.
- More than 51% women-owned.
- Have earned more than $100,000, but less than $499,999 in gross annual revenue.

Name: Clean Energy Leadership Institute 2026 Fall Fellowship
Description: The 2026 CELI Fellowship is a July 29–December 3, 2026 leadership program for early- to mid-career professionals committed to advancing an equitable clean energy transition, with fully virtual cohorts (by U.S. time zone) and in-person cohorts in the Bay Area, Chicago, NYC, and Washington, DC. Applications open now with tiered deadlines (Feb 18 free “Early Bird,” Mar 16 $25, Mar 18 $100), interviews in mid-April, and acceptance notifications on May 20, 2026. Tuition is $5,900 (employer-supported) or $3,750 (self-pay) with financial assistance.

Name: Verizon Small Business Digital Ready Amplify Your Brand
Description: Verizon Digital Ready’s Amplify Your Brand promotion will select five U.S.-based for-profit small businesses to win a professionally produced content package from The LemonAd Stand valued at $17,000, including a strategic content plan, a 2–3 minute promo video plus short reels, a custom landing page, and launch-ready marketing assets. To apply, participants must register on Digital Ready, complete three eligible courses/events in online marketing, branding, or website design, and submit an application by March 18, 2026 (11:59 PM PT).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply for the Amplify Your Brand Promotion, you must meet the following criteria:
- Be a for-profit business based in one of the 50 United States or Washington, D.C. Non-profits are not eligible to apply.
- Be 18 years of age or older.
- Have a market-ready product or service, meaning you are already selling to or actively serving customers.
- Have a verifiable online business presence, demonstrated by at least one of the following:
-- A live website
-- Business social media account (e.g., Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X)
-- Google Business Profile 
- Have an established marketing channel to reach customers – this can be either:
-- An email list and email marketing platform (e.g., MailChimp, Constant Contact) or
-- An existing business social media account 
- Have an established brand, meaning you already have a business logo and/or a brand color palette.
- Be able to provide required business and financial verification documentation (W-9s, ACH, etc. if selected as a finalist.

Name: Ripple Digital Leap Forward Accelerator
Description: Accion Opportunity Fund and Ripple are launching the fully virtual Ripple Digital Leap Forward Accelerator to help 50 small business owners strengthen their digital systems and growth capabilities. The 8-week program includes expert-led training (tools, automation, payments, marketing, operations/HR/finance), a personalized digital roadmap, capital-preparedness support, networking, and a $10,000 grant upon completion. Eligible businesses must be at least 1 year old with $100K–$1.5M revenue, 1–5 employees (excluding the owner), a working website and business bank account, and applications are due March 18, 2026 at 5:00pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small business owners may apply if they:
- Have operated their business for at least 1 year
- Generate $100,000 – $1,500,000  in annual revenue
