- Employ 1–5 staff (not including the owner)
- Have a functioning business website
- Hold a business bank account
- Commit to fully participating for the duration of the program

Name: SESSION Foundation Grant
Description: The SESSION Foundation is accepting applications for a 2026 grant of $80,000 aimed at female-founded businesses based in North Texas. The grant mirrors the original funding used to launch SESSION Pilates and includes both capital and mentorship from leading female founders in the region. Female-founded businesses looking to fund their next stage of growth are encouraged to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: female-founded business in North Texas

Name: DAG Foundation Prize
Description: The DAG Foundation offers three annual $20,000 prizes in Literature, Music, and Visual Art, each designed to support innovative, emerging-to-mid-career artists whose work pushes the boundaries of their respective fields. Recipients must have some professional track record but not yet have received major recognition, and funds can be used flexibly for project-related expenses like research, recording, materials, or studio space. Each prize is intended to support a specific new project already in progress or in development.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Literature: 
- You have published, as of the application deadline, one book of prose for an adult readership with a nationally distributed U.S. press. Online publication and self-publication do not meet this criterion, nor do books first published in another country or in a language other than English.
- You aim to publish a second book of prose in the U.S., written in English.
- This second project must be substantially underway.
- You reside in the United States as of the application deadline.
- A “book of prose” may contain elements of poetry, visual art, or other forms but should be primarily recognized/categorized as prose.
- If you have won, or been a finalist or shortlisted for, the Pulitzer Prize, a National Book Award, a National Book Critics Circle Award, an award from the American Academy for Arts and Letters, a PEN America Literary Award, the PEN/Faulkner Award, or the Booker Prize, you are not eligible for the DAG Prize.
- If you have published a second book of prose, or have a second book of prose under contract, by the application deadline, you are not eligible for the DAG Prize.
- We do not invite or accept nominations from agents, editors, mentors, or peers.

Music: 
- You are a working musician, songwriter or producer/engineer.
- You have some combination of the following:
    - History of national and/or international touring.
    - Releases on an established label or recognized distributor.
    - Songwriting credits on an album, film, television project or other significant body of work.
    - Production credit on an album, film, television project or other significant body of work.
    - Publishing deal with established publishing company.
    - Dedicated following as indicated by ticket sales, touring history, headlining shows, and/or social media engagement.
    - Significant live or recorded collaborations with more established artists.
- You reside in the United States as of the application deadline.
- If you have won a major national or international music award (Grammy, Juno, etc.), or currently have a major label/publishing deal or a major commercially successful release (gold/platinum record, etc.)  you are not eligible for the DAG Prize. 

Visual Art: 
- You have at least two of the following:
    - A small art grant or prize.
    - Residency at a reputable arts colony.
    - MFA from an accredited studio arts program.
    - Solo show at a curated gallery or artist-run space.
    - Participation in a group show at a curated gallery or artist-run space.
    - Reviews or interviews in reputable arts publications.
    - One or more pieces in a prestigious gallery or museum.

Name: Arts Foundation for Tucson and Southern Arizona Artist Grant
Description: The Arts Foundation for Tucson and Southern Arizona is offering 2026 Artist Grants of up to $10,000 to individual artists living and working in Tucson/Southern Arizona (including Tribal Nations) to pay artist fees/wages for providing specific arts services to an identified “client” (e.g., a nonprofit, business, school, community group, or government agency). Applications are open Dec 11, 2025–Mar 19, 2026 for projects running July 1, 2026–May 31, 2027; no match is required, but applicants must submit work samples, a budget, and a co-signed MOU with the client, and awards are decided via peer panel based on capacity, impact, and civic/community benefit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must have been practicing as an artist since 2019.
- Reside and provide services in counties and regions south of the Gila River. This includes Pima, Santa Cruz and Cochise counties and southern portions of Pinal, Yuma, Greenlee, Graham, Maricopa County and/or Native Sovereign Nations of Ak-Chin Indian Community, Sovereign
Nation of the Cocopah, Quechan Tribe of the Fort Yuma Indian Reservation, Gila River Indian Community, Pascua Yaqui Tribe, Tohono O’odham Nation, San Carlos Apache Nation

Name: Sprouts Pitch Slam with Startup CPG
Description: Startup CPG is hosting an application-only “Grocery Run: Forager Finds Pitch Slam” on May 14 in Phoenix, giving selected brands an in-person slot to pitch Sprouts for potential placement in the Sprouts Innovation Set and to meet category managers via roundtables and 1:1s. Brands must apply by March 19, be the applicant from the business (not an agency), and be in the Startup CPG Slack channel and brand database. If chosen, you’ll get an email with next steps to confirm your meeting.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Meetings are IN PERSON and you need to go to Arizona for the pitch
- Application must be submitted by someone in the business, not an agency, third party, etc.
- You must also be in the Startup CPG Slack channel and brand database

Name: Prince George's County Community Resilience Hub Grant Program
Description: The Prince George's County Community Resilience Hub Grant Program, administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust, funds projects that help communities prepare for and recover from climate-related events such as extreme heat and flooding. Grants of up to $50,000 are available to nonprofits, faith-based organizations, municipalities, and other community groups for projects in Prince George's County, Maryland, with roughly $217,000 in total funding available. The next application deadline is March 19, 2026 at 4:00 PM EST, with awards anticipated in June 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Prince George’s County and the Trust welcome applicants from the following organizations:

Nonprofit organizations
Community associations, including homeowner associations (HOAs)
Faith-based organizations
Municipalities
Watershed organizations
Public and independent higher educational institutions

Name: City of Philadelphia Neighborhood Economic Development Grant
Description: The City of Philadelphia's Department of Commerce is offering the Neighborhood Economic Development Grant, providing between $50,000 and $500,000 to nonprofit organizations working to create economic opportunities and revitalize neighborhoods for low- and moderate-income residents. Funding can be used for commercial space projects across four categories: planning, pre-development, development, and acquisition. The application deadline is March 19, 2026 at 5 p.m., and applications must be submitted through eContract Philly using Opportunity Number 21260128120838.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The next round of funding for the Neighborhood Economic Development Grant is open! The grant helps nonprofit organizations, including community development corporations, increase their funding capacity to create economic opportunities that revitalize the neighborhoods they serve.

Nonprofit organizations can apply for a proposed compensation of between $50,000 and $500,000 to fund commercial space for businesses providing goods and services accessible to low- and moderate-income residents, while increasing job creation. Eligible projects can be funded in the following four categories: planning, pre-development, development, and acquisition.

Name: Naturally Network Naturally Rising Pitch Slam
Description:
Naturally Rising is a pitch competition for purpose-driven, retail-ready natural product (CPG) brands that are Naturally Network members, U.S.-based, and generally under $2M in revenue. Brands apply once to be considered for their regional chapter competition, where finalists receive mentorship and retail-readiness resources, and regional winners advance to the national finals at Newtopia Now in Denver (Aug 18–20, 2026) with perks like a complimentary booth. Application deadlines vary by chapter, running from Feb 6 to March 20, 2026.

Application Deadlines:
- February 6, 2026 - Colorado, NorCal
- February 13, 2026 - San Diego 
- March 20, 2026 - Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Minnesota, New England, New York, Seattle, Wisconsin

Name: Field Foundation Leaders for a New Chicago Award
Description: The Leaders for a New Chicago Awards will recognize 8 Chicago-based grassroots civic leaders, awarding $50,000 each to individuals driving transformative change in the city in partnership with the MacArthur Foundation. Each awardee’s affiliated nonprofit will also receive a $25,000 general operating grant.

Name: National Grid Foundation RFP
Description: The National Grid Foundation has launched an RFP to award $250,000 annually in general operating support grants to small nonprofits in New York and Massachusetts. Eligible 501(c)(3) organizations with budgets of $1 million or less must align with focus areas such as STEM/early literacy, food insecurity, workforce readiness, or energy affordability and efficiency. Applications are due by March 20, 2026, and the funding aims to strengthen nonprofits’ long-term sustainability and community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Be a 501(c)(3) located within National Grid’s New York or Massachusetts service area
- Have an annual budget of $1 million or less
- Align with one or more of the Foundation’s focus areas:
-- Out of School Time STEM/STEAM Programs (K-5) and Early Literacy Programs (pre-K-3)
-- Food Insecurity
-- Workforce Readiness
-- Energy Affordability, Energy Literacy, and Energy Efficiency

Name: The Coalition Community Quarterback Grant for Small Business
Description: The Community Quarterback for Small Business Grant provides up to $50,000 to 501(c)(3) nonprofits in 14 designated market areas to help them serve as “community quarterbacks” that coordinate and strengthen local small business ecosystems, particularly in under-resourced communities. In addition to funding, grantees receive advisory services, technical assistance, templates, and training to map and build a more connected support system for small businesses. Applications are due March 20, 2026, with awards supporting staff capacity and ecosystem-building projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organizations must:
- Be designated by the IRS as a 501(c)3 organization or have a fiscal sponsor that is designated by the IRS as a 501(c)3 organization
- Have the ability to measure and report on established outcomes-based success metrics aligned to strategic objectives, which includes providing a forecast of expected outcomes in the application and may also require periodic impact reports with actual project/program results.
- Be located in an eligible Market Area: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Maryland, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio (Cincinnati Only), Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia

Name: Brooklyn Org Neighborhood Collective Impact Project
Description: Brooklyn Org's Neighborhood Collective Impact Projects offer up to $25,000 each to three selected partnerships of at least two community-based nonprofits collaborating to address pressing neighborhood challenges in Brooklyn, with a focus on affordability, public safety, and mental health.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
- The lead organization must be a 501(c)(3) or fiscally sponsored nonprofit with a minimum annual budget of $100,000, and proposals must advance racial justice and serve historically underserved BIPOC communities.

Name: Arizona Startup Spring Training
Description: Startup Spring Training is a free month-long program running March 16 to April 10, 2026, offering Arizona entrepreneurs four virtual workshops, an in-person Launch Camp on March 27, and a Showcase Celebration marking the program's fifth year. Topics cover funding, marketing, technology, and cash flow, with sessions led by experienced small business professionals. The program is open to entrepreneurs at any stage, from idea-phase to growing businesses, across a range of industries.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Arizona based entrepreneurs
- First-time participants ready to strengthen their foundation
- Returning SST participants who want to sharpen their skills and reconnect with community
- Food and beverage businesses
- Retail and product-based businesses
- Wellness practitioners and creatives
- Skilled trades and local service businesses
- Idea-stage, early-revenue, and growing small businesses

Name: BGE Community Safety Grants
Description: BGE's 2026 Community Safety Grant Program awards between $2,500 and $10,000 to community organizations for projects focused on neighborhood safety, emergency response, and resilience building, with all projects required to be completed by June 2026. Applications are open through March 22, 2026, and funded projects must align with BGE's commitment to partnering with emergency responders and strengthening community safety.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organization must be a 501c3 non-profit.

The project must be geographically located in the BGE service territory

Grant range - $2,500-$10,000

Projects must be completed before June 2, 2027.

Grants are considered for new and existing programs that fall within the description guidelines and requests funding that clearly demonstrates collaboration in response efforts to urgent needs of the community. 

All applications must include a project budget indicating how the grant will be spent.

Applicants requesting funding for basic operating expenses or capital projects will not be accepted.

Applicants will be notified of the status of their application by June 1, 2026. 

Organizations who receive a Community Safety Grant will not be eligible for another grant in 2026.

Community Safety Grant applications will close on March 22, 2026. Late submissions will not be accepted.

Click here to apply

Name: National Endowment for the Arts Research Awards
Description: The NEA’s Research Awards program funds arts research through two tracks: Research Grants in the Arts (studies on the value/impact of the arts in American life) and NEA Research Labs (long-term, interdisciplinary research agendas that produce multiple studies and public-facing outputs). Funding ranges from $20,000–$100,000 for Research Grants and $100,000–$300,000 for Research Labs, with a 1:1 cost share required; eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state/local/tribal entities (and for Labs, also U.S. higher-ed institutions). Applications are submitted in two parts, with Grants.gov due March 23, 2026 and the NEA Applicant Portal due April 2, 2026, and the earliest project start date is January 1, 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Research Grants in the Arts*: 
Organizations eligible to apply include:
- Nonprofit, tax-exempt 501(c)(3), U.S. organizations;
- Units of state or local government; or
- Federally recognized tribal communities or tribes.
- Applicant organizations must have completed at least 5 years of operating history prior to the application deadline.

NEA Research Labs*: 
Organizations eligible to apply include:
- U.S. institutions of higher education, or
- Nonprofit, tax-exempt 501(c)(3), U.S. organizations.
- Applicant organizations must have a five-year history of commissioning and conducting research in the behavioral or social sciences, and communicating research findings and policy implications through reports and/or convenings, at the time of application.

*Both programs:
- Funding is not available in either program for individuals, applications submitted by a fiscal sponsor, commercial/for-profit enterprises, State Arts Agencies, or Regional Arts Organizations.
- Full Eligibility criteria can be found in each opportunity’s Program Guidelines document.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Planet & Purpose Grant
Description: The Planet & Purpose Grant, presented by the KSI Foundation, will award $5,000 to a U.S.-based woman entrepreneur who owns at least 51% of an established CPG (consumer packaged goods) business with a strong sustainability focus. Eligible businesses must be product-based (food, beverage, or CPG), operating for over six months, generating at least $5,000 in revenue, and demonstrate meaningful environmental integration in their brand and operations. Applications close March 23, 2026, with the winner announced April 22, and funds to be used between May and September 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Identify as a woman entrepreneur who owns 51% of an established business. 
- Business must be an entrepreneur’s full-time job. 
- Be in business for more than six months. 
- The company has earned at least $5,000 in revenue. 
- The company demonstrates a clear commitment to sustainability and environmental responsibility that is meaningfully integrated into their brand’s product, operations, or long-term strategy. 
- Be a U.S. Citizen.
- Have a product-based business (food, beverage, or consumer packaged good).

Name: The Pearce Summer Fellows Program
Description: The Pearce Summer Fellows Program is a summer startup program run by Underscore VC in Boston, offering academic innovators (students, researchers, or professors) funding starting at $50K, office space, mentorship, and access to a broad network of industry experts.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
Academic Innovators: Current students (undergraduate through PhD), researchers, or professors from any Boston-area academic institution. At least one founding team member must have an academic affiliation. Whether you're at the idea stage or already have users, we want to hear from you. It’s never too early. The program offers flexible financing to meet you where you are.

Additional Info: 
The program runs June through August and requires at least one founding team member to have an academic affiliation.

Name: LearnLaunch Fund + Breakthrough to Scale Accelerator
Description: LearnLaunch’s Breakthrough to Scale 2026 is a 10-week accelerator (remote with 1 week on-site in Boston) for early-revenue edtech and workforce learning companies, combining a $50K initial investment, milestone-based follow-on funding, expert masterclasses, and hands-on support from a dedicated Venture Partner and mentors. It targets startups with a working product and market traction (typically $200K+ ARR for those seeking funding) across K–12, higher ed, workforce development, or lifelong learning. Requires attending an informational webinar before applying.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- INDUSTRY:  We are looking for companies that are building innovative products and services for the K-12, Higher Ed, Workforce development & Lifelong learning markets.
- BUSINESS MODELS: We invest into companies that transact direct-to-consumer (B2C), business-to-government (B2G), or with enterprise clients.
- STAGE: Applicants must have a product, revenue, and have entered the market but need targeted help to deeply analyze customer needs, advance go-to-market tactics, design scale into operations and, importantly, deliver impactful, efficacy-driven outcomes. Companies seeking funding should have at least $200k in annual recurring revenue (ARR).
- INVESTMENT: Companies are eligible for investment broken down into two phases: first, a $50k initial investment upon acceptance to the Program, and second, follow-on funding based on individual milestones evaluated 6 months after the Program completion.
- PARTICIPATION REQUIREMENTS: At least one co-founder, usually the CEO, must be available to attend the Program (approximately 6 hours per week of participation and projects). We do not work with companies that plan to attend other accelerator Programs during the time of the Program.

Name: CFDA x NY Forward Grant Fund
Description: The CFDA x NY Forward Grant Fund is a partnership between the CFDA and New York State’s Department of State to support innovation and local production in the Garment District. The program provides partially matching grants covering up to two-thirds of eligible costs for new machinery, related capital improvements, software, and training. Eligible applicants must operate within the Garment District Strategic Investment Area, have at least two years of revenue under $10M annually, and include contract manufacturers, innovative material producers, or brands with small-batch in-house production.

Name: IBM Impact Accelerator
Description: IBM’s Impact Accelerator is a two-year, no-cost program inviting nonprofits, government entities, and academic institutions worldwide to propose education and workforce development initiatives – ideally AI-driven – that expand access to learning, clarify career pathways, and strengthen workforce systems. Selected organizations collaborate with IBM experts and technology (e.g., watsonx/Granite, IBM Cloud, consulting) to build human-centered solutions like AI-enabled teaching tools, career navigation platforms, and workforce analytics. Proposals are due March 25, 2026, and finalists will be contacted later in spring 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - Nonprofit organizations and government entities, including academic institutions across the globe interested in developing AI-driven solutions for educational and workforce development challenges.

Name: Latino Business Action Network (LBAN) Startup Accelerator
Description: The LBAN Startup Accelerator is a 9-week hybrid program held at Stanford Graduate School of Business designed for early-stage U.S.-based founders who have raised between $200K and $1.5M in venture or angel funding. The program combines two in-person weekends at Stanford with weekly online curriculum, focusing on product-market fit, go-to-market strategy, team building, and fundraising. The next cohort runs March 27 – May 31, 2026, and is offered once per year each spring.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We welcome startup founders of all backgrounds and industries based in the U.S. who:

Lead a U.S.-based startup and reside in the U.S.

 
Have raised $200K–$1.5M from venture capital or angel investors

 
Hold one of the top two leadership roles (e.g., CEO, COO)

 
Are actively working to define product-market fit and prepare for growth

Open to founders from any industry or U.S. state.

Designed for founders who are ready to engage deeply, challenge their assumptions, and commit to building a scalable business while contributing to a stronger entrepreneurial ecosystem

Name: XRC Ventures x SHOPLINE Brand Builder Grant
Description: The XRC Brand Builder Grant, powered by SHOPLINE, offers $20K–$50K+ in non-dilutive funding to early-stage, post-launch CPG brands generating under $15M in annual revenue to help them scale their e-commerce operations. In addition to funding, selected brands receive a fully managed migration to SHOPLINE, tech stack integrations, workshops, mentorship, and access to a network of founders, operators, and investors. The program runs from May to September 2026, requires participants to migrate to SHOPLINE, and includes both virtual programming and in-person events in Los Angeles.

Name: Carolina Career-Connected Learning Challenge
Description: The Leon Levine Foundation’s Carolina Career-Connected Learning Challenge is a multi-million-dollar competition offering one-year grants (typically $125,000–$250,000, up to $500,000) to scale proven career-connected learning programs serving Grades 7–14 in North and South Carolina. The initiative aims to boost economic mobility for low-income and first-generation students by aligning K–12, postsecondary education, and employers around pathways to livable-wage, AI-resilient jobs. Eligible 501(c)(3) organizations with at least $500,000 in contributed revenue must demonstrate strong outcomes, employer co-design, scalability, and sustainability, with full applications due March 27 and awards announced in June.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Status: 501(c)(3) organizations or those with a fiscal sponsor. Collaborations and partnerships are welcome, but one organization must serve as the lead applicant.
- Financials: Minimum of $500,000 in non-governmental contributed revenue (per latest IRS Form 990).
- Geography: While organizations can be based anywhere, the project must serve students in North or South Carolina.
- Focus: Programs must currently serve students in Grades 7-14 or first-generation college students, with a primary focus on low-income populations.

Name: WeddingPro Grant Program
Description: The 2026 WeddingPro Grant Program is a $500,000 initiative supporting small wedding businesses through grants of $10,000–$50,000 or one year of free advertising on The Knot and WeddingWire, plus mentorship, education, and promotional opportunities. It is open to U.S.-based wedding businesses operating for at least six months, with at least 50% of revenue from weddings and under $250,000 in annual revenue. Applications require a short video explaining the business and use of funds, and are open February 23–March 27, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- At least 6 months in business with an established LLC (or equivalent legal entity)
- An active revenue stream from operations
- At least 50% of total business activity comes from weddings

Name: 2026 Diverse Teacher Pipeline Grant
Description: The Center for Black Educator Development is offering the 2026 Diverse Teacher Pipeline Grant, providing up to $100,000 to nonprofit organizations or public schools working to recruit, develop, or retain diverse teachers in their communities. Eligible applicants must be a 501(c)(3) or public school institution that has been operating for at least one year, has at least one full-time employee, and has filed the required financial documents. The application deadline is March 27, 2026, and while organizations nationwide can apply, priority is given to those serving specific states including North Carolina, California, New York, and several others.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Please note that this is a one-year grant, and the requested grant funds must be used strictly for the purposes outlined in the proposal and budget. Upon grant reporting, all expenditures must align with the goals and objectives specified. 

Additional eligibility criteria include: 

The organization is a 501(c)(3) organization or public school institution that seeks to address the need to recruit and/or retain more diverse teachers. 
The organization is based in and doing work on behalf of communities in our priority regions.  
The organization has been operating for at least one year.  
The organization employs at least one full-time equivalent employee.  
A 990 or 990 EZ Form has been filed on behalf of the organization for the most recent fiscal year, or the organization's most recent audited financial statement can be provided.  
The deadline to apply for this opportunity is Friday, March 27, 2026 at 11:59pm EST. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact Mimi (Woldeyohannes) McKee at mimi.woldeyohannes (at) cbed.org 

*Please note, that this grant opportunity does not discriminate or consider the racial background of any grant applicant and is open to organizations of all racial backgrounds.

Name: Gravy Wealth Pitch Competition 2026
Description: Gravy Wealth’s Owner Mode: Pitch Competition 2026 will invest $25,000 each in four pre-seed to seed, AI-first or automation-first startups building “access infrastructure,” with a focus on expanding who can build wealth, invest, and participate in value creation. Applications are open through March 27, finalists will be notified April 13, and winners will be announced live on May 22 at the Owner Mode Summit; selected founders also get access to Gravy’s customer, operator, and investor network.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible companies are pre-seed to seed, industry agnostic, and building access infrastructure with an automation or AI-first approach. Companies should be at or below a $13M post-money valuation.

Name: Healing Arts Chicago Summit - Creative Producer 2026 RFQ
Description: The Chicago Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events is seeking an experienced Creative Producer (or team) to plan and execute the 2026 Healing Arts Chicago Summit, a citywide event focused on arts, health, and wellness, scheduled for October 10, 2026. The selected producer will receive a $75,000 contract covering both their fee and production budget, and must demonstrate strong experience in community-focused event production, collaboration, and arts/health initiatives; applications are due March 27.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must:
• Be at least 18 years old
• Include a resume/CV with at least 5 years of professional experience as an administrator, educator, and/or facilitator
• Currently have or be able to secure commercial general liability insurance and other necessary insurance and documentation at the time of contracting; consultants/teams selected to interview will receive a copy of the insurance requirements
• City of Chicago employees are not eligible to apply

QUALIFICATIONS
• Must be an organization, business, team or individual with at least five years of experience providing successful management and oversight of community focused arts
• Bachelor’s Degree in a related field supplemented with 4-6 years of experience; or an equivalent combination of education and training required
• Have organizational capacity to carry out the activities
• Have experience in successfully delivering similar activities previously
• Demonstrate experience and a strong record of managing large dollar contracts
• Deep knowledge of Chicago arts, culture, and/or community health ecosystems
• Applicants should have some understanding of and experience in arts and health practices and/or research 
• Must be self-directed, innovative, and able to project manage event coordination
effectively
• Excellent oral and written communication skills required with the ability to effectively interact with personnel at all levels (both inside and outside of the organization)
• Must be able to work well within a culturally diverse environment with the ability to handle all situations with tact and diplomacy
• Must be flexible, innovative and possess excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
• Must have the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and demands
• Bilingual applicants are highly encouraged to apply

Name: WURD Radio Presents: Level Up Contest 2026
Description: WURD Radio's Level Up contest celebrates Women's History Month by spotlighting Black women business owners and entrepreneurs making an impact in the Philadelphia area. Nominees — either self-nominated or nominated by others — can win a $5,000 marketing and community outreach prize package that includes radio advertising, an on-air interview, social media promotion, newsletter features, and website placement. The nomination deadline was March 27, 2026 at 5pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Level Up CONTEST:

A Celebration of Women Entrepreneurs and Innovators

In celebration of Women's History Month, the Level Up contest is back! Each year, we highlight women business owners. You can nominate your business or your favorite woman-owned business.

How It Works:

Throughout March, WURD will feature Black women business owners and entrepreneurs who are making a difference in Philadelphia communities. We invite you to nominate Black women business owners — or nominate your own business. The contest is open to businesses based in the Philadelphia area. 

Please complete the nomination form and submit it by Friday, March 27, at 5 p.m. ET. 

Winners will receive a marketing and community outreach prize package valued at $5,000, including:


Radio advertising on WURD Radio 
On-air interview on WURD 
Social media outreach on WURD platforms 
Acknowledgment in an edition of the weekly digital WURD newsletter 
Business featured on WURD Radio website (wurdradio.com)
The Level Up competition is sponsored by Comcast and PECO.

Name: Build In Tulsa Women Entrepreneur (W.E.) Accelerator
Description: W.E. Build is a full-time, in-person 12-week accelerator in Tulsa, Oklahoma for women founders leading revenue-generating tech, tech-enabled, or CPG ventures who are ready to scale by 25% or more. Accepted founders receive a $25,000 non-dilutive business award, business training, mentorship, legal consultation, coworking space, and cost-of-living stipends for housing and childcare, but must commit to full-time residency in Tulsa for the program duration of September 2–November 20, 2026. The application deadline was March 27, 2026, with up to 10 companies accepted per cohort.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
W.E. Build is a full-time, in-person accelerator in Tulsa, OK, built for founders who are already generating revenue and ready to grow.

Each cohort includes up to 10 companies at the emerging or strong product-market fit stage. Over three months, founders focus on what actually drives growth: closing more sales, clearly defining their ideal customers, tightening up their financials, and building repeatable systems that support 25% growth.

W.E. Builders don’t just follow a playbook—they create their own. The program helps founders develop a customized growth strategy while also strengthening their personal and professional brands. This is a performance-based accelerator for founders who want results.

You’ll learn how to set the right goals, track what matters, generate leads consistently, and use data to make smarter decisions—fast.

The W.E. BUILD Program Requirements
Startups must be U.S.-based legal entities incorporated as an LLC, S-Corp, or C-Corp.
Accepted founders are required to maintain a full-time presence in Tulsa, Oklahoma—via local residency or relocation—for the program’s duration (September 2 – November 20, 2026) with a 40-hour weekly commitment.
Founders must lead a scalable Tech, Tech-enabled, or CPG venture.
Founders should have a clear intent to scale venture revenue by 25% or more during the 12-week program.

Name: Lansing Economic Area Partnership (LEAP) Elevate x Ascend: Business Accelerator Program
Description: Elevate x Ascend is a free 16-week business accelerator program by the Lansing Economic Area Partnership (LEAP) designed for established BIPOC-owned businesses in Clinton, Eaton, or Ingham County, Michigan. The program offers structured learning, one-on-one coaching, and peer networking focused on revenue growth, financial clarity, branding, and capital readiness. Applications close March 29, with the program running from May through September 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business owner identifies as Black, Indigenous, or People of Color (BIPOC) – including Black, Indigenous, Asian, Pacific Islander, Middle Eastern, Latino/a/x, and other entrepreneurs of color
- For-profit business
- Have completed the TREK Small Business Support Hub
- Business has been operating for at least one year
- Business has active or recent customers and consistent revenue
- Business is founded or registered in Clinton, Eaton, or Ingham County (MI)
- Business is not a franchise or national chain

Name: Create & Cultivate 100 List
Description: The Create & Cultivate 100 List honors 100 women each year who are leading, building, and shaping culture across industries such as beauty, fashion, tech, money, sports, and more. The 2026 list spans generations and career stages – from rising stars to legacy leaders – and nominations are open for individuals making meaningful impact at scale. Applicants must submit nominee details, social links, and a statement explaining why the nominee deserves recognition.

Name: NYC 2026 Borough Cultural Grant
Description: The 2026 Borough Cultural Grant, funded by the New York City Tourism Foundation and Borough Presidents’ Offices, supports NYC-based nonprofit (501(c)(3)) organizations in promoting cultural programs and events that attract tourism, with typical awards of $5,000 or less. Eligible projects must take place in 2026, focus on marketing and promotion (not operational or production costs), and require a complete application including a project proposal, budget, and supporting documents.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- All grant recipients must be registered as a 501(c)3 with the State of New York.
- Applicants’ projects must fall primarily within calendar year 2026.
- All recipients must be in compliance with prior funding requirements.
- Projects eligible for funding under the program should be tourist facing and shall include, but are not limited to, promotional materials for cultural institutions, programs, and events (i.e., paid media, print or digital content, and/or videos).

Name: Google Creative Fellowship
Description: Google's Creative Fellowship is a paid, 6-month full-time program (mid-June to mid-December 2026) that places emerging creative talent on in-house Google teams — including Brand Studio, Creative Lab, Google Cloud, and YouTube Creative Studio — to work on real projects in roles spanning motion design, copywriting, creative technology, and more. Applicants must be new professionals with 5 years or less of experience, have U.S. work authorization, and be able to live in the city of their applied role (New York, San Francisco, or Los Angeles). The application deadline is March 30, and interested candidates can apply for up to two roles at creative-fellowship@google.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The program is for emerging creative thinkers (0 - 5 years of experience) who have a clear point of view and passion for making things and telling stories. We’re looking for individuals excited to bring their unique voice and craft to Google’s creative teams. Each creative team at Google is looking for something different, so we encourage creatives to apply with work that best captures their craft.

Name: Bundle x Joy Women's History Month Giveaway
Description: Bundle x Joy, a female-founded pet wellness brand, is celebrating Women’s History Month with a $25,000 giveaway to support women entrepreneurs through cash prizes, mentorship, travel, and business opportunities. Applications open March 2, 2026 via @bundlexjoy on Instagram, with entries due March 30 and winners announced March 31.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This giveaway is open to U.S. residents 18 and older, including:
- Small business owners
- Early-stage entrepreneurs
- Women with a vision to create positive change

Name: City of Chicago Food Equity Council Stipend Application: Urban Agriculture Subcommittee
Description: The City of Chicago's Food Equity Council Urban Agriculture Subcommittee is offering five $2,500 stipends to Chicago residents with hands-on experience growing food locally, in exchange for participating in policy development and advising on urban agriculture priorities between April and October 2026, representing an estimated 16–25 hour commitment. Priority is given to growers operating in low food access neighborhoods who have experience navigating city processes to establish their operations. The application deadline is March 30, 2026 at 11:59pm.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The City of Chicago’s Food Equity Council Urban Agriculture Subcommittee is seeking Chicago residents with lived experience in growing food locally to join the Food Equity Council. This Food Equity Council is a mayoral advisory body that works to shape policies and strategies that strengthen Chicago’s food system and improve access to healthy, affordable, and culturally relevant food. 

The Food Equity Council is committed to co-governance; centering community voices, rebuilding trust between residents and government, and creating a culture of shared decision-making that fosters real civic power. Participants will contribute their knowledge, experience, and perspective to inform City policies and programs through structured, facilitated meetings with community leaders, advocates, and City staff.

Selected participants will also join an Urban Ag Policy Sprint Group to work with City partners to:

1. Develop 2026-2027 policy priorities and implementation plans

2. Support the mapping of a comprehensive Urban Ag Policy plan.

To honor the value of this expertise and the time required, participants will receive a $2,500 stipend, reflecting an estimated 16-25 hour commitment between April and October 2026. There are a total of 5 stipends available.  

The Urban Ag Subcommittee will select growers operating with varied growing and distribution models who have experience navigating City processes to establish their growing operations. Priority will be given to growers operating in neighborhoods experiencing Low food access



This opportunity is supported by the Chicago United for Equity (CUE)/Office of Equity and Racial Justice (OERJ) Co-governance Pilot Initiative

Please read this Food Equity Council Urban Ag Subcommittee Charter  to understand the expectations of Food Equity Council Urban Agriculture Subcommittee participants and stipended participation.

Name: Arch Grants Startup Competition
Description: Arch Grants’ 2026 Startup Competition is a global search for innovative, scalable, job-creating early-stage startups (idea-stage to pre–Series A), offering $75,000 in non-dilutive funding (plus $25,000 for companies relocating to St. Louis) along with programming, fundraising support, and access to the Arch Grants network. To participate, companies must headquarter in the City of St. Louis for at least one year and meet founder residency and full-time founder involvement requirements.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Looking for:
- Founders with idea-stage to pre-Series A companies
- Companies with an innovative and scalable business model
- Technology-enabled solutions
- Diverse Founder teams who have a desire to help the St. Louis ecosystem grow

Also require:
- The Company locate their headquarters in the City of St. Louis for at least one year
- 51% of the founding team or one founder and 51% of the team need to live in St. Louis for the program year
- At least one founder is working on the company as their primary or full-time professional role

Name: LA County Small Business Mobility Fund
Description: LA County DEO’s Small Business Mobility Fund offers small businesses countywide a chance to access grants and technical assistance through three tracks: Launch Grants ($5,000 for non-retail commercial spaces or $10,000 for retail storefronts in unincorporated LA County), Entrepreneurship Academy Grants ($2,000 for EMI Academy graduates), and Formalization Grants for sidewalk vendors in unincorporated areas. It’s aimed at reducing barriers to business success by providing capital plus support (e.g., permitting, improvements, branding, equipment).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Launch Grants
- $5,000 grants – For businesses launching a business in a brick-and-mortar non-retail commercial space, such as an office or warehouse, in the unincorporated areas of the County. If already opened, must have opened after September 1, 2025. Businesses operating from shared spaces that are temporary in nature or operating from non-brick-and-mortar locations do not qualify (i.e. open-air swap meets, farmer’s markets, sidewalk vending, etc.)
- $10,000 grants – For businesses launching a business in a brick-and-mortar retail commercial space with a storefront in the unincorporated areas of the County. If already opened, must have opened after September 1, 2025. Businesses in shared spaces of any kind do not qualify

Entrepreneurship Academy Grants
- $2,000 grants – For business owners or entrepreneurs that graduated from the EMI Entrepreneurship Academy Program seeking to launch their business or take their business to the next level
- Launch a business: refers to the process of establishing and formally introducing a new enterprise by developing a viable business concept, completing required legal and regulatory steps, securing initial resources, and beginning operations with the intent to offer goods or services to the market. (e.g. new website or new business location, as well as other costs associated with formalizing a business)
- Take a business to the next level: refers to the deliberate process of advancing an organization beyond its current stage of performance. (e.g. new product or service, expansion to new customer segment, rebrand, new online store, transition to a brick-and-mortar location, and new equipment to expand product offerings

Name: Verizon Digital Ready New York $5,000 Grant
Description: The New York $5,000 Grant is part of Verizon’s Small Business Digital Ready program, run with LISC, and will award 25 New York-based small businesses a $5,000 grant. To apply, owners must be 18+, operate a U.S. for-profit business with a primary address in New York, complete one Digital Ready resource between Jan 1–Mar 31, 2026, and submit the application by March 31, 2026 (11:59 pm PT), with finalists notified around the week of May 17, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply for the New York $5,000 Grant, you must meet the following criteria:
- Have an account on Verizon Small Business Digital Ready. Complete one resource which can be a Digital Ready course, virtual event (including recorded events), or in-person event* between January 1, 2026
and March 31, 2026, and submit a grant application by March 31, 2026.
- Be a U.S.-based, for-profit business with a primary business address located in the state of New York.
- Business address will be required during the application process and verified for applicants who are selected as finalists.
- Be 18 years of age or older.
- Can share and provide proper business and financial verification documentation (W-9s, ACH) if selected as a finalist.

Description: The California $5,000 Grant is part of Verizon’s Small Business Digital Ready program, run with LISC, and will award 25 California-based small businesses a $5,000 grant. To be eligible to apply for the California $5,000 Grant, you must meet the following criteria:
- Be a for-profit business. Nonprofits are not eligible to apply. 
- Be U.S.-based with a primary business address located in the state of California. Business address will be required during the application process and verified for applicants who are selected as finalists. 
- Be 18 years of age or older.
- Can share and provide proper business and financial verification documentation (W-9s, ACH) if selected as a finalist.

Name: Morgan Stanley Inclusive & Sustainable Ventures (MSISV) Accelerator
Description: Accelerator program supporting early-stage startups and nonprofits with access to capital, a curated multi-month program, mentorship, networking, and firm resources. Startups receive an equity investment and nonprofits receive a grant.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Startups: pre-seed to Series A, product in market with demonstrable revenues, measurable impact in MSISV categories.
- Nonprofits: 501(c)(3) or recognized international equivalent, demonstrable plan and sustainable funding structures, measurable impact in MSISV categories.
Industry: Social Impact,Climate & Sustainability,Health / Wellness,Economic Empowerment,Education & Child Care

Name: TAP EDGE (The Acceleration Project)
Description: TAP EDGE is a free 8-month financial health coaching program for small business owners in New York City or Westchester County, offering virtual small-group sessions and 1:1 coaching focused on the FinHealth framework: Spend, Save, Borrow, Plan. Applications are due February 18 at 5:00 PM ET, and participants who complete all modules can qualify to compete for a $10,000 prize pool through finalist impact stories and awards.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - Entrepreneurs/founders aligned with TAP EDGE program focus and able to participate in program requirements.

Name: Pilot Small Business Growth Fund
Description: The Pilot Small Business Growth Fund (Hello Alice + Pilot) offers grants to help U.S. small businesses grow, awarding 18 total grants: one $50,000, two $25,000, and fifteen $10,000. Winners also receive a year of free Pilot bookkeeping services. Applications are open through March 31, 2026, for for-profit U.S. businesses with a legal entity and $5,000–$5,000,000 in 2025 gross revenue, and some finalists may be asked to submit a short video.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- For-profit businesses in the US with a legal entity that generated between $5,000 and $5,000,000 in gross revenue in 2025 are welcome to apply.
- Select applicants may be invited to submit a brief video as part of the final selection process. Submitting the requested video is a prerequisite to being able to win.

Name: Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators (SCBWI) Work-In-Progress Award
Description: The SCBWI Work-in-Progress (WIP) Award supports children’s book writers with completed manuscripts that are not under contract, selecting one winner in categories such as Picture Book, Middle Grade, Young Adult, Nonfiction, and Underrepresented Voices. Winners have their work showcased to a curated group of acquiring editors, offering valuable industry exposure though not guaranteed publication. Applicants must be current SCBWI members and submit a cover page, synopsis (or logline for picture books), and the first ten pages of their manuscript following specific formatting guidelines.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- You must be a current SCBWI member when your work is submitted and when the award is announced.
- You may not submit a work that is under contract. If the work becomes under contract before the award is announced, you will become ineligible. It is your responsibility to notify SCBWI and withdraw your application.
- Each member may submit only one manuscript to the WIP awards each year.

Name: America250 - America's Startup Contest
Description: America's Startup is a national collegiate competition open to U.S. undergraduate and trade school students that invites early-stage business ideas with the potential to shape America's future innovation and progress. Participants submit a written proposal and pitch video, with 30 semi-finalists advancing to a live pitch experience in San Mateo, CA on May 1–3, 2026, where 10 winners are selected. Each winning team receives $25,000 in non-dilutive grant funding along with national recognition and potential mentorship opportunities. The submission deadline is March 31, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- U.S. students enrolled as undergraduates in accredited U.S. colleges, universities, or trade schools
- Founders working individually or in small teams
- Early-stage ideas, concepts, or ventures across industries

Name: Publishing Grants for Collections, Exhibitions, and Conferences
Description: The Decorative Arts Trust offers publishing grants of $5,000–$50,000 (up to $50,000 total per year) to support book-length publications tied to collections, exhibitions, and conferences that advance scholarship in decorative arts and material culture, with a focus on objects made or used in an American context. Independent scholars, nonprofit organizations, and international authors are eligible, and projects that promote diversity or include early-career professionals receive preference.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
- As part of the funding guidelines, institutions that receive grant support are expected to have at least one staff member maintain a Trust membership for the duration of the project. The website outlines the various membership levels. 

- Applications are due March 31 annually, with successful applicants notified by June 30.


Eligibility Criteria:
- They use the terms decorative arts and material culture in relation to three-dimensional objects but will also consider proposals that focus on decorative painting, prints, maps, and wallpaper as well as those that analyze the interiors for which objects were designed or in which they were placed.

- Proposed topics should focus on objects made or used in an American context, defined as North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean.
The Trust encourages projects that advance diversity in the study of American decorative arts and material culture.

- Publications are expected to contain original research which yields information of high scholarly value.

- Proposals from authors located outside of the United States will be accepted.

- They support in-print as well as digital publications, with an expectation that in-print books will have some level of digital accessibility.

- Publication teams that include early career professionals will receive preference.

- Independent scholars and nonprofit organizations are welcome to apply.

- Acceptable costs for printed publications are: printing, binding, design, layout, editing, indexing, and production. Funding cannot be used for authors fees, overhead, photography, or licensing, reproduction, copyright, and marketing costs.

- Publications do not need to be under contract at the time of application.

- As part of the funding guidelines, institutions that receive grant support are expected to have at least one staff member maintain a Trust membership for the duration of the project. Our website outlines the various membership levels.

Name: UBS Project Female Founder
Description: UBS Project Female Founder is a free, year-long global accelerator program designed to help early-stage female entrepreneurs scale their ventures, particularly in fintech and enterprise technology, across more than 25 countries.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
- Open to ventures that are majority-owned and led by women, it is sector-agnostic and tailored to founders with products in development or early commercialization. Participants gain access to curated content, regional events, and introductions to UBS’s entrepreneurial networks, including the Industry Leaders Network.
- The program includes an intensive 8-week accelerator followed by a 12-month activation phase, offering investor-readiness training, mentoring, and connections to over 100 venture capital mentors and UBS's global investor networks. 

Eligibility: 
- Your company is beyond the idea stage, with a product or service in development (prototype) or already available on the market
- You have raised up to USD 1m to date
- You are now seeking early-stage capital (beyond self-funding), such as seed or Series A funding
- The company is majority-owned (51% or more) by women
- The company is majority-led by a woman in a senior leadership role (founder, co-founder, CEO, President, or equivalent).
- The company is registered as a legal entity in its operating region
- You are able to commit to the program timeline and participate in the majority of online sessions

Name: The Creativity Grant - Maryland State Arts Council
Description: The Maryland State Arts Council's Creativity Grants for Projects awards between $1,000 and $4,000 to independent artists and small arts organizations in Maryland for either planning and development work or implementation of a specific arts project. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through March 31, 2026, with monthly reviews.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Be an Independent Artist, or 
- Be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for one year or more and within grant income requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school.
- Organizations applying through fiscal sponsorships can be funded if the Fiscal Agency and the Organization operate within a Model A sponsorship. (Note: in a “Model A” sponsorship, the assets, liabilities, and exempt activities collectively referred to as the project are housed within the fiscal sponsor.)
- Identify a specific event, activity or project to occur within the application time frame.

Name: Sephora Accelerate
Description: Sephora Accelerate is Sephora’s brand incubation program for emerging beauty founders, offering mentorship, industry resources, and retail-readiness training to help brands build, refine, and grow. Participants gain access to Sephora’s network and curriculum, and some may ultimately earn the opportunity to launch their products at Sephora.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Persons of all backgrounds are welcome to apply to Sephora Accelerate! Applicants must lead a North America-incorporated beauty brand company (ex. an LLC incorporated in the US for distribution would allow a brand to be eligible to apply). Your brand should be in its early stages, not yet widely distributed. We are only considering companies with at least a working prototype or lab sample of product.

Your brand must be founded or co-founded by a person who is at least 18 years old. Applications must be filled out by the founder/co-founder and either the founder/co-founder is required to be the active/primary participant of the program. If selected, founder(s) must be able to attend the program in its entirety, including digital and in-person programming.

Name: Ysabel Jurado's Microenterprise Grant Program
Description: Councilmember Ysabel Jurado's Microenterprise Grant Program offers grants of up to $3,000 to small businesses operating in Los Angeles City Council District 14, funded through federal Community Development Block Grant dollars. Funds can be used for operating expenses such as payroll, rent, insurance, and inventory, with priority given to businesses that have not previously received city, state, or federal assistance. The application deadline was extended to March 31, 2026, and is available in six languages through the City of Los Angeles Economic and Workforce Development Department.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Businesses

The business must fall under an eligible business type/industry. Please refer to the “INELIGIBLE BUSINESSES” tab to determine if your business is eligible.

The business must be a for-proﬁt business located within Los Angeles City Council District 14 limits. Please use your business address to check Zimas data to determine if your business is eligible and is located in CD14 under the “Jurisdictional” tab. https://zimas.lacity.org/

Annual revenue cannot exceed $1 million.

The business must have an active Business Tax Registration Certificate (BTRC) with the City of Los Angeles that is current and in good standing.

The business must have ﬁve (5) or fewer personnel, including the owner(s).

The business must demonstrate that the grant funds will be used for eligible purposes.

The business must disclose whether they have received funding from other federal, state, or local sources (including PPP and EIDL). Applicants who have received funding are still eligible, provided the funds are not currently being spent on the same expenses covered by the Microenterprise Grant.

If applicable, the business must be in good standing with the Secretary of State.

Grant funds must help create and/or retain at least one job held by or made available to low and moderate-income persons, as defined by HUD. The current income limits are provided in the table below.

Name: 2026 Agora Venture Competition
Description: Agora’s 2026 Venture Competition is open from March 9 to March 31 and gives eligible founders the chance to pitch live on May 13 in Washington, DC, for a $10,000 non-dilutive cash prize, with additional cash and in-kind prizes also available. It’s open to DC, Maryland, or Virginia-based female or non-binary founders who hold at least 25% equity, serve in a C-suite role, lead a for-profit company with venture-scale potential, and have raised under $1 million in equity funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility requirements:

Gender Identity: Applicants must self-identify as either female or non-binary. If selected to pitch, co-founders are invited to join you on the stage only if they, too, identify as female or non-binary.

Location: Applicants must be based in DC, Maryland, or Virginia.

Role & Equity: Applicants should be a founder with at least 25% equity stake and hold a C-suite executive position in the company they are representing.

Venture-Ready Scale: The company should demonstrate the potential for venture-scale growth, indicating a capacity for rapid expansion and significant market impact. (Note: Founders of consultancies or other businesses that do not meet this criteria are welcome to reach out to explore other paths for involvement.)

Business Type: The company must be incorporated as a for-profit entity.

Funding Restrictions: Companies must have raised less than $1,000,000 in equity funding.

Name: The Charles and Joan Hermanowski Family Foundation
Description: This foundation awards grants of up to $10,000 to 501(c)(3) nonprofits for one-year projects serving children and youth from birth to age 21, with a preference for organizations in Florida and Virginia that don't receive wide public support. Grants must be fully utilized within the grant year, with any remaining funds returned to the foundation, and a completion report is required. No application deadline was listed in the content provided, so interested organizations should visit the foundation's website directly for deadline information.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Letters of Interest will not be reviewed and considered

Submitted on the required form. See(Submit Letter of Interest)
Project duration is listed for the year following the grant.
Amount requested does not exceed $10,000.00.
Group to be served is between the ages of birth and twenty-one.
Projects are within the United States. The foundation responds more favorably to requests coming from Florida and Virginia.
Grants are made only to organizations that are tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.

Grants are not made to political organizations.

Grants are not made to large public charities such as the United Way, the March of Dimes, the American Cancer Society, The Salvation Army, etc. The foundation prefers to fund organizations that do not receive wide public support.

Grants are to be fully utilized in the year following the grant. Any amounts remaining after project completion must be returned to the foundation.

Grants are for one (1) year and not automatically renewable for multiple years.

A grant evaluation report must be submitted to the foundation upon completion of the project

Name: Dermascope Open Door Grant
Description: The Open Door Grant from DERMASCOPE awards one $5,000 grant to a licensed U.S. aesthetician who is preparing to launch or expand a spa or solo practice but faces financial barriers. It supports expenses such as education, equipment, and startup or expansion costs, and applicants are evaluated based on readiness, momentum, financial need, and the potential long-term impact on their business.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Open Door Grant is intended for licensed aestheticians who can demonstrate readiness, preparation, and a clear plan for growth. 

Strong applicants may include aestheticians who are: 
- Preparing to launch a spa or solo practice within the next 6–12 months 
- Expanding an existing spa or solo practice to the next phase of growth 
- Seeking funding for education, equipment, or infrastructure tied directly to business advancement 

Applicants must: 
- Hold an active aesthetician license at the time of application and award 
- Be the owner or co-owner of the business 
- Operate within the United States 
- Provide documentation demonstrating meaningful preparation or progress 
- Solo suites, storefront spas, and legally permitted home studios all qualify.

Name: Leading Ladies Connect Pitch 2026
Description: Pitch competition for women founders offering cash prizes and visibility through the Leading Ladies Connect community. Selected entrepreneurs pitch to judges for a chance to win funding and resources.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Women founders/entrepreneurs (per program requirements).
- Completed application submitted before the deadline.

Name: Miami WaveMaker Grant
Description: The WaveMaker Grant at Locust Projects awards up to $6,000 to Miami-based artists for innovative, artist-driven projects shared with the public in unconventional spaces, with funding available across three categories: New Work/Projects, Long-Haul Projects, and Research & Development + Implementation. The grants are made possible through the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program. Applications for the 2026 cycle are open now with a deadline of April 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Visual artists, curators, cultural organizers, collectives, and collaborators who reside in Miami-Dade County are encouraged to apply.

Name: ArtPrize 2026 Featured Public Project Grant
Description: ArtPrize is offering a $25,000 Featured Public Project Grant for one artist or designer to create a large-scale public artwork at a high-visibility outdoor location in downtown Grand Rapids, MI during the ArtPrize event (September 17 – October 3, 2026). The grant covers costs like artwork creation, installation, permits, transportation, and lodging, and is open to artists 18 and older — including international artists. The application deadline is April 1, 2026, with applicants notified the week of April 13.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who can apply?
➢ Artists 18 years or older
29 PEARL ST NW • GRAND RAPIDS, MI ARTPRIZE.ORG • SEPT 17-OCT 03, 2026
➢ Preference is given to artists with experience in large-scale public art
➢ Must comply with Grand Rapids City Commission policies on public art

Are international artists eligible?
➢ Yes, but a 30% federal tax withholding applies to grants awarded to non-U.S. citizens.

Is the grantee eligible to compete in ArtPrize 2026?
➢ Yes! The grantee must register as an ArtPrize 2026 Artist and is eligible for public voting
and juried awards.

FAQ:

The project must be installed in a designated exterior public space downtown.
Alternative locations may be proposed, but all installations require approval from the
City of Grand Rapids.
Locations available for 2026:
➢ Blue Bridge
➢ Calder Plaza
➢ 555 Monroe

How can the grant funds be used?
Funds support:

29 PEARL ST NW • GRAND RAPIDS, MI ARTPRIZE.ORG • SEPT 17-OCT 03, 2026
