Name: Creative Capital Award – 2027 Open Call
Description: Creative Capital supports artists with funding and professional development services for new, discrete artistic projects. Applications open in March 2026 and close in early April 2026 for the 2027 award cycle.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Artists applying with a new, discrete artistic project (not a nonprofit/business request).
- Project must be eligible under Creative Capital’s discipline and project rules (see handbook).

Name: NYC Cultural Development Fund (CDF)
Description: The NYC Department of Cultural Affairs is accepting applications for its Fiscal Year 2027 Cultural Development Fund, which provides grants to nonprofit arts and cultural organizations based in New York City for programming taking place between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. Eligible organizations must be 501(c)(3) nonprofits incorporated in New York State, administratively based in NYC, and have at least two consecutive years of arts and cultural programming in the city. The application deadline is April 2, 2026 at 5pm ET, with no exceptions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
About CDF

The NYC Department of Cultural Affairs (DCLA) is a mayoral agency charged with the administration of city funds in support of arts and culture throughout New York City’s five boroughs. The Cultural Development Fund (CDF) is DCLA’s competitive, peer-evaluated grant process that supports a broad, multidisciplinary group of diverse nonprofit organizations for their cultural services to city residents. It is managed by the agency’s Program Services Unit under the supervision of the Commissioner. Annually, the CDF supports over 1,000 grantees for programmatic funding. On average, over 75% of applicants receive funding, which is provided by the Mayor and City Council. This process allows public funds to be widely distributed through every council district and in every cultural discipline.

An eligible organization must:

Be either (a) a nonprofit arts or cultural organization, or (b) a nonprofit organization that has an arts or culture component in its broader mission.
Demonstrate successful delivery of arts and cultural services in New York City for the last two consecutive years.
Be based in New York City and able to demonstrate administrative and programmatic operations within any of the five boroughs of New York City. Your administrative address is primarily determined by the address listed on your IRS 990 for the fiscal year ending in 2024, with the organization’s 501(c)(3) letter, and other publicly available information also taken into consideration.
Possess a unique Federal Employee Identification Number (EIN).
Be certified as tax exempt under Internal Revenue Service Code Section 501(c)(3); or be an incorporated nonprofit that uses a DCLA pre-approved, New York State incorporated tax-exempt fiscal sponsor. Only nonprofit organizations are eligible to apply, regardless of whether they use a fiscal sponsor. Limited Liability Companies, Benefit corporations, Limited Partnerships, S corporations, individual artists, and unincorporated artist collectives are not eligible to apply. 
Be incorporated in New York State as a not-for-profit organization no later than the organization’s fiscal year 2024.

Name: PeopleFund BIPOC Small Business Accelerator
Description: PeopleFund's BIPOC Small Business Accelerator provides Texas-based entrepreneurs in low-to-moderate income communities with training, business planning support, expedited loan access, and a grant of $3,000–$5,000 upon successful graduation from the program. The Q2 2026 cohort runs weekly on Wednesdays from April 15–June 3, is open statewide to both startups and existing businesses, and admits the first 70 eligible applicants on a first-come, first-served basis. The application window for Q2 2026 closes April 2, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Program Eligibility
The program is based on first-come, first-serve and we will admit the first 70 eligible applicants.

To qualify for the BIPOC Small Business Accelerator, applicants must meet the following criteria:

Must be located in the state of Texas
Participants must demonstrate at least one of the following three criteria:
Their business is located in a low to moderate-income area OR
That the address of the individual is in a low to moderate-income area OR
That the household income of the participant is low to moderate-income
Open to start-up and existing businesses
Must be able to support a loan payment through available global cash flow
Must meet credit and lending qualifications
No bankruptcies within the last 5 years
U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident
Not currently in active litigation
Not currently past-due on federal obligations or are on a recovery plan
Total collections, derogatory marks, and past due items cannot exceed 10% of the total loan amount up to $5,000
Not involved in felony-level criminal activity, crimes of moral turpitude, or financial
Not engaged in any of the following industries: adult entertainment, gambling or gaming, real estate investments or housing projects, passive activity (rental), anything federally illegal, multi-level marketing, and nonprofit activities
Program Benefits
Participants will have access to:

Qualify for a PeopleFund loan product (dependent on approval)
A grant amount between $3,000 and a maximum of $5,000
Connections to business and professional resources in the community
Completion of a business plan, financial statements, and capital portfolio
Access to tools and technology including LivePlan business planning software and the Verizon Digital Ready Program
Curriculum guide within an online learning platform
Ongoing support and aftercare through dedicated business coaching and mentorship
Networking opportunities within the cohort

Name: City of Boston Arts and Culture: City Hall Plaza Engagement Grant 2026
Description: The City Hall Plaza Engagement Grant, offered by Boston's Mayor's Office of Arts & Culture, provides funding from $15,000 to $100,000 across four tiers to support free, public arts and cultural programming on City Hall Plaza between September and December 2026. The grant prioritizes individuals, nonprofits, and collectives — especially those with annual budgets under $100,000 — whose work centers historically underrepresented communities and addresses the loss of cultural spaces in Boston.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Vision: Programming that elevates arts, culture, and/or creative expression
- Commitment to Equity: City Hall Plaza is a space for everyone and we are committed to funding programs that make space for historically underrepresented communities.
- Need for Space: All programs will demonstrate the need for additional cultural spaces in Boston due to the loss of space or inability to afford space. 
- Cultural Relevance & Responsiveness: All proposed programs should directly engage with present-day social, cultural, or civic issues that will contribute to the strengthening of Boston’s communities.  
- Community Partnerships: All programs should center partnerships with community members, artists and key stakeholders toward a shared vision of uplifting Boston’s arts and culture sector. 
- Location: City Hall Plaza will highlight organizations and artists who are located in the Greater Boston Area, communities residing east I-495 in Massachusetts, and/or national partners who have had a longstanding relationship with Boston communities (reference map).

Name: Lake County Communities of Waukegan, North Chicago, and Zion - 2026 Small Business Growth Initiative
Description: The 2026 Small Business Growth Initiative (SBGI) is a grant program for small businesses located in Waukegan, North Chicago, or Zion (Lake County, IL) that have been operating for at least one year and generate $50,000 or more in annual revenue. In addition to grant funding, the program includes one-on-one business coaching and monthly development meetings running from May through September. The application deadline is April 3rd at 5:00 PM, and questions can be directed to granthelp@a4cb.org or (312)-275-3000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small business owners in Waukegan, North Chicago, or Zion
Able to attend the first cohort meeting on May 18 at 3 PM
Able to commit to the 4-month learning cohort

Name: Multilingual by Design
Description: Multilingual by Design is a philanthropic initiative that pairs K-8 education nonprofits with AI builders to co-create tools designed specifically for multilingual students in math and literacy. Applications are open through April 3, 2026, and selected teams will be invited to an in-person prototyping workshop in Washington, D.C. from June 2-4, with expenses covered. Following the workshop, 3-5 partnerships will receive grants of up to $350,000 to develop and pilot their tools in real classrooms through 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 

Multilingual by Design welcomes applications from individuals and organizations that fit into one of three tracks:

1. Education Nonprofits
U.S.-based 501(c)(3) organizations serving K‑8 multilingual learners and their families 
What we're looking for: Experience with multilingual math or literacy education and a commitment to improving outcomes for multilingual students

You might be: A nonprofit supporting teachers or developing instructional models, an academic researcher focused on multilingual pedagogy, a curriculum developer, or a community-based organization serving multilingual families


2. AI Builders & Developers
Individuals and teams ready to design and build AI-enabled tools
What we're looking for: Technical skills and experience building functional AI products, along with interest in collaborating with educators to solve real classroom challenges

You might be: An independent AI developer or designer, a small EdTech team or consultancy, a founder-track grad student or researcher, or a tech company exploring education and social impact work


3. Existing Teams
Nonprofit + AI builder partnerships already working on multilingual education
What we're looking for: Existing teams with both multilingual learning expertise and proven AI development experience who are ready to take their work to the next level

You might be: A nonprofit with an established technical partner, a university research team collaborating with community organizations, or a nonprofit with in-house AI capacity

Name: L.O.C.A.L. Long Island Small Business Grant Program
Description: The L.O.C.A.L. Small Business Grant Program provides funding to small businesses in Nassau and Suffolk Counties to support growth, innovation, and community impact. In 2026, it will award 40 grants of $5,000 each and two $20,000 grand prizes for businesses facing financial hardship, with applications due April 3, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Businesses Must: 
- Be based in Nassau County or Suffolk County.
- Clearly demonstrate how the requested funding will support business growth and positively impact the local community in which they operate (not pay past debt).
- Operate a brick-and-mortar storefront or spend the majority of their time serving clients within the local community (for example: a landscaping company, licensed child care facility, or food truck).
- Submit background checks: One more the majority owner(s), and one for the business.

Name: Yes/Boston Innovation Challenge
Description: The Yes/Boston Innovation Challenge invites early-stage ventures to apply with solutions that improve reliable access to affordable, nutritious food in Boston, particularly at the intersection of health access, resilience, and sustainable food systems. Focus areas include food production, logistics, nutritious meals (including Food Is Medicine), and food information access, with an emphasis on AI-enabled and data-driven innovations. Selected ventures will join the UpLink Innovation Ecosystem and receive visibility, strategic connections, and targeted support to pilot, scale, and grow their solutions in Boston.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Local presence: The start-up must show active or planned engagement with the Boston food and health ecosystem, evidenced by customers, pilots, partnerships, or a Boston-focused go-to-market plan. 
- Operating model: For-profit start-ups or social enterprises with revenue-generating models or funded pilots. 
- Scale and replicability: Ventures with proven pilots that can be deployed in Boston within 12 months of selection. 
- Stage: Impact-oriented start-ups that are in seed funding or Series A stage. Submissions representing the “idea” or “prototype” phase will not be considered.
- Solution focus: Solutions directly aligned with challenge focus areas.  
- Previous UpLink Ventures are not eligible.

Name: 2026 Cleantech Open Accelerator
Description: Cleantech Open is the world's largest cleantech accelerator, offering 100–150 U.S. companies per year a 12-week program of mentoring, training, investor meetings, and showcasing opportunities. Since 2005, over 70% of their alumni companies are still operating and have collectively raised more than $3 billion in external funding. Their 2026 Accelerator is now accepting applications, with a kickoff webinar on March 18, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
Cleantech Open provides tangible benefits:

World-class mentoring: receive intensive, tailored mentoring from experienced business experts and gain access to one of the world's only cleantech-specific expert networks.
Hands-on training: 12-week series of intensive workshops, boot camps, and webinars to launch your startup to the next level.
Prizes: In 2026, U.S. Cleantech Open plans to award a mix of cash and in-kind services to the winners of its showcasing events. This includes:
Networking: connect to a powerful national network of influencers and entrepreneurs.
Visibility: showcase your startup to investors, strategic partners, and customers through specialized connection events as well as through social media and press releases.
Alumni: ongoing engagement for teams who’ve completed Cleantech Open, including introductions to investors and corporate partners, participation in Challenges, and networking events.
As with most endeavors, what you get out of Cleantech Open is based on the effort and intensity of what you put in.  Don’t expect to simply sign up and expect to win a prize!

*All awards are subject to change at Cleantech Open’s sole discretion and may vary from region to region. The cash component of each award may be provided as a grant or as seed capital (investment). The grand prize is provided as a SAFE note.


REQUIREMENTS: 
1) Technology

Your technology must fit into one of these categories.
Energy Generation
Energy Distribution & Storage
Energy Efficiency
Chemicals & Advanced Materials
Information & Communications Technologies (ICT)
Green Building
Transportation
Agriculture, Water & Waste
Confused about how your technology fits? Please view the FAQs tab. 



2) Funding 

Cleantech Open supports early-stage startups.  Most startups in our program have less than $2MM in funding from private investors and less than $10MM in funding from family, friends, and grants.  There are exceptions, however, and we encourage you to apply even if your funding levels are higher.  We'll evaluate your fit with the program holistically, considering your company's ability to benefit from the program. If we determine your funding levels are too high, we may offer you the opportunity to participate in the Accelerator but not be eligible to compete in the culminating pitch events.



3) Company

You must have at least two members.



4) Location

Much of the value Cleantech Open creates for participating startups is centered around relationships and network connections. For this reason, it is important for your team to participate in the Cleantech Open events over the program year, including the National Academy (East or West), Business Clinics, Workshops, Networking events, Regional Awards & Innovation Showcase, and our Global Forum. Please confirm that you'll be able to participate in our program in this way AS THE NATIONAL ACADEMY AND GLOBAL FORUM ARE REQUIRED EVENTS. Travel and accommodation costs are at the expense of the participating company and its members. 



5) Participation

At least one team member must actively engage with the Accelerator by participating in meetings or events that are part of the program, and by submitting final deliverables before Final Judging. There are only two mandatory events at the National level: 1) the National Academy (East or West determined) and 2) the Global Forum.  There are several mandatory events at the Regional level: 1) Business Clinics and 2) Regional Showcase. 



6) Conflict of Interest

You MAY NOT apply if you are an Accelerator volunteer, judge, expert, advisor, mentor, chair, regional director, or if you are in any other way involved with the organization or operation of the accelerator. Immediate family members of the aforementioned people are also ineligible.

You MAY apply if you are affiliated with the accelerator's sponsors and/or partners, as long as you or a family member are not directly involved in the operation of the Cleantech Open, as above.

If you are accepted as an entrepreneur or company participating in the Cleantech Open Accelerator, individuals involved in the running of the Cleantech Open may advise or mentor you, within the rules of the Accelerator, but such individuals may not take a direct interest in your company (such as an equity stake or a paid position) and may not participate as company members until after the Global Forum in the year of your participation.

Name: The Coramino Fund
Description: The Coramino Fund is a nationwide small business grant program created by LISC in partnership with Kevin Hart and Gran Coramino Tequila to support entrepreneurs in under-resourced communities. Its fourth round will award $10,000 grants to eligible small businesses in Atlanta, Chicago, Detroit, Houston, and Los Angeles, with applications open from March 31 to April 6, 2026. Businesses must meet requirements such as being five years old or less, having no more than 30 employees, and providing financial verification documents.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Registered business entity in Atlanta, Chicago, Detroit, Houston, or Los Angeles 
- Owned by an individual 21 years of age or older (who must be the applicant)
- In operation for 5 years or less
- Have no more than 3 locations and 30 employees
- Have a business bank account
- Can share and provide proper business and financial verification documentation (W-9s, voided checks, bank statements, etc.)
Business owner(s) must not be an equity holder, owner, partner, member, director, manager, officer, employee, consultant or agent of any beverage alcohol retail licensee, or have any other interest, direct or indirect, in any beverage alcohol retail licensee. As a manufacturer of a distilled spirit, Gran Coramino® Tequila is legally prohibited from providing monetary funds to licensed accounts.

Name: NYC Love Your Block Grant
Description: Love Your Block (LYB) is an NYC Service program that provides volunteer-led community groups with mini-grants of up to $3,000 and support to revitalize local public spaces through projects like gardens, murals, and events. The six-month program helps groups mobilize volunteers, access city resources, and strengthen neighborhood ties, with applications for 2026 open until April 7 (rolling, with preference for early applicants).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
· Be a local, 100% volunteer-led group with no paid staff; operate within the neighborhood being served
· Propose a creative project that revitalizes their block and engages the community
· Host at least one community activation (e.g., block party, volunteer series, or creation/enhancement of a community space such as a garden or fridge)
· Mobilize at least 15 volunteers over the six-month program period
· Participate in volunteer data tracking and financial record keeping, and attend required meetings
This program is meant for community groups that may otherwise not have access to funding or connections to city agencies. Some examples of groups that would be eligible for LYB funding are:
· Block/Tenants Associations
· Mutual Aid Groups
· Grassroots Groups
· Community Clubs
· Resident Led Groups

LYB also welcomes applicants who are in the very early stages of mobilizing a resident-led group; while previous experience is welcomed, it is not a requirement to apply.

Name: Charlotte-Mecklenberg Community Connector Grant
Description: The Community Connector Grant supports creative individuals in Charlotte-Mecklenburg in developing or expanding programs that broaden access to arts, culture, science, and history experiences. Grants of up to $20,000 are available for project-based work, with projects required to begin between June 1 and December 31, 2026, and run no later than June 30, 2027. Applications opened March 11, 2026 and are accepted until April 8, 2026 at noon, with only one application permitted per applicant per cycle.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Individual creatives who operate as a sole proprietorship or LLC.
• ASC encourages collaborative projects. Artists working together should identify a
single applicant that will complete this process.
• The applicant’s book of work must be focused on arts, science, history, or heritage programming.
• Applicants must be 18 years of age, reside and/or have an artistic business/studio in, and
primarily serve Mecklenburg County (over 75% of their work taking place in Mecklenburg County).
• Applicants must have created and/or produced community or public programming previously
within Mecklenburg County. Applicants will be asked to provide context around this experience
within the application.

Name: DivInc Innovation & Influence Accelerator
Description: DivInc’s Innovation & Influence Accelerator is a 10-week hybrid program for early-stage, under-resourced founders building tech or tech-enabled companies who are working toward an MVP, traction, and growth readiness. Starting May 4, 2026, the program includes workshops, mentorship, and investor-prep support, plus two in-person weeks in Austin, ending with a Demo Day; applications are due Sunday, April 5 at 11:59 PM.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: This accelerator supports founders who are in the early stages of building their company and are working toward launching an MVP, gaining traction, and developing a strong foundation for growth. Companies may include software, hardware, or tech-enabled consumer products.

Name: Northeastern University City and Community Engagement - 2026 Community Grants
Description: Northeastern University's Office of City and Community Engagement is awarding grants between $5,000 and $15,000 (totaling $30,000) to 501(c)(3) organizations supporting college readiness and student success for youth in the Fenway, Mission Hill, South End, Back Bay, and Roxbury neighborhoods. Eligible proposals should focus on one of four areas: college exploration and career awareness, academic success, mentorship and student support, or college access.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What is the goal of a Community Grant?
The goal of the Community Grants is to help fund the projects and initiatives of our community partners whose work aligns with CCE’s vision and the key goal areas we’ve identified in partnership with community members. These grants serve to support local initiatives focused on college readiness, including college exploration, career awareness, academic success, mentorship and student support, and college access.

College Exploration and Career Awareness: exposure to wide range of college and career opportunities, career exploration for top industries such as: creative professions, healthcare, or artificial intelligence.
Academic Success: tutoring, test prep 
Mentorship & Student Support: social-emotional support, leadership skill development, support for first-gen college students
College Access: education about affordability, college application coaching


Eligibility: 
Any Boston-area based community organization, nonprofit, or school that works to support youth in personal, academic, and career development. Organizations or proposals that demonstrate impact in Roxbury, Mission Hill, South End, Fenway, and Back Bay are prioritized based on our decision making criteria.

Your organization’s office does not have to reside in these neighborhoods, but rather that you serve people primarily from these neighborhoods. Programs that engage students in BPS, but may not be based in these neighborhoods are eligible to apply, though priority is given to those that specifically target these communities.

Name: Rare Impact Fund RFP
Description: The Rare Impact Fund is launching a $2.5M+ grant initiative to strengthen the U.S. nonclinical youth mental health workforce, supporting programs that recruit, train, place, and retain roles like peer specialists, community health workers, and care navigators. Eligible nonprofits can apply for two-year grants of $250,000 to $500,000 through a two-stage process, with LOIs due April 10, 2026, and invited full proposals due June 12, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
• The applicant is registered as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or an international equivalent.
• The applicant operates in the United States, and the program activities are focused within the United States.
• The applicant is independent of political parties and ensures that the proposed program does not involve lobbying or political activity.
• Each applicant may submit no more than one LOI.
• Each applicant may request a total of $250,000 to $500,000 for the full grant period.
• Commit to participation in:
- Annual cohort convenings
-  Learning sessions (up to quarterly)
- Occasional communications or storytelling opportunities, as appropriate and mutually agreed upon
- Submission of annual reports

Name: The Building Her Community Grant
Description: The Building Her Community Grant, presented by Freelancing Females and Heartbeat, awards $5,000 cash plus a year of Heartbeat and Freelancing Females memberships, concierge setup support, and coaching to help founders, freelancers, and entrepreneurs grow a business or community. Applications are open March 10 to April 10, open worldwide to applicants age 18+, and the winner will be announced on April 17.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.
- This grant is designed to support and uplift women founders, freelancers, entrepreneurs, and community builders.
While our mission centers around empowering women in business, applications are open to individuals of all genders who align with this mission and are building impactful businesses or communities.
- Applicants should be the founder, owner, or primary operator of the business, project, or community they are applying with.

Name: With Youth for Youth for Southeast Michigan Grant
Description: The With Youth For Youth (WYFY) Grant Opportunity provides youth-directed funding for afterschool and out-of-school time programs across Southeast Michigan's seven counties, with more than $2 million available and a focus on programs where young people play meaningful roles in shaping their own experiences. The initiative is coordinated by Youthprise and funded by the Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation, with a 17-member youth advisory council making the actual grantmaking decisions. The application deadline is April 10, 2026 at 5pm, with no exceptions, and applications must be submitted online.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
With Youth For Youth (WYFY) Grant Opportunity for Southeast Michigan
Afterschool With Youth for Youth (WYFY) is a multifaceted initiative empowering young people to redesign afterschool programming from the ground up. Coordinated by Youthprise and funded by the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation and the Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation, the project connects five partner sites across the United States: (Missouri, Minnesota, Southeast Michigan, Vermont, and Western New York). WYFY builds upon two earlier efforts, the Generator Z project, funded by the Wilson Foundation, and the Powered by Youth Voice project, funded by the Mott Foundation. Both projects aimed to amplify the voices of young people by expanding channels for youth to contribute to program decisions and practice leadership. WYFY builds upon that foundation by deepening youth decision-making power and investing in youth-led solutions within out-of-school time (OST) systems. 

Eligibility: 
Funds are allocated for youth programs that occur outside of school hours, specifically supporting young people in the seven-county region of Southeast Michigan (Livingston, Macomb, Monroe, Oakland, St. Clair, Washtenaw, and Wayne). Funding will be released after all grant requirements and obligations have been signed and returned. 

Please note that capital costs are not allowable under this grant program.

Name: Shark Minded Mastermind: Female Founders Pro Pitch Event
Description: The Shark Minded Mastermind Female Founders Pro Pitch Competition is a live pitch event on April 22, 2026 in Wilmington, Delaware, where eight selected female founders will pitch to a judging panel that includes ABC's Shark Tank winner Joelle Flynn for a chance to win a $5,000 grand prize or a $1,000 audience choice award. Selected pitchers pay a $333 entry fee and receive a 5-minute pitch slot, a vendor table, and social media recognition, but are only charged if selected. Applications are due April 10, 2026, at 8pm ET, with selected participants announced April 13, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Officially apply before April 10th 2026 at 8pmEST by selecting the button below and submitting our form.

Selection Sunday - April 12th 2026 with social media announcement highlighting our eight (8) selected pitching ventures Monday April 13th

By selecting the button below you agree (if selected) to be a Pitching Venture & Exhibitor ($333 entry fee - only 8 available) Wednesday April 22nd from 2-6pm at CSC Station in Wilmington, DE. No, you will not be charged if you are not selected.

Name: Baruch CEO Business Plan & Pitch Competition
Description: The Baruch CEO Business Plan & Pitch Competition is open to all CUNY students and offers prizes of $5,000 (first), $2,500 (second), and $1,000 (third) for early-stage business ideas that have not yet generated revenue, received funding, or been legally incorporated. Applicants must submit a business plan as a PDF deck of no more than 25 slides, with six finalists selected to pitch their ideas in person on May 1, 2026. The application deadline was extended to April 12th, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Pitch Competition Requirements
Be prepared to pitch your business plan for no more than 4 minutes and discuss MITB
Market - is there a market for your product; how big?
Idea - Is this a good idea; is there a real problem; does your product/service
solve it?
Team - Who is the management team; Skills, experiences, knowledge about the
industry; why are you the best person to solve this problem?
Business Plan - How well and detailed you executed the business plan.


Competition Rules:
A business plan may be submitted by an individual or a team consisting of multiple people, but at least one team member must be a current students at a CUNY College and be the one to submit the application. ALL entries must be early-stage ideas, and not fully developed businesses.  Specifically, the idea:

Cannot be currently generating revenues
Cannot already have received funding or financing of any form (other than competition prize money)
Cannot have any legal form of incorporation
Okay to include non-CUNY teammates, but at least one, must be a current CUNY student.

Name: 2026 Austin FC Dream Starter Competition
Description: Dream Starter is an annual venture funding competition from Austin FC and Q2 that awards $100,000 to an entrepreneur from an underrepresented community in the Austin area to help grow a high-potential business. It is focused on for-profit companies within 75 miles of Q2 Stadium and evaluates applicants on problem/market fit, traction, team strength, and growth potential. Applications open March 25, 2026 and close April 13, 2026, with finalists pitching on May 27, 2026.

Name: Ignite Fund
Description: The Ignite Fund offers six $10,000 grants for Chicago-area artists and artist-led collectives to produce and present bold new projects rooted in the visual arts. They prioritize public-facing work that embraces accessibility, fosters community impact and/or participation, and responds to the issues shaping our social climate. In this spirit, The Ignite Fund shines a light on the vibrancy, creativity, and resilience of the Chicago arts ecosystem.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicant Eligibility
Who can apply?

Artists living in the Chicago metropolitan area (Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry, Lake, and Will counties).

18 years or older.

Must legally be able to receive taxable income in the United States. Citizens, permanent residents, or anyone who can provide a W9 and a Social Security Number (SSN) or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) are eligible.

Not currently enrolled in a full-time degree-granting program (high school, college, or university).

Who cannot apply?

Artists living outside of the Chicago metropolitan area (Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry, Lake, and Will counties).

Artists who are younger than 18 years old.

Artists not legally be able to receive taxable income in the United States. Citizens, permanent residents, or anyone who can provide a W9 and a Social Security Number (SSN) or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) are eligible.

Full-time students currently enrolled in high school, college, or university.

Artists led by incorporated entities (LLCs, B Corps, 501(C)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations), universities and schools (private, public, charter), and religious entities.

Artists or Artist collectives who received an Ignite Fund grant the previous round

Artist collectives may apply if the lead applicant meets all of the criteria above. Other collective members do not need to meet all eligibility criteria.

Project Eligibility
What types of projects are eligible?

Projects proposed by visual artists or artists with a history of presenting their work in visual art contexts.

Projects proposed by artists with an active artistic practice that can demonstrate recent work and supply work samples.

Projects must center contemporary visual arts practice as the primary root and impulse. The Ignite Fund embraces a broad understanding of the visual arts. Applicants will be required to describe how a strong visual context plays a critical role in presenting your project.

Projects that can be completed within a one-year grant term.

A new project or the new phase of a project. Keep in mind The Ignite Fund grant is intended to help individuals and collective groups of artists take new risks with their work. The Ignite Fund will not allocate resources to finished projects or support individuals looking to document pre-existing or finished projects.

Name: Sundance Institute Sandbox Fund
Description: The Sundance Institute's Sandbox Fund, administered in partnership with Sandbox Films, offers grants to independent filmmakers working at the intersection of science and nonfiction storytelling, with support available at the development (up to $40,000), production, and post-production stages (up to $100,000 each). The fund is open to U.S. and international feature-length documentary projects, with priority given to work that uses creative narrative techniques and highlights diversity in science. The 2026 Spring Cycle application deadline is April 13, 2026, with notifications sent within 4–6 months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Sandbox Fund offers grants, engagement events, and other opportunities for independent artists seeking to explore the intrinsic link between science and culture through innovative storytelling. The program is administered by the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund in collaboration with Sandbox Films, a documentary production studio that illuminates the art and beauty of scientific inquiry. 

Grants are offered to independent artists who are working at the intersection of science and nonfiction storytelling. The partnership identifies and supports nonfiction projects that inspire a deeper interest in science, especially among those who don’t think of themselves as science enthusiasts.

Submissions are accepted at any production phase, from development through post-production. All proposals must convey some vision for a finished film. Projects that have not yet secured characters or participants, cannot articulate a story or structure, or cannot explain the project’s driving central question are discouraged. We are unable to consider proposals for story research. You do not need any prior funding or a fiscal sponsor in order to apply.

Once your film premieres, we are unable to provide post-production funding support. We therefore encourage applicants to apply at least six months before an anticipated premiere. Picture-locked cuts are also ineligible for post-production funding.

WHAT WILL I NEED IN ORDER TO APPLY?

Written proposal

Proposal checklist

Line-item budget (sample budget: PDF) (Source: IDA/Robert Bahar)

Visual samples

Completed previous directing sample (any length or genre) — optional

Current sample/rough cut

Development applicants are encouraged (but not required) to include visual material such as scene selects, teasers, pitch decks, or other edited footage (up to 15 minutes).

Production applicants are required to submit a sample of at least 10 minutes. The sample should demonstrate your access to characters, visual treatment, and the developing tone and style. We encourage applicants to submit a complete scene that provides the viewer insight into the team’s ability to communicate their intention. 

Post-production applications require a sample of at least 20 minutes that demonstrates access to characters, story arc or concept, and visual treatment. If available, a rough cut may be submitted.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I APPLY?

Applications go through a multistage review. Grant deliberations are made in collaboration with our partners at Sandbox Films. Applications are evaluated on their use of artful and innovative film language, clear storytelling, originality, feasibility, contemporary cultural relevance, and the potential to reach and connect with the intended audience. Additionally, science-related considerations are evaluated to ensure the projects selected reflect the intended purpose of this opportunity. Incomplete applications will be reviewed as received.

Name: Berkeley Film Foundation Documentary Grant Program
Description: The Berkeley Film Foundation's 2026 Documentary Grant Program offers competitive grants ranging from $5,000 to $25,000 to independent documentary filmmakers who live or work in Berkeley, Emeryville, Albany, El Cerrito, Richmond, Alameda, or Oakland, covering production, post-production, and distribution stages only. The program prioritizes socially conscious films that highlight underrepresented communities, civil rights, environmental issues, or untold stories, and includes several special awards up to $25,000 for outstanding projects. The application deadline is April 13, 2026 at 11:59pm PST, with award decisions announced by the end of July 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility

The Berkeley Film Foundation only funds filmmakers who work or live in the cities of Berkeley, Emeryville, Albany, El Cerrito, Richmond, Alameda or Oakland. You must provide a physical address in one of these cities in the application – a P.O. Box unfortunately doesn’t count. The applicant must be the primary creator of the work as in the Director or Producer, i.e., the editor cannot apply for a grant. Additionally, the applicant must be:

•	At least 18 years of age when submitting as a professional,

•	Residing or working in a qualified city for at least one year prior to the application deadline,

•	A credited Executive Producer is not eligible to apply. 

As stated above in the introduction, Narrative/fiction short film projects (animation or live action) will not be accepted in this cycle. Instead, a separate grant cycle will be opening later this summer for Narrative films only. 

If you are a previous grant award winner, you may not reapply with the same project in consecutive years. In a non-consecutive year, if you are reapplying for the same project, it should be for funding in another category (i.e. if you received production or post-production funding, you may reapply for outreach and community engagement funding. For ITVS funded films, we can only accept applications for distribution. However, BFF will consider projects that have received an ITVS Diversity Development Grant.) 

Finally, BFF will not consider a new film proposal from a former grant recipient until the prior funded film is completed.

Eligible Categories in April 2026:

•	Short Documentary (30 minutes or less)

•	Long Documentary (over 30 minutes)

Name: Sloss.Tech Ideas Pitch Competition
Description: Sloss.Tech/Ideas is a Southeast U.S. pitch competition for early-stage startups in sectors like agtech, healthtech, talent and productivity tech, and emerging tech, offering $135,000 in total prizes including a $100,000 grand prize. Eligible startups from 10 Southeastern states can apply by April 10, 2026, and finalists receive benefits like travel stipends, pitch coaching, VIP conference access, and exposure to investors, partners, and customers at the June 24, 2026 event in Birmingham, Alabama.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
What are the eligibility requirements for applicants?
- Product or service must not have been commercially launched earlier than January 2021.
- Companies must not have raised more than $5 million from combined funding sources.
- Startups can only enter one product or service in the competition.
- Founders of the company applying must retain majority ownership (51% or more) of the company at the time of the competition.
- Prior finalist restriction: 2025 Sloss.Tech/Ideas Pitch Competition finalists are ineligible for 2026; 2025 alternates who did not receive cash prizes remain eligible.
- Startups must be legally registered business entities and compliant with all relevant regulations and laws in at least one of the Southeast Region states (defined here as Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee)

Name: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation: Learning from Abroad to Reimagine Health Knowledge Systems for Equity and Wellbeing
Description: The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation is offering up to 15 grants of up to $500,000 each (for up to 36 months) to U.S.-based organizations that look to international models to help build a more equitable and inclusive health knowledge system in the United States. Projects should be community-driven and focus on areas such as centering lived experience in data and policymaking, integrating Indigenous and traditional health frameworks, and combating misinformation. Priority is given to organizations new to RWJF funding since January 1, 2021, with brief proposals due April 13, 2026 at 3pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility & Selection Criteria: 
- All organizations based in the U.S. or its territories are eligible to apply. Submissions from teams that include both U.S. and international members are eligible, but all projects must focus on improving health equity in the U.S. Projects that solely focus on improving health equity outside the U.S. are ineligible for funding. International applicants are eligible to apply, and if selected, will be recommended for an award from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Global Ideas Fund, a donor-advised fund of Charities Aid Foundation of America (CAF America). Please see the program-specific FAQs for more information. 

- We welcome applications from organizations with principal investigators/project directors/leads of all personal and professional backgrounds.

- We especially encourage applications from project director(s) and teams having backgrounds and life experiences that are under increased threats in the current political climate, including Indigenous, Black, Latino, and other persons of color; LGBTQ+ community members; people whose country of origin is not the U.S.; and other historically marginalized groups.  

- RWJF will not select, exclude, or prioritize applicants based on their race, ethnicity, national origin, gender, or other protected characteristics.

- For this funding opportunity, we are prioritizing organizations that are new to RWJF. Organizations are not eligible if they have been awarded any funds from RWJF since January 1, 2021. Your organization is not eligible if it has received any awards from RWJF, whether directly or through a fiscal sponsor, as a grant, program contract, or other type of award since January 1, 2021. If your organization served as a fiscal sponsor since January 1, 2021, please see the program-specific FAQs regarding your eligibility.

- Biomedical, clinical, and bench science projects, as well as medicinal remedies, are not eligible for this funding opportunity.

- If necessary, the applicant organization may utilize the services of a fiscal sponsor to support the project’s financial management, grants management, and reporting activities.  

From FAQs: 
What types of organizations do you fund?
- The vast majority of our funding is to nonprofit organizations and public agencies. Historically, a small percentage  less than one percent of our funding has been to for-profit organizations, and always in instances where the institution's project is an excellent fit with our strategies and we felt they were best suited to do the work.

Name: Blueprint: Tulsa
Description: Blueprint: Tulsa is a 12-week, in-person founder program for 20 early-stage founders in Tulsa and across eligible Southern states who are building tech-enabled or venture-backable startups. Participants receive a $10,000 non-dilutive grant, hands-on workshops, and access to a supportive founder community, with applications open through April 12 and interviews taking place by June 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Blueprint: Tulsa program will accept founders from the following Southern states of the U.S.:
Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, Tennessee, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Florida, Arkansas, Texas, and Oklahoma.

Name: The 2026 Loan Mantra She Leads SC Grant
Description: The Loan Mantra She Leads SC Grant is a $5,000 award for female entrepreneurs in South Carolina — including startups, early-stage founders, and established business owners launching new products or lines — along with up to three hours of complimentary financial strategy sessions with Loan Mantra's CEO. In its inaugural year, three finalists will be selected by a committee and then put to a public community vote in May 2026, with the winner announced on National South Carolina Day, August 31, 2026. The application deadline is April 14, 2026 at 5pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: Applicants must meet the following criteria:
- Business ownership: The following female applicants are eligible:
- The Prospective Owner: Start-ups, concepts, and mission-driven initiatives are welcome.
- The Early-Stage Founder: Your business is less than 3 years old.
- The Innovator: Your business is established, but you are launching a brand-new product or business line to expand the existing model.
- Note: For established businesses, grant capital must be dedicated to building and scaling new expansion, helping female owners push beyond their current business models.

Location: Business must be owned and operated in South Carolina or planning to operate in South Carolina (priority given to projects with a strong community impact).

​Commitment: Funds must be used for the specific growth or community-focused needs outlined in the application.

Name: Neurodiverse Entrepreneur Program
Description: The Neurodiverse Entrepreneur Program supports startups and small businesses led by neurodiverse founders – such as individuals with autism, ADHD, dyslexia, or learning disabilities – by expanding leadership opportunities and celebrating neurodiversity as a driver of innovation. Selected companies receive over $19,000 in grants and services, including a $4,000 microgrant, mentorship, business accelerator participation, and Innovation DuPage membership.

Name: Portland (OR) Parks Foundation Small Grants Program
Description: The Portland Parks Foundation's Small Grants Program awards $2,000 grants to community-based organizations in Portland that work to expand equitable access to parks, natural areas, community gardens, and recreation centers, with priority given to groups serving low-income populations, communities of color, and historically marginalized groups. The program accepts applications once per year in the spring cycle (the fall cycle is currently on hold), with the current application window open March 1–April 15, 2026. Award decisions are announced within 8 weeks of the deadline, with funded programs expected to be completed within 12 months of notification.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Portland Parks Foundation’s Small Grants Program awards financial support to community-based organizations within the city of Portland who foster equitable access to our urban parks, natural areas, community gardens and community recreation centers.  The program is founded on a generous bequest from Nancy Hebb Freeman, an artist, hiker and lover of Portland parks. 

Who can apply:
Community-based/grassroots organizations who care for or provide programming in public
parks, nature spaces, community gardens or community centers THAT ARE:
● Located within the city of Portland AND ARE A
● 501(c)(3) organization, or a non-501(c)(3) organization applying with a fiscal sponsor*,
● AND HAS Not received Small Grants Funds from PPF for the last 12 months

Name: World Business Chicago Horizon Lines - Visions for Chicago
Description: Horizon Lines is a World Business Chicago initiative inviting architects, designers, community leaders, artists, and other teams to submit bold, future-focused ideas for how Chicago could evolve by 2050, with submissions due April 15. Selected visions may be featured in a summer 2026 exhibition at the Chicago Cultural Center and will receive visibility, expert feedback, city engagement, and honoraria.

Name: NYU AI Pitch Competition
Description: The NYU AI Pitch Competition is an event hosted at NYU Stern School of Business on April 30, 2026, where entrepreneurs, students, researchers, and early-stage founders can pitch AI-powered solutions for a chance to win up to $50,000 in AWS partner funding. The competition is open to individuals and teams, with the only requirement being that the solution incorporates artificial intelligence in some way. The submission deadline is April 15, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
About the Competition: 
The NYU AI Pitch Competition brings together aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators to present AI-powered solutions addressing real-world challenges. Hosted by NYU in partnership with Eficens, SBDC, and AWS, this event provides a platform to showcase your startup, receive expert feedback, and connect with the tech community.


Who Can Apply: 
Open to business owners, researchers, students, and early-stage founders
Solution must incorporate artificial intelligence
Individual or team submissions welcome
All submissions must be received before the deadline

Name: Lenovo Backing Every Business Grant
Description: Lenovo’s Back Every Business Grant supports small businesses that have been operating for at least 12 months, use Microsoft 365 as their primary system, and meet size and funding limits (≤250 employees, <$50M revenue, and <$3M raised). Selected businesses receive a comprehensive package that includes grant funding, Lenovo AI-powered devices, software and services, hands-on mentoring, AI training, and My Lenovo Rewards points to use on Lenovo.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Legal residents of the fifty (50) states of the United States and District of Columbia (“U.S.”), United Kingdom, Japan (must reside in or have a business located in either Tokyo and/or Osaka), and Mexico (“Eligibility Area”), representing a Small Business (as defined below) located and registered in the Eligibility Area, and who (i) are at least 18 years of age and the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence as of date of entry, (ii) either own an eligible Small Business or have the authority from a Business Owner to submit an entry on behalf of such Small Business, (iii) speaks English, (iv) use Microsoft 365 as their Small Business’ primary computer operating system, (v) have been actively operating for at least twelve (12) months, (vi). “Small Business” is defined as a business with no more than 250 employees (excluding franchisees, licensees and independent owner/operators of larger business entities), which is located and operating in the Eligibility Area with revenue over the previous twelve (12) months of less than $50M USD, and such Business must not have raised more than $3,000,000 in investment capital.

"In addition, to be eligible, the Small Business must (1) be in good standing under the jurisdiction whose law it is incorporated/organized: (2) NOT be a party to any existing or pending litigation; and (3) NOT be engaged in certain trades or areas as set forth in Exhibit A of the Official Rules.

Winners of the 2023 Lenovo Evolve Small Grant Contest, the Lenovo 2025 Evolve Small AI Grant Contest, and the 2026 Lenovo Growth Lab Contest are not eligible to win a prize in this Contest.

In order to win a Prize, Entrant, Business Owner (whether or not he/she/they actually submitted the Entry, defined below) as well as the Small Business itself must be willing to participate in Lenovo marketing activities (e.g., PR, case studies, being included in video or photo content/footage)."

Name: The National Foster Care Innovation Challenge
Description: The National Foster Care Innovation Challenge is an $800K dual-track funding opportunity for nonprofits and social enterprises developing innovative solutions in foster care, family preservation, and youth transitions. The nonprofit track offers $700K in grants — including four $100,000 first-place awards, four $50,000 runner-up awards, and two $50,000 audience choice awards — while the for-profit track offers a $100,000 equity investment in one mission-driven technology company. Applications are open March 18–April 17, 2026, and organizations led by people with lived experience in foster care are especially encouraged to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible
Nonprofit Track: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations or fiscally sponsored projects
Social Enterprise Track: For-profit organizations with an explicit social mission, including registered B-Corps and benefit corporations
Annual Revenue: Under $5 million (or pre-revenue for startups)
Reach: Currently serving at least 50 families or youth annually, or a clear plan to reach this scale within 12 months
Geography: Based in or serving communities in the United States
Stage: Early-stage organizations are prioritized, though mid-size organizations piloting new technology or innovative approaches are also eligible

Name: Ellis-Beauregard Documentary Film Award
Description: The Ellis-Beauregard Foundation, in partnership with Points North Institute, is offering a $50,000 unrestricted award to one feature-length documentary film currently in post-production, along with an invitation for the director and editor to attend a creative editing retreat at the 2026 Camden International Film Festival in Maine. The award is open to U.S. permanent residents age 18 or older at any career stage, with priority given to artist-driven, formally adventurous projects on track for completion by Summer 2027. Applications close April 16, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The selected filmmaker will receive:

$50,000 in unrestricted funding to support post-production from Ellis-Beauregard Foundation
An invitation for the director and editor to attend a dedicated Points North editing retreat, timed to coincide with the 2026 Camden International Film Festival (CIFF)
Transportation from a location in the US and lodging provided for the retreat for Director and Editor.
During the retreat, the director and editor will share a work-in-progress in Ellis-Beauregard Foundation’s FLEX space on their new state-of-the-art campus. Points North will convene leading documentary editors, producers, and creative advisers in an intimate, supportive environment. The goal is to provide tailored feedback and rigorous conversation, to be metabolized and used to fuel editing progress for the project during the retreat.

Projects that are anticipated to be completed by Summer 2027 are preferred. Finished work will be considered for inclusion in the program at the Camden International Film Festival 2027.

Eligible projects must:

Be nonfiction, feature-length documentaries.
Be in post-production at the time of application.
Be led by applicants at any stage of their career.
Be submitted by an individual artist (funds will be disbursed directly to an individual, not an entity). The applicant must be the individual award recipient. 
Be submitted by a Director who is a U.S. permanent resident age 18 or older.

Name: Kitty Fund Mompreneur Business Grant
Description: The Kitty Fund Mompreneur Business Grant (Founders First CDC) is a national program for mother-owned U.S. businesses that will award 20 finalists a $1,000 micro-grant (total $20,000) plus free access to one of two accelerator-style programs: Passport Community (weekly scaling sessions) or Zebra Leadership (6-session CEO/team-building program). Eligibility includes identifying as a mom owner/CEO, being in business at least 1 year, having 2–100 employees, and ≤$5M in annual revenue.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Identify as a Mom business owner
- Must be a CEO, President, or Business Owner
- Must have an active U.S. based business
- Business annual revenue does not exceed $5M
- Must have between 2 to 100 employees
- Minimum of 1 year in business

Name: FoodLab Chicago 7.0 Cohort
Description: FoodLab Chicago 7.0 is a free educational program by the Greater Chatham Initiative designed for Black and Brown food service entrepreneurs in Chicago who have been operating for at least 12–18 months, offering training in Menu Engineering, Plate Costing, Food Service Accounting, Financial Management, Marketing, and more. The cohort kicks off April 20, 2026, with weekly in-person sessions every Monday from 9am–12pm at 639 E. 87th Street. Seating is limited, so early applications are encouraged — contact ciera@greaterchathaminitiative.org with questions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: - Chefs, restaurateurs, caterers, food truck vendors, bakers, culinary artist, and other food-related businesses

Name: Replit Agent 4 Buildathon
Description: Replit’s Agent 4 Buildathon is a three-week competition running from March 24 to April 16, 2026, where participants use Agent 4 to explore an idea, build it into a product, and launch it, with support through weekly programming, office hours, and a private Discord community. The event offers $50k+ in prizes, including weekly awards, a $10,000 grand prize, and category prizes for projects such as best mobile app, most creative, and best use of Agent 4.

Name: 2026 Target x Shipt Garden Grants
Description: Target and Shipt's 2026 Garden Grants Program awards $6,000 each to up to 50 community-led urban garden projects across Chicago, Detroit, New York, and Birmingham, Alabama, with funds usable for infrastructure, planting supplies, and educational materials. Eligible applicants include accredited K-12 schools and 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving senior living or community-based organizations, and new gardens that haven't broken ground yet are welcome to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
- Accredited K-12 schools
- 501 (c)(3) nonprofit organizations serving senior living communities or community-based organizations leading or planning an urban garden initiative

Name: Downtown Baltimore BOOST Program
Description: The Downtown Partnership of Baltimore's BOOST Program supports local entrepreneurs in occupying vacant retail storefronts within Baltimore's 106-block downtown business improvement district, with funding support from JPMorganChase, the City of Baltimore, and the Baltimore Civic Fund. Eligible applicants must be for-profit retail or personal services businesses that have been operating for at least two years, are in good standing with the State of Maryland, and will operate at least five days a week at their downtown location. The application deadline is April 17, 2026 at 11:59pm ET, with priority given to businesses locating in targeted downtown corridors such as Charles Street, Howard Street, and the CFG Bank Arena area.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
BOOST Application
Downtown Partnership of Baltimore (DPOB), is proud to release this application for the BOOST Program. BOOST supports local entrepreneurship and the activation of vacant retail storefronts in the 106-block business improvement district managed by DPOB. This BOOST cohort is a key component of the Vacants to Vibrancy Initiative, with support from JPMorganChase, the City of Baltimore, and the Baltimore Civic Fund. 



Applications must be completed by 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time on Friday, April 17, 2026. For additional information, please visit the BOOST Program information page on DPOB's website.
