*
Upload Evidence of Good Standing with the State of Maryland.
*

Name: Short Film Grant From Adobe x NAACP
Description: The NAACP's 2026 Cinematic Shorts Competition, in partnership with Adobe, selects six filmmakers to each receive a $10,000 grant to produce a short film addressing social justice issues, in collaboration with the NAACP Hollywood Bureau and NAACP+ Studios. All filmmakers in the cohort also receive an all-expenses-paid trip to Los Angeles to attend the 58th NAACP Image Awards, including red carpet access and meetings with industry executives. The competition takes place during the 117th NAACP National Convention in Chicago, July 16–22, 2026, with an application deadline of April 17, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Film as Activism
The 2026 Cinematic Shorts Competition in partnership with Adobe, will take place during the 117th NAACP National Convention in Chicago, IL from July 16th – 22nd. This exciting competition will give SIX (6) filmmakers the opportunity to produce a short film addressing issues of social justice. The winning filmmakers will each be awarded a $10K grant to produce a short film in conjunction with the NAACP Hollywood Bureau and NAACP+ Studios.

In addition, ALL the filmmakers in this year's cohort will receive an all-expense paid trip to Los Angeles to attend the 58th NAACP Image Awards, where they will walk the red carpet, and attend informational meetings with industry executives.



Eligibility: 
In order to participate in the Cinematic Shorts Competition, filmmakers:

Must be between the ages of 18-29 by April 17, 2026.
Must submit one creative sample (short film, commercial or photography) that demonstrates your skill set as a filmmaker.
Must submit a written personal biography 150-200 words.
Must submit a written statement between 250-300 words answering ONE of the essay questions on the application.
Must provide your own transportation to and from Chicago, IL for the competition. (Local hotel accommodations will be provided for selected filmmakers/activists).

Name: M&F Bank Empowering Growth Small Business Grant
Description: M&F Bank’s Empowering Growth Small Business Grant reflects its mission to strengthen communities by investing in local entrepreneurs and helping small businesses thrive across North Carolina. For 2026, the program will award a $10,000 grant to one Durham-area business, with applications open from March 6 to April 17, 2026. Eligible applicants must have $750,000 or less in gross revenue, 25 or fewer employees, have been in business 10 years or less, maintain a website, and hold an M&F Bank business account in good standing since January 31, 2024 or earlier.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Your business must have gross revenues of $750,000 or less
- You must have been in business for ten (10) years or less as of January 31, 2026
- The business entity listed in the application must have been an M&F Bank customer since January 31, 2024 or earlier
- Your small business must have 25 employees or less, including yourself
- Your business must have a website
- Your M&F Bank business account(s) must be in good standing

Name: Pennsylvania Agricultural Innovation Grant Program
Description: Pennsylvania’s Agricultural Innovation Grant Program offers reimbursement grants to help farmers and agriculture-related businesses adopt new technologies, conservation practices, and renewable energy innovations that boost profitability and sustainability. Applications for this round must be submitted online between February 2, 2026 (8 a.m.) and April 18, 2026 (11:59 p.m.), with eligible projects ranging from on-farm efficiency and biosecurity upgrades to energy generation from agricultural sources. Funding is available for innovation planning, onsite implementation, and larger regional-impact projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- A person who grows an agricultural commodity and who has anticipated sales greater than $2,000 per year.
- A person who processes an agricultural commodity and has anticipated sales greater than $10,000 per year.
- A person who provides technical assistance or services to farmers for conservation, engineering, veterinary care, animal disease management, farm management, agricultural commodity production, nutrient management, or similar services.
- A person or cooperative association that utilizes agricultural commodities to create products or energy.

Name: Utility x Chase Restaurant Pitch Competition
Description: The Utility Show Restaurant Pitch Competition, presented with Chase, invites U.S.-based entrepreneurs age 18+ who plan to open or expand a restaurant concept within the next 12 months to compete for funding by submitting a pitch deck, financial projections, a one-minute video, and written responses. One winner receives a $20,000 grand prize, two runners-up receive $2,500 each, and finalists pitch live in Chicago on May 17–18, 2026; the entry deadline was extended to April 18, 2026 or until 300 eligible submissions are received.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Promotion is open to legal residents of the United States, including the District of Columbia, who are legally authorized to work in the United States, age 18 or older at the time of entry and are planning to open a new restaurant or expand an existing concept within the next 12 months. Void in Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, outside the U.S., and wherever else prohibited by law. Entrant must NOT be under any contractual obligation that would conflict with this Contest or the Official Rules. Employees of the Sponsor, JPMC, and their respective subsidiaries, affiliates, advertising and promotion agencies, and the immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, and siblings and their spouses) of, and/or those living in the same household of each, are not eligible to enter. Promotion is subject to all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations.

Name: 2026 I Be Black Girl Gives (IBBGives) Grant Application
Description: I Be Black Girl Gives (IBBGives) is a giving circle and philanthropic platform in Nebraska where Black women and femmes collectively decide which projects receive funding. Grants prioritize Nebraska-based organizations or projects where at least 80% of leadership and beneficiaries identify as underserved populations — particularly Black women, femmes, or girls — with total budgets under $50,000, and a 501(c)(3) designation is not required. The 2026 grant application closes April 20, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
I Be Black Girl (IBBG) Overview:

IBBG serves as a collective for Black women, femmes and girls to actualize their full potential to authentically be, through autonomy, abundance and liberation.

About IBBGives:

I Be Black Girl Gives (IBBGives) is a first of its kind giving circle and philanthropic platform in Nebraska that creates opportunities for Black women to give in meaningful and collective ways. Voting members, Black women and femmes who invested $150 or more in the previous year, collectively decide which projects receive funding. 

Friends of IBBG also have the ability to contribute to the available grant pool and sponsor eligible voting members. 

IBBGives is prioritizing funding for:

Organizations or projects/programs located in Nebraska.
Organizations or projects/programs in which at least 80% of leadership and project/program beneficiaries identify as underserved populations, including but not limited to Black women, femmes, or girls.
Organizations or projects/programs do NOT need to be affiliated with a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
Organizations or projects/programs whose budgets do not exceed $50,000.

Name: Startup CPG Grocery Run with KeHE
Description: Startup CPG’s Grocery Run with KeHE is a curated sampling event for 70 emerging brands not yet carried by KeHE to showcase their products to 300+ KeHE retailers, reps, and buyers in Chicago on June 9, 2026, ahead of the KeHE Holiday Show. Selected brands get table space and buyer exposure, but must meet eligibility requirements, respond quickly if chosen, and pay an estimated $200 participation fee to help cover venue costs.

Name: Open Pitch at Invest Fest
Description: Open Pitch is a startup pitch competition taking place August 7–9, 2026 in Atlanta, GA at Invest Fest, where early-stage tech companies compete for a $125,000 investment prize. Hundreds of startups apply, with five finalists pitching live on stage to venture capital investors and business leaders, and one ultimate winner selected. The application deadline is April 10, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Additional Information: 
Open Pitch is a high-energy startup competition built to discover and support the most promising early-stage tech companies. With hundreds of applicants, 5 finalists, and 1 ultimate winner, Open Pitch is where breakout startups get their first shot at funding and national exposure. Throughout the competition, top startups pitch live to business leaders and venture capitalists with a proven track record of backing category-defining companies—spotlighting bold ideas, breakthrough technologies, and the founders building what’s next.

The winning startup receives a $125,000 investment in exchange for 7% equity in the company. 6% via a YCombinator style SAFE and 1% equity grant to Earn Your Leisure. The investment needs to be made into a Delaware C corp. 

Who should apply: 
Open Pitch is for early-stage tech founders at any point in the building process. Whether you’ve launched a product, built an MVP, or are just starting to show traction, we want to hear from you. If you’ve got a clear vision, a real problem you are solving, and the drive to build something big—this is your stage.

Name: SAMHSA Implementing Zero Suicide In Health Systems NOFO
Description: A SAMHSA grant that provides funding to healthcare systems and community-based primary care or behavioral health organizations to implement the Zero Suicide framework for adults at risk of suicide. Eligibility is limited to settings such as community-based primary care or behavioral health care organizations, emergency departments, state mental health agencies, public health agencies, U.S. territories, and tribes/tribal organizations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligibility is statutorily limited to community-based primary care or behavioral health care settings, emergency departments, State mental health agencies, public health agencies, United States territories, and Indian Tribes/tribal organizations.

Name: San Fernando Small Business Assistance Program
Description: The City of San Fernando's Small Business Assistance Program offers grants of up to $10,000 to local businesses for exterior façade improvements, including anti-graffiti coatings, paint, awnings, signage (up to $3,000), green walls, security cameras, and architectural upgrades. Priority is given to businesses with a high incidence of graffiti, and the program aims to enhance both the appearance and economic vitality of San Fernando. No application deadline was listed in the content provided — interested businesses should contact the City at Info@SanFernando.gov or call (818) 898-1200 for current details.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Small Business Assistance Program
The City is proud to launch the Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP), offering grants of up to $10,000 for exterior façade improvements, such as graffiti-resistant window coverings, green walls, signage (up to $3,000), paint, awnings, security cameras with police access, and architectural upgrades. Priority will be given to businesses with a high incidence of graffiti. This initiative supports local businesses while enhancing San Fernando's aesthetic and economic vitality.

Use of Grant Funds
Grant funds are earmarked for various improvements including, but not limited to:

Anti-graffiti coating and graffiti-resistant window covering.
Exterior vertical landscape (green wall).
Signage (up to $3,000).
Paint.
Awning or window shade cover.
Exterior security cameras with direct access granted to the San Fernando Police Department.
Exterior architectural details (e.g., replacing existing security gate with alternatives, architectural appropriate window bars).

Name: Global Arts Prize
Description: The Global Arts Prize celebrates innovative artists and cultural initiatives that are redefining the role of the arts in today’s society. Each year, it awards a total of $60,000 to two winners, offering unrestricted funding to support their creative vision without the constraints of traditional grants. Open to organizations worldwide, the prize recognizes both emerging and established leaders driving forward-thinking work across the arts and humanities.

Name: The Pitch by Deel
Description: “The Pitch” by Deel is a global startup competition where founders can apply in minutes to pitch their company for a chance to win up to $1 million in investment. Startups compete first at regional events, where winners receive $50K and advance to a global finale for the grand prize. Beyond funding, participants gain exposure, networking opportunities, and access to a community and startup perks.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Any seed-stage startup with a minimum viable product (MVP) can apply. We’re looking for companies at the pre-seed or seed stage that have incorporated (we can help with that!) and are ready to scale.

Name: LA2050 Grants Challenge
Description: The LA2050 Grants Challenge is a Los Angeles–focused funding opportunity offering awards of up to $75,000 to social impact organizations working to make LA the best place to connect, create, learn, live, and play. The 2026 challenge uses a public voting model, where Angelenos help decide funding priorities, with Part 1 (organization screening) due April 22 and final awards announced October 2026. Organizations advancing to Part 2 will submit a project proposal aligned with the community’s top-voted issue areas.

Name: USDA Value-Added Producer Grant
Description: The USDA Value-Added Producer Grant (VAPG) program provides funding to agricultural producers to help them create and market value-added products from their raw commodities, increasing income and expanding market opportunities. Grants can support planning activities (like feasibility studies or business plans) up to $50,000 or working capital (such as processing, packaging, marketing, and inventory) up to $200,000, with a required 1:1 funding match. Priority is often given to beginning farmers, small family farms, and cooperative or regional food system projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants include:
- Agricultural producers (including harvesters and steering committees)
- Agricultural producer groups
- Farmer- or rancher-cooperatives
- Majority-controlled producer-based business ventures

Applicants must demonstrate that they:
- Own and produce more than 50% of the raw commodity
- Will retain greater revenue from the value-added product than from the raw commodity alone

Name: H-E-B Quest for Texas Best
Description: H-E-B's Quest for Texas Best is an annual competition open to locally owned, small Texas food, beverage, and general merchandise businesses for a chance to win $25,000 and get their products placed on H-E-B shelves. Applicants must submit a 2-minute video showcasing how and where their product is made, imagery of the product, and why H-E-B should select it. The application deadline is April 22, 2026 at 4:59pm, and informational webinars are available to help applicants prepare their submissions
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Local products made by Texans

The best from across the Lone Star state

For the last thirteen years, H‑E‑B has set out on a quest to find the best in Texas – the best local products made by Texans! From the Panhandle to the Rio Grande Valley, from West Texas to Beaumont, the H‑E‑B “Quest for Texas Best” is an open call for locally owned, small food, beverage, and general merchandise suppliers to have their items considered for placement on H‑E‑B shelves and $25,000 in their pocket!

Name: L'Oréal x NAACP Inclusive Beauty Fund Grant
Description: The NAACP and L'Oréal USA have partnered to offer six grants of $25,000 each to entrepreneurs in the beauty industry through the Inclusive Beauty Fund Grant, open to a wide range of businesses including salons, spas, barber shops, makeup artists, and beauty schools. Applications are open March 23–April 23, 2026, with selected recipients announced in May 2026. The grant is administered in collaboration with Deed and aims to advance equitable opportunities in the beauty industry.

Name: DC Department of Small and Local Business Development Dream Accelerator Program
Description: The Dream Accelerator Program is a cohort-based business training program for microbusinesses in Washington, DC’s Wards 7 and 8, offering support in business foundations, marketing, finance, operations, and AI. Applications are open from March 23 to April 23, 2026, and selected participants will compete in a pitch competition for cash awards ranging from $2,500 to $7,500.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Microbusinesses located in Wards 7 and 8.

Name: 2026 BMO Celebrating Women Grant Program
Description: The BMO Celebrating Women Grant Program will award 15 grants of $10,000 to U.S. for-profit small businesses that can show a clear growth strategy and demonstrate how they support the advancement of women. Eligible businesses must be active, in good standing, have $50 million or less in annual revenue, have been selling a product or service for at least two years as of April 2, 2026, and be located in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, Wisconsin, or Wyoming. Applicants must be U.S. business owners of legal age who have not previously received this grant and are not affiliated with BMO.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Criteria for applicants:

- You’re the owner of a business
- You’re a resident of the U.S.
- You’ve reached the legal age of majority in the state where your business resides
- You have not received a grant from any previous BMO Celebrating Women Grant Program
- You are not a BMO employee, shareholder or agent and have not been involved in the development or judging of the BMO Celebrating Women 
Grant Program

Criteria for businesses:
- Currently active and operating in the U.S.
- Has a physical location (or a mailing address for their headquarters) in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming. Businesses located in Michigan or Texas must be within 100 miles of a BMO full-service retail branch
- Must be a for-profit business with annual revenue of $50 million USD or less
- In good standing in the state in which the business is registered
- In operation selling a product or service for at least two years as of April 2, 2026

Name: Sweet Home South Chicago Pitch Competition
Description: The TechRise Sweet Home South Chicago Pitch Competition will select five early-stage small businesses rooted in South Chicago to pitch at the June 13 vendor marketplace event, where one winner will receive a $25,000 prize. Beyond the competition, selected founders get hands-on coaching, resources, and connections to help them prepare and grow, with applications open through April 23.

Name: Culver City Special Events Grant Program
Description: Culver City’s 2026–27 Special Events Grant Program provides funding and sponsorship support for public events that benefit the community or promote the city regionally. Applicants must attend a required virtual pre-application meeting on March 24, 2026, before applying, and eligible events must be open to the public, take place in or near Culver City, and occur between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. Applications open March 25 and are due by April 24, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible events include:
- Community or charitable events with recreational, cultural, or social benefits to residents
- Larger-scale events that promote Culver City regionally

Additional eligibility requirements:
- Must be open to the general public
- Must take place in Culver City or immediately adjacent
- Must occur between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027
- Funding is not available to individuals or for political events or organizations

Name: Baltimore Community Catalyst Grants
Description: Baltimore’s Community Catalyst Grants Program supports neighborhood-based organizations in historically disinvested areas that are leading community-driven revitalization efforts. For Round 6 in 2026, the city is offering up to $1.02 million in operating funds, with applications open from March 23 to April 24, 2026. Eligible applicants include community development corporations and other neighborhood-based groups working on locally driven neighborhood transformation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible organizations include community development corporations, neighborhood-based development organizations, umbrella organizations and other neighborhood-based organizations. Eligible projects support locally-driven revitalization initiatives and help advance neighborhood revitalization and transformation.

Name: NBCUniversal Local Impact Grants
Description: The NBCUniversal Local Impact Grants program will award a total of $2.5 million in 2026 to nonprofits in 11 NBC- and Telemundo-owned station markets, supporting organizations working in youth education and empowerment, next generation storytellers, and community engagement. It offers unrestricted general operating support to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits and fiscally sponsored groups with annual expenses between $100,000 and $1,000,000, with applications open March 24 to April 24, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Organization must be a tax exempt 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization and the associated EIN must have been active for more than a year.
- Fiscally sponsored organizations are eligible. If you are a fiscally sponsored organization, please work with your fiscal sponsor to complete the application. If you have any questions about applying through a fiscal sponsor, please reach out to CorporateSocialResponsibility@nbcuni.com.
- The applying organization’s total expenses must be between $100,000 and $1,000,000.
- The applying organization’s revenue must be greater than $100,000.
- Grant award will not be over 30% of the organization’s total expenses.
- The applying organization must have been in existence and in operation for at least one year.
- The applying organization must self-identify in one of the three categories that best characterizes their work and impact as an organization:
-- Youth Education and Empowerment - In-school and community-based programs that equip youth with the tools they need to succeed, including STEM/STEAM education and youth entrepreneurship. These programs primarily serve people under 24 years of age. Examples include: academic enrichment programs, youth development programs, science, tech, engineering, art or math programs/camps.
-- Next Generation Storytellers - Programs that develop pathways for emerging talent and youth voices to explore careers in communications, arts, news, sports and entertainment. Examples include: arts education, filmmaking training, or storytelling programs.
-- Community Engagement - Programs that help foster community unity by enabling individuals to engage with and volunteer in their regions. Examples include: citizen engagement programs, volunteering events, campaigns responding to community member’s needs (e.g. food insecurity, health services).
- Organization must not have received any cash, grant funding, or sponsorship from Comcast NBCUniversal or an NBC and/or Telemundo-owned television station in an amount equal to or exceeding $10,000 per year during any of the past three (3) years. This includes but is not limited to previous NBCUniversal Local Impact Grant winners, Comcast NBCUnites partners, or NBC/Telemundo-owned station partners and Comcast Corporation or Foundation grantees.
- NBCUniversal Local Impact Grants will only award one grant per Tax ID number, across all eleven markets. If your organization shares a Tax ID number, please coordinate internally as only one application across all markets will be accepted for consideration as a finalist for a grant.
- Comcast NBCUniversal and NBCUniversal Local are committed to supporting the interests and needs of our communities.

The following organizations are not eligible to apply:
- Labor Organizations, Causes or Programs
- Political Organizations, Causes or Programs
- Religious Organizations, Causes or Programs
- Schools, Educational Institutions and their affiliated fundraising entities and foundations (including elementary, secondary and universities).
- Fiscally sponsored schools are not eligible.
- 501(c)4 Organizations

Name: Empromptu Builder Fund
Description: The Empromptu Builder Fund offers a $15,000 cash grant to one U.S.-based founder or co-founding team building an AI-powered product, plus $500 in Empromptu platform credits to 10 runner-ups. The application is open to early-stage founders 18 or older with no minimum revenue or technical background required. Applications closes April 25, 2026, with the winner announced in May 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements
- No minimum revenue. No required technical background. Just a real idea and the drive to ship it.

You must: 
- Be a founder or co-founder of an active startup or early-stage product
- Be building something with an AI component
- Be based in the United States
- Be 18 or older
- Create a free Empromptu account to apply

Name: Schnucks Springboard Business Accelerator
Description: Schnucks Springboard is a business accelerator for small Midwestern CPG brands (located in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota or Wisconsin) that have existing retail sales, offering weekly in-person classes in St. Louis, a limited in-store shelf trial, networking opportunities, and up to $5,000 in equity-free funding for participants who meet program requirements. Applications for the 2026/2027 cohort are open through April 25, 2026, and eligible companies must be privately owned, have under $1 million in annual CPG revenue, fewer than 50 employees, fewer than 10 years in business, and products that have never been sold at Schnucks.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify for Schnucks Springboard, a privately-owned company must have a consumer packaged good (CPG) product with existing retail sales and meet the following criteria:
- Annual CPG product revenue of less than $1 Million
- Fewer than 10 years in the CPG business
- Fewer than 50 employees
- Open exclusively to companies whose products have never been sold at Schnucks or any of its banners
- Be based in one of twelve Midwestern states (as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau): Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota or Wisconsin.
- If selected – have the ability to attend all classes in-person and to also meet food safety and insurance requirements for a product shelf trial.

Name: City of Raleigh Building Up-fit Grant
Description: The City of Raleigh’s Building Up-fit Grant supports local economic growth by helping property owners activate vacant or underutilized commercial space within city limits. The matching reimbursement program covers up to 50% of qualified interior construction costs to create new business uses or jobs. Residential properties, franchises, and exterior projects are not eligible.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Business Insurance Grant
Description: The Enthuse Foundation Business Insurance Grant, sponsored by Alera Group, provides $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur who runs a full-time consumer packaged goods (CPG) business. The funding is intended to help cover business-related insurance or related costs such as product, equipment, homeowners, or car insurance. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and a clear plan for how the funds will support their business, with the winner announced in June 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants Must:
- Identify as a woman entrepreneur with an established consumer packaged goods (CPG) business. For example, food, beverage, skincare, household goods, personal hygiene, etc (tangible product). E-mail info@enthusefoundation.org with specific questions.
- Business must be the entrepreneur's full-time job
- Prove use of funds (documentation, proof from external agency)
- Be a U.S. Citizen
- If selected, submit Required New Vendor Forms (will be provided by our Foundation)
- Submit most recent W2 form (if selected as a finalist)
- Use the funds between June 2026 – June 2027
Industry: Food & Beverage,Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care

Description: This grant awards $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur with an established full-time CPG business to support digital marketing expenses, such as website improvements, promotion, and social media strategy. Applicants must demonstrate financial need, explain how the funding will help grow the business, provide a clear spending plan, and, if selected as a finalist, submit a W-2 and vendor forms; the deadline is Monday, April 27, with the winner announced in June 2026.

Be a U.S. Citizen.

Industry: Food & Beverage,Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care

Description: This grant offers $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur who runs an established full-time CPG business to help cover essential business technology and tools, such as website, domain, or payment-processing costs. Applicants must show financial need, have a clear plan for the funds, and, if selected as a finalist, provide documentation like a W-2 and vendor forms; the application deadline is Monday, April 27, and the winner will be announced in June 2026.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Healthcare Grant
Description: The Enthuse Foundation Healthcare Grant, sponsored by Cross Agency, awards $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur with an established, full-time CPG business to help cover health insurance or other medical expenses. Applicants must show financial need, explain how the funding will support their business, and provide documentation of how the funds are used; the application deadline is April 27.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants Must:
- Identify as a woman entrepreneur with an established consumer packaged goods (CPG) business. For example, food, beverage, skincare, household goods, personal hygiene, etc (tangible product). E-mail info@enthusefoundation.org with specific questions.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Retirement Grant
Description: The Enthuse Foundation Retirement Grant, sponsored by Alliant, provides $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur with an established, full-time CPG business to put toward retirement savings. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and a clear plan for using the funds, with finalists submitting additional documentation and interviewing before the winner is announced in June 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants Must: 
- Identify as a woman entrepreneur with an established consumer packaged goods (CPG) business. For example, food, beverage, skincare, household goods, personal hygiene, etc (tangible product). E-mail info@enthusefoundation.org with specific questions.
- Business must be the entrepreneur's full-time job
- Prove use of funds (documentation, proof from external agency).
- Be a U.S. Citizen.
- If selected, submit the Required New Vendor Forms (which will be provided by our Foundation).
- Submit most recent W2 form (if selected as a finalist).
- Use the funds between July 2026 – June 2027
Industry: Food & Beverage,Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care

Name: 3pts Artists & Makers Impact Fund
Description: The 3pts Artists & Makers Impact Fund awards a single $3,500 grant to one U.S.-based mid-career artist or maker who produces tangible objects or goods and is actively working to grow a sustainable creative business. Eligible applicants must be at least 21, have a legally registered U.S. business, and demonstrate a history of intentional business development beyond day-to-day production, such as classes, workshops, or community participation. The application deadline is April 27, 2026 at 11:59pm ET, with a $10 non-refundable application fee required to submit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The 3pts Artists & Makers Impact Fund is a $3,500 award supporting U.S.-based artists and makers who create tangible objects or goods and are working to sustain and grow a business. Funding may be used for materials, equipment, workspace costs, professional development, production expenses, or other needs that strengthen an artist or maker’s practice.

Applicant Qualifications:
Be 21 years of age or older
Be based in the United States
Have their business legally registered in the United States
Be a mid-career artist with an established practice
Produce a tangible object, artwork, or good
Provide a history of how they’ve worked on their business, not just in their business (self-directed education and development, classes, programs, community, workshops, etc.)
Have a clear vision for the future of their creative and business practice

Name: SEED SPOT x Walmart Road to Open Call
Description: SEED SPOT’s Road to Open Call is an in-person pitch opportunity for DMV-based founders with shelf-ready, U.S.-made products to present directly to Walmart buyers. Selected entrepreneurs get prep workshops, live feedback, and a chance to earn a fast-pass to Walmart’s 2026 Open Call in Bentonville, with applications due April 27, 2026 and the pitch event on May 27, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This opportunity is for brands that
- Have a product that is made, grown, or assembled in the United States.
- Have previous retail and online sales experience and are looking to expand into national retail, including mass-market retailers like Walmart.
- Have a shelf-ready product across any Walmart product category that is complete with approved packaging and UPCs.
- Have strong marketing and social media strategies.
- Are eager to refine their pitch and retail strategy with expert guidance.

Name: Enthuse Foundation Professional Services Grant
Description: The Enthuse Foundation Professional Services Grant, sponsored by Accountability, awards $2,500 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur with an established, full-time CPG business to hire outside professional support such as a lawyer, brand manager, business manager, or distributor. Applicants must show financial need, explain how the funding will help grow their business, and provide a clear plan for using the grant, with the winner announced in June 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants Must:

Be a U.S. Citizen.

Name: Gates Foundation Global Grand Challenge: AI to Accelerate Charitable Giving
Description: The Gates Foundation's Grand Challenges program is offering grants of up to $150,000 for one-year projects that use artificial intelligence to help donors give more and give sooner, with a focus on applications relevant to global health and development. Eligible applicants include nonprofits, mission-driven for-profit organizations, and collaborative partnerships, and proposals must address at least one of three challenge areas: helping donors discover causes, reducing barriers to giving, or building foundational AI infrastructure for philanthropy. The application deadline is April 28, 2026 at 11:30am PDT.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Challenge
We are seeking applications and use cases of AI that address the core question: How might AI support donors to give more and give sooner?

This RFP is focused on supporting donor-facing applications and underlying systems of giving that test and demonstrate bold, innovative applications of AI that strengthen and expand philanthropic giving. Desired outputs include generating practical evidence and examples to inform broader practice across the philanthropic sector. We are particularly interested in solutions that increase support for GH&D.

For this RFP, GH&D refers broadly to efforts that improve health, economic opportunity, and human well-being in low- and middle-income countries. Within this field, we are especially interested in efforts that reduce preventable mortality, combat infectious diseases, and expand pathways out of extreme poverty, consistent with the Gates Foundation's long-term goals.

Projects do not need to focus exclusively on GH&D to be competitive. However, proposals that clearly demonstrate applicability to GH&D challenges, or that generate insights relevant to these priorities, will receive additional consideration. We welcome proposals that address the needs of various donor types including everyday donors, high-net-worth individuals, foundations, or other entities relevant to the challenge areas below.


Eligibility Criteria
Applicants must be able to conduct all project activities and reporting in English and be willing and able to participate in up to three virtual and/or in-person learning convenings with peer grantees over the one-year grant period. Eligible entities for this initiative include:

Nonprofit and Civil Society Organizations, including registered nonprofits and charities, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and community-based organizations.
Mission-Driven For-Profit Organizations. For-profit entities that have a clear public-benefit mission aligned with the goals of the RFP are eligible. Funding cannot be used for core commercial product development or general business operations. Proposed activities must advance equitable, responsible, or safe uses of AI in ways that benefit society.
Consortia, Partnerships, & Collaborative Proposals. Proposals may be submitted through partnerships and other collaborative arrangements. In such cases, one lead organization must serve as the primary applicant and submit the proposal, with partner organizations included as sub-grantees.

Name: Beyond Barriers Innovation Accelerator
Description: The 2026 Beyond Type 1 Innovation Accelerator provides $5K–$50K grants plus mentorship to organizations and entrepreneurs developing solutions to improve diabetes care, particularly in underserved communities. It focuses on innovations like earlier detection, reducing stigma, and expanding access to care, with applications due April 28, 2026. Selected participants receive funding, structured support, and join a cohort program running May–November 2026 to help scale their impact.

Name: Illinois Capital Development Board Art-in-Architecture Program
Description: The Illinois Capital Development Board's Art-in-Architecture Program is seeking qualified Illinois-based professional artists to create four permanent exterior public art installations for the IDOT Coalfield Rest Areas in Waggoner, Illinois, with a total project budget of $82,000. The artwork will be installed on large granite walls at the entrances of the north and southbound rest areas, celebrating the history of coal mining in central Illinois, and must be durable and weather-resistant. At least three semi-finalists will each receive $1,500 to develop site-specific proposals, with the submission deadline of April 29, 2026 at 3:00pm.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applications submitted via Email to: CDB.ArtinArchitecture@illinois.gov

The Fine Arts Review Committee will review the portfolios of eligible applicants. At least three artists/teams will be selected as semi-finalists and paid a fee of $1,500 each to develop and present a site-specific design proposal. After the presentations, the Committee will select a winning artist/team for the commission. Correspondence will be sent to the semi-finalists

The project budget is $82,000

ELIGIBILITY
These public art commissions and potential purchases are open to all professional
artists, artisans, or artist-led teams that live and work in the state of Illinois.
• An artist/artisan is defined as a skilled practitioner that generates designs
and concepts for creative works that reflect form, beauty, and aesthetic
perception. All artists on a team must be from Illinois.
• Subcontractors may be used and are defined as those providing technical
implementation such as construction, fabrication, and/or assembly for
portions or all of a finished product under direct supervision and control of an
artist.
• Faculty and staff of IDOT are not eligible to apply for this commission.

Name: This Woman Knows Grant
Description: Grant supporting women entrepreneurs to advance their businesses with capital and visibility.

Name: Vilcek Foundation Grants
Description: Vilcek Foundation Grants support U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits that specifically focus on helping immigrants in the arts, sciences, education, or through social services, with a preference for organizations pursuing creative, distinctive projects and operations. The foundation is currently accepting applications for its 2026 grants (deadline April 30, 2026) and requires standard nonprofit documentation like a W-9, IRS determination letter, Form 990, and audited financials.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply for a grant:
- An organization must be a nonprofit organization operating under U.S. IRC Section 501(c)(3). 
- An organization must be based in the United States or U.S. territories.
- An organization’s activities and expenditures must primarily be based in the United States or U.S. territories.
- An organization must abide by all laws and regulations governing nonprofit organizations under IRC Section 501(c)(3) in the United States.
- An organization must be in good standing and hold tax-exempt status with the IRS.
- An organization must be able to provide the following documents:
Signed W-9 with a valid EIN for the organization
IRS determination letter
- A recent Form 990, Form 990-PF, Form 990-EZ, or Form 990-N
- An audited financial statement
- Annual operating budget and proposal budget when applicable

Restrictions
- The foundation does not award grants to organizations working with fiscal sponsors. 
- The foundation does not award grants in support of scientific research. 
- The foundation does not award grants in support of capital projects or campaigns.
- The foundation does not award grants to organizations seeking support to cover the costs of galas, award ceremonies, or other events primarily intended as fundraisers.
- The foundation does not award grants to K-12 schools or to charter schools. While we recognize the significant need for arts program support in schools, this is not our current focus or area of expertise. 
- The foundation does not participate in or provide support to any political campaigns on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for elective public office.
- The foundation does not offer renewals on grants; all grants awarded by the foundation are intended as one-time, non-renewable awards. 
- The foundation requires a two-cycle waiting period before past Vilcek Foundation grantees may reapply (e.g., a 2025 grantee may reapply in 2028).

Name: Local Development Corporation of East New York Opportunity Fund Grant
Description: The LDCENY Opportunity Fund (in partnership with HSBC, the Brooklyn Women’s Business Center, and EBBID) offers up to $10,000 in grant funding for aspiring entrepreneurs and early-stage businesses (5 years old or less) based in East New York, Brownsville, Canarsie, Starrett City, or Cypress Hills. Name: O'Shaughnessy Fellowships
Description: The O’Shaughnessy Fellowships & Grants is a one-year program that gives researchers, builders, and creatives $100,000 to turn ambitious ideas into reality while keeping 100% ownership (no equity). It’s designed to fund bold projects without corporate control, thesis requirements, or committee approvals, and applications close April 30, 2026.

Name: Mass Cultural Council Creative Experiences Grants
Description: The Mass Cultural Council Creative Experiences program offers one-year grants of $2,500 or $5,000 to Massachusetts-based organizations, schools, businesses, and government entities funding arts, humanities, and science activities taking place between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. Applications are open through April 30, 2026, with priority given to BIPOC-centered organizations, first-time applicants, and those serving low-income communities. Eligible applicants must be based in Massachusetts and responsible for producing or presenting the proposed experience.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
THE ARTS are the creation of work in the crafts and performing, visual, media, folk, design, literary, and interdisciplinary arts. They also include the presentation and preservation of, and education about, works in these disciplines.

THE HUMANITIES are types of learning that deal with human values and aspirations, human thought and culture, language, and creativity. Examples include, but are not limited to, history, social studies, philosophy, criticism, and literature.

THE SCIENCES are limited to the cultural, interpretive, and educational expression of science and refers to types of learning that deal with nature, science, and technology in ways that explain how they relate to people’s lives. Some organizations that conduct this type of activity include aquariums, botanical gardens, nature centers, natural history museums, planetariums, and science centers.

The Agency takes a broad view of “arts, humanities, and sciences” and includes disciplines like fashion, competitive dance, magic shows, circus arts, balloon twisters, reenactments, sand art and ice sculptures and robotics. Public art, topiary or landscape art, and interior design may also be eligible types of arts. Other types of arts or recreational activities such as martial arts, culinary arts, boating, gymnastics, etc. may be considered arts, humanities, and sciences if they’re tied into a cultural context. The definition of arts, humanities, and sciences are not exclusive to these examples.

Name: Knight Cities Challenge
Description: The Knight Foundation is launching the Knight Cities Challenge, a $5 million open call for creative project ideas across its 26 communities. Applications open April 1, 2026 and close April 30, 2026, with grants of up to $200,000 available for projects focused on local news, economic opportunity, or arts and culture. Projects must be completable within one year, and both nonprofits and individuals are eligible to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Your project must focus on at least one of Knight’s three investment areas: strengthening local news and information, creating pathways for economic opportunity or cultivating connection through arts, culture and the places that bring people together. See here for more information about these categories.
Your project must take place in one or more of the 26 Knight communities:

Aberdeen, SD
Akron, OH
Biloxi, MS

Charlotte, NC
Columbia, SC
Columbus, GA
Detroit, MI
Duluth, MN
Fort Wayne, IN
Gary, IN

Myrtle Beach, SC
Palm Beach County, FL

San Jose, CA
St. Paul, MN
State College, PA
Tallahassee, FL
Wichita, KS

Our Investment Focus Areas
Knight Foundation works to ignite in every person the power to shape thriving communities. We invest to strengthen people’s agency through a sustainable ecosystem of quality information and evidence; to foster community resilience by expanding economic mobility; and to cultivate connection by revitalizing cultural vibrancy, supporting free expression and building common ground.

These strategic focus areas guide our program strategies and often intersect across and within our grants. They are grounded in the values expressed in the First Amendment, which we believe are essential to vital, engaged communities.


1. Information Ecosystem
Strengthening information ecosystems by expanding access to reliable information, advancing sustainable business models for journalism, and investing in research and field-building efforts that inform policy and public debate. We look for investments that boost agency and understanding— whether at the local level, across media systems, or within broader policy and societal contexts.

2. Economic Mobility
Expanding local economic opportunity by supporting entrepreneurs, tapping into community economic potential, and advancing climate solutions that result in economic benefits for residents. We look for projects that build community resilience, help residents gain stability, and give people more ways to shape the future of their neighborhoods.

3. Cultural Vibrancy
Advancing local arts and culture, bolstering civic institutions as hubs for free expression, and enhancing shared places that bring people together. We look for projects that cultivate connection and shared purpose, reflect local identity, and foster the exchange of ideas.

Name: CENTRO 2026-2027 Rooted + Relational Community Micro-Grant
Description: The Center for Puerto Rican Studies (CENTRO) at Hunter College is offering up to 12 micro-grants of $5,000 each for community-based individuals, groups, and organizations — excluding anyone affiliated with a college or university — working on artistic, cultural, activist, or agricultural projects connected to Puerto Rican communities in Puerto Rico, the U.S., or its territories. The 2026-2027 theme is "Black Cuerpas: Race, Body Politics & Culture," focusing on how race, Blackness, gender, and body politics shape Boricua lives and histories. The application deadline is April 30, 2026 at 11:59pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Micro-Grant Eligibility Requirements: 

Applicants must be community-based individuals, groups, or organizations engaged in artistic, community-driven, agricultural, activist, or cultural projects.

Applicants must be 18 years of age or older.
Past Rooted & Relational Grant Recipients are not eligible.

Name: Pasadena Women's Business Center: Back in Business- LA Wildfire Relief Grant Application
Description: The Pasadena Women's Business Center's "Back In Business" LA Wildfire Relief Grant offers awards of $10,000–$20,000 plus one-on-one business advising through the end of 2026 to women-owned small businesses impacted by the Southern California wildfires. Name: San Diego Foundation Growing Green Spaces 2026 Grant Program
Description: The San Diego Foundation's Growing Green Spaces 2026 Grant Program offers implementation grants of $15,000 to $40,000 to 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving San Diego County for shovel-ready green space projects such as tree planting, community gardens, rain gardens, and native plant restoration that deliver measurable climate and community health benefits. The program prioritizes neighborhoods experiencing climate and environmental challenges, and all projects must be completed within 12 months of the grant award. The application deadline is April 30, 2026 at 5:00pm PST.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:

1. Applications must be led by a nonprofit with 501(c)(3) public charity status or an equivalent tax-exempt

Name: Showcase Atlanta Community Engagement Grant
Description: Showcase Atlanta's Community Engagement Grant offers Atlanta-based community organizations $3,000 to $4,000 in activation funding plus a professional outdoor LED screen and sound system to host free, public FIFA World Cup watch party events across the city during June–July 2026. Up to 8 grants will be awarded to eligible organizations including neighborhood associations, nonprofits, faith communities, and civic groups, with priority given to applicants in designated underserved city zones. The application deadline is April 30, 2026 at 11:59pm, with awardees announced May 10, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who Can Apply
This grant is open to community-based organizations, neighborhood associations, business associations, Neighborhood Planning Units (NPUs), nonprofits, faith communities, and civic groups based in the City of Atlanta.

To be eligible, your organization must:

· Be a registered community-based organization, neighborhood association, NPU, nonprofit, faith community, business association or civic group

· Hold a valid City of Atlanta business license or be registered with the Georgia Secretary of State

· Be based within the City of Atlanta

· Be able to receive payment via invoice (no individual awardees)

· Have a confirmed event lead and point of contact

· Have a venue confirmed or in progress at time of application

· Plan a free, public event during the FIFA World Cup (June–July 2026)

· Include at least one Atlanta-based small business or vendor at your event

Not eligible: Individual promoters, event production companies or businesses applying without a community organization partner.

Grant Details
Activation grants range from $3,000 to $4,000 based on expected attendance and zone priority.

Events may be 1 to 3 days in length and must screen at least one FIFA World Cup match. Events must be free and open to the public — no admission fee, no purchase required to attend.

Up to 8 grants will be awarded. At least one grant will be awarded per city zone if a qualified application is received.

Name: The Provident Bank Foundation 2026 Empowerment Grant
Description: The Provident Bank Foundation's 2026 Empowerment Grant provides two years of flexible funding to nonprofits serving communities near Provident Bank branches in New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania, across three priority areas: education, human services, and workforce development. Grant amounts range from $5,000–$10,000 per year for organizations with budgets of $50,000–$1 million, and $10,000–$25,000 per year for those with budgets of $1 million–$15 million. The application window is April 1–April 30, 2026, with award notifications on or around July 31, 2026 and the grant term running August 1, 2026–July 31, 2028.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Provident Bank Foundation invests in marginalized communities within Provident Bank’s branch
network by collaborating with nonprofit organizations that align with the values we care about. Together,
we empower individuals on their paths to economic self-sufficiency by addressing the multifaceted issues
that perpetuate the cycle of poverty.

The Empowerment Grant program provides two years of flexible funding support for programs, projects, or

Organizations must meet a specific set of eligibility criteria to apply for an Empowerment Grant based on the size of

Empowerment Grants will be awarded in the range of $5,000-$10,000 per year for two years for organizations with
operating budgets between $50,000-$1 million per year, and in the range of $10,000-$25,000 per year for two years
for organizations with operating budgets between $1 million-$15 million per year.

Name: Mothers as Entrepreneurs Grant
Description: The Mothers as Entrepreneurs Grant supports mothers and primary maternal caregivers in the U.S. who are actively leading formally registered businesses or organizations — for-profit or nonprofit — that contribute positively to their communities through family support, health, education, or mission-driven impact. Name: MFF Venture Together Competition
Description: The Michigan Founders Fund Venture Together Competition is a pitch competition where teams of 4-5 Michigan-based startup founders collaborate to pitch how they will support each other's growth while benefiting people, place, or the planet. Eligible applicants must be working full-time on an incorporated Michigan startup with at least a proof of concept, committed to in-state growth, and must not have raised more than $2 million in equity funding. The initial individual application deadline is April 30, 2026 at 11:59pm ET, with finalists pitching on stage at Michigan Tech Week.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
MFF Venture Together Competition Application 2026
What Is It?

Michigan Founders Fund (MFF) Venture Together is a pitch competition where high-growth founders join together to showcase how they'll build exceptional companies alongside a commitment to people, places, or the planet in Michigan. The goal is to partner with other founders to enact a plan that benefits all of your businesses as well as the community.

How It Works

There are three steps to win. One: apply individually and find eligible teammates. Two: submit a team statement to determine finalists. Three: finalists will pitch on stage at MTW in front of judges.

In a 5-minute pitch, your team must explain how you will leverage each company’s unique attributes to support one another in achieving mutual success and growth. Your pitch must also include at least two of the following category considerations:
People: How will your team contribute to the well-being and prosperity of people either inside of your companies or across your community?
Place: How will your businesses grow in-state, support local opportunities, and/or contribute to a thriving community? ‍
Planet: How will your team help reduce your environmental footprint, innovate with sustainable practices, and/or contribute to the health of our planet?
Eligibility Requirements

Each founder must be working on their startup full-time.
Each company must be incorporated (or LLC) with headquarters in Michigan.
Must be building a high-growth startup with at least a proof of concept.
Must be committed to growing their business/team in-state (does not exclude growing out of state as well).
Companies who have already raised $2 million or more in equity funding are not eligible.
Past winners (recipients of prize funding) of this competition are not eligible.
Each TEAM must include exactly 4 or 5 founders that fit all the categories above. (You can apply individually and be matched with teammates later).

Initial Application Deadline: April 30, 2026 - 11:59pm ET

Name: Arizona Community Foundation Grants
Description: The Arizona Community Foundation / Arizona Public Service grant supports qualified nonprofit organizations that have operated for at least three years and serve residents in Arizona’s West Valley. Funding is intended to help nonprofits address community needs and support local growth within the defined service area, bounded roughly by Bell Road, 459th Avenue, Estrella/Gillespie Dam, and 19th Avenue.

Name: Jacksonville Public Service Grant Program
Description: The Public Service Grant Program (PSG) offers City funding to nonprofits serving “Most Vulnerable Persons and/or Needs,” such as elderly, low-income residents, or people with urgent safety, medical, social, or housing needs, with categories set annually by the PSG Council. To apply, organizations must attend a mandatory May training workshop to receive a certificate, use the courtesy review period, and then submit their application.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Public Service Grants are available to nonprofits that serve categories of Most Vulnerable Persons (MVP) and/or Needs. Most Vulnerable Persons and/or Needs are groups of citizens or the common needs and traits requiring services from Requesting Agencies, whose needs have justified priority consideration over other deserving populations or groups in competition for City funding. The PSG Council assesses the needs of the community and recommends the categories of Most Vulnerable Persons and/or Needs for the upcoming fiscal year.

Name: 2026 Halstead Grant
Description: The Halstead Grant is an annual award for emerging silver jewelry artists, designed to help jewelry entrepreneurs sharpen their business strategy. The grand prize includes a $7,500 cash grant (plus additional benefits).
