Featured Grant term is 24 months (2 years).
Featured Grant size is $35,000 to $50,000 paid over a two-year period.
Only organizations with budgets of $100,000 and above may apply.
Only organizations with operating budgets between $100,000 and $1 million can apply for capacity building grants. These grants can span all operational aspects (e.g., technology, strategic planning, monitoring and evaluation, staff training), with restrictions that apply to all featured grants.
Organizations may receive no more than one Featured Grant per four-year period.

Name: American Craft Made Baltimore
Description: American Craft Made Baltimore is the largest juried craft fair on the East Coast, now in its 50th year, taking place February 19–21, 2027 at the Baltimore Convention Center with 380+ exhibitors and 10,000+ attendees. Applications are open through June 5, 2026, with a $45 application fee (50% discount for ACC members), and booth fees ranging from $850 for a 10x5 space to $2,700 for a 10x20 space, with subsidized $400 booths available for Early Career Artists. The fair is open to U.S.-based artists 18 and older working in handmade craft mediums including ceramics, jewelry, glass, fiber, wood, metal, and more.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
General information.
American Craft Made Baltimore is the largest juried craft fair on the East Coast of the United States (see last year’s fair), with more than 380 artists presenting their work alongside activities, demonstrations, talks, and hands-on experiences. Now in its 50th year, this immersive and interactive annual event held in the Baltimore Convention Center attracts an audience of more than 10,000 craft enthusiasts.

Participation is open to artists and makers from across the country who create work that reflects the diversity of contemporary craft. Apply now to participate in this opportunity to share your story and sell your work to ACC’s audience of craft enthusiasts and supporters.

American Craft Made is produced by the American Craft Council, one of the country’s leading non-profit organizations committed to supporting craft and its makers. ACC is a member-based nonprofit located in Minneapolis, MN. In addition to hosting large-scale craft fairs like American Craft Made, ACC offers ongoing educational programs and events for artists and makers.

Event dates:
February 19–21, 2027

Location:
Baltimore Convention Center

Hours:
10 a.m.–6 p.m. Friday & Saturday / 11 a.m.–5 p.m. Sunday
The box office opens one hour prior to the start of the fair each day.

Event Size:
380+ exhibitors
10,000+ attendees

Name: USDA Local Agriculture Market Program
Description: The USDA's Local Agriculture Market Program (LAMP) is an umbrella grant program supporting the development and expansion of local and regional food markets, direct producer-to-consumer marketing, and value-added agricultural products. LAMP encompasses four sub-programs: the Farmers Market Promotion Program (FMPP), Local Food Promotion Program (LFPP), Regional Food System Partnerships Program (RFSP), and Value-Added Producer Grants (VAPG) — interested applicants should visit each sub-program's individual page on ams.usda.gov for current funding opportunities and deadlines.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
All applicants must be domestic entities owned, operated, and located within the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, American Samoa, Guam, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or the U.S. Virgin Islands to be considered eligible. Entities that are eligible to apply include:

Agricultural businesses and cooperatives.
Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) networks and associations.
Food councils.
Economic development corporations.
Local governments.
Nonprofit and public benefit corporations.
Producer networks or associations.
Regional farmers’ market authorities.
Tribal governments.

Name: USDA Local Food Promotion Program
Description: The USDA Local Food Promotion Program provides grants for projects that support local and regional food businesses that process, distribute, aggregate, or store locally produced food products. The FY26 application period is open through June 5, 2026, with funding ranging from $25,000 to $500,000 depending on project type. Eligible applicants include domestic agricultural businesses, cooperatives, CSAs, food councils, local governments, nonprofits, producer networks, regional farmers’ market authorities, and Tribal governments, with a required 25% cost share.

Name: The Chicago Media & Entertainment Tech Summit Pitch Competition
Description: The CMET Summit pitch competition selects five elite finalists from Chicago's creative technology sector, with finalists required to have at least one year of operation and recorded operating income. Winners receive $50K+ in total awards including cash prizes, equity investment opportunities, hardware and software packages, 2112 memberships, professional pitch videos, and one finalist earns a spot to pitch at the Music Tectonics Conference in Santa Monica. An additional 15–20 entrepreneurs will be spotlighted throughout the event.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: An elite pitch competition spotlighting Chicago's most compelling creative technology companies, with direct pathways to capital and global exposure. Finalists must have a minimum of one year of operation and recorded operating income.

Name: LA Community Council District 9 Community Grant
Description: The CD9 Community Grant, established by Los Angeles City Councilmember Curren Price, is offering a second round of funding with approximately $3 million available in grants ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 for organizations serving Council District 9. Priority is given to CD9-based nonprofits, faith-based organizations, schools, and Neighborhood Councils bringing innovative projects and programming to the area. The application deadline is June 7, 2026 at 11:59pm.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Priority is given to CD9-based nonprofits, faith-based organizations, schools, and Neighborhood Councils bringing innovative projects and programming to the area.

Name: The Embark Program by REI Co-op Path Ahead Ventures
Description: REI Co-op's Embark program, developed with Founded Outdoors, is a free virtual 3-month accelerator for early-stage entrepreneurs from Black, Indigenous, Latina/o/x, and AAPI communities building outdoor industry businesses, with founders receiving a $5,000 grant upon completion. Eligible applicants must have a business idea at the design or prototype stage (or have started within the last year with less than $20K in revenue), be U.S.-based and at least 18 years old, and be building a product, service, or experience in the outdoor space. Applications open May 4, 2026 and close June 7, 2026, with the program running September 8–November 19, 2026, including an in-person kickoff at REI headquarters September 17-19.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Check out our application criteria:

You have a business idea at the design or prototype stage and are serious about turning it into a company in the next six months OR you've started your company in the last year but haven't yet done manufacturing and have made less than <$20k revenue.
You are building a product, service, or experience that inspires and equips people in their lives outside including gear, apparel, furniture, mobile app, website, e-commerce, retail, outdoor experience, service, food and beverage, skincare, etc.
You identify as a person of color from the Black, Indigenous, Latina/o/x, Asian American and Pacific Islander communities.
You are based in the United States (US Citizenship is not required) and you are at least 18 years old.

Name: Bronze Valley Investment Accelerator 2026
Description: The Bronze Valley Investment Accelerator, powered by gener8tor, invests $100,000 in exchange for 5% equity via SAFE in up to five high-growth startups per cohort across two programs — one in Alabama and one in Delaware — with each cohort participating in a 12-week mentorship-driven accelerator with 60+ mentor introductions and 30+ investor introductions. The program is industry-agnostic and open to U.S.-based early-stage startups with an MVP and early traction, though founders must relocate full-time to either Birmingham, Alabama or Wilmington, Delaware for the duration. The Alabama Summer 2026 cohort has an application deadline of June 7, 2026, with the program running September 10–December 4, 2026, while the Delaware program has rolling applications with dates TBD.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Bronze Valley Investment Accelerator invests in up to five high-growth startups per cohort, regardless of industry or business model.

Name: TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200
Description: TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 is a global startup competition at Disrupt that showcases 200 early-stage companies, offering major exposure, investor access, perks like free exhibit space and networking, and a chance to win a $100,000 equity-free prize; past alumni include companies like Dropbox and Discord. For 2026, nominations are now open (after 2025 applications closed), and eligible startups—those with a working MVP and no Series A—must first be nominated, then complete a full application by May 27, 2026 to be considered.

Name: SBA Patriot Pitch Competition
Description: SBA’s Freedom 250 initiative celebrates America’s 250th anniversary by spotlighting small businesses through national programs like the Patriot Pitch Competition and a 50-stop Main Street Tour. The Patriot Pitch Competition invites eligible U.S. small businesses to submit a pitch by June 10, 2026, for a chance to compete in Washington, D.C. for a share of a $1 million prize pool. Eligible businesses must be at least 3 years old, generate at least $100,000 in annual revenue, be U.S.-based and 100% U.S.-owned, be in good standing, drive innovation, and have used an SBA capital product such as a 7(a) loan, 504 loan, Microloan Intermediary loan, SBIR/STTR funding, or SBIC financing.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The competition is open to:

U.S. citizens who are at least 18 years of age at the time of submission (or teams of such individuals)
Private entities or teams that meet SBA’s definition of a small business
Individuals submitting on behalf of corporations, nonprofits, or other organizations or groups of individuals (such as an academic class or other team) must meet the eligibility requirements for individual contestants. 
An individual cannot belong to more than one team submitting an entry in this competition.  
Your business must:

Have a minimum of 3 years in business operation
Have a gross revenue production of at least $100,000 annually
Have benefited from one or more of the following SBA capital products:
7(a) loans (including Paycheck Protection Program loans) 
504 loans 
Microloan Intermediary loans 
SBIR / STTR funded entities 
SBIC financed small business concerns 
Note: participants who received COVID-19 EIDL loans or SBA Disaster loans are not eligible based on those loans but may be eligible if they received the capital products listed above. 
Be current and in good standing on any federal obligations. Businesses that have, at any time, defaulted on a federal loan or federally-guaranteed financing that has resulted in the federal government or any of its agencies or departments sustaining a loss in any of its programs and businesses owned or controlled a person who previously owned, operated, or controlled a business which defaulted on a federal loan or guaranteed financing and caused the federal government or any of its agencies or departments to sustain a loss in any of its programs are ineligible to apply for the competition.  For purposes of the competition, a compromise agreement as described at 31 C.F.R. 3711 shall also be considered a loss. 
Be headquartered and operated in the United States and/or its territories 
Be 100% owned by U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents 
Actively drive innovation in your sector, leveraging new technologies or strategies to modernize operations or strengthen your competitive edge 
Finalists must be available to travel for the national pitch competition, which will occur on one day between September 8th – 18th (to be finalized at a later time), at their own expense. 

Eligible participants must agree to assume risks of personal injury/property damage arising from their participation in the competition and waive such claims against the government or competition judges to enter the competition.

Name: Jobber Grants
Description: Jobber Grants is awarding nine grants totaling $250,000 to blue collar home service businesses in the U.S. and Canada, with individual awards ranging from $10,000 to $100,000 that can be used freely to support business growth, equipment, staffing, or operations. All finalists will be invited to an all-expenses-paid in-person retreat featuring time with Shark Tank's Daymond John, who is partnering with Jobber to help select recipients. Phase 1 applications are open through June 11, 2026, with grant recipients announced in August 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is eligible for Jobber Grants?
Any blue collar business owner or aspiring business owner aged 18 or older residing in the U.S. and Canada, excluding Québec.

What is a blue collar business?
A blue collar business, also referred to as a home service business, provides a one time or recurring install, repair, maintenance, or mobile services to clients at residential or commercial properties.

Examples include landscaping, residential and commercial cleaning, contracting, painting, HVAC, plumbing, pool maintenance, mobile car detailing, etc.

Blue collar businesses do not include home-based or retail businesses that primarily provide or sell goods and services online, from home, or from brick-and-mortar locations. These types of businesses are not eligible for Jobber Grants.

Name: Louisiana Project Grants

The program is administered jointly by the Louisiana Division of the Arts and the Arts Council of Greater Baton Rouge, and funded activities must take place between October 1, 2026 and September 30, 2027.

organization as a fiscal agent. The project must directly benefit the community and include community participation. The fiscal agent assumes legal and financial responsibility for theproject (more on fiscal agents below).

Name: Wayne F. Placek Grant
Description: The American Psychological Foundation's Wayne F. Placek Grant awards two grants of up to $15,000 each to support research that increases public understanding of homosexuality and sexual orientation and reduces stress experienced by LGBTQIA+ individuals. One of the two grants — the Wayne F. Placek Grant in Memorial of John Peterson — is specifically focused on research concerning Black LGBTQIA+ individuals and communities, conducted by scholars of color. Eligible applicants include doctoral-level researchers and graduate students affiliated with educational institutions or 501(c)(3) nonprofit research organizations, with the application deadline of June 12, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Wayne F. Placek Grant encourages research to increase the general public’s understanding of homosexuality and sexual orientation, and to alleviate the stress that LGBTQIA+ individuals experience in this and future civilizations. Since 1995, the Placek Fund has granted more than $1 million.

The Wayne F. Placek Grant encourages research that addresses the following topics:

heterosexuals’ attitudes and behaviors toward LGBTQIA+ people, including prejudice, discrimination, and violence
family and workplace issues relevant to LGBTQIA+people
special concerns of sectors of the LGBTQIA+ population that have historically been underrepresented in scientific research
issues concerning Black LGBTQIA+ individuals and communities
APF will give away two Wayne F. Placek Grants in 2025. One of these grants, the Wayne F. Placek Grant in Memorial of John Peterson, will be focused on psychological research into issues concerning Black LGBTQIA+ individuals and communities, that is conducted by scholars of color.

Wayne F. Placek was initially a research subject of Evelyn Hooker, a groundbreaking psychologist whose 1950s research laid the foundation for the view that homosexuality was not a form of psychopathology. Ultimately, Hooker’s research led to the removal of homosexuality as a clinical diagnosis. Placek, who identified as a gay man, was a participant in Hooker’s studies. Placek was so moved by Hooker’s work that he left his entire estate to her. He instructed that the money be used to advance the general public’s understanding of LGBTQIA+ individuals and reduce the stress and adversity experienced by members of the LGBTQIA+ community. Today, the Wayne F. Placek Grant has funded over $1 million in LGBTQIA+ research.

Eligibility
APF encourages applicants from diverse backgrounds with respect to age, race, color, religion, creed, nationality, ability, sexual orientation, gender, and geography.

Applicants must be either a doctoral-level researcher or graduate student affiliated with an educational institution or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research organization.

Graduate students and early career researchers are encouraged to apply.

Name: Women in Innovation Awards 2026
Description: The Women in Innovation Awards 2026 recognizes women and organizations making an impact through innovation across six award categories: Organization B2B, Organization B2C, the Luminary Award (20+ year career legacy), Rising Star (first 10 years of career), Movers & Makers (mid-to-senior level innovators), and the Startup Award (early-stage startups with a woman on the founding team that have raised less than $5 million). Nominations are open for self-nomination or nominating others, with the extended submission deadline of June 20, 2026. The culminating awards ceremony will be held in New York City in November 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
How It Works
Decide which awards you’d like to apply for. You can do as many as you’d like, across as many categories as you choose. Nominate someone you know, or yourself! Don’t forget you can be your own champion! 

Register with your information—even if you are nominating a friend or colleague. 

We’re excited to offer early bird pricing—the costs help to support the WIN community. The earlier you apply, the better the rate!

You will not be prompted to pay until you are ready to SUBMIT your nomination.

We’ll ask you to share information on the nominee—it should take no more than 15 minutes. You can save your application to come back to at any time. Our judges are eager to know about your nominee's key achievements, what makes them standout leaders, and all the ways they are making a difference through the lens of innovation.

To learn more about Award Categories, review all Application Questions, and see our FAQ, click here!

Complete your application and finish the checkout process. Once our extended submission period wraps on June 20th, our incredible panel of judges will evaluate and be in touch.

The Women in Innovation Awards 2026 Categories

The Organization [B2B] Award

The Organization [B2B] Award celebrates companies that embrace forward-thinking solutions, systems, and approaches that shift categories and shape society for the better. Nominees demonstrate a defined commitment to innovation, a track record of bold initiatives, and tangible impact across their industry and ecosystem.

Nominees should be organizations of any size that have integrated innovation into their core business practices and demonstrated a commitment to pushing boundaries for the greater good. 

Organizations must provide:

Case Studies: Examples of projects, initiatives, or collaborations that showcase their approach to innovation.
Process & Culture: Insight into how they foster innovation internally—whether through dedicated teams, cross-functional collaboration, or unique methodologies.
Impact Evidence: Tangible results demonstrating how their innovation efforts have driven meaningful change, whether in their industry, community, or beyond.
The Organizations [B2B] Award will honor three finalists and one winner.

The Organization [B2C] Award

The Organizations B2C Award celebrates consumer and community-facing companies or nonprofits bringing novel offerings to market with meaningful impact on the people they serve. Nominees demonstrate a commitment to genuine innovation, evidence of category impact, and a culture that supports pushing boundaries.

Nominees should be organizations of any size that have integrated innovation into their core business practices and demonstrated a commitment to pushing boundaries for the greater good. 

Organizations must provide:

Case Studies: Examples of projects, initiatives, or collaborations that showcase their approach to innovation.
Process & Culture: Insight into how they foster innovation internally—whether through dedicated teams, cross-functional collaboration, or unique methodologies.
Impact Evidence: Tangible results demonstrating how their innovation efforts have driven meaningful change, whether in their industry, community, or beyond.
The Organizations [B2C] Award will honor three finalists and one winner.

The Luminary Award 

The Luminary Award honors an innovator whose career of 20 or more years of achievement has transformed their industry, challenged the status quo, and opened doors for the leaders who came after them. Nominees demonstrate a legacy of impact, a history of bold thinking, and a body of work that has meaningfully shaped their field and the women within it.

Nominees should be established leaders in the later stages of their career—typically with 20+ years of experience—who have:

Led transformative initiatives and shaped long-term industry progress.
Challenged the status quo and championed creativity, equity, and bold thinking.
Mentored and uplifted others, playing an active role in developing the next generation of leaders.
Built a legacy of impact, with tangible contributions that have influenced their field, community, or broader society over time.
Earned a reputation as a role model through both their work and their leadership values.
The Luminary Award will honor three finalists and one winner.

The Rising Star Award 

The Rising Star Award recognizes exceptional women in the first decade of their careers who are already shaping the future of their industries through innovation, leadership, and impact. Nominees demonstrate future-forward thinking, early quantifiable impact, and a track record of taking initiative and influencing others.

To be eligible, nominees must:

Be in the early stages of their career (typically within the first 10 years of professional experience). This award is not intended for senior leaders, executives, or C-suite professionals.
Demonstrate future-forward thinking, with a clear example of an innovative idea, a solution, or an approach they have introduced.
Shows initial quantifiable impact through contributions that have driven positive change or advancements in their field.
Exhibit leadership potential, with a track record of taking initiative, influencing others, and positioning themselves as a future industry leader.
The Rising Star Award will honor three finalists and one winner.

The Movers & Makers Award

The Movers & Makers Award honors women who are disrupting and reimagining their specific categories through bold, tangible innovation, creativity, and leadership. Nominees demonstrate a proven track record of meaningful change, a clear point of view on what their industry could become, and measurable impact that others in their field can point to.

Nominees should be mid-career or senior-level professionals with a proven track record of creating meaningful change. We’re looking for:

Innovation: You’ve developed or significantly improved a product, service, process, or initiative that addresses a real-world challenge.
Impact: Your work has resulted in clear, measurable benefits to your community, industry, or society—locally or globally.
Leadership: You’ve played a key role in bringing your ideas to life, mobilizing others, and pushing boundaries.
Community Engagement: You are actively connected to the community or ecosystem your work serves, fostering collaboration and inclusion.
The Movers and Makers Award will honor ten finalists.

The Startup Award

The Startup Award recognizes early-stage startups whose products or services are pushing the boundaries of innovation in their industry. Nominees demonstrate a clear value proposition, a disruptive approach to their category, and a woman on the founding team. Startups must have raised less than $5M and have been in business for less than five years. If chosen as a finalist applicant is ideally available to pitch in-person in NYC as part of our Demo Day program.

Innovation Sub-Categories include the following industries:
Realestate & Proptech 
Healthcare & Biotech
Finance & Fintech
Emerging Tech (AI/Meta/Web3)
Sustainability & Climate Tech 
Reproductive health & Femtech 
Social Innovation 
Retail & Commerce 
Nominees must be early-stage startups that have raised less than $5 million USD in funding and have been in business for less than 5 years. 
They must have a product or service that is disrupting their industry and driving innovation forward. 
They must also have a woman on the founding team.

The Startup Award will honor five finalists and one winner.

Name: Michigan Virtual Edtech Catalyst
Description: Michigan Virtual's EdTech Catalyst Pitch Contest awards cash prizes to Michigan-based education technology innovators, with first place receiving $10,000, second place $6,000, third place $4,000, and two additional finalists each receiving $1,000, plus startup legal consultation for the top three. Parents of school-aged children (PreK–12)

Name: USBC 360°
Description: USBC 360° is a selective 12-week growth accelerator for product-based CPG founders in categories like food, beauty, wellness, apparel, accessories, and gifts. The program helps businesses strengthen margins, clarify unit economics, build systems, and choose growth channels intentionally, with hands-on mentorship and an 18–24 month operations and growth plan. Top performers may compete for a share of $100,000 in non-dilutive growth capital.

Consumer packaged goods (CPG) product companies
Based in the United States
Actively selling in at least one channel (DTC, retail, wholesale, etc.)
Generating at least $100K in revenue in the past 12 months
In business and selling products for at least 12 months
Able to participate August–October, including the two required 3-day in-person intensives in Washington, D.C. (August and October)
Currently compliant with required business licenses, permits, and tax filings

Name: NJ Department of Health Specific Population Community Grant
Description: The New Jersey Department of Health's Office of Minority and Multicultural Health is offering one Specific Population Community Grant of up to $200,000 per year for up to four years (July 2026–June 2030) to a single community-based or faith-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization serving the Black and African American population in New Jersey. The grantee will provide health navigation services, conduct community outreach and education, develop a community needs assessment, and convene stakeholders to address health disparities and social determinants of health. A Letter of Interest must be submitted by May 18, 2026, with the full application due June 12, 2026 at 5pm EDT via the SAGE grants system.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
ELIGIBILITY
Nonprofit organizations with 501 (c)(3) IRS status:
Community-based organizations
Faith-based organizations

Name: Global Citizen Waislitz Awards
Description: The Global Citizen Waislitz Awards offer three prizes of $100,000 each (totaling $300,000) to individuals doing innovative work to end extreme poverty — including a grand prize judged on all five criteria, a Disruptor Award for exceptional innovation, and a Global Citizens' Choice Award determined by public voting. Applicants must have at least 1-2 years of demonstrated impact and are evaluated on global citizenship, proof of concept, disruption, scalability, and adaptability. Applications are open through June 14, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Entrants aged eighteen (18) years of age or older from anywhere in the world are eligible to apply for the awards.

Name: Montgomery Thriving Small Business Grant Program
Description: The Montgomery Thriving Small Business Grant Program, funded through ARPA, is a new grant program launching in May 2026 to support small businesses in the City of Montgomery and Montgomery County, Alabama with funding to expand operations, stabilize, and grow. Eligible businesses must have 1–50 employees, generate less than $5 million in annual revenue, operate as a for-profit business in good standing within the area, and demonstrate economic hardship or need. The application period runs May 11–June 15, 2026, with grant amounts not yet specified — business owners can sign up for updates and access the full program details at https://bit.ly/mtsbg starting May 4, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Exciting New Grant Program to Support Montgomery’s Small Businesses

Name: Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
Description: The Sundance Institute Documentary Fund is a global funding opportunity for independent filmmakers creating feature-length documentary films of 52 minutes or longer, supporting projects from development through release. The fund prioritizes creative, culturally relevant nonfiction projects with strong artistic vision, social impact potential, and filmmaker-held creative and editorial control, with a preference for budgets under $1.2 million excluding distribution and impact costs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Sundance Institute Documentary Fund seeks to support independent voices through an equitable and inclusive selection process. Projects are eligible for consideration based on the following criteria:

Format: We support feature-length documentary films (52 minutes and longer).
Creative Independence: To ensure the artist’s vision remains central, creative and editorial control must be held by the project’s key creative team.
Project Stage: We welcome projects in development, production, or post-production. Applicants should have confirmed participants and be prepared to articulate the project’s story or structure, and central driving questions. We cannot provide support for early story research or projects that have reached picture lock. We recommend applying at least eight months before your anticipated picture lock to align with our review timeline.
Thematic and Artistic Scope: We embrace a wide range of aesthetic and storytelling traditions from across the globe and encourage experimentation in form. Our fund is not restricted to specific themes or issues. We remain committed to projects that elevate and advance cultural dialogue, expand the form through creativity and innovation, and have the potential to generate social impact around some of the most compelling issues of our time. We do not fund NGO, advocacy, or educational films, or branded content. We also typically do not fund historical or biographical films unless they show clear contemporary relevance or innovation in form.
Budget: We prioritize budgets under $1.2 million USD excluding distribution and impact expenses. Prior funding or a fiscal sponsor is not required.

Name: Cartier Women's Initiative
Description: The Cartier Women’s Initiative is a global annual program (founded in 2006) that supports women-led, women-owned impact businesses across any country and sector that are driving social and/or environmental change. For the 2027 edition, applications run April 16–June 16, 2026, and selected regional fellows receive a mix of grant funding (up to $100K) plus a fellowship offering leadership training, mentorship, and international visibility to help scale their impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Regional Awards of the Cartier Women’s Initiative are looking for women-owned and women-led impact-driven businesses. Entrepreneurs across all sectors and geographies are encouraged to apply. Applicants with disabilities are encouraged to apply, and every effort will be made to include them appropriately.

To be considered for this award, the applicant and the applicant’s business must meet the following eligibility criteria:

Positive impact: The business should demonstrate that it has realized positive impact in its industry and that it has the potential to realize even more impact as it scales. It should contribute to at least one of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The SDGs are a collection of 17 global goals set by the United Nations for the year 2030 as a universal call to tackle a range of social, economic and environmental challenges.

For-profit: The business should be designed to generate sufficient revenue to support its operations and return some level of profit to its owners. Non-profit enterprises are not eligible. That said, the business does not have to be profitable at the time of application.

Stage: The business should have generated annual revenue between $50,000 USD and $5 million USD in its last closed fiscal year as of the date of application and should employ between 5 and 250 team members (i.e. full-time employees, part-time employees, seasonal workers, or contractors).

Fundraising: The business should not have raised more than $2 million USD in dilutive or potentially dilutive funding (i.e. equity, quasi-equity like SAFE or Convertible Notes) as of the date of application. Dilutive funding is any kind of funding that consists of a transfer of the ownership of your company at the time of the funding or in the future under specified terms. Businesses that have not raised any external funding are also encouraged to apply.

Leadership: The applicant must be a woman and fill one of the main leadership positions, for example as CEO, COO, CTO, General Manager, or Managing Director of the business.

Independent entity: The business entity and its finances must be independent from the founder(s). Moreover, it must be an original creation, wholly conceived of by the team; a completely new concept, meaning it cannot be a spin-off or franchise of an existing concept.

Ownership: The business must be incorporated and majority owned by its founders and team members at the time of application. The applicant must be part of the founding team and own a share greater or equal to that of each of her co-founder(s). 

Legal entry age: The applicant must be at least 18 years of age on the day of the application deadline (June 16, 2026).

English proficiency: A good command of the English language is required. We require the Common European Framework of Reference Level B2 or above. This level requires an understanding of the main ideas of complex text, technical discussion in business and your field of specialization, and an ability to interact with fluency and spontaneity with native speakers. English proficiency is important because this is the common language for the Cartier Women's Initiative team, its partners, the jury members and the overall community. Being proficient will allow the fellow to fully participate in the community and in the fellowship.

Name: Farm-To-Neighbor Microgrant
Description: The New Connecticut Farmers Alliance is offering up to $500 in microgrants for Connecticut for-profit farms to host a small community event — a dinner, harvest day, tasting, class, or similar gathering — that connects farmers with their local neighbors. Applicants must provide a 50% match (cash or in-kind, but not their own labor or farm products), and priority is given to new, beginning, and urban farmers. Applications are open May 19 – June 16, 2026, events must be held by March 31, 2027, and receipts are due May 1, 2027. Questions can be directed to Melissa at nctfacomms@gmail.com (English) or Ella Kennen at newctfarmers@gmail.com (Spanish).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Farm-to-Neighbor Microgrant is open to any for-profit farm in Connecticut. We will give priority consideration to applications from new/beginning farmers and urban farmers.

Name: USDA Beginning Farmer and Rancher Development Program
Description: The USDA-NIFA Beginning Farmer and Rancher Development Program (BFRDP) provides competitive grants to support education, outreach, training, and technical assistance that helps beginning farmers and ranchers in the U.S. and its territories start, build, and manage successful farm, ranch, or nonindustrial private forest operations. For FY 2026, the program has approximately $44.4 million available, with individual awards generally ranging from $49,999 to $750,000 depending on grant type. Applications are due June 16, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, and eligible applicants must apply as collaborative state, tribal, local, or regional partnerships; a 25% nonfederal match is required unless waived or reduced.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Other junior and four-year colleges or universities or foundations maintained by a college or university.
State Cooperative Extension Services
Federal, State, Municipal or Tribal agencies
Community-Based Organizations (CBOs)
Nongovernmental Organizations (NGOs)
Private For-Profit Organizations

The applicant must be a collaborative state, tribal, local, or regionally based network or partnership of qualified public and/or private entities.

Name: Visionaries Pitch Competition
Description: The Visionaries Pitch Competition offers tens of thousands in non-dilutive funding for women-owned, for-profit, revenue-generating U.S. businesses (51%+ woman-owned) that haven’t raised Series A–C or taken more than $500K in equity investment, with a $20 admin fee and a required 60-second video in Round 1. Applications run March 2–May 31, 2026, leading to a Top 50 virtual semifinal pitch and audience voting in August, then 10 finalists receive mentorship and pitch in person in Los Angeles at Visionary Live on Sept. 28, 2026, when winners are announced.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a revenue-generating US-based business, legally registered to do business in the US
- Founder/Co-Founder/CEO must be a woman and company must be at least 51% woman-owned
- Your business must not have received Series A, B, or C funding, or equity-based investment exceeding $500,000 USD 
- Must be able to attend the Pitch Bootcamp during the week of July 20, 2026 (exceptions may be made on a case-by-case basis in writing)
- Must be able to pitch live at the Virtual Pitch Semifinals on August 6, 2026 (strictly required)
- Must be able to travel to and pitch live and in-person at Visionary Live in Los Angeles on September 27, 2026
- Businesses in the cannabis, weapons, or adult entertainment industries are not eligible
- Must be a for-profit business; no non-profits will be considered

Name: Simply Business Big Dreams Grant
Description: The Simply Business Big Dreams Grant awards $5,000 each to five U.S.-based small business owners who are ready to scale, plus a one-year membership to Sky’s the Limit’s Launchpad accelerator and mentorship program. Eligible applicants must be 18 or older, based in the U.S., and have generated at least $25,000 in gross revenue over the past 12 months; 20 runners-up will also receive a six-month Launchpad membership.

Name: BRIDGE Accelerator 8
Description: The BRIDGE Accelerator 8 is a 25-week, seed-funding accelerator for startup and early-stage civic engagement and social justice nonprofits operating in Texas, offering $50,000 in unrestricted funding (disbursed in two $25,000 installments), support raising an additional $50,000+ through donor networks, executive coaching, retreats, workshops, strategic planning, and back-office capacity support. The priority application deadline is June 5, 2026 and the final deadline is June 22, 2026 at 11:59pm CST, with the cohort starting January 11, 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who Should Apply to BRIDGE Accelerator

BRIDGE centers our work on building a diverse, multiracial network of grassroots organizations, projects, and coalitions led by organizers, activists, storytellers, data nerds, and founders from across Texas.


Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: BRIDGE highly encourages Black, Indigenous, people of color (BIPOC), women, queer, and trans-led and-serving initiatives to apply to our programs.


Organization Lifecycle: For BRIDGE Accelerator, we welcome applications from idea, startup, and early growth stage organizations. Utilizing, Stevens' nonprofit lifecycle model, we define these stages as:
Startup: Marked by high energy, limited funding, and a newly acquired 501c3 status, startups are out to prove their business case by experimenting with program design. 
Growth: As the organization hits its stride, becoming a growth-stage operation, it focuses on standardizing and deepening programs to meet the needs of its constituents, and formalizing its structure and processes to ensure organizational vitality.
See the model visualization below for more information.


Organization Structure: Formally structured initiatives must be a 501(c)(3) charitable nonprofit organization and/or a 501(c)(4) social welfare organization. Multi-entity organizations or those projects with desires to manage multi-entity projects are encouraged to apply. 


Program Impact: Applicants must engage Texans year-round in progressive-values based:
Civic engagement/democracy activities such as voter registration, voter education, get out the vote (GOTV) efforts, policy advocacy, and leadership development; and/or,
Social justice activities such as issue advocacy, direct action, ballot initiatives, base building, communications, and leadership development.
We embrace the diversity of strategies and tactics needed to create a robust progressive movement.

Name: John T. Gorman Foundation’s 2026 Direct Services Grant Program (DSGP)
Description: The John T. Gorman Foundation's 2026 Direct Services Grant Program offers grants of up to $30,000 to Maine-based nonprofits, public schools, municipalities, and tribal governments providing direct services addressing food insecurity and housing/shelter needs for people experiencing poverty. This year's program has narrowed its focus exclusively to food and shelter in response to unprecedented community need and reductions in federal and state resources, and supports both specific program funding and general operating support for organizations whose missions center on serving Maine residents in poverty. Applications are accepted June 1–22, 2026 at 5:00pm EST, with one application allowed per organization per year.

Name: USDA Micro-Grants for Food Security Program
Description: The USDA Micro-Grants for Food Security Program (MGFSP) supports eligible agricultural agencies and departments in Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, and certain freely associated states to improve access to locally grown food in food-insecure communities. Funds are distributed through subawards for activities such as small-scale gardening, herding, livestock operations, and food security education or access projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants are agricultural agencies, commissions, or departments in Alaska, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Hawaii, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Republic of Palau, and the United States Virgin Islands. Organizations or individuals interested in the MGFSP should contact their state department of agriculture for more information on how to apply within the state or territory listed above.

Eligible entities include individuals, Indian tribes or tribal organizations as defined in 25 U.S.C. § 5304, nonprofit organizations that are engaged in increasing food security (e.g. religious organizations, food banks, food pantries), federally funded educational facilities (e.g. Head Start or Early head start programs, Public elementary or secondary schools, Public institutions of higher education, Tribal Colleges or Universities, Job training programs), Local or Tribal governments that may not levy local taxes under State or Federal law.

Name: Allstate Main Street Grants Program
Description: The Allstate Main Street Grants Program offers small U.S.-based for-profit businesses a chance to join a 12-week virtual Boost Camp focused on marketing, finance, operations, and growth. Up to 250 entrepreneurs will be selected for the accelerator, and 100 of them will receive $20,000 grants to strengthen their business operations. Applications are open from May 11 to June 23, 2026, and eligible businesses must have at least $25,000 in 2025 revenue and be able to participate in the July 2026 Boost Camp.

- At least 18 years old (19 in AL and NE)

The business must be:
- Be a for-profit business registered and located in one of the fifty United States, D.C., or Puerto Rico
- Not have participated in a Hello Alice Boost Camp in the past 12 months
- Must have generated a minimum of $25,000 in revenue in 2025
- Have a demonstrated need for funding and access to business coaching
- Must be willing to participate in a virtual business Boost Camp starting in July 2026

Name: National Endowment for the Humanities Media Projects
Description: The NEH Media Projects grant supports documentary films, podcasts, and radio projects that engage broad audiences with humanities ideas. It offers up to $75K for film development and up to $700K for documentary film production, but applicants must be U.S.-based eligible organizations, and projects cannot promote a particular religious, political, or ideological viewpoint.

Name: eBay Live x Up & Running Grant Program
Description: The eBay Live x Up & Running Grant Program, run by eBay and Hello Alice, supports eligible eBay sellers who want to grow through live selling. Ten selected business owners will each receive a $10,000 grant, one-on-one onboarding and marketing support from the eBay Live team, and a full kit of live-selling equipment. A legal resident of one of the fifty United States, D.C., or Puerto Rico
At least 18 years old (19 in AL and NE, 21 in MS)

Be an active seller on the eBay platform on or before December 1, 2025, with a seller rating of “Above Standard” or “Top Rated”
Not be a recipient of any previous rounds of the eBay Up & Running program

Name: Trailblazers Women Innovators Pitch Competition
Description: The Women Innovators Pitch Competition, hosted by the California Asian Pacific Chamber of Commerce and National ACE, is a national pitch competition for women entrepreneurs to pitch live in front of investors, industry leaders, and corporate decision-makers. The live event takes place August 20, 2026 from 5–8pm at UCI Beall Applied Innovation in Irvine, California.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Business applicants must meet the following requirements:

Is independently owned and operated; not a franchise location
Is a for-profit organization that is registered to conduct business in the United States
Is a legal resident of the 50 United States or D.C. (Void in Puerto Rico, Guam, and where prohibited by law)
Has been operating for one or more years
Has reached the minimum age of 18 years old or older
Must be able to travel to Long Beach, CA for the pitch event 
(Exceptions for travel will be made on a case-by-case basis.)

Name: Ulta Beauty MUSE Accelerator
Description: The Ulta Beauty MUSE Accelerator supports eight early-stage beauty brands with $50,000 in funding, a 10-week business curriculum, and mentorship from beauty founders and Ulta Beauty partners to help prepare brands for retail readiness and long-term growth. One participant will also receive an additional $10,000 in support through the Fifteen Percent Pledge.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be at least 18 years old, a U.S. or Canadian citizen and currently residing in the U.S or Canada, and their business must be registered in the U.S. or Canada.

Name: The Social Science Research Council's Just Tech Fellowship
Description: The Social Science Research Council's Just Tech Fellowship offers a one-year unrestricted award of up to $60,000 to researchers, artists, journalists, and practitioners working at the intersection of technology and society, with the fellowship period running January–December 2027. The program is open to applicants from any country who will reside in the U.S. during the fellowship year, with no formal degree requirements, though full-time students are not eligible. The application portal opens April 27, 2026 and closes June 28, 2026 at 11:59pm EST, with fellows notified in November 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
About the Just Tech Fellowship
The Social Science Research Council invites proposals from researchers working at the intersection of technology and society for the Just Tech Fellowship.

The Just Tech Fellowship supports rigorous, original, and community-grounded work that addresses pressing questions about how technology shapes society and public life. The program is designed for researchers, artists, and practitioners whose work advances thoughtful, practical, and imaginative approaches to how technology is designed, governed, and experienced in public life.

The fellowship welcomes applicants from a wide range of fields, methods, and career paths. Just Tech Fellows include artists, journalists, community-based researchers, social scientists, humanists, technologists, and others whose work expands public understanding of technology and contributes to more informed and accountable technological futures.

What the Fellowship Provides
The Just Tech Fellowship provides a one-year unrestricted award of up to $60,000 to support research, creative practice, or community-engaged work. The fellowship period runs from January 2027 through December 2027 and is designed to provide fellows with the resources and flexibility to advance ambitious projects at the intersection of technology and society.

The program includes monthly virtual gatherings, individualized mentoring, and one in-person workshop that brings fellows together for focused exchange and collaboration. Fellows engage with peers, external partners, and members of the broader Just Tech network, fostering sustained intellectual and professional connections.

In addition to the primary award, fellows may apply for seed funding to support collaborative projects within or across Just Tech cohorts. Participation in the fellowship also provides ongoing access to the Just Tech network beyond the award year.

What Fellows Commit To
Project Advancement

Dedicate sustained time over the fellowship year to advancing a proposed project. Fellows are expected to make substantive progress and to share the development of their research with the cohort.

Cohort Participation

Participate in monthly virtual gatherings and attend one in-person research workshop during the fellowship year. Engagement in these shared spaces is central to the program’s collaborative model.

Mentoring

Engage in individualized mentoring over the course of the fellowship year to support the development of the proposed project.

Collaborative Exchange

Share work in progress, offer thoughtful feedback to peers, and contribute to a rigorous, interdisciplinary exchange across fields and practices.

Reporting and Evaluation

Participate in program evaluation activities and submit one midterm report and one final report reflecting on project progress, outcomes, and future directions.

Application Requirements
To complete the online application, applicants must submit the following:

Résumé/CV: Up to two pages.

Personal Statement: A written statement of up to 1,000 words or a recorded video statement of up to five (5) minutes. The statement should describe your research or creative practice, your primary areas of focus, and the questions that guide your work. You may reference prior projects that illustrate your approach and development.

Work Proposal: The work proposal may be submitted as either a written document (maximum 3,000 words) or a project deck (up to 10 slides). The proposal should address:

Concept Description: Clearly describe your central idea. What question, problem, or area of inquiry is your research intended to address?
Engagement with Technology: Explain how the project engages digital or emerging technologies in substantive ways. This may include the design, use, analysis, critique, or governance of technological systems.
Approach and Contribution: Describe the perspective, method, or approach your project advances. What distinguishes your approach, and how does it contribute to broader conversations at the intersection of technology and society?
Feasibility: What practical, conceptual, or logistical challenges do you anticipate? How do you plan to address them during the fellowship year?
Field Context: Are you aware of other individuals, initiatives, or organizations working on related questions? If so, explain how your work relates to this broader landscape.
Public Contribution: How does this research project contribute to broader conversations about technology and society? What forms of engagement, dissemination, or evaluation do you anticipate during or beyond the fellowship year?
Work Samples: Two work samples that reflect your research, creative practice, or public-facing work. Please include brief descriptions explaining your role in each work.

AI Use in Applications: Applicants may use digital tools to assist with brainstorming, editing, or translation. However, all submitted materials must reflect the applicant’s own original ideas and voice.

Applicant Eligibility
Residency

Citizens of any country may apply. Fellows must reside in the United States for the duration of the fellowship year. The Social Science Research Council does not sponsor visas and may not be listed as an immigration sponsor.

Education

There are no formal degree requirements. Applicants may hold academic credentials or demonstrate a sustained record of research, creative practice, or public-facing work in their field.

Time Commitment

The fellowship runs from January 2027 through December 2027. Fellows are expected to participate in monthly virtual gatherings, mentoring sessions, and one in-person workshop, while making sustained progress on their proposed project.

Experience

Applicants should demonstrate engagement with substantive questions related to technology and society.

Student Status

Individuals currently enrolled as full-time students are not eligible to apply.

Name: The Kirabo Grant
Description: The Kirabo Grant awards $5,000 in non-dilutive funding, a complimentary Kirabo membership, and a business coaching session to one small business owner or founder from a historically under-resourced community, including Black, Hispanic, Indigenous, rural, and immigrant communities. Eligible applicants must be U.S.-based for-profit, nonprofit, or unregistered entities with less than $750,000 in gross profit or total funding received, and there is a non-refundable $15 application fee. The application deadline is June 28, 2026 at 11:59pm PST.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is eligible to apply?
Eligible businesses must be from historically under-resourced communities—such as Black, Hispanic, Indigenous, rural, and immigrant communities—while anyone facing systemic barriers to economic opportunities, regardless of race, is welcome to apply.


For-profit, non-profit, and unregistered entities based in the United States are eligible to apply. Proof of citizenship is not required, but the business must be based in and primarily operate within the United States.


Additionally, the business must have made less than $750,000 in gross profit or received less than $750,000 in total funding from venture capital, investors, or grants.

Name: Bank of America Nonprofit Grant Funding (Local Grants)
Description: Bank of America’s nonprofit grant funding supports organizations that advance economic mobility, with priority areas including basic needs, income creation, stable housing, and empowered communities. Its 2026 Neighborhood Builders® Program is open for eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits, providing leadership training for an executive director and emerging leader, access to a national peer network, and resources to expand community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered for a local grant, your organization:
- Must be tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, not classified as a private foundation and not operating through a fiscal agent or sponsor
- Must be based and serve communities in these markets: https://about.bankofamerica.com/en/making-an-impact/eligible-states-local-markets
- Must be aligned with our funding priorities: basic needs, income creation, stable housing, and/or empowering communities

Name: The Advancing Well-Being in the Arts Initiative
Description: The Well Being in the Arts National Art Partners Fund provides $5,000 to $40,000 in general operating support to small U.S.-based arts and culture nonprofits, especially those reflecting the Arab American or broader immigrant experience. Eligible organizations must have 501(c)(3) status or fiscal sponsorship and annual operating budgets between $25,000 and $500,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Organizations must have an annual operating budget greater than $25,000 and less than $500,000 (based on the average of the last three fiscal years or current budget, current budget, or last year's budget).
- Organization must have a valid 501(c)(3) status or be fiscally sponsored by a 501(c)(3); must be an arts and culture nonprofit based in the United States.
- Preference is given to organizations that reflect that reflect the Arab American or broader immigrant experience.
- Please note: We do not fund individuals, religious organizations, political organizations, school groups/programs at universities, or international organizations.

Name: T-Mobile Hometown Grant
Description: T-Mobile Hometown Grants is a quarterly program (part of a $25M, five-year initiative) that awards up to $50,000 to eligible small towns (pop. 50,000 or less) for public placemaking projects like revitalizing historic structures, creating downtown destinations, or improving community gathering spaces. Applicants must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) nonprofit or local government entity, and projects must be completed within 12 months of funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- This grant program is specifically open to 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(6) nonprofit organizations and local government entities.  If selected, the grant award must be managed and deployed by the nonprofit organization or government entity who applied for the grant. 
- Grant funds may not be awarded to for-profit businesses, directly or indirectly via pass-through funding to for-profit businesses. Additionally, religious congregations are​ not eligible for this grant program. 
- Applicants must be located in small rural communities with a population of 50,000 people or less. ​​ 
- Proposals must focus on a physical project benefiting the public. 
- The applicant organization must own the site where the proposed project would be implemented OR provide a description/confirmation of adequate permissions to alter the site. If the applicant organization does not own the site, one of the letters of support must come from the owner of the site.  
- Applicants may submit up to one (1) application per organization per grant cycle. Applicants may re-apply to subsequent grant cycles if they are not selected in an earlier round. 
- Previous T-Mobile Hometown Grant Program grantees are eligible to apply again for later grant cycles. Previous T-Mobile Hometown Grant Program grantees must demonstrate successful completion of their prior grant project in their application.

Name: Restaurants Care Resilience Fund
Description: The Restaurants Care Resilience Fund offers $5,000 grants to independent restaurants, caterers, and food trucks in California for needs such as kitchen equipment, technology upgrades, employee training/retention, or unforeseen hardship. The 2026 grant cycle will accept applications from June 1–30, 2026, with additional details expected soon. Since 2021, the fund has awarded $11 million across 2,087 grants to California food businesses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Independent restaurants, caterers, and food trucks across California.

Name: Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators (SCBWI) Volemos Grant
Description: The SCBWI Work-in-Progress (WIP) Award supports children’s book writers with completed manuscripts that are not under contract, selecting one winner in categories such as Picture Book, Middle Grade, Young Adult, Nonfiction, and Underrepresented Voices. Winners have their work showcased to a curated group of acquiring editors, offering valuable industry exposure though not guaranteed publication. Applicants must be current SCBWI members and submit a cover page, synopsis (or logline for picture books), and the first ten pages of their manuscript following specific formatting guidelines.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: This award is open to authors of Hispanic/Latinx/Ibero-American heritage who are early in their career (1-3 traditionally published books) or not yet traditionally published. Please note: Self-published is not considered traditionally published for this award. All applicants must be current SCBWI members and have heritage from the following countries/territories: Argentina, Belize, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Martinique, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Portugal, Puerto Rico, Saint-Barthélemy, Saint Martin, Spain, Suriname, Uruguay, Venezuela.

Name: She Seals the Deal Grant
Description: The She Seals the Deal Grant awards $5,000 to one U.S.-based woman entrepreneur — specifically coaches, consultants, or service-based business owners — who is actively selling her expertise and committed to building consistent, repeatable revenue. Applications require a $25 fee and are reviewed by a panel using a structured scoring rubric, with the recipient announced on or before July 15, 2026. The application deadline is June 30, 2026 at 11:59pm ET.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The She Seals the Deal Grant was created for women who are actively building their business and ready to turn $5,000 into a revenue-generating system.
This grant is for you if you are:

A U.S.-based coach, consultant, or service-based business owner

Actively selling (or preparing to sell) your expertise

Generating revenue - and ready to increase it

Willing to strengthen your sales skill set

An action-taker

Name: Keep Oakland Beautiful Community Grant
Description: Keep Oakland Beautiful's Community Grants program awards project grants of up to $1,000 to individuals and community groups for projects that keep Oakland clean, green, and beautiful in public spaces, such as park cleanups, murals, community gardens, tree planting, and graffiti removal. Applicants do not need to be a nonprofit or low-income to apply, and both individuals and community groups are eligible, though all projects must take place within Oakland city limits. The application deadline is June 30, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Requirements:

All project proposals must take place within Oakland city limits.

Projects on City of Oakland property must be approved by the City and have Oakland Adopt-A-Spot approval.

Projects on private property will be considered, with priority going to those that can be enjoyed by the community.

Name: TiE Women Program 2026
Description: The TiE Women Program 2026 is a global pitch competition and mentorship program for women founders across all industries, offering visibility, investor networking, and access to industry leaders. Eligible applicants must be female founders or co-founders with at least 33% equity, leading companies founded after January 1, 2019, with preference given to startups actively raising funds — idea-stage startups are not eligible.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Criteria

- Female-founded or co-founded startups ONLY. (The opportunity to pitch will only be provided to the female founder/co-founder).

- Female co-founder(s) must have minimum 33% equity in the company.

- Companies in business for less than seven years only at the time of application (Company registration after Jan 1, 2019)

- Preference to startups raising funds

Name: Google for Startups Accelerator: North America
Description: The Google for Startups Accelerator: North America is a free, equity-free 10-week hybrid program for early-stage AI for Energy startups (Pre-Seed to Series A) focused on grid optimization, demand flexibility, and energy solutions for utilities and commercial entities. Selected cohorts of 10-15 startups receive dedicated mentorship from Google experts, technical project partnerships, early access to Google AI products, cloud credits, and specialist workshops on product design, customer acquisition, and leadership. Applications are open May 4–June 30, 2026, with the program kicking off in September 2026 and Demo Day in November 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Entry criteria

Startups demonstrating traction, ideally between Pre-seed and Series A stage

Building a scalable product or service in AI for Energy with a significant total addressable market and defensible growth model

Deeply technical, leveraging machine learning and AI for Energy applications

Commitment from CTO and/or technical roles to participate and engage in required program sessions

We are committed to building accelerator classes with great startups, and encourage applications from all qualified startups

Name: Rise Women Collective Rise to Radiance Grant
Description: The Rise to Radiance Grant from Rise Women Collective provides $500–$1,000 in scholarship funding to help women enter or advance in beauty, cosmetology, and personal care careers. Funds can be used for expenses such as cosmetology school tuition, professional tools and kits, certification programs, or training workshops.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Women entering or advancing in beauty, cosmetology, hair, nails, makeup, or esthetics careers

Name: FedEx E-commerce Learning Lab
Description: The FedEx E-commerce Learning Lab from 37 Oaks, in partnership with Accion Opportunity Fund, helps U.S. small businesses launch or strengthen their e-commerce operations through a five-month program of courses, workshops, monthly 1:1 coaching, marketplace selling support, warehousing, fulfillment, marketing, and product setup assistance. Participants receive a $5,000 grant upon completion of program requirements, along with tools and support to build a profitable, scalable online business. Eligible businesses should have been operating for at least six months and actively sell shelf-stable packaged products.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Food and non-food categories
-- Shelf stable, packaged goods
-- Not refrigerated or frozen 
-- No prohibited or regulated categories (i.e: CBD, alcohol, flammables, etc)

- Products capable of being produced in large quantities. 
- Cannot accomodate uniquely made, custom, one-of-a-kind items.

- United States businesses
- Has legal permits & licenses to operate, produce, and sell product(s). 
- At least 6 months in operation
- Actively selling the product in the market. 
-- Not the best fit for businesses in the concept phase.​
- Has a business social media presence.

Name: Oregon & SW Washington Hispanic Metropolitan Chamber $5,000 Small Business Grant
Description: The Community Investment for Business Opportunities (CIBO) Program is a competitive grant for small businesses in Clark, Cowlitz, and Wahkiakum Counties, offering up to $5,000 to support business growth. Strong applicants should show business readiness, a commitment to learning, and a clear plan for how they will use the funds.

Name: Wren's 2026 Request for Climate Proposals
Description: Wren’s 2026 Request for Proposals funds organizations implementing high-impact climate solutions, with selected applicants receiving $100,000 to $500,000 through grants or carbon credit purchases over a six- to twelve-month period. The RFP focuses on nature-based solutions, policy initiatives, methane mitigation, and other tangible climate work that is scalable, durable, cost-effective, feasible, and catalytic.

Name: 2026 Navy Pier Small Business Accelerator Program Application
Description: The Navy Pier Small Business Accelerator Program, supported by BMO, is a multi-month training program for 10-12 established small business vendors covering financial strategy, operations, branding, social media, wholesale opportunities, and sales, culminating in participation at Navy Pier's Winter WonderFest Artisan Market. The program runs August 2026 through January 2027, giving participants the tools and platform to grow through retail, wholesale, and partnership opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who Should Apply
We’re looking for small business owners who are ready to grow and take their business to the next level. Ideal applicants include:
Businesses with 1–3 years of vending experience
Owners with a business plan that has been created or updated within the past 3 years
Individuals who are available to fully participate in all workshop sessions and vending dates
Businesses that offer retail products (please note: service-based businesses, nonprofits, and early-stage startups are not eligible at this time)

Name: NYC Scale Ready Studio Accelerator
Description: The Scale Ready Studio Accelerator is a 12-week, revenue-focused accelerator for women founders in New York City building businesses in innovation industries, delivered by founders who have scaled seven- to nine-figure companies. Cohort 2 focuses on the Green Economy — businesses creating economic value while reducing environmental impact — and is designed for founders who already have customers, some revenue or signed pilots, and are ready to build predictable revenue systems and operational capacity.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This accelerator is a strong fit if you:

• Are a women-identifying founder based in NYC

• Are building a company in an innovation-driven industry (includes but not limited to: technology, life sciences, climate/green economy, scalable digital or platform-based models)

• Are past ideation and actively operating your business

• Have traction (customers, contracts, pilots, or early revenue)

• Want more predictable revenue, stronger operations, and clearer systems for growth

• Are focused on building a business that can scale sustainably — regardless of funding climate

Name: BeyondCPG Accelerator
Description: BeyondCPG is a curated, operator-led accelerator for emerging, market-validated consumer packaged goods brands looking to scale. The hybrid program connects selected founders with operators, buyers, investors, mentors, sponsors, and strategic partners, while providing hands-on support across sales, marketing, operations, and finance. The program includes remote engagement, key in-person moments, a Showcase Day, and continued access to the BeyondBrands ecosystem.

Name: South Florida Startup Pitch Accelerator Regional Competition
Description: SPARC South Florida is a startup pitch accelerator and regional Startup World Cup competition for founders in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties, with applications closing July 1, 2026. Selected startups receive investor and mentor access, venture-scaling sessions, networking opportunities, and a chance to pitch at Demo Day for the South Florida Champion title and a pathway to the Startup World Cup Grand Finale, where companies compete for $1 million in investment. Both tech and non-tech/small business tracks are also automatically eligible for up to $20,000 in direct investment from The Source.
Amount: chance to complete for $1M in investment, and $20,000 direct investment
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: SPARC is designed for high-potential founders building scalable startups with clear traction or a validated concept. We look for teams committed to growth, innovation, and competing on a regional and global stage. Early-stage and growth-stage startups are welcome, provided there is a strong value proposition and execution plan.

Name: SEED SPOT Made for Retail Chicago
Description: Made for Retail Chicago helps Chicago-area CPG founders get retail-ready and move their products onto shelves. The SEED SPOT and Greenwood Archer Capital program combines a bootcamp, hands-on coaching, retail-readiness education, and a live pitch competition with access to buyers and capital providers. Five founders will pitch on August 27, 2026, with the top three receiving $25,000 in total nondilutive grants, and 10 additional brands joining an on-site marketplace.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This opportunity is for brands that
- Are headquartered in Chicago, Cook County, or surrounding Collar counties
- Have been in operation for at least one year with recorded operating income
- Have recurring monthly revenue and active sales channels beyond direct sales only
- Are seeking nondilutive capital to fuel near-term growth tied to clear business and product milestones
- Are ready to pitch to retail buyers and take their brand to the next level

Name: Home Depot Veteran Housing Grant
Description: Funding for nonprofits to build or repair housing for U.S. veterans, including accessibility modifications and critical repairs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits serving veteran housing needs; projects with measurable outcomes.

Name: Los Angeles Cleantech Incubator
Description: LACI’s Incubation Cohort 13 supports pre-seed and seed-stage U.S.-based cleantech startups working in clean energy, zero-emissions transportation, or circular economy solutions for smart and sustainable cities. The program offers a six-month curriculum, weekly advisory support, pilot funding and deployment help, investor preparation, pitch opportunities, workspace benefits, and potential access to LACI’s Impact and Debt Funds ranging from $50,000 to $500,000. Eligible startups must have a working prototype, proprietary technology, a Southern California expansion strategy, and agree to a 1.5%–3% equity warrant.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Have a cleantech solution that addresses one of our key priority areas –  clean energy, zero-emissions transportation, or circular economy with a focus on smart & sustainable cities.
- Own or hold license to a novel proprietary technology. 
- Have a strategy to expand in Southern California through commercialization, pilots, and job creation. 
- Ability to commit to a hybrid curriculum and mentorship opportunities during the first six months, with founder or key executive able to attend meetings, workshops, and events. 
- Have at least one (preferably two) full-time employee and a strategy to grow the team in Southern California. 
- Have a working prototype (TRL 4+).
- Agree to a 1.5-3% equity stake in the form of a warrant with the opportunity to earn back through achieving impact milestones. 
- Must be based in the United States.

Name: IDEAfuel Accelerator
Description: IDEAfuel is a competitive venture accelerator from The Idea Village that supports Black founders and founders of color by providing $15,000 in non-dilutive funding, 1:1 mentorship, and structured workshops. Eligible applicants must be IDEAinstitute alumni or commit to completing IDEAinstitute if accepted, and selection is based on venture readiness, product vision, founder experience, execution capacity, market opportunity, and coachability.

Name: SF Film Documentary Film Fund
Description: The SFFILM Documentary Film Fund supports feature-length documentaries in post-production that stand out for strong storytelling, compelling characters, and an innovative visual style. It awards about 3–4 projects each year with grants of $10,000–$20,000, and is open internationally to filmmakers in key creative roles whose projects are within about three months of starting post-production. The 2026 application opens March 3, with deadlines on June 9 and July 7, and finalists and recipients announced in the fall.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Applicant must be in a key creative role for the film: ideally, the producer or director.
Filmmaker may not be SFFILM employee or board member.
Filmmaker may not be a full-time student.
Project cannot be a work for hire.
Project must be a feature length documentary (60 minutes or more).
Project must be within 3 months of beginning post-production from the final grant application deadline.
Projects can be produced or based anywhere in the world.
Projects must be consistent with SFFILM’s mission and represent an imaginative contribution to the moving image art form.
Project reflects innovation in storytelling and visual style.
Projects that primarily use interviews as a storytelling device will not be considered.

Name: Next Stage Chicago Grant
Description: The Next Stage Chicago grant from DCASE provides up to $50,000 to support organizational development and capacity building for emerging Chicago-based nonprofit producing theater organizations. Eligible applicants must be Illinois-incorporated 501(c)(3) theater organizations that have operated for 3–10 years, have an adjusted operating budget of $500,000 or less, and can use funds for areas like organizational management, marketing, financial planning, production management, or strategic planning.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible to apply, organizations must meet the following criteria:

Be a nonprofit 501(c)3 organization.
Be a resident company in the city of Chicago with a valid street address (P.O. Boxes will not be accepted).
Be incorporated in the state of Illinois for at least three (3) years and no more than ten (10) prior to applying.
Have a primary mission to produce and present theater arts.
Primarily serve the residents of the city of Chicago (demonstrate that, on average, half of all programming occurs within the city of Chicago limits).
Be able to complete a grant agreement with the City of Chicago.
Provide evidence of organizational structure, including leadership and governance.
Align with the program definition of emerging producing theater organization.

Name: Old National Bank Foundation
Description: The Old National Bank Foundation provides grants to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving communities within Old National’s banking footprint in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan, Minnesota, North Dakota, Tennessee, and Wisconsin. Funding supports programs aligned with four priorities: affordable housing, workforce development, economic development, and financial empowerment, with an emphasis on underrepresented communities and low- to moderate-income people. The foundation awards over $3 million annually, with an average grant of about $15,000.

Name: BlackRock Future Builders RFP
