Description: BlackRock Future Builders is a competitive RFP supporting U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits that provide skilled trades workforce training or capacity-building tied to infrastructure sectors such as data centers, energy, transportation, or related supply chains. The program will award two-year grants of $500,000 to $1 million, with proposals due July 10, 2026, and eligible projects must request funding for a specific program or project.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Be a U.S.-based (including Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands) nonprofit organization
- Be recognized as a 501(c)(3) public charity or equivalent
- Propose funding for a specific program or project, not general operating support
- Demonstrate sound governance, leadership, and financial health
- Typically, no more than 25% of an organization’s annual budget should be directed to administrative and fundraising overhead. Applicants may request grant funding ranging from $500,000 to $1 million.

Name: New Orleans City Council 2026 Community Grants
Description: The New Orleans City Council–Cox Communications Community Grant Program funds Orleans Parish 501(c)(3) nonprofits and local projects that support education, technology training, communications, and similar youth-focused programs. The program provides at least $1,000 per application, with each Councilmember allocated $20,000 annually and the option to combine funds for larger awards.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Organizations must be 501(c)(3) non-profits.
Organizations must be in good standing with the Louisiana Secretary of State’s Office.
Organizations and projects funded under this program must have their permanent location in the Parish of Orleans.
All organizations and projects that can foster the purposes set forth above are eligible for grants.
Organizations shall not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, or disability.
No grants under this program may be paid to any political campaign, political committee or other political related organization or project.
Funding under this program shall be limited to not more than 50% of the organization’s total annual budget or 25% of the annual budget of an organization that is less than a year old. The term “budget” as used herein shall mean the total of direct cash expenditures plus verified in-kind services. In-kind services shall include volunteer time, use of buildings and other facilities, and use of equipment. The value of volunteer time shall be based on the average hourly earnings of all production and non-supervisory workers on private non-farm payrolls (as determined by the Bureau of Labor Statistics) and increased by 12 percent to cover fringe benefits. The use of buildings and other facilities shall be valued at fair market value. Donated equipment shall also be valued at fair market value.

Name: Wells Fargo Neighborhood Growth Grants Program
Description: The Wells Fargo Neighborhood Growth Grants program, administered with A4CB, provides $25,000 grants to eligible for-profit small businesses in select South Side Chicago community areas, including Washington Park, Fuller Park, Grand Boulevard, Woodlawn, Douglas, Oakland, and Kenwood. Applicants must have a physical storefront, at least one year of operation, recent annual revenue between $100,000 and $2 million, a valid business bank account and state ID, and be in good standing with the Illinois Secretary of State.

Name: Watson Institute Flagship Fellowship
Description: Watson Institute's Flagship Fellowship is a free 16-week virtual program for impact-driven entrepreneurs worldwide, offering entrepreneurship and leadership training, financial tools, mentorship, pitch coaching, and a global peer community, with Fellows automatically considered for sub-fellowships including the Luff, Sustainability, Kenneth King Foundation, and Venable Fellowships. Eligible applicants must have a business operating 1–5 years with fewer than 10 employees, demonstrated traction, and must commit to weekly virtual workshops Tuesday–Thursday from 8–10am MT plus a mandatory virtual immersive August 11–18, 2026. The priority application deadline is June 28, 2026, with final selections announced July 9, 2026 and the program running August 11–November 24, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
You are a founder, entrepreneur, or community-driven innovator leading a venture with demonstrated traction and a deep commitment to building impactful solutions. You bring a strong leadership presence and a desire to grow alongside a global community of changemakers.

Your Business Stage:
Your business or organization has been operating for 1-5 years with fewer than 10 employees. You have engaged customers, measurable results, and have secured some funding through grants, investments, donations, or revenue, but you’re ready to grow to the next level.

Your Commitment:
You must be able to commit to the full 16-week program, including the mandatory virtual Immersive from August 11–18, 2026, and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 8:00 AM – 10:00 AM MT. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.

Where You Work:
Location eligibility varies by specific fellowship; however, we welcome qualified applicants from all geographic regions.

What You Are Looking For:
You seek expert-guided entrepreneurial training, a supportive community for feedback, a broad mentor network to enhance your leadership, and opportunities to challenge yourself by leading a Basecamp event and other initiatives that benefit your venture and community. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset to this work.

Demographics:
Adults 18 or Older

Name: Founder Fellowship Boston by Visible Hands
Description: A Boston-based fellowship for early-stage entrepreneurs who are representative of Greater Boston’s rich racial and gender diversity.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Startups that have raised less than $500k in dilutive funding 
- Teams with at least one co-founder currently living in one Greater Boston
- Founders/teams that can commit 2 hours a week to the Fellowship
- Founders with a gender and/or racial identity underrepresented in tech. This includes - but isn't limited to - women, non-binary and trans folks, Black, Latinx, Asian and Pacific Islander, and Indigenous American people
- Founders of a post-idea and pre-revenue early-stage company. This means you are developing a solution to a problem that people need addressed now but haven't made sales yet

Name: Better Business Bureau (BBB) Spark Awards
Description: The BBB Foundation Spark Awards for Entrepreneurship, presented by Bridge City Law, recognizes young businesses and entrepreneurs who demonstrate trust, integrity, and ethical practices, open to businesses that are three years old or less or have an owner aged 35 or younger. The award is available across multiple regions including Alaska, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, and Washington, with recognition designed to strengthen reputation, attract customers and investors, and differentiate winners in their markets. The 2026 application deadline is July 12, 2026 at 11:59pm PDT.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: If you’ve been in business for three years or less—or you’re an entrepreneur age 35 or younger—this is your chance to stand out as a leader who puts character at the core of your work.

Name: Studio Grants by Garnier
Description: Studio Grants by Garnier will award eight $5,000 grants to women producers, engineers, songwriters, and music creators to upgrade or redesign existing studio spaces. Eligible applicants must have 5+ years of professional music industry experience, own or operate the studio space, and propose improvements that support both creative workflow and wellness, such as acoustic treatment, lighting, equipment, ergonomics, accessibility, or decompression space.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Audio engineers, producers, songwriters, or similar music creators with 5+ years of experience at a professional level in the music industry.

Must have an existing studio space that you are able to make modifications to or be in the process of building or developing one—grants may not be used as seed funding for brand new projects.

Professional-level home studios and commercial studios are invited to apply. Applicant must be the studio owner or sole proprietor of the studio space.

Demonstrated need for studio improvements that will enhance creative workflow, productivity, and long-term career sustainability.

These grants are designed to go beyond gear! Applicants must include a meaningful wellness-focused component or similar element(s) related to enhancing their craft as part of the project, such as improved ergonomics, dedicated meditation or decompression space, enhanced lighting, incorporation of greenery, accessibility improvements, or other upgrades that support their holistic creative development.

Name: 2026 Unpublished Novel Award
Description: The Black List's 2026 Unpublished Novel Award offers $10,000 grants to one outstanding manuscript in each of four categories — Children's & Young Adult, Literary, Commercial Fiction, and Speculative Fiction — to support the recipient's path to publication. Any writer who has received a manuscript evaluation on the Black List's website can opt in for free, and winners retain all rights to their work. Submissions are open through July 13, 2026, with award recipients announced in December 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Unpublished Novel Award celebrates stellar unpublished manuscripts in four distinct categories: Children’s & Young Adult, Literary, Commercial Fiction (including the genres of Romance, Thriller/Suspense and Crime/Mystery) and Speculative Fiction (including the genres of Horror and Sci-Fi/Fantasy).

A panel of esteemed judges with experience in book publishing will select one exceptional manuscript in each category to receive a $10,000 grant to support it on the journey to publication. Any writer who has received  a manuscript evaluation on this site has the option to opt into consideration for this award for free. Recipients will retain all rights to their manuscript and will be free to sell them whenever and wherever they please (note: manuscripts cannot be under contract at any point during award consideration; self-published novels will not be accepted).

You must post an original, unpublished manuscript on www.blcklst.com, with at least one (1) evaluation, and opt-in to the Program during the Submission Period. 

Your manuscript should fall within one of the following categories: Children’s & Young Adult, Literary, Commercial Fiction (including the genres of Romance, Thriller/Suspense and Crime/Mystery) and Speculative Fiction (including the genres of Horror and Sci-Fi/Fantasy). Please note that The Black List reserves the right to recategorize a submission at our discretion.


ELIGIBILITY: 
To be eligible, your manuscript may not be under contract at any point during award consideration. Self-published novels, regardless of ISBN status and regardless of Black List site evaluation status, will not be considered for the award. For the avoidance of doubt, no feature screenplays, pilot scripts, plays, or musical submissions will be eligible for the Program.

You must agree to: (1) these Submission Requirements; (2) all terms relating to the Program posted on Black List’s website, which you should review and read in full; and (3) the Submission Agreement, which governs the submission of your material to Black List. The Submission Agreement includes important, legally binding terms and conditions, including arbitration of any disputes, which you must read in full before accepting.

If requested, you must submit (by a date determined by Black List) the following materials, which are also governed by the Submission Agreement:

Contact and other personal information; and

Executed originals of the Submission Agreement.

If selected by Black List for the Program, you will retain all rights in your manuscript and will be free to sell it as you please.

You must be at least 18 years of age and not a minor in the state or country of your residence at time of submission.

If the submitted materials are written by a team consisting of one or more writers: (i) each member of that writing team must comply with these Submission Requirements, including agreeing to the Submission Agreement described above; and (ii) all members of the writing team must opt-out of the Program if any other member becomes ineligible (including as a result of failing to timely agree to the Submission Agreement or failing to timely provide the materials listed above).

The submitted materials must be wholly original to you and you must be the sole owner of all rights. The submitted materials must not in any way infringe upon the copyright of any person or entity or, to the best of your knowledge in the exercise of reasonable prudence, constitute libel, defamation or invasion of privacy or any other rights of any third party.

Name: Connecting California Grants
Description: California Humanities' Connecting California Grants offer $1,000–$5,000 to California-based nonprofits and public agencies for publicly accessible activities that bring people together across difference — such as age, culture, race, faith, or politics — to foster understanding and shared values, with a required 1:1 match using non-federal funds or in-kind support. Projects may last up to 12 months and must not begin sooner than three months after the application deadline.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who Can Apply
California-based nonprofit organizations, including fiscally sponsored entities

California-based public agencies, including libraries, municipal arts councils, schools, colleges, universities, and tribal governments

Name: Zendesk Tech for Good Impact Awards
Description: Zendesk's Tech for Good Impact Awards provides free software and multiple grants ranging from $5,000 - $50,000 to global nonprofit organizations that are fostering community, promoting resilience, and creating career pathways into tech.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- You MUST submit proof of nonprofit status with your application in the "attachment" section of the application form. 
- Current Zendesk customers are not eligible for the impact awards.
- Current and past Zendesk grantees are not eligible for the impact awards.
- Only applications submitted through the application form will be considered. Zendesk will not accept emailed applications.
- At this time, Zendesk is only accepting applications written in English. 
- At this time, we are unable to grant to organizations based in: Belarus, Central African Republic, Crimea Region of Ukraine, Congo, Cuba, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Liberia, Libya, North Korea, Somalia, Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Venezuela, Yemen, and Zimbabwe.

Name: Garden Futures Grants
Description: The Garden Conservancy's 2026 Garden Futures Grants award $2,500–$10,000 in general operating support to U.S.-based nonprofit organizations and small public gardens that are making community impact through garden-based programming or contributing to garden history preservation, with priority given to organizations with annual budgets of $1 million or less. The program includes two named grants: the $10,000 Page Dickey Grant for American Gardens and the Nibbled Leaf Grant for Ecological Gardening. Applications open May 1, 2026 and close July 15, 2026 at 5pm EST, with organizations that received a Garden Conservancy grant in the past three years ineligible to apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
These grants celebrate and highlight the work of innovative and diverse gardening practices throughout the United States. They are awarded to nonprofit organizations and small public gardens across the United States that are:

Making a significant impact in their communities through garden-based programming, with a focus on the environment and diverse populations; or
Contributing to the study and preservation of garden history.

Name: Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan Community Grants
Description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan Community Grants Program funds nonprofits and public entities working on long-term, positive change across Livingston, Macomb, Monroe, Oakland, St. Clair, Washtenaw, and Wayne counties. The program awards approximately $6.5 million annually, with grants typically ranging from $15,000 to $100,000 for one year, or up to $150,000 over 24 months, to support specific projects, programs, or eligible operations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Foundation awards grants to 501(c)(3) organizations, government entities, school districts, and universities. We will consider fiscally sponsored organizations. All organizations must be physically
located in and/or operate in one or more of the seven counties of the Community Foundation’s service area: Livingston, Macomb, Monroe, Oakland, St. Clair, Washtenaw, and Wayne. We do not make grants to individuals, sectarian religious programs, or to cover deficits or other previously incurred obligations.

Name: OpenAI Foundation 2026 People-First AI Fund
Description: The 2026 People-First AI Fund will provide $50 million in unrestricted grants to U.S.-based community nonprofits exploring how AI can strengthen their missions and better serve local communities. The fund focuses on community support services, arts and cultural organizations, and community journalism/media, with eligible applicants generally needing 501(c)(3) status and annual operating budgets between $500,000 and $10 million.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
In addition to alignment with the focus areas, organizations must meet the following criteria:

U.S.-Based 501(c)(3) Organization: Organizations must be a U.S.-based public charity with a valid 501(c)(3) status and be in compliance with applicable 501(c)(3) requirements.

Primarily U.S.-Focused Operations: Organizations must be located in, and primarily conducting work within, the 50 U.S. states or the District of Columbia.

Small to Mid-Sized Budget: Organizations must have an annual operating budget between $500,000 and $10 million (except for certain regranting organizations, see below)*. Based on demand, we expect to prioritize organizations between $1-8 million operating budgets.

Standalone Organizations: We will not consider applications from programs, centers, or departments housed within larger institutions – including academic research centers, university-affiliated institutes, and think tanks – or programs fiscally sponsored by another institution, even if the program maintains separate operating budgets below $10 million.

Name: AlphaLab Accelerator
Description: AlphaLab is a Pittsburgh-based accelerator for early-stage startups in software, hardware, life sciences, and robotics, offering funding, mentorship, and connections to investors, customers, and talent. Eligible applicants must be U.S.-incorporated, have U.S. work authorization, own or exclusively license key IP, commit to significant in-person participation in Pittsburgh, and show evidence such as customer discovery, a prototype or MVP, a motivated team, and a large market opportunity.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
AlphaLab is seeking ambitious, driven, and coachable founders who are ready to take their startups to the next level. We support startups at the early stages of development and those with a unique vision for growth in sectors like software, robotics, life sciences, and hardware. Founders who join AlphaLab should be ready to fully commit to their startup’s success, engage deeply with our mentorship, and work within Pittsburgh’s vibrant tech community

To apply for AlphaLab, startups must meet the following baseline requirements:

U.S. incorporation: Applicants must have a legally incorporated entity in the United States (e.g., LLC, C-Corp, or S-Corp).
Work authorization in the U.S.: The founders must have the necessary legal authorization to work within the United States.
Commitment to presence in Pittsburgh: Founders should be prepared to spend substantial time in Pittsburgh, engaging with the local ecosystem and leveraging AlphaLab’s connections with the city’s industry leaders, universities, and investors.
Ownership of IP or exclusive license: Applicants must own or hold an exclusive license for any intellectual property critical to their business, ensuring that they can legally develop and commercialize their technology or product.
In-person participation: AlphaLab’s accelerator programming requires a significant in-person presence to maximize the benefit of face-to-face mentorship, networking, and collaboration within the Pittsburgh ecosystem.
Time commitment: Founders should be prepared to devote their full time and attention to the accelerator programming (six to eight hours per week) and their startup’s development. This includes participation in workshops, meetings, and events.

Name: Her Agenda's Groundbreakers List
Description: Her Agenda’s Groundbreakers recognition will honor 50 women transforming their fields and shaping what’s next across categories such as rising leaders, cultural influencers, business achievers, advocates, and systems builders. The nomination process asks applicants to share a nominee’s story and supporting materials to celebrate women redefining leadership on their own terms. Nominations are due July 18, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Name: Western Union Global Fellowship
Description: The Western Union Global Fellowship, powered by Watson Institute, is a free 16-week virtual program for entrepreneurs and community leaders supporting refugees, highly marginalized, or displaced populations across select cities in the U.S., Costa Rica, India, Philippines, Lithuania, Argentina, Italy, Brazil, and Peru. Fellows receive entrepreneurship and leadership training, financial tools, mentorship, pitch coaching, a community development stipend to lead a local Basecamp training event, and participation in a virtual Summit on December 3, 2026. The priority application deadline is June 28, 2026, with final selections announced July 9, 2026 and the program running August 11–December 3, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
You are an entrepreneur or community leader who has experienced the challenges of highly marginalized, refugee, or forcibly displaced communities, or who is actively working to support these populations. You are deeply committed to addressing issues affecting historically underserved communities and driving meaningful, community-centered impact. We particularly value proximate leaders—those who come from these communities or work closely with them, bringing lived experience and close connection to the challenges at hand.

Your Business Stage:
Your business or organization has been operating for 1-5 years with fewer than 10 employees. You have engaged customers, measurable results, and have secured some funding through grants, investments, donations, or revenue, and you’re ready to grow to the next level. (All legal business structures welcome: for-profit, nonprofit, social enterprise, etc.).

Your Commitment:
You must be able to commit to the full 16-week program, including the mandatory virtual Immersive and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 8:00–10:00 AM MT. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.


Where You Work:
Applicants who are located in and/or creating impact in the following countries are encouraged to apply:
United States: Denver, Austin, Miami
Costa Rica: Santa Ana
India: Pune
Philippines: Quezon City
Lithuania: Vilnius
Argentina: Buenos Aires
Italy: Rome
Brazil: São Paulo
Peru: Lima

What You Are Looking For:
You seek expert-guided entrepreneurial training through Watson Institute’s signature Flagship Fellowship curriculum, specialized mentorship from Entrepreneurs in Residence with lived experience supporting communities on the move, a supportive global community for feedback, a broad mentor network to enhance your leadership, and opportunities to challenge yourself by leading a Basecamp training program and other initiatives that benefit your venture and community. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset to this work.

Demographics:
Applicants must be 18 years or older.

Name: Northern Trust Foundation Grant
Description: The Northern Trust Foundation focuses its Chicago giving on South and West Side communities, providing operating and program grants that support low-income youth ages 16–24. Its priorities include meeting essential needs like food security, affordable housing, and accessible healthcare, plus “to-and-through college” educational programs that remove barriers to post-secondary enrollment and completion. Organizations can apply by submitting a Letter of Inquiry during the foundation’s grant cycles.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: '- All organizations must be designated a 501(c) 3 non-profit organization by the IRS and be in good standing.

Name: Summer 2026 Makers Mindset Grant
Description: The Summer 2026 Makers Mindset Grant offers $30,000 in total equity-free funding to three women-led U.S. consumer brands, with each winner receiving $10,000 plus mentorship, office hours with Nancy Twine, community access, and promotional support. It’s open to majority women-owned CPG businesses in select sectors (beauty, food, beverage, pet, tech goods, or home goods) that have operated for at least a year, have at least 51% women ownership, and earn between $50,000 and $1 million annually.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
– Businesses must be legally registered in the United States.
– Businesses must sell a CPG product in the beauty, food, beverage, pet, tech goods, or home goods sectors.
– Businesses must have at least 51% women ownership.
– Businesses must have annual revenue over $50k and no greater than $1 million.
– Businesses must have been generating revenue for at least one full year.

Name: PFund Small Business Grants
Description: PFund Small Business Grants support BIPOC LGBTQ+ small business owners and entrepreneurs in the Twin Cities Metro area with $5,000 per year for two years, plus membership in Quorum and participation in a six-month business cohort with learning sessions, mentorship, and networking. Eligible businesses must be LGBTQ+ owned, aligned with PFund’s mission, operating for at least one year, and have under $250,000 in annual gross revenue.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To apply for a Small Business Grant, businesses must:
- Align with PFund’s Mission and Vision.
I- dentify as LGBTQ+ owned.
- Have been in operation for at least one year.
- Have an annual gross revenue of less than $250,000 for your most recently completed fiscal year.

Name: Santander Cultivate Small Business Grant
Description: Santander’s Cultivate Small Business is a free, 12-week virtual, food-focused (MBA-style) training program for early-stage U.S. food entrepreneurs, with an emphasis on historically underserved founders in low-to-moderate income communities. The program features a curriculum led by Babson College professors, plus mentorship and peer networking, and provides capital support – all graduates receive a $2,500 grant, with select participants eligible for additional awards up to $20,000. Eligible businesses must be U.S.-based, operating at least one year, led by an entrepreneur working full time with fewer than 10 FTEs, and have $25,000–$1,000,000 in annual revenue. Partners include Babson College and ICIC.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Cultivate Small Business aims to strengthen entrepreneurs in food-related industries with the building blocks to be successful business owners. Program participants should represent a business that meets the following criteria:

- Business must be in a food-related industry including retail (full- or limited-service restaurants, food trucks), processing, technology, manufacturing, and food services.
- Revenue of $25,000 to $1,000,000 in the most recent full calendar year.
- Minimum of 1 year in operation as the time of application.
- Between 1 and 10 full-time equivalent employees (including the entrepreneur).
- Participants should reside in or represent a business located in a low-to-moderate income area (this will be determined by our team).

Name: Goldman Sachs 2026 Community Development Champions
Description: Goldman Sachs’ 2026 Community Development Grant Program provides general operating support to 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving low- and moderate-income communities in select counties across New York, New Jersey, and Utah. Funding is available through the one-time Change Makers Initiative and the multi-year Equity Builders Initiative, with applications evaluated based on measurable impact, community engagement, and innovation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible applicants must:

- Be a domestic, nonprofit, tax-exempt organization.
- Under section 501(c)(3) of the US Internal Revenue Code
- Have a clear focus on community development.
- Addressing the needs of LMI areas or households

Operate primarily in specified regions:
• New York: New York, Bronx, Kings, Richmond, or Queens counties
• New Jersey: Hudson or Essex counties
• Utah: Salt Lake, Summit, or Tooele counties

Name: Creative Destruction Lab
Description: Creative Destruction Lab (CDL) is a free, equity-free mentorship program for seed-stage science- and technology-based ventures with the potential for significant global scale. Participants receive guidance from experienced entrepreneurs, investors, scientists, and operators, along with personalized eight-week objectives and access to CDL’s international network.

Name: Alibaba CoCreate Pitch
Description: The Alibaba.com CoCreate Pitch 2026 is a product-based startup competition offering access to a $1,000,000+ global prize pool for U.S.-based small business owners with product-driven businesses. Applicants must register for Accio Work, Alibaba.com’s enterprise AI agent, and complete the application through the CoCreate Pitch assistant in under five minutes. Applications close July 25, 2026, with finalists announced by August 10 and selected founders pitching live in Los Angeles on September 9–10, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: US-based small business owners with a product-driven business. The General track is for established product businesses; the AI Entrepreneur track is for founders building a new product from scratch inside Accio Work.

Name: BMO Fellowship
Description: The BMO Fellowship, powered by Watson Institute, is a fully-funded 16-week virtual program for small business owners and community leaders in Chicago, Los Angeles, San Francisco Bay Area, and Denver who are expanding access to financial services, supporting small businesses, or creating homeownership pathways for underbanked communities. Fellows receive entrepreneurship training, financial tools, expert mentorship, pitch coaching, and the opportunity to lead a community training event, with businesses required to have been operating 1–5 years with fewer than 10 employees. The priority application deadline is July 12, 2026, with the program running August 25–December 15, 2026 and final selections announced July 22, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
You are a small business owner or community leader deeply committed to creating sustainable, scalable impact. You are advancing economic resilience, expanding access to opportunity, and strengthening local economies through your business. Your work aligns with one of the following:

Bringing formal financial services to underbanked communities: Providing access to financial services, tools, and literacy
Supporting small businesses: Enhancing the small business ecosystem in your market
Expanding home ownership opportunities: Creating pathways to home ownership for families locked out of wealth-building
You have an entrepreneurial spirit, a growth mindset, and are driven to grow as an effective leader.

Name: Citizens NYC Neighborhood Business Grant
Description: Neighborhood Business Grants from CitizensNYC provide New York City small businesses microgrants of up to $5,000 for projects that positively impact their local communities. Eligible applicants are profit-generating NYC businesses in the five boroughs with 10 or fewer employees and at least two years of operation, and grants are awarded in two annual cycles.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must meet the following criteria to be considered for a Neighborhood Business Grant:
- Their business must be located in one of New York City’s five boroughs.
- Their business has been operating for at least two years.
- They must have 10 or fewer employees.
- They must be profit-generating.
- They must be able to provide proof of business, such as bank statements, tax documents and POS terminal statements.
- As long as you meet the above criteria, we want to hear about your ideas for improving New York.

Name: Citizens NYC Community Leaders Grants
Description: The CitizensNYC Community Leaders Grant provides microgrants of up to $5,000 for New Yorkers leading community-building projects that improve neighborhood life, strengthen local leadership, and expand community partnerships. Eligible applicants must live in one of New York City’s five boroughs and represent a nonprofit or grassroots volunteer group with at least two volunteers, a budget under $250,000, and a project that is not profit-generating, political, religious, or ideological.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Applicants must meet the following criteria to be considered for a Community Leaders Grant:

They must live in one of New York City’s five boroughs.

Their group or project must be “community-oriented,” meaning it currently has, or will have, two or more volunteers associated with it.

Their group or project must not be profit-generating. They must be nonprofits or grassroots volunteer groups.

Their group or project must have a budget of less than $250,000 (schools and school programs are exempt).

Their group or project must not an affiliate or chapter of a larger organization.

Their group or project cannot promote religious, political, or any other ideology.

Name: Seed Capital Pitch Competition by Wells Fargo
Description: The Good Soil Forum 2026 Pitch Competition offers eight U.S.-based founders the opportunity to pitch live in Dallas for a share of a $500,000 prize pool, including a $150,000 grand prize, with every finalist receiving an award and no equity taken. Applicants choose between Tech-Enabled and Non-Tech/CPG tracks and must operate a legally incorporated for-profit business that has raised no more than $1 million. Applications are open July 15–30, 2026, and finalists must attend the forum from October 8–10, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- A for-profit business, legally incorporated and in good standing in the U.S.
-  Received no more than $1 million in prior funding
-  Not operating in an excluded industry (adult products/services, firearms, alcohol  except restaurants, gambling, MLM, or illegal activity)
 -  An owner over 18 who represents the company in all competition matters.
-   Employee annual income no more than $100,000; installment debt  no more than $200,000 (unless a convertible note)
-  One entry per company.

Name: Fueling Emerging Entrepreneurs Grant
Description: LISC LA’s Fueling Emerging Entrepreneurs program, developed with BMO, supports Los Angeles County small businesses earning up to $250,000 annually, particularly entrepreneurs in low-to-moderate-income communities who have faced barriers to capital. Selected businesses receive flexible grant funding, coaching, promotional visibility, and networking opportunities through a challenge-based application that includes assessments, digital engagement, and a final video pitch. Applications are due July 31, with priority given to businesses in designated cities including Los Angeles, Long Beach, Inglewood, Pasadena, Carson, and Pomona.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility Requirements
- Business must be based in Los Angeles County.
- Annual revenue up to $250,000.
- For-profit business only; many types eligible (e.g., makers, innovators, content creators, tech, food, consulting, health, etc.).
- Active business checking account in the business’s name.
- Owner must be at least 18 years old.
- Must have a business profile on a social media platform (Fud app, LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, etc.).
- Priority given to businesses based in specific LA County cities (such as Los Angeles, Inglewood, Long Beach, Santa Monica, etc.).
- Completion of all challenge steps (1–9), including assessments and a video pitch.
- Business must demonstrate potential for growth and community impact.

Name: Global Citizen and PayPal Small Business Impact Awards
Description: The Global Citizen and PayPal Small Business Impact Awards support independent small and medium-sized businesses that are creating positive social or environmental impact through innovative products, services, and community-centered practices. Selected businesses receive a $20,000 cash prize plus access to insights, technical training, and marketing/brand support. Eligible applicants must be active business leaders with an online presence, typically under 50 full-time employees or under $1 million in annual revenue, and based in eligible regions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Active Business Leader
Be the owner, founder or CEO that plays a crucial role in the current business.

Online Presence
Have an online presence that allows your customers to buy your product. 

Small-to-Medium Sized Business
The business must be classified as a small-medium-sized business, typically with fewer than 50 full-time employees or annual revenue under $1 million (subject to local regulations and standards). 

Demonstrate Community Impact
The business needs to have 1-5 years of impact in their community. 
The business should demonstrate significant, tangible contributions to the local community. This may include, but is not limited to:
Supporting local causes, charities, or nonprofit organizations. 
Engaging in community development projects or local partnerships. 
Implementing sustainable practices that benefit the local environment or economy. 
Creating jobs or providing educational/training opportunities for community members. 

Location
The business must be based in one of these regions:  North America,  Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Latin America

❌ Exclusions:
The business must not be affiliated with an organization from any country or entity subject to financial or other sanctions by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) or other government entity of the United States of America that may restrict the transfer of the Award 
The business must not be a franchise or part of a national or international chain, as the focus is on independent, locally owned enterprises. 
You must live and work in North America,  Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Latin America to be eligible.

Name: Nasdaq Foundation Economic Opportunity Grant Program
Description: The Nasdaq Foundation Quarterly Grant Program supports organizations that empower under-resourced communities with financial knowledge, tools, and access to capital. Eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, or for-profit businesses or consultants acting on behalf of a qualified tax-exempt entity. Grant funding is awarded to programs that demonstrate capacity and expertise, a strong governance and financial model, a proven track record, and measurable impact that can be scaled or replicated to benefit additional communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
NOT DIRECTLY AVAILABLE TO FOR-PROFIT SMALL BUSINESSES. Applicants must be 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations, or a for-profit business/consultant applying ON BEHALF OF a qualified tax-exempt entity or through a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor - the grant agreement must be signed by, and the grant paid to, the tax-exempt entity. Do not match a for-profit business client to this without a fiscal sponsor.

The Nasdaq Foundation will accept grant requests from:
- Organizations designated as tax-exempt according to §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Service code.
- A for-profit business or consultant acting on behalf of a qualified tax-exempt entity or through a fiscal sponsor that is tax-exempt.

CADENCE: Expressions of Interest are accepted BI-ANNUALLY (no longer quarterly), before two deadlines in 2026 - 13 February and 31 July. Both 2026 deadlines have passed; no 2027 dates published.

Name: Elbow Grease Accelerator
Description: A 10-week, AI-first accelerator in New York City offering workshops, hands-on mentorship, and investor connections. Backed by Gutter Capital; designed for early-stage tech founders.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage AI/tech founders able to participate in NYC-based programming.

Name: Latina Expo
Description: The Latina Expo is now accepting speaker submissions for its 2026 national tour, inviting powerful voices to inspire, educate, and uplift the Latina community. The tour will stop in Houston (May 9), Dallas (Jun 27), New Jersey/New York (August, TBD), San Diego (Jul 24), Miami (Aug 28), Chicago (Oct 23–24), and Los Angeles (Nov, TBD. Apply at thelatinaexpo.com.

Name: T-Mobile HQ Grants: Digital Access; Housing & Support for the Homeless
Description: T-Mobile's HQ Grant Program provides $25,000–$50,000 annual grants to nonprofits in the greater Seattle and greater Kansas City areas, with a primary focus on digital access (connectivity, digital literacy, and tech career pathways) and a secondary focus on housing and homelessness support. Eligible organizations must serve specific counties in either metro area, and both single-year and multi-year proposals are accepted. For 2026, the Housing deadline is April 30 and the Digital Access deadline is July 31.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in good standing with IRS
- Direct focus on one of the priority areas
- Located in the greater Seattle or Kansas City area

Name: AWP Writer to Writer Mentorship Program
Description: The AWP Writer to Writer Mentorship Program is a free, three-month program that pairs emerging writers with published author mentors for structured modules covering craft, revision, publishing, and the writing life. The program is open to all AWP members, with particular encouragement for writers without MFA backgrounds and those from underrepresented regions and cultures.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- The AWP Writer to Writer Mentorship Program is open to all AWP members who identify as emerging writers, but they particularly encourage applications from those writers who have never been associated with an MFA program, and those writing from regions, backgrounds, and cultures that are too often underrepresented in the literary world
- AWP Membership required;  $60 annual individual membership fee, $225 writing organization membership fee

Name: The Caregiver Artificial Intelligence Prize Challenge
Description: The ACL Caregiver AI Prize Challenge is a federal competition seeking innovative AI tools to support the more than 70 million paid and unpaid caregivers across the U.S., with a focus on reducing caregiver burden and addressing workforce shortages. The challenge runs across two tracks and three phases, with Phase 1 applications due July 31, 2026. Teams interested in competing can sign up for updates by emailing CaregiverAI@acl.hhs.gov.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Shall have complied with all the requirements under this section
In the case of a private entity, shall be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the U.S.  In the case of a team, the team leader shall be a citizen or permanent resident of the U. S.  However, non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents can participate as a member of a team or entity that otherwise satisfies the eligibility criteria. Non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents are not eligible to win a monetary prize (in whole or in part). Their participation as part of a winning team or entity, if applicable, may be recognized when the results are announced.  In the case of an individual, whether participating singly or in a group, shall be a citizen or permanent resident of the U.S.
Shall not be a federal entity or federal employee acting within the scope of their employment (all non-HHS federal employees must consult with their agency ethics official to determine whether the federal ethics rules will limit or prohibit the acceptance of a COMPETES Act prize)
Shall not be an employee of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS, or any other component of HHS) acting in their personal capacity
Shall not be a judge of the Challenge, or any other party involved with the design, production, execution, or distribution of the Challenge or the immediate family of such a party (i.e., spouse, parent, stepparent, child, or stepchild)
May, in the case of federal grantees, not use federal funds to develop applications unless consistent with the purpose of their grant award
May, in the case of federal contractors, not use federal funds from a contract to develop COMPETES Act challenge applications or fund efforts in support of a COMPETES Act challenge submission
Shall be 18 years of age or older at the time of submission

Name: Stanley 1913 x TOGETHXR Changing the Game Grant
Description: The Changing the Game Grant will award five $20,000 grants to U.S.-based for-profit businesses creating or reimagining food-and-beverage spaces where women’s sports are the main focus and community, wellness, and inclusivity are central. Applications are open from March 31 to July 31, 2026, with finalists reviewed in September and winners announced in October at an in-person event in New York City.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
You Qualify If
• You own or are an authorized representative of a for-profit business registered and in good standing in the U.S.
• Your business operates - or plans to operate - a food and beverage space (bar, restaurant, café, event venue, or community space).
• Your concept centers women’s sports as the main event - not a secondary broadcast or afterthought.
• You are 18+ years of age (19+ in AL and NE) and a legal U.S. resident.

Name: The AT&T Small Business Contest
Description: The AT&T Small Business Contest awards one U.S. small business a $50,000 grant, one year of AT&T service with a new device, mentorship resources, and a featured content piece by AT&T. Four runners-up will each receive $5,000, and eligible applicants must be majority owners of a U.S.-based small business with 1–5 locations and 99 or fewer employees. Applications are open through July 31, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
AT&T Small Business Contest

AT&T is looking to connect with small business owners who are ready to take their dreams to the next level. One winner will claim a $50,000 grant, connectivity, and more! Applications open May 1!

Name: Women Veterans Giving Melissa Washington Small Business Award
Description: The Melissa Washington Small Business Award from Women Veterans Giving supports woman veteran entrepreneurs who are starting or expanding a business, with an award of up to $5,000 plus coaching, assessment, recognition, and other benefits. Applicants should demonstrate innovation, resilience, and positive impact, and must submit materials such as a P&L or tax return, or financial projections for startups, along with a photo or headshot. Applications are open May 1–July 31, 2026, with three finalists announced the week of September 1 and the award presented during the VIB Network National Conference on November 2–3, 2026 in Palm Springs, California.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The MWSBA is awarded to a woman veteran to start or expand her business.

Name: America's Healthy Food Financing Initiative 2026 Fare Fund
Description: The 2026 HFFI Food Access and Retail Expansion Fund (FARE Fund) provides grant and technical assistance funding to expand access to staple and perishable foods in underserved communities through SNAP-authorized food retailers and post-harvest food retail supply chain projects. At least $5.25 million is available for planning and implementation grants of $20,000–$250,000, plus at least $1 million for technical assistance of up to $75,000 per project. Organizations must first submit a Funding Inquiry by July 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET; eligible applicants will be invited to submit full applications due October 30, 2026, with award notifications expected no earlier than January 2027.

Name: The Lego Foundation Fellowship
Description: The LEGO Foundation Fellowship provides up to 10 early- and mid-career researchers with USD $300,000 over three years to advance research on how children thrive across diverse contexts. Eligible applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent doctorate earned within the past 10 years, be employed by a university or research institute, and propose work aligned with one of three themes: young children in crisis/conflict settings, neurodivergent children’s inclusion and wellbeing, or children’s learning and development in an AI-enabled world.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Can applicants from any country apply?

Yes, applicants from any country are welcome to apply, with the exception of countries subject to EU or US sanctions. If your country is not on either sanctions list, you are eligible to apply regardless of your location.

Do I need to be employed by a university or research institute?

Yes. Applicants must be employed at a university or research institute. Funds will be awarded to and administered by the fellow’s institution.

Am I eligible to apply if I currently hold a post-doctoral position?

Yes, post-doctoral candidates are eligible to apply, provided their institution can sign the LEGO Foundation contract.

Can the fellow change institutions during the fellowship?

Yes, subject to approval and confirmation that the new institution can administer the award.

Name: Michigan Central Talent Innovation Training Fund
Description: The Michigan Central Talent Innovation Training Fund provides Southeast Michigan startups with up to $10,000 per new hire for credentialed training, or up to $5,000 per hire for structured on-the-job training. The program supports companies in industries such as technology, robotics, health sciences, clean energy, advanced manufacturing, mobility, drones, and AI, while also offering hiring, HR, onboarding, and curriculum support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
You may be a strong fit for TITF if you are:

✓ A startup headquartered in or operating across Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, or Washtenaw counties

✓ Building in tech, robotics, drones, health sciences, clean energy, advanced manufacturing, mobility, or AI

✓ Ready to make at least one new hire in the coming months

✓ Able to demonstrate your ability to pay and retain staff (revenue, capital raised, or signed contracts)

✓ Committed to paying at least $21.76/hour — Detroit’s livable wage standard

✓ Hiring talent who resides in Southeast Michigan

Name: Workday Foundation Human Connection Microgrant Program
Description: The Human Connection Microgrant Program supports grassroots nonprofits and individuals creating in-person (“IRL”) experiences that foster human connection, belonging, joy, and stronger communities. The program is intended for creative, community-centered ideas that bring people together offline.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Applicants
- Organizations must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in the US, or a registered charity if outside of the US. Organizations operating under a fiscal sponsor are eligible and must provide the fiscal sponsor's name and tax or charity ID. If your organization needs to be connected with a fiscal sponsor, please specify this in your application.
- Organizations must have an annual operating budget of less than $500,000 USD or equivalent. Small organizations including grassroots and community-based organizations are encouraged to apply.
- Organizations and their fiscal sponsors must be in good standing with applicable regulatory authorities and eligible to receive grant funds

Name: South Park Commons Founder Fellowship
Description: The SPC Founder Fellowship supports entrepreneurs at the idea stage with $400K for 7% on a SAFE, community membership, and tailored mentorship to help launch a venture-backable startup. No idea is required to apply. The Spring 2026 cohort begins at the end of March.
Amount: $400k for 7% on a SAFE, along with $600k in next venture round
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See application link here: https://airtable.com/appxDXHfPCZvb75qk/pagyqQLVvYMoPT9pg/form?mc_cid=6cb3cc39e0&mc_eid=41118533d8

Name: South Side Pitch
Description: South Side Pitch is an annual business pitch competition showcasing and celebrating the many creative and promising South Side Chicago businesses and entrepreneurs. Finalists pitch to a panel of judges and a live audience at the Polsky Exchange North, competing for over $40,000 in prizes.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Business Requirements:
- For-profit 
- Fewer than 50 employees 
- Under $1M revenue in 2025
- Headquartered in city limits of Chicago, South of Roosevelt Road 
- Not a franchise 
- Not a prior South Side Pitch finalist 
- Not a current or former IJ Clinic client 
- Beyond idea stage (with customers or pre-revenue with a prototype) 

Individual Requirements:
These individual requirements are applicable to at least one owner or founder of the eligible business, who will pitch the business on a semifinalist video and in-person at the finals if selected. 
- At least 18 years old 
- Legal Illinois resident, currently living in Illinois 
- Must show a meaningful connection to the South Side 
- Never a director, officer, owner, immediate family or household member of a current or former IJ Clinic client, or of the Institute for Justice

Name: Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Program
Description: The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub’s 2026 Innovator Program is an eight-month accelerator for startups developing scalable technologies that advance offshore wind in New York and across the U.S., especially solutions that improve performance and value for existing or near-term projects. Selected companies receive support such as seed innovation grants, corporate mentorship, industry programming, network introductions, visibility, and office access at BATWorks in Brooklyn.

Name: Project W Tech Equity Hub
Description: The Tech Equity Hub is an intensive program for women founders of pre-seed B2B or B2B2C software or AI companies who face barriers to networks and capital. The program includes virtual sessions, two in-person days in New York City, investor presentations, workshops, networking, and subsidized travel support. Eligible companies must not have raised institutional capital and should have core technology, a large market opportunity, and a pathway to revenue growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
A company that:
- Is founded or co-founded by a woman who faces barriers to networks and capital
- Has not yet raised institutional capital
- Has built its core technology for a B2B or B2B2C software or AI product that is differentiated and defensible
- Is addressing a large and growing market
- Has a demonstrated pathway to revenue growth

* The program is designed for companies building B2B vertical or AI software. CPG and DTC companies and companies that are subject to regulatory approval are not eligible.

Name: LA Community Opportunities Flexible Fund
Description: The First 5 LA Community Opportunities Flexible Fund provides 10-month grants of up to $70,000 for Los Angeles County systems-change efforts that help children prenatal to age five and their families meet basic needs, including reducing infant mortality, poverty, and housing insecurity. Eligible applicants include nonprofits, fiscally sponsored projects, membership organizations, social-impact businesses, and government or tribal entities, with strong proposals expected to be community-driven and rooted in Los Angeles County.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Do we have to be a 501(c)(3) to apply? 
No. We will accept applications from 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, fiscally sponsored projects, 501(c)(6) membership organizations, LLCs/corporations/businesses with a social benefit focus, and government or tribal entities.

May we apply if our organization has received COFF funds in the past?
Yes, as long as your grant period will have been completed by the time the new grant starts.

May funds be used to purchase equipment such as laptop computers for our work?
Yes, equipment purchases are eligible for consideration for COFF awards.

May funds be used for staffing? 
Yes. However, although grant funds may be spent primarily to support staffing, this one-time grant may not be used to support more than 30% of the salary of each individual staff member.

Are statewide groups that are not headquartered in Los Angeles but are doing work in this area eligible for funding?
Yes. However, strong applications will demonstrate significant engagement with and leadership by community members in Los Angeles County.

Are grantees of the Reimagining Systems Fund eligible to apply for COFF awards?
No, Reimagining Systems Fund (RSF) grantee organizations are not eligible to apply for COFF awards. However, we encourage RSF grantees to share information about this grant opportunity with groups you are collaborating with, as field-building is an important priority for ECPAF.

Name: Elevate Prize + Newman's Own Foundation Food Justice Grant
Description: The Newman’s Own Foundation and Elevate Prize Foundation GET LOUD Award will provide two $25,000 grants to organizations advancing food justice through sustainable food systems, nutrition education, Indigenous food sovereignty, or related work. Eligible organizations must be a 501(c)(3), fiscally sponsored organization, or public charity with annual revenue under $1 million, and at least one award will support an organization serving school-aged children in the United States.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: To qualify, organizations must be a 501(c)(3), fiscally sponsored, or a public charity with annual revenue under $1M USD.

Name: Pinterest Inclusion Fund
Description: The Pinterest Inclusion Fund is an incubator for emerging U.S. creators who are new to Pinterest and produce inclusive content across areas such as fashion, beauty, lifestyle, home, travel, gaming, and technology. Selected creators receive financial support, personalized education, expert guidance, analytics and content-strategy training, collaboration opportunities, and potential entry into the Pinterest Creator Community.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Pinterest Inclusion Fund supports content producers from all backgrounds who adhere to the following criteria.﻿

Creates content that supports Pinterest's inclusive product tools, such as skin tone and/or body type ranges 

Creates content within the fashion, beauty, and/or lifestyle space, including areas such as home, travel, gaming, and technology

Must be a legal resident of the 50 United States and D.C.

Must be 18 years of age or older

Must be an active content creator who shares content on at least two other social media platforms

Is looking to grow content creation skills on Pinterest

Can commit to office hours and program sessions

Name: Fundable Founders Learning Lab
Description: The Fundable Founders Learning Lab is a free, 10-week virtual accelerator for Florida-based founders in technology, AI, healthcare, consumer products and services, or media and entertainment who are ready to grow and attract capital. Participants receive weekly expert-led sessions, hands-on workshops, feedback, and support focused on revenue models, financial and capital readiness, customer growth, operations, scaling, and investor pitching, with top founders earning access to the Fundable Founders Forum and additional visibility with investors and corporate partners.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This program is for founders who are:

- Located in the State of Florida
- Building in Technology, AI, Healthcare, Consumer Products and  Services, or Media and Entertainment
- Ready to move beyond idea-stage into execution and growth
- Seeking capital, partnerships, or scale opportunities
- Committed to learning and executing

Name: Allies for Community Business Neighborhood Entrepreneurship Lab (NEL)
Description: A4CB’s Neighborhood Entrepreneurship Lab (NEL) is a three-month, cohort-based program that provides entrepreneurs with capital, coaching, and connections by pairing them with investors, advisors, and strategists. Each participating business receives a $20,000 grant to support growth. To be eligible, businesses must have started operations before January 1, 2024, earned at least $75,000 in 2025 revenue, and be seeking to develop a growth strategy.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be considered, applicants must meet all the following criteria:

Business Tenure: Started operations prior to January 1, 2024
Business Location: Physically located in Illinois or Indiana
Business Revenue: Had an annual gross revenue >= $75,000 in 2025
Business Structure: For-profit businesses
Business Growth: Seeking to develop a growth strategy
Business Status: In Good Standing ("Active") with the Secretary of State (This does not apply to sole proprietors.)
Program participation: Applicants must commit to actively participating in the program's hybrid learning structure from September through November, which includes 6 required in-person days at The Hatchery in Chicago's Garfield Park neighborhood scheduled 10:00 AM - 3:00 PM CST:
September 15, 16, and 17
November 3, 4, and 5

Name: U.S. Chamber of Commerce CO-100 America's Top 100 Small Business
Description: The CO—100 is an annual awards program from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce recognizing America's top 100 small businesses across 10 categories including Growth Accelerators, Community Champions, Tech Innovators, and Culture Champions, with businesses able to enter up to five categories. The top business winner receives a $25,000 award, while honorees receive national media exposure, a dedicated business profile, VIP event invitations in Washington D.C., and a one-year U.S. Chamber membership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To apply for the CO— 100, an applicant must:

Be a legal resident of the United States.
Be a for-profit business operating for at least one (1) year prior to May 4, 2025, primarily based within the United States.
Have fewer than 250 employees and gross revenues of less than $20 million for both 2024 and 2025.
Agree to all of the Award Rules, including potentially attending the award ceremony.
Employees, officers, and directors of Sponsors and any affiliated entities, and their respective immediate families (parents, spouse, children, siblings) or individuals residing in their household (whether or not related) are not eligible applicants.

Businesses named to the CO—100 in prior years are not eligible to apply for the awards program again.

Name: Multiple Autism Tech Accelerator
Description: The Multiple Autism Tech Accelerator is a 12-week program for early-stage startups building scalable solutions on the autism community's needs. Participants receive tailored mentorship, workshops, expert office hours, peer mastermind sessions, investor introductions, and pitch preparation through Multiple’s network of more than 700 members. Applications for the next cohort are due August 7.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: We seek ambitious entrepreneurs focused on the autism community's needs, early-stage companies without significant funding or revenue, and strategic thinkers with projects that are sensible, scalable, and sustainable. Our ideal candidates are committed teams ready to invest time and energy to create lasting impact, led by thoughtful leaders passionate about improving the lives of people with autism.

Name: Hubspot Grow Getter Grant
Description: The Grow Getter Grant is a pitch competition from HubSpot for Startups and Startup Grind that awards one early-stage founder a $2,500 grant along with promotional exposure and visibility. It is designed for venture-backable startups that have raised less than $2 million and are already testing, selling, and building momentum.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
A grow getter doesn’t wait for perfect conditions. They build anyway. You might be:
- Less than $2M in funding raised
- Building a venture backable startup
- Business HQ is located in US or Canada
- Be a member of HubSpot for Startups. It's free! Joining is easy (< 5 mins).

Name: Georgetown Ventures Startup Support
Description: Georgetown Ventures is a free, 10-week accelerator for early-stage startups across all industries, offering more than 150 hours of hands-on support from Georgetown student teams. Founders receive tailored help with product development, go-to-market strategy, branding, and website design without giving up equity.

Name: Environmental Sustainability Entrepreneurship Program
Description: Environmental Sustainability Entrepreneurship Program is a free 16-week program for underserved entrepreneurs in the Denver metro area building environmental products or services, funded by JPMorganChase Foundation. Must commit to weekly virtual workshops Tuesday–Thursday from 9–11am MT plus an in-person immersive August 8–13 and a Summit on November 18, 2026. The priority application deadline is June 21, 2026, with final selections announced July 13, 2026 and the program running August 8–November 18, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
You are an impact-driven entrepreneur building an environmental product or service. You are committed to creating positive, measurable change in your community and advancing environmental sustainability through your work.

Your Business Stage:
Your business or organization has been operating for 1-5 years with fewer than 10 employees. You have engaged customers, measurable results, and have secured or earned some funding through grants, investments, donations, or revenue, and you’re ready to grow to the next level. All legal business structures welcome: for-profit, nonprofit, social enterprise, etc.

Your Commitment:
You must be able to commit to the full program, including the in-person Immersive and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 9:00–11:00 AM MT. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.

Where You Work:
You are located in and creating impact in the Denver metro area. Your work directly benefits local communities through environmental products and services.

What You Are Looking For:
You seek environmental sustainability entrepreneurship training led by practioners with deep expertise, a supportive community for feedback, a broad mentor network to enhance your leadership, and the opportunity to multiply your impact by leading a Basecamp training program that supports earlier-stage entrepreneurs in your community. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset to both scaling your own venture and empowering others.

Demographics:
Adults 18 or older.

Name: Conscious Venture Lab Accelerator Program – Baltimore
Description: The Conscious Venture Lab (CVL) Accelerator Program is a 14–16 week  accelerator for early-stage, purpose-driven startups, especially those led by diverse and underestimated founders, focused on building high-growth companies that also create social impact. Selected teams receive free tuition, a structured curriculum rooted in Conscious Capitalism/Stakeholder Theory, plus hands-on mentorship, networking, and resources like workspace; companies may be eligible for up to $125,000 in post-program funding (typically for 5–10% equity) through CVL’s partner fund after the program.

Name: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville Metro East Start-Up Challenge
Description: The Metro East Start-Up Challenge is a business plan competition designed to identify and reward promising entrepreneurs in the St. Louis Metro East region. Applicants progress through an executive summary, business plan, and final pitch, with mentorship and professional support available along the way.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To participate in the 2026 Metro East Startup Challenge, prospective applicants must meet the following criteria:

1. An entrepreneur starting a for-profit small business enterprise or an existing for-profit small business established after April 30, 2023, regardless of State of initial operation or initial entity structure;

2. For existing for-profit businesses, operations must be headquartered in the nine-plus county Metro East region (Calhoun, Jersey, Madison, Bond, Clinton, St. Clair, Washington, Monroe, Randolph and now open to Macoupin, Montgomery, and Fayette Counties!).

3. For established for profit businesses to be eligible, they must be in Good Standing with the Illinois Secretary of State at time of application.

4.  For an entrepreneur purchasing an existing business, the entity will not be considered a startup.  Date will begin with previous ownership. For pre-venture entrepreneurs, proposed new business operations will need to be located in these eleven counties; Calhoun, Jersey, Madison, Bond, Clinton, St. Clair, Washington, Monroe, Randolph, Macoupin, Montgomery, and Fayette

5. No public governmental entities or public/private schools or universities may apply

6. Participants must be 18 years old prior to the first round submission deadline.

Name: AltCap Your Biz Pitch Competition
Description: The AltCap Your Biz Pitch Competition helps small businesses and nonprofits with less than $500,000 in annual revenue compete for cash prizes by submitting an application and pitch video, with five finalists advancing to a live pitch event. Awards include $35,000 for first place, $20,000 for second place, and $5,000 for the fan favorite, along with visibility and connections designed to support business growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The contest is open to owners or operators of a business or nonprofit with less than $500K in annual revenue. Applicants must be able to attend the Live Pitch event. Past winners are not eligible to apply.

Name: MIT Solve Truist Foundation Inspire Awards
Description: The Truist Foundation Inspire Awards support 501(c)(3) nonprofits in the Truist operating footprint that are developing innovative direct services, training programs, and career navigation supports for adult workers in the age of AI. Fifteen semifinalists receive $10,000 in capacity-building funding, six finalists join a six-month support program, and final pitch awards include $250,000 for first place, $150,000 for second place, $75,000 for Community Favorite, and $25,000 for each runner-up.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Inspire Awards are open to nonprofit organizations that meet the following requirements:

Hold a registered 501(c)(3) status with the IRS.
Headquartered within and directly serving the Truist operating footprint, which includes: Alabama, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Maryland, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington, D.C., and West Virginia.
The organization is operating at least at a Growth Stage of Development: A registered 501(c)(3) organization with an established product, service, or business model rolled out in one or, ideally, several communities, which is poised for further growth in multiple communities. Organizations at the Growth Stage should have a proven track record with an annual operating budget - see Organization vs. Solution for more information.
The organization’s solution is at least at the Concept Stage of Development: An idea being explored and researched for its feasibility to build a product, service, or business model, including prototypes under development. Until the solution has a functioning prototype, we would still consider it a Concept .- see Organization vs. Solution for more information. 
Team Lead must be 18 years or older to apply. Additionally, the Team Lead should be the CEO, Executive Director, Primary Investigator, or other key leader for your solution.
Mandatory Team Lead + Secondary Delegate Participation: If your solution is selected as a semifinalist, these individuals will be expected to present the solution to Advisory Council Members during an interview session. If selected as a finalist for the Inspire Awards, the Team Lead will be the lead participant in the support program and is required to attend all sessions. Alongside the Team Lead, an additional team member is expected to participate in the capacity-building components of the support program.
Please note that we are not targeting solutions that support typical degree programs, nor are we targeting solutions that are purely educational with no clear link to career pathways programming.

Name: Visible Hands' SEEN 50
Description: The SEEN 50 recognizes 50 overlooked U.S. founders building transformational technology startups and connects them with visibility, community, and fundraising opportunities. Selected founders receive a free ticket to the 2026 SEEN Summit in New York, access to an invite-only gathering with founders and funders, and the chance to pitch for funding during a live taping of The Pitch.

Name: Very Asian Foundation Creators Grant
Description: The Very Asian Foundation Creators Grant provides micro-grants to creatives who have pivoted toward their creative passions and want to develop a project through an Asian American, Native Hawaiian, or Pacific Islander lens. It supports a wide range of creators—including artists, writers, filmmakers, chefs, podcasters, and content creators—with mentorship and community connections alongside the funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must reside in the U.S., be at least 21, identify a creative project involving an AA/NHPI experience, and complete the project in 2026.

Name: Entrepreneurial Women of Impact Awards
Description: The Entrepreneurial Women of Impact Awards, presented by Women Presidents Organization (WPO) and Women Elevating Women (WEW), recognize outstanding women of color entrepreneurs who have built successful businesses and demonstrated meaningful leadership and community impact. The 2026 awards will honor 24 entrepreneurs across three revenue categories—$500K–$1M, $1M–$10M, and $10M+.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Be an entrepreneur who owns a privately held, for-profit business
Be the CEO or President of that business
Identify as a Woman of Color
Be based in North America
Have generated at least $500,000 USD in revenue during 2025
Fall into one of the three revenue categories:
$500,000–$1 million
$1 million–$10 million
$10 million+
Not be a previous recipient of the award.

Name: Delaware EDGE Grant Competition - Entrepreneurship Track
Description: Delaware’s EDGE (Encouraging Development, Growth & Expansion) Grant Competition provides matching grants to small Delaware businesses to help them expand, become more sustainable, and create jobs. It has separate Entrepreneur and STEM tracks, with awards determined partly by finalists’ pitch presentations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Majority located in Delaware; <7 years in business, ≤15 full-time employees, <$700K in assets; requires 3:1 state-to-business match.

Name: 2026 Holiday Marketplace by Grid110 & SHOPLINE
Description: The Grid110 and SHOPLINE Holiday Marketplace Program will select more than 40 product-based businesses to receive up to $20,000 in grant funding, hands-on e-commerce development, brand and merchandising training, and the opportunity to showcase their products to thousands of shoppers at a three-day holiday marketplace in Los Angeles. It is designed for established consumer brands in categories such as food and beverage, fashion, beauty, home goods, and CPG, with participation requiring founders to migrate their online store and POS system to SHOPLINE and actively engage in the program through December.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who is this program for:

Industries: Consumer packaged goods, fashion, beauty, home goods, food & beverage, and adjacent product categories
Revenue: Minimum $250K - 500K GMV. If you're below this threshold, we still encourage you to apply. We'll also consider factors such as POS sales, business traction, and growth potential
Business model: Best suited for founders selling directly to consumers through e-commerce, retail, or point-of-sale channels
Commitment: Accepted founders are expected to actively participate in the program from August through December and attend the Holiday Marketplace, which will take place during the first two weeks of December 2026
Industry: Consumer Packaged Goods,Beauty & Personal Care,Apparel & Accessories,Food & Beverage

Name: Ewing Marion Kauffman Capacity Building Grant Opportunity
Description: The Kauffman Foundation’s Capacity Building Grants provide one-time funding to organizations that need to strengthen internal capacity—such as leadership, staffing, technology, evaluation, strategic planning, communications, financial planning, or operating systems. The 2026 round is specifically designed around the Foundation’s priorities of college access and completion, workforce and career development, and entrepreneurship.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Nonprofit/charitable organization meeting Kauffman requirements.
Must align with Kauffman’s strategic priorities.
Must have a specific organizational capacity gap.
Funding is for internal organizational effectiveness—not simply funding a new program.
Grant request must be ≤1/3 of organizational budget.
The 2026 application specifically asks applicants to select among college access, workforce/career development, and entrepreneurship.

Name: The Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy
Description: The Milken-Motsepe Prize in Circular Economy offers $2 million in total awards, including a $1 million grand prize, to scalable, technology-enabled companies advancing circular economy solutions across Africa. Eligible businesses must already be operating on the continent and demonstrate commercial viability, measurable environmental and social impact, job creation, and readiness to deploy significant growth capital; selected teams also receive milestone awards, networking, and opportunities to pitch industry leaders.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
