We are seeking companies that meet the following eligibility requirements: 

Over 2 years of continuous operation 
Over $500k in revenue and raised capital 
Institutional, corporate, and/or public‑sector partnerships 
Solution currently deployed on the African continent 
Clear evidence of social impact and job creation 
Demonstrated operational readiness to deploy $1M+ in funding

Name: Southern Documentary Fund Production Grant
Description: The Southern Documentary Fund’s Production Grant provides direct funding and mentorship to documentary filmmakers working in or about the American South. The grant supports nonfiction projects that are already in production and aims to elevate Southern makers and stories that are often overlooked.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Project director must reside in or have deep roots in AL, AR, FL, GA, KY, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN, VA, or WV; project must be a nonfiction documentary currently in production. Applicants cannot be enrolled in film school or applying for a student project.

Name: 2026 Pennovation Accelerator
Description: The 2026 Pennovation Accelerator is a free six-week program for Philadelphia-area pre-seed to seed startups with a proof of concept, offering mentorship, expert-led training, networking, workspace benefits, and a final investor Pitch Day. Up to 12 companies will be selected; participants give up no equity, and Pitch Day winners will receive cash prizes plus additional Pennovation benefits.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Ideal applicants meet the following criteria
- Stage: Pre-Seed to Seed with Proof of Concept
- Capital Raised: Less than $500k

Industries include (but are not limited to)
- Health Tech & Med Tech
- AI & Robotics
- CPG with a Tech Focus
- Food Tech & AgTech
- Smart Cities & IOT

Name: Baltimore Restaurant Accelerator Program
Description: The Greater Baltimore Urban League runs an eight-to-ten-week accelerator for food and beverage entrepreneurs, delivered through in-person sessions on operations, customer service, finance, real estate, restaurant management, and supply chain. Participants receive personalized coaching and compete in a pitch competition across restaurant, caterer, food truck, and beverage categories. The program grew out of the PepsiCo Foundation and National Urban League Black Restaurant Accelerator.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Caterers, food truck owners, brick-and-mortar restaurants, ghost kitchen chefs, and beverage entrepreneurs
- In business at least two years
- Based in the Greater Baltimore area
- Pitch competition categories: brick-and-mortar restaurant, caterer, food truck, beverage business
- $100 entry fee
- Two businesses are additionally selected for National Urban League grants

Apply by September 21, 2026. $25,000 in total prizes: 1st $10,000, 2nd $6,000, 3rd $4,000, 4th $2,500, 5th $2,500. Program includes required in-person sessions and a "Taste of RAP" graduation event. Part of the National Urban League / PepsiCo Foundation Restaurant Accelerator, run by the Greater Baltimore Urban League in its 100th anniversary year. Sponsors: Wells Fargo, La Chow, Giant, TD Bank.

Name: Greatness Grant
Description: The Greatness Grant is a $1,000 business grant given out every quarter by entrepreneur Nehemiah Davis. The grant program is designed to help aspiring or new business owners who need financial support to kickstart their journey.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Anyone with a clear business idea or early-stage business is eligible to apply, regardless of industry or background. But, we must see that you have a solid foundation to work off of.

Name: Chicago Fifth Star Funds
Description: Fifth Star Funds is accepting applications to invest $25,000 in Friends & Family–stage, tech-enabled startups headquartered in Chicago, led by at least one founder who has faced racial discrimination in accessing capital. Eligible companies must have raised less than $25,000 in prior equity and will receive funding via a SAFE with a $4M post-money valuation cap and 20% discount.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We invest in startups that meet all of the following criteria:
- At least one co-founder who has faced material barriers to accessing capital due to racial discrimination
- Headquartered in Chicago
- Friends & Family stage
- Tech-enabled software business with the potential for venture scale
- Less than $25,000 previously raised in equity capital (wired equity investments only; verbal commitments and non-dilutive grants do not count)
- Corporation or LLC business entity

Name: Wharton Africa Business Form New Venture Competition
Description: The WABF33 New Venture Competition gives five early-stage ventures with a direct connection to Africa the opportunity to pitch at the Wharton Africa Business Forum in Philadelphia on November 6-7, gain exposure to leading founders and investors, and compete for non-dilutive funding. Eligible companies must have fewer than 50 employees and less than $250,000 raised, with applicants evaluated on team strength, market traction, business model, scalability, communication, and measurable impact on African communities. Businesses must have a direct link to Africa (but can be headquartered outside of Africa).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Ventures that meet the following criteria are welcome to apply: 

Fewer than 50 full-time employees
Less than $250,000 raised to date
Business must have a direct link to Africa (but can be headquartered outside of Africa)

More details: https://www.instagram.com/whartonabf/?g=5

Name: LISC and DICK'S Sporting Goods Foundation Game On–Community Places to Play Initiative
Description: The Game On–Community Places to Play Initiative is a partnership between LISC and the DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation supporting renovations and improvements to youth sports facilities in under-resourced communities. Grants have supported projects such as courts, fields, lighting, bleachers, locker rooms, fencing, and other athletic infrastructure, with LISC also providing technical assistance.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Primarily nonprofit community-based organizations leading youth sports facility renovation projects; schools and parks/recreation departments may participate in partnership with nonprofits. Past rounds targeted under-resourced communities.

Name: FL Don Quijote Awards
Description: The Don Quijote Awards recognize outstanding Hispanic entrepreneurs, professionals, and community leaders in Central Florida for leadership, innovation, business success, and community impact. Categories include Hispanic Micro-Enterprise of the Year, Hispanic Enterprise of the Year, Professional of the Year, Excellence, Hispanic Community Champion, and Lifetime Achievement.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Central Florida Hispanic entrepreneurs, businesses, professionals, and leaders; some categories have specific criteria. Self-nominations are allowed.

Name: South Chicago TechRise Pitch Competition
Description: The TechRise South Chicago Pitch Competition will select five small businesses rooted in the South Chicago neighborhood to complete a free four-week accelerator and pitch live for $25,000 in non-dilutive funding. The opportunity is designed for early-stage founders looking to use technology to support their next stage of growth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who should apply:
- Businesses in or rooted in the South Chicago neighborhood
- Founders growing a side business into their full-time venture, at the early stage and ready to grow
- Founders ready to use technology to grow their business

Name: Trusted Creator Fellowship
Description: The News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship is a virtual program for U.S.-based independent creators who share community-focused information and want to strengthen skills such as fact-checking, sourcing, and interviewing. Participants meet weekly, apply what they learn to their own platforms, gain access to a peer and alumni network, and receive a $5,000 stipend upon completing the program.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
We’re looking for independent creators who provide a service to their community, whether that’s restaurant openings, public health information, parenting discussions, or local stories. If you create content that informs or connects people, this program will teach you the tactical skills to ensure you are disseminating accurate information.

Creators only need an engaged following on a digital platform (i.e. Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Substack, YouTube, etc.), and a focus on providing information-based services to a specific community.

For the Fall 2026 cohort, we are reserving three seats for current college students. See below for more information.

Name: Literary Art Fund
Description: The Literary Arts Fund supports U.S. nonprofit literary organizations with grants for innovative projects that address structural or infrastructural challenges facing the literary-arts field. The 2026 Innovation Project Grants specifically fund new, one-time projects that strengthen nonprofits’ ability to serve creative writers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
U.S.-based independent literary nonprofits, fiscally sponsored literary organizations, or publishers; generally 3+ years old, stable leadership, and $50K+ annual operating budget. Must primarily serve adult creative writers.
Additional info: Projects must begin after Jan. 1 and end by Dec. 31, 2027. Generative AI cannot be used to produce the application narrative.

Name: The Sky Is Not The Limit Social Impact Grant
Description: The Sky Is Not the Limit Social Impact Grant provides one mission-driven organization with up to $10,000 in design, marketing, and AI services from Bombshell Impact. Open to social impact organizations worldwide, the award is intended to strengthen the winner’s brand, expand its reach, improve its digital presence, and amplify the impact of its work.

Name: Baltimore Charm City Live Vendor Application
Description: Charm City Live is a free, large-scale Baltimore music and community festival featuring live entertainment, children's activities, local businesses, food vendors, retailers, community organizations, and a job fair. The vendor application is for businesses that want to sell food or merchandise at the September 5, 2026 festival at War Memorial Plaza.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to food and merchandise vendors, including stationary and mobile vendors. Selected vendors must have Maryland sales & use tax registration, provide $1 million minimum insurance coverage, and food vendors must meet applicable food-permit requirements. Vendor spaces are limited.
Application Fee:
$125 — stationary 10×10 vendor
$150 — stationary 10×15 vendor
$225 — food/ice-cream/merchandise trucks, trailers

Name: Oklahoma Regional Startup World Cup
Description: The Startup World Cup is a global startup pitch competition, and Gradient is hosting the Oklahoma Regional on September 24, 2026. Ten selected startups will pitch live, with the regional winner advancing to the San Francisco Global Finale for the chance to compete for a $1 million investment prize.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Startups in any industry and at any stage can apply, but the startup must be a legal entity rather than just an idea. There is no restriction on how much capital the startup has raised, and startups may apply to multiple regional competitions unless they have already won a regional competition. Selection considers innovation, market opportunity, team, traction, scalability, and investment potential.

Name: Berkeley SkyDeck Accelerator
Description: A 6-month program for startups worldwide, with priority for UC-affiliated and international founders. Cohort teams (20–25 selected) receive a $200K investment, dedicated workspace, a Lead Advisor, and the opportunity to pitch at Demo Day. All teams access 600+ advisors, $750K+ in in-kind resources, weekly events, and Berkeley’s extensive industry and alumni networks.

Name: Rare Beauty x JCPenney LIFT Beauty Accelerator
Description: The LIFT Beauty Accelerator supports three early-stage, U.S.-based beauty brands led by founders from underrepresented communities. Each selected brand receives at least $10,000 in non-dilutive funding, practical mentorship, more than $24,000 in in-kind testing and design services, and the opportunity to pitch JCPenney for potential retail distribution.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This program is exclusively for beauty brands that meet the following criteria:

Applicant is 18+, from an underrepresented background in the beauty industry
Company is US-incorporated
Early stage – no institutional funding, limited distribution, less than $1m revenue
Beauty products (cosmetics, skincare, haircare, fragrance, etc.) at least at prototype stage
Previous applicants, excluding winners, are welcome to re-apply.
Please note: This program is not intended for service-based beauty businesses such as salons, spas, or individual beauty service providers.

Name: Black Women Photographers x Nikon Grant Program
Description: The BWP × Nikon Grant Fund is a year-long program supporting Black and African women photographers and visual storytellers with cash and professional camera equipment. The 2026 program has four quarterly opportunities, making it possible for creators to apply throughout the year.
Amount: $2,500 cash + Nikon Z6III 24–70mm f/4 lens kit
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Black and African women creatives/photographers; specific application requirements apply.

Name: Coefficient Giving RFP: Global Health and Wellbeing in an Era of Transformative AI
Description: This major RFP supports research, policy development, implementation, and field-building focused on how transformative AI could affect global health and economic wellbeing. Coefficient is particularly interested in work benefiting low- and middle-income countries, new organizations, and projects with a clear path from research to real-world impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individuals, universities, think tanks, nonprofits, and appropriately structured for-profits; global applicants welcome

Name: StartOut Spark Lab Incubator
Description: Spark Lab is a virtual incubator for early-stage LGBTQ+ founders who have launched a business and demonstrated initial market demand. The eight-week program provides expert mentorship, strategic workshops, peer networking, and support toward creating an investor-ready business plan.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: LGBTQ+ founders; for-profit, scalable startup; MVP developed; at least $50K annual revenue or comparable funding; U.S. subsidiary required.

Name: California Voices Emerging Creator Fellowship
Description: The Emerging Creator Fellowship supports rising Asian American and Latino creators in California who make content across areas such as food, fitness, gaming, music, parenting, technology, and self-improvement. Over three months, fellows receive a monthly stipend, creator training, content coaching, and opportunities to develop content that engages audiences with issues shaping California.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Designed for rising Asian American and Latino creators producing audience-facing content across a broad range of topics. Fellows are expected to create content engaging their audiences around issues affecting California.

Name: FY26 Ward 8 Community Investment Fund (Ward8CIF) Grant Program
Description: The DC Department of Small and Local Business Development (DSLBD) created Ward8CIF to provide capital to operating businesses based in Ward 8 and support sustainable growth and business viability. FY26 has two tracks: BOSS for businesses that completed required Back Office Support training, and Contract & Procurement Ready for eligible Certified Business Enterprises (CBEs).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be operating Ward 8-based businesses. The BOSS track requires completion of DSLBD's BOSS training; the Contract & Procurement Ready track requires an active CBE certification plus completion of the required contract/procurement training. Reimbursable expenses must have been incurred between October 1, 2025 and June 29, 2026.

Name: Portland Crafty Wonderland Holiday Art + Craft Market Vendor Application
Description: Crafty Wonderland is a large curated art and craft market featuring 200+ booths of handmade goods and art at the Oregon Convention Center. The Holiday Market gives independent artists and makers an opportunity to sell directly to holiday shoppers and be featured in the event's digital program.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Products must be handmade or hand-altered by the vendor; mass-produced/imported goods and MLM products are prohibited. Original prints and clothing featuring your own art are allowed, but AI-generated art cannot be sold. Specialty packaged foods may be accepted in limited numbers, and alcohol vendors need the required OLCC permits and insurance. Booth sharing is permitted for up to two vendors, who must apply together.
Application Fee: $10 (Booth fees are $425 for a 5' × 10' booth or $575 for a 10' × 10' booth)

Name: Amika Rooted in Growth Grant Program
Description: The Rooted in Growth Grant and Mentorship Program will award four U.S.-based hair care businesses $50,000 in flexible funding, along with strategic mentorship, industry networking, and brand visibility through Amika and the Fifteen Percent Pledge. The program is designed for underserved founders with less than $2.5 million in annual revenue who are building inclusive consumer hair care brands and want to expand into professional distribution channels.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Currently sold to or aspire to expand into professional distribution channels (e.g. salon distributors, direct-to-stylist, etc.)
U.S.-based with annual revenue under $2.5M
At least 51% owned by underserved founder(s)
Operate in the hair care space (tools, wigs, color, extensions, products)
Currently sell a CPG product
Create products that reflect inclusive values and consumer needs
Ready to share their story and engage in mentorship and brand-building opportunities.
Able to travel to NYC October 20, 2026 for in-person program kick-off and participate in a spring 2027 industry trade show
Available three times a month virtually for the mentorship program from October-February 
Demonstrate a clear mission of inclusivity and community impact

Name: DivInc Women in Tech Accelerator
Description: The DivInc Women in Tech Accelerator is a free, 10-week hybrid program for early-stage, women-led U.S. startups building technology or tech-enabled products across any industry. Participants receive intensive support with product-market fit, sales, fundraising, operations, legal readiness, and investor connections, along with more than $100,000 in partner perks and 18 months of post-program support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
U.S.-Based & For-Profit: The company must be a U.S.-based, for-profit enterprise. Non-profits and consulting firms will not be considered at this time.
Women-Led Leadership: The company must be women-led. Co-founders who are not women are highly welcome, but the company must be actively led by a woman, and the CEO must be women-identifying or non-binary.
Technology Framework: All technologies should be powered by AI/ML, SaaS, Data Analytics, or Hardware.
Product Maturity: Founders must be past the pure ideation stage. A mature MVP is not strictly required at entry, but you must have a clear path to launch, pilot, enter beta testing, or have an MVP ready for immediate use by the end of the program (including working prototypes for hardware).
Founder Mindset: We look for founders who possess a growth mindset, are highly coachable, hold a massive vision, and want to collaborate deeply with others. Coachability is key.
Time Commitment: The CEO must personally participate in the program and commit to 25 to 30 hours per week of focused work on their company and sessions.

Name: Main Street Rising Tour - Miami
Description: The Main Street Rising Tour Miami Pitch Competition gives selected small business owners the opportunity to pitch live to Hello Alice and partner judges for a cash grant to reinvest in their business. The competition is part of a free small business event that also provides practical AI training, networking, a six-week virtual accelerator, and potential consideration for the National Main Street Rising Awards.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Businesses operating in Florida
- Have a venture-scalable or venture-viable product or service as defined here; and
- Be fully operational (actively conducting business and generating revenue) and tech-enabled (utilizing digital tools, platforms, or systems to support core business operations)

Name: NC Idea Micro Grant
Description: The NC IDEA MICRO Grant provides North Carolina startups with $10,000 in project-based funding to validate key business assumptions, strengthen their business model, and reach measurable milestones. Recipients also complete an eight-week customer discovery and product launch program, receive guidance from NC IDEA staff, and gain access to mentors, funders, partners, and potential customers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Geography
NC IDEA MICRO grants are specifically targeted at companies headquartered in and that conduct a majority of corporate operations in the State of North Carolina. All publicly facing materials, including website, social media, and other marketing materials and channels should identify the business as a North Carolina company. Selected companies must agree to maintain the majority of corporate operations in the State of North Carolina for at least the 12-month period following completion of the grant.

Industry and Company Type
NC IDEA MICRO grants are awarded to companies bringing an innovative product or business model to the market. We prefer companies with proprietary intellectual property or other means of sustained competitive advantage that are solving large problems.

Companies with high capital requirements and a long runway to commercialization, such as pharmaceutical companies, are not eligible. For a full list of company types considered out of scope for grant funding, please refer to this document.

Market Opportunity
NC IDEA MICRO grants are awarded to companies addressing large, rapidly growing market opportunities with a unique value proposition and demonstrating a clear path to scale—either through venture capital within four years or by achieving $2M+ in annual revenue within seven years with potential to exceed $10M+.

Stage of Development
Competitive applicants have already been actively moving their startup forward by conducting customer discovery, developing initial prototypes, testing a product/service, bringing in initial revenue, or other activities. The grant will enable these companies to validate key assumption(s) around the existence of a problem, revenue model, size of their target market, market readiness, team skill set, or other area(s) to determine a company’s ability to catalyze its business development.

Revenue
Competitive applicants are on a path to generate revenue within 12 months of receiving a MICRO grant. However, many MICRO grant recipients have initial revenue when they apply (see below). 

Note: Consumer packaged goods must have revenue to be eligible for NC IDEA MICRO and SEED. Food and beverage companies must have an annual revenue of at least $5,000 to be eligible for MICRO and $75,000 to be eligible for SEED.

MICRO Grant Recipients: Last 12 Months Revenue at Time of Application
Cleantech, Biotech, Medical Device & Diagnostics
Generating Revenue: 20%
Consumer Products – Food and Beverage
Generating Revenue: 100%
Average Revenue $37K
Consumer Products – Advanced Manufacturing, Advanced Materials, IoT
Generating Revenue: 10%
Consumer Products – All Other
Generating Revenue: 100%
Average Revenue $37K
Software
Generating Revenue: 32%
Team
Applicants must have at least one founder living in North Carolina, and it is preferred that all founders live in NC. Competitive applicants should have a founder in NC who will be full-time within 6-12 months of applying for the grant. NC IDEA defines a full-time founder as one who works 40+ hours a week on their startup and does not spend more than 15 hours a week, either 1) working at another company; 2) working at a different startup run by the founder(s); or 3) on school-related activities (including class time and homework).

Prior Investment
Our funding is intended to help early stage companies accomplish specific milestones that demonstrate to investors and other funding sources that the company has high growth potential. Therefore, companies that have received greater than $250K in equity investment or over $1M in non-dilutive grant funding at the time of applying are less likely to be considered. Founder contributions and “friends and family” equity funding is viewed differently and will not negatively impact consideration.

Since MICRO competitive companies are at the stage of validating assumptions about their business and developing a business model, few MICRO grant recipients have prior equity investment (15% for 2022-2025). For MICRO applicants that have raised equity investment, competitive applicants will detail how past funding was used and how MICRO can still be impactful on the business.

Impact of Grant
Since NC IDEA has two MICRO grant cycles every year, NC IDEA and its reviewers assess the timing and impact for each company to receive $10K and participate in programming during a specific grant cycle.

Competitive applicants will clearly describe how MICRO funds will be used to achieve measurable milestones during the grant period to validate key assumptions about the company’s business, such as revenue model, market readiness, customer profile, and sales. The goal of MICRO is for a startup to move its business forward to be competitive for SEED within 2 years; or to secure growth through other channels, such as revenue, debt, or equity investment.

Name: SF/Oakland Grassroots Artists Advocacy Program (GAAP)
Description: The Grassroots Artists Advocacy Program (GAAP) is a cohort-based fellowship program that supports diverse artists, culture bearers, and creative workers with an artistic or cultural practice who live or work in Oakland or San Francisco. Fellows engage in advocacy and policy development to help artists and culture bearers thrive.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Age: 18 years or older
Location: Live or work in Oakland or San Francisco
Language: Proficiency in English (curriculum presented in English)
Identify as one or more of the following: (1) Artist with an artistic or creative practice (2) Culture bearer with cultural transmission or preservation experience (3) Creative worker with artistic/creative practice or cultural transmission or preservation experience

Name: Verizon Digital Ready AI Accelerator
Description: The Digital Ready AI Accelerator is a 12-week program for small-business owners learning how to apply AI to practical business challenges. Participants receive expert-led workshops, small-group coaching, access to AI tools, personalized mentoring, and help creating an actionable AI implementation roadmap.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small-business owners ready to identify and implement AI opportunities in their businesses.

Name: Portland Bazaar Vendor Application
Description: Portland Bazaar is a highly curated holiday shopping event featuring 160+ artists, makers, and small businesses selling products directly to shoppers. The 2026 season includes the flagship Portland Bazaar in December, plus Spring and European Bazaar events.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Designed for artists, makers, and small businesses whose products fit the Bazaar's curated mix of food, beverage, art, design, and retail. The organizers receive 1,500+ applications annually and curate the vendor lineup; selected vendors must carry their own insurance.

Name: CAFE Fintech Accelerator — Center for Accelerating Financial Equity
Description: CAFE’s Fintech Accelerator is a two-month, equity-free accelerator for mission-driven fintech startups that are already in market and ready to scale. Founders receive direct exposure to financial institutions, investors, regulators, and industry experts, along with coaching on customer acquisition, fundraising, compliance, risk management, and selling to financial institutions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Technology company based in the United States,
With a built product in-market,
And an initial customer base (including selling to financial institutions);
Employing a full-time founding team,
With a product that improves people’s financial lives, especially low- to moderate- income (LMI) individuals.
Founders must commit to 3 days in Newark, DE during the program.

Name: Purple Line Small Business Grant Program
Description: Operated by the Maryland Department of Transportation, this program provides grants to small businesses located along the Purple Line corridor that are impacted by construction.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for a grant, a business must meet all of the following requirements:

Business Status

1. Be an existing business in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation.  Documentation that the business is Active and in Good Standing with the State can be obtained from the Maryland Business Express website. A screenshot of the results will suffice, a formal certificate of good standing is not required.

2. The business must also be in good standing with all federal and State taxing and licensing authorities.  Grant payments are subject to interception by the IRS and/or Maryland Comptroller if outstanding debts are owed to the federal or State government.

3. The business must have been open and operational at its current location along the Purple Line alignment prior to July 1, 2023.  The business must currently be open to customers.

Location

The business must interact directly with customers primarily onsite at a business location that is within one-quarter mile of the existing or future Purple Line Light Rail tracks.  Businesses at residential locations are not eligible.

Small Business

Must be a small business, defined as one of the following:

·         An entity with 50 or fewer employees in the most recently completed fiscal year; AND

·         An entity whose annual gross sales did not exceed $2,000,000 in its most recently completed five fiscal years.

Prioritization of Funding

This is a highly competitive grant program and not all eligible applicants will receive grants. Grant awards to eligible businesses will be prioritized based on the location of the business and its proximity to the most significant construction impacts in the previous six months or anticipated for the next six months.  Grant amounts will vary based on business size and location.  All grant award decisions are final.

Name: Goldman Sachs One Million Black Women: Black in Business
Description: Goldman Sachs' Black in Business program is a free 12-week online business education initiative for sole proprietors, developed with NYU Stern, covering topics like marketing, financial planning, pricing, and access to capital. The program includes in-person learning at Goldman Sachs headquarters in NYC (all expenses paid), a powerful network, and strategic advisors to guide growth. Eligible applicants must have no full-time employees, at least one year of operation, and a minimum of $25,000 in revenue over the past 12 months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The program is open to all sole proprietors interested in creating jobs, opportunity, and economic growth in their communities.

Specific eligibility requirements:
- Sole proprietorship (no other full-time employees)
- Minimum revenue of $25,000 in the past 12 months
- Revenue-generating business
- Operating for at least one year

Name: Community Action Research Initiative (CARI) Grants
Description: The Community Action Research Initiative (CARI) Grants provide up to $3,000 for projects that use sociological knowledge and methods to address community-based problems in partnership with a community organization or action initiative. Eligible applicants must hold a PhD in sociology or be enrolled in a PhD-granting sociology graduate program; ASA membership is not required to apply but is required to receive funding.

Name: The Hatchery Chicago Incubation Cohort
Description: The Hatchery Chicago's Incubation Program is a four-month accelerator that helps early-stage food and beverage entrepreneurs launch consumer packaged goods businesses, from concept to market. Participants receive business planning support, licensing guidance, branding assistance, coaching, networking opportunities, educational classes, and access to industry experts to prepare for a successful product launch.

Name: Newark Alliance Small Business Support Pilot
Description: Newark Alliance’s pilot program provides grants and technical assistance to help small retail businesses in downtown Newark stabilize existing storefronts, attract customers, and activate the Halsey Street corridor and surrounding neighborhoods. It includes two funding tracks: a facility fit-out subsidy for businesses locating downtown and a product purchase subsidy for new or early-stage businesses.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Retail businesses with 20 or fewer employees; must be in the Newark Downtown District, with priority for Halsey Street and nearby blocks. Applicants cannot be landlords, and national or regional chains are excluded unless locally owned; businesses must meet the NJ SBA small business definition, be in good standing with NJ DOL, have no pending legal actions, and be current on tax filings.

Name: Promise Fund Imagine Award
Description: The Promise Fund invests in early-stage innovators developing community-rooted solutions for children ages 0–5 and their families. Its 2026 Imagine Award provides unrestricted funding plus a six-month learning cohort, while the larger Build Award provides substantial unrestricted funding and a year of capacity-building support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-childhood leaders with ideas focused on children ages 0–5 and their parents/caregivers/families; community-connected, equity-driven, transformative solutions prioritized.

Name: Prince George’s County Historic Property Grant Program
Description: The Historic Property Grant Program funds the rehabilitation, restoration, preservation, and acquisition of historic properties in Prince George’s County, Maryland. The county also offers a separate Non-Capital Grant Program for preservation education, research, planning, design, and community partnerships.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible historic-property owners/projects meeting county preservation requirements; FY2027 guidelines determine specific applicant/property eligibility.

Name: Belonging In Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund
Description: This fund supports Oakland-based collaborations between cultural/arts organizations and social-change organizations working toward racial justice and a more equitable Oakland. Funded collaborations develop and test community-rooted ideas, narratives, policy approaches, or structures that could create lasting civic change.
Amount: $100,000/year for 3 years + $12,000/year artist/cultural practitioner stipend + up to $25,000/year for research/documentation
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Oakland-based 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or fiscally sponsored organization with an operating budget of at least $500,000, collaborating with an appropriate cultural/arts or social-change organization. The collaboration must be deeply rooted in an Oakland community and involve civic-facing artists/cultural practitioners.
Important: This is not an individual artist grant; it requires an organizational collaboration.
Application process: Eligibility quiz → Letter of Interest → up to 10 invited to full proposal → 3 awards.

Name: Miami-Dade MDEAT Pitch Fest
Description: Pitch Fest is a business pitch competition run by the Miami-Dade Economic Advocacy Trust. Entrepreneurs with an innovative business idea or an established business ready for its next stage of growth compete for $30,000 in total prize funding, awarded as $15,000, $10,000, and $5,000 for first through third place. Applicants may attend free virtual pitch workshops before the live competition.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Applicant at least 18 years of age
- Business must have a physical location in Miami-Dade County
- Business operating at least 3 years, verified via Sunbiz.org
- Average gross revenue between $24,000 and $750,000 over the past 3 years
- Fewer than 25 employees
- Active Local Business Tax Receipt, IRS EIN documentation, and valid driver's license required
- Not in default or non-compliance with any county loan or grant program
- Franchises and businesses affiliated with national chains are ineligible

$30,000 total prize pool: 1st $15,000, 2nd $10,000, 3rd $5,000. Applications Aug 3-28; free virtual pitch workshops Aug 5-6; live competition Sept 9.

Name: Hey Helen Grant
Description: The Hey Helen Grant gives $10,000 in financial support to women founders building impactful, mission-driven businesses in the U.S. Funds can be used for operations, growth, marketing, hiring, or infrastructure.

Name: Sengo Pitch Competition
Description: Sengo runs a monthly live pitch competition where founders present to investors, executives, and exited founders for feedback, connections, and $1K+ in prizes. Founders can join free for limited first-come spots or pay for priority access, grant eligibility, investor introductions, and community resources.

Name: Money Moves Pitch Competition
Description: The Money Moves Pitch Competition, presented by JCPenney, awards $10,000 in total cash prizes to three U.S.-based, woman-owned businesses, with awards of $5,000, $3,500, and $1,500. Finalists also receive personalized coaching, mentorship, and opportunities to showcase their businesses as part of the Money Moves Summit, and both product- and service-based businesses – including those still in the idea stage – may apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: To be eligible, businesses must be a woman-owned business in the United States. Both service-based and product-based businesses, including those in the ideation phase, are encouraged to apply.

Name: Fort Worth Innovation Challenge
Description: The Fort Worth Innovation Challenge offers up to $200,000 in support for local nonprofits in Tarrant County developing innovative solutions to strengthen families, support kinship care, and help children flourish. The program is focused on community-led ideas, and selected organizations can use the funding to advance work that improves outcomes for children and families in Fort Worth.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Intended for local nonprofit organizations in Tarrant County with innovative solutions focused on family strengthening, kinship care, and child flourishing.

Name: City of Decatur, Georgia Commercial Façade Improvement Grant
Description: The CFIG helps small businesses and commercial property owners improve the exterior appearance and functionality of their properties in Decatur. Funding can support improvements such as painting, windows and doors, awnings, lighting, signage, and outdoor seating, helping strengthen individual businesses and the broader commercial district.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: mall businesses or commercial property owners; generally ≤25 employees, no more than three Georgia locations, and annual receipts ≤$3.5M for retail/restaurants and personal/professional services. Eligible work includes façade repairs, painting, awnings, windows/doors, lighting, signage, outdoor seating, and similar improvements. Grant covers up to 75% of eligible project costs, with the applicant contributing at least 25%.

Name: City of Decatur, Georgia Commercial Buildout Improvement Grant (CBIG)
Description: The CBIG helps small businesses and commercial property owners fund interior improvements to their commercial spaces. Eligible projects can include flooring, walls, ceilings, HVAC, plumbing, fire-safety systems, ADA improvements, and other buildout costs that make a space more functional and business-ready.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be eligible small businesses or commercial property owners located within the City of Decatur. Businesses generally must have 25 or fewer employees, no more than three Georgia locations, and annual receipts within the program's applicable limits; proposed projects must involve eligible exterior improvements and meet City requirements.

Name: City of Decatur, Georgia Marketing & Digital Connectivity Grant (MDCG)
Description: The MDCG helps Decatur small businesses strengthen their marketing presence and digital capabilities. Funding can support expenses such as branding and logo design, website development, professional photography or video, and digital advertising to help businesses attract and retain customers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: pplicants must be qualifying small businesses located in Decatur and must have held an active City of Decatur business license for at least six months before applying. Proposed expenses must fall within the program's eligible marketing and digital categories and meet the required matching-fund rules.

Name: Michigan Founders Fund Pre-Accelerator
Description: The Michigan Founders Fund Pre-Accelerator, powered by gener8tor, is a 7-week hybrid program helping underrepresented Michigan founders prepare for investment and build scalable companies. Selected startups receive hands-on strategy support, coaching, investor and mentor introductions, pitch opportunities, and direct non-dilutive funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to early-stage companies with local Michigan roots led by founders traditionally underrepresented in venture capital. Eligible founder groups include companies at least 51% owned by women, Black, Latino, Arab, AAPI or Indigenous founders, immigrants, children of immigrants, refugees, LGBTQIA+ people, veterans, disabled people, rural-community members, or people experiencing/having experienced poverty. Founders must be able to attend at least 85% of programming, requiring approximately 5–7 hours/week.

Name: Seattle Gobble Up Vendor Application
Description: Gobble Up is an indoor artisanal food and beverage marketplace produced by Urban Craft Uprising at Magnuson Park Hangar 30 in Seattle. Independently owned Pacific Northwest food, beverage, and food-themed craft businesses apply for booth space to sell to holiday shoppers, restaurateurs, and chefs. Vendors pay booth fees rather than receiving funding, and discounted or full scholarship slots are available through the Greenhouse Program.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Independently owned, Pacific Northwest-based food or beverage company
- Both packaged and prepared food vendors welcome, as well as food trucks
- Vendors of handmade kitchenware, kitchen/restaurant decor, and food-themed crafts also accepted

Booth fees: $275 (5'x10'), $500 (10'x10'), food trucks $175 or 20% of sales, whichever is greater.
Greenhouse Program offers discounted booth fees and full vending scholarships for BIPOC-, veteran-, LGBTQ-, and disability-owned businesses and emerging businesses new to craft shows: https://urbancraftuprising.com/greenhouse-program/

Packaged food booth deadline August 30, 2026 (food truck deadline of August 24 has passed). Notifications September 4. Event: First Bite Night November 13; main show November 14, 2026.

Name: Social Shifters Global Innovation Challenge
Description: The Social Shifters Global Innovation Challenge provides multiple grants of up to $15,000 to youth-led startups and projects already delivering measurable social or environmental impact. Eligible founders ages 18–30 also receive free application support, pitch coaching, access to a global community, and opportunities such as fellowships, paid work, networking, and learning experiences.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Young leaders, innovators and entrepreneurs everywhere are rising up to take action on the social and environmental issues that matter to them most.

If you’re a young founder (18-30 years) leading a project or startup with a focus on social impact – our Global Innovation Challenge is for you.

Name: SpringWell 360 Health Equity Grant
Description: Supports students and professionals leading projects that advance health equity in underserved communities. Open to proposals focused on education, outreach, research, or innovation.

Name: Beasley Detroit Small Business Grant Program
Description: The Beasley Detroit Small Business Grant Program will award 10 Metro Detroit and Southeast Michigan businesses with advertising packages valued at $10,000 each across Beasley Media Group’s radio stations and digital platforms. Designed to help local businesses increase visibility and attract customers, the program is open to companies with less than $5 million in annual revenue that have operated for at least two years, with recipients selected based on growth potential and community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Annual revenue less than $5 million in fiscal year 2025
- Incorporated and active as a business for a minimum of two (2) years
- May not be a business that is a religious institution, in the adult entertainment industry, a government entity, a school, a political affiliation, CBD-related or marijuana-related business.

Name: Black & Brown Founders Empower Growth Fund
Description: The BBF Empower Growth Fund awards four $5,000 micro-grants to underrepresented entrepreneurs with demonstrated revenue who are ready to scale, stabilize, or systematize their businesses. Grant funds can be used for marketing, technology upgrades, website improvements, hiring consultants, automation, or expanding operations, and applicants are evaluated based on their growth potential, business traction, and community impact.

Name: GitLab Foundation Powering Economic Opportunity Fund
Description: A $4 million open call within a two-year, $16 million partnership that funds organizations building workforce pathways into durable, living-wage careers in growing U.S. sectors such as renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, and skilled trades. The fund emphasizes employer partnerships, work-based learning, employer-aligned training, and supports that improve retention and advancement.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to U.S.-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits, fiscally sponsored entities, and other eligible partnerships working to expand access to high-quality jobs in growing sectors. Partnerships with employers, unions, public agencies, and training providers are strongly encouraged; selected organizations will be invited to submit full applications in the fall, with awards expected in early December.

Name: Helpmann Fellowships
Description: Helpmann Fellowships provide emerging creatives with funding for ambitious, self-directed projects that advance their artistic and professional development. Fellows can use the funding for new work, exhibitions, performances, residencies, specialized training, touring, recording, or longer-term professional development.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Emerging artists/creatives residing in South Australia; final-year students or graduates within 5 years of eligible undergraduate/honours study at Adelaide University, Flinders University, University of South Australia, or University of Adelaide

Name: BackBlack Impact Grant
Description: The BackBlack Impact Grant provides funding specifically to Black-led nonprofits, as part of BackBlack’s broader effort to connect Black-led organizations with grants, matching funds, and other philanthropic opportunities. The 2026 program is being offered during Black Philanthropy Month.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligibility varies by opportunity. Most opportunities are available to U.S.-based nonprofits verified as Black-led and Black-benefiting in the BackBlack Directory. Review each opportunity’s requirements before applying.

Name: Older Adult Home Modification Grant Program
Description: HUD (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development)’s Older Adult Home Modification Program funds experienced organizations to make safety and accessibility modifications to homes of low-income older adults, helping them remain safely in their homes and age in place. Projects focus on reducing fall risks, improving accessibility, and addressing functional needs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state/local governments, public housing authorities, and certain other government entities with at least 3 years' experience serving older adults. Individuals and sole proprietorships are ineligible.

Name: 92NY UpTide Accelerator
Description: UpTide is an accelerator for U.S. nonprofits that have developed scalable, replicable models that strengthen community connection and belonging. Participants receive coaching, mentorship, strategic planning, a New York City experience, and an unrestricted grant, with an opportunity for additional funding through the final showcase.
Amount: $5,000 unrestricted grant + opportunity for up to $25,000 additional funding
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 18+, full-time Executive Director/President/CEO of a U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a scalable, replicable model focused on strengthening community ties.

Name: Philadelphia Boost Your Business Program
Description: The City of Philadelphia's Boost Your Business program pairs a structured business education series with a $50,000 forgivable loan awarded to 20 selected companies. Sessions cover securing municipal contracts, increasing revenue, and creating jobs for Philadelphia residents. The loan converts to a grant when a participant attends every session and meets the growth goals stated in its application within one year of completing the program.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Business located in Philadelphia
- Annual revenue of $350,000 or more
- Operating for 2+ years
- Independently owned (independently owned franchises eligible)
- Holds a Commercial Activity License (CAL) plus all required federal, state, and local licenses and permits
- Compliant with local, state, and federal taxes
- Presents a clear budget and growth plan
- Interested in pursuing City of Philadelphia contracts

20 businesses selected. Loan is forgiven on full session attendance plus growth goals met within one year. Apply at https://phila-uyims.formstack.com/forms/boost_your_business_application

Name: Kansas Tourism Marketing Grant
Description: Kansas Tourism awards reimbursement-style grants for new, dedicated tourism advertising and marketing projects that draw visitors to Kansas destinations. Awards cover up to 40 percent of project cost, and applicants must supply at least 60 percent from leveraged assets, half of which may be in-kind. Applications go through a new online grant management system requiring account registration before the form can be started.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Nonprofits with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) status
- FOR-PROFIT organizations (explicitly eligible)
- State, county, city/township and special district governments
- Federally and non-federally recognized tribal organizations
- Minimum 60% leverage required; up to 50% of leverage may be in-kind

Deadline 8/31/2026 11:59 p.m. Account registration in the new system required first. 2025 awards ranged $1,938 - $8,000; no hard maximum is published. Written for DMOs and tourism communities but for-profits are named as eligible.

Name: Reno-Tahoe Airport Concessions RFP (Food & Beverage and Retail)
Description: The Reno-Tahoe Airport Authority has issued RFP 25/26-17 seeking concessionaires to operate food and beverage and retail locations at Reno-Tahoe International Airport, including new space created by the MoreRNO concourse replacement program. Prime concessionaires are expected to partner with smaller local operators and ACDBE-certified firms. Separate solicitations for gaming, advertising and lounge concessions follow later in 2026 and 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Concession operators bidding as prime concessionaires for food & beverage and/or retail packages
- Small and local businesses encouraged to join a prime's team rather than bid alone
- ACDBE (Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprise) participation sought
- Documents via the Authority's solicitations page or NGEM (nevada.ionwave.net); bidders responsible for checking addenda

Due 8/31/2026 at 2:00 p.m. PT. Gaming RFP due 10/27/2026; Advertising Q4 2026/Q1 2027; Lounge Q1 2027. No cash award - this is a multi-year concession lease.

Name: George A. Ramlose Foundation Grant
Description: The Ramlose Foundation funds 501(c)(3) organizations working in early education, human services, special needs and youth development, and gives priority to newer organizations. There is no minimum budget or minimum years-in-operation requirement. The application is a 17-item Google Form requiring financial documents and a project budget; awards are announced by email on or before December 15.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) organizations. No stated minimum budget or years-operating requirement; the funder prioritizes newer organizations. Focus areas: early education, human services, special needs, youth development.

Name: National Household Wasted Food Prevention Project Grant
Description: WWF is administering the National Household Wasted Food Prevention Project, a grant program aimed at reducing household food waste 10% nationally and 20% in supported communities by 2030. Funded by the EPA, the program will pair a national Ad Council media campaign with localized community grants targeting behavior change — things like meal planning, proper food storage, and using leftovers — among parents and adults 18–35. Grants range from $75,000 to $750,000 across roughly 15 awards, with projects running January 2027 through February 2030. Eligible applicants include nonprofits, local and Tribal governments, and educational institutions; for-profit businesses and individuals are not eligible. Applications are due September 1, 2026, with an informational webinar on May 28.

Name: World Summit AI Startup Showcase
Description: The World Summit AI Startup Showcase gives AI startups the opportunity to pitch on the World Summit AI stage before industry judges and an international AI audience. Selected startups receive conference access, networking opportunities, expert feedback, and significant visibility through the Summit's media channels.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Pathfounders Startup Battleground, taking place during World Summit AI 2026 on 7–8 October 2026 at Taets Art & Event Park, Amsterdam.

Name: Shirley Raines Legacy Grant
Description: The Shirley Raines Legacy Grant, created by Beauty 2 The Streetz in memory of founder Shirley Raines, provides unrestricted microgrants to people doing grassroots work supporting individuals experiencing homelessness. The goal is to continue Raines’s community-centered legacy by giving small-scale community leaders flexible funding to strengthen their work.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to individuals and small organizations actively serving people experiencing homelessness in the U.S. No nonprofit/501(c)(3) status, formal organization, or large following is required. Applicants/nominees provide basic contact information, location, a description of their work, photos or a short video, and social media/website links if available.

Name: Naturally New York The Next Fairway Find Pitch Competition
Description: Naturally New York and Fairway Market’s Next Fairway Find Pitch Competition gives emerging CPG brands the chance to pitch directly to Fairway buyers for potential placement in four Manhattan stores and a $12,000 prize package. The competition takes place September 22, 2026 at Fairway’s Upper West Side location; applicants must have an active Naturally New York membership.

Name: Lifting Up Small Businesses in The Bronx
Description: A grant program run by the Bronx Chamber of Commerce with Optimum Business, awarding 25 grants of $5,000 plus one $20,000 grand prize, totaling $145,000, to Bronx small businesses with brick-and-mortar locations. Applicants describe how the funds would support business growth and strengthen their community. All applicants also receive complimentary Bronx Chamber of Commerce membership.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Brick-and-mortar business location in a community served by Optimum
- 10 or fewer employees
- Open and operating for a minimum of 1 year
- Must describe growth plans and community impact in the application
- Must agree to participate in promotional materials for the grant program
- Subject to a background check before funds are disbursed

Application window August 10 - September 1, 2026 (11:59 p.m. ET). Applicants receive 6 months complimentary Bronx Chamber membership; new-member recipients get a full year. Applications submitted at https://www.optimum.com/business/bronx

Name: California Business Launchpad for Food, Farm and Ranch Businesses
Description: UC Agriculture and Natural Resources and the Southwest Regional Food Business Center run a nine-week training program covering business planning, financial literacy, regulatory compliance, and marketing and branding. Participants attend one roughly two-and-a-half-hour virtual session weekly from October through December, plus one-on-one coaching and in-person networking events in Northern, Central and Southern California. Up to forty participants are accepted statewide.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Small to mid-size California farmers, ranchers, fishers, food producers and food business owners
- Business must operate in California
- Seeking help with business finances or operations

Applications 7/15/2026 - 9/1/2026; acceptances notified by 9/10/2026. Cohort runs October-December 2026. Up to 40 seats statewide. Free to participate - no cash award, the value is the training and coaching.

Name: VMFA Aaron Siskind Award for Photography
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents 18 or older working in still photo-based media, with photography as a primary vocation. Targets early- to mid-career artists and established photographers without significant critical recognition. No application fee. Submissions through the Picter portal (opened July 1, 2026) require a CV, artist statement, and 10-15 images. Portal closes September 1, 2026 at 11:59pm EST. Questions: siskindfellowship@vmfa.museum.

Name: Alternative Exposure Grant Program for Bay Area Artist-led Public Projects
Description: Southern Exposure’s Alternative Exposure Round 20 supports Bay Area visual arts projects that present work by multiple artists, with funding available to individuals, collectives, and informal art spaces with annual budgets under $100,000. Projects must be publicly accessible in an eligible Bay Area county, take place between October 1, 2026 and June 30, 2028, and demonstrate artistic strength, community impact, and meaningful support for local artists—particularly those historically excluded from arts institutions.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- The lead organizer must have an address in Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Solano, or Sonoma County. For collectives or groups, additional collaborators may live outside of these counties but the majority of collaborators in the group must live in an eligible county.
- Resulting project activities must be accessible and presented to the public within at least one of the above areas.
- Funded projects must be completed before June 30, 2028 and after October 1, 2026. For projects or programs that are a part of an ongoing project, the work supported by Alternative Exposure should be completed within this timeframe.
- Applicants may be a lead organizer on more than one application, however, in these cases only one of their projects can be selected for funding.
- Applicants that have received Alternative Exposure grants from Rounds 1-17 (2007-2023) are eligible to apply again as lead organizers if the first project was successfully completed and the final report was submitted to Southern Exposure.
- Grantees from Rounds 18 (2024) or 19 (2025) are NOT eligible to apply again as lead organizers in Round 19. However, former grantees (both lead organizers and additional collaborators) from all previous rounds may participate in 2026 applications for new, unrelated projects as collaborators.
- Informally organized groups, collectives, or art spaces with budgets under $100,000 are all eligible to apply.

Name: Unreal Engine Epic MegaGrants
Description: Epic MegaGrants is a funding program from Epic Games that awards grants ranging from $5,000 to $150,000 to solo developers, small teams, and innovators building projects using Unreal Engine, including indie games, Fortnite experiences, open source tools, and film or animation projects. The program is open globally, applicants retain full ownership of their IP, and grants are not limited to U.S.-based creators. The current Cycle 1 submission window closed March 20, 2026, with Cycle 2 submissions opening June 29, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who’s eligible for an Epic

MegaGrant?

Epic MegaGrants are investments Epic Games makes to sponsor the development of exciting projects that may not otherwise have enough funding to fully realize. They’re specifically meant for smaller teams, solo developers, and innovators who are using our technology to bring bold, challenging, and insanely creative dreams to life.

Name: AltaLab Founder Program
Description: AltaLab is a hands-on founder program run by AltaIR Capital, an early-stage VC firm whose portfolio includes Deel, Miro, Turing, and Perplexity. It runs in three stages: a three-week remote Online Sprint, an optional Founder Residency with one-on-one mentorship, and a path to either build-stage support or investment conversations with AltaIR. It serves founders refining an idea, seeking product-market fit, or preparing to raise.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Open to founders at three stages: early idea, working toward product-market fit, or raising with traction
- Applicants may be based anywhere globally; the Online Sprint is fully remote
- A co-founder is not required
- Existing traction is not required
- No participation fee; the program is free

Structure: three-week remote Online Sprint, then an optional Founder Residency with one-on-one mentorship, then either "Build with AltaLab" support or "Scale with AltaIR Capital" investment conversations. Selected teams receive investment offers, with access to funding up to $500K.

Led by Igor Ryabenkiy, founder of AltaIR Capital (400+ companies backed, 10+ unicorns), with Nikita Bogachev as head of AltaLab. Applications due September 4, 2026.

Name: Grand Junction Holiday Fine Art & Craft Fair Vendor Application
Description: The Art Center of Western Colorado holds a juried holiday fine art and craft fair, one of the Grand Valley's few juried fairs, opening with a Friday evening members' preview. Accepted artists sell handmade work from roughly eight-by-six-foot booths, with a table, chairs and electricity available on request. The Art Center retains fifteen percent of gross receipts, settled at the close of the fair.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Artists selling their own handmade work in any medium
- Manufactured, mass-produced and commercial items not eligible
- Juried selection

Application deadline 9/4/2026. $15 non-refundable jury fee. $100 booth fee charged after acceptance, plus 15% commission on gross receipts due at the fair's end. Fair runs 11/20/2026 - 11/22/2026; booth approx 8' x 6'.

Name: Shelby Facade Improvement Grant
Description: The City of Shelby, Ohio offers grants to commercial property owners and business operators in the Shelby Central Business District for exterior storefront improvements. Eligible work includes exterior painting, signage, awnings, facade cleaning or restoration, sidewalks, lighting, storefront security devices, new roofing and related exterior work. Grants are capped at ten thousand dollars per project, subject to committee review, applicant volume and project impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Commercial property owners or businesses operating within the Shelby Central Business District
- Improvements must be located in the CBD (map linked from the city notice)
- One grant per business/storefront annually
- Work must not already be completed
- Award typically capped at $10,000 per project, subject to committee review
- No match requirement is stated

DEADLINE NOTE (resolved 9/7/26): the 2026 round closed September 4, 2026, NOT September 14. The city edited its notice on 8/24/2026 and the official application PDF also states September 4; only the URL slug still says the 14th. The Deadline field has now been corrected to 09-04 and the status set to Closed. DO NOT re-derive this date from the stored URL - the slug is wrong at the source.

Name: LSI 2026 Photography Grant (Leica Society International)
Amount: $7,500 cash plus a Leica camera and lens
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open globally where legally permitted to applicants at least 18 years old by July 24, 2026. Leica camera ownership and LSI membership are not required; LSI officers, directors and past LSI grant recipients may not apply. Theme is "To Be Seen." Submit 10 images plus a project description through Picter. $35 entry fee. Closes September 4, 2026 at 11:59pm CST or when 200 applications are received, whichever comes first. Winners and first runners-up exhibit at the Leica Gallery in Paris, May/June 2027. Contact: richard@madcrouch.com, 972-233-9107 ext. 211.

Name: USI CDFI Bootcamp & Pitch Challenge
Description: Free business development program from Urban Strategies Inc.'s CDFI for for-profit entrepreneurs in participating communities. Participants complete five virtual sessions covering customer discovery, business strategy, financial management, funding, and pitch development, then compete in a local pitch competition. One winner in each participating market receives a $50,000 business prize, with $200,000 awarded across four communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be at least 18, reside in a participating USI community (St. Louis MO, Baltimore MD, Sacramento CA, or Norfolk VA), and own a legally registered for-profit business (LLC, S-Corp, C-Corp, or DBA) or be willing to complete registration with USI's assistance. Five virtual sessions run about 2.5 months, each 60-90 minutes; participants must attend at least four of five (80%) to remain eligible for the Pitch Challenge, with additional points for perfect attendance. No cost to participate — the program is fully funded for accepted participants. Contact: usi-cdfi@usi-inc.org or (314) 325-9736.

Name: Riverside County Altura Foundation Small Business Grant
Description: The Altura Foundation, the charitable arm of Altura Credit Union, awards direct cash grants to locally owned small businesses based in Riverside County, California. Five grants of $10,000 each are available in the 2026 cycle. The program targets established microbusinesses that demonstrate financial stability and provide a valuable product or service to their local community, with emphasis on underserved communities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- For-profit small business based in Riverside County, California
- 10 or fewer employees
- Minimum two years in business
- Demonstrated financial stability
- Provides a valuable product or service to the local community
- Preference for Altura Credit Union members and businesses serving underserved communities

Five grants available for 2026. Application window August 3 - September 7, 2026; awardees announced October 2026. Portal: https://altura-credit-union.wizehive.app/program/altura-foundation-small-business-grant

Name: Seattle Neighborhood Matching Fund
Description: The City of Seattle’s Neighborhood Matching Fund supports grassroots, community-led projects that strengthen neighborhoods and create lasting community improvements. The Community Partnership Fund can support community organizing, public art, park improvements, cultural events, and community facilities, with every award requiring a community match.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Neighborhood groups, community organizations, informal groups, and business groups; must be open/inclusive, significantly composed of people who live/work in Seattle, involve community members, be free/open to the public, and provide a community match.
Community match can include volunteer time, donated materials, professional services, and/or cash. Projects should be ready to begin within 1–2 months of award.

Name: Safety National Safety First Grant Program
Description: Safety National provides funding to policyholders developing innovative solutions to reduce workplace injuries and illnesses. Three policyholders receive dollar-for-dollar matching reimbursement for solutions addressing a quantified workers’ compensation risk.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Safety National will grant a dollar-for-dollar matching reimbursement for the three policyholders with the most creative risk control solutions.

1st Place = $10,000
2nd Place = $5,000
3rd Place = $2,500
The solutions must relate to an identifiable and quantified loss source and nominations must meet the following requirements:

Nominees must be current Safety National workers’ compensation policyholders for the entire timeline of the application and award process.
Nominees must be registered for at least one Safety National MAP Client Services® resource. If not already registered, click here to access the form.
Only one application allowed per policyholder, per application period.
The risk-reducing solutions must apply to workers’ compensation and must include an estimate of injury cost savings that can be anticipated for that policyholder.
Submissions must address pre-injury risk management solutions.
Policyholders must be willing to share the details of the winning solutions for promotional pieces and as a resource to other Safety National policyholders.

Name: The Merchants Fund - City of Philadelphia Stabilization Grant
Description: The Merchants Fund offers Stabilization Grants twice a year to small businesses in Philadelphia with annual revenue between $50,000 and $750,000, prioritizing businesses in historically underserved communities. Eligible businesses must be independently owned, have a physical storefront, have been operating for at least two years, and must not have applied for or received a Stabilization Grant within the past 12 to 24 months. The current spring cycle opened March 15, 2026, with applications accepted through April 15, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Philadelphia only. Business must be independently owned and operated, be the owner's primary source of income, have annual sales between $50,000 and $750,000, have been in operation at least 2 years, and have a physical storefront (food trucks and kiosks permitted). Must be in compliance with all federal, state, and local taxes (or on an approved payment plan), hold required licenses and permits, and demonstrate financial need. Cannot have applied for a Stabilization grant within the last year or received one within the last 24 months. INELIGIBLE: professional services (medical, legal, counseling), graphic design, architecture, real estate, childcare and eldercare, and nonprofits. The fall 2026 cycle opened August 15 and closed September 9, 2026. The program runs twice yearly — spring and fall. No application fee.

Name: Sundance Collab x TikTok Micro-Series Challenge
Description: Sundance Collab and TikTok are running a global challenge for creators working in short-form serialized storytelling. An industry jury selects five finalists, each receiving an unrestricted five thousand dollar grant, a Sundance Collab course package, and a place in an online workshop with a Sundance Collab advisor. Finalists then pitch their series live and online directly to the TikTok team.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants must be 18 or older at time of submission
- One entry per person; multiple entries result in disqualification
- Co-writers/co-creators may submit as a team of up to two via one submission; a winning team SHARES the single $5,000 grant, though each member receives a course package
- All submitted materials must be created by the submitter
- Applications and materials must be in English
- GENERATIVE AI MAY NOT be used to create, develop or revise submissions
- Entries cannot be edited after submission

IMPORTANT: entering grants TikTok a "first-look" opportunity on the series idea. TikTok has 21 days from notification to decide whether to extend an offer.

Submission package required: title, genre, logline, character bios (2-4 characters, max 500 words), synopsis (up to 500 words), script for the first 30 episodes (up to 45 pages, standard screenplay format), and a 1-3 page series bible.

Timeline: submissions opened August 19, 2026; deadline 11:59 p.m. PT September 9, 2026; finalists notified October 30, 2026; online pitch workshop November 3, 2026; finalists pitch event November 6, 2026. Accessibility accommodations via accessibility@sundance.org

Name: Community-Centered Wellness Microgrants
Description: Microgrants from SGA Youth & Family Services, in partnership with the Chicago Department of Public Health, funding Chicago organizations to expand or sustain existing culturally responsive, trauma-informed wellness activities. Eligible activities include health screenings (blood pressure, glucose, cholesterol, BMI, stress, HIV/STD/STI), cancer screening awareness and education, public benefits enrollment assistance, community fitness classes, food access, and job training.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits only — applicants must be a registered 501(c)(3) or apply through a fiscal sponsor. Must be headquartered in Chicago, in good standing with the City of Chicago, hold a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov, contribute matching resources (in-kind support, volunteer hours, or other funding), and have an existing program to enhance or expand. The 2026 round closed September 9, 2026 at 11:59 PM CST; SGA states another funding opportunity is coming in 2027.

Name: Black Fund of Central Texas
Description: The Black Fund of Central Texas provides grants to Black-led organizations in Central Texas working to generate renewed prosperity for Black communities. The current cycle distributes $250,000 across 20 awards, with additional capacity-building support available to applicants who are not selected for funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Location: Nonprofit organizations must operate in one the 6-county Central Texas region: Travis, Bastrop, Burnet, Caldwell, Hays, and Williamson counties.
Tax Status: Organizations must be tax-exempt under Sections 501(c)(3) or 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) of the Internal Revenue Code, a fiscally sponsored project or be a government unit.
Grant Eligibility for Awardees: 2025 Awardees (except Committee Choice Awards participants) are ineligible for funding in this current grant cycle immediately following their award.
Non-Lobbying Advocacy: Organizations that engage in non-lobbying advocacy (e.g., public education, community organizing, policy research) are eligible.
Strategic Alignment: Eligible programs should focus on initiatives that align with the strategies of The Black Fund of Central Texas.
Faith-Based Entities: Eligible programs focus on inclusive community serving capacities, delivering direct community benefits; excluding religious instruction, religious extremism, worship or increasing church memberships.

Name: Texas State Trade Expansion Program (STEP)
Description: The Texas Department of Agriculture administers STEP, an SBA-funded program helping Texas small businesses begin or expand exporting. Funds support export training workshops, state-sponsored trade missions and trade show participation, market analysis, e-commerce and website costs, translation, marketing material design, sales trips and other pre-approved export activities. Applicants must self-certify as an eligible small business concern using a required form.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Texas-based small businesses
- Must qualify as an eligible small business concern and submit the self-representation form
- Activities must be export-related and pre-approved

Applications must be received by 9/10/2026 before 5:00 p.m. Central. Contact: Bradine Griffiths, STEP Director, Grants@TexasAgriculture.gov, 833-380-8282.

Name: Small Business Expo – Las Vegas 2026
Description: Free one-day business-to-business expo and conference at the Plaza Hotel & Casino Convention Center in downtown Las Vegas on September 10, 2026 (10:00am–5:00pm; check-in from 9:30am): workshops and sessions, exhibitor floor, keynote speakers, speed-networking sessions, industry color-coded networking badges, exclusive attendee promotions and free parking. Small Business Expo runs similar events in other U.S. cities (e.g., San Diego, South San Francisco).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Entrepreneurs and small business owners; registration is free and includes full event access.

Name: Makers Future Fund: Bay Area
Description: Nest’s Makers Future Fund: Bay Area, in partnership with Gap Inc., is a six-month program for Bay Area-based handcrafted product businesses that combines financial-readiness training, individualized business coaching, peer community, and a $2,500 grant. Thirty makers will be selected, and participants may also be invited to the 2026 Gap Inc. x Nest Holiday Makers Market and other Gap Inc. engagements.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants must be located in California’s Bay Area.
- Applicants must use a US bank account for managing their business.
- Applicants' businesses must make handcrafted products (i.e., products must be predominantly made by hand, using techniques that involve direct manual effort and craftsmanship). Examples of eligible products include, but are not limited to: textiles, ceramics, jewelry, woodwork, small batch personal care products, etc. 
- While the use of hand tools and electric hand tools are permitted (e.g. heat molds/presses, sewing machines, die-cutting machines, etc.), items produced using industrial machinery or 3D printers are not eligible.

Name: ArtsKC Inspiration Grant
Description: ArtsKC awards Inspiration Grants of $3,500 to individual practicing artists in the five-county Kansas City metro area - Jackson, Clay and Platte counties in Missouri and Johnson and Wyandotte in Kansas. One artist per round also receives the $5,000 Paul Tyler Inspiration Award. Applicants must be 18 or older with established professional achievement; organizations are not eligible.
