Funded projects run September 30, 2026 through March 25, 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists only - organizations are not eligible. 18+; must reside in Jackson, Clay, Platte (MO), Johnson or Wyandotte (KS). One application per year; must sit out one round before reapplying. Round I of the 2026-2027 cycle.

Name: Social Justice Fund's Brooklyn Pitch Competition
Description: The Brooklyn Pitch Competition will award $450,000 in unrestricted grant funding to selected Brooklyn-based businesses, including a $150,000 grand prize and finalist awards of $25,000 to $75,000. Eligible applicants are established businesses headquartered or primarily operating in Brooklyn with $1 million to $5 million in annual revenue, a strong growth strategy, and demonstrated community or economic impact. Finalists will pitch live at Barclays Center in November and receive additional support such as investor introductions, capital matchmaking, advisory sessions, and growth connections.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible businesses should meet the following criteria:
- Be headquartered or primarily operating in Brooklyn
- Generate between $1 million and $5 million in annual revenue
- Demonstrate a clear growth strategy and strong potential for expansion
- Show evidence of innovation, execution capacity, and business momentum
- Contribute to Brooklyn’s economy through job creation, local hiring, community impact, or neighborhood investment
- Be prepared to participate in a competitive screening process and pitch event if selected as a finalist

Name: Delaware EDGE Grant Competition - STEM Track
Description: Delaware’s EDGE (Encouraging Development, Growth & Expansion) Grant Competition provides matching grants to small Delaware businesses to help them expand, become more sustainable, and create jobs. It has separate Entrepreneur and STEM tracks, with awards determined partly by finalists’ pitch presentations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Be majority located in Delaware
Be in business for less than 7 years
Have 15 or fewer full-time employees
Have less than $700K in assets
Have a 3:1 match

Name: Strategic Education, Inc. — Signal Labs
Description: Signal Labs is an edtech innovation and commercial-pilot program connecting proven education-technology companies with Strategic Education and leading education investors. The program is looking for ready-to-scale innovators with existing customers and demonstrated results whose products can expand access to affordable, career-relevant education for working adults and lifelong learners.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Industry: Companies building in higher education and future of work.

 
Stage: Preference for companies with an established product, revenue, and user base.

 
Engagement: At least one member of your core team must be able to work with Strategic Education business specialists.

Name: Impact Kickstart
Description: Impact Kickstart supports underrepresented documentary filmmakers with funding, mentorship, impact-strategy development, and a year-long peer cohort. The program is specifically designed to help feature-length documentaries develop audience-engagement and impact campaigns capable of addressing important social issues
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must be 18+, identify as underrepresented filmmakers, and submit a feature-length documentary (40+ minutes) that is recently completed, finishing at least at fine-cut stage, or in release. The film must be far enough along for Working Films to review a fine cut by the deadline; only one proposal per applicant is allowed. Selected filmmakers participate in monthly cohort meetings from December 2026–December 2027.

Name: NYC Culture & Arts Administrator Mentorship Program
Description: NYC CAAMP is a professional mentorship program designed to support emerging arts and culture administrators in New York City through mentorship, professional development, and connections within NYC's cultural sector. It is intended to help participants build leadership and administrative skills while developing relationships with experienced arts professionals.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Intended for emerging/current arts and culture administrators seeking professional mentorship in NYC's cultural sector. Exact current eligibility requirements should be checked in the application materials.

Name: Alexandria Del Ray Artisans Holiday Market Call for Artists
Description: Del Ray Artisans runs a three-weekend holiday market at the Colasanto Center in Alexandria, Virginia, selecting different artists across varied media for each weekend. All work must be handmade by the artist and originally created within the last three years; reproductions are allowed where the original meets that window. Selected makers sell Friday evenings plus Saturdays and Sundays across December 4-20, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Work must be handmade by the artist and original within the last 3 years. Preference given to Del Ray Artisans members. Different artists selected per weekend by medium. Applications via JotForm link on the call page. Market runs December 4-20, 2026 (Fri 6-9pm, Sat 9am-5pm, Sun 11am-5pm) at Nicholas A. Colasanto Center, 2704 Mount Vernon Ave, Alexandria VA.

Name: IMG Leave Your Mark Grant
Description: Funding opportunity to support social good organizations with global outreach efforts. Five winners will be selected: two organizations will each receive $3,500, and three individuals participating in a mission, volunteer, or service trip will each receive $1,000.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: The Grant is open to adult participants worldwide; you must be at least 18 years of age to enter and not subject to 18 U.S.C. § 1033. Employees of IMG are not eligible to participate in the Grant. No groups, clubs, newsletters or organizations can participate in this Grant on behalf of the group, club or organization. Sponsor reserves the right at its sole discretion to disqualify any individual it finds to be tampering with the operation of the Grant or any website, or to be acting in any manner deemed by Sponsor to be in violation of the rules; or to be acting in any manner deemed by Sponsor to be disruptive, or with intent to annoy, abuse, threaten or harass any other person.

Name: Ignite WBDC Grant Program
Description: The Women's Business Development Council (WBDC) Ignite Grant Program provides competitive $2,500–$10,000 grants to qualified women-owned small businesses in Connecticut for clearly defined projects that will measurably support business growth and profitability. Funds cannot be used for operating expenses, inventory, marketing, salaries, real estate improvements, past purchases, or debt repayment, and applicants generally must have invested at least $2,500 in their business within the past 12 months.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible, the business must:

Be 51% or more woman-owned
Be headquartered in CT, registered in the state of CT, and owned by a CT resident
Have been in business for at least two years before the deadline of the application round, with a record of sales
Have a record of annual sales/revenue in the last twelve months greater than $25,000 and less than $2,000,000
Be in good standing with the CT Department of Revenue Services (DRS)
Have an established business bank account
Currently utilize a formal, digital bookkeeping/financial system (e.g. QuickBooks, Sage, FreshBooks, Wave Accounting)
Be a for-profit business
Be owned by a woman at least 18 years old
Have invested at least $2,500 into the business in the last 12 months, unless the business is located in a distressed municipality
 

The following businesses are not eligible:

Childcare businesses
If your business is in the childcare industry, WBDC has other programs for you. We encourage you to visit our Child Care Business Opportunity Fund page to learn more or reach out to us at childcaregrants@ctwbdc.org. 
Any individual or business that has already received an Ignite Grant, Equity Match Grant, or WBDC Municipal Grant
Non-profit organizations
Businesses established as sole proprietorships
Businesses must be registered as an LLC or other structure.
Current vendors or contractors of WBDC
Former vendors are eligible to apply a year after completing work with the WBDC.
Medical marijuana; liquor stores and alcohol distributors; adult businesses such as strip clubs; vape retailers; tobacco shops and smoking lounges; businesses having to do with gambling; gun stores and ranges; cash advance, check cashing, or pawn shops; bail bonds; collection agencies or services; and auction or bankruptcy or fire or “lost-our-lease” or “going-out-of-business” or similar sale

Name: gBETA Prosper Healthtech
Description: gBETA Prosper Healthtech is a free, seven-week, equity-free pre-accelerator in Birmingham, AL for early-stage Alabama-based healthtech, healthcare, and life sciences startups. Selected companies (up to five per cohort) receive intensive coaching, mentor swarms, investor pitch opportunities, and post-program support to help them scale and prepare for fundraising, though no investment is made during the program. The Spring 2026 cohort runs April 16–June 5, 2026, with applications due March 22, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Startups Primed for Growth: This program is ideal for early-stage healthtech, life sciences, and healthcare-focused startups that want to scale, validate their business model, and prepare for future growth and investment.
- Industry Focused: The program supports innovators across health, healthcare, and life sciences, including software-driven and regulated technologies advancing patient care, research, and healthcare delivery.
- Who this isn’t for? Brick-and-mortar healthcare clinics, traditional service-based businesses, or non-technology healthcare practices.

Name: Stanley 1913 Creators Fund
Description: The Stanley 1913 Creators Fund supports emerging nonprofit leaders with bold ideas for strengthening their communities. Selected organizations receive unrestricted funding to develop and implement innovative ideas, with the fund supporting a broad range of causes and approaches worldwide.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage nonprofits led by emerging leaders; the organization should have an innovative idea that strengthens communities. The fund has supported organizations across a wide range of causes and countries.

Name: Sag Harbor Holiday Makers Market Vendor Call
Description: The Church, an arts center in Sag Harbor, New York, is accepting applications for its sixth annual Holiday Makers Market, a juried two-day selling event for makers, artisans and artists. Selected vendors choose from three booth sizes with tables included and must staff both days using their own point-of-sale system. Applying is free; booth fees are charged only after selection.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Makers, artisans, artists, and retailers of artisanal objects
- Goods made or designed on the East End and/or handcrafted receive priority
- Must commit to both market days and provide own point-of-sale system
- Non-incorporated vendors may need to sign additional liability waivers

Applications due before 5 p.m. 9/13/2026; selections emailed by 9/30/2026. Booth fee due in full by 5 p.m. 10/4/2026 or the space is forfeited. Booths: 8'x5' $150 (one table); 8'x10' $300 (two tables); 16'x5' $300 (two tables). Vendor setup 11/27/2026. Venue: 48 Madison Street, Sag Harbor, NY 11963.

Name: Project W + JPMorganChase Women Entrepreneurs Boot Camp | Consumer Program
Description: The Women Entrepreneurs Boot Camp (WEB) is a one-day intensive program for women founders of seed- and Series A-stage companies, focused on scaling, revenue growth, fundraising, and building investor relationships. The Consumer track specifically supports founders creating products and experiences that improve lives, including sustainable/healthy products, solutions for families on the go, and products for overlooked consumer markets.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Companies that have:

At least one woman founder with a significant equity stake and in a C-suite position

Raised a Seed or Series A round or achieved equivalent traction through revenue growth or alternative funding

Built a business in CPG, apparel, consumer internet, hybrid brick/mortar and online, or scalable “four wall” concept

An experienced team capable of growing the business

Demonstrate strong year-over-year customer and revenue growth

NYC; 10/22/26
Industry: Retail,Beauty & Personal Care,Consumer Packaged Goods,Food & Beverage

Name: Illinois Hispanic Chamber Small Business Microgrant
Description: The Illinois Hispanic Chamber of Commerce Foundation is offering $5,000 microgrants to small businesses affected by immigration enforcement activity, with funding intended to help cover expenses such as rent, payroll, and essential inventory. Phase 1 is open to businesses with 10 or fewer employees in select Chicagoland communities, including Pilsen, Little Village, Back of the Yards, Chicago Lawn/West Lawn, Berwyn/Cicero, and others, and applicants must demonstrate how recent immigration enforcement actions have negatively affected their revenue or operations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Minimum 2 years in operation
- Registered and active with the State of Illinois (LLC or sole proprietor)
- Active business license required
- 10 or fewer employees
- One business/location per owner only
- Must demonstrate how immigration enforcement actions affected the business, with documented revenue loss

Phase 1 communities: Pilsen; Brighton Park / McKinley Park / Archer Heights; Back of the Yards; Little Village; Chicago Lawn / West Lawn; Berwyn / Cicero.

52 grants of $5,000 total, released across three funding phases. Phase 1 closes September 14. Applications available digitally or as printable PDFs in English and Spanish. Contact: (312) 425-9500.

Name: Community Enterprise Accelerator (CEA) Fellowship – Cohort 4
Description: A nine-month fellowship for Bronx entrepreneurs that provides $15,000 in grant capital, distributed monthly, plus personalized business coaching, strategic planning support, weekly workshops and check-ins, monthly in-person gatherings, and connections to advisors and Bronx business leaders. The program runs January–September 2027 and takes no equity; the grant requires no repayment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicants must own a for-profit business operating primarily in the Bronx, have been in business for at least one year, have generated more than $75,000 in total sales, and be committed to growing the business and contributing to the Bronx community. The fellowship includes weekly coaching/workshops and monthly in-person events. Priority consideration is given to Black and Hispanic/Latino entrepreneurs, but this is not stated as an exclusive eligibility requirement. Applications close September 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

Name: Bronx Summit Pitch
Description: The Bronx Summit Pitch Competition will award $1,500 to one Bronx-based entrepreneur working in the creative economy and/or social impact sector. Applications are due Monday, September 14 at 5 pm ET. Selected finalists will pitch live in person on Saturday, September 26 at Dream Charter High School, with a 3-minute pitch followed by judge Q&A.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Bronx based entrepreneurs working in the creative economy and/or social impact sector (ranging from fashion to film, built environment and architecture to gaming, social entrepreneurship to technology).

Name: Artadia Awards - Boston
Description: The Artadia Awards provide unrestricted financial support, exposure, and recognition to visual artists, allowing them to use funds in any way. Awardees also gain access to the Artadia Network for professional connections, resource sharing, and online Artist Registry visibility, helping advance careers. Three Awardees are chosen to receive $15,000 each.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Applicants must be a contemporary visual artist, making artwork for presentation in a contemporary art context: museum, galleries, arts non-profit, the public art realm, etc. Artadia does not fund filmmakers making films for distribution in cinematic venues, or those working in choreography presented outside of a contemporary art context.
- Applicants must be currently living and working within the city’s eligible counties and resided there for at least two years prior to the application deadline.
- Not currently be enrolled in an art-related degree program, nor be planning to attend an art-related degree program in the coming year.
- Not be related to Artadia staff or directors in any way.
- Have never received an award from Artadia or from The Art Council (Artadia’s former name) for or above the sum of $10,000. Please note that former finalists are eligible to apply.
- If you are enrolled in a long-term artist residency program, please note you are only eligible to apply in the Award city where you permanently reside. Additionally, you must make yourself available to meet with jurors for a 45 minute virtual studio visit should you be chosen as a Finalist.
- Unless applying as a collaborative, you must be the sole conceptual author of the artwork submitted in the application; if there are collaborators that share authorship of submitted work they must be clearly identified and credited.

Name: Graham Foundation for Advanced Studies in the Fine Arts
Description: The Graham Foundation provides project-based grants to individual practitioners whose work develops and communicates challenging ideas about architecture, design, and the built environment, including work that crosses into the arts, humanities, and sciences. Grants can support either the development/research phase of a project or the production and public presentation of completed work, including film/video, new media, exhibitions, public programs, and publications.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Individuals may apply for Production & Presentation or Research & Development grants.
Collaborative projects are eligible, but collaborators must be co-authors of the project, rather than people simply providing contracted services.
Individuals may submit only one Inquiry Form per year.
Previous Graham Foundation grantees must have completed all prior grant requirements before applying again.
A fiscal agent is not required for individuals.

Name: FoundersBoost Healthcare & Accessibility Accelerator
Description: The Healthcare & Accessibility Accelerator, run by FoundersBoost in partnership with MVMT Ventures, supports early-stage startups developing technology addressing healthcare, disability, and accessibility. The six-week program combines mentorship, pitch coaching, investor preparation, non-dilutive funding, and opportunities to showcase at Demo Day and CES.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Early-stage, tech-based, scalable startups addressing healthcare and/or accessibility; small dedicated teams with some initial customer traction are a strong fit. Diverse and underrepresented founder teams are encouraged.

Name: Princeton Hodder Fellowship
Description: The Hodder Fellowship supports writers, artists, and humanists who want a year of uninterrupted time to pursue a major creative or scholarly project. Fellows are given the freedom to focus almost entirely on their own work and do not have teaching obligations.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open internationally to artists and humanists, including writers, composers, choreographers, visual artists, performance artists, and others. Applicants should have demonstrated exceptional creative/intellectual ability and be pursuing a substantial project; the fellowship is intended for artists who would benefit from a year devoted to developing that work.

Name: Guggenheim Fellowship
Description: The Guggenheim Fellowship is a mid-career award supporting individuals who have made notable contributions across more than fifty disciplines in the arts, humanities, and sciences. Roughly 200 Fellows are selected annually from a highly competitive pool, with recent success rates averaging around 5%. Fellows propose a significant project; award amounts vary according to the Fellow's existing resources and the scope of the work proposed.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Citizens or permanent residents of the United States or Canada
- Mid-career professionals who have made notable contributions to their field
- Must propose a significant project and demonstrate preparedness to carry it out
- Individuals or pairs may apply
- Prior Guggenheim Fellows, current students, and organizations are ineligible

Timeline: applications due September 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. EST); work samples due September 29, 2026; reference letters due October 13, 2026; Fellowships announced late April 2027. The Foundation charges no application fee and does not guarantee that it will fully fund any project.

Name: SF Healthtech x AI Pitch Competition
Description: Berkeley Pharma Tech Foundation runs this pitch competition with Funding Breakthrough Lab, One-Way Summit and Startup Grind for early-stage startups working at the intersection of healthcare and artificial intelligence. Five startups are selected to pitch in person in San Francisco, each getting four minutes to present plus Q&A and expert feedback. The selected finalist advances to pitch at the One-Way Summit in October.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Startup developing a product, platform or technology at the intersection of healthcare and artificial intelligence
- Must have raised less than $2 million in cumulative DILUTIVE funding; non-dilutive funding such as grants does not count toward the limit
- Startups may be based in the United States or internationally
- At least one founder must be an immigrant to the United States
- At least one founder must be available to pitch in person in San Francisco in late September
- If selected as finalist, at least one founder must attend and pitch in person at the One-Way Summit, October 28-29, San Francisco (~1000 attendees)

Applications close September 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST; founders notified of results by September 22. Pitch event is the last week of September, 5-8 PM, San Francisco (address TBA). Format: five startups, 4 minute pitch + 4 minute Q&A + 4 minute feedback. Application asks for a 6-slide pitch deck.

No cash prize is stated - the award is the finalist slot at the One-Way Summit plus expert feedback and investor exposure. Categories named: AI diagnostics, digital health, medtech, healthcare SaaS, clinical AI, remote monitoring, AI drug discovery, computational biology.

Link note: the Google Form is the application and the best available link. Berkeley Pharma Tech Foundation's own site (berkeleypharmatechfoundation.org, Sacramento CA, 501(c)(3)) has no page for this competition. Contact: vanloannguyen@berkeleypharmatechfoundation.org

Name: GESAwards (Global EdTech Startup Awards)
Description: Global competition for early- and growth-stage edtech startups, with 23 regional semifinals across 155 countries feeding into global finals at Bett Global in London. Award categories are Best EdTech Solution, Innovation, Social Impact, and Emerging Markets. Prizes and support come from partners including AWS and MindCET Labs.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to early- and growth-stage edtech startups worldwide. Regional semifinals run October-November 2026, with regional champions advancing to the global finals at Bett Global in London in January 2027. No application fee listed. Winners receive international recognition plus access to investors, mentors, and partners; specific prize amounts are set by partner sponsors and are not published.

Name: Turner School of Construction Management Chicago (TSCM)
Description: The Turner School of Construction Management is a free training program from Turner Construction for small, local, and emerging construction businesses. Coursework strengthens business operations, expands industry knowledge, and builds relationships that support long-term growth. The application collects business details including trade discipline, years in business, student status, and MBE, WBE, or SBA certification status. Applications for the Fall 2026 session are open.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Small, local, and emerging construction businesses
- Application collects: company name, industry discipline/trade, business address, years in business, student status, prior program participation
- Certification status collected: MBE, WBE, SBA

Free program. Fall 2026 session; applications due September 16, 2026.

Name: Women's Fast Pitch
Description: Women's Venture Summit runs a national virtual pitch competition for women-led startups, selecting ten founders from across the United States to compete. The champion receives a package worth more than forty-five thousand dollars in professional services rather than cash, including pro bono legal support from Cooley, marketing support and business advisory services. Five regional finalists also gain the opportunity to launch a crowdfunding campaign through Wefunder.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Founder must be 18 or older
- Company must be MORE THAN 50% woman-owned AND woman-led
- Registered U.S. business entity
- Pre-Seed through Seed stage
- Must be open to equity crowdfunding
- Must be based in an applicable U.S. region
- All industries eligible

NOTE: the prize is IN-KIND professional services, not cash. Champion receives $25,000 in pro bono legal services from Cooley, $10,000 in marketing support, and $10,000 in business advisory services. All five regional finalists get the opportunity to launch a $50,000 crowdfunding campaign through Wefunder.

Applications close September 16, 2026. Ten founders compete in the virtual national competition October 1, 2026. Five regional finalists advance to the Women's Venture Summit in San Diego, November 2-5, 2026. No fee to apply.

Name: Camelback Fellowship
Description: The Camelback Fellowship supports early-stage social impact entrepreneurs tackling systemic inequities in Education and Conscious Technology, providing $50K plus a 16-week hybrid accelerator experience offering coaching, capital, connections, community, and curriculum, with lifelong membership in the Camelback network.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The Camelback Fellowship supports early-stage entrepreneurs dedicated to addressing  inequities in the education and technology sectors. We prioritize founders who have a deep, personal connection to the issues they aim to solve and who are committed to serving under-resourced communities. Eligible applicants must:
- Be over the age of 18.
- Be able to commit approximately 10 hours per week for 16 weeks to Fellowship activities.
- Hold a leadership role (Founder, Co-founder, CEO, or Executive Director) in your venture.
- Reside in the United States or a U.S. Territory.
- Have proficiency in English.
- Fellows are not required to relocate; we believe the greatest impact comes from staying and serving your community.

Name: Detroit Green Grocer Program Grant
Description: The Green Grocer Program provides grants of up to $25,000 to help Detroit retailers open neighborhood grocery stores or expand existing stores with fresh food, produce, and grocery essentials. Funding can be used for equipment, technology, inventory, and store buildouts, with future loan financing of up to $50,000 (or $100,000 for certain larger-format stores) also planned to support healthy food access across Detroit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To participate in the Green Grocer Program and be eligible for assistance, the business must be:
- A registered for-profit business in good standing with a business address located within the City of Detroit

Name: Anthem Awards
Description: The Anthem Awards recognize mission-driven work from individuals, nonprofits, companies, and organizations worldwide. Categories span Content & Media, Community Engagement, Education, Art & Culture, Human & Civil Rights, Humanitarian Action, Technology, Sustainability, and more.
Industry: Education & Child Care,Health / Wellness,Climate & Sustainability,Technology,Social Impact,Nonprofit

Name: MD City of Bowie Arts Grant
Description: Supports individuals or groups developing interactive arts experiences for Bowie residents, such as workshops, performances, community music, dance, theater, visual arts, and hands-on creative activities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to individuals and groups developing projects that involve Bowie residents in an interactive arts experience. You do not necessarily need to live in Bowie, but the project must involve Bowie residents.

Name: MD City of Bowie Education Grant
Description: Provides reimbursable grants for creative educational projects that enrich the learning experiences of Bowie children. Examples include student workshops, classroom enrichment, school art experiences, and assemblies.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Teachers, parent groups, and other interested individuals associated with eligible community schools can apply. A total of $28,000 is available for the 2026–27 cycle.

Name: MD City of Bowie Community Outreach Grant
Description: Supports projects and programs addressing the needs of Bowie residents, particularly in health, social and human services, youth, seniors, diversity, community-centered programs, and cultural education. Individuals, groups, and organizations can apply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individuals, groups, and organizations are eligible. Applicants do not have to live in Bowie, but the funded program must directly benefit residents of the incorporated City of Bowie.

Name: LA Craft Contemporary Seasonal Markets Vendor Application
Description: Craft Contemporary, a Los Angeles craft museum, selects artisans to sell handmade goods at two curated seasonal markets: the Autumn Harvest Market in Culver City's Helms Design District and the Makers Market at the museum's Wilshire Boulevard courtyard. Accepted vendors pay a table fee and retain all sales proceeds. Categories include ceramics, jewelry, textiles, apparel, printed goods, candles, florals, and non-perishable foods.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Makers and artisans selling handcrafted goods; vintage or imported handcrafted goods accepted if ethically sourced
- Autumn Harvest Market emphasizes the food-craft intersection: non-perishable foods, functional pottery, tableware, garden items, florals
- Makers Market covers clothing, ceramics, jewelry, textiles, printed goods, candles, and similar
- Must provide a seller's permit
- Must submit product photos and descriptions with the application
- Must staff the table continuously during all event hours

Table fees on acceptance: $200 (Autumn Harvest) or $300 (Makers Market). Applications close September 18, 2026; notifications September 23. Events: Autumn Harvest Market October 10, 2026, Culver City; Makers Market December 4-6, 2026, 5814 Wilshire Blvd.
Industry: Arts & Crafts,Visual & Fine Arts,Apparel & Accessories,Food & Beverage,Retail,Creative Economy,Design

Name: Tampa Bay Wave HealthTech|X Accelerator
Description: HealthTech|X is a zero-equity accelerator run by Tampa Bay Wave with the Brock Innovation Center and Vanderbilt Health for seed and Series A healthcare technology startups working on behavioral health and addiction solutions. The cohort attends four in-person session weeks split between Tampa and Nashville, covering mentorship, investor readiness, and customer access, and concludes with a virtual demo day in January 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Startup with proprietary technology in behavioral health or addiction solutions
- Seed or Series A stage
- Management team with at least two full-time positions
- Demonstrated market validation
- Investable, scalable business model
- Minimum 6-12 months of financial runway
- Mandatory in-person attendance at all four session weeks

Zero equity taken. Applications close September 14, 2026. Session 1 Tampa Oct 27-29, 2026; Session 2 Nashville Nov 3-5, 2026; Session 3 Tampa Jan 12-14, 2027; Session 4 Nashville Jan 19-21, 2027; virtual Demo Day Jan 27, 2027.

Name: Transform Business Grant
Description: The Transform Business Grant awards a $1,000 microgrant paired with a customized, year-long business strategy and development program. It is aimed at United States business owners from systemically marginalized groups whose companies are built on anticapitalist and antiracist values and work to challenge systems of oppression. Applications are accepted only during two defined windows each year and cannot be accepted outside them.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Owner identifies as part of a systemically marginalized group
- Business aligned with anticapitalist and antiracist values
- Social-impact-oriented business that challenges systems of oppression
- Demonstrated financial need
- US-based; citizenship and immigration status are not barriers
- Ineligible: political organizations, religious organizations for religious purposes, debt payments, and businesses focused on medicinal or clinical practice

2026 windows: March 9-20 and September 8-18. Applications cannot be accepted outside these windows. Award is $1,000 plus a year-long business strategy and development program.

Name: Rally LA - DTLA Small Business Cohort
Description: Rally LA is an initiative of the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce with corporate supporters and community organizations, preparing small businesses for the major sporting and live events coming to the region. The Downtown LA cohort selects independent brick-and-mortar storefronts for a cash grant plus visibility campaigns, corporate network connections, a neighborhood block party, tailored operational resources and co-branding opportunities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- At least one Downtown LA location - PERMANENT OR POP-UP both qualify
- Independent brick-and-mortar storefront
- Sector must be one of: Food & Beverage, Retail, Creative & Production, Personal Services, or Entertainment
- Under $10M average annual revenue AND fewer than 50 employees
- Operating for a minimum of 12 months

Selected members receive a cash grant distributed by the LA Area Chamber of Commerce, plus visibility campaigns, corporate network connections, a neighborhood block party, tailored operational resources, and co-branding opportunities.

Applications close September 8, 2026. Run by the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce in partnership with corporate supporters and community organizations.
Industry: Food & Beverage,Retail,Creative Economy,Beauty & Personal Care,Film & Media,Brick-and-Mortar

Name: PDX Pop-Up Shop Program
Description: Downtown Portland Clean & Safe places emerging retail businesses into vacant downtown storefronts for the holiday season, covering rent and utilities in full plus exterior signage, marketing inclusion and on-site team support. Selected businesses trade from November 13 to December 26, 2026, and supply only their own POS, internet and merchandising materials. Applicants need a federal tax ID, liability insurance, sellable inventory and staffing; franchises are ineligible.
Amount: Free storefront rent and utilities (Nov 13 - Dec 26, 2026)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Federal tax ID and liability insurance required; must have products to sell and staff to run the shop; must provide own POS, internet and merchandising. Franchises ineligible. Food/beverage businesses welcome subject to licensing. Generally open Wed-Sun 10am-6pm; some locations require seven-day operation. Applications reviewed in September; finalist interviews week of September 21; notifications early October.

Name: NJ Accelerate
Description: The New Jersey Economic Development Authority encourages New Jersey entrepreneurs to join high-quality accelerator programs through two benefits. Companies graduating from an approved accelerator can receive up to $250,000 in convertible notes with warrants, plus up to six months of rent support at an approved collaborative workspace. Approved accelerators separately receive sponsorship grants for hosting programmatic events in New Jersey.
Amount: up to $250,000 (convertible notes) plus up to $25,000 rent support
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
NOTE: the company-facing benefit is a convertible note with warrants - this is DILUTIVE capital, not a grant. The rent support and the accelerator sponsorship grants are non-dilutive.

For GRADUATE COMPANIES:
- At least 50% of the company workforce works in, or pays taxes in, New Jersey
- Minimum two founders working 100% professionally in the company
- Must operate in an NJEDA-designated targeted industry
- Current New Jersey tax clearance certificate required
- Benefit: up to $250,000 in convertible notes with warrants, plus up to 6 months of rent (not exceeding $25,000) at an approved collaborative workspace
- 5% bonus amounts available for women-owned or minority-owned businesses

For ACCELERATORS seeking approval:
- Minimum two graduated cohorts
- Structured curriculum focused on startup growth
- Access to 50+ active mentors
- At least 35% of graduates receiving follow-on funding or achieving strategic acquisitions/exits
- Must support one of NJEDA's targeted industries
- Benefit: sponsorship grants up to $2,000 per event, capped at $20,000 total

Applications close September 19, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST, or earlier if funds are exhausted. Administered by the New Jersey Economic Development Authority. Contact: njaccelerate@njeda.gov

Name: 100 Voices of Florida Grant
Description: 100 Voices of Florida awards grants of up to $5,000 to filmmakers and screenwriters who demonstrate an authentic, original creative voice. Judging weighs emotional impact and pacing alongside vision. Winners also receive a meeting with an industry professional and a one-on-one career coaching session. Applicants must be 18 or older; a Florida connection is optional but lowers the entry fee. The 2026 cycle is open and closes September 20.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 18+. Florida connection optional - there is an unrestricted track at the higher fee. Application fee $25 with a Florida connection, $35 for all others.

Name: NCI SBIR Innovative Concept Award
Description: National Cancer Institute SBIR contract award supporting small businesses developing highly innovative, transformative technologies for pediatric and rare cancers — spanning research, prevention, detection, diagnosis, and treatment. Built for high-risk, high-reward concepts: preliminary data is not required and is not used in evaluation, and review criteria weight innovation heavily. NCI describes an expedited funding process after submission.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicant must be a for-profit U.S. small business with 500 or fewer employees including affiliates, based in the U.S. with work performed in the U.S. Ownership must be more than 50% by U.S. individuals, or by another business concern that is itself majority individually owned, or by venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, or private equity firms (SBIR only). Universities and nonprofit research institutions cannot be the applicant — they may only subcontract. Offerors are expected to participate in the NIH I-Corps program, with additional I-Corps funding provided on top of the award. Solicitation number 75N98026R00109; proposals due September 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET via the NIH Electronic Contract Proposal Submission site (ecps.nih.gov), not Grants.gov. NCI accepts contract submissions once per year. No application fee.

Name: 2026 Fund Her Future Grant from H&R Block
Description: H&R Block, in partnership with Hello Alice, will award up to four women-owned, for-profit U.S. businesses a $50,000 grant package, consisting of $45,000 in funding and one year of bookkeeping, tax preparation, payroll, and business structure services valued at $5,000. Eligible applicants must be at least 18 years old (19 in Alabama and Nebraska) and serve as the business’s primary executive.
Amount: $45,000 (plus one year of small business services)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To qualify, an owner must be:
- The main executive (Founder, President, CEO, CFO, COO, or similar title) of a business that meets the criteria below.
- Eighteen (18) years of age or older (19 in AL and NE).

To be eligible, a business must be:
- A for-profit business located and registered in one of the fifty United States, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory.

Name: Texas StartHER Grant
Description: The Center for Women Entrepreneur’s StartHER Grant Program supports Texas women-owned startups in launching new initiatives and driving early-stage growth through innovative projects.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible businesses must satisfy all of the following conditions:

- Existing Texas woman-owned businesses (51% directly owned and controlled by one or more women who are U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents) with five or fewer employees may apply (including the owner.)
- The business must currently be set up as a legal entity.
- The business must be located and operated within the state of Texas.
Business must be five years or less (formed after 10/04/2019 - current.) – No date exceptions
- The business must be a for-profit corporation, partnership, LLP, LLC, or sole proprietorship. Non Profit Organizations are not eligible.
- If the business or business owner owns the premises where the business operates, all property taxes must be current.
- All sales, payroll, and other taxes must be current.
- Business owner(s) must not have any felonies or convictions for a crime of dishonesty or breach of trust.
- The business, business owner, and applicant must not be involved in any pending or current litigation.
- The business, owner, and applicant operate with all required permits and licenses and conform to all state laws.  Please check the Texas Taxable Entity Search page to verify your business is in good standing with the state:  https://mycpa.cpa.state.tx.us/coa/

Name: Enthuse Foundation Pitch Competition
Description: The Enthuse Foundation Pitch Competition is an annual competition for women entrepreneurs in food, beverage, and consumer packaged goods (CPG). Five finalists pitch their businesses live in New York City for cash prizes and substantial business-building services, including coaching, financial planning, marketing, and retail strategy support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
At least 51% women-owned

Brand must be a physical product in the food, beverage, or consumer package goods (CPG) business (wellness, beauty, etc). 

Business and primary market must be U.S.-based

At least one founder must be a U.S. citizen

Company must have at least $100K and less than $999K in annual revenue

Companies must have been in business for less than four (4) years (any company founded before January 1, 2022, will not qualify)

Previous grant winners and pitch competition finalists can apply if they meet the criteria

Available to attend a LIVE IN-PERSON pitch night on November 5, 2026, in NYC, if selected as a finalist.
Stipend is provided for out-of-town finalists

Founders are expected to participate in our on-site marketplace

Finalists must send product samples if selected and are expected to remain connected to the Enthuse Foundation, providing annual revenue information to the organization

Name: Michigan Out-of-School Time (OST) Grant
Description: Michigan's Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential is distributing $135 million to fund in-person before-school, after-school and summer programming for students in grades K-12. The 2026-2027 grant supports organizations delivering out-of-school time and summer learning across the state. Eligible applicants are nonprofits, tribal governments, higher education institutions, public libraries, municipalities and intermediate districts; for-profit businesses are excluded.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
FOR-PROFIT BUSINESSES ARE NOT ELIGIBLE. This is a nonprofit and public-entity grant - flagged here because it does not fit the usual small-business profile of this database.

Eligible applicants:
- 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations
- Federally recognized Indian Tribal governments
- Institutions of higher education
- Public libraries
- Cities or municipalities
- Intermediate school districts

Funds in-person before-school, after-school or summer programming for grades K-12. Application window August 24, 2026 through September 23, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EDT. $135 million allocated across the program; per-award amounts are not published on this page. Administered by MiLEAP. Contact: MiLEAP-OST@Michigan.gov

Name: Main Street Rising Tour - New York
Description: Hello Alice brings its Main Street Rising Tour to New York, where registered attendees can apply to pitch their business live to a panel of judges from Hello Alice and partner organizations. Selected founders present at the morning event at Google NYC, and winners take home a cash prize to reinvest in their business. Registration and attendance at the event are both required to be considered.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Businesses operating in New York
- Must have a venture-scalable or venture-viable product or service
- Must be fully operational: actively conducting business AND generating revenue
- Must be tech-enabled: using digital tools, platforms or systems to support core business operations
- MUST REGISTER FOR AND ATTEND THE EVENT to be considered for the pitch opportunity

Pitch application deadline September 23, 2026. Event October 7, 2026, 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM EDT at Google NYC. Free to apply, no fees; application takes about 15 minutes. Event is free to attend for selected ambassadors, but pitch recipients cover their own travel and accommodation.

Amount not published - the page says only that winners take home a cash prize and that applicants can "potentially win thousands of dollars."

This is one stop on a multi-city tour; the Miami stop is a separate record in this database (closed 8/23/2026).

Name: Found/LA Multicultural Entrepreneur Program (MEP) at ELAC
Description: No-cost six-month entrepreneurship development program for established multicultural business owners in Los Angeles, delivered by the Dr. Yasmin Davidds Leadership Institute at East Los Angeles College's Susan Rubio Entrepreneurship & Innovation Center. Combines a three-day in-person launch with ongoing leadership training, mentorship from faculty and entrepreneurship leaders, a roughly 35-person peer cohort, access-to-capital readiness preparation, and an individualized Business Growth Plan.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NO CASH GRANT — the award is a fully funded cohort seat. Applicant must be a multicultural entrepreneur or small business owner in the Los Angeles area, must own and actively operate an existing business, generally in business at least one year, with typical revenue of $75,000 to $1 million annually. Nonprofits are NOT eligible. Must commit to the full program schedule. No cost to participate for selected entrepreneurs. Applications opened August 17, 2026 and close September 16, 2026; program runs November 17-19, 2026 (three-day in-person launch) through March 17, 2027. Contact: Zulema Bastien, Managing Director, zulema@dryasmininstitute.com.

Name: The Movement x Black List Ladder Commission
Description: Commissioning award from The Movement Theatre Company, a Harlem-based Off-Broadway company developing new work by artists of color, in partnership with The Black List. Housed within The Movement's Ladder Series new-work development program, the commission gives one generative artist $10,000 to write an entirely new stage work plus a year of funding and development support — monthly meetings, a workshop, and a public staged reading.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to generative artists — artists from any discipline who create new work for the stage. The proposal must be for work that is brand new: never written, workshopped, or produced. Work should center complex stories about communities of color that are bold, risky and unapologetic. No geographic or career-stage restriction stated on the public call. Deadline September 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT; applications go through a JotForm linked from the homepage. No application fee stated. The Movement also awards a separate Jody Falco and Jeffrey Steinman Commission of $5,000, but that one has no open application call and appears to be selected internally.

Name: Target Essentials & Beauty Discovery Day 2026
Description: Target brings a select group of founders to Target HQ for a day of networking and business conversations with the Essentials and Beauty teams. Run through Target Accelerators, the same platform behind Target Forward Founders and Target Takeoff. Aimed at brands in home care, pets, personal care, health, baby, or beauty. The draw is direct access to Target merchants and a potential path to retail placement, not funding.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NO CASH AWARD — this is a buyer-access and networking event, not funding. Target is seeking founders building brands in home care, pets, personal care, health, baby, or beauty. Applicants complete a form on the Target Accelerators site; Target then emails next steps to collect any missing information, and confirms afterward whether the applicant is selected to attend at Target HQ on Thursday, November 12, 2026. No application fee listed. Revenue thresholds, business stage, certifications, and demographic criteria are not published on the page.
Industry: Beauty & Personal Care,Consumer Packaged Goods,Health / Wellness,Retail

Name: Chicago Booth Angels Network Pitch/Demo Day
Description: Semiannual pitch event run by the Booth Angels Network of Chicago & New York, an alumni-run angel network of the University of Chicago Booth School of Business with roughly 55 members. Selected startups pitch to an audience of seasoned angel investors and University of Chicago alumni. There is no cash prize — the value is investor exposure and potential angel investment.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT A GRANT — no cash prize; this is investor exposure and a path to potential angel investment. Startups do NOT have to be affiliated with the University of Chicago to apply (stated verbatim on the site). Criteria: U.S.-based company; executive team with relevant background and a successful track record; unique solution, clear target customer, and large market; existing product, paying customers, and recurring revenue; post-money valuation up to $15 million. Fall 2026 applications close September 25, 2026 for the Fall Pitch/Demo Day on October 14, 2026 at 4:00 PM CT / 5:00 PM ET. Due to application volume, the network only contacts startups selected for an interview. Applications go through Gust: gust.com/organizations/chicago-booth-angels-chicago/public_profile (select 'Chicago Booth Angels Network of Chicago'). Contact: BoothAngels@boothangelschicago.com.

Name: 2026 OPEN Chicago Annual Conference Pitch Competition
Description: The OPEN Chicago Pitch Competition gives five early-stage startups the opportunity to present on the main stage at its annual conference, gain visibility, receive feedback from experienced judges, and build connections with founders, mentors, and operators. The winner receives a $5,000 prize, and the competition is open to students, professionals, and founders from angel or pre-seed stage through Series A across all industries. OPEN Chicago is a nonprofit chapter of the global OPEN network that supports entrepreneurs and professionals through networking, mentorship, educational programming, and community-building.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Open to All
Students, professionals, and early-stage entrepreneurs from all backgrounds and industries with ideas that address real-world challenges or opportunities

Company Stage
Early-stage founders. From Angel/Pre-Seed stage to Series A.

Original Work
All submissions must reflect the team’s original work and unique ideas. While teams may consult mentors, advisors and external insights, any third-party content must be properly cited and attributed.

Name: Twilio AI Startup Searchlight
Description: Twilio AI Startup Searchlight recognizes AI startups building innovative approaches to communications and customer engagement, particularly those using technologies such as generative AI, conversational AI, LLM-powered agents, voice, or identity on the Twilio platform. The 2026 program has two tracks—Breakthrough Builders for early-stage startups and Scaling Visionaries for startups with proven traction.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be an AI startup with a product already in the market, able to provide a working functional demo showing emerging technology integrated with Twilio, and have raised less than $200 million in venture funding. You also need a Twilio account to apply.

Name: Lane County Community & Economic Development Grant
Description: Lane County's competitive Community & Economic Development grant funds high-impact projects that raise wages or job counts, deliver business assistance, support business innovation, and revitalize Main Streets, downtowns and commercial districts across the county. Roughly $200,000 is available for the 2026-2027 round, awarded in amounts from $5,000 to $30,000. Applications are distributed through Lane County's Bid Locker portal, with an informational webinar held in advance.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT open to for-profit businesses - 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and cities serving Lane County residents only. Applications open August 19, 2026 and close September 25, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Apply via Bid Locker: https://bidlocker.us/a/lanecounty/ShowAll . Informational webinar held August 26, 2026. Contact: Jason Harris, CED Manager.

Name: J.W. Couch Foundation Grants
Description: Houston-based private family foundation making national grants across three pillars: Preservation (wildlife conservation, historic preservation, biodiversity, food and waste management, animal welfare), Education (early childhood, 21st-century learning, teacher support), and Wellness (mental health, digital wellbeing, outdoor access, mentorship). A separate Storytelling Grant funds nonprofits across all three pillars to document and communicate their community impact.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits only — the foundation states it accepts unsolicited applications from U.S.-based nonprofits. INVITATION-GATED: you do not submit a grant application directly. Applicants complete a short 'Tell Your Story' intake form at jwcouchfoundation.org/qualify; the foundation reviews it and invites qualified organizations to apply. Two cycles per year — the Q3 2026 cycle closes September 25, 2026 with decisions by October 30, 2026 (the Q1 cycle closed March 27, 2026). U.S.-based organizations only, no state restriction. No application fee.
Industry: Nonprofit,Climate & Sustainability,Education & Child Care,Health / Wellness,Social Impact

Name: STRAUSS Trades Business Booster Contest
Description: Workwear brand STRAUSS is awarding one small trades business a $10,000 business grant and two tickets to Game One of the 2026 MLB World Series; three finalists each receive two tickets to a 2026 MLB Postseason game. Open to businesses in skilled trades, construction, manufacturing, logistics, field services and warehousing that are physically located in one of the 50 states, with 100 or fewer employees and average annual gross receipts of $15 million or less over the previous three years. Owners 18 or older submit the story behind their operation and how the $10,000 would help the business grow through the campaign website linked in the announcement; one entry per business.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Businesses in skilled trades, construction, manufacturing, logistics, field services, warehousing or skilled labor
- Physically located in one of the 50 states
- 100 or fewer employees; average annual gross receipts of $15M or less over the previous three years
- For-profit and nonprofit organizations may enter; entrant must be an owner, 18+
- One entry per business; submit the business story through the campaign website

Announced 9/10/2026 (STRAUSS press release on GlobeNewswire); deadline 9/25/2026, no time zone stated. The 2026 campaign site URL could not be confirmed within the research cap - the press release links to it. us.strauss.com/pages/strauss-business-booster is the 2025 LAFC edition (closed), not this one.

Name: eWEAR Health Prize at Stanford University
Description: The 2026 eWEAR Health Prize awards $25,000 to an emerging company developing breakthrough deep-tech or AI innovations in health or medicine; up to five finalists will pitch in person at Stanford on November 6, 2026. Eligible applicants must be founders or co-founders ages 18–35, lead a U.S.-incorporated company with a U.S. business location, be raising pre-seed or pre-Series A funding, and work in brain-machine interfaces, longevity, precision health, wearables, or robotics.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The company must fit the theme of Deep Tech and AI in the medical/health sector with innovation in one or more of the following areas: brain-machine interfaces, longevity, precision health, wearables, or robotics.

Companies should be at a very early stage, seeking pre-seed funding, or seed funding that is pre-A round funding.  Companies seeking A-round funding or later will not be considered.

Applicants should be the founder (or co-founder) of the company and be 18 to 35 years old on November 6, 2026. The company must be incorporated in the U.S.A. and have a business location in the U.S.A.

The applicant must travel to Stanford U. to pitch in-person. Sending an alternate to pitch instead is discouraged, and is subject to the alternate meeting all eligibility and other requirements.

Name: Midway Contemporary Art Visual Arts Fund
Description: Midway Contemporary Art distributes $60,000 through the Visual Arts Fund as six $10,000 grants for artist-organized, self-initiated visual arts projects in the Twin Cities. Lead organizers must live in the seven-county metro region, and a publicly accessible component must take place there. Projects cannot charge admission. Funded by the Andy Warhol Foundation's regional regranting program, the 2026 round opened September 1 and closes September 26.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT open to incorporated businesses or 501(c)(3)s - individual artist-organizers only (PhD students eligible; other students not). Lead organizer must reside in the seven-county Twin Cities metro. Publicly accessible component must take place in the metro. No admission fees permitted. Funded by the Andy Warhol Foundation regional regranting program.

Name: Houston Let Creativity Happen Grant
Description: Houston Arts Alliance's Let Creativity Happen program awards up to $2,500 for programs that amplify artistic creativity and innovation across Houston. Round 3 of the 2026 cycle is open to individual artists, arts nonprofits and fiscally sponsored projects residing within Houston city limits. Funded projects must include a dedicated public component. Recipients of earlier 2026 grants are ineligible, though previous 2026 applicants who were not funded may reapply.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists, arts nonprofits and fiscally sponsored projects; applicant must reside within Houston city limits. 2026 grant recipients ineligible for Round 3; unfunded 2026 applicants may reapply. Funded projects must include a dedicated public component.

Name: Houston City's Initiative Grant
Description: Houston Arts Alliance's City's Initiative awards up to $10,000 for strategic creative opportunities that engage Houston residents and visitors. Round 3 of the 2026 cycle is open to individual artists, arts nonprofits and fiscally sponsored projects based within Houston city limits. Budgets may cover artist fees, materials, production and marketing, and every funded project must include a dedicated public component. Prior 2026 grant recipients are not eligible for this round.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual artists, arts nonprofits and fiscally sponsored projects; applicant must reside within Houston city limits. Budgets may include artist fees, materials, production and marketing. Every funded project must include a dedicated public component. Prior 2026 grant recipients ineligible.

Name: Brooklyn, NY 9th Annual Wallabout Wonderland Holiday Market Vendor Application
Description: Wallabout Wonderland is a large holiday market at the Brooklyn Navy Yard featuring local makers, artists, designers, food vendors, and small businesses. The market has historically featured 150+ vendors selling items such as clothing, jewelry, home décor, artisanal foods, and other handmade products.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Requirements -All participants must:
- Fill out this submission form on or before the deadline. (SEPTEMBER 25)

- Participate in the market on December 5

- Be available for set up on Friday, December 4 between the hours of 4:00pm - 8:00pm 

- Have at least one dedicated person to work the booth at all times

- Provide a sales report at the end of the day to a designated BNYDC staff member

- Be available for load out on December 5 between the hours of 8:00pm - 10:00pm

- Sell products/ items at a range of price points

Additional Information:
- There is a $175 Vendor fee if selected; $275 for food court vendors


- All participants will receive one (1) 8' X 30" table, two (2) chairs, and one (1) table cloth.

If you require any additional items for set up, please feel free to bring those items to make your section “pop” along with signage so attendees can find you


- All major fabrication MUST be finished prior to installation


- All participants are responsible for providing their own point-of-sale equipment

Name: SheBuilds on Lovable (Women's Buildathon)
Description: A 48-hour remote buildathon and community from Lovable that empowers women to build apps, run seasonally. No coding experience required — participants get 48 hours, unlimited Lovable credits during the event, and mentorship to take an idea to a working product.
Amount: $5,000 in Lovable credits (prior season); unlimited Lovable credits during the event
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to women globally — the program describes welcoming everyone from first-time builders to executives, and states no coding skills are required ("a laptop, an idea, and the willingness to build it"). 100% remote, 48-hour format. Participants are selected by application; previous applicants are encouraged to reapply. No entry fee mentioned, and accepted participants receive unlimited Lovable credits for the event. Run by Lovable. Applications go through shebuilds.lovable.app.

Name: SEED SPOT Emerging Retail Brand Accelerator Midwest
Description: The SEED SPOT Emerging Retail Brand Accelerator Midwest is a hybrid eight-week program for revenue-generating consumer product brands in Chicago, Michigan, Indiana, Wisconsin, Iowa, and Northeast Ohio that are preparing to scale into retail. Participants receive retail-focused workshops, one-on-one mentorship, pitch coaching, and support with branding, sales strategy, financial projections, manufacturing, supply chains, fulfillment, and retailer compliance; strong candidates generally have at least $25,000 in annual revenue or a validated product with demonstrated traction.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
This program could be the right fit if you are:
- Generating $25,000 or more in annual revenue and ready to scale
- Producing a product at home with steady sales and ready to move into a manufacturing facility
- Working with a validated prototype and strong manufacturing practices and ready to grow your sales channels
- Headquartered and operated in the Midwest ( NE Ohio, Chicago, Michigan, Indiana, Wisconsin, Iowa).

Name: NC GWBC Perfect Pitch / WBENCPitch
Description: The Greater Women's Business Council runs Perfect Pitch, a competition giving WBENC-certified women-owned businesses in North Carolina the chance to pitch for a regional cash prize and advance toward the national WBENCPitch competition. Regional winners receive one thousand dollars, and businesses advancing to the national stage can win up to twenty thousand. Applicants must already hold WBENC certification and be in good standing.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must already be WBENC-certified and in good standing
- Women-owned business based in North Carolina
- Retail businesses are eligible
- Regional winners advance toward the national WBENCPitch competition

Regional prize $1,000; national winners can receive up to $20,000. Deadline September 8, 2026.

Link note: the JotForm is the application as supplied. The Greater Women's Business Council's own program page was not located, so the form is the stored link; if a GWBC host page exists it should replace this.

Name: Exton Chester County Library Holiday Craft Show Vendor Application
Description: The Chester County Library and District Center is accepting vendor applications for its 15th Annual Holiday Craft Show, a single-day, high-traffic community event in Exton, Pennsylvania. Artists and makers show and sell work to several hundred shoppers in the library's public space. Applications are reviewed and accepted vendors are notified in early October, several weeks ahead of the December show date.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to artists and makers. Applications reviewed; accepted vendors notified by Monday, October 5, 2026. Direct application form: https://bit.ly/CCLCraftShowApp2026 . Event Saturday, December 12, 2026, 9:30am-3:00pm at Chester County Library & District Center, 450 Exton Square Parkway, Exton PA 19341.

Name: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists
Description: The Queens Museum and Jerome Foundation award two $20,000 fellowships to emerging visual artists living in New York City's five boroughs, paid in two installments across the 2027-28 fellowship year. Applicants must have resided in the city at least a year before January 2027 and be two to ten years into their practice outside degree programs, without solo shows at established commercial galleries or museums.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NYC five boroughs, 1+ year residency prior to January 2027. 2-10 years into practice outside degree programs. No prior solo shows at established commercial galleries or museums; no major mid-career grants. Individuals or collectives of up to two. Paid in two installments across the 2027-28 fellowship year.

Name: Saltbox Chamblee Next Stop Grant
Description: Saltbox is awarding one Georgia physical-products business $5,000 in membership credit toward a warehouse suite at its new Chamblee, Atlanta location, timed to that site's launch. Membership includes loading dock access, Wi-Fi, trash service, conference rooms, a photo studio, and on-site support. Judges score on Fit (30%), Need/Impact (30%), Traction (25%), and Local Connection (15%).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: IN-KIND, NOT CASH — the award is membership credit applied against monthly Saltbox fees until exhausted; no cash redemption option is stated. Business must operate in Georgia with a Georgia business address (statewide, not restricted to Chamblee or metro Atlanta) and must make, sell, store, or ship physical products, or perform project work requiring warehouse/dock space. Minimum six months operating as of August 31, 2026. Applicant must be 18+ and authorized to represent the business. Excluded: warehousing, self-storage, logistics, or otherwise competing businesses; Saltbox employees, officers, directors, judges and their immediate families. Deadline September 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT; finalists notified October 2; recipient announced October 7, 2026 at the Chamblee launch party. THE WINNER MUST COMMENCE MEMBERSHIP ON OR BEFORE NOVEMBER 1, 2026. Free to apply.

Name: West Virginia STEP Program
Description: The West Virginia Division of Economic Development is offering $325,000 in funding (Oct 1, 2024 – Sept 29, 2026) through the U.S. SBA’s State Trade Expansion Program (STEP) to help small businesses expand into global markets. Eligible businesses can receive up to $15,000 in reimbursements (covering 75% of costs) for export-related activities such as trade missions, trade shows, market sales trips, U.S. Dept. of Commerce services, translations, and international marketing.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Find details about eligibility here: https://westvirginia.gov/export-promotion-guidelines/

Name: VentureWell E-Team Program
Description: The E-Team Program supports student teams commercializing science and engineering based inventions that address social, health, or environmental challenges. Teams first receive a $5,000 Pioneer grant to investigate the best market for their invention, then may advance to a $20,000 Propel grant to build and test a business model. Funding is non-dilutive and paired with hands-on workshops, expert coaching, and peer networking.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Team must include two or more students plus a faculty advisor
- All members must be currently enrolled at U.S.-based institutions
- Invention must be science- and engineering-based
- Project should address a pressing social, health, or environmental challenge
- Applicants must demonstrate commitment to exploring commercialization
- Propel funding is available only to teams that have completed Pioneer

$5,000 Pioneer stage plus $20,000 Propel stage; non-dilutive. Winter 2027 cycle: applications opened July 27, 2026, deadline September 29, 2026. Pioneer workshop January 14-15, 2027; Propel workshop January 27-28, 2027. Workshops are fully funded.

Name: Golden Bean The Americas Coffee Roasting Competition
Description: Golden Bean is the largest coffee roasting competition in the Americas, awarding gold, silver, and bronze medals by category plus an overall champion ("Roaster of the Year"). Roasters mail one unbranded 500g sample per category to the Denver judging site; the 2026 competition runs September 30 – October 3, 2026 at the Art Hotel Denver. Entry is $150 per coffee.
Amount: Gold, silver, and bronze medals (no cash)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to coffee roasters in the Americas (individual roasters plus small- and large-chain categories). Entries must arrive by mail by 5pm on Friday, September 25, 2026, or be hand-delivered on Tuesday, September 29, 2026; samples ship in unbranded 500g bags with a printed packing slip. Roasters entering six coffees receive one complimentary VIP attendance ticket. Entry portal: https://goldenbean.awardsplatform.com/

Name: Philadelphia Growth & Sustainability Pitch powered by Citizens Bank
Description: The Growth & Sustainability Pitch Competition, presented by Entrepreneur Works and Citizens, gives eligible small businesses in Philadelphia and Delaware County the chance to win a $10,000 cash grant to support business growth or sustainability. Applicants should be active businesses with a clear growth vision and community impact; selected participants complete a required workshop, create a 1–3 minute public pitch video, and compete through public voting, with the top five advancing to a live pitch competition.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Active small business located in Philadelphia or Delaware County, PA, with a clear growth vision and commitment to positive community impact. Applicants submit a 1-3 minute video and must tag @EntreWorks on social media. 2026 timeline: applications opened September 1 and close September 29, 2026; participants notified October 2; mandatory 'Communicating Your Business' workshop October 7 at 6:00 PM ET; public voting October 12-23; finalists announced October 26; finalist coaching November 2-13; live pitch event Tuesday, November 17, 2026. No application fee.

Name: Credibly Small Business Award
Description: The Credibly Small Business Award celebrates small business owners creating community impact. Winners receive growth funding: $30,000 (first place), $20,000 (second place), and $10,000 (third place).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- U.S.-based active small businesses
- Operating for at least 6 months
- Must use a business banking account
- For-profit ( Non-Profit organizations are not eligible)

Name: High Five Grant
Description: The High Five Grant for Moms is an annual grant competition co-hosted by The Mama Ladder and Belly Bandit, providing equity-free funding to mom-owned businesses. Applicants submit during a one-month window, followed by judging and a public voting round before winners are announced. The program has awarded more than $115,500 in cash since 2018, plus over $43,000 in goods and services.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must be a mom, including expecting mothers, stepmoms and foster moms
- Must own at least 50% of a for-profit business
- Annual revenue between $10,000 and $500,000 over the past 12 months
- Business headquartered in the US or Canada

2026 CYCLE: applications open September 1 and close September 30, 2026. Judging October 1-19; public voting October 19-26; winner announced October 27, 2026.

The Deadline field holds the expected OPEN date (9/1/2026) per the Coming Soon convention; the closing date is 9/30/2026.

2025 prize structure was $10,000 grand prize, $5,000 first runner-up, $2,500 second runner-up, and $1,000 for five honorable mentions. The 2026 breakdown is not published yet.

Name: Innovate Grant
Description: Innovate Grant awards two unrestricted $1,800 grants per quarter, one to a visual artist and one to a photographer. The application is intentionally brief, requiring only basic contact information and 3–10 images of work, and is open to artists and photographers 18 and older worldwide. Previous winners are eligible to reapply after five years, and there is no limit on the number of applications submitted per cycle.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Visual Artists and Photographers 18 years and older, from all around the world, US + International, are eligible to apply. All media and genres are accepted:

Art
- Painting
- Printmaking
- Drawing
- Sculpture
- Film / Video
- Mixed Media
- Installation
- New Media
- Photography

Portrait
- Conceptual
- Still Life
- Black + White
- Documentary
- Street
- Composite
- Collage

Name: Giving Joy Grant
Description: Giving Joy is a global nonprofit that awards one-time micro-grants of up to $500 to women entrepreneurs worldwide, providing critical resources to start or sustain businesses, acquire skills, and advance gender equality. Since its founding in 2018, the organization has funded 102 women across 35 countries, and grantees gain access to an exclusive online alumni community after receiving their award.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility/ FAQ: 
Who can apply for a Giving Joy grant?
Women ages 18 and up.  

Do I have to own a business to apply?
No. You can use the grant to start a new business, or expand your existing business. You can also use the grant to start or expand a nonprofit, non-governmental organization (NGO), charity, or propose a specific activity or project you would like to implement.          

Are the grants limited to a certain geography?
No. You can apply for a grant from any country or state or territory in the world. 

Are the grants limited to a specific field (like health)?
Absolutely not. You can propose activities in any field, trade, occupation, or craft. However, your business/organization/idea must focus on women, girls and/or families. And all activities must be LEGAL!

Name: mHUB Chicago Founder Access Initiative
Description: The Founder Access Initiative is a fully sponsored program for West Side Chicago hardtech founders that provides six months of mHUB shared workspace access, personalized support, mentorship, and use of prototyping labs and resources. It is open to founders building physical products who live in Austin, Humboldt Park, Garfield Park, or North Lawndale.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: This program is open to founders building physical products. To qualify, participants must be a resident of one of these Chicago West Side neighborhoods – Austin, Humboldt Park, Garfield Park, and North Lawndale.

Name: Fresno Expanded Access to Arts and Culture (EAAC) Grant Program
Description: The Expanded Access to Arts and Culture Grant Program offers $1,000–$75,000 for individual artists and unincorporated groups developing publicly accessible cultural projects for Fresno residents. ACTA is accepting up to 10 fiscal sponsorship applicants, with priority for traditional arts, folklife, cultural heritage, and community-based cultural traditions; ACTA will retain a 10% administrative fee from awarded funds. Eligibility screenings are due August 15, 2026, and full applications are due September 30, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
ACTA is looking for traditional artists, folk artists, and culture bearers to be our fiscal sponsees. 

Folk and traditional arts are part of a community’s daily life and culture. They come from groups of people who share a common background, such as language, history, beliefs, work, or place. These art forms are learned and passed on from one generation to the next through families, elders, and community members. By learning together, practicing, and sharing skills, these traditions stay active, grow over time, and continue to support strong communities.

Projects can include any kind of traditional art, such as:⁠

Dance⁠
Music⁠
Food traditions⁠
Crafts and material arts⁠
Storytelling and oral traditions⁠
And other cultural practices⁠

Name: Detroit NextUp 313
Description: NextUP 313 supports Detroit residents ages 18–30 through entrepreneurship education, business training, networking, microinternships, pop-up retail opportunities, and connections to local small business and technology startup resources. Eligible participants may also apply for grant funding through a competitive application process designed to help young founders launch and grow businesses in Detroit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Detroit Resident
- Between the Ages of 18-30
- Interested in learning about entrepreneurship and innovation

Name: Eddie C. and C. Sylvia Brown Family Foundation Grant
Description: Thirty-plus years of family philanthropy focused on Baltimore's African American community, administered by the Baltimore Community Foundation. Four priorities: mental health services in African American communities, cancer prevention and treatment, youth arts programming (often featuring African American artists), and K-12 educational enrichment for disadvantaged children. Strong preference for programs serving a core group of children or youth over an extended period.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits only — applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities that do not discriminate on the basis of race, creed, national origin, color, physical handicap, gender or sexual orientation.
