Individuals and for-profit businesses are not eligible. Baltimore metropolitan area only. Significant exclusions: will not fund new organizations or new programs, capital projects, individuals, multi-year grants, or higher-education institutions. Applications accepted July 1 - September 30, 2026 via the GoApply portal at goapply2.akoyago.com/bcf. No application fee. Contact: Maya Smith, Program Administrator, msmith@bcf.org.
Industry: Nonprofit,Health / Wellness,Education & Child Care,Visual & Fine Arts,Community-Based Organization

Name: Louisiana Nexus Technology Cup
Description: The Nexus Technology Cup is a statewide competition for Louisiana founders, independent developers, college teams, and high school students building prototype-stage or more advanced software, hardware, and technology-enabled solutions. Participants compete across separate tracks for a share of $150,000 in prizes and the opportunity to present their work to investors, corporate partners, and leaders in Louisiana’s technology ecosystem.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Open Track
For founders and independent builders developing scalable, market-ready technology.

Open to Louisiana-based entrepreneurs, early-stage startups, and independent developers.
Teams may include professionals, hobbyists, and industry enthusiasts.
Projects must be in the prototype stage or beyond (no conceptual-only ideas).

Name: SoCal Asian Pacific Community Fund Operating Grant
Description: APCF's Operating Grant provides flexible core operating support to nonprofits serving low-income or underserved Asian American and Pacific Islander communities in Southern California. Beyond funding, APCF emphasizes long-term partnerships and capacity-building resources to strengthen the local AAPI nonprofit sector.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits serving low-income or underserved AAPI communities locally and meeting the specific strategic criteria for the grant.

Name: Queens Economic Development Corp Flash Grants
Description: The QEDC Flash Grants program, sponsored by Maspeth Federal Savings, will award $1,000 each to five Queens small businesses to cover practical needs such as repairs, updates, equipment, or other small expenses. Eligible operating or soon-to-open Queens businesses, including home-based businesses, must complete a QEDC intake form and submit a one-paragraph explanation of how they would use the funds.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- All applicants must complete a standard QEDC client intake form and one-paragraph pitch by 11:59PM on September 30 to be considered for funding.
- Businesses must be currently operating or have imminiment plans to open in Queens. Home-based businesses from Queens residents are eligible.
- Only businesses are eligible. Non-profits, government entities, political organizations, and private individuals are ineligible.
- Winners will be selected at the sole discretion of QEDC and Maspeth Federal Savings. Applications do not guarantee funding.
- All applicants agree to receiving communications from QEDC and Maspeth Federal Savings about this initiative and other programs/offers.
- Applicants agree that if they are selected, that QEDC and Maspeth Federal Savings may use their name, description, and relevant imagery in marketing and communication related to this program.

Name: Baton Rouge Front Door Refresh Facade Grant
Description: Build EBR offers grant funding to small businesses and commercial property owners for storefront and exterior improvements along the Plank Road corridor. Eligible work includes storefront renovation, exterior painting, facade restoration, signage, awnings, landscaping and accessibility upgrades. The program can cover up to 100 percent of eligible project costs subject to program caps, and requires a pre-application, site visit, full application with contractor estimates, and committee and board approval.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Small businesses and commercial property owners along the Plank Road corridor
- Initial phase limited to Plank Road between North 22nd Street and Clayton Street
- Grant may cover up to 100% of eligible project costs, subject to program caps - no match stated
- Eligible work: storefront renovation, exterior painting, facade restoration, signage, awnings/canopies, landscaping, accessibility improvements
- Seven-step process: pre-application, site visit, design/scope, full application with contractor estimates, Grant Committee scoring, Board approval, construction
- Program operates only while grant funds are available

Applications opened July 2026.

Name: She Believed She Could Impact Grant
Description: The Emerging Founder Grant supports female entrepreneurs building early-stage businesses with strong potential for growth, innovation, and impact. The recipient receives a $2,500 cash grant plus a private half-day strategy intensive covering areas such as brand positioning, marketing and audience growth, partnerships, fundraising, and revenue strategy, along with visibility through the She Believed She Could network. Applicants are evaluated based on demonstrated impact, leadership and vision, growth potential, and commitment to serving others and creating meaningful change.

Name: Inland Empire Nonprofit Loan Fund
Description: A revolving loan fund from the Inland Empire Community Foundation offering below-market-rate loans of $100,000 to $400,000 to established nonprofits serving the City of Riverside or San Bernardino County. As borrowers repay, the capital revolves back out to other nonprofits in the region.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Nonprofits only — open exclusively to 501(c)(3) organizations. Applicants must have a minimum $500,000 in annual revenue, demonstrate an unrestricted operating surplus in two of the last three years, and serve residents of the City of Riverside or San Bernardino County. Application round runs Sept 1-30, 2026. Applicants begin by completing an online Assessment Survey to determine eligibility and apply. Rates are below-market; specific interest rates and repayment terms are not published.

Name: LA County Financial Clinic
Description: A no-cost technical assistance program launched by the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity in August 2026 to strengthen small business financial health. Participants receive one-on-one coaching, a financial assessment, educational workshops, debt management support, and help with budgeting, cash-flow management, capital readiness and credit building. The program is aimed at owners preparing to access capital or stabilise their finances.
Amount: In-kind - free one-on-one financial coaching, assessment and workshops
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business located in Los Angeles County with 100 or fewer employees and $19 million or less in annual revenue. No cost to participate. Announcement: https://opportunity.lacounty.gov/la-county-launches-new-technical-assistance-programs-to-help-small-businesses-access-capital-and-strengthen-financial-health/

Name: PDX Retail Residency Program
Description: The Port of Portland offers locally based businesses a 12-month residency in move-in-ready retail space at Portland International Airport. Two businesses are selected per cycle and receive a 500-square-foot turnkey storefront, dedicated storage at no cost, and ongoing support, education and mentoring from Port staff. Rent is charged at 10% of gross sales rather than a fixed lease. Residencies from the current cycle begin in early March 2027.
Amount: In-kind - 500 sq ft turnkey airport storefront, rent at 10% of gross sales, free storage, mentoring
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must have a current brick-and-mortar location in Oregon or Southwest Washington; annual gross sales $500,000-$2,000,000; owner with at least two consecutive years operating the business; retail or grab-and-go food only (no on-site food preparation). Application window September 1-30, 2026. Two businesses selected. Residencies begin early March 2027.

Name: Ascend ABQ Small Business Concessions Program
Description: Albuquerque International Sunport's small business concessions program creates a pathway for local businesses into airport retail. Nine concessionaires operate six Retail Merchandising Units across the airport under short-term, low-risk agreements of three to twelve months, renewable. Selected businesses complete a two-to-three-week in-person Boot Camp, gain exposure to thousands of daily travelers, and access industry networking and potential wholesale opportunities.
Amount: In-kind - Retail Merchandising Unit space (3-12 month renewable terms) plus Boot Camp training
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Small, local and regional New Mexico businesses. Selection via application review, on-site business evaluation and interviews. Direct application: https://ascendabqapp.paperform.co/ - submit by September 30, 2026 for the Class of 2027 (begins spring 2027); later submissions reviewed for future cycles. Contact: Ebony Gaynor, EGaynor@CABQ.GOV.

Name: South Arts Emerging Traditional Artists Program
Description: South Arts awards $5,000 to early-career folk and traditional artists in the Southeast, paid in a single installment at the start of the award period. Eligibility covers Central Appalachia and Delta Regional Authority counties across Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North and South Carolina and Tennessee, plus members of state or federally recognized tribes. A two-year residency is required. Awardees are notified by December 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual folk/traditional artists, early career. 18+ by deadline, US citizen or permanent resident. Two-year residency in eligible Central Appalachia or Delta Regional Authority counties across AL, GA, KY, LA, MS, NC, SC, TN - or membership of a state or federally recognized tribe. Past ETAP or In These Mountains Master Artist Fellowship awardees ineligible. Portal opened 2026-07-15; awardees notified by 2026-12-01.

Name: Community Foundation of Monroe County – Pocono Mountain Free Art and Craft Workshops Grant
Description: Funds at least two free arts and craft workshops each year in Monroe County, PA. Workshops must be free to attend; organizations and businesses must have legal standing, and individual artists apply through a fiscal sponsor. Applications are submitted through the grant portal linked at the top of the foundation’s Grants page. Contact Samantha Holbert at director@cfmcpa.org or 570-213-9083.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Organizations and businesses with legal standing; individual artists need a fiscal sponsor. Workshops must be free to attend and held in Monroe County, PA. Application window September 1–30 each year.

Name: Community Foundation of Monroe County – Myra Kyle Fund for the Arts Grant
Description: The Myra Kyle Fund for the Arts awards grants to support community arts projects and programs organized by individuals, arts organizations, businesses and nonprofits. Projects must benefit the public in Monroe County, PA; organizations and businesses must have legal standing, and individual artists apply through a fiscal sponsor. Applications are submitted through the grant portal linked at the top of the foundation’s Grants page. Contact Samantha Holbert at director@cfmcpa.org or 570-213-9083.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individuals, arts organizations, businesses and nonprofits with legal standing; individual artists need a fiscal sponsor. Projects must benefit the public in Monroe County, PA. Application window September 1–30 each year.

Name: Utah Economic Assistance Grant (Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity)
Description: The State of Utah's Economic Assistance Grant funds one-time projects by for-profit or nonprofit entities whose principal place of business is in Utah and that are registered in good standing with the Utah Division of Corporations and Commercial Code. Projects serve industry, education, community development or infrastructure, with priority for projects that develop Utah's five targeted industries, and must be completed within 18 months of award. Applicants are expected to leverage other funding sources or propose matching funds, though no set match percentage is required. The FY 2027 cycle has $4.5 million available. Apply through the GOEO grant portal; new users must request a portal account first (about one business day to process). Questions: (801) 538-8680, with "EAG" in the subject line of emails.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit or nonprofit entities with principal place of business in Utah, registered in good standing with the Utah Division of Corporations and Commercial Code; government entities excluded. Projects in industry, education, community development or infrastructure; priority for Utah's five targeted industries. Project must be completed within 18 months. Matching/leveraged funds expected (no set percentage). FY 2027 window: Sept 15, 2026 9am MDT to Sept 30, 2026 5pm MDT.

Name: Marblehead Artisans' Holiday Marketplace Vendor Application
Description: The Marblehead Festival of Arts runs a juried Artisans' Holiday Marketplace on 5-6 December 2026 at Abbot Hall in Marblehead, Massachusetts, with roughly 20 vendor spaces. Applications are open 1-30 September 2026 and are reviewed by a three- to five-person jury, with acceptances issued in the first week of October. Artists and artisans submit photos of new work and a table setup.
Amount: In-kind: juried vendor space at a two-day holiday market
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to artists and artisans. Application requires 3-5 photos of new work, a photo of the table setup and a short description. Applications open 1-30 September 2026; a 3-5 person jury selects vendors and notifies applicants in the first week of October. Event 5-6 December 2026 (Sat 10am-5pm, Sun 10am-4pm), top floor of Abbot Hall, Marblehead MA; approximately 20 spaces. Booth fees due 15 October 2026: $250 for approx 8'x10', $175 for approx 5'x10'. Accepted vendors are asked to donate 2-3 dozen baked goods for the public cookie table. Apply by creating a profile at Users.marbleheadfestival.org and selecting 'Artisans Market-Marketplaces'.

Name: Motor City Match Grant
Description: Supports Detroit-based entrepreneurs at every stage - from idea to expansion. Offers grants and expert support to help launch or grow businesses in Detroit’s commercial corridors. Winners must commit to staying in Detroit for 3+ years and show job creation or community benefit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who Can Apply for Motor City Match
- New businesses seeking to open in the city of Detroit in a currently vacant commercial space.
- New businesses just starting out that are not yet operational
- Operational businesses opening in their first permanent location
- Operational businesses opening a new, additional location

Applicants must also be…
- For-profit businesses connected to Detroit by residency or location.

Connected by residency
- Businesses applying to the Plan or Develop Track that do not have a location in Detroit must be residents of the city of Detroit to be eligible

Connected by location
- Businesses applying to the Design or Cash Track must have a location secured in the city of Detroit with a letter of intent, lease, deed, land contract, or other legal claim

Name: Buffalo Institute for Art Micro Grant
Description: The BICA Microgrant offers a no-strings-attached $300 grant to artists and curators producing exhibitions, performances, or other visual arts projects in the greater Buffalo area. Projects must include at least one public event and occur within three months before or after the application date. Applications are submitted online and are due quarterly on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1.

Name: Atherton Family Foundation
Description: The Atherton Family Foundation Capital Grant supports Hawai‘i-serving nonprofits with tangible capital assets such as equipment, vehicles, buildings, or other depreciable improvements; the average capital award is about $41,500. Applicants must be a 501(c)(3) or apply through a qualified fiscal sponsor, and technology-related requests require a 1:1 match.

Name: USDA Cold Chain Grants for Emergency Food Assistance
Description: USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service awards competitive funding to nonprofit corporations that administer subaward programs distributing cold storage and distribution equipment. Subawards go to food banks, food pantries, and other emergency food assistance operations so they can handle meat, eggs, seafood, dairy, and fresh produce. The goal is expanding cold chain capacity so vulnerable populations can access perishable foods from American farmers.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Prime applicants must be nonprofit corporations with 501(c)(3) status
- Must demonstrate capacity to run a competitive subaward program: solicitation, review, award, and oversight
- Must be located in the 50 states, DC, or listed U.S. territories
- No cost share at prime level; 10% cash cost share required at the subaward level
- Subawards cover cold chain equipment plus documented delivery, installation, and ancillary supplies

Approximately $7.5 million total available. Applications due October 1, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. Contact: AMS.CCG@usda.gov

Name: Spokane Wildfires DoorDash Local Business Disaster Relief Fund
Description: DoorDash's Local Business Disaster Relief Fund is running a round for local businesses damaged by the Spokane wildfires. Grants of five thousand dollars, drawn from a fifty thousand dollar commitment, help cover expenses such as rent, repairs, lost inventory and payroll. Applicants must be brick-and-mortar businesses in eligible categories with three or fewer locations, fifty or fewer employees per location, and three million dollars or less in revenue.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Brick-and-mortar business impacted by the Spokane wildfires
- Eligible categories: restaurants, flower shops, liquor stores, convenience stores, pet stores, local grocery stores
- 3 or fewer locations; 50 or fewer employees per location
- Open at least six months; $3M or less in revenue per location
- No DoorDash partnership required

Applications close 10/1/2026. Notification within 30 days of the deadline; funds distributed the month after the application period closes. Administered through Hello Alice. $50,000 is the total round commitment; the per-business award is $5,000.

Name: Black Public Media 2026 Open Call
Description: Black Public Media funds and develops nonfiction feature-length projects (60 minutes or longer) in pre-production, production, or early post-production. Five selected projects receive $20,000 and enter BPM's talent development program, and become eligible to pitch at PitchBLACK 2027 for production funding of up to $150,000. BPM funding awards are structured as licensing agreements for public media distribution rather than grants.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Applicant must be the producer or director and a U.S. citizen with at least three years of professional experience (or have a senior producer attached), and must hold artistic control, budgetary oversight and copyright. Project must be nonfiction and feature-length (60+ minutes) in pre-production, production or early post-production. At least one key team member must be of African descent or a person of color. No foreign-based or student projects.

Name: Jamestown Arts Center Holiday Arts Market Call for Artists
Description: The Jamestown Arts Center in Rhode Island juries artists and makers into its two-day Holiday Arts Market, held as a Friday-evening pre-party and Saturday public shopping day in December 2026. Painters, jewellers, potters, sculptors, clothing designers, photographers, woodworkers and glass artists are all eligible. Vendors staff their own table for both days; electricity is provided and table sizes range from half to L-shaped.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to painters, jewelers, potters, sculptors, clothing designers, photographers, woodworkers, glass artists and similar makers. All submissions juried for artistic quality and diversity. Vendors must staff their booth both days. Fees: half table $95, full table $185, L-shaped table $250 (limited, first come), additional wall space $30. Acceptance notification 2026-10-17; payment due 2026-11-21. Event Dec 4 (5:30-7:30pm pre-party) and Dec 5, 2026 (10am-4pm). Spaces approx 4'x6'. Contact artsmarket@jamestownartcenter.org.

Name: Start:ME Accelerator (Atlanta)
Description: Free 14-week community-based accelerator for microentrepreneurs in four under-resourced metro Atlanta neighborhoods, run by Emory University's Goizueta Business School with community nonprofit partners. Participants get business training, a volunteer mentor team, and access to networks and capital. At graduation, cohort members peer-select which businesses receive grant capital: Grow Grants of $4,000-$5,000, Start Grants of $1,000-$3,000, and $500 recognition awards. More than $552,000 in peer-selected capital has gone to 583 ventures across 37 cohorts since 2013.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to for-profit small businesses — 97% of alumni operate for-profits. Nonprofits may apply only if they generate the majority of revenue from product or service sales. Hard geographic requirement: the applicant must live, work, or provide services in one of four metro Atlanta communities — Clarkston (incl. Avondale, North Decatur, Scottdale, Stone Mountain, Tucker), East Lake (East Lake, Edgewood, Kirkwood), Atlanta's Southside (south of I-20, Fort McPherson to Thomasville Heights), or Atlanta's Westside (Bankhead, Center Hill, Vine City and others). Entrepreneurs with no tie to a community are not eligible. No stage, sales, or profitability requirement — idea-stage through operating businesses; the 2026 cohort had median revenue of $13,000. Free for all selected entrepreneurs. Winter 2027 applications opened September 1, 2026 and close October 1, 2026; the program runs 14 weeks, January-April 2027. Grants are peer-selected at graduation and are not guaranteed to every participant.

Name: Santa Monica Small Business Relief Microgrant Program
Description: The City of Santa Monica has launched a $100,000 microgrant fund awarding one-time $5,000 grants to roughly 20 existing brick-and-mortar small businesses in the city. The program is intended to help retain locally owned businesses, encourage investment in commercial corridors and support storefront activation. The first round closes 1 October 2026, with awards announced in early November; further rounds open while funds remain.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Existing brick-and-mortar businesses physically located in Santa Monica, CA. One-time $5,000 grant; approximately 20 awards from a $100,000 fund. First round 16 Sept - 1 Oct 2026; additional rounds will open while funds remain. Guidelines published in English and Spanish. Technical-assistance workshops held 15 and 17 Sept 2026. Contact Business.Concierge@santamonica.gov. Announcement: https://www.santamonica.gov/press/2026/09/16/city-of-santa-monica-launches-100-000-small-business-relief-microgrant-program

Name: Skip $10,000 Grants
Description: Skip's $10,000 Grants program awards $10,000 cash grants to U.S.-based entrepreneurs and small business owners aged 18 and over. One $10,000 grant is open to all eligible applicants. Skip runs multiple rounds each year, including year-end, spring, and summer cycles, each with its own application window and deadline.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility and how to apply:
- All U.S.-based entrepreneurs and small business owners, age 18+
- By entering, you agree to the Official Terms
- Click Start Applying and complete all required questions
- Click Submit Application before the deadline; no late applications are accepted

Grant structure:
- 1 x $10,000 grant open to all eligible applicants

Name: Oregon Metro Community Placemaking Grant
Description: Metro’s Community Placemaking Grant supports community-led, equity-focused projects using arts and culture to strengthen connections between people and the places they care about. Examples include cultural festivals, public art, storytelling, youth arts programs, community workshops, and other creative placemaking activities.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) nonprofits; community groups or individuals working with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor; public agencies/institutions; and Tribes. Businesses and individuals without a nonprofit partner are not eligible. Projects must be community-led, arts/culture-based, equity-focused, and take place within Metro’s Urban Growth Boundary; operating-support-only proposals are not eligible.
Industry: Community-Based Organization,Arts & Crafts,Education & Child Care,Social Impact

Name: Maine Solid Waste Diversion Grant Program
Description: The Maine Department of Environmental Protection funds projects that keep material out of disposal through organics diversion, source reduction, upcycling and reuse, composting and digestion. Municipalities, regional associations and Maine businesses may all apply, though statute directs the Department to give highest priority to municipal and regional association applicants. Proposals referencing landfilling or waste-to-energy incineration are not considered.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Municipalities, regional associations, AND Maine businesses are all eligible
- IMPORTANT: statute directs DEP to give HIGHEST PRIORITY to municipal and regional association applicants, so a for-profit business competes at a disadvantage
- Projects must involve organic waste diversion education, source reduction, upcycling and material reuse, or composting and digestion
- Proposals referencing landfilling or waste-to-energy incineration WILL NOT be considered

PRIORITY GIVEN TO: expanding composting infrastructure, increasing organics recovery, education and outreach, pilot programs, serving underserved areas, regional economies of scale, and reuse/repair initiatives.

Applications are submitted through Maine's Vendor Self Service (VSS) procurement portal, not a DEP form. Contact: David R. Madore, Deputy Commissioner, david.madore@maine.gov

Rounds run on varying schedules including special organics rounds - check the current RFP rather than assuming an annual date.

Name: Anoka Rumriver Art Center Holiday Art Market Call for Artists
Description: Rumriver Art Center in Anoka, Minnesota selects artists, crafters and makers for a five-week consignment holiday market running mid-November to mid-December 2026. There is no application fee; the centre takes a 35 percent commission on sales and handles selling, so artists do not staff a booth. Handmade work only, with AI-generated content expressly barred and a fifty-item cap per artist.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to all ages - community art centre. Work must be handmade; no AI-generated content. Minimum 3 artwork images required. Maximum 50 items plus up to 50 additional cards/prints/stickers. All items must be for sale. In-person drop-off and pickup required. Rumriver takes 35% commission on sale price. No application fee. Notifications by 2026-10-16. Market runs Nov 14 - Dec 19, 2026 at 2665 4th Avenue, Suite 103, Anoka MN.

Name: Feet First Philly Public Space Enhancement Mini-Grant
Description: The Public Space Enhancement Mini-Grant supports Philadelphia communities in making their neighborhoods safer, more accessible, and easier to walk and roll in. It prioritizes communities that have historically experienced less investment in the built environment and city services, and has funded projects such as asphalt art crosswalks and other small-scale public-space improvements.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Designed for community-led projects that improve walkability and public spaces. Feet First Philly emphasizes resident-led ideas and prioritizes communities historically experiencing underinvestment. Awardees generally submit a brief interim report and final report.

Name: David Amarri Foundation Grant Program
Description: The David Amarri Foundation supports emerging BIPOC artists and cultural producers in Chicago, honoring David Amarri Richard’s commitment to elevating artists of color. Its micro-grants support a broad range of creative practices, including film, photography, digital art, painting, sculpture, crafts, writing, music, and arts/event production.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
All applicants must be:
- a practicing artist, artisan, maker, curator or cultural producer of art/events in the City of Chicago 
- 29 years of age or younger at the time of application 
- identify as BIPOC
- a U.S. Citizen
- a resident of the City of Chicago (proof of residency will be required before receiving the grant) 

You are ineligible if you:
- create art that is mass produced and/or made outside of the United States
- want to create an event that does not take place in the City of Chicago
are affiliated with Found Objects (employees, board members, past recipients)

Name: Tech Turtle Small Business Growth Grant
Description: Tech Turtle is awarding $50,000 in combined in-kind website, marketing and technology services to nine Wisconsin small businesses. One Grand Growth Grant carries up to $10,000 in value, with four Digital Growth Grants and four Lead and Technology Growth Grants worth up to five thousand each. Services span website design, local SEO, analytics, conversion optimisation, CRM implementation and marketing automation.
Amount: up to $10,000 in in-kind services (1 award); up to $5,000 each (8 awards)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Must operate a legitimate small business with an active Wisconsin presence
- Must primarily serve Wisconsin customers
- Must demonstrate a genuine business need
- Applicant must have authority to represent the business

AWARD STRUCTURE (9 recipients, $50,000 total retail value):
- 1 x Grand Growth Grant, up to $10,000 value
- 4 x Digital Growth Grants, up to $5,000 each
- 4 x Lead & Technology Growth Grants, up to $5,000 each

IN-KIND ONLY - no cash is awarded. Services may include website design, local SEO, analytics setup, conversion optimisation, lead-generation infrastructure, CRM implementation, LeadRilo platform access and marketing automation, customised per recipient.

Applications open September 1, 2026; deadline October 31, 2026. No application fee and no purchase required. Selection is merit-based competitive review, not a random drawing.

Note: privately funded by a vendor whose own services form the award - the value is real but is delivered as that vendor's work rather than funds the business directs.

Name: Elevance Health Foundation Grant
Description: The Elevance Health Foundation funds community-based nonprofits working to improve health outcomes in under-resourced communities across four focus areas: Maternal/Infant Health, Food as Medicine, Behavioral Health, and Community Resiliency & Disaster Relief. Grants generally range from one to three years, with funding levels determined based on the need and proposed plan. Of the four areas, only Maternal/Infant Health is currently accepting applications, with a deadline of July 31, 2026 — the other two open categories will accept applications again in 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Maternal/ Infant Health: [Open] 
The Foundation will prioritize funding for programs that improve maternal/infant health, target disparities, address social needs, and remove barriers to care throughout the pregnancy journey—from pre-conception support to postnatal care for mothers and babies. The programs should drive specific, measurable maternal/infant health outcomes.

Locations
Elevance Health Foundation will consider proposals from qualified nonprofit organizations across the U.S. with an emphasis on:
National programs. Promoting scalable and sustainable systemic change.
or
Local programs. Implementing relevant interventions in California, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Ohio, Texas, and Virginia.

Grant Program Goals

Reducing disparities in pre-term birth rates
Reducing disparities in severe maternal morbidity (SMM) incidence
Improving maternal/infant health outcomes
Request for Proposal
Download the Maternal/Infant Health RFP

Apply
Application Deadline: July 31, 2026
Please check back in June for the application.


Food as Medicine: [CLOSED; open in 2027] 
The Foundation will prioritize funding for programs that improve clinical health outcomes for individuals with diet-related conditions and increase access to nutritious foods for populations experiencing food/nutrition insecurity.

Locations
Elevance Health will consider proposals from qualified organizations across the U.S. with an emphasis on:
National programs. Promoting scalable and sustainable systemic change.
or
Local programs. Implementing relevant interventions in California, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Ohio, Texas, and Virginia.

Grant Program Goals

Improving clinical outcomes for individuals with diet-related conditions experiencing high social risk
Increasing access to nutritious foods for populations experiencing high social risk and food/nutrition insecurity
Request for Proposal
Download the Food as Medicine RFP

Apply
Grant applications will be accepted again in 2027.




Behavioral Health [CLOSED; Open in 2027]
The Foundation will prioritize funding for programs that increase the number of individuals receiving treatment for mental health (MH) and/or substance use disorders (SUD), support prevention and early-intervention strategies, and seek to reduce loneliness among individuals with these disorders.

Locations
Elevance Health will consider proposals from qualified organizations across the U.S. with an emphasis on:
National programs. Promoting scalable and sustainable systemic change.
or
Local programs. Implementing relevant interventions in California, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Ohio, Texas, and Virginia.

Grant Program Goals

Achieve a percent increase in the number of individuals receiving treatment services for MH and/or SUD
Support prevention and early intervention strategies to reduce risks and harms associated with MH and/or SUD through screenings
Reduce feelings of loneliness among individuals with MH and/or SUD
Request for Proposal
Download the Behavioral Health RFP

Apply
Grant applications will be accepted again in 2027.

Name: Amplifier Grant
Description: The Amplifier Grant is a fund by The Outrage accepting applications on a rolling basis with at least $5,000 in funds awarded on a seasonal basis (ie. Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall) to individuals & businesses trying to make the world a better place.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: All entities ranging from high school projects, grassroots organizations, nonprofits, startups, businesses, and more are encouraged to apply.

Name: Downtown Orlando Facade Program
Description: The Downtown Orlando (DTO) Facade Program provides funding to encourage property and business owners to invest in renovations that rehabilitate and enhance their buildings. Eligible properties include commercial and certain residential buildings located within designated Focus Areas. Commercial buildings may receive up to $200,000 or 80% of the total cost of façade improvements, roof repairs, or roof replacements (whichever is less).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See for specific details about eligibility: https://www.downtownorlando.com/files/sharedassets/downtown/v/1/business/dto-fa%C3%A7ade-program-12.9.24.pdf

Name: Downtown Orlando Retail Program
Description: The Downtown Orlando (DTO) Retail Program aims to activate spaces within the Downtown Orlando Community Redevelopment Area by establishing the area as a retail destination. The program supports new and expanding retail businesses by reimbursing costs related to interior buildout and rent for newly leased properties, helping attract locals, visitors, and new retail to downtown Orlando.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: See for specific details about eligibility: https://www.downtownorlando.com/files/sharedassets/downtown/v/1/business/new-dto-retail-program-1.17.25.pdf

Name: Truist Foundation Fellowship
Description: This 16-week accelerator program supports small business owners, nonprofit leaders, and entrepreneurs driving impact in underserved or underbanked communities across the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, and South Central U.S. regions. Designed for ventures operating 1–5 years with under 10 employees, the program offers expert-led training, mentorship, peer learning, and leadership opportunities to help participants scale their organizations and deepen community impact. Participants must commit fully to the program’s workshops and immersive sessions, fostering an engaged, collaborative environment for shared growth and innovation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
- You are a small business owner, nonprofit leader, or entrepreneur with proven results building solutions for underbanked or underserved communities. This could include strengthening small businesses, building career pathways to economic mobility, and fostering thriving communities.

Your Business Stage:
- Your business or organization has been operating for 1-5 years with fewer than 10 employees. You have engaged customers, measurable results, and have secured some funding through grants, investments, donations, or revenue, but you’re ready to grow to the next level.

Your Commitment:
- You must be able to commit to the full 16-week program, including the mandatory one-day in-person Immersive and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM Eastern Time. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.

Where You Work:
- Located in and creating impact across rural and urban communities throughout:
- Southeast: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee;
- Mid-Atlantic: Maryland, Virginia, Washington D.C., and West Virginia;
- Northeast: New Jersey and Pennsylvania;
- South Central: Texas and Ohio.

What You Are Looking For:
- You seek expert-guided entrepreneurial training, a supportive community for feedback, a broad mentor network to enhance your leadership, and opportunities to challenge yourself by leading a Basecamp event and other initiatives that benefit your venture and community. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset to this work.

Demographics:
- Adults 18 or Older.

Name: NYC Risk Assessment and Preparedness Grant
Description: NYC program offering assessments and grants to help small businesses improve emergency preparedness and resilience.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Eligible NYC small businesses; participation in assessment may be required.

Name: Detroit Tech Fellowship
Description: The Detroit Tech Fellowship is a City of Detroit initiative for recent Michigan university graduates building startups, aimed at keeping and scaling high-potential ventures in Detroit and the state. Fellows receive a $2,000/month stipend for one year for living expenses plus yearlong coworking memberships at Bamboo (Downtown & Midtown), TechTown Detroit, and potentially Newlab Detroit, totaling about $31,680 in support. The program is sponsored by the Detroit Economic Growth Corporation and the City of Detroit with support from the Michigan Growth Office and partner spaces.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Detroit Tech Fellowship is looking for founders and entrepreneurs who:
- Graduated from a Michigan college or university from May 2022 and onward. Graduates may be current Michigan residents or living out-of-state but preference will be given to applicants who express willingness to live in the same building as other Detroit Tech Fellows, to strengthen the cohort experience.
- Will stay in Detroit, Michigan for a minimum of 12 consecutive months while participating in the fellowship program.
- Are a founder of an established, venture backable startup with fewer than 10 employees.
- Demonstrate interest in remaining in Detroit beyond the fellowship and will commit to engaging in local startup ecosystem spaces during the fellowship.
- Will commit to working at least 40 hours per week on scaling their startup and will not hold full-time employment elsewhere during the fellowship.

Name: Wells Fargo Grant
Description: Wells Fargo and the Wells Fargo Foundation fund nonprofits that align with their priority areas – financial opportunity, housing access/affordability, and small business growth. Eligible organizations must be 501(c)(3) (or qualified public/tribal/government entities), show fiscal stability, address critical community needs, and be able to measure/report outcomes. Invited nonprofits apply with a code, and others that fit the focus areas can submit a grant interest form.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To receive funding for any type of grant, organizations must meet the following:
- Have tax exempt status under IRS code 501(c)(3), or be a qualified governmental agency, tribal entity or public school or school system
- Demonstrate fiscal and administrative stability and
- Deliver services addressing critical community needs

Name: Wells Fargo Small Business Fellowship
Description: The Wells Fargo Small Business Fellowship is a fully funded 16-week program (run with Watson Institute) for small business owners, entrepreneurs, and nonprofit leaders who strengthen local small-business ecosystems in Baltimore, Chicago, and Washington, D.C. Fellows receive expert-led business and leadership workshops, mentorship and capital connections, plus pitch training and the opportunity to lead a short “Basecamp” workshop and present at an in-person Summit.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
'- Located in and creating impact in Baltimore, Chicago, and Washington D.C
- Adults 18 or Older
- You must be able to commit to the full 16-week program, including the mandatory one-day in-person Immersive and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 10:30 AM – 12:30 PM Eastern Time. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.
- You have engaged customers, measurable results, and have produced roughly $100,000 in revenue and/or managed operations with a budget of approximately $100,000. (All legal business structures welcome: for-profit, nonprofit, social enterprise, etc.)
- You are a small business owner, nonprofit leader, or entrepreneur with proven results supporting other businesses or connecting individuals to financial products and services in underserved communities. We prioritize:
- Small Business Owners Who Amplify Other Small Businesses: You lead a business that uplifts and amplifies your community’s small business ecosystem (e.g., selling products to small businesses, tech, business consulting, marketing services, training, among others). Your work connects other entrepreneurs to resources, growth opportunities, and financial products like business checking accounts, business loans, merchant services, and more.
- Small Business Owners Who Increase Access to Financial Products and Services: You connect individuals in your community to tangible financial products and services like checking accounts, home mortgages, home equity lines, financial literacy, credit building, and more.

Name: Comcast Innovation Fund
Description: The Comcast Innovation Fund supports technologists, researchers, and academics working on Internet- and connectivity-related research or open-source development, with 2026 focus areas including low-latency networking, Wi-Fi performance, AI/edge computing, live video streaming latency, and quantum-related cybersecurity and network optimization. Grants are typically in the ~$3,000–$150,000 range, awarded through a two-step process (pre-qualification form first, then an invited full application), and are generally for one-year projects with no indirect/overhead costs covered. The program is open to applicants globally and runs annually until that year’s funding is exhausted.

Name: Black Leaders Detroit Black History Month Grant
Description: For Black History Month, Black Leaders Detroit is investing in Detroit nonprofits doing impactful work. 20 nonprofits will receive a grant of $5,000 each, for a total award pool of $100,000. You must be a Black Leaders Detroit member to nominate a nonprofit.

Name: Advancing Black Businesses Foundation (ABBF) Small Business Revitalization (SBR) Grant
Description: The ABBF Small Business Revitalization Grant Program provides funding to Georgia-based, for-profit small businesses with fewer than 500 employees that were negatively impacted by COVID-19 and began operating on or before March 3, 2020. Grant funds can be used for eligible business expenses including payroll, rent, utilities, and other operational costs, and recipients must complete a mandatory Money Smart Business Program offered by the ABBF Grant team. No specific grant amount or application deadline was listed in the content provided, so interested businesses should contact ABBF directly for those details.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligibility: 
Business is located in Georgia
Business is for-profit
Fewer than 500 employees
Business began operating on or before March 3, 2020
Businesses experienced a negative economic impact from COVID-19

Name: Wayne Metro Neighborhood Beautification Grant
Description: The Neighborhood Beautification Program funds projects that improve public outdoor spaces in disadvantaged Detroit communities, including clean-up activities, community gardens, and public space improvements. Grants range from $500 to $15,000 and are available to eligible neighborhood associations, block clubs, nonprofits, or faith-based organizations, with requirements around site control, lot eligibility, budgets, plot plans, and supporting documents.

Name: Latino Economic Development Center MN Emergency Small Business Fund
Description: The Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) has launched the Latino & Immigrant Business Emergency Relief Fund to provide emergency grants to businesses in Minnesota facing revenue loss and disruption due to recent ICE activity, with priority for Latino-owned businesses on Saint Paul’s East Side (but businesses elsewhere in the state are encouraged to apply too). Grant funds can cover urgent needs like rent/mortgage, payroll, debt payments, and other crisis-related operating expenses, and the application is streamlined with no documents required upfront (selected applicants may be asked for financial/other documentation quickly).

Name: Watson Institute Ford Philanthropy Fellowship
Description: The Ford Philanthropy Fellowship is a fully funded leadership and entrepreneurship program for local entrepreneurs and community leaders developing solutions around community development, education, and disaster preparedness/response. It combines entrepreneurial training, mentorship, financial tools, a global network, and long-term alumni support.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Who you are:
You are a local entrepreneur or community leader deeply committed to strengthening your community through your work. Your venture is creating meaningful impact by supporting people, expanding access to essential services, or creating opportunities that help communities grow, adapt, and thrive. Your work may take many forms, including improving access to resources, supporting communities in times of need, advancing education or workforce opportunities, or building long-term community resilience.
You have firsthand experience with the challenges you seek to solve, are embedded in your community, and understand your local context. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit, a growth mindset, and a strong desire to grow as a leader while increasing your impact.

Your Business Stage:
You have been leading the work or your business/organization has been operating for 1-5 years, with fewer than 10 team members or employees. You have measurable impact to show and have secured some level or funding through grants, investments, donations, or revenue. You are ready to scale and be successful long-term.
Your Commitment:
You must be able to commit to the full program, including the virtual Immersive and weekly workshops held Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 8:00–10:00 AM MT. We prioritize participants who are fully committed to active engagement throughout the entire program. The program’s success depends on building a strong community where all participants are enthusiastic about both learning and sharing their experiences with others.

Where You Work:
Applicants located in and creating impact across Germany, Mexico, South Africa, Thailand, Brazil, and Vietnam are encouraged to apply. Priority will be given to those impacting Ford plant cities and areas that face recurring disaster declarations.
What You Are Looking For:
You seek expert-guided entrepreneurial training, a supportive community for feedback, a broad mentor network to enhance your leadership, and opportunities to challenge yourself by leading a Basecamp event and other initiatives that benefit your venture and community. You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and growth mindset to this work.
Demographics:
Adults 18 or Older.

Name: Braiding Seeds Fellowship
Description: Soul Fire Farm's Braiding Seeds Fellowship provides BIPOC beginning farmers in the northeast and southeast U.S. with a $50,000 stipend over 18 months, along with mentorship, professional development, farm finance support, and cohort gatherings. Eligible applicants must be Black, Indigenous, or people of color farmers ages 18+ with 1–3 years of experience running their own farm, based in one of 20 eligible states including NY, NC, GA, FL, VA, and others. Applications will reopen in summer 2026, with 12 runner-up mini-grants of $2,500 also available within the same application.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Beginning farmers and land stewards, ages 18+, with a minimum of 1 year of farming/land stewardship experience and no more than 3 years of experience running their own farm/land stewardship project, are welcome to apply. The fellowship is for Black, Indigenous, and people of color farmers* based in the northeast and southeast of the United States, in any of the following states: AL, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, LA, ME, MD, MA, MS, NH, NJ, NY, NC, PA, RI, SC, WV, VA, VT. The fellowship is for individuals, though fellows are welcome to share their resources with collaborators in their respective projects. Applicants should be passionate about the flourishing of Black agrarianism, Indigenous sovereignty, and the liberation of all peoples impacted by racial capitalism and settler colonialism.

Name: 500 Global Accelerator
Description: 500 Global’s Flagship Accelerator is a four-month, in-person program in Silicon Valley that helps early-stage startups scale through intensive founder programming, mentorship, and a growth-focused curriculum covering areas like product-market fit, go-to-market, pitch development, and fundraising. Companies accepted receive a $150,000 seed investment for 6% equity, plus access to 500 Global’s founder community and investor network and $1M+ in FounderHub perks/credits to support building and growth.

Name: Bold Path Fellowship
Description: The Bold Path Fellowship is a two-year, full-time program that provides $120,000 in funding, mentorship, and resources to help individuals from under-resourced or first-generation backgrounds pursue entrepreneurship after earning a degree or credential. It aims to make entrepreneurship a viable career pathway by supporting fellows through the costly and time-intensive early stages of building a business. Current and upcoming cohorts are based in Birmingham (AL), Raleigh-Durham (NC), and Minneapolis-St. Paul (MN), funded by the ECMC Group Education Impact Fund and ECMC Foundation.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Now a THREE-CITY program: Birmingham, Minneapolis-St. Paul and Raleigh-Durham, 50-mile radius each. Applicants must have finished postsecondary education in 2021 or later, show financial need, and commit full-time for two years. $120,000 over two years.

Name: Gold House Ventures Accelerator
Description: Gold House Ventures Accelerator is a 14-week immersive program for diverse-led tech startups across the U.S., originally focused on Asian Pacific founders but now expanded to support entrepreneurs from all underrepresented communities. It offers weekly masterclasses, 1:1 advising, curated investor intros, and a public Demo Day, plus strategic networking and perks, with eligibility for seed funding. Since 2020 it has backed 133 Asian Pacific-founded companies that have raised over $2B in follow-on capital.

Name: Illinois Local Food Infrastructure Grant (LFIG)
Description: The Illinois Department of Agriculture funds infrastructure that expands access to Illinois agricultural products within the state, covering the purchase, lease-to-own, rental, construction or installation of local food processing, aggregation and distribution capacity. Eligible work includes value-added and livestock processing, milling, dairy operations, refrigerated vehicles and community kitchens. Individual projects can receive up to seventy-five thousand dollars and collaborative projects up to two hundred fifty thousand.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Must be Illinois-based with 50 EMPLOYEES OR FEWER
- Eligible entity types: farms, cooperatives, processing facilities, food businesses, food hubs, nonprofits, and local governments
- Applicant must store, process, package, aggregate or distribute VALUE-ADDED products
- A match is required unless the applicant demonstrates a high-need condition, which may waive it
- ALL APPLICANTS MUST PRE-REGISTER before submitting an application

FUNDABLE: value-added processing, livestock processing, milling, dairy operations, refrigerated vehicles, community kitchens, and other local food supply chain infrastructure. Covers purchasing, leasing to own, renting, building or installing that infrastructure.

FY2027: $1.8 million available. Award ceilings $75,000 individual / $250,000 collaborative.

STATUS: FY2027 application dates have NOT been announced. Watch for the opening and pre-register early, since pre-registration gates the application itself.

Name: NH STEP Financial Assistance Award
Description: The Granite State District Export Council, through New Hampshire's Office of International Commerce and SBA's State Trade Expansion Program, reimburses 80% of eligible export-promotion costs for NH small businesses. Covered activities include trade show participation, international marketing materials, website internationalization and translation, export training, consultancy, product certification for foreign markets and eCommerce initiatives.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Application: https://nhexportassistance.com/export-promotion-grants/step-program-overview/step-faa-application - NH companies meeting SBA small-business-concern standards, seeking to export or expand internationally.

Name: South Dakota STEP Grant Program
Description: South Dakota Trade administers the SBA State Trade Expansion Program for South Dakota exporters, reimbursing up to 75% of eligible export-related expenses. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and recipients file quarterly activity reports. Two cycles have been funded to date: STEP 11 ($300,000) and STEP 12 ($333,333).
Amount: Up to 75% reimbursement of eligible export expenses (no per-company cap published)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Direct application: https://southdakotatrade.com/apply-for-the-step-grant-program - South Dakota-based eligible small business concern; profitable U.S. operations; product or service with at least 51% U.S. content; good standing with the SD Dept. of Revenue and IRS; agree to limited media release.

Name: Farm to Stay Grant Program (American Farmland Trust x Airbnb)
Description: National partnership between Airbnb and American Farmland Trust, run through AFT's Brighter Future Fund, funding for-profit farms and ranches that are creating or expanding farm stays and on-farm guest experiences as an additional income stream. Cash grants of a minimum $5,000 and up to $10,000 per recipient, with approximately 25-30 grants awarded from a $250,000 total pool.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Open to for-profit production agriculture operations — farmers and ranchers — that want to develop or expand a farm stay. This is explicitly a for-profit farm program, not a nonprofit program. Must be based in the United States or U.S. territories. Full eligibility guidelines, including any farm size or revenue limits, will be published before applications open in late November 2026. Applications are reviewed in the order received, with approximately 350 applications accepted, so applying early matters more than the closing date. Submitted through a secure portal on SurveyMonkey Apply. No application fee mentioned.

Name: The David Prize
Description: The David Prize awards $200,000 each to five New Yorkers with bold, transformative visions to improve life across the city’s five boroughs. Open to individuals — whether independent or affiliated with an organization — the Prize celebrates people with the conviction and creativity to strengthen communities, culture, and the city’s future. Funding is unrestricted.

Name: The Looking Out Foundation Grant
Description: The Looking Out Foundation awards grants of $5,000–$25,000 to 501(c)(3) nonprofits twice a year, with a focus on LGBTQIA2S+ support, disadvantaged youth, public health, women, the arts, food insecurity, and housing.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Grant decisions are made in May and November, with application deadlines of January 15 and July 1, respectively. Organizations may only apply once within any 12-month period, and previous grantees are encouraged to seek funding from other sources.

Name: Startup CPG Founders & Funders
Description: Startup CPG’s Founders & Funders 2026 is a highly selective, invite-only conference on December 10, 2026 in New York City connecting up to 150 emerging CPG brands with approximately 100 active investors through networking, panels, live pitches, and potential pre-scheduled 1:1 investor meetings. The program is primarily for brands raising pre-seed or seed capital, with eligibility limited to companies under $10M in retail revenue that are actively fundraising or expect to within 12 months; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a $350 ticket fee for accepted brands.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: This conference is primarily designed for CPG brands seeking pre-seed & seed funding. We're limiting attendance to 150 brands to ensure quality connections and meaningful interactions. Brands must apply to be considered for the conference, and will be notified if they are selected. Please understand we expect this to be very competitive, and we are really sorry we can't accommodate everyone, so please put your best foot forward in this application. If accepted, there will be a $350 ticket price for each brand for admission to the full day event, food/drinks provided, etc. Note: only one person per brand will be admitted to this event.

Name: SF La Cocina Incubator Program
Description: La Cocina is a San Francisco nonprofit incubator for food businesses run primarily by low-income women, immigrants, and people of color. The program provides affordable licensed commercial kitchen space, permitting help, sales and market opportunities, graphic design, food photography, legal advice, and business consulting over a roughly 4–5 month curriculum. Applications for Cohort 2026.03 open October 19 and close October 30, 2026; applicants must attend a free orientation first.
Amount: In-kind: subsidized kitchen space, consulting, and market access
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Prepared-food or packaged/CPG food businesses in the San Francisco Bay Area; applicants must meet La Cocina's low-income qualifications and attend an orientation before applying. The application requires a business plan, resume, two reference letters, and proof of income. Application window: October 19–30, 2026 (Cohort 2026.03).

Name: Boundless Futures Foundation EmpowHer Grant
Description: Boundless Futures Foundation’s EmpowHer Grants support U.S.-based female founders running revenue-generating, for-profit businesses that are five years old or less and create a clear social impact in areas like poverty/hunger/humanitarian aid or sustainability/environment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis during open cycles, with grants awarded twice a year (spring and fall).
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Eligible Applicants: 
- Female founders 22 years of age and older with businesses registered and operating in the United States. An applicant’s business must:
- Make a clear social impact;
- Be a registered for-profit entity;
- Be earning revenue, and 
- Not be more than five years old.

To be awarded grant funding, applicants must self-report a credit score and agree to a third-party background check. Please refer to the Boundless Futures Foundation website for more information.

Businesses that are eligible for an EmpowHer grant address one of the following social issues through their product or business model: 
- Poverty, Hunger, or Humanitarian Aid
- Sustainability & the Environment

Name: NIA Start-Up Challenge and Accelerator
Description: Prize competition and five-month immersive accelerator from the National Institute on Aging, aimed at aging research and life-science entrepreneurship. Focus areas include aging-related diseases, Alzheimer's and related dementias, healthy-aging solutions, and caregiver-support technologies. Beyond cash prizes, participants receive weekly virtual entrepreneurial education, 1:1 mentorship, pitch coaching, business, regulatory and reimbursement guidance, two sponsored in-person events, and investor and industry networking — with a core purpose of preparing participants to compete for NIH SBIR/STTR funding.
Amount: $24,000 (up to 21 finalists); $70,000 (up to 7 winners); $994,000 total purse
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Submissions open December 1, 2026 and close January 15, 2027; informational webinar December 3, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET. Individuals must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents and 18+; entities must be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the U.S. A company is NOT required at entry, but participants must form or have formed a U.S.-owned and operated small business meeting SBIR/STTR eligibility by November 1, 2027. Applicants may not be a principal investigator on an NIH SBIR/STTR award active at the close of the submission period, and may not have been a finalist in a previous NIA Start-Up Challenge. Federal and HHS employees are excluded. Non-U.S. citizens may join teams but cannot receive prize money. Run under America COMPETES Act prize authority. No application fee. Program hub: nia.nih.gov/research/sbir/start-challenge.

Name: Aurora Tech Award
Description: The Aurora Tech Award 2026, created by inDrive, is a global competition recognizing women founders of tech startups working to create positive social impact. The program offers an $85,000 prize fund—with $50K, $20K, and $15K awarded to the top three winners—alongside mentorship from industry leaders, VC feedback, and global media exposure. Eligible startups must be women-led, under five years old, with functional prototypes and less than $6M in funding.
Amount: up to $100K total / up to $50K non-dilutive per winner
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To participate, your startup is required to…
- Be founded or co-founded and led by a woman
- Have a functional prototype of a product
- Fit in the investment limit of $6 million in funding, including the seed round
- Be less than 5 years old
- Provide a presentation in the English language

Name: Women's Fund of Hawaii
Description: The Women's Fund of Hawaii awards grants of up to $10,000 to nonprofit organizations serving women and girls in Hawaii, with a focus on programs that promote financial security, dignity, and girls' leadership across a wide range of issues including housing, health, economic self-sufficiency, and violence prevention. The fund has a special interest in girls' programs, Native Hawaiian women and girls, and organizations in rural areas, and prefers that a majority of board members and program leadership are women. General operating costs, special projects, and small capital projects are all eligible. Next deadline is March 31st for Spring Grants Period.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
II. Grant Making Priorities
Women’s Fund of Hawaii supports programs serving women and girls in Hawaii that embody the above values and beliefs.

We give to a wide range of programs, particularly those that promote women’s financial security and dignity, and girls’ strengths and leadership.
We fund programs that build on the gifts, strengths, and assets of women and girls and promote their well-being.
We fund organizations that address factors that can stand in the way of women and girls’ success, including:
Abused/Neglected Girls
Adolescent Pregnancy
Culture/Arts
Disabilities
Economic Self-sufficiency
Education/Technology
Health (physical)
Homelessness
Homophobia
Immigration Status
Incarceration/Criminal Justice
Lack of Affordable Childcare
Lack of Affordable Housing
Mental Health
Poverty
Racism
Reproductive Rights/Health
Self Esteem
Sexual Exploitation of Women and Girls
Sports Inequities
Substance Abuse
Trafficking/Prostitution
Violence (sexual, physical)
We have a special interest in (but our funding is not limited to):

Funding girls’ programs
Funding programs serving Native Hawaiian women and girls
Funding programs in rural areas throughout the state
III.  Other Information
We prefer that a majority (51% or more) of Board members and program leadership are women, and that Board and staff reflect the population being served.
While we have a preference for funding smaller organizations, we will not exclude any organization from consideration because of size.
We fund nonprofit organizations, as well as programs that are sponsored projects of nonprofit organizations serving as fiscal agents. (We do not require those fiscal agents to have female Board leadership, but the program itself should have majority female leadership; also, we prefer that the fee for serving as fiscal agent be not more than 10% of the project budget.)
We fund startup and existing organizations/projects.
We fund general operating costs, special projects, and small capital projects.
We fund organizations or programs designed exclusively for women or girls. We do not fund general operating funds if it is unclear if those funds will specifically support women and girls’ programs.
If funded, the grantee is expected to submit a final report.
If you have the resources to send a press release to publicize this grant, we request that you share your draft with us before publication and provide a copy when it’s published.
Any organization that receives funding from Women’s Fund is welcome to apply for repeat funding. In order to be eligible to apply again, an organization must first use all of the original grant funds and submit a final report.
Our grants are up to $10,000.

Name: Pride Fund for LGBTQIA+ Business Owners
Description: Founders First CDC's National Pride Grant offers 20 LGBTQIA+ small business owners a $1,000 micro-grant plus free access to one of two business accelerator programs — Passport Community or Zebra Leadership — valued at up to $1,699. Eligible applicants must identify as LGBTQIA+, lead a U.S.-based business with 2–100 employees, at least one year in operation, and annual revenue under $5 million. The full application opens April 2026, with pre-registration available now.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
The LGBTQIA+ National Grant provides eligible small businesses the chance to receive one of 25 grant packages totaling $25,000. Founders First is committed to increasing the number of diverse founder-led businesses generating over $1 million dollars in revenues.

Eligibility Requirements:

Founder identifies as LGBTQIA+
Must be a CEO, President, or Business Owner
Must have an active U.S. based business
Business annual revenue does not exceed $5M
Must have between 2 to 100 employees
Minimum of 1 year in business

Name: Salt Lick Incubator Artist Project Grant
Description: The Salt Lick Incubator Artist Project Grant supports emerging independent musicians with $5,000–$15,000 for projects like recording music, creating videos or social media assets, touring, pressing vinyl, and strengthening branding or marketing. Eligible applicants must be U.S.-based artists or small groups, own their master recordings, be early in their careers, and not be signed to a label or using the grant for a project tied to an advance.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
To be eligible for a grant, applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

Be at least 18 years of age
Be a U.S. citizen or eligible to work in the United States
Be individuals or small groups (i.e., duos, trios, bands)
Be an emerging artist in the early stages of their professional artist careers
Must own the master recordings of your music
Must not have accepted an advance for the project being submitted
Cannot be in an active contract with a record label
Must not have released more than three (3) full-length albums of original music to date
This grant is not subject to commission by any industry partners, managers, etc. - all funds must go directly to the artist

If you believe that your work is aligned with our mission, values, and criteria, we welcome your application.

Name: Feed the Soul Foundation Restaurant Business Development Program
Description: A six-month cohort program for marginalized-owned culinary businesses, delivering roughly $15,000 in business development assistance per participant across finance and accounting, marketing, business expansion, operating procedures and HR, plus follow-on educational training. Earlier cohorts also carried $10,000 cash stipends; the current page frames the value as services rather than a direct grant, with the awarded amount set by a review process.
Amount: ~$15,000 in business development assistance (45 spots across 10 cities)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Direct application: https://feedthesoul.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gPK0ODLAxlJQRE - At least 51% owned by marginalized individuals (Black, Indigenous, Latinx, LGBTQIA+, senior, formerly incarcerated, veteran, or disabled); U.S. or Puerto Rico; operating at least 2 years. Annual window Feb 1 - Apr 15.

Name: Seattle Tenant Improvement Program
Description: Seattle's Office of Economic Development helps small businesses pay for physical improvements and equipment through two award tracks: a sign package worth up to $15,000 and an equipment package worth up to $50,000. Awards are structured as a 0% interest forgivable loan that converts to a grant after one year of continued operation, provided public benefit requirements are met. The 2026 cycle ran March through April.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit, independently owned business (no franchises), operating at least 2 years, fewer than 50 full-time employees, annual gross revenue under $2 million. Owner must have 3+ years of business experience and hold an active Seattle Business License with B&O taxes filed. Sign package up to $15,000; equipment package up to $50,000. Structured as a 0% interest forgivable loan converting to a grant after one year of continued operations. The 2026 cycle opened March 2, 2026 and closed April 13, 2026 at 5 p.m., with notifications in June 2026.

Name: Alamance County Chamber Small Business Grant Program
Description: The Alamance County Area Chamber of Commerce runs an annual two-track grant for businesses in Alamance County, North Carolina. Launch Grants of $1,500 to $5,000 serve businesses under two years old; Growth Grants of $5,000 to $15,000 serve established businesses with at least two years of tax filings. The 2026 round closed June 26 with awards announced in early September, and the chamber runs the program annually.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must operate in Alamance County, NC, and hold a separate business bank account and EIN. Launch track requires less than 2 years of operation; Growth track requires at least 2 years of tax filings. The chamber states the deadline is firm and no extensions are granted. 2026 cycle closed June 26, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET, with awards announced on/around September 4, 2026.

Name: Pittsburgh URA Commercial Facade Grant Program
Description: The Urban Redevelopment Authority of Pittsburgh reimburses up to 75% of eligible facade renovation costs, to a maximum of $20,000, for small businesses and property owners in the city's neighbourhood business districts. Eligible work covers lighting, signage, windows, doors, brick pointing and paint. Roughly 25 businesses are supported per funding round, and free technical assistance is available to applicants preparing a submission.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must be located within the City of Pittsburgh and operate in, or own, a building in commercial use (food, retail, professional services). Reimbursement grant - the applicant must finance 100% of project costs upfront and remains responsible for at least 25% of costs after reimbursement. Up to 75% reimbursed, maximum $20,000; approximately 25 businesses supported per round. Technical assistance available at business@ura.org. The 2026 round opened April 13, 2026 and closed May 29, 2026 at 5 p.m.

Name: Pow Wow Pitch
Description: Pow Wow Pitch is an annual pitch competition for Indigenous entrepreneurs across Canada and the United States, awarding $100,000 in total cash prizes. Entrants submit a one-minute video pitch; the top 100-plus advance as semi-finalists earning $1,000 each, and the Grand Finale awards $25,000, $10,000, $5,000 and a $5,000 Alumni Choice prize. A parallel in-person Trail circuit runs at community events. All entrants receive free mentorship and training.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Must identify as First Nation, Inuit, Metis, Native American, Alaska Native or Native Hawaiian, live in Canada or the United States, and be 10 years or older. Open to any business stage and any industry, including vendors and artists. 2026 cycle opened April 1 and closed June 14, 2026. No application fee. Participants receive free mentorship, training and a free .CA domain from CIRA. 2026 Grand Finale held October 21, 2026.

Name: IMPACT Pitch Competition
Description: Business Impact NW runs a four-round pitch competition for entrepreneurs across Alaska, Idaho, Oregon and Washington, progressing from written narrative through financial projections to a live final in Seattle. Forty-six thousand dollars is distributed across three ten-thousand-dollar grand prizes by business stage, ten one-thousand-dollar finalist grants with Canva Pro subscriptions, five community impact awards and an audience voting award. There is no application fee.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Owners must be 18+. Must hold a business licence from Alaska, Idaho, Oregon or Washington by the round-one deadline. Business must demonstrate direct impact in its immediate community. Prior grand prize winners ineligible. Excluded: nonprofits, tech companies, financial/lending businesses, cannabis operations and others. No application fee. 2026 cycle: applications opened April 27, Round 1 closed June 1 at 5pm PST; live final October 1, 2026 at the Brockey Center, South Seattle College. Prize pool $46,000 total.

Name: Downtown Detroit Markets Vendor Program
Description: Bedrock, the Downtown Detroit Partnership, the Gilbert Family Foundation and TechTown select product-based Michigan businesses to trade from heated chalets at Cadillac Square across the holiday season. Beyond the retail window, each selected vendor receives three thousand dollars to support the business during and after the season, plus TechTown mentoring, Wi-Fi, heat, electricity, furniture and security. A cross-organisation committee makes the selection each spring.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Product-based businesses only (not service-based); Michigan-registered with a valid sales tax licence; in business at least two years with minimum $10,000 annual revenue; $1 million general liability insurance required. Booth fees: $1,500 initial payment plus a second payment of $600 or $1,000 depending on space size (approx 10x10 or 10x13). 2026 cycle: applications opened April 28, closed June 1, notifications July 9; market ran November 11, 2026 - January 3, 2027 at Cadillac Square.

Name: Southern Minnesota SMIF Economic Development Grant
Description: The Southern Minnesota Initiative Foundation awards grants of up to $10,000 for economic development projects across its 20-county region and Native nation, with preference for organizations serving communities under 10,000 population. Applicants need not be located in the region provided the project creates measurable impact there. The 2026 cycle closed August 10 with awards announced by November 16; eligibility widens to government units and public institutions in 2027.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT open to for-profit businesses - IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofits only for 2026; other 501(c) organizations and informal groups may apply through a 501(c)(3) fiscal host. Individuals and businesses are ineligible. Government units and public institutions become eligible in 2027. Projects must impact SMIF's 20-county southern Minnesota region and Native nation. Apply via https://goapply2.akoyago.com/SMIF/ . Contact Jennifer Heien, 507-214-7040.

Name: USDA Rural Business Development Grant
Description: USDA Rural Development's Rural Business Development Grant funds projects that benefit small and emerging rural businesses. Enterprise Grants support training, technical assistance, land and facility acquisition, equipment, revolving loan funds, business incubators and transportation improvements; Opportunity Grants fund economic development planning, feasibility studies and entrepreneur training. There is no set maximum award and no cost-share requirement, though smaller requests receive scoring priority.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: NOT open to for-profit businesses - only public bodies and government entities, federally recognized Indian Tribes, and nonprofit organizations serving rural areas may apply; individuals and sole proprietors are ineligible. Funds pass through to benefit small and emerging rural businesses. SAM.gov registration required; submitted via Grants.gov by 4:30 p.m. local time.
