FY2026 had two deadlines - June 15, 2026 for Strategic Economic and Community Development applications and June 30, 2026 for all others. Contact your state Rural Development office before applying.

Name: ActivatOR Outdoor Recreation Growth Accelerator
Description: New Mexico's Economic Development Department and Outdoor Recreation Division run a free seven-week hybrid accelerator for outdoor recreation businesses headquartered in the state. The cohort covers financial management, funding strategy, marketing, AI tools, rural entrepreneurship and pitch development, delivered through regional learning hubs with expert mentorship, individualised support and limited travel support for eligible participants. Both for-profit and nonprofit businesses up to fifty employees qualify.
Amount: Free seven-week accelerator (mentorship, workshops, limited travel support)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: For-profit and nonprofit businesses headquartered in New Mexico, up to 50 employees, from startups to established companies, in the outdoor recreation sector. Apply at activatenm.com/activator. 2026 cycle: announced July 22, 2026; applications closed August 31, 2026 at 11:59pm MT; participants notified by September 8, 2026; cohort ran September 16 - October 30, 2026. Delivered via regional hybrid learning hubs across New Mexico.

Name: PA CDFI Network BASC & Microgrants Program
Description: The PA CDFI Network delivers microgrants of $7,500 to $20,000 to historically disadvantaged Pennsylvania entrepreneurs, paired with free regional business coaching through seven Business Assistance Service Centers covering all 67 counties. Award size is set by business size, demonstrated need, revenue and program guidelines. The 2026 cycle ran July 9 to August 10 and is now closed; the program runs in defined annual windows supported by CDFIs and SBDCs statewide.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must be for-profit and operating in Pennsylvania, at least 51% owned or controlled by one or more historically disadvantaged individuals who are PA residents, have fewer than 100 full-time employees, generate at least 51% of revenue in PA, file Pennsylvania tax returns, and be actively operating when funds are awarded. Seven regional Business Assistance Service Centers provide free coaching year-round regardless of grant cycle.

Name: PitchMI Startup Competition
Description: The Michigan Economic Development Corporation and the MSU Research Foundation run one of the country's largest founder-focused startup competitions, distributing two million dollars across four regional semifinals and a statewide championship. Each of four semifinal winners takes two hundred and fifty thousand dollars and the championship winner takes one million. Semifinals are themed by sector - defence and aerospace, AI and software, advanced manufacturing and materials, and healthcare and life sciences.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Michigan-based startups. Applications submitted via PitchMI.org. 2026-27 cycle: applications closed August 10, 2026. Semifinals - Grand Rapids (Defense & Aerospace) September 15; Kalamazoo (AI & Software) September 22; Marquette (Advanced Manufacturing, Materials & Outdoors) September 24; Detroit (Healthcare & Life Sciences) October 1. $250,000 to each of four semifinal winners plus $1 million statewide championship.

Name: Dunn County Small Business Development Grant
Description: The Dunn Economic Development Corporation awards up to $10,000 per business to for-profit small businesses in Dunn County, Wisconsin, across three tracks: technical assistance, commercial space support and economic development loan fund matching. The inaugural 2025 round awarded nearly $115,000 to 27 businesses and startups. The second round closed 18 September 2026 and the program appears to run annually in late summer.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Business must be located in Dunn County, WI and cannot relocate there solely to receive funds. 25 or fewer full-time employees. Must be a for-profit business. Both startups and established businesses qualify. Three funding tracks: technical assistance, commercial space support, economic development loan fund matching. Round 2 application (now closed): https://mailchi.mp/779c05c3a152/small-business-development-grant

Name: HIGH FIVE Grant for Moms
Description: The Mama Ladder runs an annual grant competition for mom-owned businesses, with finalists sharing grant awards and a public voting round deciding the grand prize. The 2026 cycle ran September 1-30 with judging in October; the program has awarded funds every year since 2018. Applications are expected to reopen around September 1, 2027.
Amount: Finalist grants (program has awarded $115,500 since 2018; historically $1,000-$10,000 tiers)
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: 2026 application form: https://form.jotform.com/crystalee/2026HighFiveGrant - Mothers (including expecting, step and foster moms) owning at least 50% of a for-profit business, verified revenue $10,000-$500,000/yr, HQ in US or Canada.

Name: TX TWU Center for Women Entrepreneurs StartUP Grant
Description: Texas Woman's University's Center for Women Entrepreneurs awards ten $5,000 StartUP Grants to help eligible Texas startups launch new initiatives and accelerate growth. Approved uses include equipment, technology, inventory, marketing and property improvements; wages, salaries and sales tax are excluded. Recipients must complete a business plan, participate in business advising, and finish a virtual small-business training course.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Direct application: https://texaswomansuniversity.submittable.com/submit/a6b2ef42-9b6d-41da-b010-c967ac5d0cba/2026-startup-grant - For-profit business operating in Texas; no more than 10 FTEs excluding the owner; no TWU affiliation required. Annual window Sept 1 - Sept 23.

Name: Roanoke Business Equipment Incentive Program
Description: The Roanoke Economic Development Authority reimburses half the cost of equipment purchases by established businesses in the city, up to twenty thousand dollars for manufacturing and industrial firms and five thousand for retail and commercial firms. Equipment must be taxed as business personal property or subject to the machinery and tools tax, cost at least five hundred dollars per item, and exclude motor vehicles.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
- Operating in a commercially zoned City of Roanoke location for at least one year prior to the round opening
- Current on all city business taxes, valid city business license where required
- Manufacturing/industrial: minimum 2 full-time W-2 employees. Retail/commercial: minimum 1 full-time W-2 employee
- Not a recipient in the prior year's round
- Equipment taxed as Business Personal Property or under Machinery & Tools Tax; minimum $500 per item; maximum 10 items; motor vehicles excluded
- Grant equals 50% of actual purchase price

DEADLINE CORRECTION: 9/30/2026 is the date awarded purchases must be COMPLETED, not an application deadline. Applications close when funds are fully committed. The next round opens 10/1/2026 - the Deadline field holds that expected open date.

Name: CERF+ Emergency Relief Grant
Description: CERF+ provides emergency relief grants of $3,000 to individual craft artists whose work has been disrupted by a recent, unforeseeable emergency such as fire, flood, theft, accident, injury or major illness. Funds help artists recover their studios, tools and practices. Applications are normally accepted year-round with no deadline, but CERF+ has suspended all grantmaking for the remainder of fiscal year 2026 and expects to resume awards on October 1, 2026.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info: Individual craft artists aged 18+; must have lived and worked in the US or US territories for at least two years; active, recent engagement in the craft community. Qualifying emergency must be unforeseeable, outside the applicant's control, recent and substantially disruptive to craft practice (fire, flood, theft, accident, injury, major illness) - not routine medical care, unemployment or ongoing circumstances. Ineligible practices: painting, photography, digital art, performing arts, and jewelry assembled from factory-made parts. Requires ID verification and documentation of artistic practice. No application fee.

Name: Detroit Black Farmer Land Fund
Description: The Detroit Black Farmer Land Fund (DBFLF) is a coalition of three Detroit urban farming organizations working to rebuild intergenerational land ownership for Black farmers in Detroit, offering a competitive Land Grant to help Black farmers secure property. The grant application opens on Juneteenth, June 19, 2026, and the fund hosted an Application Tour at Detroit public libraries in April 2026 to help prospective applicants learn about the program and get one-on-one support completing their applications. For more information, interested farmers can contact detroitblackfarmerlandfund@gmail.com.
Eligibility Criteria / Additional Info:
Link is to register for the application tour. See details for application tour below. 

About the Application Tour
The application tour will stop at various Detroit public libraries, making it convenient for community members to learn about the program, access resources, and complete their applications. These sessions will include:

Guidance on completing applications to maximize the chances of success.
One-on-one support from DBFLF representatives.
Opportunities to network with other aspiring farmers and local agricultural advocates.
Information on funding, resources, and next steps for land acquisition.
Benefits of Participating

Ownership and Empowerment: The fund helps break down barriers to land ownership, fostering economic independence and food security within Black communities.
Cultural Preservation: This initiative supports the continuation of agricultural traditions rooted in Black history and the African diaspora.
Community Impact: With more local growers, Detroit benefits from improved access to fresh, healthy, and affordable produce, building a stronger, more resilient local food system.
Environmental Stewardship: Participants can contribute to sustainable farming practices, improving urban green spaces and ecological health.
